/commands/CLAUDE.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 1 | # Commands Module
 2 | 
 3 | **Purpose**: Defines async command handlers for long-running operations via `surreal-commands` job queue system.
 4 | 
 5 | ## Key Components
 6 | 
 7 | ### Embedding Commands
 8 | 
 9 | - **`embed_note_command`**: Embeds a single note using unified embedding pipeline with content-type aware processing. Uses MARKDOWN content type detection. Retry: 5 attempts, exponential jitter 1-60s.
10 | - **`embed_insight_command`**: Embeds a single source insight. Uses MARKDOWN content type. Retry: 5 attempts, exponential jitter 1-60s.
11 | - **`embed_source_command`**: Embeds a source by chunking full_text with content-type aware splitters (HTML, Markdown, plain), then batch embedding all chunks. Uses single Esperanto API call. Retry: 5 attempts, exponential jitter 1-60s.
12 | - **`create_insight_command`**: Creates a source insight with automatic retry on transaction conflicts. Creates the DB record, then submits `embed_insight` command (fire-and-forget). Retry: 5 attempts, exponential jitter 1-60s. Used by `Source.add_insight()`.
13 | - **`rebuild_embeddings_command`**: Submits individual embed_* commands for all sources/notes/insights. Returns immediately; actual embedding happens async. No retry (coordinator only).
14 | 
15 | ### Other Commands
16 | 
17 | - **`process_source_command`**: Ingests content through `source_graph`, creates embeddings (optional), and generates insights. Retries on transaction conflicts (exp. jitter, max 15×, 1-120s).
18 | - **`run_transformation_command`**: Runs a transformation on an existing source to generate an insight. Executes the transformation graph (LLM call) then creates insight via `create_insight_command`. Used by `POST /sources/{id}/insights` API endpoint. Retry: 5 attempts, exponential jitter 1-60s.
19 | - **`generate_podcast_command`**: Creates podcasts via `podcast-creator` library using stored episode/speaker profiles.
20 | - **`process_text_command`** (example): Test fixture for text operations (uppercase, lowercase, reverse, word_count).
21 | - **`analyze_data_command`** (example): Test fixture for numeric aggregations.
22 | 
23 | ## Important Patterns
24 | 
25 | - **Pydantic I/O**: All commands use `CommandInput`/`CommandOutput` subclasses for type safety and serialization.
26 | - **Error handling**: Permanent errors (ValueError) return failure output; all other exceptions auto-retry via surreal-commands.
27 | - **Retry configuration**: Uses `stop_on: [ValueError]` (blocklist approach) - retries all exceptions EXCEPT ValueError. This is more resilient than allowlist as new exception types auto-retry.
28 | - **Fire-and-forget embedding**: Domain models submit embed_* commands via `submit_command()` without waiting. Commands process asynchronously.
29 | - **Content-type aware chunking**: `embed_source_command` uses `chunk_text()` with automatic content type detection (HTML, Markdown, plain text) for optimal text splitting. Default: 1500 char chunks with 225 char overlap.
30 | - **Batch embedding**: `embed_source_command` uses `generate_embeddings()` for single API call efficiency instead of per-chunk calls.
31 | - **Mean pooling for large content**: `embed_note_command` and `embed_insight_command` use `generate_embedding()` which handles content larger than chunk size via mean pooling.
32 | - **Model dumping**: Recursive `full_model_dump()` utility converts Pydantic models → dicts for DB/API responses.
33 | - **Logging**: Uses `loguru.logger` throughout; logs execution start/end and key metrics (processing time, counts).
34 | - **Time tracking**: All commands measure `start_time` → `processing_time` for monitoring.
35 | 
36 | ## Dependencies
37 | 
38 | **External**: `surreal_commands` (command decorator, job queue, submit_command), `loguru`, `pydantic`, `podcast_creator`
39 | **Internal**: `open_notebook.domain.notebook` (Source, Note, SourceInsight), `open_notebook.utils.chunking` (chunk_text, detect_content_type), `open_notebook.utils.embedding` (generate_embedding, generate_embeddings), `open_notebook.database.repository` (repo_query, repo_insert)
40 | 
41 | ## Quirks & Edge Cases
42 | 
43 | - **source_commands**: `ensure_record_id()` wraps command IDs for DB storage; transaction conflicts trigger exponential backoff retry. ValueError exceptions are permanent (not retried).
44 | - **embedding_commands**: Content type detection uses file extension as primary source, heuristics as fallback. Chunks >1800 chars trigger secondary splitting. Empty/whitespace-only content returns ValueError (not retried).
45 | - **rebuild_embeddings_command**: Returns "jobs_submitted" not "processed_items" - embedding is async. Individual commands handle failures with their own retries.
46 | - **podcast_commands**: Profiles loaded from SurrealDB by name (must exist); briefing can be extended with suffix. Episode records created mid-execution.
47 | - **Example commands**: Accept optional `delay_seconds` for testing async behavior; not for production.
48 | 
49 | ## Code Example
50 | 
51 | ```python
52 | @command("process_source", app="open_notebook", retry={
53 |     "max_attempts": 5,
54 |     "wait_strategy": "exponential_jitter",
55 |     "stop_on": [ValueError],  # Don't retry validation errors
56 | })
57 | async def process_source_command(input_data: SourceProcessingInput) -> SourceProcessingOutput:
58 |     start_time = time.time()
59 |     try:
60 |         transformations = [await Transformation.get(id) for id in input_data.transformations]
61 |         source = await Source.get(input_data.source_id)
62 |         result = await source_graph.ainvoke({...})
63 |         return SourceProcessingOutput(success=True, ...)
64 |     except ValueError as e:
65 |         return SourceProcessingOutput(success=False, error_message=str(e))  # No retry
66 |     except Exception as e:
67 |         raise  # Retry all other exceptions
68 | ```
69 |

  1 | /**
  2 |  * Runtime configuration for the frontend.
  3 |  * This allows the same Docker image to work in different environments.
  4 |  */
  5 | 
  6 | import { AppConfig, BackendConfigResponse } from '@/lib/types/config'
  7 | 
  8 | // Build timestamp for debugging - set at build time
  9 | const BUILD_TIME = new Date().toISOString()
 10 | 
 11 | let config: AppConfig | null = null
 12 | let configPromise: Promise<AppConfig> | null = null
 13 | 
 14 | /**
 15 |  * Get the API URL to use for requests.
 16 |  *
 17 |  * Priority:
 18 |  * 1. Runtime config from API server (/api/config endpoint)
 19 |  * 2. Environment variable (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL)
 20 |  * 3. Default fallback (http://localhost:5055)
 21 |  */
 22 | export async function getApiUrl(): Promise<string> {
 23 |   // If we already have config, return it
 24 |   if (config) {
 25 |     return config.apiUrl
 26 |   }
 27 | 
 28 |   // If we're already fetching, wait for that
 29 |   if (configPromise) {
 30 |     const cfg = await configPromise
 31 |     return cfg.apiUrl
 32 |   }
 33 | 
 34 |   // Start fetching config
 35 |   configPromise = fetchConfig()
 36 |   const cfg = await configPromise
 37 |   return cfg.apiUrl
 38 | }
 39 | 
 40 | /**
 41 |  * Get the full configuration.
 42 |  */
 43 | export async function getConfig(): Promise<AppConfig> {
 44 |   if (config) {
 45 |     return config
 46 |   }
 47 | 
 48 |   if (configPromise) {
 49 |     return await configPromise
 50 |   }
 51 | 
 52 |   configPromise = fetchConfig()
 53 |   return await configPromise
 54 | }
 55 | 
 56 | /**
 57 |  * Fetch configuration from the API or use defaults.
 58 |  */
 59 | async function fetchConfig(): Promise<AppConfig> {
 60 |   const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'
 61 |   
 62 |   if (isDev) {
 63 |     console.log('🔧 [Config] Starting configuration detection...')
 64 |     console.log('🔧 [Config] Build time:', BUILD_TIME)
 65 |   }
 66 | 
 67 |   // STEP 1: Try to get runtime config from Next.js server-side endpoint
 68 |   // This allows API_URL to be set at runtime (not baked into build)
 69 |   // Note: Endpoint is at /config (not /api/config) to avoid reverse proxy conflicts
 70 |   let runtimeApiUrl: string | null = null
 71 |   try {
 72 |     if (isDev) console.log('🔧 [Config] Attempting to fetch runtime config from /config endpoint...')
 73 |     const runtimeResponse = await fetch('/config', {
 74 |       cache: 'no-store',
 75 |     })
 76 |     if (runtimeResponse.ok) {
 77 |       const runtimeData = await runtimeResponse.json()
 78 |       runtimeApiUrl = runtimeData.apiUrl
 79 |       // Treat empty string as "not set" to allow fallback to env var or default
 80 |       if (runtimeApiUrl === '') {
 81 |         runtimeApiUrl = null
 82 |       }
 83 |       if (isDev) console.log('✅ [Config] Runtime API URL from server:', runtimeApiUrl)
 84 |     } else {
 85 |       if (isDev) console.log('⚠️ [Config] Runtime config endpoint returned status:', runtimeResponse.status)
 86 |     }
 87 |   } catch (error) {
 88 |     if (isDev) console.log('⚠️ [Config] Could not fetch runtime config:', error)
 89 |   }
 90 | 
 91 |   // STEP 2: Fallback to build-time environment variable
 92 |   const envApiUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL
 93 |   if (isDev) console.log('🔧 [Config] NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL from build:', envApiUrl || '(not set)')
 94 | 
 95 |   // STEP 3: Smart default - prefer relative path to use Next.js Rewrites
 96 |   // This avoids CORS issues and port mapping complexities by proxying through Next.js
 97 |   const defaultApiUrl = ''
 98 | 
 99 |   if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && isDev) {
100 |       console.log('🔧 [Config] Using relative path (rewrites) as default')
101 |   }
102 | 
103 |   // Priority: Runtime config > Build-time env var > Smart default
104 |   // Note: runtimeApiUrl must be checked against null explicitly as empty string might be valid if intended (though we treat '' as null above)
105 |   const baseUrl = runtimeApiUrl !== null && runtimeApiUrl !== undefined ? runtimeApiUrl : (envApiUrl || defaultApiUrl)
106 |   if (isDev) {
107 |     console.log('🔧 [Config] Final base URL to try:', baseUrl)
108 |     console.log('🔧 [Config] Selection priority: runtime=' + (runtimeApiUrl ? '✅' : '❌') +
109 |                 ', build-time=' + (envApiUrl ? '✅' : '❌') +
110 |                 ', smart-default=' + (!runtimeApiUrl && !envApiUrl ? '✅' : '❌'))
111 |   }
112 | 
113 |   try {
114 |     if (isDev) console.log('🔧 [Config] Fetching backend config from:', `${baseUrl}/api/config`)
115 |     // Try to fetch runtime config from backend API
116 |     const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/api/config`, {
117 |       cache: 'no-store',
118 |     })
119 | 
120 |     if (response.ok) {
121 |       const data: BackendConfigResponse = await response.json()
122 |       config = {
123 |         apiUrl: baseUrl, // Use baseUrl from runtime-config (Python no longer returns this)
124 |         version: data.version || 'unknown',
125 |         buildTime: BUILD_TIME,
126 |         latestVersion: data.latestVersion || null,
127 |         hasUpdate: data.hasUpdate || false,
128 |         dbStatus: data.dbStatus, // Can be undefined for old backends
129 |       }
130 |       if (isDev) console.log('✅ [Config] Successfully loaded API config:', config)
131 |       return config
132 |     } else {
133 |       // Don't log error here - ConnectionGuard will display it
134 |       throw new Error(`API config endpoint returned status ${response.status}`)
135 |     }
136 |   } catch (error) {
137 |     // Don't log error here - ConnectionGuard will display it with proper UI
138 |     throw error
139 |   }
140 | }
141 | 
142 | /**
143 |  * Reset the configuration cache (useful for testing).
144 |  */
145 | export function resetConfig(): void {
146 |   config = null
147 |   configPromise = null
148 | }
149 |

  2 | DEFINE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS chat_session SCHEMALESS;
  3 | 
  4 | DEFINE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS refers_to
  5 | TYPE RELATION 
  6 | FROM chat_session TO notebook;
  7 | 
  8 | REMOVE FUNCTION IF EXISTS fn::vector_search;
  9 | 
 10 | DEFINE FUNCTION IF NOT EXISTS fn::vector_search($query: array<float>, $match_count: int, $sources: bool, $show_notes: bool, $min_similarity: float) {
 11 |     let $source_embedding_search = 
 12 |         IF $sources {(
 13 |             SELECT 
 14 |                 id,
 15 |                 source.title as title,
 16 |                 content,
 17 |                 source.id as parent_id,
 18 |                 vector::similarity::cosine(embedding, $query) as similarity
 19 |             FROM source_embedding 
 20 |             WHERE vector::similarity::cosine(embedding, $query) >= $min_similarity
 21 |             ORDER BY similarity DESC
 22 |             LIMIT $match_count
 23 |         )}
 24 |         ELSE { [] };
 25 | 
 26 |     let $source_insight_search = 
 27 |         IF $sources {(
 28 |             SELECT 
 29 |                 id,
 30 |                 insight_type + ' - ' + source.title as title,
 31 |                 content,
 32 |                 source.id as parent_id,
 33 |                 vector::similarity::cosine(embedding, $query) as similarity
 34 |             FROM source_insight
 35 |             WHERE vector::similarity::cosine(embedding, $query) >= $min_similarity
 36 |             ORDER BY similarity DESC
 37 |             LIMIT $match_count
 38 |         )}
 39 |         ELSE { [] };
 40 | 
 41 | 
 42 |     let $note_content_search = 
 43 |         IF $show_notes {(
 44 |             SELECT 
 45 |                 id,
 46 |                 title,
 47 |                 content,
 48 |                 id as parent_id,
 49 |                 vector::similarity::cosine(embedding, $query) as similarity
 50 |             FROM note
 51 |             WHERE vector::similarity::cosine(embedding, $query) >= $min_similarity
 52 |             ORDER BY similarity DESC
 53 |             LIMIT $match_count
 54 |         )}
 55 |         ELSE { [] };
 56 | 
 57 | 
 58 |     let $all_results = array::union(
 59 |         array::union($source_embedding_search, $source_insight_search),
 60 |         $note_content_search
 61 |     );
 62 | 
 63 | 
 64 |     RETURN (
 65 |         SELECT 
 66 |             id, title, content, parent_id,
 67 |             math::max(similarity) as similarity
 68 |         FROM $all_results
 69 |         GROUP BY id
 70 |         ORDER BY similarity DESC
 71 |         LIMIT $match_count
 72 |     );
 73 | };
 74 | 
 75 | 
 76 | REMOVE FUNCTION IF EXISTS fn::text_search;
 77 | 
 78 | 
 79 | DEFINE FUNCTION IF NOT EXISTS fn::text_search($query_text: string, $match_count: int, $sources:bool, $show_notes:bool) {
 80 |   
 81 |     let $source_title_search = 
 82 |         IF $sources {(
 83 |             SELECT id, title, 
 84 |             search::highlight('`', '`', 1) as content,
 85 |             id as parent_id,
 86 |             math::max(search::score(1)) AS relevance
 87 |             FROM source
 88 |             WHERE title @1@ $query_text
 89 |             GROUP BY id)}
 90 |         ELSE { [] };
 91 |     
 92 |     let $source_embedding_search = 
 93 |          IF $sources {(
 94 |             SELECT id as id, source.title as title, search::highlight('`', '`', 1) as content, source.id as parent_id, math::max(search::score(1)) AS relevance
 95 |             FROM source_embedding
 96 |             WHERE content @1@ $query_text
 97 |             GROUP BY id)}
 98 |         ELSE { [] };
 99 | 
100 |     let $source_full_search = 
101 |          IF $sources {(
102 |             SELECT source.id as id, source.title as title, search::highlight('`', '`', 1) as content, source.id as parent_id, math::max(search::score(1)) AS relevance
103 |             FROM source
104 |             WHERE full_text @1@ $query_text
105 |             GROUP BY id)}
106 |         ELSE { [] };
107 |     
108 |     let $source_insight_search = 
109 |          IF $sources {(
110 |              SELECT id, insight_type + " - " + source.title as title, search::highlight('`', '`', 1) as content, source.id as parent_id,  math::max(search::score(1)) AS relevance
111 |             FROM source_insight
112 |             WHERE content @1@ $query_text
113 |             GROUP BY id)}
114 |         ELSE { [] };
115 | 
116 |     let $note_title_search = 
117 |          IF $show_notes {(
118 |              SELECT id, title, search::highlight('`', '`', 1) as content,  id as parent_id, math::max(search::score(1)) AS relevance
119 |             FROM note
120 |             WHERE title @1@ $query_text
121 |             GROUP BY id)}
122 |         ELSE { [] };
123 | 
124 |      let $note_content_search = 
125 |          IF $show_notes {(
126 |              SELECT id, title, search::highlight('`', '`', 1) as content,  id as parent_id, math::max(search::score(1)) AS relevance
127 |             FROM note
128 |             WHERE content @1@ $query_text
129 |             GROUP BY id)}
130 |         ELSE { [] };
131 | 
132 |     let $source_chunk_results = array::union($source_embedding_search, $source_full_search);
133 |     
134 |     let $source_asset_results = array::union($source_title_search, $source_insight_search);
135 | 
136 |     let $source_results = array::union($source_chunk_results, $source_asset_results );
137 |     let $note_results = array::union($note_title_search, $note_content_search );
138 |     let $final_results = array::union($source_results, $note_results );
139 | 
140 |     RETURN (SELECT id, title, content, parent_id, math::max(relevance) as relevance from $final_results
141 |         where id is not None        
142 | group by id, title, content, parent_id ORDER BY relevance DESC LIMIT $match_count);
143 |     
144 |     
145 | };
146 |

  1 | """
  2 | Transformations service layer using API.
  3 | """
  4 | 
  5 | from datetime import datetime
  6 | from typing import Any, Dict, List, Union
  7 | 
  8 | from loguru import logger
  9 | 
 10 | from api.client import api_client
 11 | from open_notebook.domain.transformation import Transformation
 12 | 
 13 | 
 14 | class TransformationsService:
 15 |     """Service layer for transformations operations using API."""
 16 | 
 17 |     def __init__(self):
 18 |         logger.info("Using API for transformations operations")
 19 | 
 20 |     def get_all_transformations(self) -> List[Transformation]:
 21 |         """Get all transformations."""
 22 |         transformations_data = api_client.get_transformations()
 23 |         # Convert API response to Transformation objects
 24 |         transformations = []
 25 |         for trans_data in transformations_data:
 26 |             transformation = Transformation(
 27 |                 name=trans_data["name"],
 28 |                 title=trans_data["title"],
 29 |                 description=trans_data["description"],
 30 |                 prompt=trans_data["prompt"],
 31 |                 apply_default=trans_data["apply_default"],
 32 |             )
 33 |             transformation.id = trans_data["id"]
 34 |             transformation.created = datetime.fromisoformat(
 35 |                 trans_data["created"].replace("Z", "+00:00")
 36 |             )
 37 |             transformation.updated = datetime.fromisoformat(
 38 |                 trans_data["updated"].replace("Z", "+00:00")
 39 |             )
 40 |             transformations.append(transformation)
 41 |         return transformations
 42 | 
 43 |     def get_transformation(self, transformation_id: str) -> Transformation:
 44 |         """Get a specific transformation."""
 45 |         response = api_client.get_transformation(transformation_id)
 46 |         trans_data = response if isinstance(response, dict) else response[0]
 47 |         transformation = Transformation(
 48 |             name=trans_data["name"],
 49 |             title=trans_data["title"],
 50 |             description=trans_data["description"],
 51 |             prompt=trans_data["prompt"],
 52 |             apply_default=trans_data["apply_default"],
 53 |         )
 54 |         transformation.id = trans_data["id"]
 55 |         transformation.created = datetime.fromisoformat(
 56 |             trans_data["created"].replace("Z", "+00:00")
 57 |         )
 58 |         transformation.updated = datetime.fromisoformat(
 59 |             trans_data["updated"].replace("Z", "+00:00")
 60 |         )
 61 |         return transformation
 62 | 
 63 |     def create_transformation(
 64 |         self,
 65 |         name: str,
 66 |         title: str,
 67 |         description: str,
 68 |         prompt: str,
 69 |         apply_default: bool = False,
 70 |     ) -> Transformation:
 71 |         """Create a new transformation."""
 72 |         response = api_client.create_transformation(
 73 |             name=name,
 74 |             title=title,
 75 |             description=description,
 76 |             prompt=prompt,
 77 |             apply_default=apply_default,
 78 |         )
 79 |         trans_data = response if isinstance(response, dict) else response[0]
 80 |         transformation = Transformation(
 81 |             name=trans_data["name"],
 82 |             title=trans_data["title"],
 83 |             description=trans_data["description"],
 84 |             prompt=trans_data["prompt"],
 85 |             apply_default=trans_data["apply_default"],
 86 |         )
 87 |         transformation.id = trans_data["id"]
 88 |         transformation.created = datetime.fromisoformat(
 89 |             trans_data["created"].replace("Z", "+00:00")
 90 |         )
 91 |         transformation.updated = datetime.fromisoformat(
 92 |             trans_data["updated"].replace("Z", "+00:00")
 93 |         )
 94 |         return transformation
 95 | 
 96 |     def update_transformation(self, transformation: Transformation) -> Transformation:
 97 |         """Update a transformation."""
 98 |         if not transformation.id:
 99 |             raise ValueError("Transformation ID is required for update")
100 | 
101 |         updates = {
102 |             "name": transformation.name,
103 |             "title": transformation.title,
104 |             "description": transformation.description,
105 |             "prompt": transformation.prompt,
106 |             "apply_default": transformation.apply_default,
107 |         }
108 |         response = api_client.update_transformation(transformation.id, **updates)
109 |         trans_data = response if isinstance(response, dict) else response[0]
110 | 
111 |         # Update the transformation object with the response
112 |         transformation.name = trans_data["name"]
113 |         transformation.title = trans_data["title"]
114 |         transformation.description = trans_data["description"]
115 |         transformation.prompt = trans_data["prompt"]
116 |         transformation.apply_default = trans_data["apply_default"]
117 |         transformation.updated = datetime.fromisoformat(
118 |             trans_data["updated"].replace("Z", "+00:00")
119 |         )
120 | 
121 |         return transformation
122 | 
123 |     def delete_transformation(self, transformation_id: str) -> bool:
124 |         """Delete a transformation."""
125 |         api_client.delete_transformation(transformation_id)
126 |         return True
127 | 
128 |     def execute_transformation(
129 |         self, transformation_id: str, input_text: str, model_id: str
130 |     ) -> Union[Dict[Any, Any], List[Dict[Any, Any]]]:
131 |         """Execute a transformation on input text."""
132 |         result = api_client.execute_transformation(
133 |             transformation_id=transformation_id,
134 |             input_text=input_text,
135 |             model_id=model_id,
136 |         )
137 |         return result
138 | 
139 | 
140 | # Global service instance
141 | transformations_service = TransformationsService()
142 |

 14 | from open_notebook.graphs.transformation import (

 26 | 
 27 | class TestGraphTools:

 30 |     def test_get_current_timestamp_format(self):
 31 |         """Test timestamp tool returns correct format."""
 32 |         timestamp = get_current_timestamp.func()

138 |

140 |             <Button type="button" variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>

/open_notebook/utils/README.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # ContextBuilder
  2 | 
  3 | A flexible and generic ContextBuilder class for the Open Notebook project that can handle any parameters and build context from sources, notebooks, insights, and notes.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Features
  6 | 
  7 | - **Flexible Parameters**: Accepts any parameters via `**kwargs` for future extensibility
  8 | - **Priority-based Management**: Automatic prioritization and sorting of context items
  9 | - **Token Counting**: Built-in token counting and truncation to fit limits
 10 | - **Deduplication**: Automatic removal of duplicate items based on ID
 11 | - **Type-based Grouping**: Separates sources, notes, and insights in output
 12 | - **Async Support**: Fully async for database operations
 13 | 
 14 | ## Basic Usage
 15 | 
 16 | ```python
 17 | from open_notebook.utils.context_builder import ContextBuilder, ContextConfig
 18 | 
 19 | # Simple notebook context
 20 | builder = ContextBuilder(notebook_id="notebook:123")
 21 | context = await builder.build()
 22 | 
 23 | # Single source with insights
 24 | builder = ContextBuilder(
 25 |     source_id="source:456",
 26 |     include_insights=True,
 27 |     max_tokens=2000
 28 | )
 29 | context = await builder.build()
 30 | ```
 31 | 
 32 | ## Convenience Functions
 33 | 
 34 | ```python
 35 | from open_notebook.utils.context_builder import (
 36 |     build_notebook_context,
 37 |     build_source_context,
 38 |     build_mixed_context
 39 | )
 40 | 
 41 | # Build notebook context
 42 | context = await build_notebook_context(
 43 |     notebook_id="notebook:123",
 44 |     max_tokens=5000
 45 | )
 46 | 
 47 | # Build single source context
 48 | context = await build_source_context(
 49 |     source_id="source:456",
 50 |     include_insights=True
 51 | )
 52 | 
 53 | # Build mixed context
 54 | context = await build_mixed_context(
 55 |     source_ids=["source:1", "source:2"],
 56 |     note_ids=["note:1", "note:2"],
 57 |     max_tokens=3000
 58 | )
 59 | ```
 60 | 
 61 | ## Advanced Configuration
 62 | 
 63 | ```python
 64 | from open_notebook.utils.context_builder import ContextConfig
 65 | 
 66 | # Custom configuration
 67 | config = ContextConfig(
 68 |     sources={
 69 |         "source:doc1": "insights",
 70 |         "source:doc2": "full content", 
 71 |         "source:doc3": "not in"  # Exclude
 72 |     },
 73 |     notes={
 74 |         "note:summary": "full content",
 75 |         "note:draft": "not in"  # Exclude
 76 |     },
 77 |     include_insights=True,
 78 |     max_tokens=3000,
 79 |     priority_weights={
 80 |         "source": 120,  # Higher priority
 81 |         "note": 80,     # Medium priority  
 82 |         "insight": 100  # High priority
 83 |     }
 84 | )
 85 | 
 86 | builder = ContextBuilder(
 87 |     notebook_id="notebook:project",
 88 |     context_config=config
 89 | )
 90 | context = await builder.build()
 91 | ```
 92 | 
 93 | ## Programmatic Item Management
 94 | 
 95 | ```python
 96 | from open_notebook.utils.context_builder import ContextItem
 97 | 
 98 | builder = ContextBuilder()
 99 | 
100 | # Add custom items
101 | item = ContextItem(
102 |     id="source:important",
103 |     type="source",
104 |     content={"title": "Key Document", "summary": "..."},
105 |     priority=150  # Very high priority
106 | )
107 | builder.add_item(item)
108 | 
109 | # Apply management operations
110 | builder.remove_duplicates()
111 | builder.prioritize()
112 | builder.truncate_to_fit(1000)
113 | 
114 | context = builder._format_response()
115 | ```
116 | 
117 | ## Flexible Parameters
118 | 
119 | The ContextBuilder accepts any parameters via `**kwargs`, making it extensible for future features:
120 | 
121 | ```python
122 | builder = ContextBuilder(
123 |     notebook_id="notebook:123",
124 |     include_insights=True,
125 |     max_tokens=2000,
126 |     
127 |     # Custom parameters for future extensions
128 |     user_id="user:456",
129 |     custom_filter="advanced",
130 |     experimental_feature=True
131 | )
132 | 
133 | # Access custom parameters
134 | user_id = builder.params.get('user_id')
135 | ```
136 | 
137 | ## Output Format
138 | 
139 | The ContextBuilder returns a structured response:
140 | 
141 | ```python
142 | {
143 |     "sources": [...],           # List of source contexts
144 |     "notes": [...],             # List of note contexts  
145 |     "insights": [...],          # List of insight contexts
146 |     "total_tokens": 1234,       # Total token count
147 |     "total_items": 10,          # Total number of items
148 |     "notebook_id": "notebook:123",  # If provided
149 |     "metadata": {
150 |         "source_count": 5,
151 |         "note_count": 3,
152 |         "insight_count": 2,
153 |         "config": {
154 |             "include_insights": true,
155 |             "include_notes": true,
156 |             "max_tokens": 2000
157 |         }
158 |     }
159 | }
160 | ```
161 | 
162 | ## Architecture
163 | 
164 | The ContextBuilder follows these design principles:
165 | 
166 | 1. **Separation of Concerns**: Context building, item management, and formatting are separate
167 | 2. **Extensibility**: Uses `**kwargs` and flexible configuration for future features
168 | 3. **Performance**: Token-aware truncation and efficient deduplication
169 | 4. **Type Safety**: Proper type hints and data classes for structure
170 | 5. **Error Handling**: Graceful handling of missing items and database errors
171 | 
172 | ## Integration
173 | 
174 | The ContextBuilder integrates seamlessly with the existing Open Notebook architecture:
175 | 
176 | - Uses existing domain models (`Source`, `Notebook`, `Note`)
177 | - Leverages the repository pattern for database access
178 | - Follows the same async patterns as other services
179 | - Integrates with the token counting utilities
180 | 
181 | ## Error Handling
182 | 
183 | The ContextBuilder handles errors gracefully:
184 | 
185 | - Missing notebooks/sources/notes are logged but don't stop execution
186 | - Database errors are wrapped in `DatabaseOperationError`
187 | - Invalid parameters raise `InvalidInputError`
188 | - All errors include detailed context information

 13 |     compare_versions,

 17 | router = APIRouter()

 19 | # In-memory cache for version check results
 20 | _version_cache: dict = {
 21 |     "latest_version": None,
 22 |     "has_update": False,
 23 |     "timestamp": 0,
 24 |     "check_failed": False,
 25 | }
 26 | 
 27 | # Cache TTL in seconds (24 hours)
 28 | VERSION_CACHE_TTL = 24 * 60 * 60
 29 | 
 30 | 
 31 | def get_version() -> str:
 32 |     """Read version from pyproject.toml"""
 33 |     try:
 34 |         pyproject_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "pyproject.toml"
 35 |         with open(pyproject_path, "rb") as f:
 36 |             pyproject = tomllib.load(f)
 37 |             return pyproject.get("project", {}).get("version", "unknown")
 38 |     except Exception as e:
 39 |         logger.warning(f"Could not read version from pyproject.toml: {e}")
 40 |         return "unknown"
 41 | 
 42 | 
 43 | async def get_latest_version_cached(current_version: str) -> tuple[Optional[str], bool]:
 44 |     """
 45 |     Check for the latest version from GitHub with caching.
 46 | 
 47 |     Returns:
 48 |         tuple: (latest_version, has_update)
 49 |         - latest_version: str or None if check failed
 50 |         - has_update: bool indicating if update is available
 51 |     """
 52 |     global _version_cache
 53 | 
 54 |     # Check if cache is still valid (within TTL)
 55 |     cache_age = time.time() - _version_cache["timestamp"]
 56 |     if _version_cache["timestamp"] > 0 and cache_age < VERSION_CACHE_TTL:
 57 |         logger.debug(f"Using cached version check result (age: {cache_age:.0f}s)")
 58 |         return _version_cache["latest_version"], _version_cache["has_update"]
 59 | 
 60 |     # Cache expired or not yet set
 61 |     if _version_cache["timestamp"] > 0:
 62 |         logger.info(f"Version cache expired (age: {cache_age:.0f}s), refreshing...")
 63 | 
 64 |     # Perform version check with strict error handling
 65 |     try:
 66 |         logger.info("Checking for latest version from GitHub...")
 67 | 
 68 |         # Fetch latest version from GitHub with 10-second timeout
 69 |         latest_version = await get_version_from_github_async(
 70 |             "https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook", "main"
 71 |         )
 72 | 
 73 |         logger.info(
 74 |             f"Latest version from GitHub: {latest_version}, Current version: {current_version}"
 75 |         )
 76 | 
 77 |         # Compare versions
 78 |         has_update = compare_versions(current_version, latest_version) < 0
 79 | 
 80 |         # Cache the result
 81 |         _version_cache["latest_version"] = latest_version
 82 |         _version_cache["has_update"] = has_update
 83 |         _version_cache["timestamp"] = time.time()
 84 |         _version_cache["check_failed"] = False
 85 | 
 86 |         logger.info(f"Version check complete. Update available: {has_update}")
 87 | 
 88 |         return latest_version, has_update
 89 | 
 90 |     except Exception as e:
 91 |         logger.warning(f"Version check failed: {e}")
 92 | 
 93 |         # Cache the failure to avoid repeated attempts
 94 |         _version_cache["latest_version"] = None
 95 |         _version_cache["has_update"] = False
 96 |         _version_cache["timestamp"] = time.time()
 97 |         _version_cache["check_failed"] = True
 98 | 
 99 |         return None, False
100 | 
101 | 
102 | async def check_database_health() -> dict:
103 |     """
104 |     Check if database is reachable using a lightweight query.
105 | 
106 |     Returns:
107 |         dict with 'status' ("online" | "offline") and optional 'error'
108 |     """
109 |     try:
110 |         # 2-second timeout for database health check
111 |         result = await asyncio.wait_for(repo_query("RETURN 1"), timeout=2.0)
112 |         if result:
113 |             return {"status": "online"}
114 |         return {"status": "offline", "error": "Empty result"}
115 |     except asyncio.TimeoutError:
116 |         logger.warning("Database health check timed out after 2 seconds")
117 |         return {"status": "offline", "error": "Health check timeout"}
118 |     except Exception as e:
119 |         logger.warning(f"Database health check failed: {e}")
120 |         return {"status": "offline", "error": str(e)}
121 | 
122 | 
123 | @router.get("/config")
124 | async def get_config(request: Request):
125 |     """
126 |     Get frontend configuration.
127 | 
128 |     Returns version information and health status.
129 |     Note: The frontend determines the API URL via its own runtime-config endpoint,
130 |     so this endpoint no longer returns apiUrl.
131 | 
132 |     Also checks for version updates from GitHub (with caching and error handling).
133 |     """
134 |     # Get current version
135 |     current_version = get_version()
136 | 
137 |     # Check for updates (with caching and error handling)
138 |     # This MUST NOT break the endpoint - wrapped in try-except as extra safety
139 |     latest_version = None
140 |     has_update = False
141 | 
142 |     try:
143 |         latest_version, has_update = await get_latest_version_cached(current_version)
144 |     except Exception as e:
145 |         # Extra safety: ensure version check never breaks the config endpoint
146 |         logger.error(f"Unexpected error during version check: {e}")
147 | 
148 |     # Check database health
149 |     db_health = await check_database_health()
150 |     db_status = db_health["status"]
151 | 
152 |     if db_status == "offline":
153 |         logger.warning(f"Database offline: {db_health.get('error', 'Unknown error')}")
154 | 
155 |     return {
156 |         "version": current_version,
157 |         "latestVersion": latest_version,
158 |         "hasUpdate": has_update,
159 |         "dbStatus": db_status,
160 |     }

 66 |     @field_validator("speakers")
 67 |     @classmethod
 68 |     def validate_speakers(cls, v):
 69 |         if not 1 <= len(v) <= 4:
 70 |             raise ValueError("Must have between 1 and 4 speakers")
 71 | 
 72 |         required_fields = ["name", "voice_id", "backstory", "personality"]
 73 |         for speaker in v:
 74 |             for field in required_fields:
 75 |                 if field not in speaker:
 76 |                     raise ValueError(f"Speaker missing required field: {field}")
 77 |         return v
 78 | 
 79 |     @classmethod
 80 |     async def get_by_name(cls, name: str) -> Optional["SpeakerProfile"]:
 81 |         """Get speaker profile by name"""
 82 |         result = await repo_query(
 83 |             "SELECT * FROM speaker_profile WHERE name = $name", {"name": name}
 84 |         )
 85 |         if result:
 86 |             return cls(**result[0])
 87 |         return None

119 |     async def get_job_status(self) -> Optional[str]:
120 |         """Get the status of the associated command"""
121 |         if not self.command:
122 |             return None
123 | 
124 |         try:
125 |             from surreal_commands import get_command_status
126 | 
127 |             status = await get_command_status(str(self.command))
128 |             return status.status if status else "unknown"
129 |         except Exception:
130 |             return "unknown"
131 |

135 |         if isinstance(value, str):
136 |             return ensure_record_id(value)
137 |         return value

140 |         """Override to ensure command field is always RecordID format for database"""
141 |         data = super()._prepare_save_data()
142 |

144 |         if data.get("command") is not None:

 38 | async def execute_command(request: CommandExecutionRequest):
 39 |     """
 40 |     Submit a command for background processing.
 41 |     Returns immediately with job ID for status tracking.
 42 | 
 43 |     Example request:
 44 |     {
 45 |         "command": "process_text",
 46 |         "app": "open_notebook",
 47 |         "input": {
 48 |             "text": "Hello world",
 49 |             "operation": "uppercase"
 50 |         }
 51 |     }
 52 |     """
 53 |     try:
 54 |         # Submit command using app name (not module name)
 55 |         job_id = await CommandService.submit_command_job(
 56 |             module_name=request.app,  # This should be "open_notebook"
 57 |             command_name=request.command,
 58 |             command_args=request.input,
 59 |         )
 60 | 
 61 |         return CommandJobResponse(
 62 |             job_id=job_id,
 63 |             status="submitted",
 64 |             message=f"Command '{request.command}' submitted successfully",
 65 |         )
 66 | 
 67 |     except Exception as e:
 68 |         logger.error(f"Error submitting command: {str(e)}")
 69 |         raise HTTPException(
 70 |             status_code=500, detail="Failed to submit command"
 71 |         )

148 |                     commands_dict[item.app_id] = []
149 |                 commands_dict[item.app_id].append(item.name)
150 |         except Exception:

152 | 
153 |         return {
154 |             "total_commands": len(all_items),
155 |             "commands_by_app": commands_dict,
156 |             "command_items": command_items,

 15 | function modelsByProvider(models: Model[], type: Model['type']) {
 16 |   return models

 18 |     .reduce<Record<string, string[]>>((acc, model) => {
 19 |       if (!acc[model.provider]) {
 20 |         acc[model.provider] = []
 21 |       }
 22 |       acc[model.provider].push(model.name)
 23 |       return acc
 24 |     }, {})
 25 | }

 83 |     content_state = state["content_state"]
 84 | 
 85 |     # Get existing source using the provided source_id
 86 |     source = await Source.get(state["source_id"])
 87 |     if not source:
 88 |         raise ValueError(f"Source with ID {state['source_id']} not found")
 89 | 
 90 |     # Update the source with processed content
 91 |     source.asset = Asset(url=content_state.url, file_path=content_state.file_path)
 92 |     source.full_text = content_state.content
 93 | 
 94 |     # Preserve existing title if none provided in processed content
 95 |     if content_state.title:
 96 |         source.title = content_state.title
 97 | 
 98 |     await source.save()
 99 | 
100 |     # NOTE: Notebook associations are created by the API immediately for UI responsiveness
101 |     # No need to create them here to avoid duplicate edges
102 | 
103 |     if state["embed"]:
104 |         logger.debug("Embedding content for vector search")
105 |         await source.vectorize()
106 | 
107 |     return {"source": source}
108 | 
109 | 
110 | def trigger_transformations(state: SourceState, config: RunnableConfig) -> List[Send]:
111 |     if len(state["apply_transformations"]) == 0:
112 |         return []
113 | 
114 |     to_apply = state["apply_transformations"]
115 |     logger.debug(f"Applying transformations {to_apply}")
116 | 
117 |     return [
118 |         Send(
119 |             "transform_content",
120 |             {
121 |                 "source": state["source"],
122 |                 "transformation": t,
123 |             },
124 |         )
125 |         for t in to_apply
126 |     ]
127 | 
128 | 
129 | async def transform_content(state: TransformationState) -> Optional[dict]:
130 |     source = state["source"]
131 |     content = source.full_text
132 |     if not content:
133 |         return None
134 |     transformation: Transformation = state["transformation"]
135 | 
136 |     logger.debug(f"Applying transformation {transformation.name}")
137 |     result = await transform_graph.ainvoke(
138 |         dict(input_text=content, transformation=transformation)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
139 |     )
140 |     await source.add_insight(transformation.title, result["output"])
141 |     return {
142 |         "transformation": [
143 |             {
144 |                 "output": result["output"],
145 |                 "transformation_name": transformation.name,
146 |             }
147 |         ]
148 |     }
149 | 
150 | 
151 | # Create and compile the workflow
152 | workflow = StateGraph(SourceState)
153 | 
154 | # Add nodes
155 | workflow.add_node("content_process", content_process)
156 | workflow.add_node("save_source", save_source)
157 | workflow.add_node("transform_content", transform_content)
158 | # Define the graph edges
159 | workflow.add_edge(START, "content_process")
160 | workflow.add_edge("content_process", "save_source")
161 | workflow.add_conditional_edges(
162 |     "save_source", trigger_transformations, ["transform_content"]
163 | )
164 | workflow.add_edge("transform_content", END)
165 | 
166 | # Compile the graph
167 | source_graph = workflow.compile()
168 |

/open_notebook/ai/CLAUDE.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # AI Module
  2 | 
  3 | Model configuration, provisioning, and management for multi-provider AI integration via Esperanto.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Purpose
  6 | 
  7 | Centralizes AI model lifecycle: database models for model metadata (provider, type), default model configuration, and factory for instantiating LLM/embedding/speech models at runtime with fallback logic.
  8 | 
  9 | ## Architecture Overview
 10 | 
 11 | **Two-tier system**:
 12 | 1. **Database models** (`Model`, `DefaultModels`): Metadata storage and default configuration
 13 | 2. **ModelManager**: Factory for provisioning models with intelligent fallback (large context detection, config override)
 14 | 
 15 | All models use Esperanto library as provider abstraction (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, Ollama, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter).
 16 | 
 17 | ## Component Catalog
 18 | 
 19 | ### models.py
 20 | 
 21 | #### Model (ObjectModel)
 22 | - Database record: name, provider, type (language/embedding/speech_to_text/text_to_speech)
 23 | - `get_models_by_type()`: Async query to fetch all models of a specific type
 24 | - Stores provider-model pairs for AI factory instantiation
 25 | 
 26 | #### DefaultModels (RecordModel)
 27 | - Singleton configuration record (record_id: `open_notebook:default_models`)
 28 | - Fields: default_chat_model, default_transformation_model, large_context_model, default_text_to_speech_model, default_speech_to_text_model, default_embedding_model, default_tools_model
 29 | - `get_instance()`: Always fetches fresh from database (overrides parent caching for real-time updates)
 30 | - Returns fresh instance on each call (no singleton cache)
 31 | 
 32 | #### ModelManager
 33 | - Stateless factory for instantiating AI models
 34 | - `get_model(model_id)`: Retrieves Model by ID, creates via AIFactory.create_* based on type
 35 | - `get_defaults()`: Fetches DefaultModels configuration
 36 | - `get_default_model(model_type)`: Smart lookup (e.g., "chat" → default_chat_model, "transformation" → default_transformation_model with fallback to chat)
 37 | - `get_speech_to_text()`, `get_text_to_speech()`, `get_embedding_model()`: Type-specific convenience methods with assertions
 38 | - **Global instance**: `model_manager` singleton exported for use throughout app
 39 | 
 40 | ### provision.py
 41 | 
 42 | #### provision_langchain_model()
 43 | - Factory for LangGraph nodes needing LLM provisioning
 44 | - **Smart fallback logic**:
 45 |   - If tokens > 105,000: Use `large_context_model`
 46 |   - Elif `model_id` specified: Use specific model
 47 |   - Else: Use default model for type (e.g., "chat", "transformation")
 48 | - Returns LangChain-compatible model via `.to_langchain()`
 49 | - Logs model selection decision
 50 | 
 51 | ## Common Patterns
 52 | 
 53 | - **Type dispatch**: Model.type field drives factory logic (4 model types)
 54 | - **Provider abstraction**: Esperanto handles provider differences; ModelManager unaware of provider specifics
 55 | - **Fresh defaults**: DefaultModels.get_instance() always fetches from database (not cached) for live config updates
 56 | - **Config override**: provision_langchain_model() accepts kwargs passed to AIFactory.create_* methods
 57 | - **Token-based selection**: provision_langchain_model() detects large contexts and upgrades model automatically
 58 | - **Type assertions**: get_speech_to_text(), get_embedding_model() assert returned type (safety check)
 59 | 
 60 | ## Key Dependencies
 61 | 
 62 | - `esperanto`: AIFactory.create_language(), create_embedding(), create_speech_to_text(), create_text_to_speech()
 63 | - `open_notebook.database.repository`: repo_query, ensure_record_id
 64 | - `open_notebook.domain.base`: ObjectModel, RecordModel base classes
 65 | - `open_notebook.utils`: token_count() for context size detection
 66 | - `loguru`: Logging for model selection decisions
 67 | 
 68 | ## Important Quirks & Gotchas
 69 | 
 70 | - **Token counting rough estimate**: provision_langchain_model() uses token_count() which estimates via cl100k_base encoding (may differ 5-10% from actual model)
 71 | - **Large context threshold hard-coded**: 105,000 token threshold for large_context_model upgrade (not configurable)
 72 | - **DefaultModels.get_instance() fresh fetch**: Intentionally bypasses parent singleton cache to pick up live config changes; creates new instance each call
 73 | - **Type-specific getters use assertions**: get_speech_to_text() asserts isinstance (catches misconfiguration early)
 74 | - **No validation of model existence**: ModelManager.get_model() raises ValueError if model not found (not caught upstream)
 75 | - **Esperanto caching**: Actual model instances cached by Esperanto (not by ModelManager); ModelManager stateless
 76 | - **Fallback chain specificity**: "transformation" type falls back to default_chat_model if not explicitly set (convention-based)
 77 | - **kwargs passed through**: provision_langchain_model() passes kwargs to AIFactory but doesn't validate what's accepted
 78 | 
 79 | ## How to Extend
 80 | 
 81 | 1. **Add new model type**: Add type string to Model.type enum, add create_* method in AIFactory, handle in ModelManager.get_model()
 82 | 2. **Add new default configuration**: Extend DefaultModels with new field (e.g., default_vision_model), add getter in ModelManager
 83 | 3. **Change fallback logic**: Modify provision_langchain_model() token threshold or fallback chain
 84 | 4. **Add model filtering**: Extend Model.get_models_by_type() with additional filters (e.g., by provider)
 85 | 5. **Implement model caching**: Wrap ModelManager methods with functools.lru_cache (be aware of kwargs mutability)
 86 | 
 87 | ## Usage Example
 88 | 
 89 | ```python
 90 | from open_notebook.ai.models import model_manager
 91 | 
 92 | # Get default chat model
 93 | chat_model = await model_manager.get_default_model("chat")
 94 | 
 95 | # Get specific model by ID
 96 | embedding_model = await model_manager.get_model("model:openai_embedding")
 97 | 
 98 | # Get embedding model with config override
 99 | embedding_model = await model_manager.get_embedding_model(temperature=0.1)
100 | 
101 | # Provision model for LangGraph (auto-detects large context)
102 | from open_notebook.ai.provision import provision_langchain_model
103 | langchain_model = await provision_langchain_model(
104 |     content=long_text,
105 |     model_id=None,  # Use default
106 |     default_type="chat",
107 |     temperature=0.7
108 | )
109 | ```
110 |

  1 | 'use client'

  3 | import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
  4 | import { Dialog, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle } from '@/components/ui/dialog'
  5 | import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
  6 | import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'

 10 | import { useInsight } from '@/lib/hooks/use-insights'
 11 | import { useModalManager } from '@/lib/hooks/use-modal-manager'
 12 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
 13 | 
 14 | interface SourceInsightDialogProps {
 15 |   open: boolean
 16 |   onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void
 17 |   insight?: {
 18 |     id: string
 19 |     insight_type?: string
 20 |     content?: string
 21 |     created?: string
 22 |     source_id?: string
 23 |   }
 24 |   onDelete?: (insightId: string) => Promise<void>
 25 | }
 26 | 
 27 | export function SourceInsightDialog({ open, onOpenChange, insight, onDelete }: SourceInsightDialogProps) {
 28 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 29 |   const { openModal } = useModalManager()
 30 |   const [showDeleteConfirm, setShowDeleteConfirm] = useState(false)
 31 |   const [isDeleting, setIsDeleting] = useState(false)
 32 | 
 33 |   // Ensure insight ID has 'source_insight:' prefix for API calls
 34 |   const insightIdWithPrefix = insight?.id
 35 |     ? (insight.id.includes(':') ? insight.id : `source_insight:${insight.id}`)
 36 |     : ''
 37 | 
 38 |   const { data: fetchedInsight, isLoading } = useInsight(insightIdWithPrefix, { enabled: open && !!insight?.id })
 39 | 
 40 |   // Use fetched data if available, otherwise fall back to passed-in insight
 41 |   const displayInsight = fetchedInsight ?? insight
 42 | 
 43 |   // Get source_id from fetched data (preferred) or passed-in insight
 44 |   const sourceId = fetchedInsight?.source_id ?? insight?.source_id
 45 | 
 46 |   const handleViewSource = () => {
 47 |     if (sourceId) {
 48 |       openModal('source', sourceId)
 49 |     }
 50 |   }
 51 | 
 52 |   const handleDelete = async () => {
 53 |     if (!insight?.id || !onDelete) return
 54 |     setIsDeleting(true)
 55 |     try {
 56 |       await onDelete(insight.id)
 57 |       onOpenChange(false)
 58 |     } finally {
 59 |       setIsDeleting(false)
 60 |       setShowDeleteConfirm(false)
 61 |     }
 62 |   }
 63 | 
 64 |   // Reset delete confirmation when dialog closes
 65 |   useEffect(() => {
 66 |     if (!open) {
 67 |       setShowDeleteConfirm(false)
 68 |     }
 69 |   }, [open])
 70 | 
 71 |   return (
 72 |     <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>
 73 |       <DialogContent className="sm:max-w-3xl max-h-[90vh] flex flex-col">
 74 |         <DialogHeader>
 75 |           <DialogTitle className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
 76 |             <span>{t.sources.sourceInsight}</span>
 77 |             <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
 78 |               {displayInsight?.insight_type && (
 79 |                 <Badge variant="outline" className="text-xs uppercase">
 80 |                   {displayInsight.insight_type}
 81 |                 </Badge>
 82 |               )}
 83 |               {sourceId && (
 84 |                 <Button
 85 |                   variant="outline"
 86 |                   size="sm"
 87 |                   onClick={handleViewSource}
 88 |                   className="gap-1"
 89 |                 >
 90 |                   <FileText className="h-3 w-3" />
 91 |                   {t.sources.viewSource}
 92 |                 </Button>
 93 |               )}
 94 |             </div>
 95 |           </DialogTitle>
 96 |         </DialogHeader>
 97 | 
 98 |         {showDeleteConfirm ? (
 99 |           <div className="flex flex-col items-center justify-center py-8 gap-4">
100 |             <p className="text-center text-muted-foreground">
101 |               {t.sources.deleteInsightConfirm.split(/[?？]/)[0]}?<br />
102 |               <span className="text-sm">{t.sources.deleteInsightConfirm.split(/[?？]/)[1]?.trim() || t.common.deleteForever}</span>
103 |             </p>
104 |             <div className="flex gap-2">
105 |               <Button
106 |                 variant="outline"
107 |                 onClick={() => setShowDeleteConfirm(false)}
108 |                 disabled={isDeleting}
109 |               >
110 |                 {t.common.cancel}
111 |               </Button>
112 |               <Button
113 |                 variant="destructive"
114 |                 onClick={handleDelete}
115 |                 disabled={isDeleting}
116 |               >
117 |                 {isDeleting ? t.common.deleting : t.common.delete}
118 |               </Button>
119 |             </div>
120 |           </div>
121 |         ) : (
122 |           <div className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto min-h-0">
123 |             {isLoading ? (
124 |               <div className="flex items-center justify-center py-10">
125 |                 <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{t.common.loading}</span>
126 |               </div>
127 |             ) : displayInsight ? (
128 |               <div className="prose prose-sm prose-neutral dark:prose-invert max-w-none">
129 |                 <ReactMarkdown
130 |                   remarkPlugins={[remarkGfm]}
131 |                   components={{
132 |                     table: ({ children }) => (
133 |                       <div className="my-4 overflow-x-auto">
134 |                         <table className="min-w-full border-collapse border border-border">{children}</table>
135 |                       </div>
136 |                     ),
137 |                     thead: ({ children }) => <thead className="bg-muted">{children}</thead>,
138 |                     tbody: ({ children }) => <tbody>{children}</tbody>,
139 |                     tr: ({ children }) => <tr className="border-b border-border">{children}</tr>,
140 |                     th: ({ children }) => <th className="border border-border px-3 py-2 text-left font-semibold">{children}</th>,
141 |                     td: ({ children }) => <td className="border border-border px-3 py-2">{children}</td>,
142 |                   }}
143 |                 >
144 |                   {displayInsight.content}
145 |                 </ReactMarkdown>
146 |               </div>
147 |             ) : (
148 |               <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{t.sources.noInsightSelected}</p>
149 |             )}
150 |           </div>
151 |         )}
152 |       </DialogContent>
153 |     </Dialog>
154 |   )
155 | }
156 |

  1 | # Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration
  2 | 
  3 | Open Notebook can be seamlessly integrated into your AI workflows using the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**, enabling direct access to your notebooks, sources, and chat functionality from AI assistants like Claude Desktop and VS Code extensions.
  4 | 
  5 | ## What is MCP?
  6 | 
  7 | The [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) is an open standard that allows AI applications to securely connect to external data sources and tools. With the Open Notebook MCP server, you can:
  8 | 
  9 | - 📚 **Access your notebooks** directly from Claude Desktop or VS Code
 10 | - 🔍 **Search your research content** without leaving your AI assistant
 11 | - 💬 **Create and manage chat sessions** with your research as context
 12 | - 📝 **Generate notes** and insights on-the-fly
 13 | - 🤖 **Automate workflows** using the full Open Notebook API
 14 | 
 15 | ## Quick Setup
 16 | 
 17 | ### For Claude Desktop
 18 | 
 19 | 1. **Install the MCP server** (automatically from PyPI):
 20 | 
 21 |    ```bash
 22 |    # No manual installation needed! Claude Desktop will use uvx to run it automatically
 23 |    ```
 24 | 
 25 | 2. **Configure Claude Desktop**:
 26 | 
 27 |    **macOS/Linux**: Edit `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
 28 | 
 29 |    ```json
 30 |    {
 31 |      "mcpServers": {
 32 |        "open-notebook": {
 33 |          "command": "uvx",
 34 |          "args": ["open-notebook-mcp"],
 35 |          "env": {
 36 |            "OPEN_NOTEBOOK_URL": "http://localhost:5055",
 37 |            "OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD": "your_password_here"
 38 |          }
 39 |        }
 40 |      }
 41 |    }
 42 |    ```
 43 | 
 44 |    **Windows**: Edit `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`
 45 | 
 46 |    ```json
 47 |    {
 48 |      "mcpServers": {
 49 |        "open-notebook": {
 50 |          "command": "uvx",
 51 |          "args": ["open-notebook-mcp"],
 52 |          "env": {
 53 |            "OPEN_NOTEBOOK_URL": "http://localhost:5055",
 54 |            "OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD": "your_password_here"
 55 |          }
 56 |        }
 57 |      }
 58 |    }
 59 |    ```
 60 | 
 61 | 3. **Restart Claude Desktop** and start using your notebooks in conversations!
 62 | 
 63 | ### For VS Code (Cline and other MCP-compatible extensions)
 64 | 
 65 | Add to your VS Code settings or `.vscode/mcp.json`:
 66 | 
 67 | ```json
 68 | {
 69 |   "servers": {
 70 |     "open-notebook": {
 71 |       "command": "uvx",
 72 |       "args": ["open-notebook-mcp"],
 73 |       "env": {
 74 |         "OPEN_NOTEBOOK_URL": "http://localhost:5055",
 75 |         "OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD": "your_password_here"
 76 |       }
 77 |     }
 78 |   }
 79 | }
 80 | ```
 81 | 
 82 | ## Configuration
 83 | 
 84 | - **OPEN_NOTEBOOK_URL**: URL to your Open Notebook API (default: `http://localhost:5055`)
 85 | - **OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD**: Optional - only needed if you've enabled password protection
 86 | 
 87 | ### For Remote Servers
 88 | 
 89 | If your Open Notebook instance is running on a remote server, update the URL accordingly:
 90 | 
 91 | ```json
 92 | "OPEN_NOTEBOOK_URL": "http://192.168.1.100:5055"
 93 | ```
 94 | 
 95 | Or with a domain:
 96 | 
 97 | ```json
 98 | "OPEN_NOTEBOOK_URL": "https://notebook.yourdomain.com/api"
 99 | ```
100 | 
101 | ## What You Can Do
102 | 
103 | Once connected, you can ask Claude or your AI assistant to:
104 | 
105 | - _"Search my research notebooks for information about [topic]"_
106 | - _"Create a new note summarizing the key points from our conversation"_
107 | - _"List all my notebooks"_
108 | - _"Start a chat session about [specific source or topic]"_
109 | - _"What sources do I have in my [notebook name] notebook?"_
110 | - _"Add this PDF to my research notebook"_
111 | - _"Show me all notes in [notebook name]"_
112 | 
113 | The MCP server provides full access to Open Notebook's capabilities, allowing you to manage your research seamlessly from within your AI assistant.
114 | 
115 | ## Available Tools
116 | 
117 | The Open Notebook MCP server exposes these capabilities:
118 | 
119 | ### Notebooks
120 | 
121 | - List notebooks
122 | - Get notebook details
123 | - Create new notebooks
124 | - Update notebook information
125 | - Delete notebooks
126 | 
127 | ### Sources
128 | 
129 | - List sources in a notebook
130 | - Get source details
131 | - Add new sources (links, files, text)
132 | - Update source metadata
133 | - Delete sources
134 | 
135 | ### Notes
136 | 
137 | - List notes in a notebook
138 | - Get note details
139 | - Create new notes
140 | - Update notes
141 | - Delete notes
142 | 
143 | ### Chat
144 | 
145 | - Create chat sessions
146 | - Send messages to chat sessions
147 | - Get chat history
148 | - List chat sessions
149 | 
150 | ### Search
151 | 
152 | - Vector search across content
153 | - Text search across content
154 | - Filter by notebook
155 | 
156 | ### Models
157 | 
158 | - List configured AI models
159 | - Get model details
160 | - Create model configurations
161 | - Update model settings
162 | 
163 | ### Settings
164 | 
165 | - Get application settings
166 | - Update settings
167 | 
168 | ## MCP Server Repository
169 | 
170 | The Open Notebook MCP server is developed and maintained by the Epochal team:
171 | 
172 | **🔗 GitHub**: [Epochal-dev/open-notebook-mcp](https://github.com/Epochal-dev/open-notebook-mcp)
173 | 
174 | Contributions, issues, and feature requests are welcome!
175 | 
176 | ## Finding the Server
177 | 
178 | The Open Notebook MCP server is published to the official MCP Registry:
179 | 
180 | - **Registry**: Search for "open-notebook" at [registry.modelcontextprotocol.io](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io)
181 | - **PyPI**: [pypi.org/project/open-notebook-mcp](https://pypi.org/project/open-notebook-mcp)
182 | - **GitHub**: [Epochal-dev/open-notebook-mcp](https://github.com/Epochal-dev/open-notebook-mcp)
183 | 
184 | ## Troubleshooting
185 | 
186 | ### Connection Errors
187 | 
188 | 1. Verify the `OPEN_NOTEBOOK_URL` is correct and accessible
189 | 2. If using password protection, ensure `OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD` is set correctly
190 | 3. For remote servers, make sure port 5055 is accessible from your machine
191 | 4. Check firewall settings if connecting to a remote server
192 | 
193 | ## Using with Other MCP Clients
194 | 
195 | The Open Notebook MCP server follows the standard MCP protocol and can be used with any MCP-compatible client. Check your client's documentation for configuration details.
196 | 
197 | ## Learn More
198 | 
199 | - [Model Context Protocol Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
200 |

 26 | 
 27 | interface ModelSelectorProps {
 28 |   currentModel?: string
 29 |   onModelChange: (model?: string) => void
 30 |   disabled?: boolean
 31 | }
 32 | 
 33 | export function ModelSelector({ 
 34 |   currentModel, 
 35 |   onModelChange,
 36 |   disabled = false 
 37 | }: ModelSelectorProps) {
 38 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 39 |   const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
 40 |   const [selectedModel, setSelectedModel] = useState(currentModel || 'default')
 41 |   const { data: models, isLoading } = useModels()
 42 |   const { data: defaults } = useModelDefaults()
 43 | 
 44 |   useEffect(() => {
 45 |     setSelectedModel(currentModel || 'default')
 46 |   }, [currentModel])
 47 | 
 48 |   // Filter for language models only and sort by name
 49 |   const languageModels = useMemo(() => {
 50 |     if (!models) {
 51 |       return []
 52 |     }
 53 |     return [...models]
 54 |       .filter((model) => model.type === 'language')
 55 |       .sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))
 56 |   }, [models])
 57 | 
 58 |   const defaultModel = useMemo(() => {
 59 |     if (!defaults?.default_chat_model) return undefined
 60 |     return languageModels.find(model => model.id === defaults.default_chat_model)
 61 |   }, [defaults?.default_chat_model, languageModels])
 62 | 
 63 |   const currentModelName = useMemo(() => {
 64 |     if (currentModel) {
 65 |       return languageModels.find(model => model.id === currentModel)?.name || currentModel
 66 |     }
 67 |     if (defaultModel) {
 68 |       return defaultModel.name
 69 |     }
 70 |     return t.common.default
 71 |   }, [currentModel, languageModels, defaultModel, t.common.default])
 72 | 
 73 |   const handleSave = () => {
 74 |     onModelChange(selectedModel === 'default' ? undefined : selectedModel)
 75 |     setOpen(false)
 76 |   }
 77 | 
 78 |   const handleReset = () => {
 79 |     setSelectedModel('default')
 80 |     onModelChange(undefined)
 81 |     setOpen(false)
 82 |   }
 83 | 
 84 |   return (
 85 |     <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
 86 |       <DialogTrigger asChild>
 87 |         <Button 
 88 |           variant="outline" 
 89 |           size="sm"
 90 |           disabled={disabled}
 91 |           className="gap-2"
 92 |         >
 93 |           <Settings2 className="h-4 w-4" />
 94 |           <span className="text-xs">
 95 |             {currentModelName}
 96 |           </span>
 97 |         </Button>
 98 |       </DialogTrigger>
 99 |       <DialogContent className="sm:max-w-[425px]">
100 |         <DialogHeader>
101 |           <DialogTitle className="flex items-center gap-2">
102 |             <Sparkles className="h-5 w-5" />
103 |             {t.common.modelConfiguration}
104 |           </DialogTitle>
105 |           <DialogDescription>
106 |             {t.transformations.overrideModelDesc}
107 |           </DialogDescription>
108 |         </DialogHeader>
109 |         <div className="grid gap-4 py-4">
110 |           <div className="grid gap-2">
111 |             <Label htmlFor="model">{t.common.model}</Label>
112 |             <Select value={selectedModel} onValueChange={setSelectedModel}>
113 |               <SelectTrigger id="model">
114 |                 <SelectValue placeholder={t.models.selectModelPlaceholder} />
115 |               </SelectTrigger>
116 |               <SelectContent>
117 |                 <SelectItem value="default">
118 |                   <div className="flex items-center justify-between w-full">
119 |                     <span>
120 |                       {defaultModel 
121 |                         ? `${t.common.default} (${defaultModel.name})` 
122 |                         : t.transformations.systemDefault}
123 |                     </span>
124 |                     {defaultModel?.provider && (
125 |                       <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground ml-2">
126 |                         {defaultModel.provider}
127 |                       </span>
128 |                     )}
129 |                   </div>
130 |                 </SelectItem>
131 |                 {isLoading ? (
132 |                   <div className="flex items-center justify-center py-2">
133 |                     <LoadingSpinner size="sm" />
134 |                   </div>
135 |                 ) : (
136 |                   languageModels.map((model) => (
137 |                     <SelectItem key={model.id} value={model.id}>
138 |                       <div className="flex items-center justify-between w-full">
139 |                         <span>{model.name}</span>
140 |                         <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground ml-2">
141 |                           {model.provider}
142 |                         </span>
143 |                       </div>
144 |                     </SelectItem>
145 |                   ))
146 |                 )}
147 |               </SelectContent>
148 |             </Select>
149 |           </div>
150 |           {selectedModel && selectedModel !== 'default' && (
151 |             <div className="rounded-lg bg-muted p-3">
152 |               <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
153 |                 {t.transformations.sessionUseReplacement.replace(
154 |                   '{name}', 
155 |                   languageModels.find(m => m.id === selectedModel)?.name || selectedModel
156 |                 )}
157 |               </p>
158 |             </div>
159 |           )}
160 |         </div>
161 |         <DialogFooter className="flex justify-between">
162 |           <Button variant="outline" onClick={handleReset}>
163 |             {t.common.resetToDefault}
164 |           </Button>
165 |           <Button onClick={handleSave}>
166 |             {t.common.saveChanges}
167 |           </Button>
168 |         </DialogFooter>
169 |       </DialogContent>
170 |     </Dialog>
171 |   )
172 | }

  1 | # AI Providers - Comparison & Selection Guide
  2 | 
  3 | Open Notebook supports 15+ AI providers. This guide helps you **choose the right provider** for your needs.
  4 | 
  5 | > 💡 **Just want to set up a provider?** Skip to the [Configuration Guide](../5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md) for detailed setup instructions.
  6 | 
  7 | ---
  8 | 
  9 | ## Quick Decision: Which Provider?
 10 | 
 11 | ### Cloud Providers (Easiest)
 12 | 
 13 | **OpenAI (Recommended)**
 14 | - Cost: ~$0.03-0.15 per 1K tokens
 15 | - Speed: Very fast
 16 | - Quality: Excellent
 17 | - Best for: Most users (best quality/price balance)
 18 | 
 19 | → [Setup Guide](../5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md#openai)
 20 | 
 21 | **Anthropic (Claude)**
 22 | - Cost: ~$0.80-3.00 per 1M tokens
 23 | - Speed: Fast
 24 | - Quality: Excellent
 25 | - Best for: Long context (200K tokens), reasoning, latest AI
 26 | - Advantage: Superior long-context handling
 27 | 
 28 | → [Setup Guide](../5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md#anthropic-claude)
 29 | 
 30 | **Google Gemini**
 31 | - Cost: ~$0.075-0.30 per 1K tokens
 32 | - Speed: Very fast
 33 | - Quality: Good to excellent
 34 | - Best for: Multimodal (images, audio, video)
 35 | - Advantage: Longest context (up to 2M tokens)
 36 | 
 37 | → [Setup Guide](../5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md#google-gemini)
 38 | 
 39 | **Groq (Ultra-Fast)**
 40 | - Cost: ~$0.05 per 1M tokens (cheapest)
 41 | - Speed: Ultra-fast (fastest available)
 42 | - Quality: Good
 43 | - Best for: Budget-conscious, transformations, speed-critical tasks
 44 | - Disadvantage: Limited model selection
 45 | 
 46 | → [Setup Guide](../5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md#groq)
 47 | 
 48 | **OpenRouter (100+ Models)**
 49 | - Cost: Pay-per-model (varies widely)
 50 | - Speed: Varies by model
 51 | - Quality: Varies by model
 52 | - Best for: Model comparison, testing, unified billing
 53 | - Advantage: One API key for 100+ models from different providers
 54 | 
 55 | → [Setup Guide](../5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md#openrouter)
 56 | 
 57 | ### Local / Self-Hosted (Free)
 58 | 
 59 | **Ollama (Recommended for Local)**
 60 | - Cost: Free (electricity only)
 61 | - Speed: Depends on hardware (slow on CPU, fast on GPU)
 62 | - Quality: Good (open-source models)
 63 | - Setup: 10 minutes
 64 | - Best for: Privacy-first, offline use
 65 | - Privacy: 100% local, nothing leaves your machine
 66 | 
 67 | → [Setup Guide](../5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md#ollama-recommended-for-local)
 68 | 
 69 | **LM Studio (Alternative)**
 70 | - Cost: Free (electricity only)
 71 | - Speed: Depends on hardware
 72 | - Quality: Good (same models as Ollama)
 73 | - Setup: 15 minutes (GUI interface)
 74 | - Best for: Non-technical users who prefer GUI over CLI
 75 | - Privacy: 100% local
 76 | 
 77 | → [Setup Guide](../5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md#lm-studio-local-alternative)
 78 | 
 79 | ### Enterprise
 80 | 
 81 | **Azure OpenAI**
 82 | - Cost: Same as OpenAI (usage-based)
 83 | - Speed: Very fast
 84 | - Quality: Excellent (same models as OpenAI)
 85 | - Setup: 10 minutes (more complex)
 86 | - Best for: Enterprise, compliance (HIPAA, SOC2), VPC integration
 87 | 
 88 | → [Setup Guide](../5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md#azure-openai)
 89 | 
 90 | ---
 91 | 
 92 | ## Comparison Table
 93 | 
 94 | | Provider | Speed | Cost | Quality | Privacy | Setup | Context |
 95 | |----------|-------|------|---------|---------|-------|---------|
 96 | | **OpenAI** | Very Fast | $$ | Excellent | Low | 5 min | 128K |
 97 | | **Anthropic** | Fast | $$ | Excellent | Low | 5 min | 200K |
 98 | | **Google** | Very Fast | $$ | Good-Excellent | Low | 5 min | 2M |
 99 | | **Groq** | Ultra Fast | $ | Good | Low | 5 min | 32K |
100 | | **OpenRouter** | Varies | Varies | Varies | Low | 5 min | Varies |
101 | | **Ollama** | Slow-Medium | Free | Good | Max | 10 min | Varies |
102 | | **LM Studio** | Slow-Medium | Free | Good | Max | 15 min | Varies |
103 | | **Azure** | Very Fast | $$ | Excellent | High | 10 min | 128K |
104 | 
105 | ---
106 | 
107 | ## Choosing Your Provider
108 | 
109 | ### I want the easiest setup
110 | → **OpenAI** — Most popular, best community support
111 | 
112 | ### I have unlimited budget
113 | → **OpenAI** — Best quality
114 | 
115 | ### I want to save money
116 | → **Groq** — Cheapest cloud ($0.05 per 1M tokens)
117 | 
118 | ### I want privacy/offline
119 | → **Ollama** — Free, local, private
120 | 
121 | ### I want a GUI (not CLI)
122 | → **LM Studio** — Desktop app
123 | 
124 | ### I'm in an enterprise
125 | → **Azure OpenAI** — Compliance, support
126 | 
127 | ### I need long context (200K+ tokens)
128 | → **Anthropic** — Best long-context model
129 | 
130 | ### I need multimodal (images, audio, video)
131 | → **Google Gemini** — Best multimodal support
132 | 
133 | ### I want access to many models with one API key
134 | → **OpenRouter** — 100+ models, unified billing
135 | 
136 | ---
137 | 
138 | ## Ready to Set Up Your Provider?
139 | 
140 | Now that you've chosen a provider, follow the detailed setup instructions:
141 | 
142 | → **[AI Providers Configuration Guide](../5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md)**
143 | 
144 | This guide includes:
145 | - Step-by-step setup instructions for each provider
146 | - Environment variable configuration
147 | - Model selection and recommendations
148 | - Provider-specific troubleshooting
149 | - Hardware requirements (for local providers)
150 | - Cost optimization tips
151 | 
152 | ---
153 | 
154 | ## Cost Estimator
155 | 
156 | ### OpenAI
157 | ```
158 | Light use (10 chats/day): $1-5/month
159 | Medium use (50 chats/day): $10-30/month
160 | Heavy use (all-day use): $50-100+/month
161 | ```
162 | 
163 | ### Anthropic
164 | ```
165 | Light use: $1-3/month
166 | Medium use: $5-20/month
167 | Heavy use: $20-50+/month
168 | ```
169 | 
170 | ### Groq
171 | ```
172 | Light use: $0-1/month
173 | Medium use: $2-5/month
174 | Heavy use: $5-20/month
175 | ```
176 | 
177 | ### Ollama
178 | ```
179 | Any use: Free (electricity only)
180 | 8GB GPU running 24/7: ~$10/month electricity
181 | ```
182 | 
183 | ---
184 | 
185 | ## Next Steps
186 | 
187 | 1. ✅ **You've chosen a provider** (from this comparison guide)
188 | 2. 📖 **Follow the setup guide**: [AI Providers Configuration](../5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md)
189 | 3. ⚙️ **Configure your environment** (detailed in the setup guide)
190 | 4. 🧪 **Test your setup** in Settings → Models
191 | 5. 🚀 **Start using Open Notebook!**
192 | 
193 | ---
194 | 
195 | ## Need Help?
196 | 
197 | - **Setup issues?** See [AI Providers Configuration](../5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md) for detailed troubleshooting per provider
198 | - **General problems?** Check [Troubleshooting Guide](../6-TROUBLESHOOTING/index.md)
199 | - **Questions?** Join [Discord community](https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w)
200 |
