  1 | 'use client'
  2 | 
  3 | import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
  4 | import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
  5 | import { useAuth } from '@/lib/hooks/use-auth'
  6 | import { useAuthStore } from '@/lib/stores/auth-store'
  7 | import { getConfig } from '@/lib/config'
  8 | import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
  9 | import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
 10 | import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
 11 | import { AlertCircle } from 'lucide-react'
 12 | import { LoadingSpinner } from '@/components/common/LoadingSpinner'
 13 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
 14 | 
 15 | export function LoginForm() {
 16 |   const { t, language } = useTranslation()
 17 |   const [password, setPassword] = useState('')
 18 |   const { login, isLoading, error } = useAuth()
 19 |   const { authRequired, checkAuthRequired, hasHydrated, isAuthenticated } = useAuthStore()
 20 |   const [isCheckingAuth, setIsCheckingAuth] = useState(true)
 21 |   const [configInfo, setConfigInfo] = useState<{ apiUrl: string; version: string; buildTime: string } | null>(null)
 22 |   const router = useRouter()
 23 | 
 24 |   // Load config info for debugging
 25 |   useEffect(() => {
 26 |     getConfig().then(cfg => {
 27 |       setConfigInfo({
 28 |         apiUrl: cfg.apiUrl,
 29 |         version: cfg.version,
 30 |         buildTime: cfg.buildTime,
 31 |       })
 32 |     }).catch(err => {
 33 |       console.error('Failed to load config:', err)
 34 |     })
 35 |   }, [])
 36 | 
 37 |   // Check if authentication is required on mount
 38 |   useEffect(() => {
 39 |     if (!hasHydrated) {
 40 |       return
 41 |     }
 42 | 
 43 |     const checkAuth = async () => {
 44 |       try {
 45 |         const required = await checkAuthRequired()
 46 | 
 47 |         // If auth is not required, redirect to notebooks
 48 |         if (!required) {
 49 |           router.push('/notebooks')
 50 |         }
 51 |       } catch (error) {
 52 |         console.error('Error checking auth requirement:', error)
 53 |         // On error, assume auth is required to be safe
 54 |       } finally {
 55 |         setIsCheckingAuth(false)
 56 |       }
 57 |     }
 58 | 
 59 |     // If we already know auth status, use it
 60 |     if (authRequired !== null) {
 61 |       if (!authRequired && isAuthenticated) {
 62 |         router.push('/notebooks')
 63 |       } else {
 64 |         setIsCheckingAuth(false)
 65 |       }
 66 |     } else {
 67 |       void checkAuth()
 68 |     }
 69 |   }, [hasHydrated, authRequired, checkAuthRequired, router, isAuthenticated])
 70 | 
 71 |   // Show loading while checking if auth is required
 72 |   if (!hasHydrated || isCheckingAuth) {
 73 |     return (
 74 |       <div className="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center bg-background">
 75 |         <LoadingSpinner />
 76 |       </div>
 77 |     )
 78 |   }
 79 | 
 80 |   // If we still don't know if auth is required (connection error), show error
 81 |   if (authRequired === null) {
 82 |     return (
 83 |       <div className="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center bg-background p-4">
 84 |         <Card className="w-full max-w-md">
 85 |           <CardHeader className="text-center">
 86 |             <CardTitle>{t.common.connectionError}</CardTitle>
 87 |             <CardDescription>
 88 |               {t.common.unableToConnect}
 89 |             </CardDescription>
 90 |           </CardHeader>
 91 |           <CardContent>
 92 |             <div className="space-y-4">
 93 |               <div className="flex items-start gap-2 text-red-600 text-sm">
 94 |                 <AlertCircle className="h-4 w-4 mt-0.5 flex-shrink-0" />
 95 |                 <div className="flex-1">
 96 |                   {error || t.auth.connectErrorHint}
 97 |                 </div>
 98 |               </div>
 99 | 
100 |               {configInfo && (
101 |                 <div className="space-y-2 text-xs text-muted-foreground border-t pt-3">
102 |                   <div className="font-medium">{t.common.diagnosticInfo}:</div>
103 |                   <div className="space-y-1 font-mono">
104 |                     <div>{t.common.version}: {configInfo.version}</div>
105 |                     <div>{t.common.built}: {new Date(configInfo.buildTime).toLocaleString(language === 'zh-CN' ? 'zh-CN' : language === 'zh-TW' ? 'zh-TW' : 'en-US')}</div>
106 |                     <div className="break-all">{t.common.apiUrl}: {configInfo.apiUrl}</div>
107 |                     <div className="break-all">{t.common.frontendUrl}: {typeof window !== 'undefined' ? window.location.href : 'N/A'}</div>
108 |                   </div>
109 |                   <div className="text-xs pt-2">
110 |                     {t.common.checkConsoleLogs}
111 |                   </div>
112 |                 </div>
113 |               )}
114 | 
115 |               <Button
116 |                 onClick={() => window.location.reload()}
117 |                 className="w-full"
118 |               >
119 |                 {t.common.retryConnection}
120 |               </Button>
121 |             </div>
122 |           </CardContent>
123 |         </Card>
124 |       </div>
125 |     )
126 |   }
127 | 
128 |   const handleSubmit = async (e: React.FormEvent) => {
129 |     e.preventDefault()
130 |     if (password.trim()) {
131 |       try {
132 |         await login(password)
133 |       } catch (error) {
134 |         console.error('Unhandled error during login:', error)
135 |         // The auth store should handle most errors, but this catches any unhandled ones
136 |       }
137 |     }
138 |   }
139 | 
140 |   return (
141 |     <div className="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center bg-background p-4">
142 |       <Card className="w-full max-w-md">
143 |         <CardHeader className="text-center">
144 |           <CardTitle>{t.auth.loginTitle}</CardTitle>
145 |           <CardDescription>
146 |             {t.auth.loginDesc}
147 |           </CardDescription>
148 |         </CardHeader>
149 |         <CardContent>
150 |           <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="space-y-4">
151 |             <div>
152 |               <Input
153 |                 type="password"
154 |                 placeholder={t.auth.passwordPlaceholder}
155 |                 value={password}
156 |                 onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)}
157 |                 disabled={isLoading}
158 |               />
159 |             </div>
160 | 
161 |             {error && (
162 |               <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-red-600 text-sm">
163 |                 <AlertCircle className="h-4 w-4" />
164 |                 {error}
165 |               </div>
166 |             )}
167 | 
168 |             <Button
169 |               type="submit"
170 |               className="w-full"
171 |               disabled={isLoading || !password.trim()}
172 |             >
173 |               {isLoading ? t.auth.signingIn : t.auth.signIn}
174 |             </Button>
175 | 
176 |             {configInfo && (
177 |               <div className="text-xs text-center text-muted-foreground pt-2 border-t">
178 |                 <div>{t.common.version} {configInfo.version}</div>
179 |                 <div className="font-mono text-[10px]">{configInfo.apiUrl}</div>
180 |               </div>
181 |             )}
182 |           </form>
183 |         </CardContent>
184 |       </Card>
185 |     </div>
186 |   )
187 | }

/open_notebook/database/CLAUDE.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Database Module
  2 | 
  3 | SurrealDB abstraction layer providing repository pattern for CRUD operations and async migration management.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Purpose
  6 | 
  7 | Encapsulates all database interactions: connection pooling, async CRUD operations, relationship management, and schema migrations. Provides clean interface for domain models and API endpoints to interact with SurrealDB without direct query knowledge.
  8 | 
  9 | ## Architecture Overview
 10 | 
 11 | Two-tier system:
 12 | 1. **Repository Layer** (repository.py): Raw async CRUD operations on SurrealDB via AsyncSurreal client
 13 | 2. **Migration Layer** (async_migrate.py): Schema versioning and migration execution
 14 | 
 15 | Both leverage connection context manager for lifecycle management and automatic cleanup.
 16 | 
 17 | ## Component Catalog
 18 | 
 19 | ### repository.py
 20 | 
 21 | **Connection Management**
 22 | - `get_database_url()`: Resolves `SURREAL_URL` or constructs from `SURREAL_ADDRESS`/`SURREAL_PORT` (backward compatible)
 23 | - `get_database_password()`: Falls back from `SURREAL_PASSWORD` to legacy `SURREAL_PASS` env var
 24 | - `db_connection()`: Async context manager handling sign-in, namespace/database selection, and cleanup
 25 |   - Opens AsyncSurreal, authenticates, selects namespace/database, yields connection, closes on exit
 26 | 
 27 | **Query Operations**
 28 | - `repo_query(query_str, vars)`: Execute raw SurrealQL with parameter substitution; returns list of dicts
 29 | - `repo_create(table, data)`: Insert record; auto-adds `created`/`updated` timestamps; removes any existing `id` field
 30 | - `repo_insert(table, data_list, ignore_duplicates)`: Bulk insert multiple records; optionally ignores "already contains" errors
 31 | - `repo_upsert(table, id, data, add_timestamp)`: MERGE operation for create-or-update; optionally adds `updated` timestamp
 32 | - `repo_update(table, id, data)`: Update existing record by table+id or full record_id; auto-adds `updated`, parses ISO dates
 33 | - `repo_delete(record_id)`: Delete record by RecordID
 34 | - `repo_relate(source, relationship, target, data)`: Create graph relationship; optional relationship data
 35 | 
 36 | **Utilities**
 37 | - `parse_record_ids(obj)`: Recursively converts SurrealDB RecordID objects to strings (deep tree traversal)
 38 | - `ensure_record_id(value)`: Coerces string or RecordID to RecordID type
 39 | 
 40 | ### async_migrate.py
 41 | 
 42 | **Migration Classes**
 43 | - `AsyncMigration`: Single migration wrapper
 44 |   - `from_file(path)`: Load .surrealql file; strips comments and whitespace
 45 |   - `run(bump)`: Execute SQL; call bump_version() on success (bump=True) or lower_version() (bump=False)
 46 | 
 47 | - `AsyncMigrationRunner`: Sequences multiple migrations
 48 |   - `run_all()`: Execute pending migrations from current_version to end
 49 |   - `run_one_up()`: Run next migration
 50 |   - `run_one_down()`: Rollback latest migration
 51 | 
 52 | - `AsyncMigrationManager`: Main orchestrator
 53 |   - Loads 9 up migrations + 9 down migrations (hard-coded in __init__)
 54 |   - `get_current_version()`: Query max version from _sbl_migrations table
 55 |   - `needs_migration()`: Boolean check (current < total migrations available)
 56 |   - `run_migration_up()`: Run all pending migrations with logging
 57 | 
 58 | **Version Tracking**
 59 | - `get_latest_version()`: Query max version; returns 0 if _sbl_migrations table missing
 60 | - `get_all_versions()`: Fetch all migration records; returns empty list on error
 61 | - `bump_version()`: INSERT new entry into _sbl_migrations with version + applied_at timestamp
 62 | - `lower_version()`: DELETE latest migration record (rollback)
 63 | 
 64 | ### migrate.py
 65 | 
 66 | **Backward Compatibility**
 67 | - `MigrationManager`: Sync wrapper around AsyncMigrationManager
 68 |   - `get_current_version()`: Wraps async call with asyncio.run()
 69 |   - `needs_migration` property: Checks if migration pending
 70 |   - `run_migration_up()`: Execute migrations synchronously
 71 | 
 72 | ## Common Patterns
 73 | 
 74 | - **Async-first design**: All operations async via AsyncSurreal; sync wrapper provided for legacy code
 75 | - **Connection per operation**: Each repo_* function opens/closes connection (no pooling); designed for serverless/stateless API
 76 | - **Auto-timestamping**: repo_create() and repo_update() auto-set `created`/`updated` fields
 77 | - **Error resilience**: RuntimeError for transaction conflicts (retriable, logged at DEBUG level); catches and re-raises other exceptions
 78 | - **RecordID polymorphism**: Functions accept string or RecordID; coerced to consistent type
 79 | - **Graceful degradation**: Migration queries catch exceptions and treat table-not-found as version 0
 80 | 
 81 | ## Key Dependencies
 82 | 
 83 | - `surrealdb`: AsyncSurreal client, RecordID type
 84 | - `loguru`: Logging with context (debug/error/success levels)
 85 | - Python stdlib: `os` (env vars), `datetime` (timestamps), `contextlib` (async context manager)
 86 | 
 87 | ## Important Quirks & Gotchas
 88 | 
 89 | - **No connection pooling**: Each repo_* operation creates new connection; adequate for HTTP request-scoped operations but inefficient for bulk workloads
 90 | - **Hard-coded migration files**: AsyncMigrationManager lists migrations 1-9 explicitly; adding new migration requires code change (not auto-discovery)
 91 | - **Record ID format inconsistency**: repo_update() accepts both `table:id` format and full RecordID; path handling can be subtle
 92 | - **ISO date parsing**: repo_update() parses `created` field from string to datetime if present; assumes ISO format
 93 | - **Timestamp overwrite risk**: repo_create() always sets new timestamps; can't preserve original created time on reimport
 94 | - **Transaction conflict handling**: RuntimeError from transaction conflicts logged at DEBUG level without stack trace (prevents log spam during concurrent operations)
 95 | - **Graceful null returns**: get_all_versions() returns [] on table missing; allows migration system to bootstrap cleanly
 96 | 
 97 | ## How to Extend
 98 | 
 99 | 1. **Add new CRUD operation**: Follow repo_* pattern (open connection, execute query, handle errors, close)
100 | 2. **Add migration**: Create migration file in `/migrations/N.surrealql` and `/migrations/N_down.surrealql`; update AsyncMigrationManager to load new files
101 | 3. **Change timestamp behavior**: Modify repo_create()/repo_update() to not auto-set `updated` field if caller-provided
102 | 4. **Implement connection pooling**: Replace db_connection context manager with pool.acquire() pattern (for high-throughput scenarios)
103 | 
104 | ## Integration Points
105 | 
106 | - **API startup** (api/main.py): FastAPI lifespan handler calls AsyncMigrationManager.run_migration_up() on server start
107 | - **Domain models** (domain/*.py): All models call repo_* functions for persistence
108 | - **Commands** (commands/*.py): Background jobs use repo_* for state updates
109 | - **Streamlit UI** (pages/*.py): Deprecated migration check; relies on API to run migrations
110 | 
111 | ## Usage Example
112 | 
113 | ```python
114 | from open_notebook.database.repository import repo_create, repo_query, repo_update
115 | 
116 | # Create
117 | record = await repo_create("notebooks", {"title": "Research"})
118 | 
119 | # Query
120 | results = await repo_query("SELECT * FROM notebooks WHERE title = $title", {"title": "Research"})
121 | 
122 | # Update
123 | await repo_update("notebooks", record["id"], {"title": "Updated Research"})
124 | ```
125 |

 12 | def get_database_url():
 13 |     """Get database URL with backward compatibility"""
 14 |     surreal_url = os.getenv("SURREAL_URL")
 15 |     if surreal_url:
 16 |         return surreal_url
 17 | 
 18 |     # Fallback to old format - WebSocket URL format

 20 |     port = os.getenv("SURREAL_PORT", "8000")

 25 |     """Get password with backward compatibility"""

 29 | def parse_record_ids(obj: Any) -> Any:
 30 |     """Recursively parse and convert RecordIDs into strings."""
 31 |     if isinstance(obj, dict):
 32 |         return {k: parse_record_ids(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
 33 |     elif isinstance(obj, list):
 34 |         return [parse_record_ids(item) for item in obj]
 35 |     elif isinstance(obj, RecordID):
 36 |         return str(obj)
 37 |     return obj

 40 | def ensure_record_id(value: Union[str, RecordID]) -> RecordID:
 41 |     """Ensure a value is a RecordID."""
 42 |     if isinstance(value, RecordID):
 43 |         return value
 44 |     return RecordID.parse(value)

 47 | @asynccontextmanager
 48 | async def db_connection():
 49 |     db = AsyncSurreal(get_database_url())
 50 |     await db.signin(
 51 |         {
 52 |             "username": os.environ.get("SURREAL_USER"),
 53 |             "password": get_database_password(),
 54 |         }
 55 |     )
 56 |     await db.use(
 57 |         os.environ.get("SURREAL_NAMESPACE"), os.environ.get("SURREAL_DATABASE")
 58 |     )
 59 |     try:
 60 |         yield db
 61 |     finally:
 62 |         await db.close()

 65 | async def repo_query(
 66 |     query_str: str, vars: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
 67 | ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
 68 |     """Execute a SurrealQL query and return the results"""
 69 | 
 70 |     async with db_connection() as connection:
 71 |         try:
 72 |             result = parse_record_ids(await connection.query(query_str, vars))
 73 |             if isinstance(result, str):
 74 |                 raise RuntimeError(result)
 75 |             return result
 76 |         except RuntimeError as e:
 77 |             # RuntimeError is raised for retriable transaction conflicts - log at debug to avoid noise
 78 |             logger.debug(str(e))
 79 |             raise
 80 |         except Exception as e:
 81 |             logger.exception(e)
 82 |             raise
 83 | 
 84 | 
 85 | async def repo_create(table: str, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 86 |     """Create a new record in the specified table"""
 87 |     # Remove 'id' attribute if it exists in data
 88 |     data.pop("id", None)
 89 |     data["created"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
 90 |     data["updated"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
 91 |     try:
 92 |         async with db_connection() as connection:
 93 |             result = parse_record_ids(await connection.insert(table, data))
 94 |             # SurrealDB may return a string error message instead of the expected record
 95 |             if isinstance(result, str):
 96 |                 raise RuntimeError(result)
 97 |             return result
 98 |     except RuntimeError as e:
 99 |         logger.error(str(e))
100 |         raise
101 |     except Exception as e:
102 |         logger.exception(e)
103 |         raise RuntimeError("Failed to create record")
104 | 
105 | 
106 | async def repo_relate(
107 |     source: str, relationship: str, target: str, data: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
108 | ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
109 |     """Create a relationship between two records with optional data"""
110 |     if data is None:
111 |         data = {}
112 |     query = f"RELATE {source}->{relationship}->{target} CONTENT $data;"
113 |     # logger.debug(f"Relate query: {query}")
114 | 
115 |     return await repo_query(
116 |         query,
117 |         {
118 |             "data": data,
119 |         },
120 |     )
121 | 
122 | 
123 | async def repo_upsert(
124 |     table: str, id: Optional[str], data: Dict[str, Any], add_timestamp: bool = False
125 | ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
126 |     """Create or update a record in the specified table"""
127 |     data.pop("id", None)
128 |     if add_timestamp:
129 |         data["updated"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
130 |     query = f"UPSERT {id if id else table} MERGE $data;"
131 |     return await repo_query(query, {"data": data})
132 | 
133 | 
134 | async def repo_update(
135 |     table: str, id: str, data: Dict[str, Any]
136 | ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
137 |     """Update an existing record by table and id"""
138 |     # If id already contains the table name, use it as is
139 |     try:
140 |         if isinstance(id, RecordID) or (":" in id and id.startswith(f"{table}:")):
141 |             record_id = id
142 |         else:
143 |             record_id = f"{table}:{id}"
144 |         data.pop("id", None)
145 |         if "created" in data and isinstance(data["created"], str):
146 |             data["created"] = datetime.fromisoformat(data["created"])
147 |         data["updated"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
148 |         query = f"UPDATE {record_id} MERGE $data;"
149 |         # logger.debug(f"Update query: {query}")
150 |         result = await repo_query(query, {"data": data})
151 |         # if isinstance(result, list):
152 |         #     return [_return_data(item) for item in result]
153 |         return parse_record_ids(result)
154 |     except Exception as e:
155 |         raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to update record: {str(e)}")
156 | 
157 | 
158 | async def repo_delete(record_id: Union[str, RecordID]):
159 |     """Delete a record by record id"""
160 | 
161 |     try:
162 |         async with db_connection() as connection:
163 |             return await connection.delete(ensure_record_id(record_id))
164 |     except Exception as e:
165 |         logger.exception(e)
166 |         raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to delete record: {str(e)}")
167 | 
168 | 
169 | async def repo_insert(
170 |     table: str, data: List[Dict[str, Any]], ignore_duplicates: bool = False
171 | ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
172 |     """Create a new record in the specified table"""
173 |     try:
174 |         async with db_connection() as connection:
175 |             result = parse_record_ids(await connection.insert(table, data))
176 |             # SurrealDB may return a string error message instead of the expected records
177 |             if isinstance(result, str):
178 |                 raise RuntimeError(result)
179 |             return result
180 |     except RuntimeError as e:
181 |         if ignore_duplicates and "already contains" in str(e):
182 |             return []
183 |         # Log transaction conflicts at debug level (they are expected during concurrent operations)
184 |         error_str = str(e).lower()
185 |         if "transaction" in error_str or "conflict" in error_str:
186 |             logger.debug(str(e))
187 |         else:
188 |             logger.error(str(e))
189 |         raise
190 |     except Exception as e:
191 |         if ignore_duplicates and "already contains" in str(e):
192 |             return []
193 |         logger.exception(e)
194 |         raise RuntimeError("Failed to create record")
195 |

  1 | """
  2 | Unified embedding utilities for Open Notebook.
  3 | 
  4 | Provides centralized embedding generation with support for:
  5 | - Single text embedding (with automatic chunking and mean pooling for large texts)
  6 | - Batch text embedding (multiple texts in a single API call)
  7 | - Mean pooling for combining multiple embeddings into one
  8 | 
  9 | All embedding operations in the application should use these functions
 10 | to ensure consistent behavior and proper handling of large content.
 11 | """
 12 | 
 13 | from typing import List, Optional
 14 | 
 15 | import numpy as np
 16 | from loguru import logger
 17 | 
 18 | from open_notebook.ai.models import model_manager
 19 | 
 20 | from .chunking import CHUNK_SIZE, ContentType, chunk_text
 21 | 
 22 | 
 23 | async def mean_pool_embeddings(embeddings: List[List[float]]) -> List[float]:
 24 |     """
 25 |     Combine multiple embeddings into a single embedding using mean pooling.
 26 | 
 27 |     Algorithm:
 28 |     1. Normalize each embedding to unit length
 29 |     2. Compute element-wise mean
 30 |     3. Normalize the result to unit length
 31 | 
 32 |     This approach ensures the final embedding has the same properties as
 33 |     individual embeddings (unit length) regardless of input count.
 34 | 
 35 |     Args:
 36 |         embeddings: List of embedding vectors (each is a list of floats)
 37 | 
 38 |     Returns:
 39 |         Single embedding vector (mean pooled and normalized)
 40 | 
 41 |     Raises:
 42 |         ValueError: If embeddings list is empty or embeddings have different dimensions
 43 |     """
 44 |     if not embeddings:
 45 |         raise ValueError("Cannot mean pool empty list of embeddings")
 46 | 
 47 |     if len(embeddings) == 1:
 48 |         # Single embedding - just normalize and return
 49 |         arr = np.array(embeddings[0], dtype=np.float64)
 50 |         norm = np.linalg.norm(arr)
 51 |         if norm > 0:
 52 |             arr = arr / norm
 53 |         return arr.tolist()
 54 | 
 55 |     # Convert to numpy array
 56 |     arr = np.array(embeddings, dtype=np.float64)
 57 | 
 58 |     # Verify all embeddings have same dimension
 59 |     if arr.ndim != 2:
 60 |         raise ValueError(f"Expected 2D array, got shape {arr.shape}")
 61 | 
 62 |     # Normalize each embedding to unit length
 63 |     norms = np.linalg.norm(arr, axis=1, keepdims=True)
 64 |     # Avoid division by zero
 65 |     norms = np.where(norms > 0, norms, 1.0)
 66 |     normalized = arr / norms
 67 | 
 68 |     # Compute mean
 69 |     mean = np.mean(normalized, axis=0)
 70 | 
 71 |     # Normalize the result
 72 |     mean_norm = np.linalg.norm(mean)
 73 |     if mean_norm > 0:
 74 |         mean = mean / mean_norm
 75 | 
 76 |     return mean.tolist()
 77 | 
 78 | 
 79 | async def generate_embeddings(
 80 |     texts: List[str], command_id: Optional[str] = None
 81 | ) -> List[List[float]]:
 82 |     """
 83 |     Generate embeddings for multiple texts in a single API call.
 84 | 
 85 |     This is more efficient than calling generate_embedding() multiple times
 86 |     when you have multiple texts to embed (e.g., source chunks).
 87 | 
 88 |     Args:
 89 |         texts: List of text strings to embed
 90 |         command_id: Optional command ID for error logging context
 91 | 
 92 |     Returns:
 93 |         List of embedding vectors, one per input text
 94 | 
 95 |     Raises:
 96 |         ValueError: If no embedding model is configured
 97 |         RuntimeError: If embedding generation fails
 98 |     """
 99 |     if not texts:
100 |         return []
101 | 
102 |     embedding_model = await model_manager.get_embedding_model()
103 |     if not embedding_model:
104 |         raise ValueError(
105 |             "No embedding model configured. Please configure one in the Models section."
106 |         )
107 | 
108 |     model_name = getattr(embedding_model, "model_name", "unknown")
109 | 
110 |     # Log text sizes for debugging
111 |     text_sizes = [len(t) for t in texts]
112 |     logger.debug(
113 |         f"Generating embeddings for {len(texts)} texts "
114 |         f"(sizes: min={min(text_sizes)}, max={max(text_sizes)}, "
115 |         f"total={sum(text_sizes)} chars)"
116 |     )
117 | 
118 |     try:
119 |         # Single API call for all texts
120 |         embeddings = await embedding_model.aembed(texts)
121 |         logger.debug(f"Generated {len(embeddings)} embeddings")
122 |         return embeddings
123 |     except Exception as e:
124 |         # Log at debug level - the calling command will log at appropriate level
125 |         # based on whether retries are exhausted
126 |         cmd_context = f" (command: {command_id})" if command_id else ""
127 |         logger.debug(
128 |             f"Embedding API error using model '{model_name}' "
129 |             f"for {len(texts)} texts (sizes: {min(text_sizes)}-{max(text_sizes)} chars)"
130 |             f"{cmd_context}: {e}"
131 |         )
132 |         raise RuntimeError(
133 |             f"Failed to generate embeddings using model '{model_name}': {e}"
134 |         ) from e
135 | 
136 | 
137 | async def generate_embedding(
138 |     text: str,
139 |     content_type: Optional[ContentType] = None,
140 |     file_path: Optional[str] = None,
141 |     command_id: Optional[str] = None,
142 | ) -> List[float]:
143 |     """
144 |     Generate a single embedding for text, handling large content via chunking and mean pooling.
145 | 
146 |     For short text (<= CHUNK_SIZE):
147 |         - Embeds directly and returns the embedding
148 | 
149 |     For long text (> CHUNK_SIZE):
150 |         - Chunks the text using appropriate splitter for content type
151 |         - Embeds all chunks in a single API call
152 |         - Combines embeddings via mean pooling
153 | 
154 |     Args:
155 |         text: The text to embed
156 |         content_type: Optional explicit content type for chunking
157 |         file_path: Optional file path for content type detection
158 |         command_id: Optional command ID for error logging context
159 | 
160 |     Returns:
161 |         Single embedding vector (list of floats)
162 | 
163 |     Raises:
164 |         ValueError: If text is empty or no embedding model configured
165 |         RuntimeError: If embedding generation fails
166 |     """
167 |     if not text or not text.strip():
168 |         raise ValueError("Cannot generate embedding for empty text")
169 | 
170 |     text = text.strip()
171 | 
172 |     # Check if chunking is needed
173 |     if len(text) <= CHUNK_SIZE:
174 |         # Short text - embed directly
175 |         logger.debug(f"Embedding short text ({len(text)} chars) directly")
176 |         embeddings = await generate_embeddings([text], command_id=command_id)
177 |         return embeddings[0]
178 | 
179 |     # Long text - chunk and mean pool
180 |     logger.debug(f"Text exceeds chunk size ({len(text)} chars), chunking...")
181 | 
182 |     chunks = chunk_text(text, content_type=content_type, file_path=file_path)
183 | 
184 |     if not chunks:
185 |         raise ValueError("Text chunking produced no chunks")
186 | 
187 |     if len(chunks) == 1:
188 |         # Single chunk after splitting
189 |         embeddings = await generate_embeddings(chunks, command_id=command_id)
190 |         return embeddings[0]
191 | 
192 |     logger.debug(f"Embedding {len(chunks)} chunks and mean pooling")
193 | 
194 |     # Embed all chunks in single API call
195 |     embeddings = await generate_embeddings(chunks, command_id=command_id)
196 | 
197 |     # Mean pool to get single embedding
198 |     pooled = await mean_pool_embeddings(embeddings)
199 | 
200 |     logger.debug(f"Mean pooled {len(embeddings)} embeddings into single vector")
201 |     return pooled
202 |

  1 | import { create } from 'zustand'
  2 | import { persist } from 'zustand/middleware'
  3 | import { getApiUrl } from '@/lib/config'
  4 | 
  5 | interface AuthState {
  6 |   isAuthenticated: boolean
  7 |   token: string | null
  8 |   isLoading: boolean
  9 |   error: string | null
 10 |   lastAuthCheck: number | null
 11 |   isCheckingAuth: boolean
 12 |   hasHydrated: boolean
 13 |   authRequired: boolean | null
 14 |   setHasHydrated: (state: boolean) => void
 15 |   checkAuthRequired: () => Promise<boolean>
 16 |   login: (password: string) => Promise<boolean>
 17 |   logout: () => void
 18 |   checkAuth: () => Promise<boolean>
 19 | }
 20 | 
 21 | export const useAuthStore = create<AuthState>()(
 22 |   persist(
 23 |     (set, get) => ({
 24 |       isAuthenticated: false,
 25 |       token: null,
 26 |       isLoading: false,
 27 |       error: null,
 28 |       lastAuthCheck: null,
 29 |       isCheckingAuth: false,
 30 |       hasHydrated: false,
 31 |       authRequired: null,
 32 | 
 33 |       setHasHydrated: (state: boolean) => {
 34 |         set({ hasHydrated: state })
 35 |       },
 36 | 
 37 |       checkAuthRequired: async () => {
 38 |         try {
 39 |           const apiUrl = await getApiUrl()
 40 |           const response = await fetch(`${apiUrl}/api/auth/status`, {
 41 |             cache: 'no-store',
 42 |           })
 43 | 
 44 |           if (!response.ok) {
 45 |             throw new Error(`Auth status check failed: ${response.status}`)
 46 |           }
 47 | 
 48 |           const data = await response.json()
 49 |           const required = data.auth_enabled || false
 50 |           set({ authRequired: required })
 51 | 
 52 |           // If auth is not required, mark as authenticated
 53 |           if (!required) {
 54 |             set({ isAuthenticated: true, token: 'not-required' })
 55 |           }
 56 | 
 57 |           return required
 58 |         } catch (error) {
 59 |           console.error('Failed to check auth status:', error)
 60 | 
 61 |           // If it's a network error, set a more helpful error message
 62 |           if (error instanceof TypeError && error.message.includes('Failed to fetch')) {
 63 |             set({
 64 |               error: 'Unable to connect to server. Please check if the API is running.',
 65 |               authRequired: null  // Don't assume auth is required if we can't connect
 66 |             })
 67 |           } else {
 68 |             // For other errors, default to requiring auth to be safe
 69 |             set({ authRequired: true })
 70 |           }
 71 | 
 72 |           // Re-throw the error so the UI can handle it
 73 |           throw error
 74 |         }
 75 |       },
 76 | 
 77 |       login: async (password: string) => {
 78 |         set({ isLoading: true, error: null })
 79 |         try {
 80 |           const apiUrl = await getApiUrl()
 81 | 
 82 |           // Test auth with notebooks endpoint
 83 |           const response = await fetch(`${apiUrl}/api/notebooks`, {
 84 |             method: 'GET',
 85 |             headers: {
 86 |               'Authorization': `Bearer ${password}`,
 87 |               'Content-Type': 'application/json'
 88 |             }
 89 |           })
 90 |           
 91 |           if (response.ok) {
 92 |             set({ 
 93 |               isAuthenticated: true, 
 94 |               token: password, 
 95 |               isLoading: false,
 96 |               lastAuthCheck: Date.now(),
 97 |               error: null
 98 |             })
 99 |             return true
100 |           } else {
101 |             let errorMessage = 'Authentication failed'
102 |             if (response.status === 401) {
103 |               errorMessage = 'Invalid password. Please try again.'
104 |             } else if (response.status === 403) {
105 |               errorMessage = 'Access denied. Please check your credentials.'
106 |             } else if (response.status >= 500) {
107 |               errorMessage = 'Server error. Please try again later.'
108 |             } else {
109 |               errorMessage = `Authentication failed (${response.status})`
110 |             }
111 |             
112 |             set({ 
113 |               error: errorMessage,
114 |               isLoading: false,
115 |               isAuthenticated: false,
116 |               token: null
117 |             })
118 |             return false
119 |           }
120 |         } catch (error) {
121 |           console.error('Network error during auth:', error)
122 |           let errorMessage = 'Authentication failed'
123 |           
124 |           if (error instanceof TypeError && error.message.includes('Failed to fetch')) {
125 |             errorMessage = 'Unable to connect to server. Please check if the API is running.'
126 |           } else if (error instanceof Error) {
127 |             errorMessage = `Network error: ${error.message}`
128 |           } else {
129 |             errorMessage = 'An unexpected error occurred during authentication'
130 |           }
131 |           
132 |           set({ 
133 |             error: errorMessage,
134 |             isLoading: false,
135 |             isAuthenticated: false,
136 |             token: null
137 |           })
138 |           return false
139 |         }
140 |       },
141 |       
142 |       logout: () => {
143 |         set({ 
144 |           isAuthenticated: false, 
145 |           token: null, 
146 |           error: null 
147 |         })
148 |       },
149 |       
150 |       checkAuth: async () => {
151 |         const state = get()
152 |         const { token, lastAuthCheck, isCheckingAuth, isAuthenticated } = state
153 | 
154 |         // If already checking, return current auth state
155 |         if (isCheckingAuth) {
156 |           return isAuthenticated
157 |         }
158 | 
159 |         // If no token, not authenticated
160 |         if (!token) {
161 |           return false
162 |         }
163 | 
164 |         // If we checked recently (within 30 seconds) and are authenticated, skip
165 |         const now = Date.now()
166 |         if (isAuthenticated && lastAuthCheck && (now - lastAuthCheck) < 30000) {
167 |           return true
168 |         }
169 | 
170 |         set({ isCheckingAuth: true })
171 | 
172 |         try {
173 |           const apiUrl = await getApiUrl()
174 | 
175 |           const response = await fetch(`${apiUrl}/api/notebooks`, {
176 |             method: 'GET',
177 |             headers: {
178 |               'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`,
179 |               'Content-Type': 'application/json'
180 |             }
181 |           })
182 |           
183 |           if (response.ok) {
184 |             set({ 
185 |               isAuthenticated: true, 
186 |               lastAuthCheck: now,
187 |               isCheckingAuth: false 
188 |             })
189 |             return true
190 |           } else {
191 |             set({
192 |               isAuthenticated: false,
193 |               token: null,
194 |               lastAuthCheck: null,
195 |               isCheckingAuth: false
196 |             })
197 |             return false
198 |           }
199 |         } catch (error) {
200 |           console.error('checkAuth error:', error)
201 |           set({ 
202 |             isAuthenticated: false, 
203 |             token: null,
204 |             lastAuthCheck: null,
205 |             isCheckingAuth: false 
206 |           })
207 |           return false
208 |         }
209 |       }
210 |     }),
211 |     {
212 |       name: 'auth-storage',
213 |       partialize: (state) => ({
214 |         token: state.token,
215 |         isAuthenticated: state.isAuthenticated
216 |       }),
217 |       onRehydrateStorage: () => (state) => {
218 |         state?.setHasHydrated(true)
219 |       }
220 |     }
221 |   )
222 | )

 16 | 
 17 | const createNoteSchema = z.object({
 18 |   title: z.string().optional(),
 19 |   content: z.string().min(1, 'Content is required'),
 20 | })
 21 | 
 22 | type CreateNoteFormData = z.infer<typeof createNoteSchema>
 23 | 
 24 | interface NoteEditorDialogProps {
 25 |   open: boolean
 26 |   onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void
 27 |   notebookId: string
 28 |   note?: { id: string; title: string | null; content: string | null }
 29 | }
 30 | 
 31 | export function NoteEditorDialog({ open, onOpenChange, notebookId, note }: NoteEditorDialogProps) {
 32 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 33 |   const createNote = useCreateNote()
 34 |   const updateNote = useUpdateNote()
 35 |   const queryClient = useQueryClient()
 36 |   const isEditing = Boolean(note)
 37 | 
 38 |   // Ensure note ID has 'note:' prefix for API calls
 39 |   const noteIdWithPrefix = note?.id
 40 |     ? (note.id.includes(':') ? note.id : `note:${note.id}`)
 41 |     : ''
 42 | 
 43 |   const { data: fetchedNote, isLoading: noteLoading } = useNote(noteIdWithPrefix, { enabled: open && !!note?.id })
 44 |   const isSaving = isEditing ? updateNote.isPending : createNote.isPending
 45 |   const {
 46 |     handleSubmit,
 47 |     control,
 48 |     formState: { errors },
 49 |     reset,
 50 |     setValue,
 51 |   } = useForm<CreateNoteFormData>({
 52 |     resolver: zodResolver(createNoteSchema),
 53 |     defaultValues: {
 54 |       title: '',
 55 |       content: '',
 56 |     },
 57 |   })
 58 |   const watchTitle = useWatch({ control, name: 'title' })
 59 |   const [isEditorFullscreen, setIsEditorFullscreen] = useState(false)
 60 | 
 61 |   useEffect(() => {
 62 |     if (!open) {
 63 |       reset({ title: '', content: '' })
 64 |       return
 65 |     }
 66 | 
 67 |     const source = fetchedNote ?? note
 68 |     const title = source?.title ?? ''
 69 |     const content = source?.content ?? ''
 70 | 
 71 |     reset({ title, content })
 72 |   }, [open, note, fetchedNote, reset])
 73 | 
 74 |   useEffect(() => {
 75 |     if (!open) return
 76 | 
 77 |     const observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
 78 |       setIsEditorFullscreen(!!document.querySelector('.w-md-editor-fullscreen'))
 79 |     })
 80 |     observer.observe(document.body, { subtree: true, attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['class'] })
 81 |     return () => observer.disconnect()
 82 |   }, [open])
 83 | 
 84 |   const onSubmit = async (data: CreateNoteFormData) => {
 85 |     if (note) {
 86 |       await updateNote.mutateAsync({
 87 |         id: noteIdWithPrefix,
 88 |         data: {
 89 |           title: data.title || undefined,
 90 |           content: data.content,
 91 |         },
 92 |       })
 93 |       // Only invalidate notebook-specific queries if we have a notebookId
 94 |       if (notebookId) {
 95 |         queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.notes(notebookId) })
 96 |       }
 97 |     } else {
 98 |       // Creating a note requires a notebookId
 99 |       if (!notebookId) {
100 |         console.error('Cannot create note without notebook_id')
101 |         return
102 |       }
103 |       await createNote.mutateAsync({
104 |         title: data.title || undefined,
105 |         content: data.content,
106 |         note_type: 'human',
107 |         notebook_id: notebookId,
108 |       })
109 |     }
110 |     reset()
111 |     onOpenChange(false)
112 |   }
113 | 
114 |   const handleClose = () => {
115 |     reset()
116 |     setIsEditorFullscreen(false)
117 |     onOpenChange(false)
118 |   }
119 | 
120 |   return (
121 |     <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={handleClose}>
122 |       <DialogContent className={cn(
123 |           "sm:max-w-3xl w-full max-h-[90vh] overflow-hidden p-0",
124 |           isEditorFullscreen && "!max-w-screen !max-h-screen border-none w-screen h-screen"
125 |       )}>
126 |         <DialogTitle className="sr-only">
127 |           {isEditing ? t.sources.editNote : t.sources.createNote}
128 |         </DialogTitle>
129 |         <form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onSubmit)} className="flex h-full flex-col">
130 |           {isEditing && noteLoading ? (
131 |             <div className="flex-1 flex items-center justify-center py-10">
132 |               <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{t.common.loading}</span>
133 |             </div>
134 |           ) : (
135 |             <>
136 |               <div className="border-b px-6 py-4">
137 |                 <InlineEdit
138 |                   id="note-title"
139 |                   name="title"
140 |                   value={watchTitle ?? ''}
141 |                   onSave={(value) => setValue('title', value || '')}
142 |                   placeholder={t.sources.addTitle}
143 |                   emptyText={t.sources.untitledNote}
144 |                   className="text-xl font-semibold"
145 |                   inputClassName="text-xl font-semibold"
146 |                 />
147 |               </div>
148 | 
149 |               <div className={cn(
150 |                   "flex-1 overflow-y-auto",
151 |                   !isEditorFullscreen && "px-6 py-4")
152 |               }>
153 |                 <Controller
154 |                   control={control}
155 |                   name="content"
156 |                   render={({ field }) => (
157 |                     <MarkdownEditor
158 |                       key={note?.id ?? 'new'}
159 |                       textareaId="note-content"
160 |                       value={field.value}
161 |                       onChange={field.onChange}
162 |                       height={420}
163 |                       placeholder={t.sources.writeNotePlaceholder}
164 |                       className={cn(
165 |                           "w-full h-full min-h-[420px] max-h-[500px] overflow-hidden [&_.w-md-editor]:!static [&_.w-md-editor]:!w-full [&_.w-md-editor]:!h-full [&_.w-md-editor-content]:overflow-y-auto",
166 |                           !isEditorFullscreen && "rounded-md border"
167 |                       )}
168 |                     />
169 |                   )}
170 |                 />
171 |                 {errors.content && (
172 |                   <p className="text-sm text-red-600 mt-1">{errors.content.message}</p>
173 |                 )}
174 |               </div>
175 |             </>
176 |           )}
177 | 
178 |           <div className="border-t px-6 py-4 flex justify-end gap-2">
179 |             <Button type="button" variant="outline" onClick={handleClose}>
180 |               {t.common.cancel}
181 |             </Button>
182 |             <Button
183 |               type="submit"
184 |               disabled={isSaving || (isEditing && noteLoading)}
185 |             >
186 |               {isSaving
187 |                 ? isEditing ? `${t.common.saving}...` : `${t.common.creating}...`
188 |                 : isEditing
189 |                   ? t.sources.saveNote
190 |                   : t.sources.createNoteBtn}
191 |             </Button>
192 |           </div>
193 |         </form>
194 |       </DialogContent>
195 |     </Dialog>
196 |   )
197 | }

  1 | import time

  3 | from typing import Optional
  4 |

  6 | from pydantic import BaseModel
  7 | from surreal_commands import CommandInput, CommandOutput, command
  8 | 
  9 | from open_notebook.config import DATA_FOLDER
 10 | from open_notebook.database.repository import ensure_record_id, repo_query
 11 | from open_notebook.podcasts.models import EpisodeProfile, PodcastEpisode, SpeakerProfile
 12 | 
 13 | try:
 14 |     from podcast_creator import configure, create_podcast
 15 | except ImportError as e:
 16 |     logger.error(f"Failed to import podcast_creator: {e}")
 17 |     raise ValueError("podcast_creator library not available")

 19 | 
 20 | def full_model_dump(model):
 21 |     if isinstance(model, BaseModel):
 22 |         return model.model_dump()
 23 |     elif isinstance(model, dict):
 24 |         return {k: full_model_dump(v) for k, v in model.items()}
 25 |     elif isinstance(model, list):
 26 |         return [full_model_dump(item) for item in model]
 27 |     else:
 28 |         return model
 29 | 
 30 | 
 31 | class PodcastGenerationInput(CommandInput):
 32 |     episode_profile: str
 33 |     speaker_profile: str
 34 |     episode_name: str
 35 |     content: str
 36 |     briefing_suffix: Optional[str] = None
 37 | 
 38 | 
 39 | class PodcastGenerationOutput(CommandOutput):
 40 |     success: bool
 41 |     episode_id: Optional[str] = None
 42 |     audio_file_path: Optional[str] = None
 43 |     transcript: Optional[dict] = None
 44 |     outline: Optional[dict] = None
 45 |     processing_time: float
 46 |     error_message: Optional[str] = None
 47 | 
 48 | 
 49 | @command("generate_podcast", app="open_notebook")
 50 | async def generate_podcast_command(
 51 |     input_data: PodcastGenerationInput,
 52 | ) -> PodcastGenerationOutput:
 53 |     """
 54 |     Real podcast generation using podcast-creator library with Episode Profiles
 55 |     """
 56 |     start_time = time.time()
 57 | 
 58 |     try:
 59 |         logger.info(
 60 |             f"Starting podcast generation for episode: {input_data.episode_name}"
 61 |         )
 62 |         logger.info(f"Using episode profile: {input_data.episode_profile}")
 63 | 
 64 |         # 1. Load Episode and Speaker profiles from SurrealDB
 65 |         episode_profile = await EpisodeProfile.get_by_name(input_data.episode_profile)
 66 |         if not episode_profile:
 67 |             raise ValueError(
 68 |                 f"Episode profile '{input_data.episode_profile}' not found"
 69 |             )
 70 | 
 71 |         speaker_profile = await SpeakerProfile.get_by_name(
 72 |             episode_profile.speaker_config
 73 |         )
 74 |         if not speaker_profile:
 75 |             raise ValueError(
 76 |                 f"Speaker profile '{episode_profile.speaker_config}' not found"
 77 |             )
 78 | 
 79 |         logger.info(f"Loaded episode profile: {episode_profile.name}")
 80 |         logger.info(f"Loaded speaker profile: {speaker_profile.name}")
 81 | 
 82 |         # 3. Load all profiles and configure podcast-creator
 83 |         episode_profiles = await repo_query("SELECT * FROM episode_profile")
 84 |         speaker_profiles = await repo_query("SELECT * FROM speaker_profile")
 85 | 
 86 |         # Transform the surrealdb array into a dictionary for podcast-creator
 87 |         episode_profiles_dict = {
 88 |             profile["name"]: profile for profile in episode_profiles
 89 |         }
 90 |         speaker_profiles_dict = {
 91 |             profile["name"]: profile for profile in speaker_profiles
 92 |         }
 93 | 
 94 |         # 4. Generate briefing
 95 |         briefing = episode_profile.default_briefing
 96 |         if input_data.briefing_suffix:
 97 |             briefing += f"\n\nAdditional instructions: {input_data.briefing_suffix}"
 98 | 
 99 |         # Create the a record for the episose and associate with the ongoing command
100 |         episode = PodcastEpisode(
101 |             name=input_data.episode_name,
102 |             episode_profile=full_model_dump(episode_profile.model_dump()),
103 |             speaker_profile=full_model_dump(speaker_profile.model_dump()),
104 |             command=ensure_record_id(input_data.execution_context.command_id)
105 |             if input_data.execution_context
106 |             else None,
107 |             briefing=briefing,
108 |             content=input_data.content,
109 |             audio_file=None,
110 |             transcript=None,
111 |             outline=None,
112 |         )
113 |         await episode.save()
114 | 
115 |         configure("speakers_config", {"profiles": speaker_profiles_dict})
116 |         configure("episode_config", {"profiles": episode_profiles_dict})
117 | 
118 |         logger.info("Configured podcast-creator with episode and speaker profiles")
119 | 
120 |         logger.info(f"Generated briefing (length: {len(briefing)} chars)")
121 | 
122 |         # 5. Create output directory
123 |         output_dir = Path(f"{DATA_FOLDER}/podcasts/episodes/{input_data.episode_name}")
124 |         output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
125 | 
126 |         logger.info(f"Created output directory: {output_dir}")
127 | 
128 |         # 6. Generate podcast using podcast-creator
129 |         logger.info("Starting podcast generation with podcast-creator...")
130 | 
131 |         result = await create_podcast(
132 |             content=input_data.content,
133 |             briefing=briefing,
134 |             episode_name=input_data.episode_name,
135 |             output_dir=str(output_dir),
136 |             speaker_config=speaker_profile.name,
137 |             episode_profile=episode_profile.name,
138 |         )
139 | 
140 |         episode.audio_file = (
141 |             str(result.get("final_output_file_path")) if result else None
142 |         )
143 |         episode.transcript = {
144 |             "transcript": full_model_dump(result["transcript"]) if result else None
145 |         }
146 |         episode.outline = full_model_dump(result["outline"]) if result else None
147 |         await episode.save()
148 | 
149 |         processing_time = time.time() - start_time
150 |         logger.info(
151 |             f"Successfully generated podcast episode: {episode.id} in {processing_time:.2f}s"
152 |         )
153 | 
154 |         return PodcastGenerationOutput(
155 |             success=True,
156 |             episode_id=str(episode.id),
157 |             audio_file_path=str(result.get("final_output_file_path"))
158 |             if result
159 |             else None,
160 |             transcript={"transcript": full_model_dump(result["transcript"])}
161 |             if result.get("transcript")
162 |             else None,
163 |             outline=full_model_dump(result["outline"])
164 |             if result.get("outline")
165 |             else None,
166 |             processing_time=processing_time,
167 |         )
168 | 
169 |     except Exception as e:
170 |         processing_time = time.time() - start_time
171 |         logger.error(f"Podcast generation failed: {e}")
172 |         logger.exception(e)
173 | 
174 |         # Check for specific GPT-5 extended thinking issue
175 |         error_msg = str(e)
176 |         if "Invalid json output" in error_msg or "Expecting value" in error_msg:
177 |             # This often happens with GPT-5 models that use extended thinking (<think> tags)
178 |             # and put all output inside thinking blocks
179 |             error_msg += (
180 |                 "\n\nNOTE: This error commonly occurs with GPT-5 models that use extended thinking. "
181 |                 "The model may be putting all output inside <think> tags, leaving nothing to parse. "
182 |                 "Try using gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, or gpt-4-turbo instead in your episode profile."
183 |             )
184 | 
185 |         return PodcastGenerationOutput(
186 |             success=False, processing_time=processing_time, error_message=error_msg
187 |         )
188 |

/api/routers/embedding_rebuild.py:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException
  2 | from loguru import logger
  3 | from surreal_commands import get_command_status
  4 | 
  5 | from api.command_service import CommandService
  6 | from api.models import (
  7 |     RebuildProgress,
  8 |     RebuildRequest,
  9 |     RebuildResponse,
 10 |     RebuildStats,
 11 |     RebuildStatusResponse,
 12 | )
 13 | from open_notebook.database.repository import repo_query
 14 | 
 15 | router = APIRouter()
 16 | 
 17 | 
 18 | @router.post("/rebuild", response_model=RebuildResponse)
 19 | async def start_rebuild(request: RebuildRequest):
 20 |     """
 21 |     Start a background job to rebuild embeddings.
 22 | 
 23 |     - **mode**: "existing" (re-embed items with embeddings) or "all" (embed everything)
 24 |     - **include_sources**: Include sources in rebuild (default: true)
 25 |     - **include_notes**: Include notes in rebuild (default: true)
 26 |     - **include_insights**: Include insights in rebuild (default: true)
 27 | 
 28 |     Returns command ID to track progress and estimated item count.
 29 |     """
 30 |     try:
 31 |         logger.info(f"Starting rebuild request: mode={request.mode}")
 32 | 
 33 |         # Import commands to ensure they're registered
 34 |         import commands.embedding_commands  # noqa: F401
 35 | 
 36 |         # Estimate total items (quick count query)
 37 |         # This is a rough estimate before the command runs
 38 |         total_estimate = 0
 39 | 
 40 |         if request.include_sources:
 41 |             if request.mode == "existing":
 42 |                 # Count sources with embeddings
 43 |                 result = await repo_query(
 44 |                     """
 45 |                     SELECT VALUE count(array::distinct(
 46 |                         SELECT VALUE source.id
 47 |                         FROM source_embedding
 48 |                         WHERE embedding != none AND array::len(embedding) > 0
 49 |                     )) as count FROM {}
 50 |                     """
 51 |                 )
 52 |             else:
 53 |                 # Count all sources with content
 54 |                 result = await repo_query(
 55 |                     "SELECT VALUE count() as count FROM source WHERE full_text != none GROUP ALL"
 56 |                 )
 57 | 
 58 |             if result and isinstance(result[0], dict):
 59 |                 total_estimate += result[0].get("count", 0)
 60 |             elif result:
 61 |                 total_estimate += result[0] if isinstance(result[0], int) else 0
 62 | 
 63 |         if request.include_notes:
 64 |             if request.mode == "existing":
 65 |                 result = await repo_query(
 66 |                     "SELECT VALUE count() as count FROM note WHERE embedding != none AND array::len(embedding) > 0 GROUP ALL"
 67 |                 )
 68 |             else:
 69 |                 result = await repo_query(
 70 |                     "SELECT VALUE count() as count FROM note WHERE content != none GROUP ALL"
 71 |                 )
 72 | 
 73 |             if result and isinstance(result[0], dict):
 74 |                 total_estimate += result[0].get("count", 0)
 75 |             elif result:
 76 |                 total_estimate += result[0] if isinstance(result[0], int) else 0
 77 | 
 78 |         if request.include_insights:
 79 |             if request.mode == "existing":
 80 |                 result = await repo_query(
 81 |                     "SELECT VALUE count() as count FROM source_insight WHERE embedding != none AND array::len(embedding) > 0 GROUP ALL"
 82 |                 )
 83 |             else:
 84 |                 result = await repo_query(
 85 |                     "SELECT VALUE count() as count FROM source_insight GROUP ALL"
 86 |                 )
 87 | 
 88 |             if result and isinstance(result[0], dict):
 89 |                 total_estimate += result[0].get("count", 0)
 90 |             elif result:
 91 |                 total_estimate += result[0] if isinstance(result[0], int) else 0
 92 | 
 93 |         logger.info(f"Estimated {total_estimate} items to process")
 94 | 
 95 |         # Submit command
 96 |         command_id = await CommandService.submit_command_job(
 97 |             "open_notebook",
 98 |             "rebuild_embeddings",
 99 |             {
100 |                 "mode": request.mode,
101 |                 "include_sources": request.include_sources,
102 |                 "include_notes": request.include_notes,
103 |                 "include_insights": request.include_insights,
104 |             },
105 |         )
106 | 
107 |         logger.info(f"Submitted rebuild command: {command_id}")
108 | 
109 |         return RebuildResponse(
110 |             command_id=command_id,
111 |             total_items=total_estimate,
112 |             message=f"Rebuild operation started. Estimated {total_estimate} items to process.",
113 |         )
114 | 
115 |     except Exception as e:
116 |         logger.error(f"Failed to start rebuild: {e}")
117 |         logger.exception(e)
118 |         raise HTTPException(
119 |             status_code=500, detail=f"Failed to start rebuild operation: {str(e)}"
120 |         )
121 | 
122 | 
123 | @router.get("/rebuild/{command_id}/status", response_model=RebuildStatusResponse)
124 | async def get_rebuild_status(command_id: str):
125 |     """
126 |     Get the status of a rebuild operation.
127 | 
128 |     Returns:
129 |     - **status**: queued, running, completed, failed
130 |     - **progress**: processed count, total count, percentage
131 |     - **stats**: breakdown by type (sources, notes, insights, failed)
132 |     - **timestamps**: started_at, completed_at
133 |     """
134 |     try:
135 |         # Get command status from surreal_commands
136 |         status = await get_command_status(command_id)
137 | 
138 |         if not status:
139 |             raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Rebuild command not found")
140 | 
141 |         # Build response based on status
142 |         response = RebuildStatusResponse(
143 |             command_id=command_id,
144 |             status=status.status,
145 |         )
146 | 
147 |         # Extract metadata from command result
148 |         if status.result and isinstance(status.result, dict):
149 |             result = status.result
150 | 
151 |             # Build progress info
152 |             if "total_items" in result and "jobs_submitted" in result:
153 |                 total = result["total_items"]
154 |                 submitted = result["jobs_submitted"]
155 |                 response.progress = RebuildProgress(
156 |                     processed=submitted,
157 |                     total=total,
158 |                     percentage=round((submitted / total * 100) if total > 0 else 0, 2),
159 |                 )
160 | 
161 |             # Build stats
162 |             response.stats = RebuildStats(
163 |                 sources=result.get("sources_submitted", 0),
164 |                 notes=result.get("notes_submitted", 0),
165 |                 insights=result.get("insights_submitted", 0),
166 |                 failed=result.get("failed_submissions", 0),
167 |             )
168 | 
169 |         # Add timestamps
170 |         if hasattr(status, "created") and status.created:
171 |             response.started_at = str(status.created)
172 |         if hasattr(status, "updated") and status.updated:
173 |             response.completed_at = str(status.updated)
174 | 
175 |         # Add error message if failed
176 |         if (
177 |             status.status == "failed"
178 |             and status.result
179 |             and isinstance(status.result, dict)
180 |         ):
181 |             response.error_message = status.result.get("error_message", "Unknown error")
182 | 
183 |         return response
184 | 
185 |     except HTTPException:
186 |         raise
187 |     except Exception as e:
188 |         logger.error(f"Failed to get rebuild status: {e}")
189 |         logger.exception(e)
190 |         raise HTTPException(
191 |             status_code=500, detail=f"Failed to get rebuild status: {str(e)}"
192 |         )
193 |

190 | 	@pgrep -f "surreal-commands-worker" >/dev/null && echo "  ✅ Running" || echo "  ❌ Not running"
191 | 	@echo "Next.js Frontend:"
192 | 	@pgrep -f "next dev" >/dev/null && echo "  ✅ Running" || echo "  ❌ Not running"
193 | 
194 | # === Documentation Export ===
195 | export-docs:
196 | 	@echo "📚 Exporting documentation..."
197 | 	@uv run python scripts/export_docs.py
198 | 	@echo "✅ Documentation export complete!"
199 | 
200 | # === Cleanup ===
201 | clean-cache:
202 | 	@echo "🧹 Cleaning cache directories..."
203 | 	@find . -name "__pycache__" -type d -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
204 | 	@find . -name ".mypy_cache" -type d -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
205 | 	@find . -name ".ruff_cache" -type d -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
206 | 	@find . -name ".pytest_cache" -type d -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
207 | 	@find . -name "*.pyc" -type f -delete 2>/dev/null || true
208 | 	@find . -name "*.pyo" -type f -delete 2>/dev/null || true
209 | 	@find . -name "*.pyd" -type f -delete 2>/dev/null || true
210 | 	@echo "✅ Cache directories cleaned!"

/docs/3-USER-GUIDE/citations.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Citations - Verify and Trust AI Responses
  2 | 
  3 | Citations connect AI responses to your source materials. This guide covers how to use and verify them.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## Why Citations Matter
  8 | 
  9 | Every AI-generated response in Open Notebook includes citations to your sources. This lets you:
 10 | 
 11 | - **Verify claims** - Check that AI actually read what it claims
 12 | - **Find original context** - See the full passage around a quote
 13 | - **Catch hallucinations** - Spot when AI makes things up
 14 | - **Build credibility** - Your notes have traceable sources
 15 | 
 16 | ---
 17 | 
 18 | ## Quick Start: Using Citations
 19 | 
 20 | ### Reading Citations
 21 | 
 22 | ```
 23 | AI Response:
 24 | "The study found a 95% accuracy rate [1] using the proposed method."
 25 | 
 26 | [1] = Click to see source
 27 | 
 28 | What happens when you click:
 29 | → Opens the source document
 30 | → Highlights the relevant section
 31 | → You can verify the claim
 32 | ```
 33 | 
 34 | ### Requesting Better Citations
 35 | 
 36 | If a response lacks citations, ask:
 37 | 
 38 | ```
 39 | "Please cite the specific page or section for that claim."
 40 | "Where in the document does it say that?"
 41 | "Can you quote the exact text?"
 42 | ```
 43 | 
 44 | ---
 45 | 
 46 | ## How Citations Work
 47 | 
 48 | ### Automatic Generation
 49 | 
 50 | When AI references your sources, citations are generated automatically:
 51 | 
 52 | ```
 53 | 1. AI analyzes your question
 54 | 2. Retrieves relevant source chunks
 55 | 3. Generates response with inline citations
 56 | 4. Links citations to original source locations
 57 | ```
 58 | 
 59 | ### Citation Format
 60 | 
 61 | ```
 62 | Inline format:
 63 | "The researchers concluded X [1] and Y [2]."
 64 | 
 65 | Reference list:
 66 | [1] Paper Title - Section 3.2
 67 | [2] Report Name - Page 15
 68 | 
 69 | Clickable: Each [number] links to the source
 70 | ```
 71 | 
 72 | ---
 73 | 
 74 | ## Verifying Citations
 75 | 
 76 | ### The Verification Workflow
 77 | 
 78 | ```
 79 | Step 1: Read AI response
 80 |         "The model achieved 95% accuracy [1]"
 81 | 
 82 | Step 2: Click citation [1]
 83 |         → Opens source document
 84 |         → Shows relevant passage
 85 | 
 86 | Step 3: Verify the claim
 87 |         Does source actually say 95%?
 88 |         Is context correct?
 89 |         Any nuance missed?
 90 | 
 91 | Step 4: Trust or correct
 92 |         ✓ Accurate → Use the insight
 93 |         ✗ Wrong → Ask AI to correct
 94 | ```
 95 | 
 96 | ### What to Check
 97 | 
 98 | | Check | Why |
 99 | |-------|-----|
100 | | **Exact numbers** | AI sometimes rounds or misremembers |
101 | | **Context** | Quote might mean something different in context |
102 | | **Attribution** | Is this the source's claim or someone they cited? |
103 | | **Completeness** | Did AI miss important caveats? |
104 | 
105 | ---
106 | 
107 | ## Citations in Different Features
108 | 
109 | ### Chat Citations
110 | 
111 | ```
112 | Context: Sources you selected
113 | Citations: Reference chunks used in response
114 | Verification: Click to see original text
115 | Save: Citations preserved when saving as note
116 | ```
117 | 
118 | ### Ask Feature Citations
119 | 
120 | ```
121 | Context: Auto-searched across all sources
122 | Citations: Multiple sources synthesized
123 | Verification: Each source linked separately
124 | Quality: Often more comprehensive than Chat
125 | ```
126 | 
127 | ### Transformation Citations
128 | 
129 | ```
130 | Context: Single source being transformed
131 | Citations: Points back to original document
132 | Verification: Compare output to source
133 | Use: When you need structured extraction
134 | ```
135 | 
136 | ---
137 | 
138 | ## Saving Citations
139 | 
140 | ### In Notes
141 | 
142 | When you save an AI response as a note, citations are preserved:
143 | 
144 | ```
145 | Original response:
146 | "According to the paper [1], the method works by..."
147 | 
148 | Saved note includes:
149 | - The text
150 | - The citation link
151 | - Reference to source document
152 | ```
153 | 
154 | ### Exporting
155 | 
156 | Citations work in exports:
157 | 
158 | | Format | Citation Behavior |
159 | |--------|-------------------|
160 | | **Markdown** | Links preserved as `[text](link)` |
161 | | **Copy/Paste** | Plain text with reference numbers |
162 | | **PDF** | Clickable references (if supported) |
163 | 
164 | ---
165 | 
166 | ## Citation Quality Tips
167 | 
168 | ### Get Better Citations
169 | 
170 | **Be specific in questions:**
171 | ```
172 | Poor: "What does it say about X?"
173 | Good: "What does page 15 say about X? Please quote directly."
174 | ```
175 | 
176 | **Request citation format:**
177 | ```
178 | "Include page numbers for each claim."
179 | "Cite specific sections, not just document names."
180 | ```
181 | 
182 | **Use Full Content context:**
183 | ```
184 | Summary Only → Less precise citations
185 | Full Content → Exact quotes possible
186 | ```
187 | 
188 | ### When Citations Are Missing
189 | 
190 | | Situation | Cause | Solution |
191 | |-----------|-------|----------|
192 | | No citations | AI used general knowledge | Ask: "Base your answer only on my sources" |
193 | | Vague citations | Source not in Full Content | Change context level |
194 | | Wrong citations | AI confused sources | Ask to verify with quotes |
195 | 
196 | ---
197 | 
198 | ## Common Issues
199 | 
200 | ### "Citation doesn't match claim"
201 | 
202 | ```
203 | Problem: AI says X, but source says Y
204 | 
205 | What happened:
206 | - AI paraphrased incorrectly
207 | - AI combined multiple sources confusingly
208 | - Source was taken out of context
209 | 
210 | Solution:
211 | 1. Click citation to see original
212 | 2. Note the discrepancy
213 | 3. Ask AI: "The source says Y, not X. Please correct."
214 | ```
215 | 
216 | ### "Can't find cited section"
217 | 
218 | ```
219 | Problem: Citation link doesn't show relevant text
220 | 
221 | What happened:
222 | - Source was chunked differently than expected
223 | - Information spread across multiple sections
224 | - Processing missed some content
225 | 
226 | Solution:
227 | 1. Search within source for key terms
228 | 2. Ask AI for more specific location
229 | 3. Re-process source if needed
230 | ```
231 | 
232 | ### "No citations at all"
233 | 
234 | ```
235 | Problem: AI response has no source references
236 | 
237 | What happened:
238 | - Sources not in context
239 | - Question asked for opinion/general knowledge
240 | - Model didn't find relevant content
241 | 
242 | Solution:
243 | 1. Check context settings
244 | 2. Rephrase: "Based on my sources, what..."
245 | 3. Add more relevant sources
246 | ```
247 | 
248 | ---
249 | 
250 | ## Best Practices
251 | 
252 | ### For Research Integrity
253 | 
254 | 1. **Always verify important claims** - Don't trust AI blindly
255 | 2. **Check context** - Quotes can be misleading out of context
256 | 3. **Note limitations** - AI might miss nuance
257 | 4. **Keep source access** - Don't delete sources you cite
258 | 
259 | ### For Academic Work
260 | 
261 | 1. **Use Full Content** for documents you'll cite
262 | 2. **Request specific page numbers**
263 | 3. **Cross-check with original sources**
264 | 4. **Document your verification process**
265 | 
266 | ### For Professional Use
267 | 
268 | 1. **Verify before sharing** - Check claims clients will see
269 | 2. **Keep citation trail** - Save notes with sources linked
270 | 3. **Be transparent** - Note when insights are AI-assisted
271 | 
272 | ---
273 | 
274 | ## Summary
275 | 
276 | ```
277 | Citations = Your verification system
278 | 
279 | How to use:
280 | 1. Read AI response
281 | 2. Note citation markers [1], [2], etc.
282 | 3. Click to see original source
283 | 4. Verify claim matches source
284 | 5. Trust verified insights
285 | 
286 | When citations fail:
287 | - Ask for specific quotes
288 | - Change to Full Content
289 | - Request page numbers
290 | - Verify manually
291 | 
292 | Why it matters:
293 | - AI can hallucinate
294 | - Context can change meaning
295 | - Trust requires verification
296 | - Good research needs sources
297 | ```
298 | 
299 | Citations aren't just references — they're your quality control. Use them to build research you can trust.
300 |

 74 | DEFINE FUNCTION IF NOT EXISTS fn::text_search($query_text: string, $match_count: int, $sources:bool, $show_notes:bool) {
 75 |   
 76 |     let $source_title_search = 
 77 |         IF $sources {(
 78 |             SELECT id as item_id, math::max(search::score(1)) AS relevance
 79 |             FROM source
 80 |             WHERE title @1@ $query_text
 81 |             GROUP BY item_id)}
 82 |         ELSE { [] };
 83 |     
 84 |     let $source_embedding_search = 
 85 |          IF $sources {(
 86 |              SELECT source as item_id, math::max(search::score(1)) AS relevance
 87 |             FROM source_embedding
 88 |             WHERE content @1@ $query_text
 89 |             GROUP BY item_id)}
 90 |         ELSE { [] };
 91 | 
 92 |     let $source_full_search = 
 93 |          IF $sources {(
 94 |             SELECT source as item_id, math::max(search::score(1)) AS relevance
 95 |             FROM source
 96 |             WHERE full_text @1@ $query_text
 97 |             GROUP BY item_id)}
 98 |         ELSE { [] };
 99 |     
100 |     let $source_insight_search = 
101 |          IF $sources {(
102 |              SELECT source as item_id, math::max(search::score(1)) AS relevance
103 |             FROM source_insight
104 |             WHERE content @1@ $query_text
105 |             GROUP BY item_id)}
106 |         ELSE { [] };
107 | 
108 |     let $note_title_search = 
109 |          IF $show_notes {(
110 |              SELECT id as item_id, math::max(search::score(1)) AS relevance
111 |             FROM note
112 |             WHERE title @1@ $query_text
113 |             GROUP BY item_id)}
114 |         ELSE { [] };
115 | 
116 |      let $note_content_search = 
117 |          IF $show_notes {(
118 |              SELECT id as item_id, math::max(search::score(1)) AS relevance
119 |             FROM note
120 |             WHERE content @1@ $query_text
121 |             GROUP BY item_id)}
122 |         ELSE { [] };
123 | 
124 |     let $source_chunk_results = array::union($source_embedding_search, $source_full_search);
125 |     
126 |     let $source_asset_results = array::union($source_title_search, $source_insight_search);
127 | 
128 |     let $source_results = array::union($source_chunk_results, $source_asset_results );
129 |     let $note_results = array::union($note_title_search, $note_content_search );
130 |     let $final_results = array::union($source_results, $note_results );
131 | 
132 |     RETURN (SELECT item_id, math::max(relevance) as relevance from $final_results
133 |         group by item_id ORDER BY relevance DESC LIMIT $match_count);
134 |     
135 |     
136 | };
137 | 
138 | 
139 | DEFINE FUNCTION IF NOT EXISTS fn::vector_search($query: array<float>, $match_count: int, $sources:bool, $show_notes:bool) {
140 |    
141 |     let $source_embedding_search = 
142 |          IF $sources {(
143 |             SELECT source as item_id, content, vector::similarity::cosine(embedding, $query) as similarity
144 |             FROM source_embedding LIMIT $match_count)}
145 |         ELSE { [] };
146 | 
147 |     
148 |     let $source_insight_search = 
149 |          IF $sources {(
150 |              SELECT source as item_id, content, vector::similarity::cosine(embedding, $query) as similarity
151 |                 FROM source_insight LIMIT $match_count)}
152 |         ELSE { [] };
153 | 
154 |     
155 |      let $note_content_search = 
156 |          IF $show_notes {(
157 |                 SELECT id as item_id, content, vector::similarity::cosine(embedding, $query) as similarity
158 |                 FROM note LIMIT $match_count)}
159 | 
160 |         ELSE { [] };
161 | 
162 |     let $source_chunk_results = array::union($source_embedding_search, $source_insight_search);
163 |     
164 |     let $source_results = array::union($source_chunk_results, $source_insight_search);
165 | 
166 |     let $note_results = $note_content_search;
167 |     let $final_results = array::union($source_results, $note_results );
168 | 
169 |     RETURN (SELECT item_id, math::max(similarity) as similarity from $final_results
170 |         group by item_id ORDER BY similarity DESC LIMIT $match_count);
171 |     
172 |     
173 | };
