/docs/7-DEVELOPMENT/contributing.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Contributing to Open Notebook
  2 | 
  3 | Thank you for your interest in contributing to Open Notebook! We welcome contributions from developers of all skill levels. This guide will help you understand our contribution workflow and what makes a good contribution.
  4 | 
  5 | ## 🚨 Issue-First Workflow
  6 | 
  7 | **To maintain project coherence and avoid wasted effort, please follow this process:**
  8 | 
  9 | 1. **Create an issue first** - Before writing any code, create an issue describing the bug or feature
 10 | 2. **Propose your solution** - Explain how you plan to implement the fix or feature
 11 | 3. **Wait for assignment** - A maintainer will review and assign the issue to you if approved
 12 | 4. **Only then start coding** - This ensures your work aligns with the project's vision and architecture
 13 | 
 14 | **Why this process?**
 15 | - Prevents duplicate work
 16 | - Ensures solutions align with our architecture and design principles
 17 | - Saves your time by getting feedback before coding
 18 | - Helps maintainers manage the project direction
 19 | 
 20 | > ⚠️ **Pull requests without an assigned issue may be closed**, even if the code is good. We want to respect your time by making sure work is aligned before it starts.
 21 | 
 22 | ## Code of Conduct
 23 | 
 24 | By participating in this project, you are expected to uphold our Code of Conduct. Be respectful, constructive, and collaborative.
 25 | 
 26 | ## How Can I Contribute?
 27 | 
 28 | ### Reporting Bugs
 29 | 
 30 | 1. **Search existing issues** - Check if the bug was already reported
 31 | 2. **Create a bug report** - Use the [Bug Report template](https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml)
 32 | 3. **Provide details** - Include:
 33 |    - Steps to reproduce
 34 |    - Expected vs actual behavior
 35 |    - Logs, screenshots, or error messages
 36 |    - Your environment (OS, Docker version, Open Notebook version)
 37 | 4. **Indicate if you want to fix it** - Check the "I would like to work on this" box if you're interested
 38 | 
 39 | ### Suggesting Features
 40 | 
 41 | 1. **Search existing issues** - Check if the feature was already suggested
 42 | 2. **Create a feature request** - Use the [Feature Request template](https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml)
 43 | 3. **Explain the value** - Describe why this feature would be helpful
 44 | 4. **Propose implementation** - If you have ideas on how to implement it, share them
 45 | 5. **Indicate if you want to build it** - Check the "I would like to work on this" box if you're interested
 46 | 
 47 | ### Contributing Code (Pull Requests)
 48 | 
 49 | **IMPORTANT: Follow the issue-first workflow above before starting any PR**
 50 | 
 51 | Once your issue is assigned:
 52 | 
 53 | 1. **Fork the repo** and create your branch from `main`
 54 | 2. **Understand our vision and principles** - Read [design-principles.md](design-principles.md) to understand what guides our decisions
 55 | 3. **Follow our architecture** - Refer to the architecture documentation to understand project structure
 56 | 4. **Write quality code** - Follow the standards outlined in [code-standards.md](code-standards.md)
 57 | 5. **Test your changes** - See [testing.md](testing.md) for test guidelines
 58 | 6. **Update documentation** - If you changed functionality, update the relevant docs
 59 | 7. **Create your PR**:
 60 |    - Reference the issue number (e.g., "Fixes #123")
 61 |    - Describe what changed and why
 62 |    - Include screenshots for UI changes
 63 |    - Keep PRs focused - one issue per PR
 64 | 
 65 | ### What Makes a Good Contribution?
 66 | 
 67 | ✅ **We love PRs that:**
 68 | - Solve a real problem described in an issue
 69 | - Follow our architecture and coding standards
 70 | - Include tests and documentation
 71 | - Are well-scoped (focused on one thing)
 72 | - Have clear commit messages
 73 | 
 74 | ❌ **We may close PRs that:**
 75 | - Don't have an associated approved issue
 76 | - Introduce breaking changes without discussion
 77 | - Conflict with our architectural vision
 78 | - Lack tests or documentation
 79 | - Try to solve multiple unrelated problems
 80 | 
 81 | ## Git Commit Messages
 82 | 
 83 | - Use the present tense ("Add feature" not "Added feature")
 84 | - Use the imperative mood ("Move cursor to..." not "Moves cursor to...")
 85 | - Limit the first line to 72 characters or less
 86 | - Reference issues and pull requests liberally after the first line
 87 | 
 88 | ## Development Workflow
 89 | 
 90 | ### Branch Strategy
 91 | 
 92 | We use a **feature branch workflow**:
 93 | 
 94 | 1. **Main Branch**: `main` - production-ready code
 95 | 2. **Feature Branches**: `feature/description` - new features
 96 | 3. **Bug Fixes**: `fix/description` - bug fixes
 97 | 4. **Documentation**: `docs/description` - documentation updates
 98 | 
 99 | ### Making Changes
100 | 
101 | 1. **Create a feature branch**:
102 | ```bash
103 | git checkout -b feature/amazing-new-feature
104 | ```
105 | 
106 | 2. **Make your changes** following our coding standards
107 | 
108 | 3. **Test your changes**:
109 | ```bash
110 | # Run tests
111 | uv run pytest
112 | 
113 | # Run linting
114 | uv run ruff check .
115 | 
116 | # Run formatting
117 | uv run ruff format .
118 | ```
119 | 
120 | 4. **Commit your changes**:
121 | ```bash
122 | git add .
123 | git commit -m "feat: add amazing new feature"
124 | ```
125 | 
126 | 5. **Push and create PR**:
127 | ```bash
128 | git push origin feature/amazing-new-feature
129 | # Then create a Pull Request on GitHub
130 | ```
131 | 
132 | ### Keeping Your Fork Updated
133 | 
134 | ```bash
135 | # Fetch upstream changes
136 | git fetch upstream
137 | 
138 | # Switch to main and merge
139 | git checkout main
140 | git merge upstream/main
141 | 
142 | # Push to your fork
143 | git push origin main
144 | ```
145 | 
146 | ## Pull Request Process
147 | 
148 | When you create a pull request:
149 | 
150 | 1. **Link your issue** - Reference the issue number in PR description
151 | 2. **Describe your changes** - Explain what changed and why
152 | 3. **Provide test evidence** - Screenshots, test results, or logs
153 | 4. **Check PR template** - Ensure you've completed all required sections
154 | 5. **Wait for review** - A maintainer will review your PR within a week
155 | 
156 | ### PR Review Expectations
157 | 
158 | - Code review feedback is about the code, not the person
159 | - Be open to suggestions and alternative approaches
160 | - Address review comments with clarity and respect
161 | - Ask questions if feedback is unclear
162 | 
163 | ## Current Priority Areas
164 | 
165 | We're actively looking for contributions in these areas:
166 | 
167 | 1. **Frontend Enhancement** - Help improve the Next.js/React UI with real-time updates and better UX
168 | 2. **Testing** - Expand test coverage across all components
169 | 3. **Performance** - Async processing improvements and caching
170 | 4. **Documentation** - API examples and user guides
171 | 5. **Integrations** - New content sources and AI providers
172 | 
173 | ## Getting Help
174 | 
175 | ### Community Support
176 | 
177 | - **Discord**: [Join our Discord server](https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w) for real-time help
178 | - **GitHub Discussions**: For longer-form questions and ideas
179 | - **GitHub Issues**: For bug reports and feature requests
180 | 
181 | ### Documentation References
182 | 
183 | - [Design Principles](design-principles.md) - Understanding our project vision
184 | - [Code Standards](code-standards.md) - Coding guidelines by language
185 | - [Testing Guide](testing.md) - How to write tests
186 | - [Development Setup](development-setup.md) - Getting started locally
187 | 
188 | ## Recognition
189 | 
190 | We recognize contributions through:
191 | 
192 | - **GitHub credits** on releases
193 | - **Community recognition** in Discord
194 | - **Contribution statistics** in project analytics
195 | - **Maintainer consideration** for active contributors
196 | 
197 | ---
198 | 
199 | Thank you for contributing to Open Notebook! Your contributions help make research more accessible and private for everyone.
200 | 
201 | For questions about this guide or contributing in general, please reach out on [Discord](https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w) or open a GitHub Discussion.
202 |

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | 'use client'
  2 | 
  3 | import { useState, useEffect, useMemo } from 'react'
  4 | import { LoaderIcon, BookOpen, Check } from 'lucide-react'
  5 | import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
  6 | import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
  7 | import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/checkbox'
  8 | import { ScrollArea } from '@/components/ui/scroll-area'
  9 | import { useNotebooks } from '@/lib/hooks/use-notebooks'
 10 | import { useAddSourcesToNotebook, useRemoveSourceFromNotebook } from '@/lib/hooks/use-sources'
 11 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
 12 | 
 13 | interface NotebookAssociationsProps {
 14 |   sourceId: string
 15 |   currentNotebookIds: string[]
 16 |   onSave?: () => void
 17 | }
 18 | 
 19 | export function NotebookAssociations({
 20 |   sourceId,
 21 |   currentNotebookIds,
 22 |   onSave,
 23 | }: NotebookAssociationsProps) {
 24 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 25 |   const [selectedNotebookIds, setSelectedNotebookIds] = useState<string[]>(currentNotebookIds)
 26 |   const [isSaving, setIsSaving] = useState(false)
 27 | 
 28 |   const { data: notebooks, isLoading } = useNotebooks()
 29 |   const addSources = useAddSourcesToNotebook()
 30 |   const removeFromNotebook = useRemoveSourceFromNotebook()
 31 | 
 32 |   // Update selected notebooks when current changes (after save)
 33 |   useEffect(() => {
 34 |     setSelectedNotebookIds(currentNotebookIds)
 35 |   }, [currentNotebookIds])
 36 | 
 37 |   const hasChanges = useMemo(() => {
 38 |     const current = new Set(currentNotebookIds)
 39 |     const selected = new Set(selectedNotebookIds)
 40 | 
 41 |     if (current.size !== selected.size) return true
 42 | 
 43 |     for (const id of current) {
 44 |       if (!selected.has(id)) return true
 45 |     }
 46 | 
 47 |     return false
 48 |   }, [currentNotebookIds, selectedNotebookIds])
 49 | 
 50 |   const handleToggleNotebook = (notebookId: string) => {
 51 |     setSelectedNotebookIds(prev =>
 52 |       prev.includes(notebookId)
 53 |         ? prev.filter(id => id !== notebookId)
 54 |         : [...prev, notebookId]
 55 |     )
 56 |   }
 57 | 
 58 |   const handleSave = async () => {
 59 |     if (!hasChanges) return
 60 | 
 61 |     try {
 62 |       setIsSaving(true)
 63 | 
 64 |       const current = new Set(currentNotebookIds)
 65 |       const selected = new Set(selectedNotebookIds)
 66 | 
 67 |       // Determine which notebooks to add and remove
 68 |       const toAdd = selectedNotebookIds.filter(id => !current.has(id))
 69 |       const toRemove = currentNotebookIds.filter(id => !selected.has(id))
 70 | 
 71 |       // Execute additions
 72 |       if (toAdd.length > 0) {
 73 |         await Promise.allSettled(
 74 |           toAdd.map(notebookId =>
 75 |             addSources.mutateAsync({
 76 |               notebookId,
 77 |               sourceIds: [sourceId],
 78 |             })
 79 |           )
 80 |         )
 81 |       }
 82 | 
 83 |       // Execute removals
 84 |       if (toRemove.length > 0) {
 85 |         await Promise.allSettled(
 86 |           toRemove.map(notebookId =>
 87 |             removeFromNotebook.mutateAsync({
 88 |               notebookId,
 89 |               sourceId,
 90 |             })
 91 |           )
 92 |         )
 93 |       }
 94 | 
 95 |       onSave?.()
 96 |     } catch (error) {
 97 |       console.error('Error saving notebook associations:', error)
 98 |     } finally {
 99 |       setIsSaving(false)
100 |     }
101 |   }
102 | 
103 |   const handleCancel = () => {
104 |     setSelectedNotebookIds(currentNotebookIds)
105 |   }
106 | 
107 |   if (isLoading) {
108 |     return (
109 |       <Card>
110 |         <CardHeader>
111 |           <CardTitle className="flex items-center gap-2">
112 |             <BookOpen className="h-5 w-5" />
113 |             {t.sources.manageNotebooks}
114 |           </CardTitle>
115 |           <CardDescription>
116 |             {t.sources.manageNotebooksDesc}
117 |           </CardDescription>
118 |         </CardHeader>
119 |         <CardContent>
120 |           <div className="flex items-center justify-center py-8">
121 |             <LoaderIcon className="h-6 w-6 animate-spin text-muted-foreground" />
122 |           </div>
123 |         </CardContent>
124 |       </Card>
125 |     )
126 |   }
127 | 
128 |   if (!notebooks || notebooks.length === 0) {
129 |     return (
130 |       <Card>
131 |         <CardHeader>
132 |           <CardTitle className="flex items-center gap-2">
133 |             <BookOpen className="h-5 w-5" />
134 |             {t.sources.manageNotebooks}
135 |           </CardTitle>
136 |           <CardDescription>
137 |             {t.sources.manageNotebooksDesc}
138 |           </CardDescription>
139 |         </CardHeader>
140 |         <CardContent>
141 |           <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{t.sources.noNotebooksAvailable}</p>
142 |         </CardContent>
143 |       </Card>
144 |     )
145 |   }
146 | 
147 |   return (
148 |     <Card>
149 |       <CardHeader>
150 |         <CardTitle className="flex items-center gap-2">
151 |           <BookOpen className="h-5 w-5" />
152 |           {t.sources.manageNotebooks}
153 |         </CardTitle>
154 |         <CardDescription>
155 |           {t.sources.manageNotebooksDesc}
156 |         </CardDescription>
157 |       </CardHeader>
158 |       <CardContent className="space-y-4">
159 |         <ScrollArea className="h-[300px] border rounded-md p-4">
160 |           <div className="space-y-3">
161 |             {notebooks
162 |               .filter(nb => !nb.archived)
163 |               .map((notebook) => {
164 |                 const isSelected = selectedNotebookIds.includes(notebook.id)
165 |                 const isCurrentlyLinked = currentNotebookIds.includes(notebook.id)
166 | 
167 |                 return (
168 |                   <div
169 |                     key={notebook.id}
170 |                     className={`flex items-start gap-3 p-3 rounded-lg border transition-colors ${
171 |                       isSelected ? 'bg-accent border-accent-foreground/20' : 'hover:bg-accent/50'
172 |                     }`}
173 |                   >
174 |                     <Checkbox
175 |                       checked={isSelected}
176 |                       onCheckedChange={() => handleToggleNotebook(notebook.id)}
177 |                       className="mt-0.5"
178 |                     />
179 |                     <div className="flex-1 min-w-0">
180 |                       <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
181 |                         <h4 className="font-medium text-sm truncate">
182 |                           {notebook.name}
183 |                         </h4>
184 |                         {isCurrentlyLinked && !hasChanges && (
185 |                           <Check className="h-4 w-4 text-green-600" />
186 |                         )}
187 |                       </div>
188 |                       {notebook.description && (
189 |                         <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground line-clamp-1">
190 |                           {notebook.description}
191 |                         </p>
192 |                       )}
193 |                     </div>
194 |                   </div>
195 |                 )
196 |               })}
197 |           </div>
198 |         </ScrollArea>
199 | 
200 |         {hasChanges && (
201 |           <div className="flex items-center justify-end gap-2 pt-2 border-t">
202 |             <Button
203 |               variant="outline"
204 |               size="sm"
205 |               onClick={handleCancel}
206 |               disabled={isSaving}
207 |             >
208 |               {t.common.cancel}
209 |             </Button>
210 |             <Button
211 |               size="sm"
212 |               onClick={handleSave}
213 |               disabled={isSaving}
214 |             >
215 |               {isSaving ? (
216 |                 <>
217 |                   <LoaderIcon className="mr-2 h-4 w-4 animate-spin" />
218 |                   {t.common.saving}...
219 |                 </>
220 |               ) : (
221 |                 t.common.saveChanges
222 |               )}
223 |             </Button>
224 |           </div>
225 |         )}
226 |       </CardContent>
227 |     </Card>
228 |   )
229 | }
230 |

/docs/6-TROUBLESHOOTING/index.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Troubleshooting - Problem Solving Guide
  2 | 
  3 | Having issues? Use this guide to diagnose and fix problems.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## How to Use This Guide
  8 | 
  9 | **Step 1: Identify your problem**
 10 | - What's the symptom? (error message, behavior, something not working?)
 11 | - When did it happen? (during install, while using, after update?)
 12 | 
 13 | **Step 2: Find the right guide**
 14 | - Look below for your symptom
 15 | - Go to the specific troubleshooting guide
 16 | 
 17 | **Step 3: Follow the steps**
 18 | - Guides are organized by symptom, not by root cause
 19 | - Each has diagnostic steps and solutions
 20 | 
 21 | ---
 22 | 
 23 | ## Quick Problem Map
 24 | 
 25 | ### During Installation
 26 | 
 27 | - **Docker won't start** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#9-services-wont-start-or-docker-error)
 28 | - **Port already in use** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#3-port-x-already-in-use)
 29 | - **Permission denied** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#9-services-wont-start-or-docker-error)
 30 | - **Can't connect to database** → [Connection Issues](connection-issues.md)
 31 | 
 32 | ### When Starting
 33 | 
 34 | - **API won't start** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#9-services-wont-start-or-docker-error)
 35 | - **Frontend won't load** → [Connection Issues](connection-issues.md)
 36 | - **"Cannot connect to server" error** → [Connection Issues](connection-issues.md)
 37 | 
 38 | ### Settings / Configuration
 39 | 
 40 | - **Models not showing** → [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md)
 41 | - **"Invalid API key"** → [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md)
 42 | - **Can't find Settings** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md)
 43 | 
 44 | ### Using Features
 45 | 
 46 | - **Chat not working** → [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md)
 47 | - **Chat responses are slow** → [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md)
 48 | - **Chat gives bad answers** → [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md)
 49 | 
 50 | ### Adding Content
 51 | 
 52 | - **Can't upload PDF** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#4-cannot-process-file-or-unsupported-format)
 53 | - **File won't process** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#4-cannot-process-file-or-unsupported-format)
 54 | - **Web link won't extract** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#4-cannot-process-file-or-unsupported-format)
 55 | 
 56 | ### Search
 57 | 
 58 | - **Search returns no results** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#7-search-returns-nothing)
 59 | - **Search returns wrong results** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#7-search-returns-nothing)
 60 | 
 61 | ### Podcasts
 62 | 
 63 | - **Can't generate podcast** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#8-podcast-generation-failed)
 64 | - **Podcast audio is robotic** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#8-podcast-generation-failed)
 65 | - **Podcast generation times out** → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#8-podcast-generation-failed)
 66 | 
 67 | ---
 68 | 
 69 | ## Troubleshooting by Error Message
 70 | 
 71 | ### "Cannot connect to server"
 72 | → [Connection Issues](connection-issues.md) — Frontend can't reach API
 73 | 
 74 | ### "Invalid API key"
 75 | → [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md) — Wrong or missing API key
 76 | 
 77 | ### "Models not available"
 78 | → [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md) — Model not configured
 79 | 
 80 | ### "Connection refused"
 81 | → [Connection Issues](connection-issues.md) — Service not running or port wrong
 82 | 
 83 | ### "Port already in use"
 84 | → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#3-port-x-already-in-use) — Port conflict
 85 | 
 86 | ### "Permission denied"
 87 | → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#9-services-wont-start-or-docker-error) — File permissions issue
 88 | 
 89 | ### "Unsupported file type"
 90 | → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#4-cannot-process-file-or-unsupported-format) — File format not supported
 91 | 
 92 | ### "Processing timeout"
 93 | → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#5-chat-is-very-slow) — File too large or slow processing
 94 | 
 95 | ---
 96 | 
 97 | ## Troubleshooting by Component
 98 | 
 99 | ### Frontend (Browser/UI)
100 | - Can't access UI → [Connection Issues](connection-issues.md)
101 | - UI is slow → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md)
102 | - Button/feature missing → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md)
103 | 
104 | ### API (Backend)
105 | - API won't start → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#9-services-wont-start-or-docker-error)
106 | - API errors in logs → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#9-services-wont-start-or-docker-error)
107 | - API is slow → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md)
108 | 
109 | ### Database
110 | - Can't connect to database → [Connection Issues](connection-issues.md)
111 | - Data lost after restart → [FAQ](faq.md#how-do-i-backup-my-data)
112 | 
113 | ### AI / Chat
114 | - Chat not working → [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md)
115 | - Bad responses → [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md)
116 | - Cost too high → [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md#high-api-costs)
117 | 
118 | ### Sources
119 | - Can't upload file → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#4-cannot-process-file-or-unsupported-format)
120 | - File won't process → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#4-cannot-process-file-or-unsupported-format)
121 | 
122 | ### Podcasts
123 | - Won't generate → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#8-podcast-generation-failed)
124 | - Bad audio quality → [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md#8-podcast-generation-failed)
125 | 
126 | ---
127 | 
128 | ## Diagnostic Checklist
129 | 
130 | **When something isn't working:**
131 | 
132 | - [ ] Check if services are running: `docker ps`
133 | - [ ] Check logs: `docker compose logs api` (or frontend, surrealdb)
134 | - [ ] Verify ports are exposed: `netstat -tlnp` or `lsof -i :5055`
135 | - [ ] Test connectivity: `curl http://localhost:5055/health`
136 | - [ ] Check environment variables: `docker inspect <container>`
137 | - [ ] Try restarting: `docker compose restart`
138 | - [ ] Check firewall/antivirus isn't blocking
139 | 
140 | ---
141 | 
142 | ## Getting Help
143 | 
144 | If you can't find the answer here:
145 | 
146 | 1. **Check the relevant guide** — Read completely, try all steps
147 | 2. **Check the FAQ** — [Frequently Asked Questions](faq.md)
148 | 3. **Search our Discord** — Others may have had same issue
149 | 4. **Check logs** — Most issues show error messages in logs
150 | 5. **Report on GitHub** — Include error message, steps to reproduce
151 | 
152 | ### How to Report an Issue
153 | 
154 | Include:
155 | 1. Error message (exact)
156 | 2. Steps to reproduce
157 | 3. Logs: `docker compose logs`
158 | 4. Your setup: Docker/local, provider, OS
159 | 5. What you've already tried
160 | 
161 | → [Report on GitHub](https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook/issues)
162 | 
163 | ---
164 | 
165 | ## Guides
166 | 
167 | ### [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md)
168 | Top 10 most common issues with 1-minute solutions.
169 | 
170 | ### [Connection Issues](connection-issues.md)
171 | Frontend can't reach API, network problems.
172 | 
173 | ### [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md)
174 | Chat not working, bad responses, slow performance.
175 | 
176 | ### [FAQ](faq.md)
177 | Frequently asked questions about usage, costs, and best practices.
178 | 
179 | ---
180 | 
181 | ## Common Solutions
182 | 
183 | **Service won't start?**
184 | ```bash
185 | # Check logs
186 | docker compose logs
187 | 
188 | # Restart everything
189 | docker compose restart
190 | 
191 | # Nuclear option: rebuild
192 | docker compose down
193 | docker compose up --build
194 | ```
195 | 
196 | **Port conflict?**
197 | ```bash
198 | # Find what's using port 5055
199 | lsof -i :5055
200 | # Kill it or use different port
201 | ```
202 | 
203 | **Can't connect?**
204 | ```bash
205 | # Test API directly
206 | curl http://localhost:5055/health
207 | # Should return: {"status":"ok"}
208 | ```
209 | 
210 | **Slow performance?**
211 | ```bash
212 | # Check resource usage
213 | docker stats
214 | 
215 | # Reduce concurrency in .env
216 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS=2
217 | ```
218 | 
219 | **High costs?**
220 | ```bash
221 | # Switch to cheaper model
222 | # In Settings → Models → Choose gpt-4o-mini (OpenAI)
223 | # Or use Ollama (free)
224 | ```
225 | 
226 | ---
227 | 
228 | ## Still Stuck?
229 | 
230 | **Before asking for help:**
231 | 1. Read the relevant guide completely
232 | 2. Try all the steps
233 | 3. Check the logs
234 | 4. Restart services
235 | 5. Search existing issues on GitHub
236 | 
237 | **Then:**
238 | - **Discord**: https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w (fastest response)
239 | - **GitHub Issues**: https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook/issues
240 |

/docs/0-START-HERE/quick-start-local.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Quick Start - Local & Private (5 minutes)
  2 | 
  3 | Get Open Notebook running with **100% local AI** using Ollama. No cloud API keys needed, completely private.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Prerequisites
  6 | 
  7 | 1. **Docker Desktop** installed
  8 |    - [Download here](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
  9 |    - Already have it? Skip to step 2
 10 | 
 11 | 2. **Local LLM** - Choose one:
 12 |    - **Ollama** (recommended): [Download here](https://ollama.ai/)
 13 |    - **LM Studio** (GUI alternative): [Download here](https://lmstudio.ai)
 14 | 
 15 | ## Step 1: Choose Your Setup (1 min)
 16 | 
 17 | ### 🏠 Local Machine (Same Computer)
 18 | Everything runs on your machine. Recommended for testing/learning.
 19 | 
 20 | ### 🌐 Remote Server (Raspberry Pi, NAS, Cloud VM)
 21 | Run on a different computer, access from another. Needs network configuration.
 22 | 
 23 | ---
 24 | 
 25 | ## Step 2: Create Configuration (1 min)
 26 | 
 27 | Create a new folder `open-notebook-local` and add this file:
 28 | 
 29 | **docker-compose.yml**:
 30 | ```yaml
 31 | services:
 32 |   surrealdb:
 33 |     image: surrealdb/surrealdb:v2
 34 |     command: start --user root --pass password --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 rocksdb:/mydata/mydatabase.db
 35 |     ports:
 36 |       - "8000:8000"
 37 |     volumes:
 38 |       - ./surreal_data:/mydata
 39 | 
 40 |   open_notebook:
 41 |     image: lfnovo/open_notebook:v1-latest-single
 42 |     pull_policy: always
 43 |     ports:
 44 |       - "8502:8502"  # Web UI (React frontend)
 45 |       - "5055:5055"  # API (required!)
 46 |     environment:
 47 |       # NO API KEYS NEEDED - Using Ollama (free, local)
 48 |       - OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://ollama:11434
 49 | 
 50 |       # Database (required)
 51 |       - SURREAL_URL=ws://surrealdb:8000/rpc
 52 |       - SURREAL_USER=root
 53 |       - SURREAL_PASSWORD=password
 54 |       - SURREAL_NAMESPACE=open_notebook
 55 |       - SURREAL_DATABASE=open_notebook
 56 |     volumes:
 57 |       - ./notebook_data:/app/data
 58 |       - ./surreal_data:/mydata
 59 |     depends_on:
 60 |       - surrealdb
 61 |     restart: always
 62 | 
 63 |   ollama:
 64 |     image: ollama/ollama:latest
 65 |     ports:
 66 |       - "11434:11434"
 67 |     volumes:
 68 |       - ./ollama_models:/root/.ollama
 69 |     environment:
 70 |       # Optional: set GPU support if available
 71 |       - OLLAMA_NUM_GPU=0
 72 |     restart: always
 73 | 
 74 | ```
 75 | 
 76 | **That's it!** No API keys, no secrets, completely private.
 77 | 
 78 | ---
 79 | 
 80 | ## Step 3: Start Services (1 min)
 81 | 
 82 | Open terminal in your `open-notebook-local` folder:
 83 | 
 84 | ```bash
 85 | docker compose up -d
 86 | ```
 87 | 
 88 | Wait 10-15 seconds for all services to start.
 89 | 
 90 | ---
 91 | 
 92 | ## Step 4: Download a Model (2-3 min)
 93 | 
 94 | Ollama needs at least one language model. Pick one:
 95 | 
 96 | ```bash
 97 | # Fastest & smallest (recommended for testing)
 98 | docker exec open_notebook-ollama-1 ollama pull mistral
 99 | 
100 | # OR: Better quality but slower
101 | docker exec open_notebook-ollama-1 ollama pull neural-chat
102 | 
103 | # OR: Even better quality, more VRAM needed
104 | docker exec open_notebook-ollama-1 ollama pull llama2
105 | ```
106 | 
107 | This downloads the model (will take 1-5 minutes depending on your internet).
108 | 
109 | ---
110 | 
111 | ## Step 5: Access Open Notebook (instant)
112 | 
113 | Open your browser:
114 | ```
115 | http://localhost:8502
116 | ```
117 | 
118 | You should see the Open Notebook interface.
119 | 
120 | ---
121 | 
122 | ## Step 6: Configure Local Model (1 min)
123 | 
124 | 1. Click **Settings** (top right) → **Models**
125 | 2. Set:
126 |    - **Language Model**: `ollama/mistral` (or whichever model you downloaded)
127 |    - **Embedding Model**: `ollama/nomic-embed-text` (auto-downloads if missing)
128 | 3. Click **Save**
129 | 
130 | ---
131 | 
132 | ## Step 7: Create Your First Notebook (1 min)
133 | 
134 | 1. Click **New Notebook**
135 | 2. Name: "My Private Research"
136 | 3. Click **Create**
137 | 
138 | ---
139 | 
140 | ## Step 8: Add Local Content (1 min)
141 | 
142 | 1. Click **Add Source**
143 | 2. Choose **Text**
144 | 3. Paste some text or a local document
145 | 4. Click **Add**
146 | 
147 | ---
148 | 
149 | ## Step 9: Chat With Your Content (1 min)
150 | 
151 | 1. Go to **Chat**
152 | 2. Type: "What did you learn from this?"
153 | 3. Click **Send**
154 | 4. Watch as the local Ollama model responds!
155 | 
156 | ---
157 | 
158 | ## Verification Checklist
159 | 
160 | - [ ] Docker is running
161 | - [ ] You can access `http://localhost:8502`
162 | - [ ] Models are configured
163 | - [ ] You created a notebook
164 | - [ ] Chat works with local model
165 | 
166 | **All checked?** 🎉 You have a completely **private, offline** research assistant!
167 | 
168 | ---
169 | 
170 | ## Advantages of Local Setup
171 | 
172 | ✅ **No API costs** - Free forever
173 | ✅ **No internet required** - True offline capability
174 | ✅ **Privacy first** - Your data never leaves your machine
175 | ✅ **No subscriptions** - No monthly bills
176 | 
177 | **Trade-off:** Slower than cloud models (depends on your CPU/GPU)
178 | 
179 | ---
180 | 
181 | ## Troubleshooting
182 | 
183 | ### "ollama: command not found"
184 | 
185 | Docker image name might be different:
186 | ```bash
187 | docker ps  # Find the Ollama container name
188 | docker exec <container_name> ollama pull mistral
189 | ```
190 | 
191 | ### Model Download Stuck
192 | 
193 | Check internet connection and restart:
194 | ```bash
195 | docker compose restart ollama
196 | ```
197 | 
198 | Then retry the model pull command.
199 | 
200 | ### "Address already in use" Error
201 | 
202 | ```bash
203 | docker compose down
204 | docker compose up -d
205 | ```
206 | 
207 | ### Low Performance
208 | 
209 | Check if GPU is available:
210 | ```bash
211 | # Show available GPUs
212 | docker exec open_notebook-ollama-1 ollama ps
213 | 
214 | # Enable GPU in docker-compose.yml:
215 | # - OLLAMA_NUM_GPU=1
216 | ```
217 | 
218 | Then restart: `docker compose restart ollama`
219 | 
220 | ### Adding More Models
221 | 
222 | ```bash
223 | # List available models
224 | docker exec open_notebook-ollama-1 ollama list
225 | 
226 | # Pull additional model
227 | docker exec open_notebook-ollama-1 ollama pull neural-chat
228 | ```
229 | 
230 | ---
231 | 
232 | ## Next Steps
233 | 
234 | **Now that it's running:**
235 | 
236 | 1. **Add Your Own Content**: PDFs, documents, articles (see 3-USER-GUIDE)
237 | 2. **Explore Features**: Podcasts, transformations, search
238 | 3. **Full Documentation**: [See all features](../3-USER-GUIDE/index.md)
239 | 4. **Scale Up**: Deploy to a server with better hardware for faster responses
240 | 5. **Benchmark Models**: Try different models to find the speed/quality tradeoff you prefer
241 | 
242 | ---
243 | 
244 | ## Alternative: Using LM Studio Instead of Ollama
245 | 
246 | **Prefer a GUI?** LM Studio is easier for non-technical users:
247 | 
248 | 1. Download LM Studio: https://lmstudio.ai
249 | 2. Open the app, download a model from the library
250 | 3. Go to "Local Server" tab, start server (port 1234)
251 | 4. Update your docker-compose.yml:
252 |    ```yaml
253 |    environment:
254 |      - OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:1234/v1
255 |      - OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY=not-needed
256 |    ```
257 | 5. Configure in Settings → Models → Select your LM Studio model
258 | 
259 | **Note**: LM Studio runs outside Docker, use `host.docker.internal` to connect.
260 | 
261 | ---
262 | 
263 | ## Going Further
264 | 
265 | - **Switch models**: Change in Settings → Models anytime
266 | - **Add more models**:
267 |   - Ollama: Run `ollama pull <model>`
268 |   - LM Studio: Download from the app library
269 | - **Deploy to server**: Same docker-compose.yml works anywhere
270 | - **Use cloud hybrid**: Keep some local models, add OpenAI/Anthropic for complex tasks
271 | 
272 | ---
273 | 
274 | ## Common Model Choices
275 | 
276 | | Model | Speed | Quality | VRAM | Best For |
277 | |-------|-------|---------|------|----------|
278 | | **mistral** | Fast | Good | 4GB | Testing, general use |
279 | | **neural-chat** | Medium | Better | 6GB | Balanced, recommended |
280 | | **llama2** | Slow | Best | 8GB+ | Complex reasoning |
281 | | **phi** | Very Fast | Fair | 2GB | Minimal hardware |
282 | 
283 | ---
284 | 
285 | **Need Help?** Join our [Discord community](https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w) - many users run local setups!
286 |

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Frequently Asked Questions
  2 | 
  3 | Common questions about Open Notebook usage, configuration, and best practices.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## General Usage
  8 | 
  9 | ### What is Open Notebook?
 10 | 
 11 | Open Notebook is an open-source, privacy-focused alternative to Google's Notebook LM. It allows you to:
 12 | - Create and manage research notebooks
 13 | - Chat with your documents using AI
 14 | - Generate podcasts from your content
 15 | - Search across all your sources with semantic search
 16 | - Transform and analyze your content
 17 | 
 18 | ### How is it different from Google Notebook LM?
 19 | 
 20 | **Privacy**: Your data stays local by default. Only your chosen AI providers receive queries.
 21 | **Flexibility**: Support for 15+ AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, local models, etc.)
 22 | **Customization**: Open source, so you can modify and extend functionality
 23 | **Control**: You control your data, models, and processing
 24 | 
 25 | ### Can I use Open Notebook offline?
 26 | 
 27 | **Partially**: The application runs locally, but requires internet for:
 28 | - AI model API calls (unless using local models like Ollama)
 29 | - Web content scraping
 30 | 
 31 | **Fully offline**: Possible with local models (Ollama) for basic functionality.
 32 | 
 33 | ### What file types are supported?
 34 | 
 35 | **Documents**: PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown
 36 | **Web Content**: URLs, YouTube videos
 37 | **Media**: MP3, WAV, M4A (audio), MP4, AVI, MOV (video)
 38 | **Other**: Direct text input, CSV, code files
 39 | 
 40 | ### How much does it cost?
 41 | 
 42 | **Software**: Free (open source)
 43 | **AI API costs**: Pay-per-use to providers:
 44 | - OpenAI: ~$0.50-5 per 1M tokens
 45 | - Anthropic: ~$3-75 per 1M tokens
 46 | - Google: Often free tier available
 47 | - Local models: Free after initial setup
 48 | 
 49 | **Typical monthly costs**: $5-50 for moderate usage.
 50 | 
 51 | ---
 52 | 
 53 | ## AI Models and Providers
 54 | 
 55 | ### Which AI provider should I choose?
 56 | 
 57 | **For beginners**: OpenAI (reliable, well-documented)
 58 | **For privacy**: Local models (Ollama) or European providers (Mistral)
 59 | **For cost optimization**: Groq, Google (free tier), or OpenRouter
 60 | **For long context**: Anthropic (200K tokens) or Google Gemini (1M tokens)
 61 | 
 62 | ### Can I use multiple providers?
 63 | 
 64 | **Yes**: Configure different providers for different tasks:
 65 | - OpenAI for chat
 66 | - Google for embeddings
 67 | - ElevenLabs for text-to-speech
 68 | - Anthropic for complex reasoning
 69 | 
 70 | ### What are the best model combinations?
 71 | 
 72 | **Budget-friendly**:
 73 | - Language: `gpt-4o-mini` (OpenAI) or `deepseek-chat`
 74 | - Embedding: `text-embedding-3-small` (OpenAI)
 75 | 
 76 | **High-quality**:
 77 | - Language: `claude-3-5-sonnet` (Anthropic) or `gpt-4o` (OpenAI)
 78 | - Embedding: `text-embedding-3-large` (OpenAI)
 79 | 
 80 | **Privacy-focused**:
 81 | - Language: Local Ollama models (mistral, llama3)
 82 | - Embedding: Local embedding models
 83 | 
 84 | ### How do I optimize AI costs?
 85 | 
 86 | **Model selection**:
 87 | - Use smaller models for simple tasks (gpt-4o-mini, claude-3-5-haiku)
 88 | - Use larger models only for complex reasoning
 89 | - Leverage free tiers when available
 90 | 
 91 | **Usage optimization**:
 92 | - Use "Summary Only" context for background sources
 93 | - Ask more specific questions
 94 | - Use local models (Ollama) for frequent tasks
 95 | 
 96 | ---
 97 | 
 98 | ## Data Management
 99 | 
100 | ### Where is my data stored?
101 | 
102 | **Local storage**: By default, all data is stored locally:
103 | - Database: SurrealDB files in `surreal_data/`
104 | - Uploads: Files in `data/uploads/`
105 | - Podcasts: Generated audio in `data/podcasts/`
106 | - No external data transmission (except to chosen AI providers)
107 | 
108 | ### How do I backup my data?
109 | 
110 | ```bash
111 | # Create backup
112 | tar -czf backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz data/ surreal_data/
113 | 
114 | # Restore backup
115 | tar -xzf backup-20240101.tar.gz
116 | ```
117 | 
118 | ### Can I sync data between devices?
119 | 
120 | **Currently**: No built-in sync functionality.
121 | **Workarounds**:
122 | - Use shared network storage for data directories
123 | - Manual backup/restore between devices
124 | 
125 | ### What happens if I delete a notebook?
126 | 
127 | **Soft deletion**: Notebooks are marked as archived, not permanently deleted.
128 | **Recovery**: Archived notebooks can be restored from the database.
129 | 
130 | ---
131 | 
132 | ## Best Practices
133 | 
134 | ### How should I organize my notebooks?
135 | 
136 | - **By topic**: Separate notebooks for different research areas
137 | - **By project**: One notebook per project or course
138 | - **By time period**: Monthly or quarterly notebooks
139 | 
140 | **Recommended size**: 20-100 sources per notebook for best performance.
141 | 
142 | ### How do I get the best search results?
143 | 
144 | - Use descriptive queries ("data analysis methods" not just "data")
145 | - Combine multiple related terms
146 | - Use natural language (ask questions as you would to a human)
147 | - Try both text search (keywords) and vector search (concepts)
148 | 
149 | ### How can I improve chat responses?
150 | 
151 | - Provide context: Reference specific sources or topics
152 | - Be specific: Ask detailed questions rather than general ones
153 | - Request citations: "Answer with page citations"
154 | - Use follow-up questions: Build on previous responses
155 | 
156 | ### What are the security best practices?
157 | 
158 | - Never share API keys publicly
159 | - Use `OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD` for public deployments
160 | - Use HTTPS for production (via reverse proxy)
161 | - Keep Docker images updated
162 | - Encrypt backups if they contain sensitive data
163 | 
164 | ---
165 | 
166 | ## Technical Questions
167 | 
168 | ### Can I use Open Notebook programmatically?
169 | 
170 | **Yes**: Open Notebook provides a REST API:
171 | - Full API documentation at `http://localhost:5055/docs`
172 | - Support for all UI functionality
173 | - Authentication via password header
174 | 
175 | ### Can I run Open Notebook in production?
176 | 
177 | **Yes**: Designed for production use with:
178 | - Docker deployment
179 | - Security features (password protection)
180 | - Monitoring and logging
181 | - Reverse proxy support (nginx, Caddy, Traefik)
182 | 
183 | ### What are the system requirements?
184 | 
185 | **Minimum**:
186 | - 4GB RAM
187 | - 2 CPU cores
188 | - 10GB disk space
189 | 
190 | **Recommended**:
191 | - 8GB+ RAM
192 | - 4+ CPU cores
193 | - SSD storage
194 | - For local models: 16GB+ RAM, GPU recommended
195 | 
196 | ---
197 | 
198 | ## Timeout and Performance
199 | 
200 | ### Why do I get timeout errors?
201 | 
202 | **Common causes**:
203 | - Large context (too many sources)
204 | - Slow AI provider
205 | - Local models on CPU (slow)
206 | - First request (model loading)
207 | 
208 | **Solutions**:
209 | ```bash
210 | # In .env:
211 | API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=600  # 10 minutes for slow setups
212 | ESPERANTO_LLM_TIMEOUT=180  # 3 minutes for model inference
213 | ```
214 | 
215 | ### Recommended timeouts by setup:
216 | 
217 | | Setup | API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT |
218 | |-------|-------------------|
219 | | Cloud APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic) | 300 (default) |
220 | | Local Ollama with GPU | 600 |
221 | | Local Ollama with CPU | 1200 |
222 | | Remote LM Studio | 900 |
223 | 
224 | ---
225 | 
226 | ## Getting Help
227 | 
228 | ### My question isn't answered here
229 | 
230 | 1. Check the troubleshooting guides in this section
231 | 2. Search existing GitHub issues
232 | 3. Ask in the Discord community
233 | 4. Create a GitHub issue with detailed information
234 | 
235 | ### How do I report a bug?
236 | 
237 | Include:
238 | - Steps to reproduce
239 | - Expected vs actual behavior
240 | - Error messages and logs
241 | - System information
242 | - Configuration details (without API keys)
243 | 
244 | Submit to: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook/issues)
245 | 
246 | ### Where can I get help?
247 | 
248 | - **Discord**: https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w (fastest)
249 | - **GitHub Issues**: Bug reports and feature requests
250 | - **Documentation**: This docs site
251 | 
252 | ---
253 | 
254 | ## Related
255 | 
256 | - [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md) - Common issues with 1-minute solutions
257 | - [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md) - Model and chat problems
258 | - [Connection Issues](connection-issues.md) - Network and API problems
259 |

  1 | from typing import ClassVar, Dict, Optional, Union
  2 | 
  3 | from esperanto import (
  4 |     AIFactory,
  5 |     EmbeddingModel,
  6 |     LanguageModel,
  7 |     SpeechToTextModel,
  8 |     TextToSpeechModel,
  9 | )
 10 | from loguru import logger
 11 | 
 12 | from open_notebook.database.repository import ensure_record_id, repo_query
 13 | from open_notebook.domain.base import ObjectModel, RecordModel
 14 | 
 15 | ModelType = Union[LanguageModel, EmbeddingModel, SpeechToTextModel, TextToSpeechModel]
 16 | 
 17 | 
 18 | class Model(ObjectModel):
 19 |     table_name: ClassVar[str] = "model"
 20 |     name: str
 21 |     provider: str
 22 |     type: str
 23 | 
 24 |     @classmethod
 25 |     async def get_models_by_type(cls, model_type):
 26 |         models = await repo_query(
 27 |             "SELECT * FROM model WHERE type=$model_type;", {"model_type": model_type}
 28 |         )
 29 |         return [Model(**model) for model in models]
 30 | 
 31 | 
 32 | class DefaultModels(RecordModel):
 33 |     record_id: ClassVar[str] = "open_notebook:default_models"
 34 |     default_chat_model: Optional[str] = None
 35 |     default_transformation_model: Optional[str] = None
 36 |     large_context_model: Optional[str] = None
 37 |     default_text_to_speech_model: Optional[str] = None
 38 |     default_speech_to_text_model: Optional[str] = None
 39 |     # default_vision_model: Optional[str]
 40 |     default_embedding_model: Optional[str] = None
 41 |     default_tools_model: Optional[str] = None
 42 | 
 43 |     @classmethod
 44 |     async def get_instance(cls) -> "DefaultModels":
 45 |         """Always fetch fresh defaults from database (override parent caching behavior)"""
 46 |         result = await repo_query(
 47 |             "SELECT * FROM ONLY $record_id",
 48 |             {"record_id": ensure_record_id(cls.record_id)},
 49 |         )
 50 | 
 51 |         if result:
 52 |             if isinstance(result, list) and len(result) > 0:
 53 |                 data = result[0]
 54 |             elif isinstance(result, dict):
 55 |                 data = result
 56 |             else:
 57 |                 data = {}
 58 |         else:
 59 |             data = {}
 60 | 
 61 |         # Create new instance with fresh data (bypass singleton cache)
 62 |         instance = object.__new__(cls)
 63 |         object.__setattr__(instance, "__dict__", {})
 64 |         super(RecordModel, instance).__init__(**data)
 65 |         return instance
 66 | 
 67 | 
 68 | class ModelManager:
 69 |     def __init__(self):
 70 |         pass  # No caching needed
 71 | 
 72 |     async def get_model(self, model_id: str, **kwargs) -> Optional[ModelType]:
 73 |         """Get a model by ID. Esperanto will cache the actual model instance."""
 74 |         if not model_id:
 75 |             return None
 76 | 
 77 |         try:
 78 |             model: Model = await Model.get(model_id)
 79 |         except Exception:
 80 |             raise ValueError(f"Model with ID {model_id} not found")
 81 | 
 82 |         if not model.type or model.type not in [
 83 |             "language",
 84 |             "embedding",
 85 |             "speech_to_text",
 86 |             "text_to_speech",
 87 |         ]:
 88 |             raise ValueError(f"Invalid model type: {model.type}")
 89 | 
 90 |         # Create model based on type (Esperanto will cache the instance)
 91 |         if model.type == "language":
 92 |             return AIFactory.create_language(
 93 |                 model_name=model.name,
 94 |                 provider=model.provider,
 95 |                 config=kwargs,
 96 |             )
 97 |         elif model.type == "embedding":
 98 |             return AIFactory.create_embedding(
 99 |                 model_name=model.name,
100 |                 provider=model.provider,
101 |                 config=kwargs,
102 |             )
103 |         elif model.type == "speech_to_text":
104 |             return AIFactory.create_speech_to_text(
105 |                 model_name=model.name,
106 |                 provider=model.provider,
107 |                 config=kwargs,
108 |             )
109 |         elif model.type == "text_to_speech":
110 |             return AIFactory.create_text_to_speech(
111 |                 model_name=model.name,
112 |                 provider=model.provider,
113 |                 config=kwargs,
114 |             )
115 |         else:
116 |             raise ValueError(f"Invalid model type: {model.type}")
117 | 
118 |     async def get_defaults(self) -> DefaultModels:
119 |         """Get the default models configuration from database"""
120 |         defaults = await DefaultModels.get_instance()
121 |         if not defaults:
122 |             raise RuntimeError("Failed to load default models configuration")
123 |         return defaults
124 | 
125 |     async def get_speech_to_text(self, **kwargs) -> Optional[SpeechToTextModel]:
126 |         """Get the default speech-to-text model"""
127 |         defaults = await self.get_defaults()
128 |         model_id = defaults.default_speech_to_text_model
129 |         if not model_id:
130 |             return None
131 |         model = await self.get_model(model_id, **kwargs)
132 |         assert model is None or isinstance(model, SpeechToTextModel), (
133 |             f"Expected SpeechToTextModel but got {type(model)}"
134 |         )
135 |         return model
136 | 
137 |     async def get_text_to_speech(self, **kwargs) -> Optional[TextToSpeechModel]:
138 |         """Get the default text-to-speech model"""
139 |         defaults = await self.get_defaults()
140 |         model_id = defaults.default_text_to_speech_model
141 |         if not model_id:
142 |             return None
143 |         model = await self.get_model(model_id, **kwargs)
144 |         assert model is None or isinstance(model, TextToSpeechModel), (
145 |             f"Expected TextToSpeechModel but got {type(model)}"
146 |         )
147 |         return model
148 | 
149 |     async def get_embedding_model(self, **kwargs) -> Optional[EmbeddingModel]:
150 |         """Get the default embedding model"""
151 |         defaults = await self.get_defaults()
152 |         model_id = defaults.default_embedding_model
153 |         if not model_id:
154 |             return None
155 |         model = await self.get_model(model_id, **kwargs)
156 |         assert model is None or isinstance(model, EmbeddingModel), (
157 |             f"Expected EmbeddingModel but got {type(model)}"
158 |         )
159 |         return model
160 | 
161 |     async def get_default_model(self, model_type: str, **kwargs) -> Optional[ModelType]:
162 |         """
163 |         Get the default model for a specific type.
164 | 
165 |         Args:
166 |             model_type: The type of model to retrieve (e.g., 'chat', 'embedding', etc.)
167 |             **kwargs: Additional arguments to pass to the model constructor
168 |         """
169 |         defaults = await self.get_defaults()
170 |         model_id = None
171 | 
172 |         if model_type == "chat":
173 |             model_id = defaults.default_chat_model
174 |         elif model_type == "transformation":
175 |             model_id = (
176 |                 defaults.default_transformation_model or defaults.default_chat_model
177 |             )
178 |         elif model_type == "tools":
179 |             model_id = defaults.default_tools_model or defaults.default_chat_model
180 |         elif model_type == "embedding":
181 |             model_id = defaults.default_embedding_model
182 |         elif model_type == "text_to_speech":
183 |             model_id = defaults.default_text_to_speech_model
184 |         elif model_type == "speech_to_text":
185 |             model_id = defaults.default_speech_to_text_model
186 |         elif model_type == "large_context":
187 |             model_id = defaults.large_context_model
188 | 
189 |         if not model_id:
190 |             logger.warning(
191 |                 f"No default model configured for type '{model_type}'. "
192 |                 f"Please go to Settings → Models and set a default model."
193 |             )
194 |             return None
195 | 
196 |         try:
197 |             return await self.get_model(model_id, **kwargs)
198 |         except ValueError as e:
199 |             logger.error(
200 |                 f"Failed to load default model for type '{model_type}': {e}. "
201 |                 f"The configured model_id '{model_id}' may have been deleted or misconfigured. "
202 |                 f"Please go to Settings → Models and reconfigure the default model."
203 |             )
204 |             return None
205 | 
206 | 
207 | model_manager = ModelManager()

  1 | """
  2 | Async migration system for SurrealDB using the official Python client.
  3 | Based on patterns from sblpy migration system.
  4 | """
  5 | 
  6 | from typing import List
  7 | 
  8 | from loguru import logger
  9 | 
 10 | from .repository import db_connection, repo_query
 11 | 
 12 | 
 13 | class AsyncMigration:
 14 |     """
 15 |     Handles individual migration operations with async support.
 16 |     """
 17 | 
 18 |     def __init__(self, sql: str) -> None:
 19 |         """Initialize migration with SQL content."""
 20 |         self.sql = sql
 21 | 
 22 |     @classmethod
 23 |     def from_file(cls, file_path: str) -> "AsyncMigration":
 24 |         """Create migration from SQL file."""
 25 |         with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
 26 |             raw_content = file.read()
 27 |             # Clean up SQL content
 28 |             lines = []
 29 |             for line in raw_content.split("\n"):
 30 |                 line = line.strip()
 31 |                 if line and not line.startswith("--"):
 32 |                     lines.append(line)
 33 |             sql = " ".join(lines)
 34 |             return cls(sql)
 35 | 
 36 |     async def run(self, bump: bool = True) -> None:
 37 |         """Run the migration."""
 38 |         try:
 39 |             async with db_connection() as connection:
 40 |                 await connection.query(self.sql)
 41 | 
 42 |             if bump:
 43 |                 await bump_version()
 44 |             else:
 45 |                 await lower_version()
 46 | 
 47 |         except Exception as e:
 48 |             logger.error(f"Migration failed: {str(e)}")
 49 |             raise
 50 | 
 51 | 
 52 | class AsyncMigrationRunner:
 53 |     """
 54 |     Handles running multiple migrations in sequence.
 55 |     """
 56 | 
 57 |     def __init__(
 58 |         self,
 59 |         up_migrations: List[AsyncMigration],
 60 |         down_migrations: List[AsyncMigration],
 61 |     ) -> None:
 62 |         """Initialize runner with migration lists."""
 63 |         self.up_migrations = up_migrations
 64 |         self.down_migrations = down_migrations
 65 | 
 66 |     async def run_all(self) -> None:
 67 |         """Run all pending up migrations."""
 68 |         current_version = await get_latest_version()
 69 | 
 70 |         for i in range(current_version, len(self.up_migrations)):
 71 |             logger.info(f"Running migration {i + 1}")
 72 |             await self.up_migrations[i].run(bump=True)
 73 | 
 74 |     async def run_one_up(self) -> None:
 75 |         """Run one up migration."""
 76 |         current_version = await get_latest_version()
 77 | 
 78 |         if current_version < len(self.up_migrations):
 79 |             logger.info(f"Running migration {current_version + 1}")
 80 |             await self.up_migrations[current_version].run(bump=True)
 81 | 
 82 |     async def run_one_down(self) -> None:
 83 |         """Run one down migration."""
 84 |         current_version = await get_latest_version()
 85 | 
 86 |         if current_version > 0:
 87 |             logger.info(f"Rolling back migration {current_version}")
 88 |             await self.down_migrations[current_version - 1].run(bump=False)
 89 | 
 90 | 
 91 | class AsyncMigrationManager:
 92 |     """
 93 |     Main migration manager with async support.
 94 |     """
 95 | 
 96 |     def __init__(self):
 97 |         """Initialize migration manager."""
 98 |         self.up_migrations = [
 99 |             AsyncMigration.from_file("open_notebook/database/migrations/1.surrealql"),
100 |             AsyncMigration.from_file("open_notebook/database/migrations/2.surrealql"),
101 |             AsyncMigration.from_file("open_notebook/database/migrations/3.surrealql"),
102 |             AsyncMigration.from_file("open_notebook/database/migrations/4.surrealql"),
103 |             AsyncMigration.from_file("open_notebook/database/migrations/5.surrealql"),
104 |             AsyncMigration.from_file("open_notebook/database/migrations/6.surrealql"),
105 |             AsyncMigration.from_file("open_notebook/database/migrations/7.surrealql"),
106 |             AsyncMigration.from_file("open_notebook/database/migrations/8.surrealql"),
107 |             AsyncMigration.from_file("open_notebook/database/migrations/9.surrealql"),
108 |             AsyncMigration.from_file("open_notebook/database/migrations/10.surrealql"),
109 |         ]
110 |         self.down_migrations = [
111 |             AsyncMigration.from_file(
112 |                 "open_notebook/database/migrations/1_down.surrealql"
113 |             ),
114 |             AsyncMigration.from_file(
115 |                 "open_notebook/database/migrations/2_down.surrealql"
116 |             ),
117 |             AsyncMigration.from_file(
118 |                 "open_notebook/database/migrations/3_down.surrealql"
119 |             ),
120 |             AsyncMigration.from_file(
121 |                 "open_notebook/database/migrations/4_down.surrealql"
122 |             ),
123 |             AsyncMigration.from_file(
124 |                 "open_notebook/database/migrations/5_down.surrealql"
125 |             ),
126 |             AsyncMigration.from_file(
127 |                 "open_notebook/database/migrations/6_down.surrealql"
128 |             ),
129 |             AsyncMigration.from_file(
130 |                 "open_notebook/database/migrations/7_down.surrealql"
131 |             ),
132 |             AsyncMigration.from_file(
133 |                 "open_notebook/database/migrations/8_down.surrealql"
134 |             ),
135 |             AsyncMigration.from_file(
136 |                 "open_notebook/database/migrations/9_down.surrealql"
137 |             ),
138 |             AsyncMigration.from_file(
139 |                 "open_notebook/database/migrations/10_down.surrealql"
140 |             ),
141 |         ]
142 |         self.runner = AsyncMigrationRunner(
143 |             up_migrations=self.up_migrations,
144 |             down_migrations=self.down_migrations,
145 |         )
146 | 
147 |     async def get_current_version(self) -> int:
148 |         """Get current database version."""
149 |         return await get_latest_version()
150 | 
151 |     async def needs_migration(self) -> bool:
152 |         """Check if migration is needed."""
153 |         current_version = await self.get_current_version()
154 |         return current_version < len(self.up_migrations)
155 | 
156 |     async def run_migration_up(self):
157 |         """Run all pending migrations."""
158 |         current_version = await self.get_current_version()
159 |         logger.info(f"Current version before migration: {current_version}")
160 | 
161 |         if await self.needs_migration():
162 |             try:
163 |                 await self.runner.run_all()
164 |                 new_version = await self.get_current_version()
165 |                 logger.info(f"Migration successful. New version: {new_version}")
166 |             except Exception as e:
167 |                 logger.error(f"Migration failed: {str(e)}")
168 |                 raise
169 |         else:
170 |             logger.info("Database is already at the latest version")
171 | 
172 | 
173 | # Database version management functions
174 | async def get_latest_version() -> int:
175 |     """Get the latest version from the migrations table."""
176 |     try:
177 |         versions = await get_all_versions()
178 |         if not versions:
179 |             return 0
180 |         return max(version["version"] for version in versions)
181 |     except Exception:
182 |         # If migrations table doesn't exist, we're at version 0
183 |         return 0
184 | 
185 | 
186 | async def get_all_versions() -> List[dict]:
187 |     """Get all versions from the migrations table."""
188 |     try:
189 |         result = await repo_query("SELECT * FROM _sbl_migrations ORDER BY version;")
190 |         return result
191 |     except Exception:
192 |         # If table doesn't exist, return empty list
193 |         return []
194 | 
195 | 
196 | async def bump_version() -> None:
197 |     """Bump the version by adding a new entry to migrations table."""
198 |     current_version = await get_latest_version()
199 |     new_version = current_version + 1
200 | 
201 |     await repo_query(
202 |         f"CREATE _sbl_migrations:{new_version} SET version = {new_version}, applied_at = time::now();",
203 |     )
204 | 
205 | 
206 | async def lower_version() -> None:
207 |     """Lower the version by removing the latest entry from migrations table."""
208 |     current_version = await get_latest_version()
209 |     if current_version > 0:
210 |         await repo_query(f"DELETE _sbl_migrations:{current_version};")
211 |

 28 | export function StreamingResponse({
 29 |   isStreaming,
 30 |   strategy,

 33 | }: StreamingResponseProps) {
 34 |   const [strategyOpen, setStrategyOpen] = useState(false)
 35 |   const [answersOpen, setAnswersOpen] = useState(false)
 36 |   const { openModal } = useModalManager()
 37 |   const { t } = useTranslation()

 39 |   const handleReferenceClick = (type: string, id: string) => {
 40 |     const modalType = type === 'source_insight' ? 'insight' : type as 'source' | 'note' | 'insight'
 41 | 
 42 |     try {
 43 |       openModal(modalType, id)
 44 |       // Note: The modal system uses URL parameters and doesn't throw errors for missing items.
 45 |       // The modal component itself will handle displaying "not found" states.
 46 |       // This try-catch is here for future enhancements or unexpected errors.
 47 |     } catch {
 48 |       const typeLabel = type === 'source_insight' ? 'insight' : type
 49 |       toast.error(t.common.itemNotFound.replace('{type}', typeLabel))
 50 |     }
 51 |   }
 52 | 
 53 |   if (!strategy && !answers.length && !finalAnswer && !isStreaming) {
 54 |     return null
 55 |   }
 56 | 
 57 |   return (
 58 |     <div
 59 |       className="space-y-4 mt-6 max-h-[60vh] overflow-y-auto pr-2"
 60 |       role="region"
 61 |       aria-label={t.common.accessibility.askResponse}
 62 |       aria-live="polite"
 63 |       aria-busy={isStreaming}
 64 |     >
 65 |       {/* Strategy Section - Collapsible */}
 66 |       {strategy && (
 67 |         <Collapsible open={strategyOpen} onOpenChange={setStrategyOpen}>
 68 |           <Card>
 69 |             <CardHeader>
 70 |               <CollapsibleTrigger className="flex items-center justify-between w-full hover:opacity-80">
 71 |                 <CardTitle className="text-base flex items-center gap-2">
 72 |                   <Sparkles className="h-4 w-4 text-primary" />
 73 |                   {t.common.strategy}
 74 |                 </CardTitle>
 75 |                 <ChevronDown className={`h-4 w-4 transition-transform ${strategyOpen ? 'rotate-180' : ''}`} />
 76 |               </CollapsibleTrigger>
 77 |             </CardHeader>
 78 |             <CollapsibleContent>
 79 |               <CardContent className="space-y-3 pt-0">
 80 |                 <div>
 81 |                   <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground mb-2">{t.common.reasoning}:</p>
 82 |                   <p className="text-sm">{strategy.reasoning}</p>
 83 |                 </div>
 84 |                 {strategy.searches.length > 0 && (
 85 |                   <div>
 86 |                     <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground mb-2">{t.common.searchTerms}:</p>
 87 |                     <div className="space-y-2">
 88 |                       {strategy.searches.map((search, i) => (
 89 |                         <div key={i} className="flex items-start gap-2">
 90 |                           <Badge variant="outline" className="mt-0.5">{i + 1}</Badge>
 91 |                           <div className="flex-1">

 93 |                             <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">{search.instructions}</p>
 94 |                           </div>
 95 |                         </div>
 96 |                       ))}
 97 |                     </div>
 98 |                   </div>
 99 |                 )}
100 |               </CardContent>
101 |             </CollapsibleContent>
102 |           </Card>
103 |         </Collapsible>
104 |       )}
105 | 
106 |       {/* Individual Answers Section - Collapsible */}
107 |       {answers.length > 0 && (
108 |         <Collapsible open={answersOpen} onOpenChange={setAnswersOpen}>
109 |           <Card>
110 |             <CardHeader>
111 |               <CollapsibleTrigger className="flex items-center justify-between w-full hover:opacity-80">
112 |                 <CardTitle className="text-base flex items-center gap-2">
113 |                   <Lightbulb className="h-4 w-4 text-primary" />
114 |                   {t.common.individualAnswers.replace('{count}', answers.length.toString())}
115 |                 </CardTitle>
116 |                 <ChevronDown className={`h-4 w-4 transition-transform ${answersOpen ? 'rotate-180' : ''}`} />
117 |               </CollapsibleTrigger>
118 |             </CardHeader>
119 |             <CollapsibleContent>
120 |               <CardContent className="space-y-2 pt-0">
121 |                 {answers.map((answer, i) => (
122 |                   <div key={i} className="p-3 rounded-md bg-muted">
123 |                     <p className="text-sm">{answer}</p>
124 |                   </div>
125 |                 ))}
126 |               </CardContent>
127 |             </CollapsibleContent>
128 |           </Card>
129 |         </Collapsible>
130 |       )}
131 | 
132 |       {/* Final Answer Section - Always Open */}
133 |       {finalAnswer && (
134 |         <Card className="border-primary">
135 |           <CardHeader>
136 |             <CardTitle className="text-base flex items-center gap-2">
137 |               <CheckCircle className="h-4 w-4 text-primary" />
138 |               {t.common.finalAnswer}

149 |

153 |           <LoadingSpinner size="sm" />

155 |         </div>
156 |       )}
157 |     </div>
158 |   )
159 | }

161 | // Helper component to render final answer with clickable references
162 | function FinalAnswerContent({
163 |   content,
164 |   onReferenceClick
165 | }: {
166 |   content: string
167 |   onReferenceClick: (type: string, id: string) => void
168 | }) {
169 |   // Convert references to markdown links
170 |   const markdownWithLinks = convertReferencesToMarkdownLinks(content)
171 | 
172 |   // Create custom link component
173 |   const LinkComponent = createReferenceLinkComponent(onReferenceClick)
174 | 
175 |   return (
176 |     <div className="prose prose-sm max-w-none dark:prose-invert break-words prose-a:break-all prose-p:leading-relaxed prose-headings:mt-4 prose-headings:mb-2">
177 |       <ReactMarkdown
178 |         remarkPlugins={[remarkGfm]}
179 |         components={{
180 |           a: LinkComponent,
181 |           table: ({ children }) => (
182 |             <div className="my-4 overflow-x-auto">
183 |               <table className="min-w-full border-collapse border border-border">{children}</table>
184 |             </div>
185 |           ),
186 |           thead: ({ children }) => <thead className="bg-muted">{children}</thead>,
187 |           tbody: ({ children }) => <tbody>{children}</tbody>,
188 |           tr: ({ children }) => <tr className="border-b border-border">{children}</tr>,
189 |           th: ({ children }) => <th className="border border-border px-3 py-2 text-left font-semibold">{children}</th>,
190 |           td: ({ children }) => <td className="border border-border px-3 py-2">{children}</td>,
191 |         }}
192 |       >
193 |         {markdownWithLinks}
194 |       </ReactMarkdown>
195 |     </div>
196 |   )
197 | }
198 |

 33 | class PodcastService:
 34 |     """Service layer for podcast operations"""
 35 | 
 36 |     @staticmethod
 37 |     async def submit_generation_job(
 38 |         episode_profile_name: str,
 39 |         speaker_profile_name: str,
 40 |         episode_name: str,
 41 |         notebook_id: Optional[str] = None,
 42 |         content: Optional[str] = None,
 43 |         briefing_suffix: Optional[str] = None,
 44 |     ) -> str:
 45 |         """Submit a podcast generation job for background processing"""
 46 |         try:
 47 |             # Validate episode profile exists
 48 |             episode_profile = await EpisodeProfile.get_by_name(episode_profile_name)
 49 |             if not episode_profile:
 50 |                 raise ValueError(f"Episode profile '{episode_profile_name}' not found")
 51 | 
 52 |             # Validate speaker profile exists
 53 |             speaker_profile = await SpeakerProfile.get_by_name(speaker_profile_name)
 54 |             if not speaker_profile:
 55 |                 raise ValueError(f"Speaker profile '{speaker_profile_name}' not found")
 56 | 
 57 |             # Get content from notebook if not provided directly
 58 |             if not content and notebook_id:
 59 |                 try:
 60 |                     notebook = await Notebook.get(notebook_id)
 61 |                     # Get notebook context (this may need to be adjusted based on actual Notebook implementation)
 62 |                     content = (
 63 |                         await notebook.get_context()
 64 |                         if hasattr(notebook, "get_context")
 65 |                         else str(notebook)
 66 |                     )
 67 |                 except Exception as e:
 68 |                     logger.warning(
 69 |                         f"Failed to get notebook content, using notebook_id as content: {e}"
 70 |                     )
 71 |                     content = f"Notebook ID: {notebook_id}"
 72 | 
 73 |             if not content:
 74 |                 raise ValueError(
 75 |                     "Content is required - provide either content or notebook_id"
 76 |                 )
 77 | 
 78 |             # Prepare command arguments
 79 |             command_args = {
 80 |                 "episode_profile": episode_profile_name,
 81 |                 "speaker_profile": speaker_profile_name,
 82 |                 "episode_name": episode_name,
 83 |                 "content": str(content),
 84 |                 "briefing_suffix": briefing_suffix,
 85 |             }
 86 | 
 87 |             # Ensure command modules are imported before submitting
 88 |             # This is needed because submit_command validates against local registry
 89 |             try:
 90 |                 import commands.podcast_commands  # noqa: F401
 91 |             except ImportError as import_err:
 92 |                 logger.error(f"Failed to import podcast commands: {import_err}")
 93 |                 raise ValueError("Podcast commands not available")
 94 | 
 95 |             # Submit command to surreal-commands
 96 |             job_id = submit_command("open_notebook", "generate_podcast", command_args)
 97 | 
 98 |             # Convert RecordID to string if needed
 99 |             if not job_id:
100 |                 raise ValueError("Failed to get job_id from submit_command")
101 |             job_id_str = str(job_id)
102 |             logger.info(
103 |                 f"Submitted podcast generation job: {job_id_str} for episode '{episode_name}'"
104 |             )
105 |             return job_id_str
106 | 
107 |         except Exception as e:
108 |             logger.error(f"Failed to submit podcast generation job: {e}")
109 |             raise HTTPException(
110 |                 status_code=500,
111 |                 detail=f"Failed to submit podcast generation job: {str(e)}",
112 |             )

119 |             return {

122 |                 "result": status.result if status else None,
123 |                 "error_message": getattr(status, "error_message", None)
124 |                 if status

130 |                 if status and hasattr(status, "updated") and status.updated
131 |                 else None,
