/docs/5-CONFIGURATION/local-tts.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Local Text-to-Speech Setup
  2 | 
  3 | Run text-to-speech locally for free, private podcast generation using OpenAI-compatible TTS servers.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## Why Local TTS?
  8 | 
  9 | | Benefit | Description |
 10 | |---------|-------------|
 11 | | **Free** | No per-character costs after setup |
 12 | | **Private** | Audio never leaves your machine |
 13 | | **Unlimited** | No rate limits or quotas |
 14 | | **Offline** | Works without internet |
 15 | 
 16 | ---
 17 | 
 18 | ## Quick Start with Speaches
 19 | 
 20 | [Speaches](https://github.com/speaches-ai/speaches) is an open-source, OpenAI-compatible TTS server.
 21 | 
 22 | ### Step 1: Create Docker Compose File
 23 | 
 24 | Create a folder and add `docker-compose.yml`:
 25 | 
 26 | ```yaml
 27 | services:
 28 |   speaches:
 29 |     image: ghcr.io/speaches-ai/speaches:latest-cpu
 30 |     container_name: speaches
 31 |     ports:
 32 |       - "8969:8000"
 33 |     volumes:
 34 |       - hf-hub-cache:/home/ubuntu/.cache/huggingface/hub
 35 |     restart: unless-stopped
 36 | 
 37 | volumes:
 38 |   hf-hub-cache:
 39 | ```
 40 | 
 41 | ### Step 2: Start and Download Model
 42 | 
 43 | ```bash
 44 | # Start Speaches
 45 | docker compose up -d
 46 | 
 47 | # Wait for startup
 48 | sleep 10
 49 | 
 50 | # Download voice model (~500MB)
 51 | docker compose exec speaches uv tool run speaches-cli model download speaches-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX
 52 | ```
 53 | 
 54 | ### Step 3: Test
 55 | 
 56 | ```bash
 57 | curl "http://localhost:8969/v1/audio/speech" -s \
 58 |   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 59 |   --output test.mp3 \
 60 |   --data '{
 61 |     "input": "Hello! Local TTS is working.",
 62 |     "model": "speaches-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX",
 63 |     "voice": "af_bella"
 64 |   }'
 65 | ```
 66 | 
 67 | Play `test.mp3` to verify.
 68 | 
 69 | ### Step 4: Configure Open Notebook
 70 | 
 71 | **Docker deployment:**
 72 | ```yaml
 73 | # In your Open Notebook docker-compose.yml
 74 | environment:
 75 |   - OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_TTS=http://host.docker.internal:8969/v1
 76 | ```
 77 | 
 78 | **Local development:**
 79 | ```bash
 80 | export OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_TTS=http://localhost:8969/v1
 81 | ```
 82 | 
 83 | ### Step 5: Add Model in Open Notebook
 84 | 
 85 | 1. Go to **Settings** → **Models**
 86 | 2. Click **Add Model** in Text-to-Speech section
 87 | 3. Configure:
 88 |    - **Provider**: `openai_compatible`
 89 |    - **Model Name**: `speaches-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX`
 90 |    - **Display Name**: `Local TTS`
 91 | 4. Click **Save**
 92 | 5. Set as default if desired
 93 | 
 94 | ---
 95 | 
 96 | ## Available Voices
 97 | 
 98 | The Kokoro model includes multiple voices:
 99 | 
100 | ### Female Voices
101 | | Voice ID | Description |
102 | |----------|-------------|
103 | | `af_bella` | Clear, professional |
104 | | `af_sarah` | Warm, friendly |
105 | | `af_nicole` | Energetic, expressive |
106 | 
107 | ### Male Voices
108 | | Voice ID | Description |
109 | |----------|-------------|
110 | | `am_adam` | Deep, authoritative |
111 | | `am_michael` | Friendly, conversational |
112 | 
113 | ### British Accents
114 | | Voice ID | Description |
115 | |----------|-------------|
116 | | `bf_emma` | British female, professional |
117 | | `bm_george` | British male, formal |
118 | 
119 | ### Test Different Voices
120 | 
121 | ```bash
122 | for voice in af_bella af_sarah am_adam am_michael; do
123 |   curl "http://localhost:8969/v1/audio/speech" -s \
124 |     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
125 |     --output "test_${voice}.mp3" \
126 |     --data "{
127 |       \"input\": \"Hello, this is the ${voice} voice.\",
128 |       \"model\": \"speaches-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX\",
129 |       \"voice\": \"${voice}\"
130 |     }"
131 | done
132 | ```
133 | 
134 | ---
135 | 
136 | ## GPU Acceleration
137 | 
138 | For faster generation with NVIDIA GPUs:
139 | 
140 | ```yaml
141 | services:
142 |   speaches:
143 |     image: ghcr.io/speaches-ai/speaches:latest-cuda
144 |     container_name: speaches
145 |     ports:
146 |       - "8969:8000"
147 |     volumes:
148 |       - hf-hub-cache:/home/ubuntu/.cache/huggingface/hub
149 |     restart: unless-stopped
150 |     deploy:
151 |       resources:
152 |         reservations:
153 |           devices:
154 |             - driver: nvidia
155 |               count: 1
156 |               capabilities: [gpu]
157 | 
158 | volumes:
159 |   hf-hub-cache:
160 | ```
161 | 
162 | ---
163 | 
164 | ## Docker Networking
165 | 
166 | ### Open Notebook in Docker (macOS/Windows)
167 | 
168 | ```bash
169 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_TTS=http://host.docker.internal:8969/v1
170 | ```
171 | 
172 | ### Open Notebook in Docker (Linux)
173 | 
174 | ```bash
175 | # Option 1: Docker bridge IP
176 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_TTS=http://172.17.0.1:8969/v1
177 | 
178 | # Option 2: Host networking
179 | docker run --network host ...
180 | ```
181 | 
182 | ### Remote Server
183 | 
184 | Run Speaches on a different machine:
185 | 
186 | ```bash
187 | # On server, bind to all interfaces
188 | # Then in Open Notebook:
189 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_TTS=http://server-ip:8969/v1
190 | ```
191 | 
192 | ---
193 | 
194 | ## Multi-Speaker Podcasts
195 | 
196 | Configure different voices for each speaker:
197 | 
198 | ```
199 | Speaker 1 (Host):
200 |   Model: speaches-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX
201 |   Voice: af_bella
202 | 
203 | Speaker 2 (Guest):
204 |   Model: speaches-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX
205 |   Voice: am_adam
206 | 
207 | Speaker 3 (Narrator):
208 |   Model: speaches-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX
209 |   Voice: bf_emma
210 | ```
211 | 
212 | ---
213 | 
214 | ## Troubleshooting
215 | 
216 | ### Service Won't Start
217 | 
218 | ```bash
219 | # Check logs
220 | docker compose logs speaches
221 | 
222 | # Verify port available
223 | lsof -i :8969
224 | 
225 | # Restart
226 | docker compose down && docker compose up -d
227 | ```
228 | 
229 | ### Connection Refused
230 | 
231 | ```bash
232 | # Test Speaches is running
233 | curl http://localhost:8969/v1/models
234 | 
235 | # From inside Open Notebook container
236 | docker exec -it open-notebook curl http://host.docker.internal:8969/v1/models
237 | ```
238 | 
239 | ### Model Not Found
240 | 
241 | ```bash
242 | # List downloaded models
243 | docker compose exec speaches uv tool run speaches-cli model list
244 | 
245 | # Download if missing
246 | docker compose exec speaches uv tool run speaches-cli model download speaches-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX
247 | ```
248 | 
249 | ### Poor Audio Quality
250 | 
251 | - Try different voices
252 | - Adjust speed: `"speed": 0.9` to `1.2`
253 | - Check model downloaded completely
254 | - Allocate more memory
255 | 
256 | ### Slow Generation
257 | 
258 | | Solution | How |
259 | |----------|-----|
260 | | Use GPU | Switch to `latest-cuda` image |
261 | | More CPU | Allocate more cores in Docker |
262 | | Faster model | Use smaller/quantized models |
263 | | SSD storage | Move Docker volumes to SSD |
264 | 
265 | ---
266 | 
267 | ## Performance Tips
268 | 
269 | ### Recommended Specs
270 | 
271 | | Component | Minimum | Recommended |
272 | |-----------|---------|-------------|
273 | | CPU | 2 cores | 4+ cores |
274 | | RAM | 2 GB | 4+ GB |
275 | | Storage | 5 GB | 10 GB (for multiple models) |
276 | | GPU | None | NVIDIA (optional) |
277 | 
278 | ### Resource Limits
279 | 
280 | ```yaml
281 | services:
282 |   speaches:
283 |     # ... other config
284 |     mem_limit: 4g
285 |     cpus: 2
286 | ```
287 | 
288 | ### Monitor Usage
289 | 
290 | ```bash
291 | docker stats speaches
292 | ```
293 | 
294 | ---
295 | 
296 | ## Comparison: Local vs Cloud
297 | 
298 | | Aspect | Local (Speaches) | Cloud (OpenAI/ElevenLabs) |
299 | |--------|------------------|---------------------------|
300 | | **Cost** | Free | $0.015-0.10/min |
301 | | **Privacy** | Complete | Data sent to provider |
302 | | **Speed** | Depends on hardware | Usually faster |
303 | | **Quality** | Good | Excellent |
304 | | **Setup** | Moderate | Simple API key |
305 | | **Offline** | Yes | No |
306 | | **Voices** | Limited | Many options |
307 | 
308 | ### When to Use Local
309 | 
310 | - Privacy-sensitive content
311 | - High-volume generation
312 | - Development/testing
313 | - Offline environments
314 | - Cost control
315 | 
316 | ### When to Use Cloud
317 | 
318 | - Premium quality needs
319 | - Multiple languages
320 | - Time-sensitive projects
321 | - Limited hardware
322 | 
323 | ---
324 | 
325 | ## Other Local TTS Options
326 | 
327 | Any OpenAI-compatible TTS server works. The key is:
328 | 
329 | 1. Server implements `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint
330 | 2. Set `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_TTS` to server URL
331 | 3. Add model with provider `openai_compatible`
332 | 
333 | ---
334 | 
335 | ## Related
336 | 
337 | - **[Local STT Setup](local-stt.md)** - Speech-to-text with Speaches
338 | - **[OpenAI-Compatible Providers](openai-compatible.md)** - General compatible provider setup
339 | - **[AI Providers](ai-providers.md)** - All provider configuration
340 | - **[Creating Podcasts](../3-USER-GUIDE/creating-podcasts.md)** - Using TTS for podcasts
341 |

/docs/1-INSTALLATION/docker-compose.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Docker Compose Installation (Recommended)
  2 | 
  3 | Multi-container setup with separate services. **Best for most users.**
  4 | 
  5 | > **Alternative Registry:** All images are available on both Docker Hub (`lfnovo/open_notebook`) and GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io/lfnovo/open-notebook`). Use GHCR if Docker Hub is blocked or you prefer GitHub-native workflows.
  6 | 
  7 | ## Prerequisites
  8 | 
  9 | - **Docker Desktop** installed ([Download](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/))
 10 | - **5-10 minutes** of your time
 11 | - **API key** for at least one AI provider (OpenAI recommended for beginners)
 12 | 
 13 | ## Step 1: Get an API Key (2 min)
 14 | 
 15 | Choose at least one AI provider. **OpenAI recommended if you're unsure:**
 16 | 
 17 | ```
 18 | OpenAI:     https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
 19 | Anthropic:  https://console.anthropic.com/
 20 | Google:     https://aistudio.google.com/
 21 | Groq:       https://console.groq.com/
 22 | ```
 23 | 
 24 | Add at least $5 in credits to your account.
 25 | 
 26 | (Skip this if using Ollama for free local models)
 27 | 
 28 | ---
 29 | 
 30 | ## Step 2: Create Configuration (2 min)
 31 | 
 32 | Create a folder `open-notebook` and add this file:
 33 | 
 34 | **docker-compose.yml**:
 35 | ```yaml
 36 | services:
 37 |   surrealdb:
 38 |     image: surrealdb/surrealdb:v2
 39 |     command: start --user root --pass password --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 rocksdb:/mydata/mydatabase.db
 40 |     user: root  # Required for bind mounts on Linux (SurrealDB runs as non-root by default)
 41 |     ports:
 42 |       - "8000:8000"
 43 |     volumes:
 44 |       - ./surreal_data:/mydata
 45 | 
 46 |   open_notebook:
 47 |     image: lfnovo/open_notebook:v1-latest
 48 |     pull_policy: always
 49 |     ports:
 50 |       - "8502:8502"  # Web UI
 51 |       - "5055:5055"  # API
 52 |     environment:
 53 |       # AI Provider (choose ONE)
 54 |       - OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...  # Your OpenAI key
 55 |       # - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...  # Or Anthropic
 56 |       # - GOOGLE_API_KEY=...  # Or Google
 57 | 
 58 |       # Database
 59 |       - SURREAL_URL=ws://surrealdb:8000/rpc
 60 |       - SURREAL_USER=root
 61 |       - SURREAL_PASSWORD=password
 62 |       - SURREAL_NAMESPACE=open_notebook
 63 |       - SURREAL_DATABASE=open_notebook
 64 |     volumes:
 65 |       - ./notebook_data:/app/data
 66 |     depends_on:
 67 |       - surrealdb
 68 |     restart: always
 69 | 
 70 | ```
 71 | 
 72 | **Edit the file:**
 73 | - Replace `sk-...` with your actual OpenAI API key
 74 | - (Or use Anthropic, Google, Groq keys instead)
 75 | - If you have multiple keys, uncomment the ones you want
 76 | 
 77 | ---
 78 | 
 79 | ## Step 3: Start Services (2 min)
 80 | 
 81 | Open terminal in the `open-notebook` folder:
 82 | 
 83 | ```bash
 84 | docker compose up -d
 85 | ```
 86 | 
 87 | Wait 15-20 seconds for all services to start:
 88 | ```
 89 | ✅ surrealdb running on :8000
 90 | ✅ open_notebook running on :8502 (UI) and :5055 (API)
 91 | ```
 92 | 
 93 | Check status:
 94 | ```bash
 95 | docker compose ps
 96 | ```
 97 | 
 98 | ---
 99 | 
100 | ## Step 4: Verify Installation (1 min)
101 | 
102 | **API Health:**
103 | ```bash
104 | curl http://localhost:5055/health
105 | # Should return: {"status": "healthy"}
106 | ```
107 | 
108 | **Frontend Access:**
109 | Open browser to:
110 | ```
111 | http://localhost:8502
112 | ```
113 | 
114 | You should see the Open Notebook interface!
115 | 
116 | ---
117 | 
118 | ## Step 5: First Notebook (2 min)
119 | 
120 | 1. Click **New Notebook**
121 | 2. Name: "My Research"
122 | 3. Description: "Getting started"
123 | 4. Click **Create**
124 | 
125 | Done! You now have a fully working Open Notebook instance. 🎉
126 | 
127 | ---
128 | 
129 | ## Configuration
130 | 
131 | ### Using Different AI Providers
132 | 
133 | Change `environment` section in `docker-compose.yml`:
134 | 
135 | ```yaml
136 | # For Anthropic (Claude)
137 | - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
138 | 
139 | # For Google Gemini
140 | - GOOGLE_API_KEY=...
141 | 
142 | # For Groq (fast, free tier available)
143 | - GROQ_API_KEY=...
144 | 
145 | # For local Ollama docker container (free, offline) --> Virtual machine
146 | - OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://ollama:11434
147 | # For localhost Ollama (free, offline) --> Real machine
148 | # - OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://host.docker.internal:11434
149 | ```
150 | 
151 | ### Adding Ollama container (Free Local Models)
152 | 
153 | Add to `docker-compose.yml`:
154 | 
155 | ```yaml
156 |   ollama:
157 |     image: ollama/ollama:latest
158 |     ports:
159 |       - "11434:11434"
160 |     volumes:
161 |       - ollama_models:/root/.ollama
162 |     restart: always
163 | 
164 | volumes:
165 |   surreal_data:
166 |   ollama_models:
167 | ```
168 | 
169 | Then update API service:
170 | ```yaml
171 | environment:
172 |   - OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://ollama:11434
173 | ```
174 | 
175 | Restart and pull a model:
176 | ```bash
177 | docker compose restart
178 | docker exec open_notebook-ollama-1 ollama pull mistral
179 | ```
180 | 
181 | ---
182 | 
183 | ## Environment Variables Reference
184 | 
185 | | Variable | Purpose | Example |
186 | |----------|---------|---------|
187 | | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI API key | `sk-proj-...` |
188 | | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic/Claude key | `sk-ant-...` |
189 | | `SURREAL_URL` | Database connection | `ws://surrealdb:8000/rpc` |
190 | | `SURREAL_USER` | Database user | `root` |
191 | | `SURREAL_PASSWORD` | Database password | `password` |
192 | | `API_URL` | API external URL | `http://localhost:5055` |
193 | | `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` | Frontend API URL | `http://localhost:5055` |
194 | 
195 | ---
196 | 
197 | ## Common Tasks
198 | 
199 | ### Stop Services
200 | ```bash
201 | docker compose down
202 | ```
203 | 
204 | ### View Logs
205 | ```bash
206 | # All services
207 | docker compose logs -f
208 | 
209 | # Specific service
210 | docker compose logs -f api
211 | ```
212 | 
213 | ### Restart Services
214 | ```bash
215 | docker compose restart
216 | ```
217 | 
218 | ### Update to Latest Version
219 | ```bash
220 | docker compose down
221 | docker compose pull
222 | docker compose up -d
223 | ```
224 | 
225 | ### Remove All Data
226 | ```bash
227 | docker compose down -v
228 | ```
229 | 
230 | ---
231 | 
232 | ## Troubleshooting
233 | 
234 | ### "Cannot connect to API" Error
235 | 
236 | 1. Check if Docker is running:
237 | ```bash
238 | docker ps
239 | ```
240 | 
241 | 2. Check if services are running:
242 | ```bash
243 | docker compose ps
244 | ```
245 | 
246 | 3. Check API logs:
247 | ```bash
248 | docker compose logs api
249 | ```
250 | 
251 | 4. Wait longer - services can take 20-30 seconds to start on first run
252 | 
253 | ---
254 | 
255 | ### Port Already in Use
256 | 
257 | If you get "Port 8502 already in use", change the port:
258 | 
259 | ```yaml
260 | ports:
261 |   - "8503:8502"  # Use 8503 instead
262 |   - "5055:5055"  # Keep API port same
263 | ```
264 | 
265 | Then access at `http://localhost:8503`
266 | 
267 | ---
268 | 
269 | ### API Key Not Working
270 | 
271 | 1. Double-check your API key in the file (no extra spaces)
272 | 2. Verify key is valid at provider's website
273 | 3. Check you added credits to your account
274 | 4. Restart: `docker compose restart api`
275 | 
276 | ---
277 | 
278 | ### Database Connection Issues
279 | 
280 | Check SurrealDB is running:
281 | ```bash
282 | docker compose logs surrealdb
283 | ```
284 | 
285 | Reset database:
286 | ```bash
287 | docker compose down -v
288 | docker compose up -d
289 | ```
290 | 
291 | ### Database Permission Denied (Linux)
292 | 
293 | If you see `Permission denied` or `Failed to create RocksDB directory` in SurrealDB logs:
294 | 
295 | ```bash
296 | docker compose logs surrealdb | grep -i permission
297 | ```
298 | 
299 | This happens because SurrealDB runs as a non-root user but Docker creates bind mount directories as root. Add `user: root` to the surrealdb service:
300 | 
301 | ```yaml
302 | surrealdb:
303 |   image: surrealdb/surrealdb:v2
304 |   user: root  # Fix for Linux bind mount permissions
305 |   # ... rest of config
306 | ```
307 | 
308 | Then restart:
309 | ```bash
310 | docker compose down -v
311 | docker compose up -d
312 | ```
313 | 
314 | ---
315 | 
316 | ## Next Steps
317 | 
318 | 1. **Add Content**: Sources, notebooks, documents
319 | 2. **Configure Models**: Settings → Models (choose your preferences)
320 | 3. **Explore Features**: Chat, search, transformations
321 | 4. **Read Guide**: [User Guide](../3-USER-GUIDE/index.md)
322 | 
323 | ---
324 | 
325 | ## Production Deployment
326 | 
327 | For production use, see:
328 | - [Security Hardening](https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook/blob/main/docs/deployment/security.md)
329 | - [Reverse Proxy](https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook/blob/main/docs/deployment/reverse-proxy.md)
330 | 
331 | ---
332 | 
333 | ## Getting Help
334 | 
335 | - **Discord**: [Community support](https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w)
336 | - **Issues**: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook/issues)
337 | - **Docs**: [Full documentation](../index.md)
338 |

  1 | 'use client'
  2 | 
  3 | import { Model, ProviderAvailability } from '@/lib/types/models'
  4 | import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
  5 | import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
  6 | import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
  7 | import { AddModelForm } from './AddModelForm'
  8 | import { Bot, Mic, Volume2, Search, Trash2, X, ChevronDown, ChevronUp } from 'lucide-react'
  9 | import { LoadingSpinner } from '@/components/common/LoadingSpinner'
 10 | import { useDeleteModel } from '@/lib/hooks/use-models'
 11 | import { ConfirmDialog } from '@/components/common/ConfirmDialog'
 12 | import { useState, useMemo } from 'react'
 13 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
 14 | 
 15 | interface ModelTypeSectionProps {
 16 |   type: 'language' | 'embedding' | 'text_to_speech' | 'speech_to_text'
 17 |   models: Model[]
 18 |   providers: ProviderAvailability
 19 |   isLoading: boolean
 20 | }
 21 | 
 22 | const COLLAPSED_ITEM_COUNT = 5
 23 | 
 24 | export function ModelTypeSection({ type, models, providers, isLoading }: ModelTypeSectionProps) {
 25 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 26 |   const [deleteModel, setDeleteModel] = useState<Model | null>(null)
 27 |   const [selectedProvider, setSelectedProvider] = useState<string | null>(null)
 28 |   const [isExpanded, setIsExpanded] = useState(false)
 29 |   const deleteModelMutation = useDeleteModel()
 30 | 
 31 |   const getTypeInfo = () => {
 32 |     switch (type) {
 33 |       case 'language':
 34 |         return {
 35 |           title: t.models.language,
 36 |           description: t.models.languageDesc,
 37 |           icon: Bot,
 38 |           iconColor: 'text-blue-500',
 39 |           bgColor: 'bg-blue-50 dark:bg-blue-950/20'
 40 |         }
 41 |       case 'embedding':
 42 |         return {
 43 |           title: t.models.embedding,
 44 |           description: t.models.embeddingDesc,
 45 |           icon: Search,
 46 |           iconColor: 'text-green-500',
 47 |           bgColor: 'bg-green-50 dark:bg-green-950/20'
 48 |         }
 49 |       case 'text_to_speech':
 50 |         return {
 51 |           title: t.models.tts,
 52 |           description: t.models.ttsDesc,
 53 |           icon: Volume2,
 54 |           iconColor: 'text-purple-500',
 55 |           bgColor: 'bg-purple-50 dark:bg-purple-950/20'
 56 |         }
 57 |       case 'speech_to_text':
 58 |         return {
 59 |           title: t.models.stt,
 60 |           description: t.models.sttDesc,
 61 |           icon: Mic,
 62 |           iconColor: 'text-orange-500',
 63 |           bgColor: 'bg-orange-50 dark:bg-orange-950/20'
 64 |         }
 65 |     }
 66 |   }
 67 | 
 68 |   const { title, description, icon: Icon, iconColor, bgColor } = getTypeInfo()
 69 |   
 70 |   // Filter and sort models
 71 |   const filteredModels = useMemo(() => {
 72 |     let filtered = models.filter(model => model.type === type)
 73 |     
 74 |     // Apply provider filter if selected
 75 |     if (selectedProvider) {
 76 |       filtered = filtered.filter(model => model.provider === selectedProvider)
 77 |     }
 78 |     
 79 |     // Sort by name alphabetically
 80 |     return filtered.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))
 81 |   }, [models, type, selectedProvider])
 82 | 
 83 |   // Get unique providers for this model type
 84 |   const modelProviders = useMemo(() => {
 85 |     const typeModels = models.filter(model => model.type === type)
 86 |     const uniqueProviders = [...new Set(typeModels.map(m => m.provider))]
 87 |     return uniqueProviders.sort()
 88 |   }, [models, type])
 89 | 
 90 |   const handleDelete = () => {
 91 |     if (deleteModel) {
 92 |       deleteModelMutation.mutate(deleteModel.id)
 93 |       setDeleteModel(null)
 94 |     }
 95 |   }
 96 | 
 97 |   return (
 98 |     <>
 99 |       <Card className="h-full">
100 |         <CardHeader className="pb-3">
101 |           <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-2">
102 |             <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
103 |               <div className={`rounded-lg p-2 ${bgColor}`}>
104 |                 <Icon className={`h-5 w-5 ${iconColor}`} />
105 |               </div>
106 |               <div>
107 |                 <CardTitle className="text-base">{title}</CardTitle>
108 |                 <CardDescription className="text-xs">{description}</CardDescription>
109 |               </div>
110 |             </div>
111 |             <AddModelForm modelType={type} providers={providers} />
112 |           </div>
113 |         </CardHeader>
114 |         <CardContent className="pt-0">
115 |           {/* Provider filter badges */}
116 |           {modelProviders.length > 1 && (
117 |             <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-1 mb-3">
118 |               <Badge
119 |                 variant={selectedProvider === null ? "default" : "outline"}
120 |                 className="cursor-pointer text-xs"
121 |                 onClick={() => setSelectedProvider(null)}
122 |               >
123 |                 {t.models.all}
124 |               </Badge>
125 |               {modelProviders.map(provider => (
126 |                 <Badge
127 |                   key={provider}
128 |                   variant={selectedProvider === provider ? "default" : "outline"}
129 |                   className="cursor-pointer text-xs capitalize"
130 |                   onClick={() => setSelectedProvider(provider === selectedProvider ? null : provider)}
131 |                 >
132 |                   {provider}
133 |                   {selectedProvider === provider && (
134 |                     <X className="ml-1 h-2.5 w-2.5" />
135 |                   )}
136 |                 </Badge>
137 |               ))}
138 |             </div>
139 |           )}
140 | 
141 |           {isLoading ? (
142 |             <div className="flex items-center justify-center py-6">
143 |               <LoadingSpinner />
144 |             </div>
145 |           ) : filteredModels.length === 0 ? (
146 |             <div className="text-center py-6 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
147 |               {selectedProvider 
148 |                 ? t.models.noProviderModelsConfigured.replace('{provider}', selectedProvider)
149 |                 : t.models.noModelsConfigured
150 |               }
151 |             </div>
152 |           ) : (
153 |             <div className="space-y-2">
154 |               <div className={`space-y-2 ${!isExpanded && filteredModels.length > COLLAPSED_ITEM_COUNT ? 'max-h-[280px] overflow-hidden relative' : ''}`}>
155 |                 {filteredModels.slice(0, isExpanded ? undefined : COLLAPSED_ITEM_COUNT).map(model => (
156 |                   <div key={model.id} className="flex items-center gap-2 group">
157 |                     <div className="flex-1 flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-2 rounded-md border bg-muted/30">
158 |                       <span className="font-medium text-sm">{model.name}</span>
159 |                       <Badge variant="outline" className="text-xs">
160 |                         {model.provider}
161 |                       </Badge>
162 |                     </div>
163 |                     <Button
164 |                       variant="ghost"
165 |                       size="icon"
166 |                       className="h-8 w-8 opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 transition-opacity"
167 |                       onClick={() => setDeleteModel(model)}
168 |                     >
169 |                       <Trash2 className="h-3.5 w-3.5 text-muted-foreground hover:text-destructive" />
170 |                     </Button>
171 |                   </div>
172 |                 ))}
173 |                 {!isExpanded && filteredModels.length > COLLAPSED_ITEM_COUNT && (
174 |                   <div className="absolute bottom-0 left-0 right-0 h-20 bg-gradient-to-t from-background to-transparent pointer-events-none" />
175 |                 )}
176 |               </div>
177 |               {filteredModels.length > COLLAPSED_ITEM_COUNT && (
178 |                 <Button
179 |                   variant="ghost"
180 |                   size="sm"
181 |                   onClick={() => setIsExpanded(!isExpanded)}
182 |                   className="w-full mt-2"
183 |                 >
184 |                   {isExpanded ? (
185 |                     <>
186 |                       <ChevronUp className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
187 |                       {t.models.seeLess}
188 |                     </>
189 |                   ) : (
190 |                     <>
191 |                       <ChevronDown className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
192 |                       {t.models.showMore.replace('{count}', (filteredModels.length - COLLAPSED_ITEM_COUNT).toString())}
193 |                     </>
194 |                   )}
195 |                 </Button>
196 |               )}
197 |             </div>
198 |           )}
199 |         </CardContent>
200 |       </Card>
201 | 
202 |       <ConfirmDialog
203 |         open={!!deleteModel}
204 |         onOpenChange={(open) => !open && setDeleteModel(null)}
205 |         title={t.models.deleteModel}
206 |         description={t.models.deleteModelDesc.replace('{name}', deleteModel?.name || '')}
207 |         confirmText={t.common.delete}
208 |         confirmVariant="destructive"
209 |         onConfirm={handleDelete}
210 |       />
211 |     </>
212 |   )
213 | }

/docs/5-CONFIGURATION/security.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Security Configuration
  2 | 
  3 | Protect your Open Notebook deployment with password authentication and production hardening.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## When to Use Password Protection
  8 | 
  9 | ### Use it for:
 10 | - Public cloud deployments (PikaPods, Railway, DigitalOcean)
 11 | - Shared network environments
 12 | - Any deployment accessible beyond localhost
 13 | 
 14 | ### You can skip it for:
 15 | - Local development on your machine
 16 | - Private, isolated networks
 17 | - Single-user local setups
 18 | 
 19 | ---
 20 | 
 21 | ## Quick Setup
 22 | 
 23 | ### Docker Deployment
 24 | 
 25 | ```yaml
 26 | # docker-compose.yml
 27 | services:
 28 |   open_notebook:
 29 |     image: lfnovo/open_notebook:v1-latest-single
 30 |     pull_policy: always
 31 |     environment:
 32 |       - OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
 33 |       - OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=your_secure_password
 34 |     # ... rest of config
 35 | ```
 36 | 
 37 | Or using environment file:
 38 | 
 39 | ```bash
 40 | # docker.env
 41 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
 42 | OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=your_secure_password
 43 | ```
 44 | 
 45 | ### Development Setup
 46 | 
 47 | ```bash
 48 | # .env
 49 | OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=your_secure_password
 50 | ```
 51 | 
 52 | ---
 53 | 
 54 | ## Password Requirements
 55 | 
 56 | ### Good Passwords
 57 | 
 58 | ```bash
 59 | # Strong: 20+ characters, mixed case, numbers, symbols
 60 | OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=MySecure2024!Research#Tool
 61 | OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=Notebook$Dev$2024$Strong!
 62 | 
 63 | # Generated (recommended)
 64 | OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -base64 24)
 65 | ```
 66 | 
 67 | ### Bad Passwords
 68 | 
 69 | ```bash
 70 | # DON'T use these
 71 | OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=password123
 72 | OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=opennotebook
 73 | OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=admin
 74 | ```
 75 | 
 76 | ---
 77 | 
 78 | ## How It Works
 79 | 
 80 | ### Frontend Protection
 81 | 
 82 | 1. Login form appears on first visit
 83 | 2. Password stored in browser session
 84 | 3. Session persists until browser closes
 85 | 4. Clear browser data to log out
 86 | 
 87 | ### API Protection
 88 | 
 89 | All API endpoints require authentication:
 90 | 
 91 | ```bash
 92 | # Authenticated request
 93 | curl -H "Authorization: Bearer your_password" \
 94 |   http://localhost:5055/api/notebooks
 95 | 
 96 | # Unauthenticated (will fail)
 97 | curl http://localhost:5055/api/notebooks
 98 | # Returns: {"detail": "Missing authorization header"}
 99 | ```
100 | 
101 | ### Unprotected Endpoints
102 | 
103 | These work without authentication:
104 | 
105 | - `/health` - System health check
106 | - `/docs` - API documentation
107 | - `/openapi.json` - OpenAPI spec
108 | 
109 | ---
110 | 
111 | ## API Authentication Examples
112 | 
113 | ### curl
114 | 
115 | ```bash
116 | # List notebooks
117 | curl -H "Authorization: Bearer your_password" \
118 |   http://localhost:5055/api/notebooks
119 | 
120 | # Create notebook
121 | curl -X POST \
122 |   -H "Authorization: Bearer your_password" \
123 |   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
124 |   -d '{"name": "My Notebook", "description": "Research notes"}' \
125 |   http://localhost:5055/api/notebooks
126 | 
127 | # Upload file
128 | curl -X POST \
129 |   -H "Authorization: Bearer your_password" \
130 |   -F "file=@document.pdf" \
131 |   http://localhost:5055/api/sources/upload
132 | ```
133 | 
134 | ### Python
135 | 
136 | ```python
137 | import requests
138 | 
139 | class OpenNotebookClient:
140 |     def __init__(self, base_url: str, password: str):
141 |         self.base_url = base_url
142 |         self.headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {password}"}
143 | 
144 |     def get_notebooks(self):
145 |         response = requests.get(
146 |             f"{self.base_url}/api/notebooks",
147 |             headers=self.headers
148 |         )
149 |         return response.json()
150 | 
151 |     def create_notebook(self, name: str, description: str = None):
152 |         response = requests.post(
153 |             f"{self.base_url}/api/notebooks",
154 |             headers=self.headers,
155 |             json={"name": name, "description": description}
156 |         )
157 |         return response.json()
158 | 
159 | # Usage
160 | client = OpenNotebookClient("http://localhost:5055", "your_password")
161 | notebooks = client.get_notebooks()
162 | ```
163 | 
164 | ### JavaScript/TypeScript
165 | 
166 | ```javascript
167 | const API_URL = 'http://localhost:5055';
168 | const PASSWORD = 'your_password';
169 | 
170 | async function getNotebooks() {
171 |   const response = await fetch(`${API_URL}/api/notebooks`, {
172 |     headers: {
173 |       'Authorization': `Bearer ${PASSWORD}`
174 |     }
175 |   });
176 |   return response.json();
177 | }
178 | ```
179 | 
180 | ---
181 | 
182 | ## Production Hardening
183 | 
184 | ### Docker Security
185 | 
186 | ```yaml
187 | services:
188 |   open_notebook:
189 |     image: lfnovo/open_notebook:v1-latest-single
190 |     pull_policy: always
191 |     ports:
192 |       - "127.0.0.1:8502:8502"  # Bind to localhost only
193 |     environment:
194 |       - OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=your_secure_password
195 |     security_opt:
196 |       - no-new-privileges:true
197 |     deploy:
198 |       resources:
199 |         limits:
200 |           memory: 2G
201 |           cpus: "1.0"
202 |     restart: always
203 | ```
204 | 
205 | ### Firewall Configuration
206 | 
207 | ```bash
208 | # UFW (Ubuntu)
209 | sudo ufw allow ssh
210 | sudo ufw allow 80/tcp
211 | sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
212 | sudo ufw deny 8502/tcp   # Block direct access
213 | sudo ufw deny 5055/tcp   # Block direct API access
214 | sudo ufw enable
215 | 
216 | # iptables
217 | iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
218 | iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
219 | iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
220 | iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 8502 -j DROP
221 | iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 5055 -j DROP
222 | ```
223 | 
224 | ### Reverse Proxy with SSL
225 | 
226 | See [Reverse Proxy Configuration](reverse-proxy.md) for complete nginx/Caddy/Traefik setup with HTTPS.
227 | 
228 | ---
229 | 
230 | ## Security Limitations
231 | 
232 | Open Notebook's password protection provides **basic access control**, not enterprise-grade security:
233 | 
234 | | Feature | Status |
235 | |---------|--------|
236 | | Password transmission | Plain text (use HTTPS!) |
237 | | Password storage | In memory |
238 | | User management | Single password for all |
239 | | Session timeout | None (until browser close) |
240 | | Rate limiting | None |
241 | | Audit logging | None |
242 | 
243 | ### Risk Mitigation
244 | 
245 | 1. **Always use HTTPS** - Encrypt traffic with TLS
246 | 2. **Strong passwords** - 20+ characters, complex
247 | 3. **Network security** - Firewall, VPN for sensitive deployments
248 | 4. **Regular updates** - Keep containers and dependencies updated
249 | 5. **Monitoring** - Check logs for suspicious activity
250 | 6. **Backups** - Regular backups of data
251 | 
252 | ---
253 | 
254 | ## Enterprise Considerations
255 | 
256 | For deployments requiring advanced security:
257 | 
258 | | Need | Solution |
259 | |------|----------|
260 | | SSO/OAuth | Implement OAuth2/SAML proxy |
261 | | Role-based access | Custom middleware |
262 | | Audit logging | Log aggregation service |
263 | | Rate limiting | API gateway or nginx |
264 | | Data encryption | Encrypt volumes at rest |
265 | | Network segmentation | Docker networks, VPC |
266 | 
267 | ---
268 | 
269 | ## Troubleshooting
270 | 
271 | ### Password Not Working
272 | 
273 | ```bash
274 | # Check env var is set
275 | docker exec open-notebook env | grep OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD
276 | 
277 | # Check logs
278 | docker logs open-notebook | grep -i auth
279 | 
280 | # Test API directly
281 | curl -H "Authorization: Bearer your_password" \
282 |   http://localhost:5055/health
283 | ```
284 | 
285 | ### 401 Unauthorized Errors
286 | 
287 | ```bash
288 | # Check header format
289 | curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer your_password" \
290 |   http://localhost:5055/api/notebooks
291 | 
292 | # Verify password matches
293 | echo "Password length: $(echo -n $OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD | wc -c)"
294 | ```
295 | 
296 | ### Cannot Access After Setting Password
297 | 
298 | 1. Clear browser cache and cookies
299 | 2. Try incognito/private mode
300 | 3. Check browser console for errors
301 | 4. Verify password is correct in environment
302 | 
303 | ### Security Testing
304 | 
305 | ```bash
306 | # Without password (should fail)
307 | curl http://localhost:5055/api/notebooks
308 | # Expected: {"detail": "Missing authorization header"}
309 | 
310 | # With correct password (should succeed)
311 | curl -H "Authorization: Bearer your_password" \
312 |   http://localhost:5055/api/notebooks
313 | 
314 | # Health check (should work without password)
315 | curl http://localhost:5055/health
316 | ```
317 | 
318 | ---
319 | 
320 | ## Reporting Security Issues
321 | 
322 | If you discover security vulnerabilities:
323 | 
324 | 1. **Do NOT open public issues**
325 | 2. Contact maintainers directly
326 | 3. Provide detailed information
327 | 4. Allow time for fixes before disclosure
328 | 
329 | ---
330 | 
331 | ## Related
332 | 
333 | - **[Reverse Proxy](reverse-proxy.md)** - HTTPS and SSL setup
334 | - **[Advanced Configuration](advanced.md)** - Ports, timeouts, and SSL settings
335 | - **[Environment Reference](environment-reference.md)** - All configuration options
336 |

  1 | import json
  2 | from typing import AsyncGenerator
  3 | 
  4 | from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException
  5 | from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
  6 | from loguru import logger
  7 | 
  8 | from api.models import AskRequest, AskResponse, SearchRequest, SearchResponse
  9 | from open_notebook.ai.models import Model, model_manager
 10 | from open_notebook.domain.notebook import text_search, vector_search
 11 | from open_notebook.exceptions import DatabaseOperationError, InvalidInputError
 12 | from open_notebook.graphs.ask import graph as ask_graph
 13 | 
 14 | router = APIRouter()
 15 | 
 16 | 
 17 | @router.post("/search", response_model=SearchResponse)
 18 | async def search_knowledge_base(search_request: SearchRequest):
 19 |     """Search the knowledge base using text or vector search."""
 20 |     try:
 21 |         if search_request.type == "vector":
 22 |             # Check if embedding model is available for vector search
 23 |             if not await model_manager.get_embedding_model():
 24 |                 raise HTTPException(
 25 |                     status_code=400,
 26 |                     detail="Vector search requires an embedding model. Please configure one in the Models section.",
 27 |                 )
 28 | 
 29 |             results = await vector_search(
 30 |                 keyword=search_request.query,
 31 |                 results=search_request.limit,
 32 |                 source=search_request.search_sources,
 33 |                 note=search_request.search_notes,
 34 |                 minimum_score=search_request.minimum_score,
 35 |             )
 36 |         else:
 37 |             # Text search
 38 |             results = await text_search(
 39 |                 keyword=search_request.query,
 40 |                 results=search_request.limit,
 41 |                 source=search_request.search_sources,
 42 |                 note=search_request.search_notes,
 43 |             )
 44 | 
 45 |         return SearchResponse(
 46 |             results=results or [],
 47 |             total_count=len(results) if results else 0,
 48 |             search_type=search_request.type,
 49 |         )
 50 | 
 51 |     except InvalidInputError as e:
 52 |         raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))
 53 |     except DatabaseOperationError as e:
 54 |         logger.error(f"Database error during search: {str(e)}")
 55 |         raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Search failed: {str(e)}")
 56 |     except Exception as e:
 57 |         logger.error(f"Unexpected error during search: {str(e)}")
 58 |         raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Search failed: {str(e)}")
 59 | 
 60 | 
 61 | async def stream_ask_response(
 62 |     question: str, strategy_model: Model, answer_model: Model, final_answer_model: Model
 63 | ) -> AsyncGenerator[str, None]:
 64 |     """Stream the ask response as Server-Sent Events."""
 65 |     try:
 66 |         final_answer = None
 67 | 
 68 |         async for chunk in ask_graph.astream(
 69 |             input=dict(question=question),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
 70 |             config=dict(
 71 |                 configurable=dict(
 72 |                     strategy_model=strategy_model.id,
 73 |                     answer_model=answer_model.id,
 74 |                     final_answer_model=final_answer_model.id,
 75 |                 )
 76 |             ),
 77 |             stream_mode="updates",
 78 |         ):
 79 |             if "agent" in chunk:
 80 |                 strategy_data = {
 81 |                     "type": "strategy",
 82 |                     "reasoning": chunk["agent"]["strategy"].reasoning,
 83 |                     "searches": [
 84 |                         {"term": search.term, "instructions": search.instructions}
 85 |                         for search in chunk["agent"]["strategy"].searches
 86 |                     ],
 87 |                 }
 88 |                 yield f"data: {json.dumps(strategy_data)}\n\n"
 89 | 
 90 |             elif "provide_answer" in chunk:
 91 |                 for answer in chunk["provide_answer"]["answers"]:
 92 |                     answer_data = {"type": "answer", "content": answer}
 93 |                     yield f"data: {json.dumps(answer_data)}\n\n"
 94 | 
 95 |             elif "write_final_answer" in chunk:
 96 |                 final_answer = chunk["write_final_answer"]["final_answer"]
 97 |                 final_data = {"type": "final_answer", "content": final_answer}
 98 |                 yield f"data: {json.dumps(final_data)}\n\n"
 99 | 
100 |         # Send completion signal
101 |         completion_data = {"type": "complete", "final_answer": final_answer}
102 |         yield f"data: {json.dumps(completion_data)}\n\n"
103 | 
104 |     except Exception as e:
105 |         logger.error(f"Error in ask streaming: {str(e)}")
106 |         error_data = {"type": "error", "message": str(e)}
107 |         yield f"data: {json.dumps(error_data)}\n\n"
108 | 
109 | 
110 | @router.post("/search/ask")
111 | async def ask_knowledge_base(ask_request: AskRequest):
112 |     """Ask the knowledge base a question using AI models."""
113 |     try:
114 |         # Validate models exist
115 |         strategy_model = await Model.get(ask_request.strategy_model)
116 |         answer_model = await Model.get(ask_request.answer_model)
117 |         final_answer_model = await Model.get(ask_request.final_answer_model)
118 | 
119 |         if not strategy_model:
120 |             raise HTTPException(
121 |                 status_code=400,
122 |                 detail=f"Strategy model {ask_request.strategy_model} not found",
123 |             )
124 |         if not answer_model:
125 |             raise HTTPException(
126 |                 status_code=400,
127 |                 detail=f"Answer model {ask_request.answer_model} not found",
128 |             )
129 |         if not final_answer_model:
130 |             raise HTTPException(
131 |                 status_code=400,
132 |                 detail=f"Final answer model {ask_request.final_answer_model} not found",
133 |             )
134 | 
135 |         # Check if embedding model is available
136 |         if not await model_manager.get_embedding_model():
137 |             raise HTTPException(
138 |                 status_code=400,
139 |                 detail="Ask feature requires an embedding model. Please configure one in the Models section.",
140 |             )
141 | 
142 |         # For streaming response
143 |         return StreamingResponse(
144 |             stream_ask_response(
145 |                 ask_request.question, strategy_model, answer_model, final_answer_model
146 |             ),
147 |             media_type="text/plain",
148 |         )
149 | 
150 |     except HTTPException:
151 |         raise
152 |     except Exception as e:
153 |         logger.error(f"Error in ask endpoint: {str(e)}")
154 |         raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Ask operation failed: {str(e)}")
155 | 
156 |

159 |     """Ask the knowledge base a question and return a simple response (non-streaming)."""
160 |     try:

163 |         answer_model = await Model.get(ask_request.answer_model)
164 |         final_answer_model = await Model.get(ask_request.final_answer_model)
165 | 
166 |         if not strategy_model:
167 |             raise HTTPException(
168 |                 status_code=400,
169 |                 detail=f"Strategy model {ask_request.strategy_model} not found",
170 |             )
171 |         if not answer_model:
172 |             raise HTTPException(
173 |                 status_code=400,
174 |                 detail=f"Answer model {ask_request.answer_model} not found",
175 |             )
176 |         if not final_answer_model:
177 |             raise HTTPException(
178 |                 status_code=400,
179 |                 detail=f"Final answer model {ask_request.final_answer_model} not found",
180 |             )
181 | 
182 |         # Check if embedding model is available
183 |         if not await model_manager.get_embedding_model():
184 |             raise HTTPException(
185 |                 status_code=400,
186 |                 detail="Ask feature requires an embedding model. Please configure one in the Models section.",
187 |             )
188 | 
189 |         # Run the ask graph and get final result
190 |         final_answer = None
191 |         async for chunk in ask_graph.astream(
192 |             input=dict(question=ask_request.question),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
193 |             config=dict(
194 |                 configurable=dict(
195 |                     strategy_model=strategy_model.id,
196 |                     answer_model=answer_model.id,
197 |                     final_answer_model=final_answer_model.id,
198 |                 )
199 |             ),
200 |             stream_mode="updates",
201 |         ):
202 |             if "write_final_answer" in chunk:
203 |                 final_answer = chunk["write_final_answer"]["final_answer"]
204 | 
205 |         if not final_answer:
206 |             raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="No answer generated")
207 | 
208 |         return AskResponse(answer=final_answer, question=ask_request.question)
209 | 
210 |     except HTTPException:
211 |         raise
212 |     except Exception as e:
213 |         logger.error(f"Error in ask simple endpoint: {str(e)}")
214 |         raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Ask operation failed: {str(e)}")

 21 | class TestMeanPoolEmbeddings:
 22 |     """Test suite for mean pooling functionality."""
 23 | 
 24 |     @pytest.mark.asyncio
 25 |     async def test_single_embedding(self):
 26 |         """Test mean pooling with single embedding returns normalized version."""
 27 |         embedding = [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]
 28 |         result = await mean_pool_embeddings([embedding])
 29 |         assert len(result) == 3
 30 |         # Should be normalized (already unit length)
 31 |         assert abs(result[0] - 1.0) < 0.001
 32 |         assert abs(result[1]) < 0.001
 33 |         assert abs(result[2]) < 0.001
 34 | 
 35 |     @pytest.mark.asyncio
 36 |     async def test_two_embeddings(self):
 37 |         """Test mean pooling with two embeddings."""
 38 |         embeddings = [
 39 |             [1.0, 0.0, 0.0],
 40 |             [0.0, 1.0, 0.0],
 41 |         ]
 42 |         result = await mean_pool_embeddings(embeddings)
 43 |         assert len(result) == 3
 44 |         # Mean of normalized vectors, then normalized
 45 |         # Result should be roughly [0.707, 0.707, 0]
 46 |         assert abs(result[0] - result[1]) < 0.001  # x and y should be equal
 47 |         assert abs(result[2]) < 0.001  # z should be ~0
 48 | 
 49 |     @pytest.mark.asyncio
 50 |     async def test_identical_embeddings(self):
 51 |         """Test mean pooling with identical embeddings."""
 52 |         embedding = [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5]
 53 |         embeddings = [embedding, embedding, embedding]
 54 |         result = await mean_pool_embeddings(embeddings)
 55 |         assert len(result) == 4
 56 |         # Result should be same direction, just normalized
 57 |         # Original is already normalized if we normalize it
 58 |         import numpy as np
 59 |         orig_norm = np.linalg.norm(embedding)
 60 |         expected = [v / orig_norm for v in embedding]
 61 |         for i in range(4):
 62 |             assert abs(result[i] - expected[i]) < 0.001
 63 | 
 64 |     @pytest.mark.asyncio
 65 |     async def test_empty_list_raises(self):
 66 |         """Test that empty list raises ValueError."""
 67 |         with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="empty"):
 68 |             await mean_pool_embeddings([])
 69 | 
 70 |     @pytest.mark.asyncio
 71 |     async def test_normalization(self):
 72 |         """Test that result is normalized to unit length."""
 73 |         embeddings = [
 74 |             [3.0, 4.0, 0.0],  # Not unit length
 75 |             [0.0, 5.0, 0.0],  # Not unit length
 76 |         ]
 77 |         result = await mean_pool_embeddings(embeddings)
 78 |         # Check result is unit length

  1 | 'use client'
  2 | 
  3 | import { useState, useMemo } from 'react'
  4 | import { NoteResponse } from '@/lib/types/api'
  5 | import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
  6 | import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
  7 | import {
  8 |   DropdownMenu,
  9 |   DropdownMenuContent,
 10 |   DropdownMenuItem,
 11 |   DropdownMenuTrigger,
 12 | } from '@/components/ui/dropdown-menu'
 13 | import { Plus, StickyNote, Bot, User, MoreVertical, Trash2 } from 'lucide-react'
 14 | import { LoadingSpinner } from '@/components/common/LoadingSpinner'
 15 | import { EmptyState } from '@/components/common/EmptyState'
 16 | import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
 17 | import { NoteEditorDialog } from './NoteEditorDialog'
 18 | import { getDateLocale } from '@/lib/utils/date-locale'
 19 | import { formatDistanceToNow } from 'date-fns'
 20 | import { ContextToggle } from '@/components/common/ContextToggle'
 21 | import { ContextMode } from '../[id]/page'
 22 | import { useDeleteNote } from '@/lib/hooks/use-notes'
 23 | import { ConfirmDialog } from '@/components/common/ConfirmDialog'
 24 | import { CollapsibleColumn, createCollapseButton } from '@/components/notebooks/CollapsibleColumn'
 25 | import { useNotebookColumnsStore } from '@/lib/stores/notebook-columns-store'
 26 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
 27 | 
 28 | interface NotesColumnProps {
 29 |   notes?: NoteResponse[]
 30 |   isLoading: boolean
 31 |   notebookId: string
 32 |   contextSelections?: Record<string, ContextMode>
 33 |   onContextModeChange?: (noteId: string, mode: ContextMode) => void
 34 | }
 35 | 
 36 | export function NotesColumn({
 37 |   notes,
 38 |   isLoading,
 39 |   notebookId,
 40 |   contextSelections,
 41 |   onContextModeChange
 42 | }: NotesColumnProps) {
 43 |   const { t, language } = useTranslation()
 44 |   const [showAddDialog, setShowAddDialog] = useState(false)
 45 |   const [editingNote, setEditingNote] = useState<NoteResponse | null>(null)
 46 |   const [deleteDialogOpen, setDeleteDialogOpen] = useState(false)
 47 |   const [noteToDelete, setNoteToDelete] = useState<string | null>(null)
 48 | 
 49 |   const deleteNote = useDeleteNote()
 50 | 
 51 |   // Collapsible column state
 52 |   const { notesCollapsed, toggleNotes } = useNotebookColumnsStore()
 53 |   const collapseButton = useMemo(
 54 |     () => createCollapseButton(toggleNotes, t.common.notes),
 55 |     [toggleNotes, t.common.notes]
 56 |   )
 57 | 
 58 |   const handleDeleteClick = (noteId: string) => {
 59 |     setNoteToDelete(noteId)
 60 |     setDeleteDialogOpen(true)
 61 |   }
 62 | 
 63 |   const handleDeleteConfirm = async () => {
 64 |     if (!noteToDelete) return
 65 | 
 66 |     try {
 67 |       await deleteNote.mutateAsync(noteToDelete)
 68 |       setDeleteDialogOpen(false)
 69 |       setNoteToDelete(null)
 70 |     } catch (error) {
 71 |       console.error('Failed to delete note:', error)
 72 |     }
 73 |   }
 74 | 
 75 |   return (
 76 |     <>
 77 |       <CollapsibleColumn
 78 |         isCollapsed={notesCollapsed}
 79 |         onToggle={toggleNotes}
 80 |         collapsedIcon={StickyNote}
 81 |         collapsedLabel={t.common.notes}
 82 |       >
 83 |         <Card className="h-full flex flex-col flex-1 overflow-hidden">
 84 |           <CardHeader className="pb-3 flex-shrink-0">
 85 |             <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
 86 |               <CardTitle className="text-lg">{t.common.notes}</CardTitle>
 87 |               <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
 88 |                 <Button
 89 |                   size="sm"
 90 |                   onClick={() => {
 91 |                     setEditingNote(null)
 92 |                     setShowAddDialog(true)
 93 |                   }}
 94 |                 >
 95 |                   <Plus className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
 96 |                   {t.common.writeNote}
 97 |                 </Button>
 98 |                 {collapseButton}
 99 |               </div>
100 |             </div>
101 |           </CardHeader>
102 | 
103 |           <CardContent className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto min-h-0">
104 |             {isLoading ? (
105 |               <div className="flex items-center justify-center py-8">
106 |                 <LoadingSpinner />
107 |               </div>
108 |             ) : !notes || notes.length === 0 ? (
109 |               <EmptyState
110 |                 icon={StickyNote}
111 |                 title={t.notebooks.noNotesYet}
112 |                 description={t.sources.createFirstNote}
113 |               />
114 |             ) : (
115 |               <div className="space-y-3">
116 |                 {notes.map((note) => (
117 |                   <div
118 |                     key={note.id}
119 |                     className="p-3 border rounded-lg card-hover group relative cursor-pointer"
120 |                     onClick={() => setEditingNote(note)}
121 |                   >
122 |                     <div className="flex items-start justify-between mb-2">
123 |                       <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
124 |                         {note.note_type === 'ai' ? (
125 |                           <Bot className="h-4 w-4 text-primary" />
126 |                         ) : (
127 |                           <User className="h-4 w-4 text-muted-foreground" />
128 |                         )}
129 |                         <Badge variant="secondary" className="text-xs">
130 |                           {note.note_type === 'ai' ? t.common.aiGenerated : t.common.human}
131 |                         </Badge>
132 |                       </div>
133 | 
134 |                       <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
135 |                         <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
136 |                           {formatDistanceToNow(new Date(note.updated), { 
137 |                             addSuffix: true,
138 |                             locale: getDateLocale(language)
139 |                           })}
140 |                         </span>
141 | 
142 |                         {/* Context toggle - only show if handler provided */}
143 |                         {onContextModeChange && contextSelections?.[note.id] && (
144 |                           <div onClick={(event) => event.stopPropagation()}>
145 |                             <ContextToggle
146 |                               mode={contextSelections[note.id]}
147 |                               hasInsights={false}
148 |                               onChange={(mode) => onContextModeChange(note.id, mode)}
149 |                             />
150 |                           </div>
151 |                         )}
152 | 
153 |                         {/* Ellipsis menu for delete action */}
154 |                         <DropdownMenu>
155 |                           <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
156 |                             <Button
157 |                               variant="ghost"
158 |                               size="sm"
159 |                               className="h-8 w-8 p-0 opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 transition-opacity"
160 |                               onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
161 |                             >
162 |                               <MoreVertical className="h-4 w-4" />
163 |                             </Button>
164 |                           </DropdownMenuTrigger>
165 |                           <DropdownMenuContent align="end" className="w-48">
166 |                             <DropdownMenuItem
167 |                               onClick={(e) => {
168 |                                 e.stopPropagation()
169 |                                 handleDeleteClick(note.id)
170 |                               }}
171 |                               className="text-red-600 focus:text-red-600"
172 |                             >
173 |                               <Trash2 className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
174 |                               {t.notebooks.deleteNote}
175 |                             </DropdownMenuItem>
176 |                           </DropdownMenuContent>
177 |                         </DropdownMenu>
178 |                       </div>
179 |                     </div>
180 | 
181 |                     {note.title && (
182 |                       <h4 className="text-sm font-medium mb-2">{note.title}</h4>
183 |                     )}
184 | 
185 |                     {note.content && (
186 |                       <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground line-clamp-3">
187 |                         {note.content}
188 |                       </p>
189 |                     )}
190 |                   </div>
191 |                 ))}
192 |               </div>
193 |             )}
194 |           </CardContent>
195 |         </Card>
196 |       </CollapsibleColumn>
197 | 
198 |       <NoteEditorDialog
199 |         open={showAddDialog || Boolean(editingNote)}
200 |         onOpenChange={(open) => {
201 |           if (!open) {
202 |             setShowAddDialog(false)
203 |             setEditingNote(null)
204 |           } else {
205 |             setShowAddDialog(true)
206 |           }
207 |         }}
208 |         notebookId={notebookId}
209 |         note={editingNote ?? undefined}
210 |       />
211 | 
212 |       <ConfirmDialog
213 |         open={deleteDialogOpen}
214 |         onOpenChange={setDeleteDialogOpen}
215 |         title={t.notebooks.deleteNote}
216 |         description={t.notebooks.deleteNoteConfirm}
217 |         confirmText={t.common.delete}
218 |         onConfirm={handleDeleteConfirm}
219 |         isLoading={deleteNote.isPending}
220 |         confirmVariant="destructive"
221 |       />
222 |     </>
223 |   )
224 | }

/prompts/CLAUDE.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Prompts Module
  2 | 
  3 | Jinja2 prompt templates for multi-provider AI workflows in Open Notebook.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Purpose
  6 | 
  7 | Centralized prompt repository using `ai_prompter` library to:
  8 | 1. Separate prompt engineering from Python application logic
  9 | 2. Provide reusable Jinja2 templates with variable injection
 10 | 3. Support multi-stage prompt chains (orchestrated by LangGraph workflows)
 11 | 4. Ensure consistency across similar workflows (chat, search, content generation)
 12 | 
 13 | ## Architecture Overview
 14 | 
 15 | **Template Organization by Workflow**:
 16 | - **`ask/`**: Multi-stage search synthesis (entry → query_process → final_answer)
 17 | - **`chat/`**: Conversational agent with notebook context (system prompt only)
 18 | - **`source_chat/`**: Source-focused chat with insight injection (system prompt only)
 19 | - **`podcast/`**: Podcast generation pipeline (outline → transcript)
 20 | 
 21 | **Rendering Pattern** (all workflows):
 22 | ```python
 23 | from ai_prompter import Prompter
 24 | 
 25 | # Load template + render with variables
 26 | system_prompt = Prompter(prompt_template="ask/entry", parser=parser).render(
 27 |     data=state
 28 | )
 29 | 
 30 | # Then invoke LLM
 31 | model = await provision_langchain_model(system_prompt, ...)
 32 | response = await model.ainvoke(system_prompt)
 33 | ```
 34 | 
 35 | See detailed workflow integration in `open_notebook/graphs/CLAUDE.md` for how each template fits into chat.py, ask.py, source_chat.py.
 36 | 
 37 | ## Prompt Engineering Patterns
 38 | 
 39 | ### 1. Multi-Stage Chain (Ask Workflow)
 40 | 
 41 | Three-template chain for intelligent search:
 42 | 
 43 | ```
 44 | entry.jinja (user question → search strategy)
 45 |     ↓
 46 | query_process.jinja (run each search, generate sub-answer)
 47 |     ↓ (multiple parallel)
 48 | final_answer.jinja (synthesize all results into final response)
 49 | ```
 50 | 
 51 | **Key pattern**: `entry.jinja` generates JSON-structured reasoning (via PydanticOutputParser). Each `query_process.jinja` invocation receives one search term + retrieved results. `final_answer.jinja` combines all answers with proper source citation.
 52 | 
 53 | ### 2. Conditional Variable Injection (Podcast Workflow)
 54 | 
 55 | Templates accept optional variables for context assembly:
 56 | 
 57 | ```jinja
 58 | {% if notebook %}
 59 | # PROJECT INFORMATION
 60 | {{ notebook }}
 61 | {% endif %}
 62 | 
 63 | {% if context %}
 64 | # CONTEXT
 65 | {{ context }}
 66 | {% endif %}
 67 | ```
 68 | 
 69 | Enabled by Jinja2's conditional blocks. Critical for podcast outline (handles list or string context) and source_chat (injects variable notebook/insight data).
 70 | 
 71 | ### 3. Repeated Emphasis on Citation Format (Ask & Chat)
 72 | 
 73 | All response-generating templates emphasize source citation rules:
 74 | - Document ID syntax: `[source:id]`, `[note:id]`, `[insight:id]`
 75 | - "Do not make up document IDs" repeated multiple times
 76 | - Example citations provided inline
 77 | 
 78 | **Rationale**: LLMs naturally hallucinate citations without explicit guidance; repetition + examples reduce hallucination.
 79 | 
 80 | ### 4. Format Instructions Delegation
 81 | 
 82 | Templates accept external `{{ format_instructions }}` variable:
 83 | 
 84 | ```jinja
 85 | # OUTPUT FORMATTING
 86 | {{ format_instructions }}
 87 | ```
 88 | 
 89 | Allows caller to inject JSON schema, XML format, or other output constraints without modifying template. Decouples prompt from output format evolution.
 90 | 
 91 | ### 5. JSON Output with Extended Thinking Support
 92 | 
 93 | Podcast templates include extended thinking pattern:
 94 | 
 95 | ```jinja
 96 | IMPORTANT OUTPUT FORMAT:
 97 | - If you use extended thinking with <think> tags, put ALL your reasoning inside <think></think> tags
 98 | - Put the final JSON output OUTSIDE and AFTER any <think> tags
 99 | ```
100 | 
101 | Guides models with extended thinking capability to separate reasoning from output (cleaner parsing downstream).
102 | 
103 | ## File Catalog
104 | 
105 | **`ask/` - Search Synthesis Pipeline**:
106 | - **entry.jinja**: Analyzes user question, generates search strategy with JSON output (term + instructions per search)
107 | - **query_process.jinja**: Accepts one search term + retrieved results, generates sub-answer with citations
108 | - **final_answer.jinja**: Combines all sub-answers into coherent final response, enforces source citation
109 | 
110 | **`chat/` - Conversational Agent**:
111 | - **system.jinja**: Single system prompt for general chat. Uses conditional blocks for optional notebook context. Emphasizes citation format.
112 | 
113 | **`source_chat/` - Source-Focused Chat**:
114 | - **system.jinja**: Single system prompt for source-specific discussion. Injects source metadata (ID, title, topics) + selected context. Conditional blocks for optional notebook/context data.
115 | 
116 | **`podcast/` - Podcast Generation**:
117 | - **outline.jinja**: Takes briefing + content + speaker profiles (list support via Jinja2 for-loop). Generates JSON outline with segments (name, description, size).
118 | - **transcript.jinja**: Takes outline + segment index + optional existing transcript. Generates JSON dialogue array (speaker name + dialogue). Iterates speakers with for-loop.
119 | 
120 | ## Key Dependencies
121 | 
122 | - **ai_prompter**: Prompter class for Jinja2 template rendering with optional OutputParser binding
123 | - **Jinja2** (transitive via ai_prompter): Template syntax (if/for, filters, variable interpolation)
124 | - **No external AI calls**: Templates are pure text; LLM invocation happens in calling code (graphs/)
125 | 
126 | ## How to Add New Template
127 | 
128 | 1. **Create subdirectory** in `prompts/` matching workflow name (e.g., `prompts/new_workflow/`)
129 | 2. **Define .jinja file(s)** with Jinja2 syntax:
130 |    - Use `{{ variable_name }}` for scalar injection
131 |    - Use `{% if condition %} ... {% endif %}` for optional sections
132 |    - Use `{% for item in list %} ... {% endfor %}` for iteration
133 | 3. **Document template variables** as inline comments (follow existing templates)
134 | 4. **Reference in calling code** (graphs/):
135 |    ```python
136 |    from ai_prompter import Prompter
137 |    prompt = Prompter(prompt_template="new_workflow/template_name").render(data=context_dict)
138 |    ```
139 | 5. **If structured output needed**: Pass `parser=PydanticOutputParser(...)` to Prompter
140 | 6. **Document in graphs/CLAUDE.md** how new template fits into workflow chain
141 | 
142 | ## Important Quirks & Gotchas
143 | 
144 | 1. **Template path syntax**: Uses forward slashes without `.jinja` extension in Prompter. `"ask/entry"` maps to `/prompts/ask/entry.jinja`
145 | 2. **Variable key convention**: All data passed as `data=dict` arg to `.render()`. Template accesses variables directly (e.g., `{{ question }}`). Ensure dict keys match template variable names.
146 | 3. **OutputParser binding**: When using PydanticOutputParser, Prompter auto-injects `{{ format_instructions }}` into template. If template doesn't have this placeholder, parser is ignored.
147 | 4. **Jinja2 whitespace sensitivity**: Template indentation doesn't affect output, but raw newlines do. Use explicit `\n` or trim filters if output formatting matters.
148 | 5. **Conditional blocks are loose**: Jinja2 if-condition evaluates any truthy value (non-empty string, list, dict). `{% if variable %}` is False for empty string/"" but True for any non-empty content.
149 | 6. **For-loop list assumption**: Templates using `{% for item in list %}` don't validate list type. If caller passes string instead of list, iteration happens character-by-character (bug risk).
150 | 7. **No template composition/inheritance**: Templates are flat (no `{% extends %}` or `{% include %}`). Each workflow keeps templates independent to avoid coupling.
151 | 8. **Citation ID format is caller's responsibility**: Templates emphasize citation rules but don't validate. If caller returns wrong ID format, template can't catch it upstream.
152 | 9. **Parser extraction happens post-render**: OutputParser.parse() is called AFTER `.render()` returns string. If template has syntax errors, render fails before parsing logic runs.
153 | 10. **Template cache**: Prompter likely caches loaded templates. File edits require app restart if using cached instance.
154 | 
155 | ## Testing Patterns
156 | 
157 | **Manual render test**:
158 | ```python
159 | from ai_prompter import Prompter
160 | 
161 | prompt = Prompter(prompt_template="ask/entry").render(
162 |     data={"question": "What is RAG?"}
163 | )
164 | print(prompt)  # Inspect Jinja2 output before sending to LLM
165 | ```
166 | 
167 | **With parser**:
168 | ```python
169 | from pydantic import BaseModel
170 | from langchain_core.output_parsers.pydantic import PydanticOutputParser
171 | 
172 | class Strategy(BaseModel):
173 |     reasoning: str
174 |     searches: list
175 | 
176 | parser = PydanticOutputParser(pydantic_object=Strategy)
177 | prompt = Prompter(prompt_template="ask/entry", parser=parser).render(
178 |     data={"question": "..."}
179 | )
180 | # prompt now includes {{ format_instructions }} substitution
181 | ```
182 | 
183 | **Integration test** (invoke full graph):
184 | See `open_notebook/graphs/ask.py` for how entry.jinja is invoked inside ask_graph workflow.
185 | 
186 | ## Reference Documentation
187 | 
188 | - **Jinja2 syntax guide**: See existing templates for for-loop, if-conditional, variable interpolation patterns
189 | - **Graph integration**: `open_notebook/graphs/CLAUDE.md` documents which template is used in which workflow
190 | - **Sub-directory CLAUDE.md files**: `ask/CLAUDE.md`, `chat/CLAUDE.md`, `podcast/CLAUDE.md` (if created) provide template-specific implementation notes
191 |

/docs/5-CONFIGURATION/index.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Configuration - Essential Settings
  2 | 
  3 | Configuration is how you customize Open Notebook for your specific setup. This section covers what you need to know.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## What Needs Configuration?
  8 | 
  9 | Three things:
 10 | 
 11 | 1. **AI Provider** — Which LLM/embedding service you're using (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, etc.)
 12 | 2. **Database** — How to connect to SurrealDB (usually pre-configured)
 13 | 3. **Server** — API URL, ports, timeouts (usually auto-detected)
 14 | 
 15 | ---
 16 | 
 17 | ## Quick Decision: Which Provider?
 18 | 
 19 | ### Option 1: Cloud Provider (Fastest)
 20 | - **OpenRouter (recommended)** (access to all models with one key)
 21 | - **OpenAI** (GPT)
 22 | - **Anthropic** (Claude)
 23 | - **Google Gemini** (multi-modal, long context)
 24 | - **Groq** (ultra-fast inference)
 25 | 
 26 | Setup: Get API key → Set env var → Done
 27 | 
 28 | → Go to **[AI Providers Guide](ai-providers.md)**
 29 | 
 30 | ### Option 2: Local (Free & Private)
 31 | - **Ollama** (open-source models, on your machine)
 32 | 
 33 | → Go to **[Ollama Setup](ollama.md)**
 34 | 
 35 | ### Option 3: OpenAI-Compatible
 36 | - **LM Studio** (local)
 37 | - **Custom endpoints**
 38 | 
 39 | → Go to **[OpenAI-Compatible Guide](openai-compatible.md)**
 40 | 
 41 | ---
 42 | 
 43 | ## Configuration File
 44 | 
 45 | Use the right file depending on your setup.
 46 | 
 47 | ### `.env` (Local Development)
 48 | 
 49 | You will only use .env if you are running Open Notebook locally.
 50 | 
 51 | ```
 52 | Located in: project root
 53 | Use for: Development on your machine
 54 | Format: KEY=value, one per line
 55 | ```
 56 | 
 57 | ### `docker.env` (Docker Deployment)
 58 | 
 59 | You will use this file to hold your environment variables if you are using docker-compose and prefer not to put the variables directly in the compose file. 
 60 | ```
 61 | Located in: project root (or ./docker)
 62 | Use for: Docker deployments
 63 | Format: Same as .env
 64 | Loaded by: docker-compose.yml
 65 | ```
 66 | 
 67 | ---
 68 | 
 69 | ## Most Important Settings
 70 | 
 71 | All of the settings provided below are to be placed inside your environment file (.env or docker.env depending on your setup).
 72 | 
 73 | 
 74 | ###  Surreal Database
 75 | 
 76 | This is the database used by the app.
 77 | 
 78 | ```
 79 | SURREAL_URL=ws://surrealdb:8000/rpc
 80 | SURREAL_USER=root
 81 | SURREAL_PASSWORD=root  # Change in production!
 82 | SURREAL_NAMESPACE=open_notebook
 83 | SURREAL_DATABASE=open_notebook
 84 | ```
 85 | 
 86 | > The only thing that is critical to not miss is the hostname in the `SURREAL_URL`. Check what URL to use based on your deployment, [here](database.md).
 87 | 
 88 | 
 89 | ### AI Provider (API Key or URL)
 90 | 
 91 | We need access to LLMs in order for the app to work. You can use any of the support AI Providers by adding their API Keys. 
 92 | 
 93 | ```
 94 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
 95 | ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
 96 | GOOGLE_API_KEY=...
 97 | OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...
 98 | ```
 99 | 
100 | Or, if you are planning to use only local providers, you can setup Ollama by configuring it's base URL. This will get you set and ready with text and embeddings in one go: 
101 | 
102 | ```
103 | OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434
104 | ```
105 | 
106 | > A lot of people screw up on the Ollama BASE URL by not knowing how to point to their Ollama installation. if you are having trouble connecting to Ollama, see [here](ollama.md).
107 | 
108 | You can also use LM Studio locally if you prefer by using it as an OpenAI compatible endpoint. 
109 | 
110 | ```
111 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:1234/v1
112 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_EMBEDDING=http://localhost:1234/v1
113 | ```
114 | 
115 | > For more installation on using OpenAI compatible endpoints, see [here](openai-compatible.md).
116 | 
117 | 
118 | ### API URL (If Behind Reverse Proxy)
119 | You only need to worry about this if you are deploying on a proxy or if you are changing port information. Otherwise, skip this.
120 | 
121 | ```
122 | API_URL=https://your-domain.com
123 | # Usually auto-detected. Only set if needed.
124 | ```
125 | 
126 | Auto-detection works for most setups.
127 | 
128 | ---
129 | 
130 | ## Configuration by Scenario
131 | 
132 | ### Scenario 1: Docker on Localhost (Default)
133 | ```env
134 | # In docker.env:
135 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
136 | # Everything else uses defaults
137 | # Done!
138 | ```
139 | 
140 | ### Scenario 2: Docker on Remote Server
141 | ```env
142 | # In docker.env:
143 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
144 | API_URL=http://your-server-ip:5055
145 | ```
146 | 
147 | ### Scenario 3: Behind Reverse Proxy (Nginx/Cloudflare)
148 | ```env
149 | # In docker.env:
150 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
151 | API_URL=https://your-domain.com
152 | # The reverse proxy handles HTTPS
153 | ```
154 | 
155 | ### Scenario 4: Using Ollama Locally
156 | ```env
157 | # In .env:
158 | OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://localhost:11434
159 | # No API key needed
160 | ```
161 | 
162 | ### Scenario 5: Using Azure OpenAI
163 | ```env
164 | # In docker.env:
165 | AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key
166 | AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT=https://your-instance.openai.azure.com/
167 | AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION=2024-12-01-preview
168 | ```
169 |

242 | ## How to Add Configuration
243 | 
244 | ### Method 1: Edit `.env` File (Development)
245 | 
246 | ```bash
247 | 1. Open .env in your editor
248 | 2. Find the section for your provider
249 | 3. Uncomment and fill in your API key
250 | 4. Save
251 | 5. Restart services
252 | ```
253 | 
254 | ### Method 2: Set Docker Environment (Deployment)
255 | 
256 | ```bash
257 | # In docker-compose.yml:
258 | services:
259 |   api:
260 |     environment:
261 |       - OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
262 |       - API_URL=https://your-domain.com
263 | ```
264 | 
265 | ### Method 3: Export Environment Variables
266 | 
267 | ```bash
268 | # In your terminal:
269 | export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
270 | export API_URL=https://your-domain.com
271 | 
272 | # Then start services
273 | docker compose up
274 | ```
275 | 
276 | ### Method 4: Use docker.env File
277 | 
278 | ```bash
279 | 1. Create/edit docker.env
280 | 2. Add your configuration
281 | 3. docker-compose automatically loads it
282 | 4. docker compose up
283 | ```

287 | ## Verification
288 | 
289 | After configuration, verify it works:
290 | 
291 | ```
292 | 1. Open your notebook
293 | 2. Go to Settings → Models
294 | 3. You should see your configured provider
295 | 4. Try a simple Chat question
296 | 5. If it responds, configuration is correct!
297 | ```
298 |

300 | 
301 | ## Common Mistakes
302 | 
303 | | Mistake | Problem | Fix |
304 | |---------|---------|-----|
305 | | Forget API key | Models not available | Add OPENAI_API_KEY (or your provider) |
306 | | Wrong database URL | Can't start API | Check SURREAL_URL format |
307 | | Expose port 5055 | "Can't connect to server" | Expose 5055 in docker-compose |
308 | | Typo in env var | Settings ignored | Check spelling (case-sensitive!) |
309 | | Quote mismatch | Value cut off | Use quotes: OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..." |
310 | | Don't restart | Old config still used | Restart services after env changes |
311 |

337 | 3. Start services
338 | 4. Done!
