/CLAUDE.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Open Notebook - Root CLAUDE.md
  2 | 
  3 | This file provides architectural guidance for contributors working on Open Notebook at the project level.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Project Overview
  6 | 
  7 | **Open Notebook** is an open-source, privacy-focused alternative to Google's Notebook LM. It's an AI-powered research assistant enabling users to upload multi-modal content (PDFs, audio, video, web pages), generate intelligent notes, search semantically, chat with AI models, and produce professional podcasts—all with complete control over data and choice of AI providers.
  8 | 
  9 | **Key Values**: Privacy-first, multi-provider AI support, fully self-hosted option, open-source transparency.
 10 | 
 11 | ---
 12 | 
 13 | ## Three-Tier Architecture
 14 | 
 15 | ```
 16 | ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 17 | │              Frontend (React/Next.js)                    │
 18 | │              frontend/ @ port 3000                       │
 19 | ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 20 | │ - Notebooks, sources, notes, chat, podcasts, search UI  │
 21 | │ - Zustand state management, TanStack Query (React Query)│
 22 | │ - Shadcn/ui component library with Tailwind CSS         │
 23 | └────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
 24 |                          │ HTTP REST
 25 | ┌────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
 26 | │              API (FastAPI)                              │
 27 | │              api/ @ port 5055                           │
 28 | ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 29 | │ - REST endpoints for notebooks, sources, notes, chat    │
 30 | │ - LangGraph workflow orchestration                      │
 31 | │ - Job queue for async operations (podcasts)             │
 32 | │ - Multi-provider AI provisioning via Esperanto          │
 33 | └────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
 34 |                          │ SurrealQL
 35 | ┌────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
 36 | │         Database (SurrealDB)                            │
 37 | │         Graph database @ port 8000                      │
 38 | ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 39 | │ - Records: Notebook, Source, Note, ChatSession, etc.    │
 40 | │ - Relationships: source-to-notebook, note-to-source     │
 41 | │ - Vector embeddings for semantic search                 │
 42 | └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 43 | ```
 44 | 
 45 | ---
 46 | 
 47 | ## Useful sources
 48 | 
 49 | User documentation is at @docs/
 50 | 
 51 | ## Tech Stack
 52 | 
 53 | ### Frontend (`frontend/`)
 54 | - **Framework**: Next.js 16 (React 19)
 55 | - **Language**: TypeScript
 56 | - **State Management**: Zustand
 57 | - **Data Fetching**: TanStack Query (React Query)
 58 | - **Styling**: Tailwind CSS + Shadcn/ui
 59 | - **Build Tool**: Webpack (via Next.js)
 60 | - **i18n compatible**: All front-end changes must also consider the translation keys
 61 | 
 62 | ### API Backend (`api/` + `open_notebook/`)
 63 | - **Framework**: FastAPI 0.104+
 64 | - **Language**: Python 3.11+
 65 | - **Workflows**: LangGraph state machines
 66 | - **Database**: SurrealDB async driver
 67 | - **AI Providers**: Esperanto library (8+ providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, Ollama, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI)
 68 | - **Job Queue**: Surreal-Commands for async jobs (podcasts)
 69 | - **Logging**: Loguru
 70 | - **Validation**: Pydantic v2
 71 | - **Testing**: Pytest
 72 | 
 73 | ### Database
 74 | - **SurrealDB**: Graph database with built-in embedding storage and vector search
 75 | - **Schema Migrations**: Automatic on API startup via AsyncMigrationManager
 76 | 
 77 | ### Additional Services
 78 | - **Content Processing**: content-core library (file/URL extraction)
 79 | - **Prompts**: AI-Prompter with Jinja2 templating
 80 | - **Podcast Generation**: podcast-creator library
 81 | - **Embeddings**: Multi-provider via Esperanto
 82 | 
 83 | ---
 84 | 
 85 | ## Architecture Highlights
 86 | 
 87 | ### 1. Async-First Design
 88 | - All database queries, graph invocations, and API calls are async (await)
 89 | - SurrealDB async driver with connection pooling
 90 | - FastAPI handles concurrent requests efficiently
 91 | 
 92 | ### 2. LangGraph Workflows
 93 | - **source.py**: Content ingestion (extract → embed → save)
 94 | - **chat.py**: Conversational agent with message history
 95 | - **ask.py**: Search + synthesis (retrieve relevant sources → LLM)
 96 | - **transformation.py**: Custom transformations on sources
 97 | - All use `provision_langchain_model()` for smart model selection
 98 | 
 99 | ### 3. Multi-Provider AI
100 | - **Esperanto library**: Unified interface to 8+ AI providers
101 | - **ModelManager**: Factory pattern with fallback logic
102 | - **Smart selection**: Detects large contexts, prefers long-context models
103 | - **Override support**: Per-request model configuration
104 | 
105 | ### 4. Database Schema
106 | - **Automatic migrations**: AsyncMigrationManager runs on API startup
107 | - **SurrealDB graph model**: Records with relationships and embeddings
108 | - **Vector search**: Built-in semantic search across all content
109 | - **Transactions**: Repo functions handle ACID operations
110 | 
111 | ### 5. Authentication
112 | - **Current**: Simple password middleware (insecure, dev-only)
113 | - **Production**: Replace with OAuth/JWT (see CONFIGURATION.md)
114 | 
115 | ---
116 | 
117 | ## Important Quirks & Gotchas
118 | 
119 | ### API Startup
120 | - **Migrations run automatically** on startup; check logs for errors
121 | - **Must start API before UI**: UI depends on API for all data
122 | - **SurrealDB must be running**: API fails without database connection
123 | 
124 | ### Frontend-Backend Communication
125 | - **Base API URL**: Configured in `.env.local` (default: http://localhost:5055)
126 | - **CORS enabled**: Configured in `api/main.py` (allow all origins in dev)
127 | - **Rate limiting**: Not built-in; add at proxy layer for production
128 | 
129 | ### LangGraph Workflows
130 | - **Blocking operations**: Chat/podcast workflows may take minutes; no timeout
131 | - **State persistence**: Uses SQLite checkpoint storage in `/data/sqlite-db/`
132 | - **Model fallback**: If primary model fails, falls back to cheaper/smaller model
133 | 
134 | ### Podcast Generation
135 | - **Async job queue**: `podcast_service.py` submits jobs but doesn't wait
136 | - **Track status**: Use `/commands/{command_id}` endpoint to poll status
137 | - **TTS failures**: Fall back to silent audio if speech synthesis fails
138 | 
139 | ### Content Processing
140 | - **File extraction**: Uses content-core library; supports 50+ file types
141 | - **URL handling**: Extracts text + metadata from web pages
142 | - **Large files**: Content processing is sync; may block API briefly
143 | 
144 | ---
145 | 
146 | ## Component References
147 | 
148 | See dedicated CLAUDE.md files for detailed guidance:
149 | 
150 | - **[frontend/CLAUDE.md](frontend/CLAUDE.md)**: React/Next.js architecture, state management, API integration
151 | - **[api/CLAUDE.md](api/CLAUDE.md)**: FastAPI structure, service pattern, endpoint development
152 | - **[open_notebook/CLAUDE.md](open_notebook/CLAUDE.md)**: Backend core, domain models, LangGraph workflows, AI provisioning
153 | - **[open_notebook/domain/CLAUDE.md](open_notebook/domain/CLAUDE.md)**: Data models, repository pattern, search functions
154 | - **[open_notebook/ai/CLAUDE.md](open_notebook/ai/CLAUDE.md)**: ModelManager, AI provider integration, Esperanto usage
155 | - **[open_notebook/graphs/CLAUDE.md](open_notebook/graphs/CLAUDE.md)**: LangGraph workflow design, state machines
156 | - **[open_notebook/database/CLAUDE.md](open_notebook/database/CLAUDE.md)**: SurrealDB operations, migrations, async patterns
157 | 
158 | ---
159 | 
160 | ## Documentation Map
161 | 
162 | - **[README.md](README.md)**: Project overview, features, quick start
163 | - **[docs/index.md](docs/index.md)**: Complete user & deployment documentation
164 | - **[CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md)**: Environment variables, model configuration
165 | - **[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)**: Contribution guidelines
166 | - **[MAINTAINER_GUIDE.md](MAINTAINER_GUIDE.md)**: Release & maintenance procedures
167 | 
168 | ---
169 | 
170 | ## Testing Strategy
171 | 
172 | - **Unit tests**: `tests/test_domain.py`, `test_models_api.py`
173 | - **Graph tests**: `tests/test_graphs.py` (workflow integration)
174 | - **Utils tests**: `tests/test_utils.py`, `tests/test_chunking.py`, `tests/test_embedding.py`
175 | - **Run all**: `uv run pytest tests/`
176 | - **Coverage**: Check with `pytest --cov`
177 | 
178 | ---
179 | 
180 | ## Common Tasks
181 | 
182 | ### Add a New API Endpoint
183 | 1. Create router in `api/routers/feature.py`
184 | 2. Create service in `api/feature_service.py`
185 | 3. Define schemas in `api/models.py`
186 | 4. Register router in `api/main.py`
187 | 5. Test via http://localhost:5055/docs
188 | 
189 | ### Add a New LangGraph Workflow
190 | 1. Create `open_notebook/graphs/workflow_name.py`
191 | 2. Define StateDict and node functions
192 | 3. Build graph with `.add_node()` / `.add_edge()`
193 | 4. Invoke in service: `graph.ainvoke({"input": ...}, config={"..."})`
194 | 5. Test with sample data in `tests/`
195 | 
196 | ### Add Database Migration
197 | 1. Create `migrations/XXX_description.surql`
198 | 2. Write SurrealQL schema changes
199 | 3. Create `migrations/XXX_description_down.surql` (optional rollback)
200 | 4. API auto-detects on startup; migration runs if newer than recorded version
201 | 
202 | ### Deploy to Production
203 | 1. Review [CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md) for security settings
204 | 2. Use `make docker-release` for multi-platform image
205 | 3. Push to Docker Hub / GitHub Container Registry
206 | 4. Deploy `docker compose --profile multi up`
207 | 5. Verify migrations via API logs
208 | 
209 | ---
210 | 
211 | ## Support & Community
212 | 
213 | - **Documentation**: https://open-notebook.ai
214 | - **Discord**: https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w
215 | - **Issues**: https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook/issues
216 | - **License**: MIT (see LICENSE)
217 | 
218 | ---
219 | 
220 | **Last Updated**: January 2026 | **Project Version**: 1.2.4+
221 |

155 | ## 📚 Reading Paths

  1 | import asyncio
  2 | import sqlite3
  3 | from typing import Annotated, Dict, List, Optional
  4 | 
  5 | from ai_prompter import Prompter
  6 | from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, SystemMessage
  7 | from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableConfig
  8 | from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite import SqliteSaver
  9 | from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
 10 | from langgraph.graph.message import add_messages
 11 | from typing_extensions import TypedDict
 12 | 
 13 | from open_notebook.ai.provision import provision_langchain_model
 14 | from open_notebook.config import LANGGRAPH_CHECKPOINT_FILE
 15 | from open_notebook.domain.notebook import Source, SourceInsight
 16 | from open_notebook.utils import clean_thinking_content
 17 | from open_notebook.utils.context_builder import ContextBuilder
 18 | 
 19 | 
 20 | class SourceChatState(TypedDict):
 21 |     messages: Annotated[list, add_messages]
 22 |     source_id: str
 23 |     source: Optional[Source]
 24 |     insights: Optional[List[SourceInsight]]
 25 |     context: Optional[str]
 26 |     model_override: Optional[str]
 27 |     context_indicators: Optional[Dict[str, List[str]]]
 28 | 
 29 | 
 30 | def call_model_with_source_context(
 31 |     state: SourceChatState, config: RunnableConfig
 32 | ) -> dict:
 33 |     """
 34 |     Main function that builds source context and calls the model.
 35 | 
 36 |     This function:
 37 |     1. Uses ContextBuilder to build source-specific context
 38 |     2. Applies the source_chat Jinja2 prompt template
 39 |     3. Handles model provisioning with override support
 40 |     4. Tracks context indicators for referenced insights/content
 41 |     """
 42 |     source_id = state.get("source_id")
 43 |     if not source_id:
 44 |         raise ValueError("source_id is required in state")
 45 | 
 46 |     # Build source context using ContextBuilder (run async code in new loop)
 47 |     def build_context():
 48 |         """Build context in a new event loop"""
 49 |         new_loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
 50 |         try:
 51 |             asyncio.set_event_loop(new_loop)
 52 |             context_builder = ContextBuilder(
 53 |                 source_id=source_id,
 54 |                 include_insights=True,
 55 |                 include_notes=False,  # Focus on source-specific content
 56 |                 max_tokens=50000,  # Reasonable limit for source context
 57 |             )
 58 |             return new_loop.run_until_complete(context_builder.build())
 59 |         finally:
 60 |             new_loop.close()
 61 |             asyncio.set_event_loop(None)
 62 | 
 63 |     # Get the built context
 64 |     try:
 65 |         # Try to get the current event loop
 66 |         asyncio.get_running_loop()
 67 |         # If we're in an event loop, run in a thread with a new loop
 68 |         import concurrent.futures
 69 | 
 70 |         with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
 71 |             future = executor.submit(build_context)
 72 |             context_data = future.result()
 73 |     except RuntimeError:
 74 |         # No event loop running, safe to create a new one
 75 |         context_data = build_context()
 76 | 
 77 |     # Extract source and insights from context
 78 |     source = None
 79 |     insights = []
 80 |     context_indicators: dict[str, list[str | None]] = {
 81 |         "sources": [],
 82 |         "insights": [],
 83 |         "notes": [],
 84 |     }
 85 | 
 86 |     if context_data.get("sources"):
 87 |         source_info = context_data["sources"][0]  # First source
 88 |         source = Source(**source_info) if isinstance(source_info, dict) else source_info
 89 |         context_indicators["sources"].append(source.id)
 90 | 
 91 |     if context_data.get("insights"):
 92 |         for insight_data in context_data["insights"]:
 93 |             insight = (
 94 |                 SourceInsight(**insight_data)
 95 |                 if isinstance(insight_data, dict)
 96 |                 else insight_data
 97 |             )
 98 |             insights.append(insight)
 99 |             context_indicators["insights"].append(insight.id)
100 | 
101 |     # Format context for the prompt
102 |     formatted_context = _format_source_context(context_data)
103 | 
104 |     # Build prompt data for the template
105 |     prompt_data = {
106 |         "source": source.model_dump() if source else None,
107 |         "insights": [insight.model_dump() for insight in insights] if insights else [],
108 |         "context": formatted_context,
109 |         "context_indicators": context_indicators,
110 |     }
111 | 
112 |     # Apply the source_chat prompt template
113 |     system_prompt = Prompter(prompt_template="source_chat/system").render(
114 |         data=prompt_data
115 |     )
116 |     payload = [SystemMessage(content=system_prompt)] + state.get("messages", [])
117 | 
118 |     # Handle async model provisioning from sync context
119 |     def run_in_new_loop():
120 |         """Run the async function in a new event loop"""
121 |         new_loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
122 |         try:
123 |             asyncio.set_event_loop(new_loop)
124 |             return new_loop.run_until_complete(
125 |                 provision_langchain_model(
126 |                     str(payload),
127 |                     config.get("configurable", {}).get("model_id")
128 |                     or state.get("model_override"),
129 |                     "chat",
130 |                     max_tokens=8192,
131 |                 )
132 |             )
133 |         finally:
134 |             new_loop.close()
135 |             asyncio.set_event_loop(None)
136 | 
137 |     try:
138 |         # Try to get the current event loop
139 |         asyncio.get_running_loop()
140 |         # If we're in an event loop, run in a thread with a new loop
141 |         import concurrent.futures
142 | 
143 |         with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
144 |             future = executor.submit(run_in_new_loop)
145 |             model = future.result()
146 |     except RuntimeError:
147 |         # No event loop running, safe to use asyncio.run()
148 |         model = asyncio.run(
149 |             provision_langchain_model(
150 |                 str(payload),
151 |                 config.get("configurable", {}).get("model_id")
152 |                 or state.get("model_override"),
153 |                 "chat",
154 |                 max_tokens=8192,
155 |             )
156 |         )
157 | 
158 |     ai_message = model.invoke(payload)
159 | 
160 |     # Clean thinking content from AI response (e.g., <think>...</think> tags)
161 |     content = (
162 |         ai_message.content
163 |         if isinstance(ai_message.content, str)
164 |         else str(ai_message.content)
165 |     )
166 |     cleaned_content = clean_thinking_content(content)
167 |     cleaned_message = ai_message.model_copy(update={"content": cleaned_content})
168 | 
169 |     # Update state with context information
170 |     return {
171 |         "messages": cleaned_message,
172 |         "source": source,
173 |         "insights": insights,
174 |         "context": formatted_context,
175 |         "context_indicators": context_indicators,
176 |     }
177 | 
178 | 
179 | def _format_source_context(context_data: Dict) -> str:
180 |     """
181 |     Format the context data into a readable string for the prompt.
182 | 
183 |     Args:
184 |         context_data: Context data from ContextBuilder
185 | 
186 |     Returns:
187 |         Formatted context string
188 |     """
189 |     context_parts = []
190 | 
191 |     # Add source information
192 |     if context_data.get("sources"):
193 |         context_parts.append("## SOURCE CONTENT")
194 |         for source in context_data["sources"]:
195 |             if isinstance(source, dict):
196 |                 context_parts.append(f"**Source ID:** {source.get('id', 'Unknown')}")
197 |                 context_parts.append(f"**Title:** {source.get('title', 'No title')}")
198 |                 if source.get("full_text"):
199 |                     # Truncate full text if too long
200 |                     full_text = source["full_text"]
201 |                     if len(full_text) > 5000:
202 |                         full_text = full_text[:5000] + "...\n[Content truncated]"
203 |                     context_parts.append(f"**Content:**\n{full_text}")
204 |                 context_parts.append("")  # Empty line for separation
205 | 
206 |     # Add insights
207 |     if context_data.get("insights"):
208 |         context_parts.append("## SOURCE INSIGHTS")
209 |         for insight in context_data["insights"]:
210 |             if isinstance(insight, dict):
211 |                 context_parts.append(f"**Insight ID:** {insight.get('id', 'Unknown')}")
212 |                 context_parts.append(
213 |                     f"**Type:** {insight.get('insight_type', 'Unknown')}"
214 |                 )
215 |                 context_parts.append(
216 |                     f"**Content:** {insight.get('content', 'No content')}"
217 |                 )
218 |                 context_parts.append("")  # Empty line for separation
219 | 
220 |     # Add metadata
221 |     if context_data.get("metadata"):
222 |         metadata = context_data["metadata"]
223 |         context_parts.append("## CONTEXT METADATA")
224 |         context_parts.append(f"- Source count: {metadata.get('source_count', 0)}")
225 |         context_parts.append(f"- Insight count: {metadata.get('insight_count', 0)}")
226 |         context_parts.append(f"- Total tokens: {context_data.get('total_tokens', 0)}")
227 |         context_parts.append("")
228 | 
229 |     return "\n".join(context_parts)
230 | 
231 | 
232 | # Create SQLite checkpointer
233 | conn = sqlite3.connect(
234 |     LANGGRAPH_CHECKPOINT_FILE,
235 |     check_same_thread=False,
236 | )
237 | memory = SqliteSaver(conn)
238 | 
239 | # Create the StateGraph
240 | source_chat_state = StateGraph(SourceChatState)
241 | source_chat_state.add_node("source_chat_agent", call_model_with_source_context)
242 | source_chat_state.add_edge(START, "source_chat_agent")
243 | source_chat_state.add_edge("source_chat_agent", END)
244 | source_chat_graph = source_chat_state.compile(checkpointer=memory)
245 |

  1 | 'use client'
  2 | 
  3 | import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
  4 | import { useParams } from 'next/navigation'
  5 | import { AppShell } from '@/components/layout/AppShell'
  6 | import { NotebookHeader } from '../components/NotebookHeader'
  7 | import { SourcesColumn } from '../components/SourcesColumn'
  8 | import { NotesColumn } from '../components/NotesColumn'
  9 | import { ChatColumn } from '../components/ChatColumn'
 10 | import { useNotebook } from '@/lib/hooks/use-notebooks'
 11 | import { useNotebookSources } from '@/lib/hooks/use-sources'
 12 | import { useNotes } from '@/lib/hooks/use-notes'
 13 | import { LoadingSpinner } from '@/components/common/LoadingSpinner'
 14 | import { useNotebookColumnsStore } from '@/lib/stores/notebook-columns-store'
 15 | import { useIsDesktop } from '@/lib/hooks/use-media-query'
 16 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
 17 | import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
 18 | import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from '@/components/ui/tabs'
 19 | import { FileText, StickyNote, MessageSquare } from 'lucide-react'
 20 | 
 21 | export type ContextMode = 'off' | 'insights' | 'full'
 22 | 
 23 | export interface ContextSelections {
 24 |   sources: Record<string, ContextMode>
 25 |   notes: Record<string, ContextMode>
 26 | }
 27 | 
 28 | export default function NotebookPage() {
 29 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 30 |   const params = useParams()
 31 | 
 32 |   // Ensure the notebook ID is properly decoded from URL
 33 |   const notebookId = params?.id ? decodeURIComponent(params.id as string) : ''
 34 | 
 35 |   const { data: notebook, isLoading: notebookLoading } = useNotebook(notebookId)
 36 |   const {
 37 |     sources,
 38 |     isLoading: sourcesLoading,
 39 |     refetch: refetchSources,
 40 |     hasNextPage,
 41 |     isFetchingNextPage,
 42 |     fetchNextPage,
 43 |   } = useNotebookSources(notebookId)
 44 |   const { data: notes, isLoading: notesLoading } = useNotes(notebookId)
 45 | 
 46 |   // Get collapse states for dynamic layout
 47 |   const { sourcesCollapsed, notesCollapsed } = useNotebookColumnsStore()
 48 | 
 49 |   // Detect desktop to avoid double-mounting ChatColumn
 50 |   const isDesktop = useIsDesktop()
 51 | 
 52 |   // Mobile tab state (Sources, Notes, or Chat)
 53 |   const [mobileActiveTab, setMobileActiveTab] = useState<'sources' | 'notes' | 'chat'>('chat')
 54 | 
 55 |   // Context selection state
 56 |   const [contextSelections, setContextSelections] = useState<ContextSelections>({
 57 |     sources: {},
 58 |     notes: {}
 59 |   })
 60 | 
 61 |   // Initialize and update selections when sources load or change
 62 |   useEffect(() => {
 63 |     if (sources && sources.length > 0) {
 64 |       setContextSelections(prev => {
 65 |         const newSourceSelections = { ...prev.sources }
 66 |         sources.forEach(source => {
 67 |           const currentMode = newSourceSelections[source.id]
 68 |           const hasInsights = source.insights_count > 0
 69 | 
 70 |           if (currentMode === undefined) {
 71 |             // Initial setup - default based on insights availability
 72 |             newSourceSelections[source.id] = hasInsights ? 'insights' : 'full'
 73 |           } else if (currentMode === 'full' && hasInsights) {
 74 |             // Source gained insights while in 'full' mode - auto-switch to 'insights'
 75 |             newSourceSelections[source.id] = 'insights'
 76 |           }
 77 |         })
 78 |         return { ...prev, sources: newSourceSelections }
 79 |       })
 80 |     }
 81 |   }, [sources])
 82 | 
 83 |   useEffect(() => {
 84 |     if (notes && notes.length > 0) {
 85 |       setContextSelections(prev => {
 86 |         const newNoteSelections = { ...prev.notes }
 87 |         notes.forEach(note => {
 88 |           // Only set default if not already set
 89 |           if (!(note.id in newNoteSelections)) {
 90 |             // Notes default to 'full'
 91 |             newNoteSelections[note.id] = 'full'
 92 |           }
 93 |         })
 94 |         return { ...prev, notes: newNoteSelections }
 95 |       })
 96 |     }
 97 |   }, [notes])
 98 | 
 99 |   // Handler to update context selection
100 |   const handleContextModeChange = (itemId: string, mode: ContextMode, type: 'source' | 'note') => {
101 |     setContextSelections(prev => ({
102 |       ...prev,
103 |       [type === 'source' ? 'sources' : 'notes']: {
104 |         ...(type === 'source' ? prev.sources : prev.notes),
105 |         [itemId]: mode
106 |       }
107 |     }))
108 |   }
109 | 
110 |   if (notebookLoading) {
111 |     return (
112 |       <div className="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center">
113 |         <LoadingSpinner size="lg" />
114 |       </div>
115 |     )
116 |   }
117 | 
118 |   if (!notebook) {
119 |     return (
120 |       <AppShell>
121 |         <div className="p-6">
122 |           <h1 className="text-2xl font-bold mb-4">{t.notebooks.notFound}</h1>
123 |           <p className="text-muted-foreground">{t.notebooks.notFoundDesc}</p>
124 |         </div>
125 |       </AppShell>
126 |     )
127 |   }
128 | 
129 |   return (
130 |     <AppShell>
131 |       <div className="flex flex-col flex-1 min-h-0">
132 |         <div className="flex-shrink-0 p-6 pb-0">
133 |           <NotebookHeader notebook={notebook} />
134 |         </div>
135 | 
136 |         <div className="flex-1 p-6 pt-6 overflow-x-auto flex flex-col">
137 |           {/* Mobile: Tabbed interface - only render on mobile to avoid double-mounting */}
138 |           {!isDesktop && (
139 |             <>
140 |               <div className="lg:hidden mb-4">
141 |                 <Tabs value={mobileActiveTab} onValueChange={(value) => setMobileActiveTab(value as 'sources' | 'notes' | 'chat')}>
142 |                   <TabsList className="grid w-full grid-cols-3">
143 |                     <TabsTrigger value="sources" className="gap-2">
144 |                       <FileText className="h-4 w-4" />
145 |                       {t.navigation.sources}
146 |                     </TabsTrigger>
147 |                     <TabsTrigger value="notes" className="gap-2">
148 |                       <StickyNote className="h-4 w-4" />
149 |                       {t.common.notes}
150 |                     </TabsTrigger>
151 |                     <TabsTrigger value="chat" className="gap-2">
152 |                       <MessageSquare className="h-4 w-4" />
153 |                       {t.common.chat}
154 |                     </TabsTrigger>
155 |                   </TabsList>
156 |                 </Tabs>
157 |               </div>
158 | 
159 |               {/* Mobile: Show only active tab */}
160 |               <div className="flex-1 overflow-hidden lg:hidden">
161 |                 {mobileActiveTab === 'sources' && (
162 |                   <SourcesColumn
163 |                     sources={sources}
164 |                     isLoading={sourcesLoading}
165 |                     notebookId={notebookId}
166 |                     notebookName={notebook?.name}
167 |                     onRefresh={refetchSources}
168 |                     contextSelections={contextSelections.sources}
169 |                     onContextModeChange={(sourceId, mode) => handleContextModeChange(sourceId, mode, 'source')}
170 |                     hasNextPage={hasNextPage}
171 |                     isFetchingNextPage={isFetchingNextPage}
172 |                     fetchNextPage={fetchNextPage}
173 |                   />
174 |                 )}
175 |                 {mobileActiveTab === 'notes' && (
176 |                   <NotesColumn
177 |                     notes={notes}
178 |                     isLoading={notesLoading}
179 |                     notebookId={notebookId}
180 |                     contextSelections={contextSelections.notes}
181 |                     onContextModeChange={(noteId, mode) => handleContextModeChange(noteId, mode, 'note')}
182 |                   />
183 |                 )}
184 |                 {mobileActiveTab === 'chat' && (
185 |                   <ChatColumn
186 |                     notebookId={notebookId}
187 |                     contextSelections={contextSelections}
188 |                   />
189 |                 )}
190 |               </div>
191 |             </>
192 |           )}
193 | 
194 |           {/* Desktop: Collapsible columns layout */}
195 |           <div className={cn(
196 |             'hidden lg:flex h-full min-h-0 gap-6 transition-all duration-150',
197 |             'flex-row'
198 |           )}>
199 |             {/* Sources Column */}
200 |             <div className={cn(
201 |               'transition-all duration-150',
202 |               sourcesCollapsed ? 'w-12 flex-shrink-0' : 'flex-none basis-1/3'
203 |             )}>
204 |               <SourcesColumn
205 |                 sources={sources}
206 |                 isLoading={sourcesLoading}
207 |                 notebookId={notebookId}
208 |                 notebookName={notebook?.name}
209 |                 onRefresh={refetchSources}
210 |                 contextSelections={contextSelections.sources}
211 |                 onContextModeChange={(sourceId, mode) => handleContextModeChange(sourceId, mode, 'source')}
212 |                 hasNextPage={hasNextPage}
213 |                 isFetchingNextPage={isFetchingNextPage}
214 |                 fetchNextPage={fetchNextPage}
215 |               />
216 |             </div>
217 | 
218 |             {/* Notes Column */}
219 |             <div className={cn(
220 |               'transition-all duration-150',
221 |               notesCollapsed ? 'w-12 flex-shrink-0' : 'flex-none basis-1/3'
222 |             )}>
223 |               <NotesColumn
224 |                 notes={notes}
225 |                 isLoading={notesLoading}
226 |                 notebookId={notebookId}
227 |                 contextSelections={contextSelections.notes}
228 |                 onContextModeChange={(noteId, mode) => handleContextModeChange(noteId, mode, 'note')}
229 |               />
230 |             </div>
231 | 
232 |             {/* Chat Column - always expanded, takes remaining space */}
233 |             <div className="transition-all duration-150 flex-1 lg:pr-6 lg:-mr-6">
234 |               <ChatColumn
235 |                 notebookId={notebookId}
236 |                 contextSelections={contextSelections}
237 |               />
238 |             </div>
239 |           </div>
240 |         </div>
241 |       </div>
242 |     </AppShell>
243 |   )
244 | }

/docs/5-CONFIGURATION/openai-compatible.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # OpenAI-Compatible Providers
  2 | 
  3 | Use any server that implements the OpenAI API format with Open Notebook. This includes LM Studio, Text Generation WebUI, vLLM, and many others.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## What is OpenAI-Compatible?
  8 | 
  9 | Many AI tools implement the same API format as OpenAI:
 10 | 
 11 | ```
 12 | POST /v1/chat/completions
 13 | POST /v1/embeddings
 14 | POST /v1/audio/speech
 15 | ```
 16 | 
 17 | Open Notebook can connect to any server using this format.
 18 | 
 19 | ---
 20 | 
 21 | ## Common Compatible Servers
 22 | 
 23 | | Server | Use Case | URL |
 24 | |--------|----------|-----|
 25 | | **LM Studio** | Desktop GUI for local models | https://lmstudio.ai |
 26 | | **Text Generation WebUI** | Full-featured local inference | https://github.com/oobabooga/text-generation-webui |
 27 | | **vLLM** | High-performance serving | https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm |
 28 | | **Ollama** | Simple local models | (Use native Ollama provider instead) |
 29 | | **LocalAI** | Local AI inference | https://github.com/mudler/LocalAI |
 30 | | **llama.cpp server** | Lightweight inference | https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp |
 31 | 
 32 | ---
 33 | 
 34 | ## Quick Setup: LM Studio
 35 | 
 36 | ### Step 1: Install and Start LM Studio
 37 | 
 38 | 1. Download from https://lmstudio.ai
 39 | 2. Install and launch
 40 | 3. Download a model (e.g., Llama 3)
 41 | 4. Start the local server (default: port 1234)
 42 | 
 43 | ### Step 2: Configure Environment
 44 | 
 45 | ```bash
 46 | # For language models
 47 | export OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:1234/v1
 48 | export OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY=not-needed  # LM Studio doesn't require key
 49 | ```
 50 | 
 51 | ### Step 3: Add Model in Open Notebook
 52 | 
 53 | 1. Go to **Settings** → **Models**
 54 | 2. Click **Add Model**
 55 | 3. Configure:
 56 |    - **Provider**: `openai_compatible`
 57 |    - **Model Name**: Your model name from LM Studio
 58 |    - **Display Name**: `LM Studio - Llama 3`
 59 | 4. Click **Save**
 60 | 
 61 | ---
 62 | 
 63 | ## Environment Variables
 64 | 
 65 | ### Language Models (Chat)
 66 | 
 67 | ```bash
 68 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:1234/v1
 69 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY=optional-api-key
 70 | ```
 71 | 
 72 | ### Embeddings
 73 | 
 74 | ```bash
 75 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_EMBEDDING=http://localhost:1234/v1
 76 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_EMBEDDING=optional-api-key
 77 | ```
 78 | 
 79 | ### Text-to-Speech
 80 | 
 81 | ```bash
 82 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_TTS=http://localhost:8969/v1
 83 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY_TTS=optional-api-key
 84 | ```
 85 | 
 86 | ### Speech-to-Text
 87 | 
 88 | ```bash
 89 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_STT=http://localhost:9000/v1
 90 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY_STT=optional-api-key
 91 | ```
 92 | 
 93 | ---
 94 | 
 95 | ## Docker Networking
 96 | 
 97 | When Open Notebook runs in Docker and your compatible server runs on the host:
 98 | 
 99 | ### macOS / Windows
100 | 
101 | ```bash
102 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:1234/v1
103 | ```
104 | 
105 | ### Linux
106 | 
107 | ```bash
108 | # Option 1: Docker bridge IP
109 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://172.17.0.1:1234/v1
110 | 
111 | # Option 2: Host networking mode
112 | docker run --network host ...
113 | ```
114 | 
115 | ### Same Docker Network
116 | 
117 | ```yaml
118 | # docker-compose.yml
119 | services:
120 |   open-notebook:
121 |     # ...
122 |     environment:
123 |       - OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://lm-studio:1234/v1
124 | 
125 |   lm-studio:
126 |     # your LM Studio container
127 |     ports:
128 |       - "1234:1234"
129 | ```
130 | 
131 | ---
132 | 
133 | ## Text Generation WebUI Setup
134 | 
135 | ### Start with API Enabled
136 | 
137 | ```bash
138 | python server.py --api --listen
139 | ```
140 | 
141 | ### Configure Open Notebook
142 | 
143 | ```bash
144 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5000/v1
145 | ```
146 | 
147 | ### Docker Compose Example
148 | 
149 | ```yaml
150 | services:
151 |   text-gen:
152 |     image: atinoda/text-generation-webui:default
153 |     ports:
154 |       - "5000:5000"
155 |       - "7860:7860"
156 |     volumes:
157 |       - ./models:/app/models
158 |     command: --api --listen
159 | 
160 |   open-notebook:
161 |     image: lfnovo/open_notebook:v1-latest-single
162 |     pull_policy: always
163 |     environment:
164 |       - OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://text-gen:5000/v1
165 |     depends_on:
166 |       - text-gen
167 | ```
168 | 
169 | ---
170 | 
171 | ## vLLM Setup
172 | 
173 | ### Start vLLM Server
174 | 
175 | ```bash
176 | python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
177 |   --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
178 |   --port 8000
179 | ```
180 | 
181 | ### Configure Open Notebook
182 | 
183 | ```bash
184 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1
185 | ```
186 | 
187 | ### Docker Compose with GPU
188 | 
189 | ```yaml
190 | services:
191 |   vllm:
192 |     image: vllm/vllm-openai:latest
193 |     command: --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
194 |     ports:
195 |       - "8000:8000"
196 |     volumes:
197 |       - ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface
198 |     deploy:
199 |       resources:
200 |         reservations:
201 |           devices:
202 |             - driver: nvidia
203 |               count: 1
204 |               capabilities: [gpu]
205 | 
206 |   open-notebook:
207 |     image: lfnovo/open_notebook:v1-latest-single
208 |     pull_policy: always
209 |     environment:
210 |       - OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://vllm:8000/v1
211 |     depends_on:
212 |       - vllm
213 | ```
214 | 
215 | ---
216 | 
217 | ## Adding Models in Open Notebook
218 | 
219 | ### Via Settings UI
220 | 
221 | 1. Go to **Settings** → **Models**
222 | 2. Click **Add Model** in appropriate section
223 | 3. Select **Provider**: `openai_compatible`
224 | 4. Enter **Model Name**: exactly as the server expects
225 | 5. Enter **Display Name**: your preferred name
226 | 6. Click **Save**
227 | 
228 | ### Model Name Format
229 | 
230 | The model name must match what your server expects:
231 | 
232 | | Server | Model Name Format |
233 | |--------|-------------------|
234 | | LM Studio | As shown in LM Studio UI |
235 | | vLLM | HuggingFace model path |
236 | | Text Gen WebUI | As loaded in UI |
237 | | llama.cpp | Model file name |
238 | 
239 | ---
240 | 
241 | ## Testing Connection
242 | 
243 | ### Test API Endpoint
244 | 
245 | ```bash
246 | # Test chat completions
247 | curl http://localhost:1234/v1/chat/completions \
248 |   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
249 |   -d '{
250 |     "model": "your-model-name",
251 |     "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
252 |   }'
253 | ```
254 | 
255 | ### Test from Inside Docker
256 | 
257 | ```bash
258 | docker exec -it open-notebook curl http://host.docker.internal:1234/v1/models
259 | ```
260 | 
261 | ---
262 | 
263 | ## Troubleshooting
264 | 
265 | ### Connection Refused
266 | 
267 | ```
268 | Problem: Cannot connect to server
269 | 
270 | Solutions:
271 | 1. Verify server is running
272 | 2. Check port is correct
273 | 3. Test with curl directly
274 | 4. Check Docker networking (use host.docker.internal)
275 | 5. Verify firewall allows connection
276 | ```
277 | 
278 | ### Model Not Found
279 | 
280 | ```
281 | Problem: Server returns "model not found"
282 | 
283 | Solutions:
284 | 1. Check model is loaded in server
285 | 2. Verify exact model name spelling
286 | 3. List available models: curl http://localhost:1234/v1/models
287 | 4. Update model name in Open Notebook
288 | ```
289 | 
290 | ### Slow Responses
291 | 
292 | ```
293 | Problem: Requests take very long
294 | 
295 | Solutions:
296 | 1. Check server resources (RAM, GPU)
297 | 2. Use smaller/quantized model
298 | 3. Reduce context length
299 | 4. Enable GPU acceleration if available
300 | ```
301 | 
302 | ### Authentication Errors
303 | 
304 | ```
305 | Problem: 401 or authentication failed
306 | 
307 | Solutions:
308 | 1. Check if server requires API key
309 | 2. Set OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY
310 | 3. Some servers need any non-empty key
311 | ```
312 | 
313 | ### Timeout Errors
314 | 
315 | ```
316 | Problem: Request times out
317 | 
318 | Solutions:
319 | 1. Model may be loading (first request slow)
320 | 2. Increase timeout settings
321 | 3. Check server logs for errors
322 | 4. Reduce request size
323 | ```
324 | 
325 | ---
326 | 
327 | ## Multiple Compatible Endpoints
328 | 
329 | You can use different compatible servers for different purposes:
330 | 
331 | ```bash
332 | # Chat model from LM Studio
333 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:1234/v1
334 | 
335 | # Embeddings from different server
336 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_EMBEDDING=http://localhost:8080/v1
337 | 
338 | # TTS from Speaches
339 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_TTS=http://localhost:8969/v1
340 | ```
341 | 
342 | Add each as a separate model in Open Notebook settings.
343 | 
344 | ---
345 | 
346 | ## Performance Tips
347 | 
348 | ### Model Selection
349 | 
350 | | Model Size | RAM Needed | Speed |
351 | |------------|------------|-------|
352 | | 7B | 8GB | Fast |
353 | | 13B | 16GB | Medium |
354 | | 70B | 64GB+ | Slow |
355 | 
356 | ### Quantization
357 | 
358 | Use quantized models (Q4, Q5) for faster inference with less RAM:
359 | 
360 | ```
361 | llama-3-8b-q4_k_m.gguf  → ~4GB RAM, fast
362 | llama-3-8b-f16.gguf     → ~16GB RAM, slower
363 | ```
364 | 
365 | ### GPU Acceleration
366 | 
367 | Enable GPU in your server for much faster inference:
368 | - LM Studio: Settings → GPU layers
369 | - vLLM: Automatic with CUDA
370 | - llama.cpp: `--n-gpu-layers 35`
371 | 
372 | ---
373 | 
374 | ## Comparison: Native vs Compatible
375 | 
376 | | Aspect | Native Provider | OpenAI Compatible |
377 | |--------|-----------------|-------------------|
378 | | **Setup** | API key only | Server + configuration |
379 | | **Models** | Provider's models | Any compatible model |
380 | | **Cost** | Pay per token | Free (local) |
381 | | **Speed** | Usually fast | Depends on hardware |
382 | | **Features** | Full support | Basic features |
383 | 
384 | Use OpenAI-compatible when:
385 | - Running local models
386 | - Using custom/fine-tuned models
387 | - Privacy requirements
388 | - Cost control
389 | 
390 | ---
391 | 
392 | ## Related
393 | 
394 | - **[Local TTS Setup](local-tts.md)** - Text-to-speech with Speaches
395 | - **[Local STT Setup](local-stt.md)** - Speech-to-text with Speaches
396 | - **[AI Providers](ai-providers.md)** - All provider options
397 | - **[Ollama Setup](ollama.md)** - Native Ollama integration
398 |

/docs/6-TROUBLESHOOTING/connection-issues.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Connection Issues - Network & API Problems
  2 | 
  3 | Frontend can't reach API or services won't communicate.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## "Cannot connect to server" (Most Common)
  8 | 
  9 | **What it looks like:**
 10 | - Browser shows error page
 11 | - "Unable to reach API"
 12 | - "Cannot connect to server"
 13 | - UI loads but can't create notebooks
 14 | 
 15 | **Diagnosis:**
 16 | 
 17 | ```bash
 18 | # Check if API is running
 19 | docker ps | grep api
 20 | # Should see "api" service running
 21 | 
 22 | # Check if API is responding
 23 | curl http://localhost:5055/health
 24 | # Should show: {"status":"ok"}
 25 | 
 26 | # Check if frontend is running
 27 | docker ps | grep frontend
 28 | # Should see "frontend" or React service running
 29 | ```
 30 | 
 31 | **Solutions:**
 32 | 
 33 | ### Solution 1: API Not Running
 34 | ```bash
 35 | # Start API
 36 | docker compose up api -d
 37 | 
 38 | # Wait 5 seconds
 39 | sleep 5
 40 | 
 41 | # Verify it's running
 42 | docker compose logs api | tail -20
 43 | ```
 44 | 
 45 | ### Solution 2: Port Not Exposed
 46 | ```bash
 47 | # Check docker-compose.yml has port mapping:
 48 | # api:
 49 | #   ports:
 50 | #     - "5055:5055"
 51 | 
 52 | # If missing, add it and restart:
 53 | docker compose down
 54 | docker compose up -d
 55 | ```
 56 | 
 57 | ### Solution 3: API_URL Mismatch
 58 | ```bash
 59 | # In .env, check API_URL:
 60 | cat .env | grep API_URL
 61 | 
 62 | # Should match your frontend URL:
 63 | # Frontend: http://localhost:8502
 64 | # API_URL: http://localhost:5055
 65 | 
 66 | # If wrong, fix it:
 67 | # API_URL=http://localhost:5055
 68 | # Then restart:
 69 | docker compose restart frontend
 70 | ```
 71 | 
 72 | ### Solution 4: Firewall Blocking
 73 | ```bash
 74 | # Verify port 5055 is accessible
 75 | netstat -tlnp | grep 5055
 76 | # Should show port listening
 77 | 
 78 | # If on different machine, try:
 79 | # Instead of localhost, use your IP:
 80 | API_URL=http://192.168.1.100:5055
 81 | ```
 82 | 
 83 | ### Solution 5: Services Not Started
 84 | ```bash
 85 | # Restart everything
 86 | docker compose restart
 87 | 
 88 | # Wait 10 seconds
 89 | sleep 10
 90 | 
 91 | # Check all services
 92 | docker compose ps
 93 | # All should show "Up"
 94 | ```
 95 | 
 96 | ---
 97 | 
 98 | ## Connection Refused
 99 | 
100 | **What it looks like:**
101 | ```
102 | Connection refused
103 | ECONNREFUSED
104 | Error: socket hang up
105 | ```
106 | 
107 | **Diagnosis:**
108 | - API port (5055) not open
109 | - API crashed
110 | - Wrong IP/hostname
111 | 
112 | **Solution:**
113 | 
114 | ```bash
115 | # Step 1: Check if API is running
116 | docker ps | grep api
117 | 
118 | # Step 2: Check if port is listening
119 | lsof -i :5055
120 | # or
121 | netstat -tlnp | grep 5055
122 | 
123 | # Step 3: Check API logs
124 | docker compose logs api | tail -30
125 | # Look for errors
126 | 
127 | # Step 4: Restart API
128 | docker compose restart api
129 | docker compose logs api | grep -i "error"
130 | ```
131 | 
132 | ---
133 | 
134 | ## Timeout / Slow Connection
135 | 
136 | **What it looks like:**
137 | - Page loads slowly
138 | - Request times out
139 | - "Gateway timeout" error
140 | 
141 | **Causes:**
142 | - API is overloaded
143 | - Network is slow
144 | - Reverse proxy issue
145 | 
146 | **Solutions:**
147 | 
148 | ### Check API Performance
149 | ```bash
150 | # See CPU/memory usage
151 | docker stats
152 | 
153 | # Check logs for slow operations
154 | docker compose logs api | grep "slow\|timeout"
155 | ```
156 | 
157 | ### Reduce Load
158 | ```bash
159 | # In .env:
160 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS=2
161 | API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=600
162 | 
163 | # Restart
164 | docker compose restart
165 | ```
166 | 
167 | ### Check Network
168 | ```bash
169 | # Test latency
170 | ping localhost
171 | 
172 | # Test API directly
173 | time curl http://localhost:5055/health
174 | 
175 | # Should be < 100ms
176 | ```
177 | 
178 | ---
179 | 
180 | ## 502 Bad Gateway (Reverse Proxy)
181 | 
182 | **What it looks like:**
183 | ```
184 | 502 Bad Gateway
185 | The server is temporarily unable to service the request
186 | ```
187 | 
188 | **Cause:** Reverse proxy can't reach API
189 | 
190 | **Solutions:**
191 | 
192 | ### Check Backend is Running
193 | ```bash
194 | # From the reverse proxy server
195 | curl http://localhost:5055/health
196 | 
197 | # Should work
198 | ```
199 | 
200 | ### Check Reverse Proxy Config
201 | ```nginx
202 | # Nginx example (correct):
203 | location /api {
204 |     proxy_pass http://localhost:5055/api;
205 |     proxy_http_version 1.1;
206 | }
207 | 
208 | # Common mistake (wrong):
209 | location /api {
210 |     proxy_pass http://localhost:5055;  # Missing /api
211 | }
212 | ```
213 | 
214 | ### Set API_URL for HTTPS
215 | ```bash
216 | # In .env:
217 | API_URL=https://yourdomain.com
218 | 
219 | # Restart
220 | docker compose restart
221 | ```
222 | 
223 | ---
224 | 
225 | ## Intermittent Disconnects
226 | 
227 | **What it looks like:**
228 | - Works sometimes, fails other times
229 | - Sporadic "cannot connect" errors
230 | - Works then stops working
231 | 
232 | **Cause:** Transient network issue or database conflicts
233 | 
234 | **Solutions:**
235 | 
236 | ### Enable Retry Logic
237 | ```bash
238 | # In .env:
239 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_ENABLED=true
240 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5
241 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_WAIT_STRATEGY=exponential_jitter
242 | 
243 | # Restart
244 | docker compose restart
245 | ```
246 | 
247 | ### Reduce Concurrency
248 | ```bash
249 | # In .env:
250 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS=2
251 | 
252 | # Restart
253 | docker compose restart
254 | ```
255 | 
256 | ### Check Network Stability
257 | ```bash
258 | # Monitor connection
259 | ping google.com
260 | 
261 | # Long-running test
262 | ping -c 100 google.com | grep "packet loss"
263 | # Should be 0% loss
264 | ```
265 | 
266 | ---
267 | 
268 | ## Different Machine / Remote Access
269 | 
270 | **You want to access Open Notebook from another computer**
271 | 
272 | **Solution:**
273 | 
274 | ### Step 1: Get Your Machine IP
275 | ```bash
276 | # On the server running Open Notebook:
277 | ifconfig | grep "inet "
278 | # or
279 | hostname -I
280 | # Note the IP (e.g., 192.168.1.100)
281 | ```
282 | 
283 | ### Step 2: Update API_URL
284 | ```bash
285 | # In .env:
286 | API_URL=http://192.168.1.100:5055
287 | 
288 | # Restart
289 | docker compose restart
290 | ```
291 | 
292 | ### Step 3: Access from Other Machine
293 | ```bash
294 | # In browser on other machine:
295 | http://192.168.1.100:8502
296 | # (or your server IP)
297 | ```
298 | 
299 | ### Step 4: Verify Port is Exposed
300 | ```bash
301 | # On server:
302 | docker compose ps
303 | 
304 | # Should show port mapping:
305 | # 0.0.0.0:8502->8502/tcp
306 | # 0.0.0.0:5055->5055/tcp
307 | ```
308 | 
309 | ### If Still Doesn't Work
310 | ```bash
311 | # Check firewall on server
312 | sudo ufw status
313 | # May need to open ports:
314 | sudo ufw allow 8502
315 | sudo ufw allow 5055
316 | 
317 | # Check on different machine:
318 | telnet 192.168.1.100 5055
319 | # Should connect
320 | ```
321 | 
322 | ---
323 | 
324 | ## CORS Error (Browser Console)
325 | 
326 | **What it looks like:**
327 | ```
328 | Cross-Origin Request Blocked
329 | Access-Control-Allow-Origin
330 | ```
331 | 
332 | **In browser console (F12):**
333 | ```
334 | CORS policy: Response to preflight request doesn't pass access control check
335 | ```
336 | 
337 | **Cause:** Frontend and API URLs don't match
338 | 
339 | **Solution:**
340 | 
341 | ```bash
342 | # Check browser console error for what URLs are being used
343 | # The error shows:
344 | # - Requesting from: http://localhost:8502
345 | # - Trying to reach: http://localhost:5055
346 | 
347 | # Make sure API_URL matches:
348 | API_URL=http://localhost:5055
349 | 
350 | # And protocol matches (http/https)
351 | # Restart
352 | docker compose restart frontend
353 | ```
354 | 
355 | ---
356 | 
357 | ## Testing Connection
358 | 
359 | **Full diagnostic:**
360 | 
361 | ```bash
362 | # 1. Services running?
363 | docker compose ps
364 | # All should show "Up"
365 | 
366 | # 2. Ports listening?
367 | netstat -tlnp | grep -E "8502|5055|8000"
368 | 
369 | # 3. API responding?
370 | curl http://localhost:5055/health
371 | 
372 | # 4. Frontend accessible?
373 | curl http://localhost:8502 | head
374 | 
375 | # 5. Network OK?
376 | ping google.com
377 | 
378 | # 6. No firewall?
379 | sudo ufw status | grep -E "5055|8502|8000"
380 | ```
381 | 
382 | ---
383 | 
384 | ## Checklist for Remote Access
385 | 
386 | - [ ] Server IP noted (e.g., 192.168.1.100)
387 | - [ ] Ports 8502, 5055, 8000 exposed in docker-compose
388 | - [ ] API_URL set to server IP
389 | - [ ] Firewall allows ports 8502, 5055, 8000
390 | - [ ] Can reach server from client machine (ping IP)
391 | - [ ] All services running (docker compose ps)
392 | - [ ] Can curl API from client (curl http://IP:5055/health)
393 | 
394 | ---
395 | 
396 | ## SSL Certificate Errors
397 | 
398 | **What it looks like:**
399 | ```
400 | [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed
401 | Connection error when using HTTPS endpoints
402 | Works with HTTP but fails with HTTPS
403 | ```
404 | 
405 | **Cause:** Self-signed certificates not trusted by Python's SSL verification
406 | 
407 | **Solutions:**
408 | 
409 | ### Solution 1: Use Custom CA Bundle (Recommended)
410 | ```bash
411 | # In .env:
412 | ESPERANTO_SSL_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/your/ca-bundle.pem
413 | 
414 | # For Docker, mount the certificate:
415 | # In docker-compose.yml:
416 | volumes:
417 |   - /path/to/your/ca-bundle.pem:/certs/ca-bundle.pem:ro
418 | environment:
419 |   - ESPERANTO_SSL_CA_BUNDLE=/certs/ca-bundle.pem
420 | ```
421 | 
422 | ### Solution 2: Disable SSL Verification (Development Only)
423 | ```bash
424 | # WARNING: Only use in trusted development environments
425 | # In .env:
426 | ESPERANTO_SSL_VERIFY=false
427 | ```
428 | 
429 | ### Solution 3: Use HTTP Instead
430 | If services are on a trusted local network, HTTP is acceptable:
431 | ```bash
432 | # Change endpoint from https:// to http://
433 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:1234/v1
434 | ```
435 | 
436 | > **Security Note:** Disabling SSL verification exposes you to man-in-the-middle attacks. Always prefer custom CA bundle or HTTP on trusted networks.
437 | 
438 | ---
439 | 
440 | ## Still Having Issues?
441 | 
442 | - Check [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md)
443 | - Check [FAQ](faq.md)
444 | - Check logs: `docker compose logs`
445 | - Try restart: `docker compose restart`
446 | - Check firewall: `sudo ufw status`
447 | - Ask for help on [Discord](https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w)
448 |

 10 |   SourceChatSession,
 11 |   SourceChatMessage,
 12 |   SourceChatContextIndicator,
 13 |   CreateSourceChatSessionRequest,
 14 |   UpdateSourceChatSessionRequest
 15 | } from '@/lib/types/api'
 16 | 
 17 | export function useSourceChat(sourceId: string) {
 18 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 19 |   const queryClient = useQueryClient()
 20 |   const [currentSessionId, setCurrentSessionId] = useState<string | null>(null)
 21 |   const [messages, setMessages] = useState<SourceChatMessage[]>([])
 22 |   const [isStreaming, setIsStreaming] = useState(false)
 23 |   const [contextIndicators, setContextIndicators] = useState<SourceChatContextIndicator | null>(null)
 24 |   const abortControllerRef = useRef<AbortController | null>(null)
 25 | 
 26 |   // Fetch sessions
 27 |   const { data: sessions = [], isLoading: loadingSessions, refetch: refetchSessions } = useQuery<SourceChatSession[]>({
 28 |     queryKey: ['sourceChatSessions', sourceId],
 29 |     queryFn: () => sourceChatApi.listSessions(sourceId),
 30 |     enabled: !!sourceId
 31 |   })
 32 | 
 33 |   // Fetch current session with messages
 34 |   const { data: currentSession, refetch: refetchCurrentSession } = useQuery({
 35 |     queryKey: ['sourceChatSession', sourceId, currentSessionId],
 36 |     queryFn: () => sourceChatApi.getSession(sourceId, currentSessionId!),
 37 |     enabled: !!sourceId && !!currentSessionId
 38 |   })
 39 | 
 40 |   // Update messages when session changes
 41 |   useEffect(() => {
 42 |     if (currentSession?.messages) {
 43 |       setMessages(currentSession.messages)
 44 |     }
 45 |   }, [currentSession])
 46 | 
 47 |   // Auto-select most recent session when sessions are loaded
 48 |   useEffect(() => {
 49 |     if (sessions.length > 0 && !currentSessionId) {
 50 |       // Find most recent session (sessions are sorted by created date desc from API)
 51 |       const mostRecentSession = sessions[0]
 52 |       setCurrentSessionId(mostRecentSession.id)
 53 |     }
 54 |   }, [sessions, currentSessionId])
 55 | 
 56 |   // Create session mutation
 57 |   const createSessionMutation = useMutation({
 58 |     mutationFn: (data: Omit<CreateSourceChatSessionRequest, 'source_id'>) => 
 59 |       sourceChatApi.createSession(sourceId, data),
 60 |     onSuccess: (newSession) => {
 61 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['sourceChatSessions', sourceId] })
 62 |       setCurrentSessionId(newSession.id)
 63 |       toast.success(t.chat.sessionCreated)
 64 |     },
 65 |     onError: (err: unknown) => {
 66 |       const error = err as { response?: { data?: { detail?: string } }, message?: string };
 67 |       toast.error(t(getApiErrorKey(error.response?.data?.detail || error.message, 'apiErrors.failedToCreateSession')))
 68 |     }
 69 |   })
 70 | 
 71 |   // Update session mutation
 72 |   const updateSessionMutation = useMutation({
 73 |     mutationFn: ({ sessionId, data }: { sessionId: string, data: UpdateSourceChatSessionRequest }) =>
 74 |       sourceChatApi.updateSession(sourceId, sessionId, data),
 75 |     onSuccess: () => {
 76 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['sourceChatSessions', sourceId] })
 77 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['sourceChatSession', sourceId, currentSessionId] })
 78 |       toast.success(t.chat.sessionUpdated)
 79 |     },
 80 |     onError: (err: unknown) => {
 81 |       const error = err as { response?: { data?: { detail?: string } }, message?: string };
 82 |       toast.error(t(getApiErrorKey(error.response?.data?.detail || error.message, 'apiErrors.failedToUpdateSession')))
 83 |     }
 84 |   })
 85 | 
 86 |   // Delete session mutation
 87 |   const deleteSessionMutation = useMutation({
 88 |     mutationFn: (sessionId: string) => 
 89 |       sourceChatApi.deleteSession(sourceId, sessionId),
 90 |     onSuccess: (_, deletedId) => {
 91 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['sourceChatSessions', sourceId] })
 92 |       if (currentSessionId === deletedId) {
 93 |         setCurrentSessionId(null)
 94 |         setMessages([])
 95 |       }
 96 |       toast.success(t.chat.sessionDeleted)
 97 |     },
 98 |     onError: (err: unknown) => {
 99 |       const error = err as { response?: { data?: { detail?: string } }, message?: string };
100 |       toast.error(t(getApiErrorKey(error.response?.data?.detail || error.message, 'apiErrors.failedToDeleteSession')))
101 |     }
102 |   })
103 | 
104 |   // Send message with streaming
105 |   const sendMessage = useCallback(async (message: string, modelOverride?: string) => {
106 |     let sessionId = currentSessionId
107 | 
108 |     // Auto-create session if none exists
109 |     if (!sessionId) {
110 |       try {
111 |         const defaultTitle = message.length > 30 ? `${message.substring(0, 30)}...` : message
112 |         const newSession = await sourceChatApi.createSession(sourceId, { title: defaultTitle })
113 |         sessionId = newSession.id
114 |         setCurrentSessionId(sessionId)
115 |         queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['sourceChatSessions', sourceId] })
116 |       } catch (err: unknown) {
117 |         const error = err as { response?: { data?: { detail?: string } }, message?: string };
118 |         console.error('Failed to create chat session:', error)
119 |         toast.error(t(getApiErrorKey(error.response?.data?.detail || error.message, 'apiErrors.failedToCreateSession')))
120 |         return
121 |       }
122 |     }
123 | 
124 |     // Add user message optimistically
125 |     const userMessage: SourceChatMessage = {
126 |       id: `temp-${Date.now()}`,
127 |       type: 'human',
128 |       content: message,
129 |       timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
130 |     }
131 |     setMessages(prev => [...prev, userMessage])
132 |     setIsStreaming(true)
133 | 
134 |     try {
135 |       const response = await sourceChatApi.sendMessage(sourceId, sessionId, {
136 |         message,
137 |         model_override: modelOverride
138 |       })
139 | 
140 |       if (!response) {
141 |         throw new Error('No response body')
142 |       }
143 | 
144 |       const reader = response.getReader()
145 |       const decoder = new TextDecoder()
146 |       let aiMessage: SourceChatMessage | null = null
147 | 
148 |       while (true) {
149 |         const { done, value } = await reader.read()
150 |         if (done) break
151 | 
152 |         const text = decoder.decode(value)
153 |         const lines = text.split('\n')
154 | 
155 |         for (const line of lines) {
156 |           if (line.startsWith('data: ')) {
157 |             try {
158 |               const data = JSON.parse(line.slice(6))
159 |               
160 |               if (data.type === 'ai_message') {
161 |                 // Create AI message on first content chunk to avoid empty bubble
162 |                 if (!aiMessage) {
163 |                   aiMessage = {
164 |                     id: `ai-${Date.now()}`,
165 |                     type: 'ai',
166 |                     content: data.content || '',
167 |                     timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
168 |                   }
169 |                   setMessages(prev => [...prev, aiMessage!])
170 |                 } else {
171 |                   aiMessage.content += data.content || ''
172 |                   setMessages(prev =>
173 |                     prev.map(msg => msg.id === aiMessage!.id
174 |                       ? { ...msg, content: aiMessage!.content }
175 |                       : msg
176 |                     )
177 |                   )
178 |                 }
179 |               } else if (data.type === 'context_indicators') {
180 |                 setContextIndicators(data.data)
181 |               } else if (data.type === 'error') {
182 |                 throw new Error(data.message || 'Stream error')
183 |               }
184 |             } catch (e) {
185 |               console.error('Error parsing SSE data:', e)
186 |             }
187 |           }
188 |         }
189 |       }
190 |     } catch (err: unknown) {
191 |       const error = err as { response?: { data?: { detail?: string } }, message?: string };
192 |       console.error('Error sending message:', error)
193 |       toast.error(t(getApiErrorKey(error.response?.data?.detail || error.message, 'apiErrors.failedToSendMessage')))
194 |       // Remove optimistic messages on error
195 |       setMessages(prev => prev.filter(msg => !msg.id.startsWith('temp-')))
196 |     } finally {
197 |       setIsStreaming(false)
198 |       // Refetch session to get persisted messages
199 |       refetchCurrentSession()
200 |     }
201 |   }, [sourceId, currentSessionId, refetchCurrentSession, queryClient, t])
202 | 
203 |   // Cancel streaming
204 |   const cancelStreaming = useCallback(() => {
205 |     if (abortControllerRef.current) {
206 |       abortControllerRef.current.abort()
207 |       setIsStreaming(false)
208 |     }
209 |   }, [])
210 | 
211 |   // Switch session
212 |   const switchSession = useCallback((sessionId: string) => {
213 |     setCurrentSessionId(sessionId)
214 |     setContextIndicators(null)
215 |   }, [])
216 | 
217 |   // Create session
218 |   const createSession = useCallback((data: Omit<CreateSourceChatSessionRequest, 'source_id'>) => {
219 |     return createSessionMutation.mutate(data)
220 |   }, [createSessionMutation])
221 | 
222 |   // Update session
223 |   const updateSession = useCallback((sessionId: string, data: UpdateSourceChatSessionRequest) => {
224 |     return updateSessionMutation.mutate({ sessionId, data })
225 |   }, [updateSessionMutation])
226 | 
227 |   // Delete session
228 |   const deleteSession = useCallback((sessionId: string) => {
229 |     return deleteSessionMutation.mutate(sessionId)
230 |   }, [deleteSessionMutation])
231 | 
232 |   return {
233 |     // State
234 |     sessions,
235 |     currentSession: sessions.find(s => s.id === currentSessionId),
236 |     currentSessionId,
237 |     messages,
238 |     isStreaming,
239 |     contextIndicators,
240 |     loadingSessions,
241 |     
242 |     // Actions
243 |     createSession,
244 |     updateSession,
245 |     deleteSession,
246 |     switchSession,
247 |     sendMessage,
248 |     cancelStreaming,
249 |     refetchSessions
250 |   }
251 | }
252 |

/open_notebook/utils/CLAUDE.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Utils Module
  2 | 
  3 | Utility functions and helpers for context building, text processing, chunking, embedding, tokenization, and versioning.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Purpose
  6 | 
  7 | Provides cross-cutting concerns: building LLM context from sources/insights, content-type aware text chunking, unified embedding generation with mean pooling, token counting, and version management.
  8 | 
  9 | ## Architecture Overview
 10 | 
 11 | **Six core utilities**:
 12 | 1. **context_builder.py**: Flexible context assembly from sources, notes, insights with token budgeting
 13 | 2. **chunking.py**: Content-type detection and smart text chunking for embedding operations
 14 | 3. **embedding.py**: Unified embedding generation with mean pooling for large content
 15 | 4. **text_utils.py**: Text cleaning and thinking content extraction
 16 | 5. **token_utils.py**: Token counting for LLM context windows (wrapper around encoding library)
 17 | 6. **version_utils.py**: Version parsing, comparison, and schema compatibility checks
 18 | 
 19 | Each utility is stateless and can be imported independently.
 20 | 
 21 | ## Configuration
 22 | 
 23 | ### Chunking Configuration (chunking.py)
 24 | 
 25 | The chunking behavior can be configured via environment variables:
 26 | 
 27 | - **OPEN_NOTEBOOK_CHUNK_SIZE**: Maximum chunk size in characters (default: 1200)
 28 |   - Minimum: 100 characters
 29 |   - Warnings: Values > 8192 characters or invalid values
 30 |   - Use case: Smaller models (e.g., mxbai-embed-large with limited context window)
 31 | 
 32 | - **OPEN_NOTEBOOK_CHUNK_OVERLAP**: Overlap between chunks in characters (default: 15% of CHUNK_SIZE)
 33 |   - Must be: >= 0 and < CHUNK_SIZE
 34 |   - Warnings: Invalid values or values >= CHUNK_SIZE
 35 |   - Use case: Control how much context is shared between adjacent chunks
 36 | 
 37 | Example for models with small context windows:
 38 | ```bash
 39 | export OPEN_NOTEBOOK_CHUNK_SIZE=512
 40 | export OPEN_NOTEBOOK_CHUNK_OVERLAP=50
 41 | ```
 42 | 
 43 | Note: Changes require restart of the application.
 44 | 
 45 | ## Component Catalog
 46 | 
 47 | ### context_builder.py
 48 | - **ContextItem**: Dataclass for individual context piece (id, type, content, priority, token_count)
 49 | - **ContextConfig**: Configuration for context building (sources/notes/insights selection, max tokens, priority weights)
 50 | - **ContextBuilder**: Main class assembling context
 51 |   - `add_source()`: Include source by ID with inclusion level
 52 |   - `add_note()`: Include note by ID
 53 |   - `add_insight()`: Include insight by ID
 54 |   - `build()`: Assemble context respecting token budget and priorities
 55 |   - Uses vector_search to fetch source/insight content from SurrealDB
 56 |   - Returns list of ContextItem objects sorted by priority
 57 | 
 58 | **Key behavior**:
 59 | - Token counting is automatic (calculated in ContextItem.__post_init__)
 60 | - Max token enforcement via priority weighting (higher priority items included first)
 61 | - Type-specific fetching: sources → Source.full_text, notes → Note.content, insights → SourceInsight.content
 62 | - Raises DatabaseOperationError if source/note fetch fails
 63 | 
 64 | ### chunking.py
 65 | - **ContentType**: Enum (HTML, MARKDOWN, PLAIN)
 66 | - **CHUNK_SIZE**: Configurable via `OPEN_NOTEBOOK_CHUNK_SIZE` env var (default: 1200)
 67 | - **CHUNK_OVERLAP**: Configurable via `OPEN_NOTEBOOK_CHUNK_OVERLAP` env var (default: 15% of CHUNK_SIZE)
 68 | - **detect_content_type_from_extension(file_path)**: Detect type from file extension
 69 | - **detect_content_type_from_heuristics(text)**: Detect type from content patterns (returns type + confidence)
 70 | - **detect_content_type(text, file_path)**: Combined detection (extension primary, heuristics fallback)
 71 | - **chunk_text(text, content_type, file_path)**: Split text using appropriate splitter
 72 | 
 73 | **Key behavior**:
 74 | - Uses LangChain splitters: HTMLHeaderTextSplitter, MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter, RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
 75 | - Extension-based detection is primary; heuristics can override PLAIN extensions with 0.8+ confidence
 76 | - Secondary chunking applied when HTML/Markdown splitters produce oversized chunks
 77 | - Returns list of strings, each ≤ CHUNK_SIZE characters
 78 | 
 79 | ### embedding.py
 80 | - **mean_pool_embeddings(embeddings)**: Combine multiple embeddings via normalized mean pooling
 81 | - **generate_embeddings(texts)**: Batch embedding via single Esperanto API call
 82 | - **generate_embedding(text, content_type, file_path)**: Unified embedding with automatic chunking + mean pooling
 83 | 
 84 | **Key behavior**:
 85 | - Uses model_manager.get_model("embedding") for embedding model
 86 | - Short text (≤ CHUNK_SIZE): direct embedding
 87 | - Long text: chunk → embed each → mean pool results
 88 | - Mean pooling: normalize each → mean → normalize result (using numpy)
 89 | - Raises ValueError for empty/whitespace-only text
 90 | 
 91 | ### text_utils.py
 92 | - **remove_non_ascii(text)**: Remove non-ASCII characters from text
 93 | - **remove_non_printable(text)**: Remove non-printable characters, preserving newlines/tabs
 94 | - **parse_thinking_content(content)**: Extract `<think>` tags content from AI responses
 95 | - **clean_thinking_content(content)**: Remove `<think>` blocks, return cleaned content only
 96 | 
 97 | **Key behavior**:
 98 | - parse_thinking_content handles malformed output (missing opening `<think>` tag)
 99 | - Large content (>100KB) bypasses thinking extraction for performance
100 | - Non-string input returns empty thinking and stringified content
101 | 
102 | ### token_utils.py
103 | - **token_count(text)**: Returns estimated token count for string (via tiktoken)
104 | - **token_cost(text, model)**: Calculate cost estimate for text with given model
105 | 
106 | **Key behavior**: Uses cl100k_base encoding; may differ slightly from actual model tokenization
107 | 
108 | ### version_utils.py
109 | - **compare_versions(v1, v2)**: Returns -1 (v1 < v2), 0 (equal), 1 (v1 > v2)
110 | - **get_installed_version(package)**: Get version of installed Python package
111 | - **get_version_from_github(url)**: Fetch latest version from GitHub releases
112 | 
113 | **Key behavior**: Uses packaging library for version parsing; supports pre-release tags
114 | 
115 | ## Common Patterns
116 | 
117 | - **Dataclass-driven config**: ContextConfig used by ContextBuilder (immutable after init)
118 | - **Token budgeting**: ContextBuilder respects max_tokens constraint; prioritizes high-priority items
119 | - **Content-type aware processing**: Chunking uses appropriate splitter based on detected content type
120 | - **Mean pooling for large content**: Embedding handles arbitrarily large text via chunking + pooling
121 | - **Error handling resilience**: token_count() returns estimate; context_builder catches DB errors gracefully
122 | - **Pure text functions**: text_utils functions are stateless utilities (no class needed)
123 | - **Lazy evaluation**: ContextBuilder doesn't fetch items until build() called
124 | - **Type hints throughout**: All functions use Optional, List, Dict for clarity
125 | 
126 | ## Key Dependencies
127 | 
128 | - `open_notebook.domain.notebook`: Source, Note, SourceInsight models; vector_search function
129 | - `open_notebook.ai.models`: model_manager for embedding model access
130 | - `open_notebook.exceptions`: DatabaseOperationError, NotFoundError
131 | - `langchain_text_splitters`: HTMLHeaderTextSplitter, MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter, RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
132 | - `numpy`: Mean pooling calculations
133 | - `tiktoken`: Token encoding for GPT models
134 | - `loguru`: Logging throughout
135 | 
136 | ## Important Quirks & Gotchas
137 | 
138 | - **Token count estimation**: Uses cl100k_base encoding; may differ 5-10% from actual model tokens
139 | - **Chunk size for Ollama**: 1500 chars chosen to fit within Ollama embedding model context limits
140 | - **Content type detection order**: Extension checked first, then heuristics; high-confidence heuristics (≥0.8) can override PLAIN extensions
141 | - **Mean pooling normalization**: Each embedding normalized before mean, result normalized after
142 | - **Priority weights default**: If not specified, ContextConfig uses default weights (source=1, note=0.8, insight=1.2)
143 | - **Vector search required**: ContextBuilder assumes vector_search is available on Notebook model; fails if not
144 | - **Circular import risk**: context_builder imports from domain.notebook; avoid domain importing utils
145 | - **Max tokens hard limit**: ContextBuilder stops adding items once max_tokens exceeded (not prorated)
146 | - **No caching**: Every build() call re-fetches from database (use cache layer if needed)
147 | 
148 | ## How to Extend
149 | 
150 | 1. **Add new context source type**: Create fetch method in ContextBuilder; update ContextConfig.sources dict
151 | 2. **Add content type**: Add to ContentType enum; create splitter getter; update chunk_text()
152 | 3. **Change chunk size**: Set OPEN_NOTEBOOK_CHUNK_SIZE and OPEN_NOTEBOOK_CHUNK_OVERLAP environment variables
153 | 4. **Add text preprocessing**: Add new function to text_utils (e.g., remove_urls, extract_keywords)
154 | 5. **Change tokenization**: Replace tiktoken with alternative library in token_utils; update all calls
155 | 6. **Add context filtering**: Extend ContextConfig with filter_by_date, filter_by_topic fields
156 | 
157 | ## Usage Examples
158 | 
159 | ### Chunking
160 | ```python
161 | from open_notebook.utils.chunking import chunk_text, detect_content_type, ContentType
162 | 
163 | # Auto-detect content type and chunk
164 | chunks = chunk_text(long_text, file_path="document.md")
165 | 
166 | # Explicit content type
167 | chunks = chunk_text(html_content, content_type=ContentType.HTML)
168 | ```
169 | 
170 | ### Embedding
171 | ```python
172 | from open_notebook.utils.embedding import generate_embedding, generate_embeddings
173 | 
174 | # Single text (handles chunking + mean pooling automatically)
175 | embedding = await generate_embedding(long_text)
176 | 
177 | # Batch embedding (more efficient for multiple texts)
178 | embeddings = await generate_embeddings(["text1", "text2", "text3"])
179 | ```
180 | 
181 | ### Context Building
182 | ```python
183 | from open_notebook.utils.context_builder import ContextBuilder, ContextConfig
184 | 
185 | config = ContextConfig(
186 |     sources={"source:123": "full", "source:456": "summary"},
187 |     max_tokens=2000,
188 | )
189 | builder = ContextBuilder(notebook, config)
190 | context_items = await builder.build()
191 | 
192 | for item in context_items:
193 |     print(f"{item.type}:{item.id} ({item.token_count} tokens)")
194 | ```
195 |
