/docs/6-TROUBLESHOOTING/quick-fixes.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Quick Fixes - Top 11 Issues & Solutions
  2 | 
  3 | Common problems with 1-minute solutions.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## #1: "Cannot connect to server"
  8 | 
  9 | **Symptom:** Browser shows error "Cannot connect to server" or "Unable to reach API"
 10 | 
 11 | **Cause:** Frontend can't reach API
 12 | 
 13 | **Solution (1 minute):**
 14 | 
 15 | ```bash
 16 | # Step 1: Check if API is running
 17 | docker ps | grep api
 18 | 
 19 | # Step 2: Verify port 5055 is accessible
 20 | curl http://localhost:5055/health
 21 | 
 22 | # Expected output: {"status":"ok"}
 23 | 
 24 | # If that doesn't work:
 25 | # Step 3: Restart services
 26 | docker compose restart
 27 | 
 28 | # Step 4: Try again
 29 | # Open http://localhost:8502 in browser
 30 | ```
 31 | 
 32 | **If still broken:**
 33 | - Check `API_URL` in .env (should match your frontend URL)
 34 | - See [Connection Issues](connection-issues.md)
 35 | 
 36 | ---
 37 | 
 38 | ## #2: "Invalid API key" or "Models not showing"
 39 | 
 40 | **Symptom:** Settings → Models shows "No models available"
 41 | 
 42 | **Cause:** API key missing, wrong, or not set
 43 | 
 44 | **Solution (1 minute):**
 45 | 
 46 | ```bash
 47 | # Step 1: Check your .env has API key
 48 | cat .env | grep OPENAI_API_KEY
 49 | 
 50 | # Step 2: Verify it's correct (from https://platform.openai.com/api-keys)
 51 | # Should look like: sk-proj-xxx...
 52 | 
 53 | # Step 3: Restart services
 54 | docker compose restart api
 55 | 
 56 | # Step 4: Wait 10 seconds, then refresh browser
 57 | # Go to Settings → Models
 58 | 
 59 | # If still no models:
 60 | # Check logs for error
 61 | docker compose logs api | grep -i "api key\|error"
 62 | ```
 63 | 
 64 | **If still broken:**
 65 | - Make sure key has no extra spaces
 66 | - Generate a fresh key from provider dashboard
 67 | - See [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md)
 68 | 
 69 | ---
 70 | 
 71 | ## #3: "Port X already in use"
 72 | 
 73 | **Symptom:** Docker error "Port 8502 is already allocated"
 74 | 
 75 | **Cause:** Another service using that port
 76 | 
 77 | **Solution (1 minute):**
 78 | 
 79 | ```bash
 80 | # Option 1: Stop the other service
 81 | # Find what's using port 8502
 82 | lsof -i :8502
 83 | # Kill it or close the app
 84 | 
 85 | # Option 2: Use different port
 86 | # Edit docker-compose.yml
 87 | # Change: - "8502:8502"
 88 | # To:     - "8503:8502"
 89 | 
 90 | # Then restart
 91 | docker compose restart
 92 | # Access at: http://localhost:8503
 93 | ```
 94 | 
 95 | ---
 96 | 
 97 | ## #4: "Cannot process file" or "Unsupported format"
 98 | 
 99 | **Symptom:** Upload fails or says "File format not supported"
100 | 
101 | **Cause:** File type not supported or too large
102 | 
103 | **Solution (1 minute):**
104 | 
105 | ```bash
106 | # Check if file format is supported:
107 | # ✓ PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX (documents)
108 | # ✓ MP3, WAV, M4A (audio)
109 | # ✓ MP4, AVI, MOV (video)
110 | # ✓ URLs/web links
111 | 
112 | # ✗ Pure images (.jpg without OCR)
113 | # ✗ Files > 100MB
114 | 
115 | # Try these:
116 | # - Convert to PDF if possible
117 | # - Split large files
118 | # - Try uploading again
119 | ```
120 | 
121 | ---
122 | 
123 | ## #5: "Chat is very slow"
124 | 
125 | **Symptom:** Chat responses take minutes or timeout
126 | 
127 | **Cause:** Slow AI provider, large context, or overloaded system
128 | 
129 | **Solution (1 minute):**
130 | 
131 | ```bash
132 | # Step 1: Check which model you're using
133 | # Settings → Models
134 | # Note the model name
135 | 
136 | # Step 2: Try a cheaper/faster model
137 | # OpenAI: Switch to gpt-4o-mini (10x cheaper, slightly faster)
138 | # Anthropic: Switch to claude-3-5-haiku (fastest)
139 | # Groq: Use any model (ultra-fast)
140 | 
141 | # Step 3: Reduce context
142 | # Chat: Select fewer sources
143 | # Use "Summary Only" instead of "Full Content"
144 | 
145 | # Step 4: Check if API is overloaded
146 | docker stats
147 | # Look at CPU/memory usage
148 | ```
149 | 
150 | For deep dive: See [AI & Chat Issues](ai-chat-issues.md)
151 | 
152 | ---
153 | 
154 | ## #6: "Chat gives bad responses"
155 | 
156 | **Symptom:** AI responses are generic, wrong, or irrelevant
157 | 
158 | **Cause:** Bad context, vague question, or wrong model
159 | 
160 | **Solution (1 minute):**
161 | 
162 | ```bash
163 | # Step 1: Make sure sources are in context
164 | # Click "Select Sources" in Chat
165 | # Verify relevant sources are checked and set to "Full Content"
166 | 
167 | # Step 2: Ask a specific question
168 | # Bad: "What do you think?"
169 | # Good: "Based on the paper's methodology section, what are the 3 main limitations?"
170 | 
171 | # Step 3: Try a more powerful model
172 | # OpenAI: Use gpt-4o (better reasoning)
173 | # Anthropic: Use claude-3-5-sonnet (best reasoning)
174 | 
175 | # Step 4: Check citations
176 | # Click citations to verify AI actually saw those sources
177 | ```
178 | 
179 | For detailed help: See [Chat Effectively](../3-USER-GUIDE/chat-effectively.md)
180 | 
181 | ---
182 | 
183 | ## #7: "Search returns nothing"
184 | 
185 | **Symptom:** Search shows 0 results even though content exists
186 | 
187 | **Cause:** Wrong search type or poor query
188 | 
189 | **Solution (1 minute):**
190 | 
191 | ```bash
192 | # Try a different search type:
193 | 
194 | # If you searched with KEYWORDS:
195 | # Try VECTOR SEARCH instead
196 | # (Concept-based, not keyword-based)
197 | 
198 | # If you searched for CONCEPTS:
199 | # Try TEXT SEARCH instead
200 | # (Look for specific words in your query)
201 | 
202 | # Try simpler search:
203 | # Instead of: "How do transformers work in neural networks?"
204 | # Try: "transformers" or "neural networks"
205 | 
206 | # Check sources are processed:
207 | # Go to notebook
208 | # All sources should show green "Ready" status
209 | ```
210 | 
211 | For detailed help: See [Search Effectively](../3-USER-GUIDE/search.md)
212 | 
213 | ---
214 | 
215 | ## #8: "Podcast generation failed"
216 | 
217 | **Symptom:** "Podcast generation failed" error
218 | 
219 | **Cause:** Insufficient content, API quota, or network issue
220 | 
221 | **Solution (1 minute):**
222 | 
223 | ```bash
224 | # Step 1: Make sure you have content
225 | # Select at least 1-2 sources
226 | # Avoid single-sentence sources
227 | 
228 | # Step 2: Try again
229 | # Sometimes it's a temporary API issue
230 | # Wait 30 seconds and retry
231 | 
232 | # Step 3: Check your TTS provider has quota
233 | # OpenAI: Check account has credits
234 | # ElevenLabs: Check monthly quota
235 | # Google: Check API quota
236 | 
237 | # Step 4: Try different TTS provider
238 | # In podcast generation, choose "Google" or "Local"
239 | # instead of "ElevenLabs"
240 | ```
241 | 
242 | For detailed help: See [FAQ](faq.md)
243 | 
244 | ---
245 | 
246 | ## #9: "Services won't start" or Docker error
247 | 
248 | **Symptom:** Docker error when running `docker compose up`
249 | 
250 | **Cause:** Corrupt configuration, permission issue, or resource issue
251 | 
252 | **Solution (1 minute):**
253 | 
254 | ```bash
255 | # Step 1: Check logs
256 | docker compose logs
257 | 
258 | # Step 2: Try restart
259 | docker compose restart
260 | 
261 | # Step 3: If that fails, rebuild
262 | docker compose down
263 | docker compose up --build
264 | 
265 | # Step 4: Check disk space
266 | df -h
267 | # Need at least 5GB free
268 | 
269 | # Step 5: Check Docker has enough memory
270 | # Docker settings → Resources → Memory: 4GB+
271 | ```
272 | 
273 | ---
274 | 
275 | ## #10: "Database says 'too many connections'"
276 | 
277 | **Symptom:** Error about database connections
278 | 
279 | **Cause:** Too many concurrent operations
280 | 
281 | **Solution (1 minute):**
282 | 
283 | ```bash
284 | # In .env, reduce concurrency:
285 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS=2
286 | 
287 | # Then restart:
288 | docker compose restart
289 | 
290 | # This makes it slower but more stable
291 | ```
292 | 
293 | ---
294 | 
295 | ## #11: Slow Startup or Download Timeouts (China/Slow Networks)
296 | 
297 | **Symptom:** Container crashes on startup, worker enters FATAL state, or pip/uv downloads fail
298 | 
299 | **Cause:** Slow network or restricted access to Python package repositories
300 | 
301 | **Solution:**
302 | 
303 | ### Increase Download Timeout
304 | ```yaml
305 | # In docker-compose.yml environment:
306 | environment:
307 |   - UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT=600  # 10 minutes (default is 30s)
308 | ```
309 | 
310 | ### Use Chinese Mirrors (if in China)
311 | ```yaml
312 | environment:
313 |   - UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT=600
314 |   - UV_INDEX_URL=https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple
315 |   - PIP_INDEX_URL=https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple
316 | ```
317 | 
318 | **Alternative Chinese mirrors:**
319 | - Tsinghua: `https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple`
320 | - Aliyun: `https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/`
321 | - Huawei: `https://repo.huaweicloud.com/repository/pypi/simple`
322 | 
323 | **Note:** First startup may take several minutes while dependencies download. Subsequent starts will be faster.
324 | 
325 | ---
326 | 
327 | ## Quick Troubleshooting Checklist
328 | 
329 | When something breaks:
330 | 
331 | - [ ] **Restart services:** `docker compose restart`
332 | - [ ] **Check logs:** `docker compose logs`
333 | - [ ] **Verify connectivity:** `curl http://localhost:5055/health`
334 | - [ ] **Check .env:** API keys set? API_URL correct?
335 | - [ ] **Check resources:** `docker stats` (CPU/memory)
336 | - [ ] **Clear cache:** `docker system prune` (free space)
337 | - [ ] **Rebuild if needed:** `docker compose up --build`
338 | 
339 | ---
340 | 
341 | ## Nuclear Options (Last Resort)
342 | 
343 | **Completely reset (will lose all data in Docker):**
344 | 
345 | ```bash
346 | docker compose down -v
347 | docker compose up --build
348 | ```
349 | 
350 | **Reset to defaults:**
351 | ```bash
352 | # Backup your .env first!
353 | cp .env .env.backup
354 | 
355 | # Reset to example
356 | cp .env.example .env
357 | 
358 | # Edit with your API keys
359 | # Restart
360 | docker compose up
361 | ```
362 | 
363 | ---
364 | 
365 | ## Prevention Tips
366 | 
367 | 1. **Keep backups** — Export your notebooks regularly
368 | 2. **Monitor logs** — Check `docker compose logs` periodically
369 | 3. **Update regularly** — Pull latest image: `docker pull lfnovo/open_notebook:latest`
370 | 4. **Document changes** — Keep notes on what you configured
371 | 5. **Test after updates** — Verify everything works
372 | 
373 | ---
374 | 
375 | ## Still Stuck?
376 | 
377 | - **Look up your exact error** in [Troubleshooting Index](index.md)
378 | - **Check the FAQ** in [FAQ](faq.md)
379 | - **Check logs:** `docker compose logs | head -50`
380 | - **Ask for help:** [Discord](https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w) or [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook/issues)
381 |

/docs/5-CONFIGURATION/local-stt.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Local Speech-to-Text Setup
  2 | 
  3 | Run speech-to-text locally for free, private audio/video transcription using OpenAI-compatible STT servers.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## Why Local STT?
  8 | 
  9 | | Benefit | Description |
 10 | |---------|-------------|
 11 | | **Free** | No per-minute costs after setup |
 12 | | **Private** | Audio never leaves your machine |
 13 | | **Unlimited** | No rate limits or quotas |
 14 | | **Offline** | Works without internet |
 15 | 
 16 | ---
 17 | 
 18 | ## Quick Start with Speaches
 19 | 
 20 | [Speaches](https://github.com/speaches-ai/speaches) is an open-source, OpenAI-compatible server that supports both TTS and STT. It uses [faster-whisper](https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper) for transcription.
 21 | 
 22 | ### Step 1: Create Docker Compose File
 23 | 
 24 | Create a folder and add `docker-compose.yml`:
 25 | 
 26 | ```yaml
 27 | services:
 28 |   speaches:
 29 |     image: ghcr.io/speaches-ai/speaches:latest-cpu
 30 |     container_name: speaches
 31 |     ports:
 32 |       - "8969:8000"
 33 |     volumes:
 34 |       - hf-hub-cache:/home/ubuntu/.cache/huggingface/hub
 35 |     restart: unless-stopped
 36 | 
 37 | volumes:
 38 |   hf-hub-cache:
 39 | ```
 40 | 
 41 | ### Step 2: Start and Download Model
 42 | 
 43 | ```bash
 44 | # Start Speaches
 45 | docker compose up -d
 46 | 
 47 | # Wait for startup
 48 | sleep 10
 49 | 
 50 | # Download Whisper model (~500MB for small)
 51 | docker compose exec speaches uv tool run speaches-cli model download Systran/faster-whisper-small
 52 | ```
 53 | 
 54 | Models can also be downloaded automatically on first use, but pre-downloading avoids delays.
 55 | 
 56 | ### Step 3: Test
 57 | 
 58 | ```bash
 59 | # Create a test audio file (or use your own)
 60 | # Then transcribe it:
 61 | curl "http://localhost:8969/v1/audio/transcriptions" \
 62 |   -F "file=@test.mp3" \
 63 |   -F "model=Systran/faster-whisper-small"
 64 | ```
 65 | 
 66 | You should see the transcribed text in the response.
 67 | 
 68 | ### Step 4: Configure Open Notebook
 69 | 
 70 | **Docker deployment:**
 71 | ```yaml
 72 | # In your Open Notebook docker-compose.yml
 73 | environment:
 74 |   - OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_STT=http://host.docker.internal:8969/v1
 75 | ```
 76 | 
 77 | **Local development:**
 78 | ```bash
 79 | export OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_STT=http://localhost:8969/v1
 80 | ```
 81 | 
 82 | ### Step 5: Add Model in Open Notebook
 83 | 
 84 | 1. Go to **Settings** → **Models**
 85 | 2. Click **Add Model** in Speech-to-Text section
 86 | 3. Configure:
 87 |    - **Provider**: `openai_compatible`
 88 |    - **Model Name**: `Systran/faster-whisper-small`
 89 |    - **Display Name**: `Local Whisper`
 90 | 4. Click **Save**
 91 | 5. Set as default if desired
 92 | 
 93 | ---
 94 | 
 95 | ## Available Models
 96 | 
 97 | Speaches supports various Whisper model sizes. Larger models are more accurate but slower:
 98 | 
 99 | | Model | Size | Speed | Accuracy | VRAM (GPU) |
100 | |-------|------|-------|----------|------------|
101 | | `Systran/faster-whisper-tiny` | ~75 MB | Fastest | Basic | ~1 GB |
102 | | `Systran/faster-whisper-base` | ~150 MB | Fast | Good | ~1 GB |
103 | | `Systran/faster-whisper-small` | ~500 MB | Medium | Better | ~2 GB |
104 | | `Systran/faster-whisper-medium` | ~1.5 GB | Slow | Great | ~5 GB |
105 | | `Systran/faster-whisper-large-v3` | ~3 GB | Slowest | Best | ~10 GB |
106 | | `Systran/faster-distil-whisper-small.en` | ~400 MB | Fast | Good (English only) | ~2 GB |
107 | 
108 | ### List Available Models
109 | 
110 | ```bash
111 | docker compose exec speaches uv tool run speaches-cli registry ls --task automatic-speech-recognition
112 | ```
113 | 
114 | ### Recommended Models
115 | 
116 | - **For speed**: `Systran/faster-whisper-tiny` or `Systran/faster-whisper-base`
117 | - **For balance**: `Systran/faster-whisper-small` (recommended)
118 | - **For accuracy**: `Systran/faster-whisper-large-v3`
119 | 
120 | ---
121 | 
122 | ## GPU Acceleration
123 | 
124 | For faster transcription with NVIDIA GPUs:
125 | 
126 | ```yaml
127 | services:
128 |   speaches:
129 |     image: ghcr.io/speaches-ai/speaches:latest-cuda
130 |     container_name: speaches
131 |     ports:
132 |       - "8969:8000"
133 |     volumes:
134 |       - hf-hub-cache:/home/ubuntu/.cache/huggingface/hub
135 |     environment:
136 |       - WHISPER__TTL=-1  # Keep model in VRAM (recommended if you have enough memory)
137 |     restart: unless-stopped
138 |     deploy:
139 |       resources:
140 |         reservations:
141 |           devices:
142 |             - driver: nvidia
143 |               count: 1
144 |               capabilities: [gpu]
145 | 
146 | volumes:
147 |   hf-hub-cache:
148 | ```
149 | 
150 | ### Keep Model in Memory
151 | 
152 | By default, Speaches unloads models after some time. To keep the Whisper model loaded for instant transcription:
153 | 
154 | ```yaml
155 | environment:
156 |   - WHISPER__TTL=-1  # Never unload
157 | ```
158 | 
159 | This is recommended if you have enough RAM/VRAM, as loading the model can take a few seconds.
160 | 
161 | ---
162 | 
163 | ## Docker Networking
164 | 
165 | ### Open Notebook in Docker (macOS/Windows)
166 | 
167 | ```bash
168 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_STT=http://host.docker.internal:8969/v1
169 | ```
170 | 
171 | ### Open Notebook in Docker (Linux)
172 | 
173 | ```bash
174 | # Option 1: Docker bridge IP
175 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_STT=http://172.17.0.1:8969/v1
176 | 
177 | # Option 2: Host networking
178 | docker run --network host ...
179 | ```
180 | 
181 | ### Remote Server
182 | 
183 | Run Speaches on a different machine:
184 | 
185 | ```bash
186 | # On server, bind to all interfaces
187 | # Then in Open Notebook:
188 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_STT=http://server-ip:8969/v1
189 | ```
190 | 
191 | ---
192 | 
193 | ## Language Support
194 | 
195 | Whisper supports 99+ languages. Specify the language for better accuracy:
196 | 
197 | ```bash
198 | curl "http://localhost:8969/v1/audio/transcriptions" \
199 |   -F "file=@audio.mp3" \
200 |   -F "model=Systran/faster-whisper-small" \
201 |   -F "language=ru"
202 | ```
203 | 
204 | Common language codes:
205 | - `en` - English
206 | - `ru` - Russian
207 | - `es` - Spanish
208 | - `fr` - French
209 | - `de` - German
210 | - `zh` - Chinese
211 | - `ja` - Japanese
212 | 
213 | ---
214 | 
215 | ## Troubleshooting
216 | 
217 | ### Service Won't Start
218 | 
219 | ```bash
220 | # Check logs
221 | docker compose logs speaches
222 | 
223 | # Verify port available
224 | lsof -i :8969
225 | 
226 | # Restart
227 | docker compose down && docker compose up -d
228 | ```
229 | 
230 | ### Connection Refused
231 | 
232 | ```bash
233 | # Test Speaches is running
234 | curl http://localhost:8969/v1/models
235 | 
236 | # From inside Open Notebook container
237 | docker exec -it open-notebook curl http://host.docker.internal:8969/v1/models
238 | ```
239 | 
240 | ### Model Download Fails
241 | 
242 | Models are downloaded automatically on first use. If download fails:
243 | 
244 | ```bash
245 | # Check available disk space
246 | df -h
247 | 
248 | # Check Docker logs for errors
249 | docker compose logs speaches
250 | 
251 | # Restart and try again
252 | docker compose restart speaches
253 | ```
254 | 
255 | ### Poor Transcription Quality
256 | 
257 | - Use a larger model (`faster-whisper-medium` or `large-v3`)
258 | - Specify the correct language
259 | - Ensure audio quality is good (clear speech, minimal background noise)
260 | - Try different audio formats (WAV often works better than MP3)
261 | 
262 | ### Slow Transcription
263 | 
264 | | Solution | How |
265 | |----------|-----|
266 | | Use GPU | Switch to `latest-cuda` image |
267 | | Smaller model | Use `faster-whisper-tiny` or `base` |
268 | | More CPU | Allocate more cores in Docker |
269 | | SSD storage | Move Docker volumes to SSD |
270 | 
271 | ---
272 | 
273 | ## Performance Tips
274 | 
275 | ### Recommended Specs
276 | 
277 | | Component | Minimum | Recommended |
278 | |-----------|---------|-------------|
279 | | CPU | 2 cores | 4+ cores |
280 | | RAM | 2 GB | 8+ GB |
281 | | Storage | 5 GB | 10 GB (for multiple models) |
282 | | GPU | None | NVIDIA (optional, much faster) |
283 | 
284 | ### Resource Limits
285 | 
286 | ```yaml
287 | services:
288 |   speaches:
289 |     # ... other config
290 |     mem_limit: 4g
291 |     cpus: 2
292 | ```
293 | 
294 | ### Monitor Usage
295 | 
296 | ```bash
297 | docker stats speaches
298 | ```
299 | 
300 | ---
301 | 
302 | ## Comparison: Local vs Cloud
303 | 
304 | | Aspect | Local (Speaches) | Cloud (OpenAI Whisper) |
305 | |--------|------------------|------------------------|
306 | | **Cost** | Free | $0.006/min |
307 | | **Privacy** | Complete | Data sent to provider |
308 | | **Speed** | Depends on hardware | Usually faster |
309 | | **Quality** | Excellent (same Whisper) | Excellent |
310 | | **Setup** | Moderate | Simple API key |
311 | | **Offline** | Yes | No |
312 | | **Languages** | 99+ | 99+ |
313 | 
314 | ### When to Use Local
315 | 
316 | - Privacy-sensitive content
317 | - High-volume transcription
318 | - Development/testing
319 | - Offline environments
320 | - Cost control
321 | 
322 | ### When to Use Cloud
323 | 
324 | - Limited hardware
325 | - Time-sensitive projects
326 | - No GPU available
327 | - Simple setup preferred
328 | 
329 | ---
330 | 
331 | ## Using Both TTS and STT
332 | 
333 | Speaches supports both TTS and STT in one server. Configure both:
334 | 
335 | ```bash
336 | # Same server for both
337 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_TTS=http://localhost:8969/v1
338 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_STT=http://localhost:8969/v1
339 | ```
340 | 
341 | See **[Local TTS Setup](local-tts.md)** for TTS configuration.
342 | 
343 | ---
344 | 
345 | ## Other Local STT Options
346 | 
347 | Any OpenAI-compatible STT server works:
348 | 
349 | | Server | Description |
350 | |--------|-------------|
351 | | [Speaches](https://github.com/speaches-ai/speaches) | TTS + STT in one (recommended) |
352 | | [faster-whisper-server](https://github.com/fedirz/faster-whisper-server) | Lightweight STT only |
353 | | [whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp) | C++ implementation with server mode |
354 | | [LocalAI](https://github.com/mudler/LocalAI) | Multi-model local AI server |
355 | 
356 | The key requirements:
357 | 
358 | 1. Server implements `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint
359 | 2. Set `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_STT` to server URL
360 | 3. Add model with provider `openai_compatible`
361 | 
362 | ---
363 | 
364 | ## Related
365 | 
366 | - **[Local TTS Setup](local-tts.md)** - Text-to-speech with Speaches
367 | - **[OpenAI-Compatible Providers](openai-compatible.md)** - General compatible provider setup
368 | - **[AI Providers](ai-providers.md)** - All provider configuration

206 |                           </AlertDialogAction>
207 |                         </AlertDialogFooter>
208 |                       </AlertDialogContent>

212 |               </Card>
213 |             )
214 |           })}
215 |         </div>
216 |       )}

 20 | def full_model_dump(model):
 21 |     if isinstance(model, BaseModel):
 22 |         return model.model_dump()
 23 |     elif isinstance(model, dict):
 24 |         return {k: full_model_dump(v) for k, v in model.items()}
 25 |     elif isinstance(model, list):
 26 |         return [full_model_dump(item) for item in model]
 27 |     else:
 28 |         return model

 31 | class SourceProcessingInput(CommandInput):
 32 |     source_id: str
 33 |     content_state: Dict[str, Any]
 34 |     notebook_ids: List[str]
 35 |     transformations: List[str]
 36 |     embed: bool
 37 | 
 38 | 
 39 | class SourceProcessingOutput(CommandOutput):
 40 |     success: bool
 41 |     source_id: str
 42 |     embedded_chunks: int = 0
 43 |     insights_created: int = 0
 44 |     processing_time: float
 45 |     error_message: Optional[str] = None
 46 | 
 47 | 
 48 | @command(
 49 |     "process_source",
 50 |     app="open_notebook",
 51 |     retry={
 52 |         "max_attempts": 15,  # Handle deep queues (workaround for SurrealDB v2 transaction conflicts)
 53 |         "wait_strategy": "exponential_jitter",
 54 |         "wait_min": 1,
 55 |         "wait_max": 120,  # Allow queue to drain
 56 |         "stop_on": [ValueError],  # Don't retry validation errors
 57 |         "retry_log_level": "debug",  # Avoid log noise during transaction conflicts
 58 |     },
 59 | )
 60 | async def process_source_command(
 61 |     input_data: SourceProcessingInput,
 62 | ) -> SourceProcessingOutput:
 63 |     """
 64 |     Process source content using the source_graph workflow
 65 |     """
 66 |     start_time = time.time()
 67 | 
 68 |     try:
 69 |         logger.info(f"Starting source processing for source: {input_data.source_id}")
 70 |         logger.info(f"Notebook IDs: {input_data.notebook_ids}")
 71 |         logger.info(f"Transformations: {input_data.transformations}")
 72 |         logger.info(f"Embed: {input_data.embed}")
 73 | 
 74 |         # 1. Load transformation objects from IDs
 75 |         transformations = []
 76 |         for trans_id in input_data.transformations:
 77 |             logger.info(f"Loading transformation: {trans_id}")
 78 |             transformation = await Transformation.get(trans_id)
 79 |             if not transformation:
 80 |                 raise ValueError(f"Transformation '{trans_id}' not found")
 81 |             transformations.append(transformation)
 82 | 
 83 |         logger.info(f"Loaded {len(transformations)} transformations")
 84 | 
 85 |         # 2. Get existing source record to update its command field
 86 |         source = await Source.get(input_data.source_id)
 87 |         if not source:
 88 |             raise ValueError(f"Source '{input_data.source_id}' not found")
 89 | 
 90 |         # Update source with command reference
 91 |         source.command = (
 92 |             ensure_record_id(input_data.execution_context.command_id)
 93 |             if input_data.execution_context
 94 |             else None
 95 |         )
 96 |         await source.save()
 97 | 
 98 |         logger.info(f"Updated source {source.id} with command reference")
 99 | 
100 |         # 3. Process source with all notebooks
101 |         logger.info(f"Processing source with {len(input_data.notebook_ids)} notebooks")
102 | 
103 |         # Execute source_graph with all notebooks
104 |         result = await source_graph.ainvoke(
105 |             {  # type: ignore[arg-type]
106 |                 "content_state": input_data.content_state,
107 |                 "notebook_ids": input_data.notebook_ids,  # Use notebook_ids (plural) as expected by SourceState
108 |                 "apply_transformations": transformations,
109 |                 "embed": input_data.embed,
110 |                 "source_id": input_data.source_id,  # Add the source_id to the state
111 |             }
112 |         )
113 | 
114 |         processed_source = result["source"]
115 | 
116 |         # 4. Gather processing results (notebook associations handled by source_graph)
117 |         embedded_chunks = (
118 |             await processed_source.get_embedded_chunks() if input_data.embed else 0
119 |         )
120 |         insights_list = await processed_source.get_insights()
121 |         insights_created = len(insights_list)
122 | 
123 |         processing_time = time.time() - start_time
124 |         logger.info(
125 |             f"Successfully processed source: {processed_source.id} in {processing_time:.2f}s"
126 |         )
127 |         logger.info(
128 |             f"Created {insights_created} insights and {embedded_chunks} embedded chunks"
129 |         )
130 | 
131 |         return SourceProcessingOutput(
132 |             success=True,
133 |             source_id=str(processed_source.id),
134 |             embedded_chunks=embedded_chunks,
135 |             insights_created=insights_created,
136 |             processing_time=processing_time,
137 |         )
138 | 
139 |     except ValueError as e:
140 |         # Validation errors are permanent failures - don't retry
141 |         processing_time = time.time() - start_time
142 |         logger.error(f"Source processing failed: {e}")
143 |         return SourceProcessingOutput(
144 |             success=False,
145 |             source_id=input_data.source_id,
146 |             processing_time=processing_time,
147 |             error_message=str(e),
148 |         )
149 |     except Exception as e:
150 |         # Transient failure - will be retried (surreal-commands logs final failure)
151 |         logger.debug(
152 |             f"Transient error processing source {input_data.source_id}: {e}"
153 |         )
154 |         raise
155 |

162 | class RunTransformationInput(CommandInput):
163 |     """Input for running a transformation on an existing source."""
164 | 
165 |     source_id: str
166 |     transformation_id: str
167 | 
168 | 
169 | class RunTransformationOutput(CommandOutput):
170 |     """Output from transformation command."""
171 | 
172 |     success: bool
173 |     source_id: str
174 |     transformation_id: str
175 |     processing_time: float
176 |     error_message: Optional[str] = None
177 | 
178 | 
179 | @command(
180 |     "run_transformation",
181 |     app="open_notebook",
182 |     retry={
183 |         "max_attempts": 5,
184 |         "wait_strategy": "exponential_jitter",
185 |         "wait_min": 1,
186 |         "wait_max": 60,
187 |         "stop_on": [ValueError],  # Don't retry validation errors
188 |         "retry_log_level": "debug",
189 |     },
190 | )
191 | async def run_transformation_command(
192 |     input_data: RunTransformationInput,
193 | ) -> RunTransformationOutput:
194 |     """
195 |     Run a transformation on an existing source to generate an insight.
196 | 
197 |     This command runs the transformation graph which:
198 |     1. Loads the source and transformation
199 |     2. Calls the LLM to generate insight content
200 |     3. Creates the insight via create_insight command (fire-and-forget)
201 | 
202 |     Use this command for UI-triggered insight generation to avoid blocking
203 |     the HTTP request while the LLM processes.
204 | 
205 |     Retry Strategy:
206 |     - Retries up to 5 times for transient failures (network, timeout, etc.)
207 |     - Uses exponential-jitter backoff (1-60s)
208 |     - Does NOT retry permanent failures (ValueError for validation errors)
209 |     """
210 |     start_time = time.time()
211 | 
212 |     try:
213 |         logger.info(
214 |             f"Running transformation {input_data.transformation_id} "
215 |             f"on source {input_data.source_id}"
216 |         )
217 | 
218 |         # Load source
219 |         source = await Source.get(input_data.source_id)
220 |         if not source:
221 |             raise ValueError(f"Source '{input_data.source_id}' not found")
222 | 
223 |         # Load transformation
224 |         transformation = await Transformation.get(input_data.transformation_id)
225 |         if not transformation:
226 |             raise ValueError(
227 |                 f"Transformation '{input_data.transformation_id}' not found"
228 |             )
229 | 
230 |         # Run transformation graph (includes LLM call + insight creation)
231 |         await transform_graph.ainvoke(
232 |             input=dict(source=source, transformation=transformation)
233 |         )
234 | 
235 |         processing_time = time.time() - start_time
236 |         logger.info(
237 |             f"Successfully ran transformation {input_data.transformation_id} "
238 |             f"on source {input_data.source_id} in {processing_time:.2f}s"
239 |         )
240 | 
241 |         return RunTransformationOutput(
242 |             success=True,
243 |             source_id=input_data.source_id,
244 |             transformation_id=input_data.transformation_id,
245 |             processing_time=processing_time,
246 |         )
247 | 
248 |     except ValueError as e:
249 |         # Validation errors are permanent failures - don't retry
250 |         processing_time = time.time() - start_time
251 |         logger.error(
252 |             f"Failed to run transformation {input_data.transformation_id} "
253 |             f"on source {input_data.source_id}: {e}"
254 |         )
255 |         return RunTransformationOutput(
256 |             success=False,
257 |             source_id=input_data.source_id,
258 |             transformation_id=input_data.transformation_id,
259 |             processing_time=processing_time,
260 |             error_message=str(e),
261 |         )
262 |     except Exception as e:
263 |         # Transient failure - will be retried (surreal-commands logs final failure)
264 |         logger.debug(
265 |             f"Transient error running transformation {input_data.transformation_id} "
266 |             f"on source {input_data.source_id}: {e}"
267 |         )
268 |         raise

/frontend/src/CLAUDE.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Frontend Architecture
  2 | 
  3 | Next.js React application providing UI for Open Notebook research assistant. Three-layer architecture: **pages** (Next.js App Router), **components** (feature-specific UI), and **lib** (data fetching, state management, utilities).
  4 | 
  5 | ## High-Level Data Flow
  6 | 
  7 | ```
  8 | Pages (Next.js) → Components (feature-specific) → Hooks (queries/mutations)
  9 |                                                        ↓
 10 |                           Stores (auth/modal state) → API module → Backend
 11 | ```
 12 | 
 13 | User interactions trigger mutations/queries via hooks, which communicate with the backend through the API module. Store state (auth, modals) flows back to components via hooks. Child CLAUDE.md files document specific modules in detail:
 14 | 
 15 | - **`lib/api/CLAUDE.md`**: Axios client, FormData handling, interceptors
 16 | - **`lib/hooks/CLAUDE.md`**: TanStack Query wrappers, SSE streaming, context building
 17 | - **`lib/stores/CLAUDE.md`**: Zustand auth/modal state, localStorage persistence
 18 | - **`lib/locales/CLAUDE.md`**: Internationalization (i18n) system, translation files
 19 | - **`components/ui/CLAUDE.md`**: Radix UI primitives, CVA styling, accessibility
 20 | 
 21 | ## Architectural Layers
 22 | 
 23 | ### Pages (`src/app/`) — Next.js App Router
 24 | - `(auth)/login`: Authentication entry point
 25 | - `(dashboard)/`: Protected routes (notebooks, sources, search, models, etc.)
 26 | - Directory-based routing; each `page.tsx` is a route endpoint
 27 | - **Key pattern**: Pages call hooks to fetch data, render components with state
 28 | - **Router groups** `(auth)`, `(dashboard)` organize routes by feature without affecting URL
 29 | 
 30 | ### Components (`src/components/`) — Feature-Specific UI
 31 | - **layout**: `AppShell.tsx`, `AppSidebar.tsx` — main layout wrapper used by all pages
 32 | - **providers**: `ThemeProvider`, `QueryProvider`, `ModalProvider` — app-wide context setup
 33 | - **auth**: `LoginForm.tsx` — authentication UI
 34 | - **common**: `CommandPalette`, `ErrorBoundary`, `ContextToggle`, `ModelSelector` — shared across pages
 35 | - **ui**: Reusable Radix UI building blocks (see child CLAUDE.md)
 36 | - **source**, **notebooks**, **search**, **podcasts**: Feature-specific components consuming hooks
 37 | 
 38 | **Component composition pattern**: Pages → Feature components → UI components. Feature components handle page-level state (loading, error), UI components remain stateless and styled.
 39 | 
 40 | ### Lib (`src/lib/`) — Data & State Layer
 41 | 
 42 | #### `lib/api/` — Backend Communication
 43 | - **`client.ts`**: Central Axios instance with auth interceptor, FormData handling, 10-min timeout
 44 | - **`query-client.ts`**: TanStack Query configuration
 45 | - **Resource modules** (`sources.ts`, `chat.ts`, `notebooks.ts`, etc.): Endpoint-specific functions returning typed responses
 46 | - **Pattern**: All requests go through `apiClient`; auth token auto-added from localStorage
 47 | 
 48 | #### `lib/hooks/` — React Query + Custom Logic
 49 | - **Query hooks**: `useNotebookSources`, `useSources`, `useSource` — TanStack Query wrappers with cache keys
 50 | - **Mutation hooks**: `useCreateSource`, `useUpdateSource`, `useDeleteSource` — mutations with toast feedback + cache invalidation
 51 | - **Complex hooks**: `useNotebookChat`, `useSourceChat` — session management, message streaming, context building
 52 | - **SSE streaming**: `useAsk` — parses newline-delimited JSON from backend for multi-stage workflows
 53 | - **Pattern**: Hooks return `{ data, isLoading, error, refetch }` + action functions; cache invalidation on mutations
 54 | 
 55 | #### `lib/stores/` — Application State
 56 | - **`auth-store.ts`**: Authentication state (token, isAuthenticated) with 30-second check caching
 57 | - **Zustand + persist middleware**: Auto-syncs sensitive state to localStorage
 58 | - **Pattern**: Store actions (`login()`, `logout()`, `checkAuth()`) update state; consumed via hooks in components
 59 | 
 60 | #### `lib/types/` — TypeScript Definitions
 61 | - API request/response shapes, domain models (Notebook, Source, Note, etc.)
 62 | - Ensures type safety across API calls and store mutations
 63 | 
 64 | #### `lib/locales/` — Internationalization (i18n)
 65 | - **Locale files** (`en-US/`, `pt-BR/`, `zh-CN/`, `zh-TW/`, `ja-JP/`): Translation strings organized by feature
 66 | - **`i18n.ts`**: i18next configuration with language detection
 67 | - **`use-translation.ts`**: Custom hook with Proxy-based `t.section.key` access pattern
 68 | - **Pattern**: Components call `useTranslation()` hook; access strings via `t.common.save`, `t.notebooks.title`
 69 | 
 70 | ## Data & Control Flow Walkthrough
 71 | 
 72 | ### Example: Notebook Chat
 73 | 1. **Page** (`notebooks/[id]/page.tsx`) fetches initial data, passes `notebookId` to `ChatColumn` component
 74 | 2. **Hook call** (`useNotebookChat()`):
 75 |    - Queries sessions for notebook via TanStack Query
 76 |    - Sets up message state + context building logic
 77 |    - Returns `{ messages, sendMessage(), setModelOverride() }`
 78 | 3. **Component renders**: `ChatColumn` displays messages, text input
 79 | 4. **User sends message**: Component calls `sendMessage()` hook
 80 | 5. **Hook execution**:
 81 |    - Builds context from selected sources/notes via `buildContext()` helper
 82 |    - Calls `chatApi.sendMessage()` (from API module)
 83 |    - Client-side optimistic update: adds message to local state before response
 84 | 6. **Backend response** arrives, TanStack Query updates cache
 85 | 7. **Cache invalidation** on other source/note mutations ensures stale UI refreshes
 86 | 
 87 | ### Example: File Upload with Source Creation
 88 | 1. **Component** (`SourceDialog`) renders form with file picker
 89 | 2. **Hook** (`useFileUpload`):
 90 |    - Converts file to FormData (JSON fields stringified)
 91 |    - Calls `sourcesApi.create()` with FormData
 92 |    - API client interceptor deletes Content-Type header (lets browser set multipart boundary)
 93 | 3. **Toast notifications** show progress
 94 | 4. **Cache invalidation** on success: `queryClient.invalidateQueries(['sources'])`
 95 | 5. **Related queries** auto-refetch: notebooks, sources list, etc.
 96 | 
 97 | ## Key Patterns & Cross-Layer Coordination
 98 | 
 99 | ### Caching & Invalidation
100 | - **Query keys**: `QUERY_KEYS.notebook(id)`, `QUERY_KEYS.sources(notebookId)` — hierarchical structure
101 | - **Broad invalidation**: `['sources']` invalidates all source queries; trade-off between accuracy + performance
102 | - **Auto-refetch**: `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` on frequently-changing data (sources, notebooks)
103 | 
104 | ### Auth & Protected Routes
105 | - **Proxy** (`src/proxy.ts`): Redirects root `/` to `/notebooks`
106 | - **Auth store**: Validates token via `/notebooks` API call (actual validation, not JWT decode)
107 | - **Interceptor**: Adds `Bearer {token}` to all requests; 401 response clears auth and redirects to login
108 | 
109 | ### Modal State Management
110 | - **Modal hooks**: Components query modal state from stores
111 | - **Context**: Modals pass data (e.g., notebook ID) to child components
112 | - **Pattern**: One store per modal type; triggered by button clicks + data passing via hook arguments
113 | 
114 | ### Error Handling
115 | - **API errors**: All request failures propagate to consuming code; components show toast notifications
116 | - **Toast feedback**: Mutations show success/error toasts (from `sonner` library)
117 | - **Error boundary**: App-level error boundary catches React render errors; shows fallback UI
118 | 
119 | ### FormData Handling
120 | - **JSON fields**: Nested objects (arrays, objects) must be JSON stringified before FormData
121 | - **Content-Type header**: Removed by interceptor for FormData requests (lets browser set boundary)
122 | - **Example**: `sources` array converted to string via `JSON.stringify()` before appending to FormData
123 | 
124 | ## Component Organization Within Features
125 | 
126 | - **Feature folders** (`source/`, `notebooks/`, `podcasts/`): Group related components
127 | - **Composition**: Larger components nest smaller ones; no deep prop drilling (state lifted to hooks)
128 | - **Dialog patterns**: Features define dialog components for inline actions (edit, create, delete)
129 | - **Props**: Components accept data + action callbacks from parent or hooks
130 | 
131 | ## Providers & Context Setup
132 | 
133 | **Root layout** (`app/layout.tsx`) wraps app with (outermost → innermost):
134 | 1. `ErrorBoundary` — React error boundary (catches all render errors)
135 | 2. `ThemeProvider` — next-themes for light/dark mode
136 | 3. `QueryProvider` — TanStack Query client
137 | 4. `I18nProvider` — i18next initialization and language loading overlay
138 | 5. `ConnectionGuard` — checks backend connectivity on startup
139 | 6. `Toaster` — sonner toast notification system (inside ConnectionGuard)
140 | 
141 | ## Important Gotchas & Design Decisions
142 | 
143 | - **Token storage**: Stored in localStorage under `auth-storage` key (Zustand persist); consumed by API interceptor
144 | - **Base URL discovery**: API client fetches base URL from runtime config on first request (async; can be slow on startup)
145 | - **Optimistic updates**: Chat messages added to state before server confirmation; removed on error
146 | - **Modal lifecycle**: Dialogs not auto-reset; parent must clear form state after submit
147 | - **Focus management**: Dialog auto-focuses first input; can cause layout shifts if inputs are conditional
148 | - **Cache invalidation breadth**: Trade-off between precision + simplicity; broad invalidation simpler but may over-fetch
149 | 
150 | ## How to Add a New Feature
151 | 
152 | 1. **Create page**: `app/(dashboard)/feature/page.tsx` — calls hooks, renders components
153 | 2. **Create feature components**: `components/feature/` — compose UI + business logic
154 | 3. **Add hooks** (if data needed): `lib/hooks/useFeature.ts` — TanStack Query wrapper
155 | 4. **Add API module** (if backend call needed): `lib/api/feature.ts` — resource-specific functions
156 | 5. **Add types**: `lib/types/api.ts` — request/response shapes
157 | 6. **Use UI components**: Import from `components/ui/` for consistent styling
158 | 7. **Handle auth**: Middleware redirects unauthenticated users; no special handling needed in component
159 | 
160 | ## Testing
161 | 
162 | - **Hooks**: Mock API functions, wrap in `QueryClientProvider`, assert query/mutation behavior
163 | - **Components**: Mock hooks via `vi.fn()`, test rendering + user interactions
164 | - **API calls**: Mock `axios` interceptors; test request/response shapes
165 | - **Stores**: Mock store state, test mutations via `act()`, assert state changes
166 | 
167 | See child CLAUDE.md files for module-specific testing patterns.
168 |

  9 | import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
 10 | import { Textarea } from '@/components/ui/textarea'
 11 | import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/checkbox'
 12 | import { Label } from '@/components/ui/label'
 13 | import { MarkdownEditor } from '@/components/ui/markdown-editor'
 14 | import { useCreateTransformation, useUpdateTransformation, useTransformation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-transformations'
 15 | import { Transformation } from '@/lib/types/transformations'
 16 | import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
 17 | import { TRANSFORMATION_QUERY_KEYS } from '@/lib/hooks/use-transformations'
 18 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
 19 | 
 20 | const transformationSchema = z.object({
 21 |   name: z.string().min(1),
 22 |   title: z.string().min(1),
 23 |   description: z.string().optional(),
 24 |   prompt: z.string().min(1),
 25 |   apply_default: z.boolean().optional(),
 26 | })
 27 | 
 28 | type TransformationFormData = z.infer<typeof transformationSchema>
 29 | 
 30 | interface TransformationEditorDialogProps {
 31 |   open: boolean
 32 |   onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void
 33 |   transformation?: Transformation
 34 | }
 35 | 
 36 | export function TransformationEditorDialog({ open, onOpenChange, transformation }: TransformationEditorDialogProps) {
 37 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 38 |   const nameId = useId()
 39 |   const titleId = useId()
 40 |   const defaultId = useId()
 41 |   const descriptionId = useId()
 42 |   const promptId = useId()
 43 |   const isEditing = Boolean(transformation)
 44 |   const { data: fetchedTransformation, isLoading } = useTransformation(transformation?.id ?? '', {
 45 |     enabled: open && Boolean(transformation?.id),
 46 |   })
 47 |   const createTransformation = useCreateTransformation()
 48 |   const updateTransformation = useUpdateTransformation()
 49 |   const queryClient = useQueryClient()
 50 | 
 51 |   const {
 52 |     control,
 53 |     handleSubmit,
 54 |     formState: { errors },
 55 |     reset,
 56 |   } = useForm<TransformationFormData>({
 57 |     resolver: zodResolver(transformationSchema),
 58 |     defaultValues: {
 59 |       name: '',
 60 |       title: '',
 61 |       description: '',
 62 |       prompt: '',
 63 |       apply_default: false,
 64 |     },
 65 |   })
 66 | 
 67 |   useEffect(() => {
 68 |     if (!open) {
 69 |       reset({ name: '', title: '', description: '', prompt: '', apply_default: false })
 70 |       return
 71 |     }
 72 | 
 73 |     const source = fetchedTransformation ?? transformation
 74 |     reset({
 75 |       name: source?.name ?? '',
 76 |       title: source?.title ?? '',
 77 |       description: source?.description ?? '',
 78 |       prompt: source?.prompt ?? '',
 79 |       apply_default: source?.apply_default ?? false,
 80 |     })
 81 |   }, [open, transformation, fetchedTransformation, reset])
 82 | 
 83 |   const onSubmit = async (data: TransformationFormData) => {
 84 |     if (transformation) {
 85 |       await updateTransformation.mutateAsync({
 86 |         id: transformation.id,
 87 |         data: {
 88 |           name: data.name,
 89 |           title: data.title || undefined,
 90 |           description: data.description || undefined,
 91 |           prompt: data.prompt,
 92 |           apply_default: Boolean(data.apply_default),
 93 |         },
 94 |       })
 95 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: TRANSFORMATION_QUERY_KEYS.transformation(transformation.id) })
 96 |     } else {
 97 |       await createTransformation.mutateAsync({
 98 |         name: data.name,
 99 |         title: data.title || data.name,
100 |         description: data.description || '',
101 |         prompt: data.prompt,
102 |         apply_default: Boolean(data.apply_default),
103 |       })
104 |     }
105 | 
106 |     reset()
107 |     onOpenChange(false)
108 |   }
109 | 
110 |   const handleClose = () => {
111 |     reset()
112 |     onOpenChange(false)
113 |   }
114 | 
115 |   const isSaving = transformation ? updateTransformation.isPending : createTransformation.isPending
116 | 
117 |   return (
118 |     <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={handleClose}>
119 |       <DialogContent className="sm:max-w-4xl w-full max-h-[90vh] overflow-hidden p-0">
120 |         <DialogTitle className="sr-only">
121 |           {isEditing ? t.common.edit : t.transformations.createNew}
122 |         </DialogTitle>
123 |         <DialogDescription className="sr-only">
124 |            {isEditing ? t.common.editTransformation : t.transformations.createNew}
125 |         </DialogDescription>
126 |         <form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onSubmit)} className="flex h-full flex-col">
127 |           {isEditing && isLoading ? (
128 |             <div className="flex-1 flex items-center justify-center py-10">
129 |               <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{t.common.loading}</span>
130 |             </div>
131 |           ) : (
132 |             <>
133 |               <div className="border-b px-6 py-4 space-y-4">
134 |                 <div>
135 |                   <Label htmlFor={nameId} className="text-sm font-medium">
136 |                     {t.transformations.name}
137 |                   </Label>
138 |                   <Controller
139 |                     control={control}
140 |                     name="name"
141 |                     render={({ field }) => (
142 |                         <Input
143 |                         id={nameId}
144 |                         {...field}
145 |                         placeholder={t.transformations.namePlaceholder}
146 |                         autoComplete="off"
147 |                       />
148 |                     )}
149 |                   />
150 |                   {errors.name && (
151 |                     <p className="text-sm text-red-600 mt-1">{errors.name.message}</p>
152 |                   )}
153 |                 </div>
154 | 
155 |                 <div className="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
156 |                   <div>
157 |                     <Label htmlFor={titleId} className="text-sm font-medium">
158 |                       {t.common.title}
159 |                     </Label>
160 |                     <Controller
161 |                       control={control}
162 |                       name="title"
163 |                       render={({ field }) => (
164 |                         <Input
165 |                            id={titleId}
166 |                            {...field}
167 |                            placeholder={t.transformations.titlePlaceholder}
168 |                            autoComplete="off"
169 |                          />
170 |                       )}
171 |                     />
172 |                   </div>
173 |                   <div className="flex items-center gap-2 pt-6 md:pt-8">
174 |                     <Controller
175 |                       control={control}
176 |                       name="apply_default"
177 |                       render={({ field }) => (
178 |                         <Checkbox
179 |                           id={defaultId}
180 |                           checked={field.value}
181 |                           onCheckedChange={(checked) => field.onChange(Boolean(checked))}
182 |                         />
183 |                       )}
184 |                     />
185 |                      <Label htmlFor={defaultId} className="text-sm">
186 |                        {t.transformations.suggestDefault}
187 |                      </Label>
188 |                   </div>
189 |                 </div>
190 | 
191 |                 <div>
192 |                    <Label htmlFor={descriptionId} className="text-sm font-medium">
193 |                      {t.notebooks.addDescription.replace('...', '')}
194 |                    </Label>
195 |                   <Controller
196 |                     control={control}
197 |                     name="description"
198 |                     render={({ field }) => (
199 |                       <Textarea
200 |                          id={descriptionId}
201 |                          {...field}
202 |                          placeholder={t.transformations.descriptionPlaceholder}
203 |                          rows={2}
204 |                          autoComplete="off"
205 |                       />
206 |                     )}
207 |                   />
208 |                 </div>
209 |               </div>
210 | 
211 |               <div className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto px-6 py-4">
212 |                 <Label htmlFor={promptId} className="text-sm font-medium">{t.transformations.systemPrompt}</Label>
213 |                 <Controller
214 |                   control={control}
215 |                   name="prompt"
216 |                   render={({ field }) => (
217 |                     <MarkdownEditor
218 |                       key={transformation?.id ?? 'new-transformation'}
219 |                       value={field.value}
220 |                       onChange={field.onChange}
221 |                       height={420}
222 |                       placeholder={t.transformations.promptPlaceholder}
223 |                       className="rounded-md border"
224 |                       textareaId={promptId}
225 |                       name={field.name}
226 |                     />
227 |                   )}
228 |                 />
229 |                 {errors.prompt && (
230 |                   <p className="text-sm text-red-600 mt-1">{errors.prompt.message}</p>
231 |                 )}
232 |                  <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground mt-3">
233 |                    {t.transformations.promptHint}
234 |                  </p>
235 |               </div>
236 |             </>
237 |           )}
238 | 
239 |           <div className="border-t px-6 py-4 flex justify-end gap-2">
240 |              <Button type="button" variant="outline" onClick={handleClose}>
241 |                {t.common.cancel}
242 |              </Button>
243 |               <Button type="submit" disabled={isSaving || (isEditing && isLoading)}>
244 |                 {isSaving
245 |                   ? isEditing ? `${t.common.saving}...` : `${t.common.creating}...`
246 |                   : isEditing
247 |                     ? t.common.editTransformation
248 |                     : t.transformations.createNew}
249 |               </Button>
250 |           </div>
251 |         </form>
252 |       </DialogContent>
253 |     </Dialog>
254 |   )
255 | }

  1 | 'use client'

 10 |   DropdownMenuItem,

 15 | import { EmptyState } from '@/components/common/EmptyState'
 16 | import { AddSourceDialog } from '@/components/sources/AddSourceDialog'
 17 | import { AddExistingSourceDialog } from '@/components/sources/AddExistingSourceDialog'
 18 | import { SourceCard } from '@/components/sources/SourceCard'

 20 | import { ConfirmDialog } from '@/components/common/ConfirmDialog'
 21 | import { useModalManager } from '@/lib/hooks/use-modal-manager'
 22 | import { ContextMode } from '../[id]/page'

 24 | import { useNotebookColumnsStore } from '@/lib/stores/notebook-columns-store'
 25 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
 26 | 
 27 | interface SourcesColumnProps {
 28 |   sources?: SourceListResponse[]
 29 |   isLoading: boolean
 30 |   notebookId: string
 31 |   notebookName?: string
 32 |   onRefresh?: () => void
 33 |   contextSelections?: Record<string, ContextMode>
 34 |   onContextModeChange?: (sourceId: string, mode: ContextMode) => void
 35 |   // Pagination props
 36 |   hasNextPage?: boolean
 37 |   isFetchingNextPage?: boolean
 38 |   fetchNextPage?: () => void
 39 | }
 40 | 
 41 | export function SourcesColumn({
 42 |   sources,
 43 |   isLoading,
 44 |   notebookId,
 45 |   onRefresh,
 46 |   contextSelections,
 47 |   onContextModeChange,
 48 |   hasNextPage,
 49 |   isFetchingNextPage,
 50 |   fetchNextPage,
 51 | }: SourcesColumnProps) {
 52 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 53 |   const [dropdownOpen, setDropdownOpen] = useState(false)
 54 |   const [addDialogOpen, setAddDialogOpen] = useState(false)
 55 |   const [addExistingDialogOpen, setAddExistingDialogOpen] = useState(false)
 56 |   const [deleteDialogOpen, setDeleteDialogOpen] = useState(false)
 57 |   const [sourceToDelete, setSourceToDelete] = useState<string | null>(null)
 58 |   const [removeDialogOpen, setRemoveDialogOpen] = useState(false)
 59 |   const [sourceToRemove, setSourceToRemove] = useState<string | null>(null)
 60 | 
 61 |   const { openModal } = useModalManager()
 62 |   const deleteSource = useDeleteSource()
 63 |   const retrySource = useRetrySource()
 64 |   const removeFromNotebook = useRemoveSourceFromNotebook()
 65 | 
 66 |   // Collapsible column state
 67 |   const { sourcesCollapsed, toggleSources } = useNotebookColumnsStore()
 68 |   const collapseButton = useMemo(
 69 |     () => createCollapseButton(toggleSources, t.navigation.sources),
 70 |     [toggleSources, t.navigation.sources]
 71 |   )
 72 | 
 73 |   // Scroll container ref for infinite scroll
 74 |   const scrollContainerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
 75 | 
 76 |   // Handle scroll for infinite loading
 77 |   const handleScroll = useCallback(() => {
 78 |     const container = scrollContainerRef.current
 79 |     if (!container || !hasNextPage || isFetchingNextPage || !fetchNextPage) return
 80 | 
 81 |     const { scrollTop, scrollHeight, clientHeight } = container
 82 |     // Load more when user scrolls within 200px of the bottom
 83 |     if (scrollHeight - scrollTop - clientHeight < 200) {
 84 |       fetchNextPage()
 85 |     }
 86 |   }, [hasNextPage, isFetchingNextPage, fetchNextPage])
 87 | 
 88 |   // Attach scroll listener
 89 |   useEffect(() => {
 90 |     const container = scrollContainerRef.current
 91 |     if (!container) return
 92 | 
 93 |     container.addEventListener('scroll', handleScroll)
 94 |     return () => container.removeEventListener('scroll', handleScroll)
 95 |   }, [handleScroll])
 96 |   
 97 |   const handleDeleteClick = (sourceId: string) => {
 98 |     setSourceToDelete(sourceId)
 99 |     setDeleteDialogOpen(true)
100 |   }
101 | 
102 |   const handleDeleteConfirm = async () => {
103 |     if (!sourceToDelete) return
104 | 
105 |     try {
106 |       await deleteSource.mutateAsync(sourceToDelete)
107 |       setDeleteDialogOpen(false)
108 |       setSourceToDelete(null)
109 |       onRefresh?.()
110 |     } catch (error) {
111 |       console.error('Failed to delete source:', error)
112 |     }
113 |   }
114 | 
115 |   const handleRemoveFromNotebook = (sourceId: string) => {
116 |     setSourceToRemove(sourceId)
117 |     setRemoveDialogOpen(true)
118 |   }
119 | 
120 |   const handleRemoveConfirm = async () => {
121 |     if (!sourceToRemove) return
122 | 
123 |     try {
124 |       await removeFromNotebook.mutateAsync({
125 |         notebookId,
126 |         sourceId: sourceToRemove
127 |       })
128 |       setRemoveDialogOpen(false)
129 |       setSourceToRemove(null)
130 |     } catch (error) {
131 |       console.error('Failed to remove source from notebook:', error)
132 |       // Error toast is handled by the hook
133 |     }
134 |   }
135 | 
136 |   const handleRetry = async (sourceId: string) => {
137 |     try {
138 |       await retrySource.mutateAsync(sourceId)
139 |     } catch (error) {
140 |       console.error('Failed to retry source:', error)
141 |     }
142 |   }
143 | 
144 |   const handleSourceClick = (sourceId: string) => {
145 |     openModal('source', sourceId)
146 |   }
147 | 
148 |   return (
149 |     <>
150 |       <CollapsibleColumn
151 |         isCollapsed={sourcesCollapsed}
152 |         onToggle={toggleSources}
153 |         collapsedIcon={FileText}
154 |         collapsedLabel={t.navigation.sources}
155 |       >
156 |         <Card className="h-full flex flex-col flex-1 overflow-hidden">
157 |           <CardHeader className="pb-3 flex-shrink-0">
158 |             <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
159 |               <CardTitle className="text-lg">{t.navigation.sources}</CardTitle>
160 |               <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
161 |                 <DropdownMenu open={dropdownOpen} onOpenChange={setDropdownOpen}>
162 |                   <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
163 |                     <Button size="sm">
164 |                       <Plus className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
165 |                       {t.sources.addSource}
166 |                       <ChevronDown className="h-4 w-4 ml-2" />
167 |                     </Button>
168 |                   </DropdownMenuTrigger>
169 |                   <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
170 |                     <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => { setDropdownOpen(false); setAddDialogOpen(true); }}>
171 |                       <Plus className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
172 |                       {t.sources.addSource}
173 |                     </DropdownMenuItem>
174 |                     <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => { setDropdownOpen(false); setAddExistingDialogOpen(true); }}>
175 |                       <Link2 className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
176 |                       {t.sources.addExistingTitle}
177 |                     </DropdownMenuItem>
178 |                   </DropdownMenuContent>
179 |                 </DropdownMenu>
180 |                 {collapseButton}
181 |               </div>
182 |             </div>
183 |           </CardHeader>
184 | 
185 |           <CardContent ref={scrollContainerRef} className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto min-h-0">
186 |             {isLoading ? (
187 |               <div className="flex items-center justify-center py-8">
188 |                 <LoadingSpinner />
189 |               </div>
190 |             ) : !sources || sources.length === 0 ? (
191 |               <EmptyState
192 |                 icon={FileText}
193 |                 title={t.sources.noSourcesYet}
194 |                 description={t.sources.createFirstSource}
195 |               />
196 |             ) : (
197 |               <div className="space-y-3">
198 |                 {sources.map((source) => (
199 |                   <SourceCard
200 |                     key={source.id}
201 |                     source={source}
202 |                     onClick={handleSourceClick}
203 |                     onDelete={handleDeleteClick}
204 |                     onRetry={handleRetry}
205 |                     onRemoveFromNotebook={handleRemoveFromNotebook}
206 |                     onRefresh={onRefresh}
207 |                     showRemoveFromNotebook={true}
208 |                     contextMode={contextSelections?.[source.id]}
209 |                     onContextModeChange={onContextModeChange
210 |                       ? (mode) => onContextModeChange(source.id, mode)
211 |                       : undefined
212 |                     }
213 |                   />
214 |                 ))}
215 |                 {/* Loading indicator for infinite scroll */}
216 |                 {isFetchingNextPage && (
217 |                   <div className="flex items-center justify-center py-4">
218 |                     <Loader2 className="h-5 w-5 animate-spin text-muted-foreground" />
219 |                   </div>
220 |                 )}
221 |               </div>
222 |             )}
223 |           </CardContent>
224 |         </Card>
225 |       </CollapsibleColumn>
226 | 
227 |       <AddSourceDialog
228 |         open={addDialogOpen}
229 |         onOpenChange={setAddDialogOpen}
230 |         defaultNotebookId={notebookId}
231 |       />
232 | 
233 |       <AddExistingSourceDialog
234 |         open={addExistingDialogOpen}
235 |         onOpenChange={setAddExistingDialogOpen}
236 |         notebookId={notebookId}
237 |         onSuccess={onRefresh}
238 |       />
239 | 
240 |       <ConfirmDialog
241 |         open={deleteDialogOpen}
242 |         onOpenChange={setDeleteDialogOpen}
243 |         title={t.sources.delete}
244 |         description={t.sources.deleteConfirm}
245 |         confirmText={t.common.delete}
246 |         onConfirm={handleDeleteConfirm}
247 |         isLoading={deleteSource.isPending}
248 |         confirmVariant="destructive"
249 |       />
250 | 
251 |       <ConfirmDialog
252 |         open={removeDialogOpen}
253 |         onOpenChange={setRemoveDialogOpen}
254 |         title={t.sources.removeFromNotebook}
255 |         description={t.sources.removeConfirm}
256 |         confirmText={t.common.remove}
257 |         onConfirm={handleRemoveConfirm}
258 |         isLoading={removeFromNotebook.isPending}
259 |         confirmVariant="default"
260 |       />
261 |     </>
262 |   )
263 | }

106 |             transformation_id=execute_request.transformation_id,
107 |             model_id=execute_request.model_id,
108 |         )

110 |     except HTTPException:

/docs/2-CORE-CONCEPTS/notebooks-sources-notes.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Notebooks, Sources, and Notes - The Container Model
  2 | 
  3 | Open Notebook organizes research in three connected layers. Understanding this hierarchy is key to using the system effectively.
  4 | 
  5 | ## The Three-Layer Structure
  6 | 
  7 | ```
  8 | ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
  9 | │         NOTEBOOK (The Container)    │
 10 | │     "My AI Safety Research 2026"   │
 11 | ├─────────────────────────────────────┤
 12 | │                                     │
 13 | │  SOURCES (The Raw Materials)        │
 14 | │  ├─ safety_paper.pdf                │
 15 | │  ├─ alignment_video.mp4             │
 16 | │  └─ prompt_injection_article.html   │
 17 | │                                     │
 18 | │  NOTES (The Processed Insights)     │
 19 | │  ├─ AI Summary (auto-generated)     │
 20 | │  ├─ Key Concepts (transformation)   │
 21 | │  ├─ My Research Notes (manual)      │
 22 | │  └─ Chat Insights (from conversation)
 23 | │                                     │
 24 | └─────────────────────────────────────┘
 25 | ```
 26 | 
 27 | ---
 28 | 
 29 | ## 1. NOTEBOOKS - The Research Container
 30 | 
 31 | ### What Is a Notebook?
 32 | 
 33 | A **notebook** is a *scoped container* for a research project or topic. It's your research workspace.
 34 | 
 35 | Think of it like a physical notebook: everything inside is about the same topic, shares the same context, and builds toward the same goals.
 36 | 
 37 | ### What Goes In?
 38 | 
 39 | - **A description** — "This notebook collects research on X topic"
 40 | - **Sources** — The raw materials you add
 41 | - **Notes** — Your insights and outputs
 42 | - **Conversation history** — Your chats and questions
 43 | 
 44 | ### Why This Matters
 45 | 
 46 | **Isolation**: Each notebook is completely separate. Sources in Notebook A never appear in Notebook B. This lets you:
 47 | - Keep different research topics completely isolated
 48 | - Reuse source names across notebooks without conflicts
 49 | - Control which AI context applies to which research
 50 | 
 51 | **Shared Context**: All sources and notes in a notebook inherit the notebook's context. If your notebook is titled "AI Safety 2026" with description "Focusing on alignment and interpretability," that context applies to all AI interactions within that notebook.
 52 | 
 53 | **Parallel Projects**: You can have 10 notebooks running simultaneously. Each one is its own isolated research environment.
 54 | 
 55 | ### Example
 56 | 
 57 | ```
 58 | Notebook: "Customer Research - Product Launch"
 59 | Description: "User interviews and feedback for Q1 2026 launch"
 60 | 
 61 | → All sources added to this notebook are about customer feedback
 62 | → All notes generated are in that context
 63 | → When you chat, the AI knows you're analyzing product launch feedback
 64 | → Different from your "Market Analysis - Competitors" notebook
 65 | ```
 66 | 
 67 | ---
 68 | 
 69 | ## 2. SOURCES - The Raw Materials
 70 | 
 71 | ### What Is a Source?
 72 | 
 73 | A **source** is a *single piece of input material* — the raw content you bring in. Sources never change; they're just processed and indexed.
 74 | 
 75 | ### What Can Be a Source?
 76 | 
 77 | - **PDFs** — Research papers, reports, documents
 78 | - **Web links** — Articles, blog posts, web pages
 79 | - **Audio files** — Podcasts, interviews, lectures
 80 | - **Video files** — Tutorials, presentations, recordings
 81 | - **Plain text** — Notes, transcripts, passages
 82 | - **Uploaded text** — Paste content directly
 83 | 
 84 | ### What Happens When You Add a Source?
 85 | 
 86 | ```
 87 | 1. EXTRACTION
 88 |    File/URL → Extract text and metadata
 89 |    (OCR for PDFs, web scraping for URLs, speech-to-text for audio)
 90 | 
 91 | 2. CHUNKING
 92 |    Long text → Break into searchable chunks
 93 |    (Prevents "too much context" in single query)
 94 | 
 95 | 3. EMBEDDING
 96 |    Each chunk → Generate semantic vector
 97 |    (Allows AI to find conceptually similar content)
 98 | 
 99 | 4. STORAGE
100 |    Chunks + vectors → Store in database
101 |    (Ready for search and retrieval)
102 | ```
103 | 
104 | ### Key Properties
105 | 
106 | **Immutable**: Once added, the source doesn't change. If you need a new version, add it as a new source.
107 | 
108 | **Indexed**: Sources are automatically indexed for search (both text and semantic).
109 | 
110 | **Scoped**: A source belongs to exactly one notebook.
111 | 
112 | **Referenceable**: Other sources and notes can reference this source by citation.
113 | 
114 | ### Example
115 | 
116 | ```
117 | Source: "openai_charter.pdf"
118 | Type: PDF document
119 | 
120 | What happens:
121 | → PDF is uploaded
122 | → Text is extracted (including images)
123 | → Text is split into 50 chunks (paragraphs, sections)
124 | → Each chunk gets an embedding vector
125 | → Now searchable by: "OpenAI's approach to safety"
126 | ```
127 | 
128 | ---
129 | 
130 | ## 3. NOTES - The Processed Insights
131 | 
132 | ### What Is a Note?
133 | 
134 | A **note** is a *processed output* — something you created or AI created based on your sources. Notes are the "results" of your research work.
135 | 
136 | ### Types of Notes
137 | 
138 | #### Manual Notes
139 | You write them yourself. They're your original thinking, capturing:
140 | - What you learned from sources
141 | - Your analysis and interpretations
142 | - Your next steps and questions
143 | 
144 | #### AI-Generated Notes
145 | Created by applying AI processing to sources:
146 | - **Transformations** — Structured extraction (main points, key concepts, methodology)
147 | - **Chat Responses** — Answers you saved from conversations
148 | - **Ask Results** — Comprehensive answers saved to your notebook
149 | 
150 | #### Captured Insights
151 | Notes you explicitly saved from interactions:
152 | - "Save this response as a note"
153 | - "Save this transformation result"
154 | - Convert any AI output into a permanent note
155 | 
156 | ### What Can Notes Contain?
157 | 
158 | - **Text** — Your writing or AI-generated content
159 | - **Citations** — References to specific sources
160 | - **Metadata** — When created, how created (manual/AI), which sources influenced it
161 | - **Tags** — Your categorization (optional but useful)
162 | 
163 | ### Why Notes Matter
164 | 
165 | **Knowledge Accumulation**: Notes become your actual knowledge base. They're what you take away from the research.
166 | 
167 | **Searchable**: Notes are searchable along with sources. "Find everything about X" includes your notes, not just sources.
168 | 
169 | **Citable**: Notes can cite sources, creating an audit trail of where insights came from.
170 | 
171 | **Shareable**: Notes are your outputs. You can share them, publish them, or build on them in other projects.
172 | 
173 | ---
174 | 
175 | ## How They Connect: The Data Flow
176 | 
177 | ```
178 | YOU
179 |  │
180 |  ├─→ Create Notebook ("AI Research")
181 |  │
182 |  ├─→ Add Sources (papers, articles, videos)
183 |  │    └─→ System: Extract, embed, index
184 |  │
185 |  ├─→ Search Sources (text or semantic)
186 |  │    └─→ System: Find relevant chunks
187 |  │
188 |  ├─→ Apply Transformations (extract insights)
189 |  │    └─→ Creates Notes
190 |  │
191 |  ├─→ Chat with Sources (explore with context control)
192 |  │    ├─→ Can save responses as Notes
193 |  │    └─→ Notes include citations
194 |  │
195 |  ├─→ Ask Questions (automated comprehensive search)
196 |  │    ├─→ Can save results as Notes
197 |  │    └─→ Notes include citations
198 |  │
199 |  └─→ Generate Podcast (transform notebook into audio)
200 |      └─→ Uses all sources + notes for content
201 | ```
202 | 
203 | ---
204 | 
205 | ## Key Design Decisions
206 | 
207 | ### 1. One Notebook Per Source
208 | 
209 | Each source belongs to exactly one notebook. This creates clear boundaries:
210 | - No ambiguity about which research project a source is in
211 | - Easy to isolate or export a complete project
212 | - Clean permissions model (if someone gets access to notebook, they get access to all its sources)
213 | 
214 | ### 2. Immutable Sources, Mutable Notes
215 | 
216 | Sources never change (once added, always the same). But notes can be edited or deleted. Why?
217 | - Sources are evidence → evidence shouldn't be altered
218 | - Notes are your thinking → thinking evolves as you learn
219 | 
220 | ### 3. Explicit Context Control
221 | 
222 | Sources don't automatically go to AI. You decide which sources are "in context" for each interaction:
223 | - Chat: You manually select which sources to include
224 | - Ask: System automatically figures out which sources to search
225 | - Transformations: You choose which sources to transform
226 | 
227 | This is different from systems that always send everything to AI.
228 | 
229 | ---
230 | 
231 | ## Mental Models Explained
232 | 
233 | ### Notebook as Boundaries
234 | Think of a notebook like a Git repository:
235 | - Everything in it is about the same topic
236 | - You can clone/fork it (copy to new project)
237 | - It has clear entry/exit points
238 | - You know exactly what's included
239 | 
240 | ### Sources as Evidence
241 | Think of sources like exhibits in a legal case:
242 | - Once filed, they don't change
243 | - They can be cited and referenced
244 | - They're the ground truth for what you're basing claims on
245 | - Multiple sources can be cross-referenced
246 | 
247 | ### Notes as Synthesis
248 | Think of notes like your case brief:
249 | - You write them based on evidence
250 | - They're your interpretation
251 | - You can cite which evidence supports each claim
252 | - They're what you actually share or act on
253 | 
254 | ---
255 | 
256 | ## Common Questions
257 | 
258 | ### Can I move a source to a different notebook?
259 | Not directly. Each source is tied to one notebook. If you want it in multiple notebooks, add it again (uploads are fast if it's already processed).
260 | 
261 | ### Can a note reference sources from a different notebook?
262 | No. Notes stay within their notebook and reference sources within that notebook. This keeps boundaries clean.
263 | 
264 | ### What if I want to group sources within a notebook?
265 | Use tags. You can tag sources ("primary research," "background," "methodology") and filter by tags.
266 | 
267 | ### Can I merge two notebooks?
268 | Not built-in, but you can manually copy sources from one notebook to another by re-uploading them.
269 | 
270 | ---
271 | 
272 | ## Summary
273 | 
274 | | Concept | Purpose | Lifecycle | Scope |
275 | |---------|---------|-----------|-------|
276 | | **Notebook** | Container + context | Create once, configure | All its sources + notes |
277 | | **Source** | Raw material | Add → Process → Store | One notebook |
278 | | **Note** | Processed output | Create/capture → Edit → Share | One notebook |
279 | 
280 | This three-layer model gives you:
281 | - **Clear organization** (everything scoped to projects)
282 | - **Privacy control** (isolated notebooks)
283 | - **Audit trails** (notes cite sources)
284 | - **Flexibility** (notes can be manual or AI-generated)
285 |
