/docs/7-DEVELOPMENT/development-setup.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Local Development Setup
  2 | 
  3 | This guide walks you through setting up Open Notebook for local development. Follow these steps to get the full stack running on your machine.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Prerequisites
  6 | 
  7 | Before you start, ensure you have the following installed:
  8 | 
  9 | - **Python 3.11+** - Check with: `python --version`
 10 | - **uv** (recommended) or **pip** - Install from: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv
 11 | - **SurrealDB** - Via Docker or binary (see below)
 12 | - **Docker** (optional) - For containerized database
 13 | - **Node.js 18+** (optional) - For frontend development
 14 | - **Git** - For version control
 15 | 
 16 | ## Step 1: Clone and Initial Setup
 17 | 
 18 | ```bash
 19 | # Clone the repository
 20 | git clone https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook.git
 21 | cd open-notebook
 22 | 
 23 | # Add upstream remote for keeping your fork updated
 24 | git remote add upstream https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook.git
 25 | ```
 26 | 
 27 | ## Step 2: Install Python Dependencies
 28 | 
 29 | ```bash
 30 | # Using uv (recommended)
 31 | uv sync
 32 | 
 33 | # Or using pip
 34 | pip install -e .
 35 | ```
 36 | 
 37 | ## Step 3: Environment Variables
 38 | 
 39 | Create a `.env` file in the project root with your configuration:
 40 | 
 41 | ```bash
 42 | # Copy from example
 43 | cp .env.example .env
 44 | ```
 45 | 
 46 | Edit `.env` with your settings:
 47 | 
 48 | ```bash
 49 | # Database
 50 | SURREAL_URL=ws://localhost:8000/rpc
 51 | SURREAL_USER=root
 52 | SURREAL_PASSWORD=password
 53 | SURREAL_NAMESPACE=open_notebook
 54 | SURREAL_DATABASE=development
 55 | 
 56 | # AI Providers (add your API keys)
 57 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
 58 | ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
 59 | GOOGLE_API_KEY=AI...
 60 | GROQ_API_KEY=gsk-...
 61 | 
 62 | # Application
 63 | APP_PASSWORD=  # Optional password protection
 64 | DEBUG=true
 65 | LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG
 66 | ```
 67 | 
 68 | ### AI Provider Keys
 69 | 
 70 | You'll need at least one AI provider. Popular options:
 71 | 
 72 | - **OpenAI** - https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
 73 | - **Anthropic (Claude)** - https://console.anthropic.com/
 74 | - **Google** - https://ai.google.dev/
 75 | - **Groq** - https://console.groq.com/
 76 | 
 77 | For local development, you can also use:
 78 | - **Ollama** - Run locally without API keys (see "Local Ollama" below)
 79 | 
 80 | ## Step 4: Start SurrealDB
 81 | 
 82 | ### Option A: Using Docker (Recommended)
 83 | 
 84 | ```bash
 85 | # Start SurrealDB in memory
 86 | docker run -d --name surrealdb -p 8000:8000 \
 87 |   surrealdb/surrealdb:v2 start \
 88 |   --user root --pass password \
 89 |   --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 memory
 90 | 
 91 | # Or with persistent storage
 92 | docker run -d --name surrealdb -p 8000:8000 \
 93 |   -v surrealdb_data:/data \
 94 |   surrealdb/surrealdb:v2 start \
 95 |   --user root --pass password \
 96 |   --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 file:/data/surreal.db
 97 | ```
 98 | 
 99 | ### Option B: Using Make
100 | 
101 | ```bash
102 | make database
103 | ```
104 | 
105 | ### Option C: Using Docker Compose
106 | 
107 | ```bash
108 | docker compose up -d surrealdb
109 | ```
110 | 
111 | ### Verify SurrealDB is Running
112 | 
113 | ```bash
114 | # Should show server information
115 | curl http://localhost:8000/
116 | ```
117 | 
118 | ## Step 5: Run Database Migrations
119 | 
120 | Database migrations run automatically when you start the API. The first startup will apply any pending migrations.
121 | 
122 | To verify migrations manually:
123 | 
124 | ```bash
125 | # API will run migrations on startup
126 | uv run python -m api.main
127 | ```
128 | 
129 | Check the logs - you should see messages like:
130 | ```
131 | Running migration 001_initial_schema
132 | Running migration 002_add_vectors
133 | ...
134 | Migrations completed successfully
135 | ```
136 | 
137 | ## Step 6: Start the API Server
138 | 
139 | In a new terminal window:
140 | 
141 | ```bash
142 | # Terminal 2: Start API (port 5055)
143 | uv run --env-file .env uvicorn api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5055
144 | 
145 | # Or using the shortcut
146 | make api
147 | ```
148 | 
149 | You should see:
150 | ```
151 | INFO:     Application startup complete
152 | INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:5055
153 | ```
154 | 
155 | ### Verify API is Running
156 | 
157 | ```bash
158 | # Check health endpoint
159 | curl http://localhost:5055/health
160 | 
161 | # View API documentation
162 | open http://localhost:5055/docs
163 | ```
164 | 
165 | ## Step 7: Start the Frontend (Optional)
166 | 
167 | If you want to work on the frontend, start Next.js in another terminal:
168 | 
169 | ```bash
170 | # Terminal 3: Start Next.js frontend (port 3000)
171 | cd frontend
172 | npm install  # First time only
173 | npm run dev
174 | ```
175 | 
176 | You should see:
177 | ```
178 | > next dev
179 |   ▲ Next.js 16.x
180 |   - Local:        http://localhost:3000
181 | ```
182 | 
183 | ### Access the Frontend
184 | 
185 | Open your browser to: http://localhost:3000
186 | 
187 | ## Verification Checklist
188 | 
189 | After setup, verify everything is working:
190 | 
191 | - [ ] **SurrealDB**: `curl http://localhost:8000/` returns content
192 | - [ ] **API**: `curl http://localhost:5055/health` returns `{"status": "ok"}`
193 | - [ ] **API Docs**: `open http://localhost:5055/docs` works
194 | - [ ] **Database**: API logs show migrations completing
195 | - [ ] **Frontend** (optional): `http://localhost:3000` loads
196 | 
197 | ## Starting Services Together
198 | 
199 | ### Quick Start All Services
200 | 
201 | ```bash
202 | make start-all
203 | ```
204 | 
205 | This starts SurrealDB, API, and frontend in one command.
206 | 
207 | ### Individual Terminals (Recommended for Development)
208 | 
209 | **Terminal 1 - Database:**
210 | ```bash
211 | make database
212 | ```
213 | 
214 | **Terminal 2 - API:**
215 | ```bash
216 | make api
217 | ```
218 | 
219 | **Terminal 3 - Frontend:**
220 | ```bash
221 | cd frontend && npm run dev
222 | ```
223 | 
224 | ## Development Tools Setup
225 | 
226 | ### Pre-commit Hooks (Optional but Recommended)
227 | 
228 | Install git hooks to automatically check code quality:
229 | 
230 | ```bash
231 | uv run pre-commit install
232 | ```
233 | 
234 | Now your commits will be checked before they're made.
235 | 
236 | ### Code Quality Commands
237 | 
238 | ```bash
239 | # Lint Python code (auto-fix)
240 | make ruff
241 | # or: ruff check . --fix
242 | 
243 | # Type check Python code
244 | make lint
245 | # or: uv run python -m mypy .
246 | 
247 | # Run tests
248 | uv run pytest
249 | 
250 | # Run tests with coverage
251 | uv run pytest --cov=open_notebook
252 | ```
253 | 
254 | ## Common Development Tasks
255 | 
256 | ### Running Tests
257 | 
258 | ```bash
259 | # Run all tests
260 | uv run pytest
261 | 
262 | # Run specific test file
263 | uv run pytest tests/test_notebooks.py
264 | 
265 | # Run with coverage report
266 | uv run pytest --cov=open_notebook --cov-report=html
267 | ```
268 | 
269 | ### Creating a Feature Branch
270 | 
271 | ```bash
272 | # Create and switch to new branch
273 | git checkout -b feature/my-feature
274 | 
275 | # Make changes, then commit
276 | git add .
277 | git commit -m "feat: add my feature"
278 | 
279 | # Push to your fork
280 | git push origin feature/my-feature
281 | ```
282 | 
283 | ### Updating from Upstream
284 | 
285 | ```bash
286 | # Fetch latest changes
287 | git fetch upstream
288 | 
289 | # Rebase your branch
290 | git rebase upstream/main
291 | 
292 | # Push updated branch
293 | git push origin feature/my-feature -f
294 | ```
295 | 
296 | ## Troubleshooting
297 | 
298 | ### "Connection refused" on SurrealDB
299 | 
300 | **Problem**: API can't connect to SurrealDB
301 | 
302 | **Solutions**:
303 | 1. Check if SurrealDB is running: `docker ps | grep surrealdb`
304 | 2. Verify URL in `.env`: Should be `ws://localhost:8000/rpc`
305 | 3. Restart SurrealDB: `docker stop surrealdb && docker rm surrealdb`
306 | 4. Then restart with: `docker run -d --name surrealdb -p 8000:8000 surrealdb/surrealdb:v2 start --user root --pass password --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 memory`
307 | 
308 | ### "Address already in use"
309 | 
310 | **Problem**: Port 5055 or 3000 is already in use
311 | 
312 | **Solutions**:
313 | ```bash
314 | # Find process using port
315 | lsof -i :5055  # Check port 5055
316 | 
317 | # Kill process (macOS/Linux)
318 | kill -9 <PID>
319 | 
320 | # Or use different port
321 | uvicorn api.main:app --port 5056
322 | ```
323 | 
324 | ### Module not found errors
325 | 
326 | **Problem**: Import errors when running API
327 | 
328 | **Solutions**:
329 | ```bash
330 | # Reinstall dependencies
331 | uv sync
332 | 
333 | # Or with pip
334 | pip install -e .
335 | ```
336 | 
337 | ### Database migration failures
338 | 
339 | **Problem**: API fails to start with migration errors
340 | 
341 | **Solutions**:
342 | 1. Check SurrealDB is running: `curl http://localhost:8000/`
343 | 2. Check credentials in `.env` match your SurrealDB setup
344 | 3. Check logs for specific migration error: `make api 2>&1 | grep -i migration`
345 | 4. Verify database exists: Check SurrealDB console at http://localhost:8000/
346 | 
347 | ### Migrations not applying
348 | 
349 | **Problem**: Database schema seems outdated
350 | 
351 | **Solutions**:
352 | 1. Restart API - migrations run on startup: `make api`
353 | 2. Check logs show "Migrations completed successfully"
354 | 3. Verify `/migrations/` folder exists and has files
355 | 4. Check SurrealDB is writable and not in read-only mode
356 | 
357 | ## Optional: Local Ollama Setup
358 | 
359 | For testing with local AI models:
360 | 
361 | ```bash
362 | # Install Ollama from https://ollama.ai
363 | 
364 | # Pull a model (e.g., Mistral 7B)
365 | ollama pull mistral
366 | 
367 | # Add to .env
368 | OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434
369 | ```
370 | 
371 | Then in your code, you can use Ollama through the Esperanto library.
372 | 
373 | ## Optional: Docker Development Environment
374 | 
375 | Run entire stack in Docker:
376 | 
377 | ```bash
378 | # Start all services
379 | docker compose --profile multi up
380 | 
381 | # Logs
382 | docker compose logs -f
383 | 
384 | # Stop services
385 | docker compose down
386 | ```
387 | 
388 | ## Next Steps
389 | 
390 | After setup is complete:
391 | 
392 | 1. **Read the Contributing Guide** - [contributing.md](contributing.md)
393 | 2. **Explore the Architecture** - Check the documentation
394 | 3. **Find an Issue** - Look for "good first issue" on GitHub
395 | 4. **Set Up Pre-commit** - Install git hooks for code quality
396 | 5. **Join Discord** - https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w
397 | 
398 | ## Getting Help
399 | 
400 | If you get stuck:
401 | 
402 | - **Discord**: [Join our server](https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w) for real-time help
403 | - **GitHub Issues**: Check existing issues for similar problems
404 | - **GitHub Discussions**: Ask questions in discussions
405 | - **Documentation**: See [code-standards.md](code-standards.md) and [testing.md](testing.md)
406 | 
407 | ---
408 | 
409 | **Ready to contribute?** Go to [contributing.md](contributing.md) for the contribution workflow.
410 |

Your focus is to uncover the core contributions, practical applications, methodological strengths or weaknesses, and any surprising findings. You are especially attuned to the clarity of arguments, the relevance to existing literature, and potential impacts on both the specific field and broader contexts.
 27 | 
 28 | # STEPS
 29 | 
 30 | 1. **READ AND UNDERSTAND THE PAPER**: Thoroughly read the paper, identifying its main focus, arguments, methods, results, and conclusions.

 33 |    - **Purpose**: What is the main goal or research question?
 34 |    - **Contribution**: What new knowledge or innovation does this paper bring to the field?
 35 |    - **Methods**: What methods are used, and are they novel or particularly effective?
 36 |    - **Key Findings**: What are the most critical results, and why do they matter?
 37 |    - **Limitations**: Are there any notable limitations or areas for further research?

 45 |

 47 |   - **PURPOSE**: A concise summary of the main research question or goal (1-2 sentences).
 48 |   - **CONTRIBUTION**: A bullet list of 2-3 points that describe what the paper adds to the field.
 49 |   - **KEY FINDINGS**: A bullet list of 2-3 points summarizing the critical outcomes of the study.
 50 |   - **IMPLICATIONS**: A bullet list of 2-3 points discussing the significance or potential impact of the findings on the field or broader context.
 51 |   - **LIMITATIONS**: A bullet list of 1-2 points identifying notable limitations or areas for future work.
 52 | 
 53 | - **Bullet Points** should be between 15-20 words.
 54 | - Avoid starting each bullet point with the same word to maintain variety.
 55 | - Use clear and concise language that conveys the key ideas effectively.
 56 | - Do not include warnings, disclaimers, or personal opinions.
 57 | - Output only the requested sections with their respective labels.",

 61 |        name: "Key Insights",

 63 |        description: "Extracts important insights and actionable items", 
 64 |        prompt:"# IDENTITY and PURPOSE
 65 | 
 66 | You extract surprising, powerful, and interesting insights from text content. You are interested in insights related to the purpose and meaning of life, human flourishing, the role of technology in the future of humanity, artificial intelligence and its affect on humans, memes, learning, reading, books, continuous improvement, and similar topics.
 67 | You create 15 word bullet points that capture the most important insights from the input.
 68 | Take a step back and think step-by-step about how to achieve the best possible results by following the steps below.
 69 | 
 70 | # STEPS

 72 | - Extract 20 to 50 of the most surprising, insightful, and/or interesting ideas from the input in a section called IDEAS, and write them on a virtual whiteboard in your mind using 15 word bullets. If there are less than 50 then collect all of them. Make sure you extract at least 20.
 73 | 
 74 | - From those IDEAS, extract the most powerful and insightful of them and write them in a section called INSIGHTS. Make sure you extract at least 10 and up to 25.
 75 | 
 76 | # OUTPUT INSTRUCTIONS
 77 | 
 78 | - INSIGHTS are essentially higher-level IDEAS that are more abstracted and wise.
 79 | - Output the INSIGHTS section only.
 80 | - Each bullet should be about 15 words in length.
 81 | - Do not give warnings or notes; only output the requested sections.
 82 | - You use bulleted lists for output, not numbered lists.
 83 | - Do not start items with the same opening words.
 84 | - Ensure you follow ALL these instructions when creating your output.
 85 | ",

 88 | { 
 89 |        name: "Dense Summary",
 90 |        title: "Dense Summary", 
 91 |        description: "Creates a rich, deep summary of the content", 
 92 |        prompt:"# MISSION
 93 | You are a Sparse Priming Representation (SPR) writer. An SPR is a particular kind of use of language for advanced NLP, NLU, and NLG tasks, particularly useful for the latest generation of Large Language Models (LLMs). You will be given information by the USER which you are to render as an SPR.
 94 | 
 95 | # THEORY
 96 | LLMs are a kind of deep neural network. They have been demonstrated to embed knowledge, abilities, and concepts, ranging from reasoning to planning, and even to theory of mind. These are called latent abilities and latent content, collectively referred to as latent space. The latent space of an LLM can be activated with the correct series of words as inputs, which will create a useful internal state of the neural network. This is not unlike how the right shorthand cues can prime a human mind to think in a certain way. Like human minds, LLMs are associative, meaning you only need to use the correct associations to 'prime' another model to think in the same way.
 97 | 
 98 | # METHODOLOGY
 99 | Render the input as a distilled list of succinct statements, assertions, associations, concepts, analogies, and metaphors. The idea is to capture as much, conceptually, as possible but with as few words as possible. Write it in a way that makes sense to you, as the future audience will be another language model, not a human. Use complete sentences.
100 | ",

102 |    },
103 | {

106 |        description: "Generates reflection questions from the document to help explore it further", 
107 |        prompt:"# IDENTITY and PURPOSE
108 | 
109 | You extract deep, thought-provoking, and meaningful reflections from text content. You are especially focused on themes related to the human experience, such as the purpose of life, personal growth, the intersection of technology and humanity, artificial intelligence's societal impact, human potential, collective evolution, and transformative learning. Your reflections aim to provoke new ways of thinking, challenge assumptions, and provide a thoughtful synthesis of the content.
110 | 
111 | # STEPS
112 | 
113 | - Extract 3 to 5 of the most profound, thought-provoking, and/or meaningful ideas from the input in a section called REFLECTIONS.
114 | - Each reflection should aim to explore underlying implications, connections to broader human experiences, or highlight a transformative perspective.
115 | - Take a step back and consider the deeper significance or questions that arise from the content.
116 | 
117 | # OUTPUT INSTRUCTIONS
118 | 
119 | - The output section should be labeled as REFLECTIONS.
120 | - Each bullet point should be between 20-25 words.
121 | - Avoid repetition in the phrasing and ensure variety in sentence structure.
122 | - The reflections should encourage deeper inquiry and provide a synthesis that transcends surface-level observations.
123 | - Use bullet points, not numbered lists.
124 | - Every bullet should be formatted as a question that elicits contemplation or a statement that offers a profound insight.
125 | - Do not give warnings or notes; only output the requested section.", 
126 |        apply_default: False 
127 |    },
128 | { 
129 |        name: "Table of Contents",
130 |        title: "Table of Contents", 
131 |        description: "Describes the different topics of the document", 
132 |        prompt:"# SYSTEM ROLE
133 | You are a content analysis assistant that reads through documents and provides a Table of Contents (ToC) to help users identify what the document covers more easily.
134 | Your ToC should capture all major topics and transitions in the content and should mention them in the order theh appear. 
135 | 
136 | # TASK
137 | Analyze the provided content and create a Table of Contents:
138 | - Captures the core topics included in the text
139 | - Gives a small description of what is covered", 
140 |        apply_default: False 
141 |    },
142 | { 
143 |        name: "Simple Summary",
144 |        title: "Simple Summary", 
145 |        description: "Generates a small summary of the content", 
146 |        prompt:"# SYSTEM ROLE
147 | You are a content summarization assistant that creates dense, information-rich summaries optimized for machine understanding. Your summaries should capture key concepts with minimal words while maintaining complete, clear sentences.
148 | 
149 | # TASK
150 | Analyze the provided content and create a summary that:
151 | - Captures the core concepts and key information
152 | - Uses clear, direct language
153 | - Maintains context from any previous summaries", 
154 |        apply_default: False 
155 |    },
156 | ];
157 | 
158 | -- Sets the default transformation instructions prompt
159 | UPSERT open_notebook:default_prompts 
160 |     CONTENT {transformation_instructions: "# INSTRUCTIONS
161 | 
162 |         You are my learning assistant and you help me process and transform content so that I can extract insights from them.
163 | 
164 |         # IMPORTANT
165 |         - You are working on my editorial projects. The text below is my own. Do not give me any warnings about copyright or plagiarism.
166 |         - Output ONLY the requested content, without acknowledgements of the task and additional chatting. Don't start with \"Sure, I can help you with that.\" or \"Here is the information you requested:\". Just provide the content.
167 |         - Do not stop in the middle of the generation to ask me questions. Execute my request completely. 
168 |         "};
169 |

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Transformations - Batch Processing Your Sources
  2 | 
  3 | Transformations apply the same analysis to multiple sources at once. Instead of asking the same question repeatedly, define a template and run it across your content.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## When to Use Transformations
  8 | 
  9 | | Use Transformations When | Use Chat Instead When |
 10 | |-------------------------|----------------------|
 11 | | Same analysis on many sources | One-off questions |
 12 | | Consistent output format needed | Exploratory conversation |
 13 | | Batch processing | Follow-up questions needed |
 14 | | Creating structured notes | Context changes between questions |
 15 | 
 16 | **Example**: You have 10 papers and want a summary of each. Transformation does it in one operation.
 17 | 
 18 | ---
 19 | 
 20 | ## Quick Start: Your First Transformation
 21 | 
 22 | ```
 23 | 1. Go to your notebook
 24 | 2. Click "Transformations" in navigation
 25 | 3. Select a built-in template (e.g., "Summary")
 26 | 4. Select sources to transform
 27 | 5. Click "Apply"
 28 | 6. Wait for processing
 29 | 7. New notes appear automatically
 30 | ```
 31 | 
 32 | ---
 33 | 
 34 | ## Built-in Transformations
 35 | 
 36 | Open Notebook includes ready-to-use templates:
 37 | 
 38 | ### Summary
 39 | 
 40 | ```
 41 | What it does: Creates a 200-300 word overview
 42 | Output: Key points, main arguments, conclusions
 43 | Best for: Quick reference, getting the gist
 44 | ```
 45 | 
 46 | ### Key Concepts
 47 | 
 48 | ```
 49 | What it does: Extracts main ideas and terminology
 50 | Output: List of concepts with explanations
 51 | Best for: Learning new topics, building vocabulary
 52 | ```
 53 | 
 54 | ### Methodology
 55 | 
 56 | ```
 57 | What it does: Extracts research approach
 58 | Output: How the study was conducted
 59 | Best for: Academic papers, research review
 60 | ```
 61 | 
 62 | ### Takeaways
 63 | 
 64 | ```
 65 | What it does: Extracts actionable insights
 66 | Output: What you should do with this information
 67 | Best for: Business documents, practical guides
 68 | ```
 69 | 
 70 | ### Questions
 71 | 
 72 | ```
 73 | What it does: Generates questions the source raises
 74 | Output: Open questions, gaps, follow-up research
 75 | Best for: Literature review, research planning
 76 | ```
 77 | 
 78 | ---
 79 | 
 80 | ## Creating Custom Transformations
 81 | 
 82 | ### Step-by-Step
 83 | 
 84 | ```
 85 | 1. Go to "Transformations" page
 86 | 2. Click "Create New"
 87 | 3. Enter a name: "Academic Paper Analysis"
 88 | 4. Write your prompt template:
 89 | 
 90 |    "Analyze this academic paper and extract:
 91 | 
 92 |    1. **Research Question**: What problem does this address?
 93 |    2. **Hypothesis**: What did they predict?
 94 |    3. **Methodology**: How did they test it?
 95 |    4. **Key Findings**: What did they discover? (numbered list)
 96 |    5. **Limitations**: What caveats do the authors mention?
 97 |    6. **Future Work**: What do they suggest next?
 98 | 
 99 |    Be specific and cite page numbers where possible."
100 | 
101 | 5. Click "Save"
102 | 6. Your transformation appears in the list
103 | ```
104 | 
105 | ### Prompt Template Tips
106 | 
107 | **Be specific about format:**
108 | ```
109 | Good: "List 5 key points as bullet points"
110 | Bad: "What are the key points?"
111 | ```
112 | 
113 | **Request structure:**
114 | ```
115 | Good: "Create sections for: Summary, Methods, Results"
116 | Bad: "Tell me about this paper"
117 | ```
118 | 
119 | **Ask for citations:**
120 | ```
121 | Good: "Cite page numbers for each claim"
122 | Bad: (no citation request)
123 | ```
124 | 
125 | **Set length expectations:**
126 | ```
127 | Good: "In 200-300 words, summarize..."
128 | Bad: "Summarize this"
129 | ```
130 | 
131 | ---
132 | 
133 | ## Applying Transformations
134 | 
135 | ### To a Single Source
136 | 
137 | ```
138 | 1. In Sources panel, click source menu (⋮)
139 | 2. Select "Transform"
140 | 3. Choose transformation template
141 | 4. Click "Apply"
142 | 5. Note appears when done
143 | ```
144 | 
145 | ### To Multiple Sources (Batch)
146 | 
147 | ```
148 | 1. Go to Transformations page
149 | 2. Select your template
150 | 3. Check multiple sources
151 | 4. Click "Apply to Selected"
152 | 5. Processing runs in parallel
153 | 6. One note per source created
154 | ```
155 | 
156 | ### Processing Time
157 | 
158 | | Sources | Typical Time |
159 | |---------|--------------|
160 | | 1 source | 30 seconds - 1 minute |
161 | | 5 sources | 2-3 minutes |
162 | | 10 sources | 4-5 minutes |
163 | | 20+ sources | 8-10 minutes |
164 | 
165 | Processing runs in background. You can continue working.
166 | 
167 | ---
168 | 
169 | ## Transformation Examples
170 | 
171 | ### Literature Review Template
172 | 
173 | ```
174 | Name: Literature Review Entry
175 | 
176 | Prompt:
177 | "For this research paper, create a literature review entry:
178 | 
179 | **Citation**: [Author(s), Year, Title, Journal]
180 | **Research Question**: What problem is addressed?
181 | **Methodology**: What approach was used?
182 | **Sample**: What population/data was studied?
183 | **Key Findings**:
184 | 1. [Finding with page citation]
185 | 2. [Finding with page citation]
186 | 3. [Finding with page citation]
187 | **Strengths**: What did this study do well?
188 | **Limitations**: What are the gaps?
189 | **Relevance**: How does this connect to my research?
190 | 
191 | Keep each section to 2-3 sentences."
192 | ```
193 | 
194 | ### Meeting Notes Template
195 | 
196 | ```
197 | Name: Meeting Summary
198 | 
199 | Prompt:
200 | "From this meeting transcript, extract:
201 | 
202 | **Attendees**: Who was present
203 | **Date/Time**: When it occurred
204 | **Key Decisions**: What was decided (numbered)
205 | **Action Items**:
206 | - [ ] Task (Owner, Due Date)
207 | **Open Questions**: Unresolved issues
208 | **Next Steps**: What happens next
209 | 
210 | Format as clear, scannable notes."
211 | ```
212 | 
213 | ### Competitor Analysis Template
214 | 
215 | ```
216 | Name: Competitor Analysis
217 | 
218 | Prompt:
219 | "Analyze this company/product document:
220 | 
221 | **Company**: Name and overview
222 | **Products/Services**: What they offer
223 | **Target Market**: Who they serve
224 | **Pricing**: If available
225 | **Strengths**: Competitive advantages
226 | **Weaknesses**: Gaps or limitations
227 | **Opportunities**: How we compare
228 | **Threats**: What they do better
229 | 
230 | Be objective and cite specific details."
231 | ```
232 | 
233 | ### Technical Documentation Template
234 | 
235 | ```
236 | Name: API Documentation Summary
237 | 
238 | Prompt:
239 | "Extract from this technical document:
240 | 
241 | **Overview**: What does this do? (1-2 sentences)
242 | **Authentication**: How to authenticate
243 | **Key Endpoints**:
244 | - Endpoint 1: [method] [path] - [purpose]
245 | - Endpoint 2: ...
246 | **Common Parameters**: Frequently used params
247 | **Rate Limits**: If mentioned
248 | **Error Codes**: Key error responses
249 | **Example Usage**: Simple code example if possible
250 | 
251 | Keep technical but concise."
252 | ```
253 | 
254 | ---
255 | 
256 | ## Managing Transformations
257 | 
258 | ### Edit a Transformation
259 | 
260 | ```
261 | 1. Go to Transformations page
262 | 2. Find your template
263 | 3. Click "Edit"
264 | 4. Modify the prompt
265 | 5. Click "Save"
266 | ```
267 | 
268 | ### Delete a Transformation
269 | 
270 | ```
271 | 1. Go to Transformations page
272 | 2. Find the template
273 | 3. Click "Delete"
274 | 4. Confirm
275 | ```
276 | 
277 | ### Reorder/Organize
278 | 
279 | Built-in transformations appear first, then custom ones alphabetically.
280 | 
281 | ---
282 | 
283 | ## Transformation Output
284 | 
285 | ### Where Results Go
286 | 
287 | - Each source produces one note
288 | - Notes appear in your notebook's Notes panel
289 | - Notes are tagged with transformation name
290 | - Original source is linked
291 | 
292 | ### Note Naming
293 | 
294 | ```
295 | Default: "[Transformation Name] - [Source Title]"
296 | Example: "Summary - Research Paper 2025.pdf"
297 | ```
298 | 
299 | ### Editing Output
300 | 
301 | ```
302 | 1. Click the generated note
303 | 2. Click "Edit"
304 | 3. Refine the content
305 | 4. Save
306 | ```
307 | 
308 | ---
309 | 
310 | ## Best Practices
311 | 
312 | ### Template Design
313 | 
314 | 1. **Start specific** - Vague prompts give vague results
315 | 2. **Use formatting** - Headings, bullets, numbered lists
316 | 3. **Request citations** - Make results verifiable
317 | 4. **Set length** - Prevent overly long or short output
318 | 5. **Test first** - Run on one source before batch
319 | 
320 | ### Source Selection
321 | 
322 | 1. **Similar content** - Same transformation on similar sources
323 | 2. **Reasonable size** - Very long sources may need splitting
324 | 3. **Processed status** - Ensure sources are fully processed
325 | 
326 | ### Quality Control
327 | 
328 | 1. **Review samples** - Check first few outputs before trusting batch
329 | 2. **Edit as needed** - Transformations are starting points
330 | 3. **Iterate prompts** - Refine based on results
331 | 
332 | ---
333 | 
334 | ## Common Issues
335 | 
336 | ### Generic Output
337 | 
338 | **Problem**: Results are too vague
339 | **Solution**: Make prompt more specific, add format requirements
340 | 
341 | ### Missing Information
342 | 
343 | **Problem**: Key details not extracted
344 | **Solution**: Explicitly ask for what you need in prompt
345 | 
346 | ### Inconsistent Format
347 | 
348 | **Problem**: Each note looks different
349 | **Solution**: Add clear formatting instructions to prompt
350 | 
351 | ### Too Long/Short
352 | 
353 | **Problem**: Output doesn't match expectations
354 | **Solution**: Specify word count or section lengths
355 | 
356 | ### Processing Fails
357 | 
358 | **Problem**: Transformation doesn't complete
359 | **Solution**:
360 | - Check source is processed
361 | - Try shorter/simpler prompt
362 | - Process sources individually
363 | 
364 | ---
365 | 
366 | ## Transformations vs. Chat vs. Ask
367 | 
368 | | Feature | Transformations | Chat | Ask |
369 | |---------|----------------|------|-----|
370 | | **Input** | Predefined template | Your questions | Your question |
371 | | **Scope** | One source at a time | Selected sources | Auto-searched |
372 | | **Output** | Structured note | Conversation | Comprehensive answer |
373 | | **Best for** | Batch processing | Exploration | One-shot answers |
374 | | **Follow-up** | Run again | Ask more | New query |
375 | 
376 | ---
377 | 
378 | ## Summary
379 | 
380 | ```
381 | Transformations = Batch AI Processing
382 | 
383 | How to use:
384 | 1. Define template (or use built-in)
385 | 2. Select sources
386 | 3. Apply transformation
387 | 4. Get structured notes
388 | 
389 | When to use:
390 | - Same analysis on many sources
391 | - Consistent output needed
392 | - Building structured knowledge base
393 | - Saving time on repetitive tasks
394 | 
395 | Tips:
396 | - Be specific in prompts
397 | - Request formatting
398 | - Test before batch
399 | - Edit output as needed
400 | ```
401 | 
402 | Transformations turn repetitive analysis into one-click operations. Define once, apply many times.
403 |

  1 | 'use client'
  2 | 
  3 | import { useEffect, useState, useId } from 'react'
  4 | import { useForm } from 'react-hook-form'
  5 | import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'
  6 | import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from '@/components/ui/select'
  7 | import { Label } from '@/components/ui/label'
  8 | import { Alert, AlertDescription } from '@/components/ui/alert'
  9 | import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
 10 | import { ModelDefaults, Model } from '@/lib/types/models'
 11 | import { useUpdateModelDefaults } from '@/lib/hooks/use-models'
 12 | import { AlertCircle, X } from 'lucide-react'
 13 | import { EmbeddingModelChangeDialog } from './EmbeddingModelChangeDialog'
 14 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
 15 | 
 16 | interface DefaultModelsSectionProps {
 17 |   models: Model[]
 18 |   defaults: ModelDefaults
 19 | }
 20 | 
 21 | export function DefaultModelsSection({ models, defaults }: DefaultModelsSectionProps) {
 22 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 23 |   const updateDefaults = useUpdateModelDefaults()
 24 |   const { setValue, watch } = useForm<ModelDefaults>({
 25 |     defaultValues: defaults
 26 |   })
 27 | 
 28 |   interface DefaultConfig {
 29 |     key: keyof ModelDefaults
 30 |     label: string
 31 |     description: string
 32 |     modelType: 'language' | 'embedding' | 'text_to_speech' | 'speech_to_text'
 33 |     required?: boolean
 34 |     id: string
 35 |   }
 36 | 
 37 |   const generatedId = useId()
 38 | 
 39 |   const defaultConfigs: DefaultConfig[] = [
 40 |     {
 41 |       key: 'default_chat_model',
 42 |       label: t.models.chatModelLabel,
 43 |       description: t.models.chatModelDesc,
 44 |       modelType: 'language',
 45 |       required: true,
 46 |       id: `${generatedId}-chat`,
 47 |     },
 48 |     {
 49 |       key: 'default_transformation_model',
 50 |       label: t.models.transformationModelLabel,
 51 |       description: t.models.transformationModelDesc,
 52 |       modelType: 'language',
 53 |       required: true,
 54 |       id: `${generatedId}-transformation`,
 55 |     },
 56 |     {
 57 |       key: 'default_tools_model',
 58 |       label: t.models.toolsModelLabel,
 59 |       description: t.models.toolsModelDesc,
 60 |       modelType: 'language',
 61 |       id: `${generatedId}-tools`,
 62 |     },
 63 |     {
 64 |       key: 'large_context_model',
 65 |       label: t.models.largeContextModelLabel,
 66 |       description: t.models.largeContextModelDesc,
 67 |       modelType: 'language',
 68 |       id: `${generatedId}-large-context`,
 69 |     },
 70 |     {
 71 |       key: 'default_embedding_model',
 72 |       label: t.models.embeddingModelLabel,
 73 |       description: t.models.embeddingModelDesc,
 74 |       modelType: 'embedding',
 75 |       required: true,
 76 |       id: `${generatedId}-embedding`,
 77 |     },
 78 |     {
 79 |       key: 'default_text_to_speech_model',
 80 |       label: t.models.ttsModelLabel,
 81 |       description: t.models.ttsModelDesc,
 82 |       modelType: 'text_to_speech',
 83 |       id: `${generatedId}-tts`,
 84 |     },
 85 |     {
 86 |       key: 'default_speech_to_text_model',
 87 |       label: t.models.sttModelLabel,
 88 |       description: t.models.sttModelDesc,
 89 |       modelType: 'speech_to_text',
 90 |       id: `${generatedId}-stt`,
 91 |     },
 92 |   ]
 93 | 
 94 |   // State for embedding model change dialog
 95 |   const [showEmbeddingDialog, setShowEmbeddingDialog] = useState(false)
 96 |   const [pendingEmbeddingChange, setPendingEmbeddingChange] = useState<{
 97 |     key: keyof ModelDefaults
 98 |     value: string
 99 |     oldModelId?: string
100 |     newModelId?: string
101 |   } | null>(null)
102 | 
103 |   // Update form when defaults change
104 |   useEffect(() => {
105 |     if (defaults) {
106 |       Object.entries(defaults).forEach(([key, value]) => {
107 |         setValue(key as keyof ModelDefaults, value)
108 |       })
109 |     }
110 |   }, [defaults, setValue])
111 | 
112 |   const handleChange = (key: keyof ModelDefaults, value: string) => {
113 |     // Special handling for embedding model changes
114 |     if (key === 'default_embedding_model') {
115 |       const currentEmbeddingModel = defaults[key]
116 | 
117 |       // Only show dialog if there's an existing embedding model and it's changing
118 |       if (currentEmbeddingModel && currentEmbeddingModel !== value) {
119 |         setPendingEmbeddingChange({
120 |           key,
121 |           value,
122 |           oldModelId: currentEmbeddingModel,
123 |           newModelId: value
124 |         })
125 |         setShowEmbeddingDialog(true)
126 |         return
127 |       }
128 |     }
129 | 
130 |     // For all other changes or new embedding model assignment
131 |     const newDefaults = { [key]: value || null }
132 |     updateDefaults.mutate(newDefaults)
133 |   }
134 | 
135 |   const handleConfirmEmbeddingChange = () => {
136 |     if (pendingEmbeddingChange) {
137 |       const newDefaults = {
138 |         [pendingEmbeddingChange.key]: pendingEmbeddingChange.value || null
139 |       }
140 |       updateDefaults.mutate(newDefaults)
141 |       setPendingEmbeddingChange(null)
142 |     }
143 |   }
144 | 
145 |   const handleCancelEmbeddingChange = () => {
146 |     setPendingEmbeddingChange(null)
147 |     setShowEmbeddingDialog(false)
148 |   }
149 | 
150 |   const getModelsForType = (type: 'language' | 'embedding' | 'text_to_speech' | 'speech_to_text') => {
151 |     return models.filter(model => model.type === type)
152 |   }
153 | 
154 |   const missingRequired = defaultConfigs
155 |     .filter(config => {
156 |       if (!config.required) return false
157 |       const value = defaults[config.key]
158 |       if (!value) return true
159 |       // Check if the model still exists
160 |       const modelsOfType = models.filter(m => m.type === config.modelType)
161 |       return !modelsOfType.some(m => m.id === value)
162 |     })
163 |     .map(config => config.label)
164 | 
165 |   return (
166 |     <Card>
167 |       <CardHeader>
168 |         <CardTitle>{t.models.defaultAssignments}</CardTitle>
169 |         <CardDescription>
170 |           {t.models.defaultAssignmentsDesc}
171 |         </CardDescription>
172 |       </CardHeader>
173 |       <CardContent className="space-y-6">
174 |         {missingRequired.length > 0 && (
175 |           <Alert>
176 |             <AlertCircle className="h-4 w-4" />
177 |             <AlertDescription>
178 |               {t.models.missingRequiredModels.replace('{models}', missingRequired.join(', '))}
179 |             </AlertDescription>
180 |           </Alert>
181 |         )}
182 | 
183 |         <div className="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-2">
184 |           {defaultConfigs.map((config) => {
185 |             const availableModels = getModelsForType(config.modelType)
186 |             const currentValue = watch(config.key) || undefined
187 |             
188 |             // Check if the current value exists in available models
189 |             const isValidModel = currentValue && availableModels.some(m => m.id === currentValue)
190 | 
191 |             return (
192 |               <div key={config.key} className="space-y-2">
193 |                 <Label htmlFor={config.id}>
194 |                   {config.label}
195 |                   {config.required && <span className="text-destructive ml-1">*</span>}
196 |                 </Label>
197 |                 <div className="flex gap-2">
198 |                   <Select
199 |                     value={currentValue || ""}
200 |                     onValueChange={(value) => handleChange(config.key, value)}
201 |                   >
202 |                     <SelectTrigger 
203 |                       id={config.id}
204 |                       className={
205 |                         config.required && !isValidModel && availableModels.length > 0
206 |                           ? 'border-destructive' 
207 |                           : ''
208 |                       }
209 |                     >
210 |                       <SelectValue placeholder={
211 |                         config.required && !isValidModel && availableModels.length > 0 
212 |                           ? t.models.requiredModelPlaceholder
213 |                           : t.models.selectModelPlaceholder
214 |                       } />
215 |                     </SelectTrigger>
216 |                     <SelectContent>
217 |                       {availableModels.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name)).map((model) => (
218 |                         <SelectItem key={model.id} value={model.id}>
219 |                           <div className="flex items-center justify-between w-full">
220 |                             <span>{model.name}</span>
221 |                             <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground ml-2">
222 |                               {model.provider}
223 |                             </span>
224 |                           </div>
225 |                         </SelectItem>
226 |                       ))}
227 |                     </SelectContent>
228 |                   </Select>
229 |                   {!config.required && currentValue && (
230 |                     <Button
231 |                       variant="ghost"
232 |                       size="icon"
233 |                       onClick={() => handleChange(config.key, "")}
234 |                       className="h-10 w-10"
235 |                     >
236 |                       <X className="h-4 w-4" />
237 |                     </Button>
238 |                   )}
239 |                 </div>
240 |                 <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">{config.description}</p>
241 |               </div>
242 |             )
243 |           })}
244 |         </div>
245 | 
246 |         <div className="pt-4 border-t">
247 |           <a
248 |             href="https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook/blob/main/docs/5-CONFIGURATION/ai-providers.md"
249 |             target="_blank"
250 |             rel="noopener noreferrer"
251 |             className="text-sm text-primary hover:underline"
252 |           >
253 |             {t.models.whichModelToChoose}
254 |           </a>
255 |         </div>
256 |       </CardContent>
257 | 
258 |       {/* Embedding Model Change Dialog */}
259 |       <EmbeddingModelChangeDialog
260 |         open={showEmbeddingDialog}
261 |         onOpenChange={(open) => {
262 |           if (!open) {
263 |             handleCancelEmbeddingChange()
264 |           }
265 |         }}
266 |         onConfirm={handleConfirmEmbeddingChange}
267 |         oldModelName={
268 |           pendingEmbeddingChange?.oldModelId
269 |             ? models.find(m => m.id === pendingEmbeddingChange.oldModelId)?.name
270 |             : undefined
271 |         }
272 |         newModelName={
273 |           pendingEmbeddingChange?.newModelId
274 |             ? models.find(m => m.id === pendingEmbeddingChange.newModelId)?.name
275 |             : undefined
276 |         }
277 |       />
278 |     </Card>
279 |   )
280 | }

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Interface Overview - Finding Your Way Around
  2 | 
  3 | Open Notebook uses a clean three-panel layout. This guide shows you where everything is.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## The Main Layout
  8 | 
  9 | ```
 10 | ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 11 | │  [Logo]  Notebooks  Search  Podcasts  Models  Settings      │
 12 | ├──────────────┬──────────────┬───────────────────────────────┤
 13 | │              │              │                               │
 14 | │   SOURCES    │    NOTES     │           CHAT                │
 15 | │              │              │                               │
 16 | │  Your docs   │  Your        │   Talk to AI about            │
 17 | │  PDFs, URLs  │  insights    │   your sources                │
 18 | │  Videos      │  summaries   │                               │
 19 | │              │              │                               │
 20 | │  [+Add]      │  [+Write]    │   [Type here...]              │
 21 | │              │              │                               │
 22 | └──────────────┴──────────────┴───────────────────────────────┘
 23 | ```
 24 | 
 25 | ---
 26 | 
 27 | ## Navigation Bar
 28 | 
 29 | The top navigation takes you to main sections:
 30 | 
 31 | | Icon | Page | What It Does |
 32 | |------|------|--------------|
 33 | | **Notebooks** | Main workspace | Your research projects |
 34 | | **Search** | Ask & Search | Query across all notebooks |
 35 | | **Podcasts** | Audio generation | Manage podcast profiles |
 36 | | **Models** | AI configuration | Set up providers and models |
 37 | | **Settings** | Preferences | App configuration |
 38 | 
 39 | ---
 40 | 
 41 | ## Left Panel: Sources
 42 | 
 43 | Your research materials live here.
 44 | 
 45 | ### What You'll See
 46 | 
 47 | ```
 48 | ┌─────────────────────────┐
 49 | │  Sources (5)            │
 50 | │  [+ Add Source]         │
 51 | ├─────────────────────────┤
 52 | │  ┌─────────────────┐    │
 53 | │  │ 📄 Paper.pdf    │    │
 54 | │  │ 🟢 Full Content │    │
 55 | │  │ [⋮ Menu]        │    │
 56 | │  └─────────────────┘    │
 57 | │                         │
 58 | │  ┌─────────────────┐    │
 59 | │  │ 🔗 Article URL  │    │
 60 | │  │ 🟡 Summary Only │    │
 61 | │  │ [⋮ Menu]        │    │
 62 | │  └─────────────────┘    │
 63 | └─────────────────────────┘
 64 | ```
 65 | 
 66 | ### Source Card Elements
 67 | 
 68 | - **Icon** - File type (PDF, URL, video, etc.)
 69 | - **Title** - Document name
 70 | - **Context indicator** - What AI can see:
 71 |   - 🟢 Full Content
 72 |   - 🟡 Summary Only
 73 |   - ⛔ Not in Context
 74 | - **Menu (⋮)** - Edit, transform, delete
 75 | 
 76 | ### Add Source Button
 77 | 
 78 | Click to add:
 79 | - File upload (PDF, DOCX, etc.)
 80 | - Web URL
 81 | - YouTube video
 82 | - Plain text
 83 | 
 84 | ---
 85 | 
 86 | ## Middle Panel: Notes
 87 | 
 88 | Your insights and AI-generated content.
 89 | 
 90 | ### What You'll See
 91 | 
 92 | ```
 93 | ┌─────────────────────────┐
 94 | │  Notes (3)              │
 95 | │  [+ Write Note]         │
 96 | ├─────────────────────────┤
 97 | │  ┌─────────────────┐    │
 98 | │  │ 📝 My Analysis  │    │
 99 | │  │ Manual note     │    │
100 | │  │ Jan 3, 2026     │    │
101 | │  └─────────────────┘    │
102 | │                         │
103 | │  ┌─────────────────┐    │
104 | │  │ 🤖 Summary      │    │
105 | │  │ From transform  │    │
106 | │  │ Jan 2, 2026     │    │
107 | │  └─────────────────┘    │
108 | └─────────────────────────┘
109 | ```
110 | 
111 | ### Note Card Elements
112 | 
113 | - **Icon** - Note type (manual 📝 or AI 🤖)
114 | - **Title** - Note name
115 | - **Origin** - How it was created
116 | - **Date** - When created
117 | 
118 | ### Write Note Button
119 | 
120 | Click to:
121 | - Create manual note
122 | - Add your own insights
123 | - Markdown supported
124 | 
125 | ---
126 | 
127 | ## Right Panel: Chat
128 | 
129 | Your AI conversation space.
130 | 
131 | ### What You'll See
132 | 
133 | ```
134 | ┌───────────────────────────────┐
135 | │  Chat                         │
136 | │  Session: Research Discussion │
137 | │  [+ New Session] [Sessions ▼] │
138 | ├───────────────────────────────┤
139 | │                               │
140 | │  You: What's the main         │
141 | │       finding?                │
142 | │                               │
143 | │  AI: Based on the paper [1],  │
144 | │      the main finding is...   │
145 | │      [Save as Note]           │
146 | │                               │
147 | │  You: Tell me more about      │
148 | │       the methodology.        │
149 | │                               │
150 | ├───────────────────────────────┤
151 | │  Context: 3 sources (12K tok) │
152 | ├───────────────────────────────┤
153 | │  [Type your message...]  [↑]  │
154 | └───────────────────────────────┘
155 | ```
156 | 
157 | ### Chat Elements
158 | 
159 | - **Session selector** - Switch between conversations
160 | - **Message history** - Your conversation
161 | - **Save as Note** - Keep good responses
162 | - **Context indicator** - What AI can see
163 | - **Input field** - Type your questions
164 | 
165 | ---
166 | 
167 | ## Context Indicators
168 | 
169 | These show what AI can access:
170 | 
171 | ### Token Counter
172 | 
173 | ```
174 | Context: 3 sources (12,450 tokens)
175 |          ↑          ↑
176 |          Sources    Approximate cost indicator
177 |          included
178 | ```
179 | 
180 | ### Per-Source Indicators
181 | 
182 | | Indicator | Meaning | AI Access |
183 | |-----------|---------|-----------|
184 | | 🟢 Full Content | Complete text | Everything |
185 | | 🟡 Summary Only | AI summary | Key points only |
186 | | ⛔ Not in Context | Excluded | Nothing |
187 | 
188 | Click any source to change its context level.
189 | 
190 | ---
191 | 
192 | ## Podcasts Tab
193 | 
194 | Inside a notebook, switch to Podcasts:
195 | 
196 | ```
197 | ┌───────────────────────────────┐
198 | │  [Chat]  [Podcasts]           │
199 | ├───────────────────────────────┤
200 | │  Episode Profile: [Select ▼]  │
201 | │                               │
202 | │  Speakers:                    │
203 | │  ├─ Host: Alex (OpenAI)       │
204 | │  └─ Guest: Sam (Google)       │
205 | │                               │
206 | │  Include:                     │
207 | │  ☑ Paper.pdf                  │
208 | │  ☑ My Analysis (note)         │
209 | │  ☐ Background article         │
210 | │                               │
211 | │  [Generate Podcast]           │
212 | └───────────────────────────────┘
213 | ```
214 | 
215 | ---
216 | 
217 | ## Settings Page
218 | 
219 | Access via navigation bar → Settings:
220 | 
221 | ### Key Sections
222 | 
223 | | Section | What It Controls |
224 | |---------|------------------|
225 | | **Processing** | Document and URL extraction engines |
226 | | **Embedding** | Auto-embed settings |
227 | | **Files** | Auto-delete uploads after processing |
228 | | **YouTube** | Preferred transcript languages |
229 | 
230 | ---
231 | 
232 | ## Models Page
233 | 
234 | Configure AI providers:
235 | 
236 | ```
237 | ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
238 | │  Models                               │
239 | ├───────────────────────────────────────┤
240 | │  Language Models                      │
241 | │  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐  │
242 | │  │ GPT-4o (OpenAI)         [Edit]  │  │
243 | │  │ Claude Sonnet (Anthropic)       │  │
244 | │  │ Llama 3.3 (Ollama)      [⭐]    │  │
245 | │  └─────────────────────────────────┘  │
246 | │  [+ Add Model]                        │
247 | │                                       │
248 | │  Embedding Models                     │
249 | │  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐  │
250 | │  │ text-embedding-3-small  [⭐]    │  │
251 | │  └─────────────────────────────────┘  │
252 | │                                       │
253 | │  Text-to-Speech                       │
254 | │  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐  │
255 | │  │ OpenAI TTS             [⭐]     │  │
256 | │  │ Google TTS                      │  │
257 | │  └─────────────────────────────────┘  │
258 | └───────────────────────────────────────┘
259 | ```
260 | 
261 | - **⭐** = Default model for that category
262 | - **[Edit]** = Modify configuration
263 | - **[+ Add]** = Add new model
264 | 
265 | ---
266 | 
267 | ## Search Page
268 | 
269 | Query across all notebooks:
270 | 
271 | ```
272 | ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
273 | │  Search                               │
274 | ├───────────────────────────────────────┤
275 | │  [What are you looking for?    ] [🔍] │
276 | │                                       │
277 | │  Search type: [Text ▼] [Vector ▼]     │
278 | │  Search in:   [Sources] [Notes]       │
279 | ├───────────────────────────────────────┤
280 | │  Results (15)                         │
281 | │                                       │
282 | │  📄 Paper.pdf - Notebook: Research    │
283 | │     "...the transformer model..."     │
284 | │                                       │
285 | │  📝 My Analysis - Notebook: Research  │
286 | │     "...key findings include..."      │
287 | └───────────────────────────────────────┘
288 | ```
289 | 
290 | ---
291 | 
292 | ## Common Actions
293 | 
294 | ### Create a Notebook
295 | 
296 | ```
297 | Notebooks page → [+ New Notebook] → Enter name → Create
298 | ```
299 | 
300 | ### Add a Source
301 | 
302 | ```
303 | Inside notebook → [+ Add Source] → Choose type → Upload/paste → Wait for processing
304 | ```
305 | 
306 | ### Ask a Question
307 | 
308 | ```
309 | Inside notebook → Chat panel → Type question → Enter → Read response
310 | ```
311 | 
312 | ### Save AI Response
313 | 
314 | ```
315 | Get good response → Click [Save as Note] → Edit title → Save
316 | ```
317 | 
318 | ### Change Context Level
319 | 
320 | ```
321 | Click source → Context dropdown → Select level → Changes apply immediately
322 | ```
323 | 
324 | ### Generate Podcast
325 | 
326 | ```
327 | Podcasts tab → Select profile → Choose sources → [Generate] → Wait → Download
328 | ```
329 | 
330 | ---
331 | 
332 | ## Keyboard Shortcuts
333 | 
334 | | Key | Action |
335 | |-----|--------|
336 | | `Enter` | Send chat message |
337 | | `Shift + Enter` | New line in chat |
338 | | `Escape` | Close dialogs |
339 | | `Ctrl/Cmd + F` | Browser find |
340 | 
341 | ---
342 | 
343 | ## Mobile View
344 | 
345 | On smaller screens, the three-panel layout stacks vertically:
346 | 
347 | ```
348 | ┌─────────────────┐
349 | │    SOURCES      │
350 | │    (tap to expand)
351 | ├─────────────────┤
352 | │    NOTES        │
353 | │    (tap to expand)
354 | ├─────────────────┤
355 | │    CHAT         │
356 | │    (always visible)
357 | └─────────────────┘
358 | ```
359 | 
360 | - Panels collapse to save space
361 | - Tap headers to expand/collapse
362 | - Chat remains accessible
363 | - Full functionality preserved
364 | 
365 | ---
366 | 
367 | ## Tips for Efficient Navigation
368 | 
369 | 1. **Use keyboard** - Enter sends messages, Escape closes dialogs
370 | 2. **Context first** - Set source context before chatting
371 | 3. **Sessions** - Create new sessions for different topics
372 | 4. **Search globally** - Use Search page to find across all notebooks
373 | 5. **Models page** - Bookmark your preferred models
374 | 
375 | ---
376 | 
377 | Now you know where everything is. Start with [Adding Sources](adding-sources.md) to begin your research!
378 |

147 |                             {t.podcasts.duplicate}

 77 |   }
 78 | 
 79 |   const handleStartEdit = (session: BaseChatSession) => {
 80 |     setEditingId(session.id)
 81 |     setEditTitle(session.title)
 82 |   }
 83 | 
 84 |   const handleSaveEdit = () => {
 85 |     if (editingId && editTitle.trim()) {
 86 |       onUpdateSession(editingId, editTitle.trim())
 87 |       setEditingId(null)
 88 |       setEditTitle('')
 89 |     }
 90 |   }
 91 | 
 92 |   const handleCancelEdit = () => {
 93 |     setEditingId(null)
 94 |     setEditTitle('')
 95 |   }
 96 | 
 97 |   const handleDeleteConfirm = () => {
 98 |     if (deleteConfirmId) {
 99 |       onDeleteSession(deleteConfirmId)
100 |       setDeleteConfirmId(null)
101 |     }
102 |   }
103 | 
104 |   return (
105 |     <>
106 |       <Card className="h-full flex flex-col">
107 |         <CardHeader className="pb-3">
108 |           <CardTitle className="flex items-center justify-between">
109 |             <span className="flex items-center gap-2">
110 |               <MessageSquare className="h-5 w-5" />
111 |               {t.chat.sessions}
112 |             </span>
113 |             <Button
114 |               size="sm"
115 |               variant="outline"
116 |               onClick={() => setIsCreating(true)}
117 |             >
118 |               <Plus className="h-4 w-4" />
119 |             </Button>
120 |           </CardTitle>
121 |         </CardHeader>
122 |         <CardContent className="flex-1 p-0 min-h-0">
123 |           <ScrollArea className="h-full px-4">
124 |             {isCreating && (
125 |               <div className="p-3 border rounded-lg mb-3">
126 |                 <Input
127 |                   value={newSessionTitle}
128 |                   onChange={(e) => setNewSessionTitle(e.target.value)}
129 |                   placeholder={t.chat.sessionTitlePlaceholder}
130 |                   className="mb-2"
131 |                   autoFocus
132 |                   onKeyPress={(e) => {
133 |                     if (e.key === 'Enter') handleCreateSession()
134 |                   }}
135 |                 />
136 |                 <div className="flex gap-2">
137 |                   <Button size="sm" onClick={handleCreateSession}>
138 |                     {t.common.create}
139 |                   </Button>
140 |                   <Button
141 |                     size="sm"
142 |                     variant="outline"
143 |                     onClick={() => {
144 |                       setIsCreating(false)
145 |                       setNewSessionTitle('')
146 |                     }}
147 |                   >
148 |                     {t.common.cancel}
149 |                   </Button>
150 |                 </div>
151 |               </div>
152 |             )}
153 | 
154 |             {loadingSessions ? (
155 |               <div className="text-center py-8 text-muted-foreground">
156 |                 {t.common.loading}
157 |               </div>
158 |             ) : sessions.length === 0 ? (
159 |               <div className="text-center py-8 text-muted-foreground">
160 |                 <MessageSquare className="h-12 w-12 mx-auto mb-4 opacity-50" />
161 |                 <p className="text-sm">{t.chat.noSessions}</p>
162 |                 <p className="text-xs mt-2">{t.chat.createToStart}</p>
163 |               </div>
164 |             ) : (
165 |               <div className="space-y-2 pb-4">
166 |                 {sessions.map((session) => (
167 |                   <div
168 |                     key={session.id}
169 |                     className={`p-3 rounded-lg border cursor-pointer transition-colors ${
170 |                       currentSessionId === session.id
171 |                         ? 'bg-primary/10 border-primary'
172 |                         : 'hover:bg-muted'
173 |                     }`}
174 |                     onClick={() => onSelectSession(session.id)}
175 |                   >
176 |                     {editingId === session.id ? (
177 |                       <div className="space-y-2" onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}>
178 |                         <Input
179 |                           value={editTitle}
180 |                           onChange={(e) => setEditTitle(e.target.value)}
181 |                           onKeyPress={(e) => {
182 |                             if (e.key === 'Enter') handleSaveEdit()
183 |                             if (e.key === 'Escape') handleCancelEdit()
184 |                           }}
185 |                           autoFocus
186 |                         />
187 |                         <div className="flex gap-2">
188 |                           <Button size="sm" onClick={handleSaveEdit}>
189 |                             <Check className="h-3 w-3" />
190 |                           </Button>
191 |                           <Button
192 |                             size="sm"
193 |                             variant="outline"
194 |                             onClick={handleCancelEdit}
195 |                           >
196 |                             <X className="h-3 w-3" />
197 |                           </Button>
198 |                         </div>
199 |                       </div>
200 |                     ) : (
201 |                       <>
202 |                         <div className="flex items-start justify-between mb-1">
203 |                           <h4 className="font-medium text-sm">
204 |                             {session.title}
205 |                           </h4>
206 |                           <div className="flex gap-1" onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}>
207 |                             <Button
208 |                               size="sm"
209 |                               variant="ghost"
210 |                               className="h-6 w-6 p-0"
211 |                               onClick={() => handleStartEdit(session)}
212 |                             >
213 |                               <Edit2 className="h-3 w-3" />
214 |                             </Button>
215 |                             <Button
216 |                               size="sm"
217 |                               variant="ghost"
218 |                               className="h-6 w-6 p-0"
219 |                               onClick={() => setDeleteConfirmId(session.id)}
220 |                             >
221 |                               <Trash2 className="h-3 w-3" />
222 |                             </Button>
223 |                           </div>
224 |                         </div>
225 |                         <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-xs text-muted-foreground">
226 |                           <Clock className="h-3 w-3" />
227 |                           {formatDistanceToNow(new Date(session.created), {
228 |                             addSuffix: true,
229 |                             locale: getDateLocale(language)
230 |                           })}
231 |                         </div>
232 |                         {session.message_count != null && session.message_count > 0 && (
233 |                           <Badge variant="secondary" className="mt-2 text-xs">
234 |                             {t.chat.messagesCount.replace('{count}', session.message_count.toString())}
235 |                           </Badge>
236 |                         )}
237 |                         {session.model_override && (
238 |                           <Badge variant="outline" className="mt-2 ml-2 text-xs">
239 |                             {getModelName(session.model_override)}
240 |                           </Badge>
241 |                         )}
242 |                       </>
243 |                     )}
244 |                   </div>
245 |                 ))}
246 |               </div>
247 |             )}
248 |           </ScrollArea>
249 |         </CardContent>
250 |       </Card>
251 | 
252 |       <AlertDialog open={!!deleteConfirmId} onOpenChange={() => setDeleteConfirmId(null)}>
253 |         <AlertDialogContent>
254 |           <AlertDialogHeader>
255 |             <AlertDialogTitle>{t.chat.deleteSession}</AlertDialogTitle>
256 |             <AlertDialogDescription>
257 |               {t.chat.deleteSessionDesc}
258 |             </AlertDialogDescription>
259 |           </AlertDialogHeader>
260 |           <AlertDialogFooter>
261 |             <AlertDialogCancel>{t.common.cancel}</AlertDialogCancel>
262 |             <AlertDialogAction onClick={handleDeleteConfirm}>
263 |               {t.common.delete}
264 |             </AlertDialogAction>
265 |           </AlertDialogFooter>
266 |         </AlertDialogContent>
267 |       </AlertDialog>
268 |     </>
269 |   )
270 | }

/docs/6-TROUBLESHOOTING/ai-chat-issues.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # AI & Chat Issues - Model Configuration & Quality
  2 | 
  3 | Problems with AI models, chat, and response quality.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## "Failed to send message" Error
  8 | 
  9 | **Symptom:** Chat shows "Failed to send message" toast. Logs show:
 10 | ```
 11 | Error executing chat: Model is not a LanguageModel: None
 12 | ```
 13 | 
 14 | **Cause:** No valid language model configured for chat
 15 | 
 16 | **Solutions:**
 17 | 
 18 | ### Solution 1: Check Default Model Configuration
 19 | ```
 20 | 1. Go to Settings → Models
 21 | 2. Scroll to "Default Models" section
 22 | 3. Verify "Default Chat Model" has a model selected
 23 | 4. If empty, select an available language model
 24 | 5. Click Save
 25 | ```
 26 | 
 27 | ### Solution 2: Verify Model Names (Ollama Users)
 28 | ```bash
 29 | # Get exact model names
 30 | ollama list
 31 | 
 32 | # Example output:
 33 | # NAME                   SIZE      MODIFIED
 34 | # gemma3:12b            8.1 GB    2 months ago
 35 | 
 36 | # The model name in Open Notebook must be EXACTLY "gemma3:12b"
 37 | # NOT "gemma3" or "gemma3-12b"
 38 | ```
 39 | 
 40 | ### Solution 3: Re-add Missing Models
 41 | ```
 42 | 1. Note the exact model names from your provider
 43 | 2. Go to Settings → Models
 44 | 3. Delete any misconfigured models
 45 | 4. Add models with exact names
 46 | 5. Set new defaults
 47 | ```
 48 | 
 49 | ### Solution 4: Check Model Still Exists
 50 | ```bash
 51 | # For Ollama: verify model is installed
 52 | ollama list
 53 | 
 54 | # For cloud providers: verify API key is valid
 55 | # and you have access to the model
 56 | ```
 57 | 
 58 | > **Tip:** This error often occurs when you delete a model from Ollama but forget to update the default models in Open Notebook. Always re-configure defaults after removing models.
 59 | 
 60 | ---
 61 | 
 62 | ## "Models not available" or "Models not showing"
 63 | 
 64 | **Symptom:** Settings → Models shows empty, or "No models configured"
 65 | 
 66 | **Cause:** Missing or invalid API key
 67 | 
 68 | **Solutions:**
 69 | 
 70 | ### Solution 1: Add API Key
 71 | ```bash
 72 | # Check .env has your API key:
 73 | cat .env | grep -i "OPENAI\|ANTHROPIC\|GOOGLE"
 74 | 
 75 | # Should see something like:
 76 | # OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...
 77 | 
 78 | # If missing, add it:
 79 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-your-key-here
 80 | 
 81 | # Save and restart:
 82 | docker compose restart api
 83 | 
 84 | # Wait 10 seconds, then refresh browser
 85 | ```
 86 | 
 87 | ### Solution 2: Check Key is Valid
 88 | ```bash
 89 | # Test API key directly:
 90 | curl https://api.openai.com/v1/models \
 91 |   -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-..."
 92 | 
 93 | # Should return list of models
 94 | # If error: key is invalid
 95 | ```
 96 | 
 97 | ### Solution 3: Switch Provider
 98 | ```bash
 99 | # Try a different provider:
100 | # Remove: OPENAI_API_KEY
101 | # Add: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
102 | 
103 | # Restart and check Settings → Models
104 | ```
105 | 
106 | ---
107 | 
108 | ## "Invalid API key" or "Unauthorized"
109 | 
110 | **Symptom:** Error when trying to chat: "Invalid API key"
111 | 
112 | **Cause:** API key wrong, expired, or revoked
113 | 
114 | **Solutions:**
115 | 
116 | ### Step 1: Verify Key Format
117 | ```bash
118 | # OpenAI: Should start with sk-proj-
119 | # Anthropic: Should start with sk-ant-
120 | # Google: Should be AIzaSy...
121 | 
122 | # Check in .env:
123 | cat .env | grep OPENAI_API_KEY
124 | ```
125 | 
126 | ### Step 2: Get Fresh Key
127 | ```bash
128 | # Go to provider's dashboard:
129 | # - OpenAI: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
130 | # - Anthropic: https://console.anthropic.com/
131 | # - Google: https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey
132 | 
133 | # Generate new key
134 | # Copy exactly (no extra spaces)
135 | ```
136 | 
137 | ### Step 3: Update .env
138 | ```bash
139 | # Edit .env:
140 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-new-key-here
141 | # No quotes needed, no spaces
142 | 
143 | # Save and restart:
144 | docker compose restart api
145 | ```
146 | 
147 | ### Step 4: Verify in UI
148 | ```
149 | 1. Open Open Notebook
150 | 2. Go to Settings → Models
151 | 3. Select your provider
152 | 4. Should show available models
153 | ```
154 | 
155 | ---
156 | 
157 | ## Chat Returns Generic/Bad Responses
158 | 
159 | **Symptom:** AI responses are shallow, generic, or wrong
160 | 
161 | **Cause:** Bad context, vague question, or wrong model
162 | 
163 | **Solutions:**
164 | 
165 | ### Solution 1: Check Context
166 | ```
167 | 1. In Chat, click "Select Sources"
168 | 2. Verify sources you want are CHECKED
169 | 3. Set them to "Full Content" (not "Summary Only")
170 | 4. Click "Save"
171 | 5. Try chat again
172 | ```
173 | 
174 | ### Solution 2: Ask Better Question
175 | ```
176 | Bad:     "What do you think?"
177 | Good:    "Based on the paper's methodology, what are 3 limitations?"
178 | 
179 | Bad:     "Tell me about X"
180 | Good:    "Summarize X in 3 bullet points with page citations"
181 | ```
182 | 
183 | ### Solution 3: Use Stronger Model
184 | ```
185 | OpenAI:
186 |   Current: gpt-4o-mini → Switch to: gpt-4o
187 | 
188 | Anthropic:
189 |   Current: claude-3-5-haiku → Switch to: claude-3-5-sonnet
190 | 
191 | To change:
192 | 1. Settings → Models
193 | 2. Select model
194 | 3. Try chat again
195 | ```
196 | 
197 | ### Solution 4: Add More Sources
198 | ```
199 | If:  "Response seems incomplete"
200 | Try: Add more relevant sources to provide context
201 | ```
202 | 
203 | ---
204 | 
205 | ## Chat is Very Slow
206 | 
207 | **Symptom:** Chat responses take minutes
208 | 
209 | **Cause:** Large context, slow model, or overloaded API
210 | 
211 | **Solutions:**
212 | 
213 | ### Solution 1: Use Faster Model
214 | ```bash
215 | Fastest: Groq (any model)
216 | Fast: OpenAI gpt-4o-mini
217 | Medium: Anthropic claude-3-5-haiku
218 | Slow: Anthropic claude-3-5-sonnet
219 | 
220 | Switch in: Settings → Models
221 | ```
222 | 
223 | ### Solution 2: Reduce Context
224 | ```
225 | 1. Chat → Select Sources
226 | 2. Uncheck sources you don't need
227 | 3. Or switch to "Summary Only" for background sources
228 | 4. Save and try again
229 | ```
230 | 
231 | ### Solution 3: Increase Timeout
232 | ```bash
233 | # In .env:
234 | API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=600  # 10 minutes
235 | 
236 | # Restart:
237 | docker compose restart
238 | ```
239 | 
240 | ### Solution 4: Check System Load
241 | ```bash
242 | # See if API is overloaded:
243 | docker stats
244 | 
245 | # If CPU >80% or memory >90%:
246 | # Reduce: SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS=2
247 | # Restart: docker compose restart
248 | ```
249 | 
250 | ---
251 | 
252 | ## Chat Doesn't Remember History
253 | 
254 | **Symptom:** Each message treated as separate, no context between questions
255 | 
256 | **Cause:** Chat history not saved or new chat started
257 | 
258 | **Solution:**
259 | 
260 | ```
261 | 1. Make sure you're in same Chat (not new Chat)
262 | 2. Check Chat title at top
263 | 3. If it's blank, start new Chat with a title
264 | 4. Each named Chat keeps its history
265 | 5. If you start new Chat, history is separate
266 | ```
267 | 
268 | ---
269 | 
270 | ## "Rate limit exceeded"
271 | 
272 | **Symptom:** Error: "Rate limit exceeded" or "Too many requests"
273 | 
274 | **Cause:** Hit provider's API rate limit
275 | 
276 | **Solutions:**
277 | 
278 | ### For Cloud Providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)
279 | 
280 | **Immediate:**
281 | - Wait 1-2 minutes
282 | - Try again
283 | 
284 | **Short term:**
285 | - Use cheaper/smaller model
286 | - Reduce concurrent operations
287 | - Space out requests
288 | 
289 | **Long term:**
290 | - Upgrade your account
291 | - Switch to different provider
292 | - Use Ollama (local, no limits)
293 | 
294 | ### Check Account Status
295 | ```
296 | OpenAI: https://platform.openai.com/account/usage/overview
297 | Anthropic: https://console.anthropic.com/account/billing/overview
298 | Google: Google Cloud Console
299 | ```
300 | 
301 | ### For Ollama (Local)
302 | - No rate limits
303 | - Use `ollama pull mistral` for best model
304 | - Restart if hitting resource limits
305 | 
306 | ---
307 | 
308 | ## "Context length exceeded" or "Token limit"
309 | 
310 | **Symptom:** Error about too many tokens
311 | 
312 | **Cause:** Sources too large for model
313 | 
314 | **Solutions:**
315 | 
316 | ### Solution 1: Use Model with Longer Context
317 | ```
318 | Current: GPT-4o (128K tokens) → Switch to: Claude (200K tokens)
319 | Current: Claude Haiku (200K) → Switch to: Gemini (1M tokens)
320 | 
321 | To change: Settings → Models
322 | ```
323 | 
324 | ### Solution 2: Reduce Context
325 | ```
326 | 1. Select fewer sources
327 | 2. Or use "Summary Only" instead of "Full Content"
328 | 3. Or split large documents into smaller pieces
329 | ```
330 | 
331 | ### Solution 3: For Ollama (Local)
332 | ```bash
333 | # Use smaller model:
334 | ollama pull phi  # Very small
335 | # Instead of: ollama pull neural-chat  # Large
336 | ```
337 | 
338 | ---
339 | 
340 | ## "API call failed" or Timeout
341 | 
342 | **Symptom:** Generic API error, response times out
343 | 
344 | **Cause:** Provider API down, network issue, or slow service
345 | 
346 | **Solutions:**
347 | 
348 | ### Check Provider Status
349 | ```
350 | OpenAI: https://status.openai.com/
351 | Anthropic: Check website
352 | Google: Google Cloud Status
353 | Groq: Check website
354 | ```
355 | 
356 | ### Retry Operation
357 | ```
358 | 1. Wait 30 seconds
359 | 2. Try again
360 | ```
361 | 
362 | ### Use Different Model/Provider
363 | ```
364 | 1. Settings → Models
365 | 2. Try different provider
366 | 3. If OpenAI down, use Anthropic
367 | ```
368 | 
369 | ### Check Network
370 | ```bash
371 | # Verify internet working:
372 | ping google.com
373 | 
374 | # Test API endpoint directly:
375 | curl https://api.openai.com/v1/models \
376 |   -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY"
377 | ```
378 | 
379 | ---
380 | 
381 | ## Responses Include Hallucinations
382 | 
383 | **Symptom:** AI makes up facts that aren't in sources
384 | 
385 | **Cause:** Sources not in context, or model guessing
386 | 
387 | **Solutions:**
388 | 
389 | ### Solution 1: Verify Context
390 | ```
391 | 1. Click citation in response
392 | 2. Check source actually says that
393 | 3. If not, sources weren't in context
394 | 4. Add source to context and try again
395 | ```
396 | 
397 | ### Solution 2: Request Citations
398 | ```
399 | Ask: "Answer this with citations to specific pages"
400 | 
401 | The AI will be more careful if asked for citations
402 | ```
403 | 
404 | ### Solution 3: Use Stronger Model
405 | ```
406 | Weaker models hallucinate more
407 | Switch to: GPT-4o or Claude Sonnet
408 | ```
409 | 
410 | ---
411 | 
412 | ## High API Costs
413 | 
414 | **Symptom:** API bills are higher than expected
415 | 
416 | **Cause:** Using expensive model, large context, many requests
417 | 
418 | **Solutions:**
419 | 
420 | ### Use Cheaper Model
421 | ```
422 | Expensive: gpt-4o
423 | Cheaper: gpt-4o-mini (10x cheaper)
424 | 
425 | Expensive: Claude Sonnet
426 | Cheaper: Claude Haiku (5x cheaper)
427 | 
428 | Groq: Ultra cheap but fewer models
429 | ```
430 | 
431 | ### Reduce Context
432 | ```
433 | In Chat:
434 | 1. Select fewer sources
435 | 2. Use "Summary Only" for background
436 | 3. Ask more specific questions
437 | ```
438 | 
439 | ### Switch to Ollama (Free)
440 | ```bash
441 | # Install Ollama
442 | # Run: ollama serve
443 | # Download: ollama pull mistral
444 | # Set: OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://localhost:11434
445 | # Cost: Free!
446 | ```
447 | 
448 | ---
449 | 
450 | ## Still Having Chat Issues?
451 | 
452 | - Try [Quick Fixes](quick-fixes.md)
453 | - Try [Chat Effectively Guide](../3-USER-GUIDE/chat-effectively.md)
454 | - Check logs: `docker compose logs api | grep -i "error"`
455 | - Ask for help: [Troubleshooting Index](index.md#getting-help)
456 |
