/.github/workflows/build-dev.yml:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | name: Development Build
  2 | 
  3 | on:
  4 |   pull_request:
  5 |     branches: [ main ]
  6 |   push:
  7 |     branches: [ main ]
  8 |     paths-ignore:
  9 |       - '**.md'
 10 |       - 'docs/**'
 11 |       - 'notebooks/**'
 12 |       - '.github/workflows/claude*.yml'
 13 |   workflow_dispatch:
 14 |     inputs:
 15 |       platform:
 16 |         description: 'Platform to build'
 17 |         required: true
 18 |         default: 'linux/amd64'
 19 |         type: choice
 20 |         options:
 21 |           - linux/amd64
 22 |           - linux/arm64
 23 |           - linux/amd64,linux/arm64
 24 | 
 25 | permissions:
 26 |   contents: read
 27 |   packages: write
 28 | 
 29 | env:
 30 |   GHCR_IMAGE: ghcr.io/lfnovo/open-notebook
 31 |   DOCKERHUB_IMAGE: lfnovo/open_notebook
 32 | 
 33 | jobs:
 34 |   extract-version:
 35 |     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 36 |     outputs:
 37 |       version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
 38 |       has_dockerhub_secrets: ${{ steps.check.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets }}
 39 |       is_push_to_main: ${{ steps.check.outputs.is_push_to_main }}
 40 |     steps:
 41 |       - name: Checkout
 42 |         uses: actions/checkout@v4
 43 | 
 44 |       - name: Extract version from pyproject.toml
 45 |         id: version
 46 |         run: |
 47 |           VERSION=$(grep -m1 '^version = ' pyproject.toml | cut -d'"' -f2)
 48 |           echo "version=$VERSION" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 49 |           echo "Extracted version: $VERSION"
 50 | 
 51 |       - name: Check environment
 52 |         id: check
 53 |         env:
 54 |           SECRET_DOCKER_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
 55 |           SECRET_DOCKER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}
 56 |         run: |
 57 |           # Check for Docker Hub credentials
 58 |           if [[ -n "$SECRET_DOCKER_USERNAME" && -n "$SECRET_DOCKER_PASSWORD" ]]; then
 59 |             echo "has_dockerhub_secrets=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 60 |             echo "Docker Hub credentials available"
 61 |           else
 62 |             echo "has_dockerhub_secrets=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 63 |             echo "Docker Hub credentials not available"
 64 |           fi
 65 | 
 66 |           # Check if this is a push to main (not a PR)
 67 |           if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "push" && "${{ github.ref }}" == "refs/heads/main" ]]; then
 68 |             echo "is_push_to_main=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 69 |             echo "This is a push to main - will publish v1-dev tags"
 70 |           else
 71 |             echo "is_push_to_main=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 72 |             echo "This is a PR or manual run - test build only"
 73 |           fi
 74 | 
 75 |   build-regular:
 76 |     needs: extract-version
 77 |     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 78 |     steps:
 79 |       - name: Checkout
 80 |         uses: actions/checkout@v4
 81 | 
 82 |       - name: Free up disk space
 83 |         if: needs.extract-version.outputs.is_push_to_main == 'true'
 84 |         run: |
 85 |           sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet
 86 |           sudo rm -rf /usr/local/lib/android
 87 |           sudo rm -rf /opt/ghc
 88 |           sudo rm -rf /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL
 89 |           sudo docker image prune --all --force
 90 |           df -h
 91 | 
 92 |       - name: Set up Docker Buildx
 93 |         uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
 94 | 
 95 |       - name: Login to GitHub Container Registry
 96 |         if: needs.extract-version.outputs.is_push_to_main == 'true'
 97 |         uses: docker/login-action@v3
 98 |         with:
 99 |           registry: ghcr.io
100 |           username: ${{ github.actor }}
101 |           password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
102 | 
103 |       - name: Login to Docker Hub
104 |         if: needs.extract-version.outputs.is_push_to_main == 'true' && needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets == 'true'
105 |         uses: docker/login-action@v3
106 |         with:
107 |           username: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
108 |           password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}
109 | 
110 |       - name: Cache Docker layers
111 |         uses: actions/cache@v3
112 |         with:
113 |           path: /tmp/.buildx-cache-dev
114 |           key: ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-dev-${{ github.sha }}
115 |           restore-keys: |
116 |             ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-dev-
117 | 
118 |       - name: Prepare Docker tags
119 |         id: tags
120 |         run: |
121 |           if [[ "${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.is_push_to_main }}" == "true" ]]; then
122 |             # Push to main: build and push v1-dev tags
123 |             TAGS="${{ env.GHCR_IMAGE }}:v1-dev"
124 |             if [[ "${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets }}" == "true" ]]; then
125 |               TAGS="${TAGS},${{ env.DOCKERHUB_IMAGE }}:v1-dev"
126 |             fi
127 |             echo "tags=${TAGS}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
128 |             echo "push=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
129 |             echo "platforms=linux/amd64,linux/arm64" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
130 |           else
131 |             # PR or manual: test build only
132 |             echo "tags=${{ env.DOCKERHUB_IMAGE }}:${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.version }}-dev" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
133 |             echo "push=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
134 |             echo "platforms=${{ github.event.inputs.platform || 'linux/amd64' }}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
135 |           fi
136 | 
137 |       - name: Build and push regular image
138 |         uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
139 |         with:
140 |           context: .
141 |           file: ./Dockerfile
142 |           platforms: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.platforms }}
143 |           push: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.push }}
144 |           tags: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.tags }}
145 |           cache-from: type=local,src=/tmp/.buildx-cache-dev
146 |           cache-to: type=local,dest=/tmp/.buildx-cache-dev-new,mode=max
147 | 
148 |       - name: Move cache
149 |         run: |
150 |           rm -rf /tmp/.buildx-cache-dev
151 |           mv /tmp/.buildx-cache-dev-new /tmp/.buildx-cache-dev
152 | 
153 |   build-single:
154 |     needs: extract-version
155 |     # Only build single image on push to main
156 |     if: needs.extract-version.outputs.is_push_to_main == 'true'
157 |     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
158 |     steps:
159 |       - name: Checkout
160 |         uses: actions/checkout@v4
161 | 
162 |       - name: Free up disk space
163 |         run: |
164 |           sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet
165 |           sudo rm -rf /usr/local/lib/android
166 |           sudo rm -rf /opt/ghc
167 |           sudo rm -rf /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL
168 |           sudo docker image prune --all --force
169 |           df -h
170 | 
171 |       - name: Set up Docker Buildx
172 |         uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
173 | 
174 |       - name: Login to GitHub Container Registry
175 |         uses: docker/login-action@v3
176 |         with:
177 |           registry: ghcr.io
178 |           username: ${{ github.actor }}
179 |           password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
180 | 
181 |       - name: Login to Docker Hub
182 |         if: needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets == 'true'
183 |         uses: docker/login-action@v3
184 |         with:
185 |           username: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
186 |           password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}
187 | 
188 |       - name: Cache Docker layers
189 |         uses: actions/cache@v3
190 |         with:
191 |           path: /tmp/.buildx-cache-dev-single
192 |           key: ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-dev-single-${{ github.sha }}
193 |           restore-keys: |
194 |             ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-dev-single-
195 | 
196 |       - name: Prepare Docker tags
197 |         id: tags
198 |         run: |
199 |           TAGS="${{ env.GHCR_IMAGE }}:v1-dev-single"
200 |           if [[ "${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets }}" == "true" ]]; then
201 |             TAGS="${TAGS},${{ env.DOCKERHUB_IMAGE }}:v1-dev-single"
202 |           fi
203 |           echo "tags=${TAGS}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
204 | 
205 |       - name: Build and push single-container image
206 |         uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
207 |         with:
208 |           context: .
209 |           file: ./Dockerfile.single
210 |           platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
211 |           push: true
212 |           tags: ${{ steps.tags.outputs.tags }}
213 |           cache-from: type=local,src=/tmp/.buildx-cache-dev-single
214 |           cache-to: type=local,dest=/tmp/.buildx-cache-dev-single-new,mode=max
215 | 
216 |       - name: Move cache
217 |         run: |
218 |           rm -rf /tmp/.buildx-cache-dev-single
219 |           mv /tmp/.buildx-cache-dev-single-new /tmp/.buildx-cache-dev-single
220 | 
221 |   summary:
222 |     needs: [extract-version, build-regular, build-single]
223 |     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
224 |     if: always()
225 |     steps:
226 |       - name: Development Build Summary
227 |         run: |
228 |           echo "## Development Build Summary" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
229 |           echo "**Version:** ${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.version }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
230 |           echo "**Event:** ${{ github.event_name }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
231 |           echo "**Push to Main:** ${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.is_push_to_main }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
232 |           echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
233 | 
234 |           if [[ "${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.is_push_to_main }}" == "true" ]]; then
235 |             echo "### Published Tags:" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
236 | 
237 |             if [[ "${{ needs.build-regular.result }}" == "success" ]]; then
238 |               echo "✅ **Regular:** \`${{ env.GHCR_IMAGE }}:v1-dev\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
239 |               if [[ "${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets }}" == "true" ]]; then
240 |                 echo "✅ **Regular (Docker Hub):** \`${{ env.DOCKERHUB_IMAGE }}:v1-dev\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
241 |               fi
242 |             else
243 |               echo "❌ **Regular:** Build failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
244 |             fi
245 | 
246 |             if [[ "${{ needs.build-single.result }}" == "success" ]]; then
247 |               echo "✅ **Single:** \`${{ env.GHCR_IMAGE }}:v1-dev-single\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
248 |               if [[ "${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets }}" == "true" ]]; then
249 |                 echo "✅ **Single (Docker Hub):** \`${{ env.DOCKERHUB_IMAGE }}:v1-dev-single\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
250 |               fi
251 |             elif [[ "${{ needs.build-single.result }}" == "skipped" ]]; then
252 |               echo "⏭️ **Single:** Skipped" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
253 |             else
254 |               echo "❌ **Single:** Build failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
255 |             fi
256 | 
257 |             echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
258 |             echo "### Platforms:" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
259 |             echo "- linux/amd64" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
260 |             echo "- linux/arm64" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
261 |           else
262 |             echo "### Test Build Results:" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
263 |             if [[ "${{ needs.build-regular.result }}" == "success" ]]; then
264 |               echo "✅ **Dockerfile:** Build successful" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
265 |             else
266 |               echo "❌ **Dockerfile:** Build failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
267 |             fi
268 |             echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
269 |             echo "### Notes:" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
270 |             echo "- This is a test build (no images pushed to registry)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
271 |             echo "- Merge to main to publish \`v1-dev\` tags" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
272 |             echo "- For stable releases, use the 'Build and Release' workflow" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
273 |           fi

  1 | 'use client'
  2 | 
  3 | import { useState, useEffect, useMemo, useCallback } from 'react'
  4 | import { useDebounce } from 'use-debounce'
  5 | import { Search, Link2, LoaderIcon, FileText, Link as LinkIcon, Upload } from 'lucide-react'
  6 | import {
  7 |   Dialog,
  8 |   DialogContent,
  9 |   DialogDescription,
 10 |   DialogHeader,
 11 |   DialogTitle,
 12 |   DialogFooter,
 13 | } from '@/components/ui/dialog'
 14 | import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
 15 | import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'
 16 | import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/checkbox'
 17 | import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge'
 18 | import { ScrollArea } from '@/components/ui/scroll-area'
 19 | import { searchApi } from '@/lib/api/search'
 20 | import { sourcesApi } from '@/lib/api/sources'
 21 | import { useSources, useAddSourcesToNotebook } from '@/lib/hooks/use-sources'
 22 | import { SourceListResponse } from '@/lib/types/api'
 23 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
 24 | 
 25 | interface AddExistingSourceDialogProps {
 26 |   open: boolean
 27 |   onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void
 28 |   notebookId: string
 29 |   onSuccess?: () => void
 30 | }
 31 | 
 32 | export function AddExistingSourceDialog({
 33 |   open,
 34 |   onOpenChange,
 35 |   notebookId,
 36 |   onSuccess,
 37 | }: AddExistingSourceDialogProps) {
 38 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 39 |   const [searchQuery, setSearchQuery] = useState('')
 40 |   const [debouncedSearchQuery] = useDebounce(searchQuery, 300)
 41 |   const [selectedSourceIds, setSelectedSourceIds] = useState<string[]>([])
 42 |   const [allSources, setAllSources] = useState<SourceListResponse[]>([])
 43 |   const [filteredSources, setFilteredSources] = useState<SourceListResponse[]>([])
 44 |   const [isSearching, setIsSearching] = useState(false)
 45 | 
 46 |   // Get sources already in this notebook
 47 |   const { data: currentNotebookSources } = useSources(notebookId)
 48 |   const currentSourceIds = useMemo(
 49 |     () => new Set(currentNotebookSources?.map(s => s.id) || []),
 50 |     [currentNotebookSources]
 51 |   )
 52 | 
 53 |   const addSources = useAddSourcesToNotebook()
 54 | 
 55 |   const loadAllSources = useCallback(async () => {
 56 |     try {
 57 |       setIsSearching(true)
 58 |       // Use sources API directly to get all sources (max 100 per API limit)
 59 |       const sources = await sourcesApi.list({
 60 |         limit: 100,
 61 |         offset: 0,
 62 |         sort_by: 'created',
 63 |         sort_order: 'desc',
 64 |       })
 65 | 
 66 |       setAllSources(sources)
 67 |       setFilteredSources(sources)
 68 |     } catch (error) {
 69 |       console.error('Error loading sources:', error)
 70 |     } finally {
 71 |       setIsSearching(false)
 72 |     }
 73 |   }, [])
 74 | 
 75 |   const performSearch = useCallback(async () => {
 76 |     if (!debouncedSearchQuery.trim()) {
 77 |       // Empty query - show all sources
 78 |       setFilteredSources(allSources)
 79 |       setIsSearching(false)
 80 |       return
 81 |     }
 82 | 
 83 |     try {
 84 |       setIsSearching(true)
 85 |       const response = await searchApi.search({
 86 |         query: debouncedSearchQuery,
 87 |         type: 'text',
 88 |         search_sources: true,
 89 |         search_notes: false,
 90 |         limit: 100,
 91 |         minimum_score: 0.01,
 92 |       })
 93 | 
 94 |       // Since we set search_sources=true and search_notes=false,
 95 |       // the API only returns sources, no need to filter
 96 |       const sources = response.results.map(r => ({
 97 |         id: r.parent_id,
 98 |         title: r.title || 'Untitled',
 99 |         topics: [],
100 |         asset: null,
101 |         embedded: false,
102 |         embedded_chunks: 0,
103 |         insights_count: 0,
104 |         created: r.created,
105 |         updated: r.updated,
106 |       })) as SourceListResponse[]
107 | 
108 |       setFilteredSources(sources)
109 |     } catch (error) {
110 |       console.error('Error searching sources:', error)
111 |       // On error, fall back to showing all sources
112 |       setFilteredSources(allSources)
113 |     } finally {
114 |       setIsSearching(false)
115 |     }
116 |   }, [debouncedSearchQuery, allSources])
117 | 
118 |   // Load all sources initially
119 |   useEffect(() => {
120 |     if (open) {
121 |       loadAllSources()
122 |     }
123 |   }, [open, loadAllSources])
124 | 
125 |   // Filter sources when search query changes
126 |   useEffect(() => {
127 |     if (!debouncedSearchQuery) {
128 |       setFilteredSources(allSources)
129 |       setIsSearching(false)
130 |       return
131 |     }
132 | 
133 |     performSearch()
134 |   }, [debouncedSearchQuery, allSources, performSearch])
135 | 
136 |   const handleToggleSource = (sourceId: string) => {
137 |     setSelectedSourceIds(prev =>
138 |       prev.includes(sourceId)
139 |         ? prev.filter(id => id !== sourceId)
140 |         : [...prev, sourceId]
141 |     )
142 |   }
143 | 
144 |   const handleAddSelected = async () => {
145 |     if (selectedSourceIds.length === 0) return
146 | 
147 |     try {
148 |       await addSources.mutateAsync({
149 |         notebookId,
150 |         sourceIds: selectedSourceIds,
151 |       })
152 | 
153 |       // Reset state
154 |       setSelectedSourceIds([])
155 |       setSearchQuery('')
156 |       onOpenChange(false)
157 |       onSuccess?.()
158 |     } catch (error) {
159 |       // Error handled by the hook's onError
160 |       console.error('Error adding sources:', error)
161 |     }
162 |   }
163 | 
164 |   const getSourceIcon = (source: SourceListResponse) => {
165 |     // Derive type from asset
166 |     if (source.asset?.url) {
167 |       return <LinkIcon className="h-4 w-4" />
168 |     }
169 |     if (source.asset?.file_path) {
170 |       return <Upload className="h-4 w-4" />
171 |     }
172 |     return <FileText className="h-4 w-4" />
173 |   }
174 | 
175 |   const formatDate = (dateString: string) => {
176 |     try {
177 |       return new Date(dateString).toLocaleDateString()
178 |     } catch {
179 |       return ''
180 |     }
181 |   }
182 | 
183 |   return (
184 |     <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>
185 |       <DialogContent className="max-w-2xl sm:max-w-2xl max-h-[80vh] overflow-hidden flex flex-col">
186 |         <DialogHeader>
187 |           <DialogTitle className="flex items-center gap-2">
188 |             <Link2 className="h-5 w-5" />
189 |             {t.sources.addExistingTitle}
190 |           </DialogTitle>
191 |           <DialogDescription>
192 |             {t.sources.addExistingDesc}
193 |           </DialogDescription>
194 |         </DialogHeader>
195 | 
196 |         <div className="space-y-4 flex-1 overflow-hidden flex flex-col">
197 |           {/* Search Input */}
198 |           <div className="relative">
199 |             <Search className="absolute left-3 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 h-4 w-4 text-muted-foreground" />
200 |             <Input
201 |               placeholder={t.sources.searchPlaceholder}
202 |               value={searchQuery}
203 |               onChange={(e) => setSearchQuery(e.target.value)}
204 |               className="pl-10"
205 |             />
206 |             {isSearching && (
207 |               <LoaderIcon className="absolute right-3 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 h-4 w-4 animate-spin text-muted-foreground" />
208 |             )}
209 |           </div>
210 | 
211 |           {/* Source List */}
212 |           <ScrollArea className="h-[400px] border rounded-md">
213 |             {isSearching && filteredSources.length === 0 ? (
214 |               <div className="flex flex-col items-center justify-center h-[200px] text-muted-foreground">
215 |                 <LoaderIcon className="h-12 w-12 mb-2 animate-spin" />
216 |                 <p>{t.common.loading}</p>
217 |               </div>
218 |             ) : filteredSources.length === 0 ? (
219 |               <div className="flex flex-col items-center justify-center h-[200px] text-muted-foreground">
220 |                 <FileText className="h-12 w-12 mb-2 opacity-50" />
221 |                 <p>{t.sources.noNotebooksFound}</p>
222 |               </div>
223 |             ) : (
224 |               <div className="space-y-2 p-4">
225 |                 {filteredSources.map((source) => {
226 |                   const isAlreadyLinked = currentSourceIds.has(source.id)
227 |                   const isSelected = selectedSourceIds.includes(source.id)
228 | 
229 |                   return (
230 |                     <div
231 |                       key={source.id}
232 |                       className={`flex items-start gap-3 p-3 rounded-lg border transition-colors min-w-0 ${
233 |                         isSelected ? 'bg-accent border-accent-foreground/20' : 'hover:bg-accent/50'
234 |                       }`}
235 |                     >
236 |                       <Checkbox
237 |                         checked={isSelected}
238 |                         onCheckedChange={() => handleToggleSource(source.id)}
239 |                         disabled={isAlreadyLinked}
240 |                         className="mt-1"
241 |                       />
242 |                       <div className="flex-1 min-w-0">
243 |                         <div className="flex items-start gap-2 mb-1">
244 |                           <div className="shrink-0 mt-0.5">
245 |                             {getSourceIcon(source)}
246 |                           </div>
247 |                           <h4 className="font-medium text-sm break-words line-clamp-2 flex-1 min-w-0">
248 |                             {source.title}
249 |                           </h4>
250 |                           {isAlreadyLinked && (
251 |                             <Badge variant="secondary" className="text-xs shrink-0">
252 |                               {t.common.linked}
253 |                             </Badge>
254 |                           )}
255 |                         </div>
256 |                         <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground truncate">
257 |                           {t.sources.added.replace('{date}', formatDate(source.created))}
258 |                         </p>
259 |                       </div>
260 |                     </div>
261 |                   )
262 |                 })}
263 |               </div>
264 |             )}
265 |           </ScrollArea>
266 | 
267 |           {/* Truncation Warning */}
268 |           {allSources.length >= 100 && !debouncedSearchQuery && (
269 |             <div className="text-xs text-muted-foreground bg-muted/50 p-2 rounded-md">
270 |               {t.sources.showingFirst100}
271 |             </div>
272 |           )}
273 | 
274 |           {/* Selection Summary */}
275 |           {selectedSourceIds.length > 0 && (
276 |             <div className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
277 |               {t.sources.selectedCount.replace('{count}', selectedSourceIds.length.toString())}
278 |             </div>
279 |           )}
280 |         </div>
281 | 
282 |         <DialogFooter>
283 |           <Button
284 |             variant="outline"
285 |             onClick={() => onOpenChange(false)}
286 |             disabled={addSources.isPending}
287 |           >
288 |             {t.common.cancel}
289 |           </Button>
290 |           <Button
291 |             onClick={handleAddSelected}
292 |             disabled={selectedSourceIds.length === 0 || addSources.isPending}
293 |           >
294 |             {addSources.isPending ? (
295 |               <>
296 |                 <LoaderIcon className="mr-2 h-4 w-4 animate-spin" />
297 |                 {t.common.adding}
298 |               </>
299 |             ) : (
300 |               <>{t.common.addSelected}</>
301 |             )}
302 |           </Button>
303 |         </DialogFooter>
304 |       </DialogContent>
305 |     </Dialog>
306 |   )
307 | }
308 |

 35 | const getNavigationItems = (t: TranslationKeys) => [

 39 |   { name: t.navigation.podcasts, href: '/podcasts', icon: Mic, keywords: ['audio', 'episodes', 'generate'] },
 40 |   { name: t.navigation.models, href: '/models', icon: Bot, keywords: ['ai', 'llm', 'providers', 'openai', 'anthropic'] },
 41 |   { name: t.navigation.transformations, href: '/transformations', icon: Shuffle, keywords: ['prompts', 'templates', 'actions'] },
 42 |   { name: t.navigation.settings, href: '/settings', icon: Settings, keywords: ['preferences', 'config', 'options'] },
 43 |   { name: t.navigation.advanced, href: '/advanced', icon: Wrench, keywords: ['debug', 'system', 'tools'] },
 44 | ]

 46 | const getCreateItems = (t: TranslationKeys) => [
 47 |   { name: t.common.newSource, action: 'source', icon: FileText },
 48 |   { name: t.common.newNotebook, action: 'notebook', icon: Book },
 49 |   { name: t.common.newPodcast, action: 'podcast', icon: Mic },
 50 | ]
 51 | 
 52 | const getThemeItems = (t: TranslationKeys) => [
 53 |   { name: t.common.light, value: 'light' as const, icon: Sun, keywords: ['bright', 'day'] },
 54 |   { name: t.common.dark, value: 'dark' as const, icon: Moon, keywords: ['night'] },
 55 |   { name: t.common.system, value: 'system' as const, icon: Monitor, keywords: ['auto', 'default'] },
 56 | ]
 57 | 
 58 | export function CommandPalette() {
 59 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 60 |   const commandInputId = useId()
 61 |   const navigationItems = useMemo(() => getNavigationItems(t), [t])
 62 |   const createItems = useMemo(() => getCreateItems(t), [t])
 63 |   const themeItems = useMemo(() => getThemeItems(t), [t])
 64 |   
 65 |   const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
 66 |   const [query, setQuery] = useState('')
 67 |   const router = useRouter()
 68 |   const { openSourceDialog, openNotebookDialog, openPodcastDialog } = useCreateDialogs()
 69 |   const { setTheme } = useTheme()
 70 |   const { data: notebooks, isLoading: notebooksLoading } = useNotebooks(false)
 71 | 
 72 |   // Global keyboard listener for ⌘K / Ctrl+K
 73 |   useEffect(() => {
 74 |     const down = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
 75 |       // Skip if focus is inside editable elements
 76 |       const target = e.target as HTMLElement | null
 77 |       if (
 78 |         target &&
 79 |         (target.isContentEditable ||
 80 |           ['INPUT', 'TEXTAREA', 'SELECT'].includes(target.tagName))
 81 |       ) {
 82 |         return
 83 |       }
 84 | 
 85 |       if (e.key === 'k' && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey)) {
 86 |         e.preventDefault()
 87 |         e.stopPropagation()
 88 |         setOpen((open) => !open)
 89 |       }
 90 |     }
 91 | 
 92 |     // Use capture phase to intercept before other handlers
 93 |     document.addEventListener('keydown', down, true)
 94 |     return () => document.removeEventListener('keydown', down, true)
 95 |   }, [])
 96 | 
 97 |   // Reset query when dialog closes
 98 |   useEffect(() => {
 99 |     if (!open) {
100 |       setQuery('')
101 |     }
102 |   }, [open])
103 | 
104 |   const handleSelect = useCallback((callback: () => void) => {
105 |     setOpen(false)
106 |     setQuery('')
107 |     // Use setTimeout to ensure dialog closes before action
108 |     setTimeout(callback, 0)
109 |   }, [])
110 | 
111 |   const handleNavigate = useCallback((href: string) => {
112 |     handleSelect(() => router.push(href))
113 |   }, [handleSelect, router])
114 | 
115 |   const handleSearch = useCallback(() => {
116 |     if (!query.trim()) return
117 |     handleSelect(() => router.push(`/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&mode=search`))
118 |   }, [handleSelect, router, query])
119 | 
120 |   const handleAsk = useCallback(() => {
121 |     if (!query.trim()) return
122 |     handleSelect(() => router.push(`/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&mode=ask`))
123 |   }, [handleSelect, router, query])
124 | 
125 |   const handleCreate = useCallback((action: string) => {
126 |     handleSelect(() => {
127 |       if (action === 'source') openSourceDialog()
128 |       else if (action === 'notebook') openNotebookDialog()
129 |       else if (action === 'podcast') openPodcastDialog()
130 |     })
131 |   }, [handleSelect, openSourceDialog, openNotebookDialog, openPodcastDialog])
132 | 
133 |   const handleTheme = useCallback((theme: 'light' | 'dark' | 'system') => {
134 |     handleSelect(() => setTheme(theme))
135 |   }, [handleSelect, setTheme])
136 | 
137 |   // Check if query matches any command (navigation, create, theme, or notebook)
138 |   const queryLower = query.toLowerCase().trim()
139 |   const hasCommandMatch = useMemo(() => {
140 |     if (!queryLower) return false
141 |     return (
142 |       navigationItems.some(item =>
143 |         item.name.toLowerCase().includes(queryLower) ||
144 |         item.keywords.some(k => k.includes(queryLower))
145 |       ) ||
146 |       createItems.some(item =>
147 |         item.name.toLowerCase().includes(queryLower)
148 |       ) ||
149 |       themeItems.some(item =>
150 |         item.name.toLowerCase().includes(queryLower) ||
151 |         item.keywords.some(k => k.includes(queryLower))
152 |       ) ||
153 |       (notebooks?.some(nb =>
154 |         nb.name.toLowerCase().includes(queryLower) ||
155 |         (nb.description && nb.description.toLowerCase().includes(queryLower))
156 |       ) ?? false)
157 |     )
158 |   }, [queryLower, notebooks, navigationItems, createItems, themeItems])
159 | 
160 |   // Determine if we should show the Search/Ask section at the top
161 |   const showSearchFirst = query.trim() && !hasCommandMatch
162 | 
163 |   return (
164 |     <CommandDialog
165 |       open={open}
166 |       onOpenChange={setOpen}
167 |       title={t.common.quickActions}
168 |       description={t.common.quickActionsDesc}
169 |       className="sm:max-w-lg"
170 |     >
171 |       <CommandInput
172 |         id={commandInputId}
173 |         name="command-search"
174 |         placeholder={t.searchPage.enterSearchPlaceholder}
175 |         value={query}
176 |         onValueChange={setQuery}
177 |         aria-label={t.common.search}
178 |         autoComplete="off"
179 |       />
180 |       <CommandList>
181 |         {/* Search/Ask - show FIRST when there's a query with no command match */}
182 |         {showSearchFirst && (
183 |           <CommandGroup heading={t.searchPage.searchAndAsk} forceMount>
184 |             <CommandItem
185 |               value={`__search__ ${query}`}
186 |               onSelect={handleSearch}
187 |               forceMount
188 |             >
189 |               <Search className="h-4 w-4" />
190 |               <span>{t.searchPage.searchResultsFor.replace('{query}', query)}</span>
191 |             </CommandItem>
192 |             <CommandItem
193 |               value={`__ask__ ${query}`}
194 |               onSelect={handleAsk}
195 |               forceMount
196 |             >
197 |               <MessageCircleQuestion className="h-4 w-4" />
198 |               <span>{t.searchPage.askAbout.replace('{query}', query)}</span>
199 |             </CommandItem>
200 |           </CommandGroup>
201 |         )}
202 | 
203 |         {/* Navigation */}
204 |         <CommandGroup heading={t.navigation.nav}>
205 |           {navigationItems.map((item) => (
206 |             <CommandItem
207 |               key={item.href}
208 |               value={`${item.name} ${item.keywords.join(' ')}`}
209 |               onSelect={() => handleNavigate(item.href)}
210 |             >
211 |               <item.icon className="h-4 w-4" />
212 |               <span>{item.name}</span>
213 |             </CommandItem>
214 |           ))}
215 |         </CommandGroup>
216 | 
217 |         {/* Notebooks */}
218 |         <CommandGroup heading={t.notebooks.title}>
219 |           {notebooksLoading ? (
220 |             <CommandItem disabled>
221 |               <Loader2 className="h-4 w-4 animate-spin" />
222 |               <span>{t.common.loading}</span>
223 |             </CommandItem>
224 |           ) : notebooks && notebooks.length > 0 ? (
225 |             notebooks.map((notebook) => (
226 |               <CommandItem
227 |                 key={notebook.id}
228 |                 value={`notebook ${notebook.name} ${notebook.description || ''}`}
229 |                 onSelect={() => handleNavigate(`/notebooks/${notebook.id}`)}
230 |               >
231 |                 <Book className="h-4 w-4" />
232 |                 <span>{notebook.name}</span>
233 |               </CommandItem>
234 |             ))
235 |           ) : null}
236 |         </CommandGroup>
237 | 
238 |         {/* Create */}
239 |         <CommandGroup heading={t.navigation.create}>
240 |           {createItems.map((item) => (
241 |             <CommandItem
242 |               key={item.action}
243 |               value={`create ${item.name}`}
244 |               onSelect={() => handleCreate(item.action)}
245 |             >
246 |               <Plus className="h-4 w-4" />
247 |               <span>{item.name}</span>
248 |             </CommandItem>
249 |           ))}
250 |         </CommandGroup>
251 | 
252 |         {/* Theme */}
253 |         <CommandGroup heading={t.navigation.theme}>
254 |           {themeItems.map((item) => (
255 |             <CommandItem
256 |               key={item.value}
257 |               value={`theme ${item.name} ${item.keywords.join(' ')}`}
258 |               onSelect={() => handleTheme(item.value)}
259 |             >
260 |               <item.icon className="h-4 w-4" />
261 |               <span>{item.name}</span>
262 |             </CommandItem>
263 |           ))}
264 |         </CommandGroup>
265 | 
266 |         {/* Search/Ask - show at bottom when there IS a command match */}
267 |         {query.trim() && hasCommandMatch && (
268 |           <>
269 |             <CommandSeparator />
270 |             <CommandGroup heading={t.searchPage.orSearchKb} forceMount>
271 |               <CommandItem
272 |                 value={`__search__ ${query}`}
273 |                 onSelect={handleSearch}
274 |                 forceMount
275 |               >
276 |                 <Search className="h-4 w-4" />
277 |                 <span>{t.searchPage.searchResultsFor.replace('{query}', query)}</span>
278 |               </CommandItem>
279 |               <CommandItem
280 |                 value={`__ask__ ${query}`}
281 |                 onSelect={handleAsk}
282 |                 forceMount
283 |               >
284 |                 <MessageCircleQuestion className="h-4 w-4" />
285 |                 <span>{t.searchPage.askAbout.replace('{query}', query)}</span>
286 |               </CommandItem>
287 |             </CommandGroup>
288 |           </>
289 |         )}
290 |       </CommandList>
291 |     </CommandDialog>
292 |   )
293 | }
294 |

/README.dev.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Developer Guide
  2 | 
  3 | This guide is for developers working on Open Notebook. For end-user documentation, see [README.md](README.md) and [docs/](docs/).
  4 | 
  5 | ## Quick Start for Development
  6 | 
  7 | ```bash
  8 | # 1. Clone and setup
  9 | git clone https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook.git
 10 | cd open-notebook
 11 | 
 12 | # 2. Copy environment files
 13 | cp .env.example .env
 14 | cp .env.example docker.env
 15 | 
 16 | # 3. Install dependencies
 17 | uv sync
 18 | 
 19 | # 4. Start all services (recommended for development)
 20 | make start-all
 21 | ```
 22 | 
 23 | ## Development Workflows
 24 | 
 25 | ### When to Use What?
 26 | 
 27 | | Workflow | Use Case | Speed | Production Parity |
 28 | |----------|----------|-------|-------------------|
 29 | | **Local Services** (`make start-all`) | Day-to-day development, fastest iteration | ⚡⚡⚡ Fast | Medium |
 30 | | **Docker Compose** (`make dev`) | Testing containerized setup | ⚡⚡ Medium | High |
 31 | | **Local Docker Build** (`make docker-build-local`) | Testing Dockerfile changes | ⚡ Slow | Very High |
 32 | | **Multi-platform Build** (`make docker-push`) | Publishing releases | 🐌 Very Slow | Exact |
 33 | 
 34 | ---
 35 | 
 36 | ## 1. Local Development (Recommended)
 37 | 
 38 | **Best for:** Daily development, hot reload, debugging
 39 | 
 40 | ### Setup
 41 | 
 42 | ```bash
 43 | # Start database
 44 | make database
 45 | 
 46 | # Start all services (DB + API + Worker + Frontend)
 47 | make start-all
 48 | ```
 49 | 
 50 | ### What This Does
 51 | 
 52 | 1. Starts SurrealDB in Docker (port 8000)
 53 | 2. Starts FastAPI backend (port 5055)
 54 | 3. Starts background worker (surreal-commands)
 55 | 4. Starts Next.js frontend (port 3000)
 56 | 
 57 | ### Individual Services
 58 | 
 59 | ```bash
 60 | # Just the database
 61 | make database
 62 | 
 63 | # Just the API
 64 | make api
 65 | 
 66 | # Just the frontend
 67 | make frontend
 68 | 
 69 | # Just the worker
 70 | make worker
 71 | ```
 72 | 
 73 | ### Checking Status
 74 | 
 75 | ```bash
 76 | # See what's running
 77 | make status
 78 | 
 79 | # Stop everything
 80 | make stop-all
 81 | ```
 82 | 
 83 | ### Advantages
 84 | - ✅ Fastest iteration (hot reload)
 85 | - ✅ Easy debugging (direct process access)
 86 | - ✅ Low resource usage
 87 | - ✅ Direct log access
 88 | 
 89 | ### Disadvantages
 90 | - ❌ Doesn't test Docker build
 91 | - ❌ Environment may differ from production
 92 | - ❌ Requires local Python/Node setup
 93 | 
 94 | ---
 95 | 
 96 | ## 2. Docker Compose Development
 97 | 
 98 | **Best for:** Testing containerized setup, CI/CD verification
 99 | 
100 | ```bash
101 | # Start with dev profile
102 | make dev
103 | 
104 | # Or full stack
105 | make full
106 | ```
107 | 
108 | ### Configuration Files
109 | 
110 | - `docker-compose.dev.yml` - Development setup
111 | - `docker-compose.full.yml` - Full stack setup
112 | - `docker-compose.yml` - Base configuration
113 | 
114 | ### Advantages
115 | - ✅ Closer to production environment
116 | - ✅ Isolated dependencies
117 | - ✅ Easy to share exact environment
118 | 
119 | ### Disadvantages
120 | - ❌ Slower rebuilds
121 | - ❌ More complex debugging
122 | - ❌ Higher resource usage
123 | 
124 | ---
125 | 
126 | ## 3. Testing Production Docker Images
127 | 
128 | **Best for:** Verifying Dockerfile changes before publishing
129 | 
130 | ### Build Locally
131 | 
132 | ```bash
133 | # Build production image for your platform only
134 | make docker-build-local
135 | ```
136 | 
137 | This creates two tags:
138 | - `lfnovo/open_notebook:<version>` (from pyproject.toml)
139 | - `lfnovo/open_notebook:local`
140 | 
141 | ### Run Locally
142 | 
143 | ```bash
144 | docker run -p 5055:5055 -p 3000:3000 lfnovo/open_notebook:local
145 | ```
146 | 
147 | ### When to Use
148 | - ✅ Before pushing to registry
149 | - ✅ Testing Dockerfile changes
150 | - ✅ Debugging production-specific issues
151 | - ✅ Verifying build process
152 | 
153 | ---
154 | 
155 | ## 4. Publishing Docker Images
156 | 
157 | ### Workflow
158 | 
159 | ```bash
160 | # 1. Test locally first
161 | make docker-build-local
162 | 
163 | # 2. If successful, push version tag (no latest update)
164 | make docker-push
165 | 
166 | # 3. Test the pushed version in staging/production
167 | 
168 | # 4. When ready, promote to latest
169 | make docker-push-latest
170 | ```
171 | 
172 | ### Available Commands
173 | 
174 | | Command | What It Does | Updates Latest? |
175 | |---------|--------------|-----------------|
176 | | `make docker-build-local` | Build for current platform only | No registry push |
177 | | `make docker-push` | Push version tags to registries | ❌ No |
178 | | `make docker-push-latest` | Push version + update v1-latest | ✅ Yes |
179 | | `make docker-release` | Full release (same as docker-push-latest) | ✅ Yes |
180 | 
181 | ### Publishing Details
182 | 
183 | - **Platforms:** `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`
184 | - **Registries:** Docker Hub + GitHub Container Registry
185 | - **Image Variants:** Regular + Single-container (`-single`)
186 | - **Version Source:** `pyproject.toml`
187 | 
188 | ### Creating Git Tags
189 | 
190 | ```bash
191 | # Create and push git tag matching pyproject.toml version
192 | make tag
193 | ```
194 | 
195 | ---
196 | 
197 | ## Code Quality
198 | 
199 | ```bash
200 | # Run linter with auto-fix
201 | make ruff
202 | 
203 | # Run type checking
204 | make lint
205 | 
206 | # Run tests
207 | uv run pytest tests/
208 | 
209 | # Clean cache directories
210 | make clean-cache
211 | ```
212 | 
213 | ---
214 | 
215 | ## Common Development Tasks
216 | 
217 | ### Adding a New Feature
218 | 
219 | 1. Create feature branch
220 | 2. Develop using `make start-all`
221 | 3. Write tests
222 | 4. Run `make ruff` and `make lint`
223 | 5. Test with `make docker-build-local`
224 | 6. Create PR
225 | 
226 | ### Fixing a Bug
227 | 
228 | 1. Reproduce locally with `make start-all`
229 | 2. Add test case demonstrating bug
230 | 3. Fix the bug
231 | 4. Verify test passes
232 | 5. Check with `make docker-build-local`
233 | 
234 | ### Updating Dependencies
235 | 
236 | ```bash
237 | # Add Python dependency
238 | uv add package-name
239 | 
240 | # Update dependencies
241 | uv sync
242 | 
243 | # Frontend dependencies
244 | cd frontend && npm install package-name
245 | ```
246 | 
247 | ### Adding a New Language (i18n)
248 | 
249 | Open Notebook supports internationalization. To add a new language:
250 | 
251 | 1. **Create locale file**: Copy an existing locale as template
252 |    ```bash
253 |    cp frontend/src/lib/locales/en-US/index.ts frontend/src/lib/locales/pt-BR/index.ts
254 |    ```
255 | 
256 | 2. **Translate all strings** in the new file. The structure includes:
257 |    - `common`: Shared UI elements (buttons, labels)
258 |    - `notebooks`, `sources`, `notes`: Feature-specific strings
259 |    - `chat`, `search`, `podcasts`: Module-specific strings
260 |    - `apiErrors`: Error message translations
261 | 
262 | 3. **Register the locale** in `frontend/src/lib/locales/index.ts`:
263 |    ```typescript
264 |    import { ptBR } from './pt-BR'
265 | 
266 |    export const locales = {
267 |      'en-US': enUS,
268 |      'zh-CN': zhCN,
269 |      'zh-TW': zhTW,
270 |      'pt-BR': ptBR,  // Add your locale
271 |    }
272 |    ```
273 | 
274 | 4. **Add date-fns locale** in `frontend/src/lib/utils/date-locale.ts`:
275 |    ```typescript
276 |    import { zhCN, enUS, zhTW, ptBR } from 'date-fns/locale'
277 | 
278 |    const LOCALE_MAP: Record<string, Locale> = {
279 |      'zh-CN': zhCN,
280 |      'zh-TW': zhTW,
281 |      'en-US': enUS,
282 |      'pt-BR': ptBR,  // Add your locale
283 |    }
284 |    ```
285 | 
286 | 5. **Test**: Switch languages using the language toggle in the UI header.
287 | 
288 | ### Database Migrations
289 | 
290 | Database migrations run **automatically** when the API starts.
291 | 
292 | 1. Create migration file: `migrations/XXX_description.surql`
293 | 2. Write SurrealQL schema changes
294 | 3. (Optional) Create rollback: `migrations/XXX_description_down.surql`
295 | 4. Restart API - migration runs on startup
296 | 
297 | ---
298 | 
299 | ## Troubleshooting
300 | 
301 | ### Services Won't Start
302 | 
303 | ```bash
304 | # Check status
305 | make status
306 | 
307 | # Check database
308 | docker compose ps surrealdb
309 | 
310 | # View logs
311 | docker compose logs surrealdb
312 | 
313 | # Restart everything
314 | make stop-all
315 | make start-all
316 | ```
317 | 
318 | ### Port Already in Use
319 | 
320 | ```bash
321 | # Find process using port
322 | lsof -i :5055
323 | lsof -i :3000
324 | lsof -i :8000
325 | 
326 | # Kill stuck processes
327 | make stop-all
328 | ```
329 | 
330 | ### Database Connection Issues
331 | 
332 | ```bash
333 | # Verify SurrealDB is running
334 | docker compose ps surrealdb
335 | 
336 | # Check connection settings in .env
337 | cat .env | grep SURREAL
338 | ```
339 | 
340 | ### Docker Build Fails
341 | 
342 | ```bash
343 | # Clean Docker cache
344 | docker builder prune
345 | 
346 | # Reset buildx
347 | make docker-buildx-reset
348 | 
349 | # Try local build first
350 | make docker-build-local
351 | ```
352 | 
353 | ---
354 | 
355 | ## Project Structure
356 | 
357 | ```
358 | open-notebook/
359 | ├── api/                    # FastAPI backend
360 | ├── frontend/               # Next.js React frontend
361 | ├── open_notebook/          # Python core library
362 | │   ├── domain/            # Domain models
363 | │   ├── graphs/            # LangGraph workflows
364 | │   ├── ai/                # AI provider integration
365 | │   └── database/          # SurrealDB operations
366 | ├── migrations/             # Database migrations
367 | ├── tests/                  # Test suite
368 | ├── docs/                   # User documentation
369 | └── Makefile               # Development commands
370 | ```
371 | 
372 | See component-specific CLAUDE.md files for detailed architecture:
373 | - [frontend/CLAUDE.md](frontend/CLAUDE.md)
374 | - [api/CLAUDE.md](api/CLAUDE.md)
375 | - [open_notebook/CLAUDE.md](open_notebook/CLAUDE.md)
376 | 
377 | ---
378 | 
379 | ## Environment Variables
380 | 
381 | ### Required for Local Development
382 | 
383 | ```bash
384 | # .env file
385 | SURREAL_URL=ws://localhost:8000
386 | SURREAL_USER=root
387 | SURREAL_PASS=root
388 | SURREAL_DB=open_notebook
389 | SURREAL_NS=production
390 | 
391 | # AI Provider (at least one required)
392 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
393 | # OR
394 | ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
395 | # OR configure other providers (see docs/5-CONFIGURATION/)
396 | ```
397 | 
398 | See [docs/5-CONFIGURATION/](docs/5-CONFIGURATION/) for complete configuration guide.
399 | 
400 | ---
401 | 
402 | ## Performance Tips
403 | 
404 | ### Speed Up Local Development
405 | 
406 | 1. **Use `make start-all`** instead of Docker for daily work
407 | 2. **Keep SurrealDB running** between sessions (`make database`)
408 | 3. **Use `make docker-build-local`** only when testing Dockerfile changes
409 | 4. **Skip multi-platform builds** until ready to publish
410 | 
411 | ### Reduce Resource Usage
412 | 
413 | ```bash
414 | # Stop unused services
415 | make stop-all
416 | 
417 | # Clean up Docker
418 | docker system prune -a
419 | 
420 | # Clean Python cache
421 | make clean-cache
422 | ```
423 | 
424 | ---
425 | 
426 | ## TODO: Sections to Add
427 | 
428 | - [ ] Frontend development guide (hot reload, component structure)
429 | - [ ] API development guide (adding endpoints, services)
430 | - [ ] LangGraph workflow development
431 | - [ ] Testing strategy and coverage
432 | - [ ] Debugging tips (VSCode/PyCharm setup)
433 | - [ ] CI/CD pipeline overview
434 | - [ ] Release process checklist
435 | - [ ] Common error messages and solutions
436 | 
437 | ---
438 | 
439 | ## Resources
440 | 
441 | - **Documentation:** https://open-notebook.ai
442 | - **Discord:** https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w
443 | - **Issues:** https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook/issues
444 | - **Contributing:** [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)
445 | - **Maintainer Guide:** [MAINTAINER_GUIDE.md](MAINTAINER_GUIDE.md)
446 | 
447 | ---
448 | 
449 | **Last Updated:** January 2025
450 |

/.env.example:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | 
  2 | # API CONFIGURATION
  3 | # URL where the API can be accessed by the browser
  4 | # This setting allows the frontend to connect to the API at runtime (no rebuild needed!)
  5 | #
  6 | # IMPORTANT: Do NOT include /api at the end - it will be added automatically!
  7 | #
  8 | # Common scenarios:
  9 | # - Docker on localhost: http://localhost:5055 (default, works for most cases)
 10 | # - Docker on LAN/remote server: http://192.168.1.100:5055 or http://your-server-ip:5055
 11 | # - Behind reverse proxy with custom domain: https://your-domain.com
 12 | # - Behind reverse proxy with subdomain: https://api.your-domain.com
 13 | #
 14 | # Examples for reverse proxy users:
 15 | # - API_URL=https://notebook.example.com  (frontend will call https://notebook.example.com/api/*)
 16 | # - API_URL=https://api.example.com       (frontend will call https://api.example.com/api/*)
 17 | #
 18 | # Note: If not set, the system will auto-detect based on the incoming request.
 19 | # Only set this if you need to override the auto-detection (e.g., reverse proxy scenarios).
 20 | API_URL=http://localhost:5055
 21 | 
 22 | # INTERNAL API URL (Server-Side)
 23 | # URL where Next.js server-side should proxy API requests (via rewrites)
 24 | # This is DIFFERENT from API_URL which is used by the browser client
 25 | #
 26 | # INTERNAL_API_URL is used by Next.js rewrites to forward /api/* requests to the FastAPI backend
 27 | # API_URL is used by the browser to know where to make API calls
 28 | #
 29 | # Default: http://localhost:5055 (single-container deployment - both services on same host)
 30 | # Override for multi-container: INTERNAL_API_URL=http://api-service:5055
 31 | #
 32 | # Common scenarios:
 33 | # - Single container (default): Don't set - defaults to http://localhost:5055
 34 | # - Multi-container Docker Compose: INTERNAL_API_URL=http://api:5055 (use service name)
 35 | # - Kubernetes/advanced networking: INTERNAL_API_URL=http://api-service.namespace.svc.cluster.local:5055
 36 | #
 37 | # Why two variables?
 38 | # - API_URL: External/public URL that browsers use (can be https://your-domain.com)
 39 | # - INTERNAL_API_URL: Internal container networking URL (usually http://localhost:5055 or service name)
 40 | #
 41 | # INTERNAL_API_URL=http://localhost:5055
 42 | 
 43 | # API CLIENT TIMEOUT (in seconds)
 44 | # Controls how long the frontend/Streamlit UI waits for API responses
 45 | # Increase this if you're using slow AI providers or hardware (Ollama on CPU, remote LM Studio, etc.)
 46 | # Default: 300 seconds (5 minutes) - sufficient for most transformation/insight operations
 47 | #
 48 | # Common scenarios:
 49 | # - Fast cloud APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic): 300 seconds is more than enough
 50 | # - Local Ollama on GPU: 300 seconds should work fine
 51 | # - Local Ollama on CPU: Consider 600 seconds (10 minutes) or more
 52 | # - Remote LM Studio over slow network: Consider 900 seconds (15 minutes)
 53 | # - Very large documents: May need 900+ seconds
 54 | #
 55 | # API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=300
 56 | 
 57 | # ESPERANTO LLM TIMEOUT (in seconds)
 58 | # Controls the timeout for AI model API calls at the Esperanto library level
 59 | # This is separate from API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT and applies to the actual LLM provider requests
 60 | # Only increase this if you're experiencing timeouts during model inference itself
 61 | # Default: 60 seconds (built into Esperanto)
 62 | #
 63 | # Important: This should generally be LOWER than API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT to allow proper error handling
 64 | #
 65 | # Common scenarios:
 66 | # - Fast cloud APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq): 60 seconds is sufficient
 67 | # - Local Ollama with small models: 120-180 seconds may help
 68 | # - Local Ollama with large models on CPU: 300+ seconds
 69 | # - Remote or self-hosted LLMs: 180-300 seconds depending on hardware
 70 | #
 71 | # Note: If transformations complete but you see timeout errors, increase API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT first.
 72 | # Only increase ESPERANTO_LLM_TIMEOUT if the model itself is timing out during inference.
 73 | #
 74 | # ESPERANTO_LLM_TIMEOUT=60
 75 | 
 76 | # SSL VERIFICATION CONFIGURATION
 77 | # Configure SSL certificate verification for local AI providers (Ollama, LM Studio, etc.)
 78 | # behind reverse proxies with self-signed certificates
 79 | #
 80 | # Option 1: Custom CA Bundle (recommended for self-signed certs)
 81 | # Point to your CA certificate file to verify SSL while using custom certificates
 82 | # ESPERANTO_SSL_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/your/ca-bundle.pem
 83 | #
 84 | # Option 2: Disable SSL Verification (development only)
 85 | # WARNING: Disabling SSL verification exposes you to man-in-the-middle attacks
 86 | # Only use in trusted development/testing environments
 87 | # ESPERANTO_SSL_VERIFY=false
 88 | 
 89 | # SECURITY
 90 | # Set this to protect your Open Notebook instance with a password (for public hosting)
 91 | # OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=
 92 | 
 93 | # HTTP/HTTPS PROXY
 94 | # Route all external HTTP requests through a proxy server
 95 | # Useful for corporate/firewalled environments
 96 | #
 97 | # The underlying libraries (esperanto, content-core, podcast-creator) automatically
 98 | # detect proxy settings from these standard environment variables.
 99 | #
100 | # Affects:
101 | # - AI provider API calls (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.)
102 | # - Content extraction from URLs (web scraping, YouTube)
103 | # - Podcast generation (LLM and TTS calls)
104 | #
105 | # Examples:
106 | # HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.com:8080
107 | # HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.com:8080
108 | # NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,.local
109 | 
110 | # OPENAI
111 | # OPENAI_API_KEY=
112 | 
113 | 
114 | # ANTHROPIC
115 | # ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
116 | 
117 | # GEMINI
118 | # this is the best model for long context and podcast generation
119 | # GOOGLE_API_KEY=
120 | # GEMINI_API_BASE_URL=  # Optional: Override default endpoint (for Vertex AI, proxies, etc.)
121 | 
122 | # VERTEXAI
123 | # VERTEX_PROJECT=my-google-cloud-project-name
124 | # GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=./google-credentials.json
125 | # VERTEX_LOCATION=us-east5
126 | 
127 | # MISTRAL
128 | # MISTRAL_API_KEY=
129 | 
130 | # DEEPSEEK
131 | # DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=
132 | 
133 | # OLLAMA
134 | # OLLAMA_API_BASE="http://10.20.30.20:11434"
135 | 
136 | # OPEN ROUTER
137 | # OPENROUTER_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
138 | # OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
139 | 
140 | # GROQ
141 | # GROQ_API_KEY=
142 | 
143 | # XAI
144 | # XAI_API_KEY=
145 | 
146 | # ELEVENLABS
147 | # Used only by the podcast feature
148 | # ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=
149 | 
150 | # TTS BATCH SIZE
151 | # Controls concurrent TTS requests for podcast generation (default: 5)
152 | # Lower values reduce provider load but increase generation time
153 | # Recommended: OpenAI=5, ElevenLabs=2, Google=4, Custom=1
154 | # TTS_BATCH_SIZE=2
155 | 
156 | # VOYAGE AI
157 | # VOYAGE_API_KEY=
158 | 
159 | # OPENAI COMPATIBLE ENDPOINTS
160 | # Generic configuration (applies to all modalities: language, embedding, STT, TTS)
161 | # OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:1234/v1
162 | # OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY=
163 | 
164 | # Mode-specific configuration (overrides generic if set)
165 | # Use these when you want different endpoints for different capabilities
166 | # OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_LLM=http://localhost:1234/v1
167 | # OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY_LLM=
168 | # OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_EMBEDDING=http://localhost:8080/v1
169 | # OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY_EMBEDDING=
170 | # OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_STT=http://localhost:9000/v1
171 | # OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY_STT=
172 | # OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_TTS=http://localhost:9000/v1
173 | # OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY_TTS=
174 | 
175 | # AZURE OPENAI
176 | # Generic configuration (applies to all modalities: language, embedding, STT, TTS)
177 | # AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY=
178 | # AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT=
179 | # AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION=2024-12-01-preview
180 | 
181 | # Mode-specific configuration (overrides generic if set)
182 | # Use these when you want different deployments for different AI capabilities
183 | # AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY_LLM=
184 | # AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT_LLM=
185 | # AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION_LLM=
186 | 
187 | # AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY_EMBEDDING=
188 | # AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT_EMBEDDING=
189 | # AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION_EMBEDDING=
190 | 
191 | # AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY_STT=
192 | # AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT_STT=
193 | # AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION_STT=
194 | 
195 | # AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY_TTS=
196 | # AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT_TTS=
197 | # AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION_TTS=
198 | 
199 | # USE THIS IF YOU WANT TO DEBUG THE APP ON LANGSMITH
200 | # LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=true
201 | # LANGCHAIN_ENDPOINT="https://api.smith.langchain.com"
202 | # LANGCHAIN_API_KEY=
203 | # LANGCHAIN_PROJECT="Open Notebook"
204 | 
205 | # CONNECTION DETAILS FOR YOUR SURREAL DB
206 | # New format (preferred) - WebSocket URL
207 | SURREAL_URL="ws://surrealdb/rpc:8000"
208 | SURREAL_USER="root"
209 | SURREAL_PASSWORD="root"
210 | SURREAL_NAMESPACE="open_notebook"
211 | SURREAL_DATABASE="open_notebook"
212 | 
213 | # RETRY CONFIGURATION (surreal-commands v1.2.0+)
214 | # Global defaults for all background commands unless explicitly overridden at command level
215 | # These settings help commands automatically recover from transient failures like:
216 | # - Database transaction conflicts during concurrent operations
217 | # - Network timeouts when calling external APIs
218 | # - Rate limits from LLM/embedding providers
219 | # - Temporary resource unavailability
220 | 
221 | # Enable/disable retry globally (default: true)
222 | # Set to false to disable retries for all commands (useful for debugging)
223 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_ENABLED=true
224 | 
225 | # Maximum retry attempts before giving up (default: 3)
226 | # Database operations use 5 attempts (defined per-command)
227 | # API calls use 3 attempts (defined per-command)
228 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3
229 | 
230 | # Wait strategy between retry attempts (default: exponential_jitter)
231 | # Options: exponential_jitter, exponential, fixed, random
232 | # - exponential_jitter: Recommended - prevents thundering herd during DB conflicts
233 | # - exponential: Good for API rate limits (predictable backoff)
234 | # - fixed: Use for quick recovery scenarios
235 | # - random: Use when you want unpredictable retry timing
236 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_WAIT_STRATEGY=exponential_jitter
237 | 
238 | # Minimum wait time between retries in seconds (default: 1)
239 | # Database conflicts: 1 second (fast retry for transient issues)
240 | # API rate limits: 5 seconds (wait for quota reset)
241 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_WAIT_MIN=1
242 | 
243 | # Maximum wait time between retries in seconds (default: 30)
244 | # Database conflicts: 30 seconds maximum
245 | # API rate limits: 120 seconds maximum (defined per-command)
246 | # Total retry time won't exceed max_attempts * wait_max
247 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_WAIT_MAX=30
248 | 
249 | # WORKER CONCURRENCY
250 | # Maximum number of concurrent tasks in the worker pool (default: 5)
251 | # This affects the likelihood of database transaction conflicts during batch operations
252 | #
253 | # Tuning guidelines based on deployment size:
254 | # - Resource-constrained (low CPU/memory): 1-2 workers
255 | #   Reduces conflicts and resource usage, but slower processing
256 | #
257 | # - Normal deployment (balanced): 5 workers (RECOMMENDED)
258 | #   Good balance between throughput and conflict rate
259 | #   Retry logic handles occasional conflicts gracefully
260 | #
261 | # - Large instances (high CPU/memory): 10-20 workers
262 | #   Higher throughput but more frequent DB conflicts
263 | #   Relies heavily on retry logic with jittered backoff
264 | #
265 | # Note: Higher concurrency increases vectorization speed but also increases
266 | # SurrealDB transaction conflicts. The retry logic with exponential-jitter
267 | # backoff ensures operations complete successfully even at high concurrency.
268 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS=5
269 | 
270 | # OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=
271 | 
272 | # FIRECRAWL - Get a key at https://firecrawl.dev/
273 | FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=
274 | 
275 | # JINA - Get a key at https://jina.ai/
276 | JINA_API_KEY=

/docs/7-DEVELOPMENT/code-standards.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Code Standards
  2 | 
  3 | This document outlines coding standards and best practices for Open Notebook contributions. All code should follow these guidelines to ensure consistency, readability, and maintainability.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Python Standards
  6 | 
  7 | ### Code Formatting
  8 | 
  9 | We follow **PEP 8** with some specific guidelines:
 10 | 
 11 | - Use **Ruff** for linting and formatting
 12 | - Maximum line length: **88 characters**
 13 | - Use **double quotes** for strings
 14 | - Use **trailing commas** in multi-line structures
 15 | 
 16 | ### Type Hints
 17 | 
 18 | Always use type hints for function parameters and return values:
 19 | 
 20 | ```python
 21 | from typing import List, Optional, Dict, Any
 22 | from pydantic import BaseModel
 23 | 
 24 | async def process_content(
 25 |     content: str,
 26 |     options: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
 27 | ) -> ProcessedContent:
 28 |     """Process content with optional configuration."""
 29 |     # Implementation
 30 | ```
 31 | 
 32 | ### Async/Await Patterns
 33 | 
 34 | Use async/await consistently throughout the codebase:
 35 | 
 36 | ```python
 37 | # Good
 38 | async def fetch_data(url: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 39 |     async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
 40 |         async with session.get(url) as response:
 41 |             return await response.json()
 42 | 
 43 | # Bad - mixing sync and async
 44 | def fetch_data(url: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 45 |     loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
 46 |     return loop.run_until_complete(async_fetch(url))
 47 | ```
 48 | 
 49 | ### Error Handling
 50 | 
 51 | Use structured error handling with custom exceptions:
 52 | 
 53 | ```python
 54 | from open_notebook.exceptions import DatabaseOperationError, InvalidInputError
 55 | 
 56 | async def create_notebook(name: str, description: str) -> Notebook:
 57 |     """Create a new notebook with validation."""
 58 |     if not name.strip():
 59 |         raise InvalidInputError("Notebook name cannot be empty")
 60 | 
 61 |     try:
 62 |         notebook = Notebook(name=name, description=description)
 63 |         await notebook.save()
 64 |         return notebook
 65 |     except Exception as e:
 66 |         raise DatabaseOperationError(f"Failed to create notebook: {str(e)}")
 67 | ```
 68 | 
 69 | ### Documentation (Google-style Docstrings)
 70 | 
 71 | Use Google-style docstrings for all functions, classes, and modules:
 72 | 
 73 | ```python
 74 | async def vector_search(
 75 |     query: str,
 76 |     limit: int = 10,
 77 |     minimum_score: float = 0.2
 78 | ) -> List[SearchResult]:
 79 |     """Perform vector search across embedded content.
 80 | 
 81 |     Args:
 82 |         query: Search query string
 83 |         limit: Maximum number of results to return
 84 |         minimum_score: Minimum similarity score for results
 85 | 
 86 |     Returns:
 87 |         List of search results sorted by relevance score
 88 | 
 89 |     Raises:
 90 |         InvalidInputError: If query is empty or limit is invalid
 91 |         DatabaseOperationError: If search operation fails
 92 |     """
 93 |     # Implementation
 94 | ```
 95 | 
 96 | #### Module Docstrings
 97 | ```python
 98 | """
 99 | Notebook domain model and operations.
100 | 
101 | This module contains the core Notebook class and related operations for
102 | managing research notebooks within the Open Notebook system.
103 | """
104 | ```
105 | 
106 | #### Class Docstrings
107 | ```python
108 | class Notebook(BaseModel):
109 |     """A research notebook containing sources, notes, and chat sessions.
110 | 
111 |     Notebooks are the primary organizational unit in Open Notebook, allowing
112 |     users to group related research materials and maintain separate contexts
113 |     for different projects.
114 | 
115 |     Attributes:
116 |         name: The notebook's display name
117 |         description: Optional description of the notebook's purpose
118 |         archived: Whether the notebook is archived (default: False)
119 |         created: Timestamp of creation
120 |         updated: Timestamp of last update
121 |     """
122 | ```
123 | 
124 | #### Function Docstrings
125 | ```python
126 | async def create_notebook(
127 |     name: str,
128 |     description: str = "",
129 |     user_id: Optional[str] = None
130 | ) -> Notebook:
131 |     """Create a new notebook with validation.
132 | 
133 |     Args:
134 |         name: The notebook name (required, non-empty)
135 |         description: Optional notebook description
136 |         user_id: Optional user ID for multi-user deployments
137 | 
138 |     Returns:
139 |         The created notebook instance
140 | 
141 |     Raises:
142 |         InvalidInputError: If name is empty or invalid
143 |         DatabaseOperationError: If creation fails
144 | 
145 |     Example:
146 |         ```python
147 |         notebook = await create_notebook(
148 |             name="AI Research",
149 |             description="Research on AI applications"
150 |         )
151 |         ```
152 |     """
153 | ```
154 | 
155 | ## FastAPI Standards
156 | 
157 | ### Router Organization
158 | 
159 | Organize endpoints by domain:
160 | 
161 | ```python
162 | # api/routers/notebooks.py
163 | from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query
164 | from typing import List, Optional
165 | 
166 | router = APIRouter()
167 | 
168 | @router.get("/notebooks", response_model=List[NotebookResponse])
169 | async def get_notebooks(
170 |     archived: Optional[bool] = Query(None, description="Filter by archived status"),
171 |     order_by: str = Query("updated desc", description="Order by field and direction"),
172 | ):
173 |     """Get all notebooks with optional filtering and ordering."""
174 |     # Implementation
175 | ```
176 | 
177 | ### Request/Response Models
178 | 
179 | Use Pydantic models for validation:
180 | 
181 | ```python
182 | from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
183 | from typing import Optional
184 | 
185 | class NotebookCreate(BaseModel):
186 |     name: str = Field(..., description="Name of the notebook", min_length=1)
187 |     description: str = Field(default="", description="Description of the notebook")
188 | 
189 | class NotebookResponse(BaseModel):
190 |     id: str
191 |     name: str
192 |     description: str
193 |     archived: bool
194 |     created: str
195 |     updated: str
196 | ```
197 | 
198 | ### Error Handling
199 | 
200 | Use consistent error responses:
201 | 
202 | ```python
203 | from fastapi import HTTPException
204 | from loguru import logger
205 | 
206 | try:
207 |     result = await some_operation()
208 |     return result
209 | except InvalidInputError as e:
210 |     raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))
211 | except DatabaseOperationError as e:
212 |     logger.error(f"Database error: {str(e)}")
213 |     raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Internal server error")
214 | ```
215 | 
216 | ### API Documentation
217 | 
218 | Use FastAPI's automatic documentation features:
219 | 
220 | ```python
221 | @router.post(
222 |     "/notebooks",
223 |     response_model=NotebookResponse,
224 |     summary="Create a new notebook",
225 |     description="Create a new notebook with the specified name and description.",
226 |     responses={
227 |         201: {"description": "Notebook created successfully"},
228 |         400: {"description": "Invalid input data"},
229 |         500: {"description": "Internal server error"}
230 |     }
231 | )
232 | async def create_notebook(notebook: NotebookCreate):
233 |     """Create a new notebook."""
234 |     # Implementation
235 | ```
236 | 
237 | ## Database Standards
238 | 
239 | ### SurrealDB Patterns
240 | 
241 | Use the repository pattern consistently:
242 | 
243 | ```python
244 | from open_notebook.database.repository import repo_create, repo_query, repo_update
245 | 
246 | # Create records
247 | async def create_notebook(data: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
248 |     """Create a new notebook record."""
249 |     return await repo_create("notebook", data)
250 | 
251 | # Query with parameters
252 | async def find_notebooks_by_user(user_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
253 |     """Find notebooks for a specific user."""
254 |     return await repo_query(
255 |         "SELECT * FROM notebook WHERE user_id = $user_id",
256 |         {"user_id": user_id}
257 |     )
258 | 
259 | # Update records
260 | async def update_notebook(notebook_id: str, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
261 |     """Update a notebook record."""
262 |     return await repo_update("notebook", notebook_id, data)
263 | ```
264 | 
265 | ### Schema Management
266 | 
267 | Use migrations for schema changes:
268 | 
269 | ```surrealql
270 | -- migrations/8.surrealql
271 | DEFINE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS new_feature SCHEMAFULL;
272 | DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS name ON TABLE new_feature TYPE string;
273 | DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS description ON TABLE new_feature TYPE option<string>;
274 | DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS created ON TABLE new_feature TYPE datetime DEFAULT time::now();
275 | DEFINE FIELD IF NOT EXISTS updated ON TABLE new_feature TYPE datetime DEFAULT time::now();
276 | ```
277 | 
278 | ## TypeScript Standards
279 | 
280 | ### Basic Guidelines
281 | 
282 | Follow TypeScript best practices:
283 | 
284 | - Use strict mode enabled in `tsconfig.json`
285 | - Use proper type annotations for all variables and functions
286 | - Avoid using `any` type unless absolutely necessary
287 | - Use `interface` for object shapes, `type` for unions and other advanced types
288 | 
289 | ### Component Structure
290 | 
291 | - Use functional components with hooks
292 | - Keep components focused and single-responsibility
293 | - Extract reusable logic into custom hooks
294 | - Use proper TypeScript types for props
295 | 
296 | ### Error Handling
297 | 
298 | - Handle errors explicitly
299 | - Provide meaningful error messages
300 | - Log errors appropriately
301 | - Don't suppress errors silently
302 | 
303 | ## Code Quality Tools
304 | 
305 | We use these tools to maintain code quality:
306 | 
307 | - **Ruff**: Linting and code formatting
308 |   - Run with: `uv run ruff check . --fix`
309 |   - Format with: `uv run ruff format .`
310 | 
311 | - **MyPy**: Static type checking
312 |   - Run with: `uv run python -m mypy .`
313 | 
314 | - **Pytest**: Testing framework
315 |   - Run with: `uv run pytest`
316 | 
317 | ## Common Patterns
318 | 
319 | ### Async Database Operations
320 | 
321 | ```python
322 | async def get_notebook_with_sources(notebook_id: str) -> Notebook:
323 |     """Retrieve notebook with all related sources."""
324 |     notebook_data = await repo_query(
325 |         "SELECT * FROM notebook WHERE id = $id",
326 |         {"id": notebook_id}
327 |     )
328 |     if not notebook_data:
329 |         raise InvalidInputError(f"Notebook {notebook_id} not found")
330 | 
331 |     sources_data = await repo_query(
332 |         "SELECT * FROM source WHERE notebook_id = $notebook_id",
333 |         {"notebook_id": notebook_id}
334 |     )
335 | 
336 |     return Notebook(
337 |         **notebook_data[0],
338 |         sources=[Source(**s) for s in sources_data]
339 |     )
340 | ```
341 | 
342 | ### Model Validation
343 | 
344 | ```python
345 | from pydantic import BaseModel, validator
346 | 
347 | class NotebookInput(BaseModel):
348 |     name: str
349 |     description: str = ""
350 | 
351 |     @validator('name')
352 |     def name_not_empty(cls, v):
353 |         if not v.strip():
354 |             raise ValueError('Name cannot be empty')
355 |         return v.strip()
356 | ```
357 | 
358 | ## Code Review Checklist
359 | 
360 | Before submitting code for review, ensure:
361 | 
362 | - [ ] Code follows PEP 8 / TypeScript best practices
363 | - [ ] Type hints are present for all functions
364 | - [ ] Docstrings are complete and accurate
365 | - [ ] Error handling is appropriate
366 | - [ ] Tests are included and passing
367 | - [ ] No debug code (console.logs, print statements) left behind
368 | - [ ] Commit messages are clear and follow conventions
369 | - [ ] Documentation is updated if needed
370 | 
371 | ---
372 | 
373 | **See also:**
374 | - [Testing Guide](testing.md) - How to write tests
375 | - [Contributing Guide](contributing.md) - Overall contribution workflow
376 |
