/docs/2-CORE-CONCEPTS/chat-vs-transformations.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Chat vs. Ask vs. Transformations - Which Tool for Which Job?
  2 | 
  3 | Open Notebook offers different ways to work with your research. Understanding when to use each is key to using the system effectively.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## The Three Interaction Modes
  8 | 
  9 | ### 1. CHAT - Conversational Exploration with Manual Context
 10 | 
 11 | **What it is:** Have a conversation with AI about selected sources.
 12 | 
 13 | **The flow:**
 14 | ```
 15 | 1. You select which sources to include ("in context")
 16 | 2. You ask a question
 17 | 3. AI responds using ONLY those sources
 18 | 4. You ask follow-up questions (context stays same)
 19 | 5. You change sources or context level, then continue
 20 | ```
 21 | 
 22 | **Context management:** You explicitly choose which sources the AI can see.
 23 | 
 24 | **Conversational:** Multiple questions with shared history.
 25 | 
 26 | **Example:**
 27 | ```
 28 | You: [Select sources: "paper1.pdf", "research_notes.txt"]
 29 |      [Set context: Full content for paper1, Summary for notes]
 30 | 
 31 | You: "What's the main argument in these sources?"
 32 | AI:  "Paper 1 argues X [citation]. Your notes emphasize Y [citation]."
 33 | 
 34 | You: "How do they differ?"
 35 | AI:  "Paper 1 focuses on X [citation], while your notes highlight Y [citation]..."
 36 | 
 37 | You: [Now select different sources]
 38 | 
 39 | You: "Compare to this other perspective"
 40 | AI:  "This new source takes a different approach..."
 41 | ```
 42 | 
 43 | **Best for:**
 44 | - Exploring a focused topic with specific sources
 45 | - Having a dialogue (multiple back-and-forth questions)
 46 | - When you know which sources matter
 47 | - When you want tight control over what goes to AI
 48 | 
 49 | ---
 50 | 
 51 | ### 2. ASK - Automated Comprehensive Search
 52 | 
 53 | **What it is:** Ask one complex question, system automatically finds relevant content.
 54 | 
 55 | **The flow:**
 56 | ```
 57 | 1. You ask a comprehensive question
 58 | 2. System analyzes the question
 59 | 3. System automatically searches your sources
 60 | 4. System retrieves relevant chunks
 61 | 5. System synthesizes answer from all results
 62 | 6. You get one detailed answer (not conversational)
 63 | ```
 64 | 
 65 | **Context management:** Automatic. System figures out what's relevant.
 66 | 
 67 | **Non-conversational:** One question → one answer. No follow-ups.
 68 | 
 69 | **Example:**
 70 | ```
 71 | You: "How do these papers compare their approaches to alignment?
 72 |       What does each one recommend?"
 73 | 
 74 | System:
 75 |   - Breaks down the question into search strategies
 76 |   - Searches all sources for alignment approaches
 77 |   - Searches all sources for recommendations
 78 |   - Retrieves top 10 relevant chunks
 79 |   - Synthesizes: "Paper A recommends X [citation].
 80 |                   Paper B recommends Y [citation].
 81 |                   They differ in Z."
 82 | 
 83 | You: [Get back one comprehensive answer]
 84 |      [If you want to follow up, use Chat instead]
 85 | ```
 86 | 
 87 | **Best for:**
 88 | - Comprehensive, one-time questions
 89 | - Comparing multiple sources at once
 90 | - When you want the system to decide what's relevant
 91 | - Complex questions that need multiple search angles
 92 | - When you don't need a back-and-forth conversation
 93 | 
 94 | ---
 95 | 
 96 | ### 3. TRANSFORMATIONS - Template-Based Processing
 97 | 
 98 | **What it is:** Apply a reusable template to a source and get structured output.
 99 | 
100 | **The flow:**
101 | ```
102 | 1. You define a transformation (or choose a preset)
103 |    "Extract: main argument, methodology, limitations"
104 | 
105 | 2. You apply it to ONE source at a time
106 |    (You can repeat for other sources)
107 | 
108 | 3. For the source:
109 |    - Source content + transformation prompt → AI
110 |    - Result stored as new insight/note
111 | 
112 | 4. You get back
113 |    - Structured output (main argument, methodology, limitations)
114 |    - Saved as a note in your notebook
115 | ```
116 | 
117 | **Context management:** Works on one source at a time.
118 | 
119 | **Reusable:** Apply the same template to different sources (one by one).
120 | 
121 | **Note**: Currently processes one source at a time. Batch processing (multiple sources at once) is planned for a future release.
122 | 
123 | **Example:**
124 | ```
125 | You: Define transformation
126 |      "For each academic paper, extract:
127 |       - Main research question
128 |       - Methodology used
129 |       - Key findings
130 |       - Limitations and gaps
131 |       - Recommended next research"
132 | 
133 | You: Apply to paper 1
134 | 
135 | System:
136 |   - Runs the transformation on paper 1
137 |   - Result stored as new note
138 | 
139 | You: Apply same transformation to paper 2, 3, etc.
140 | 
141 | After 10 papers:
142 |   - You have 10 structured notes with consistent format
143 |   - Perfect for writing a literature review or comparison
144 | ```
145 | 
146 | **Best for:**
147 | - Extracting the same information from each source (run repeatedly)
148 | - Creating structured summaries with consistent format
149 | - Building a knowledge base of categorized insights
150 | - When you want reusable templates you can apply to each source
151 | 
152 | ---
153 | 
154 | ## Decision Tree: Which Tool to Use?
155 | 
156 | ```
157 | What are you trying to do?
158 | 
159 | │
160 | ├─→ "I want to have a conversation about this topic"
161 | │   └─→ Is the conversation exploratory or fixed?
162 | │       ├─→ Exploratory (I'll ask follow-ups)
163 | │       │   └─→ USE: CHAT
164 | │       │
165 | │       └─→ Fixed (One question → done)
166 | │           └─→ Go to next question
167 | │
168 | ├─→ "I need to compare these sources or get a comprehensive answer"
169 | │   └─→ USE: ASK
170 | │
171 | ├─→ "I want to extract the same info from each source (one at a time)"
172 | │   └─→ USE: TRANSFORMATIONS (apply to each source)
173 | │
174 | └─→ "I just want to read and search"
175 |     └─→ USE: Search (text or vector)
176 |         OR read your notes
177 | ```
178 | 
179 | ---
180 | 
181 | ## Side-by-Side Comparison
182 | 
183 | | Aspect | CHAT | ASK | TRANSFORMATIONS |
184 | |--------|------|-----|-----------------|
185 | | **What's it for?** | Conversational exploration | Comprehensive Q&A | Template-based extraction |
186 | | **# of questions** | Multiple (conversational) | One | One template per source |
187 | | **Context control** | Manual (you choose) | Automatic (system searches) | One source at a time |
188 | | **Conversational?** | Yes (follow-ups work) | No (one question only) | No (single operation) |
189 | | **Output** | Natural conversation | Natural answer | Structured note |
190 | | **Time** | Quick (back-and-forth) | Longer (comprehensive) | Per source |
191 | | **Best when** | Exploring & uncertain | Need full picture | Want consistent format |
192 | | **Model speed** | Any | Fast preferred | Any |
193 | 
194 | ---
195 | 
196 | ## Workflow Examples
197 | 
198 | ### Example 1: Academic Research
199 | 
200 | ```
201 | Goal: Write literature review from 15 papers
202 | 
203 | Step 1: TRANSFORMATIONS
204 |   - Define: "Extract abstract, methodology, findings, relevance"
205 |   - Apply to paper 1 → get structured note
206 |   - Apply to paper 2 → get structured note
207 |   - ... repeat for all 15 papers
208 |   - Result: 15 structured notes with consistent format
209 | 
210 | Step 2: Read the notes
211 |   - Now you have consistent summaries
212 | 
213 | Step 3: CHAT or ASK
214 |   - Chat: "Help me organize these by theme"
215 |   - Ask: "What are the common methodologies across these papers?"
216 | 
217 | Step 4: Write your review
218 |   - Use the transformations as foundation
219 |   - Use chat/ask insights for structure
220 | ```
221 | 
222 | ### Example 2: Product Research
223 | 
224 | ```
225 | Goal: Understand customer feedback from interviews
226 | 
227 | Step 1: Add sources (interview transcripts)
228 | 
229 | Step 2: ASK
230 |   - "What are the top 10 pain points mentioned?"
231 |   - Get comprehensive answer with citations
232 | 
233 | Step 3: CHAT
234 |   - "Can you help me group these by severity?"
235 |   - Continue conversation to prioritize
236 | 
237 | Step 4: TRANSFORMATIONS (optional)
238 |   - Define: "Extract: pain point, frequency, who mentioned it"
239 |   - Apply to each interview (one by one)
240 |   - Get structured data for analysis
241 | ```
242 | 
243 | ### Example 3: Policy Analysis
244 | 
245 | ```
246 | Goal: Compare policy documents
247 | 
248 | Step 1: Add all policy documents as sources
249 | 
250 | Step 2: ASK
251 |   - "How do these policies differ on climate measures?"
252 |   - System searches all docs, gives comprehensive comparison
253 | 
254 | Step 3: CHAT (if needed)
255 |   - "Which policy is most aligned with X goals?"
256 |   - Have discussion about trade-offs
257 | 
258 | Step 4: Export notes
259 |   - Save AI responses as notes for reports
260 | ```
261 | 
262 | ---
263 | 
264 | ## Context Management: The Control Panel
265 | 
266 | All three modes let you control what the AI sees.
267 | 
268 | ### In CHAT and TRANSFORMATIONS
269 | ```
270 | You choose:
271 |   - Which sources to include
272 |   - Context level for each:
273 |     ✓ Full Content (send complete text)
274 |     ✓ Summary Only (send AI summary, not full text)
275 |     ✓ Not in Context (exclude entirely)
276 | 
277 | Example:
278 |   Paper A: Full Content (analyzing closely)
279 |   Paper B: Summary Only (background)
280 |   Paper C: Not in Context (confidential)
281 | ```
282 | 
283 | ### In ASK
284 | ```
285 | Context is automatic:
286 |   - System searches ALL your sources
287 |   - Retrieves most relevant chunks
288 |   - Sends those to AI
289 | 
290 | But you can:
291 |   - Search in specific notebook
292 |   - Filter by source type
293 |   - Use the results to decide context for follow-up Chat
294 | ```
295 | 
296 | ---
297 | 
298 | ## Model Selection
299 | 
300 | Each mode works with different models:
301 | 
302 | ### CHAT
303 | - **Any model** works fine
304 | - Fast models (GPT-4o mini, Claude Haiku): Quick responses, good for conversation
305 | - Powerful models (GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet): Better reasoning, better for complex topics
306 | 
307 | ### ASK
308 | - **Fast models preferred** (because it processes multiple searches)
309 | - Can use powerful models if you want deep synthesis
310 | - Example: GPT-4 for strategy planning, GPT-4o-mini for quick facts
311 | 
312 | ### TRANSFORMATIONS
313 | - **Any model** works
314 | - Fast models (cost-effective for batch processing)
315 | - Powerful models (better quality extractions)
316 | 
317 | ---
318 | 
319 | ## Advanced: Chaining Modes Together
320 | 
321 | You can combine these modes:
322 | 
323 | ```
324 | TRANSFORMATIONS → CHAT
325 |   1. Use transformations to extract structured data
326 |   2. Use chat to discuss the results
327 | 
328 | ASK → TRANSFORMATIONS
329 |   1. Use Ask to understand what matters
330 |   2. Use Transformations to extract it from remaining sources
331 | 
332 | CHAT → Save as Note → TRANSFORMATIONS
333 |   1. Have conversation (Chat)
334 |   2. Save good responses as notes
335 |   3. Use those notes as context for transformations
336 | ```
337 | 
338 | ---
339 | 
340 | ## Summary: When to Use Each
341 | 
342 | | Situation | Use | Why |
343 | |-----------|-----|-----|
344 | | "I want to explore a topic with follow-up questions" | **CHAT** | Conversational, you control context |
345 | | "I need a comprehensive answer to one complex question" | **ASK** | Automatic search, synthesized answer |
346 | | "I want consistent summaries from each source" | **TRANSFORMATIONS** | Template reuse, apply to each source |
347 | | "I'm comparing two specific sources" | **CHAT** | Select just those 2, have discussion |
348 | | "I need to categorize each source by X criteria" | **TRANSFORMATIONS** | Extract category from each source |
349 | | "I want to understand the big picture across all sources" | **ASK** | Automatic comprehensive search |
350 | | "I want to build a knowledge base" | **TRANSFORMATIONS** | Create structured note from each source |
351 | | "I want to iterate on understanding" | **CHAT** | Multiple questions, refine thinking |
352 | 
353 | The key insight: **Different questions need different tools.** Open Notebook gives you all three because research rarely fits one mode.
354 |

/frontend/src/lib/hooks/useNotebookChat.ts:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | 'use client'
  2 | 
  3 | import { useState, useCallback, useEffect } from 'react'
  4 | import { useQuery, useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
  5 | import { toast } from 'sonner'
  6 | import { getApiErrorKey } from '@/lib/utils/error-handler'
  7 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
  8 | import { chatApi } from '@/lib/api/chat'
  9 | import { QUERY_KEYS } from '@/lib/api/query-client'
 10 | import {
 11 |   NotebookChatMessage,
 12 |   CreateNotebookChatSessionRequest,
 13 |   UpdateNotebookChatSessionRequest,
 14 |   SourceListResponse,
 15 |   NoteResponse
 16 | } from '@/lib/types/api'
 17 | import { ContextSelections } from '@/app/(dashboard)/notebooks/[id]/page'
 18 | 
 19 | interface UseNotebookChatParams {
 20 |   notebookId: string
 21 |   sources: SourceListResponse[]
 22 |   notes: NoteResponse[]
 23 |   contextSelections: ContextSelections
 24 | }
 25 | 
 26 | export function useNotebookChat({ notebookId, sources, notes, contextSelections }: UseNotebookChatParams) {
 27 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 28 |   const queryClient = useQueryClient()
 29 |   const [currentSessionId, setCurrentSessionId] = useState<string | null>(null)
 30 |   const [messages, setMessages] = useState<NotebookChatMessage[]>([])
 31 |   const [isSending, setIsSending] = useState(false)
 32 |   const [tokenCount, setTokenCount] = useState<number>(0)
 33 |   const [charCount, setCharCount] = useState<number>(0)
 34 |   // Pending model override for when user changes model before a session exists
 35 |   const [pendingModelOverride, setPendingModelOverride] = useState<string | null>(null)
 36 | 
 37 |   // Fetch sessions for this notebook
 38 |   const {
 39 |     data: sessions = [],
 40 |     isLoading: loadingSessions,
 41 |     refetch: refetchSessions
 42 |   } = useQuery({
 43 |     queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.notebookChatSessions(notebookId),
 44 |     queryFn: () => chatApi.listSessions(notebookId),
 45 |     enabled: !!notebookId
 46 |   })
 47 | 
 48 |   // Fetch current session with messages
 49 |   const {
 50 |     data: currentSession,
 51 |     refetch: refetchCurrentSession
 52 |   } = useQuery({
 53 |     queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.notebookChatSession(currentSessionId!),
 54 |     queryFn: () => chatApi.getSession(currentSessionId!),
 55 |     enabled: !!notebookId && !!currentSessionId
 56 |   })
 57 | 
 58 |   // Update messages when current session changes
 59 |   useEffect(() => {
 60 |     if (currentSession?.messages) {
 61 |       setMessages(currentSession.messages)
 62 |     }
 63 |   }, [currentSession])
 64 | 
 65 |   // Auto-select most recent session when sessions are loaded
 66 |   useEffect(() => {
 67 |     if (sessions.length > 0 && !currentSessionId) {
 68 |       // Sessions are sorted by created date desc from API
 69 |       const mostRecentSession = sessions[0]
 70 |       setCurrentSessionId(mostRecentSession.id)
 71 |     }
 72 |   }, [sessions, currentSessionId])
 73 | 
 74 |   // Create session mutation
 75 |   const createSessionMutation = useMutation({
 76 |     mutationFn: (data: CreateNotebookChatSessionRequest) =>
 77 |       chatApi.createSession(data),
 78 |     onSuccess: (newSession) => {
 79 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({
 80 |         queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.notebookChatSessions(notebookId)
 81 |       })
 82 |       setCurrentSessionId(newSession.id)
 83 |       toast.success(t.chat.sessionCreated)
 84 |     },
 85 |     onError: (err: unknown) => {
 86 |       const error = err as { response?: { data?: { detail?: string } }, message?: string };
 87 |       toast.error(t(getApiErrorKey(error.response?.data?.detail || error.message, 'apiErrors.failedToCreateSession')))
 88 |     }
 89 |   })
 90 | 
 91 |   // Update session mutation
 92 |   const updateSessionMutation = useMutation({
 93 |     mutationFn: ({ sessionId, data }: {
 94 |       sessionId: string
 95 |       data: UpdateNotebookChatSessionRequest
 96 |     }) => chatApi.updateSession(sessionId, data),
 97 |     onSuccess: () => {
 98 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({
 99 |         queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.notebookChatSessions(notebookId)
100 |       })
101 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({
102 |         queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.notebookChatSession(currentSessionId!)
103 |       })
104 |       toast.success(t.chat.sessionUpdated)
105 |     },
106 |     onError: (err: unknown) => {
107 |       const error = err as { response?: { data?: { detail?: string } }, message?: string };
108 |       toast.error(t(getApiErrorKey(error.response?.data?.detail || error.message, 'apiErrors.failedToUpdateSession')))
109 |     }
110 |   })
111 | 
112 |   // Delete session mutation
113 |   const deleteSessionMutation = useMutation({
114 |     mutationFn: (sessionId: string) =>
115 |       chatApi.deleteSession(sessionId),
116 |     onSuccess: (_, deletedId) => {
117 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({
118 |         queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.notebookChatSessions(notebookId)
119 |       })
120 |       if (currentSessionId === deletedId) {
121 |         setCurrentSessionId(null)
122 |         setMessages([])
123 |       }
124 |       toast.success(t.chat.sessionDeleted)
125 |     },
126 |     onError: (err: unknown) => {
127 |       const error = err as { response?: { data?: { detail?: string } }, message?: string };
128 |       toast.error(t(getApiErrorKey(error.response?.data?.detail || error.message, 'apiErrors.failedToDeleteSession')))
129 |     }
130 |   })
131 | 
132 |   // Build context from sources and notes based on user selections
133 |   const buildContext = useCallback(async () => {
134 |     // Build context_config mapping IDs to selection modes
135 |     const context_config: { sources: Record<string, string>, notes: Record<string, string> } = {
136 |       sources: {},
137 |       notes: {}
138 |     }
139 | 
140 |     // Map source selections
141 |     sources.forEach(source => {
142 |       const mode = contextSelections.sources[source.id]
143 |       if (mode === 'insights') {
144 |         context_config.sources[source.id] = 'insights'
145 |       } else if (mode === 'full') {
146 |         context_config.sources[source.id] = 'full content'
147 |       } else {
148 |         context_config.sources[source.id] = 'not in'
149 |       }
150 |     })
151 | 
152 |     // Map note selections
153 |     notes.forEach(note => {
154 |       const mode = contextSelections.notes[note.id]
155 |       if (mode === 'full') {
156 |         context_config.notes[note.id] = 'full content'
157 |       } else {
158 |         context_config.notes[note.id] = 'not in'
159 |       }
160 |     })
161 | 
162 |     // Call API to build context with actual content
163 |     const response = await chatApi.buildContext({
164 |       notebook_id: notebookId,
165 |       context_config
166 |     })
167 | 
168 |     // Store token and char counts
169 |     setTokenCount(response.token_count)
170 |     setCharCount(response.char_count)
171 | 
172 |     return response.context
173 |   }, [notebookId, sources, notes, contextSelections])
174 | 
175 |   // Send message (synchronous, no streaming)
176 |   const sendMessage = useCallback(async (message: string, modelOverride?: string) => {
177 |     let sessionId = currentSessionId
178 | 
179 |     // Auto-create session if none exists
180 |     if (!sessionId) {
181 |       try {
182 |         const defaultTitle = message.length > 30
183 |           ? `${message.substring(0, 30)}...`
184 |           : message
185 |         const newSession = await chatApi.createSession({
186 |           notebook_id: notebookId,
187 |           title: defaultTitle,
188 |           // Include pending model override when creating session
189 |           model_override: pendingModelOverride ?? undefined
190 |         })
191 |         sessionId = newSession.id
192 |         setCurrentSessionId(sessionId)
193 |         // Clear pending model override now that it's applied to the session
194 |         setPendingModelOverride(null)
195 |         queryClient.invalidateQueries({
196 |           queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.notebookChatSessions(notebookId)
197 |         })
198 |       } catch (err: unknown) {
199 |         const error = err as { response?: { data?: { detail?: string } }, message?: string };
200 |         toast.error(t(getApiErrorKey(error.response?.data?.detail || error.message, 'apiErrors.failedToCreateSession')))
201 |         return
202 |       }
203 |     }
204 | 
205 |     // Add user message optimistically
206 |     const userMessage: NotebookChatMessage = {
207 |       id: `temp-${Date.now()}`,
208 |       type: 'human',
209 |       content: message,
210 |       timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
211 |     }
212 |     setMessages(prev => [...prev, userMessage])
213 |     setIsSending(true)
214 | 
215 |     try {
216 |       // Build context and send message
217 |       const context = await buildContext()
218 |       const response = await chatApi.sendMessage({
219 |         session_id: sessionId,
220 |         message,
221 |         context,
222 |         model_override: modelOverride ?? (currentSession?.model_override ?? undefined)
223 |       })
224 | 
225 |       // Update messages with API response
226 |       setMessages(response.messages)
227 | 
228 |       // Refetch current session to get updated data
229 |       await refetchCurrentSession()
230 |     } catch (err: unknown) {
231 |       const error = err as { response?: { data?: { detail?: string } }, message?: string };
232 |       console.error('Error sending message:', error)
233 |       toast.error(t(getApiErrorKey(error.response?.data?.detail || error.message, 'apiErrors.failedToSendMessage')))
234 |       // Remove optimistic message on error
235 |       setMessages(prev => prev.filter(msg => !msg.id.startsWith('temp-')))
236 |     } finally {
237 |       setIsSending(false)
238 |     }
239 |   }, [
240 |     notebookId,
241 |     currentSessionId,
242 |     currentSession,
243 |     pendingModelOverride,
244 |     buildContext,
245 |     refetchCurrentSession,
246 |     queryClient,
247 |     t
248 |   ])
249 | 
250 |   // Switch session
251 |   const switchSession = useCallback((sessionId: string) => {
252 |     setCurrentSessionId(sessionId)
253 |   }, [])
254 | 
255 |   // Create session
256 |   const createSession = useCallback((title?: string) => {
257 |     return createSessionMutation.mutate({
258 |       notebook_id: notebookId,
259 |       title
260 |     })
261 |   }, [createSessionMutation, notebookId])
262 | 
263 |   // Update session
264 |   const updateSession = useCallback((sessionId: string, data: UpdateNotebookChatSessionRequest) => {
265 |     return updateSessionMutation.mutate({
266 |       sessionId,
267 |       data
268 |     })
269 |   }, [updateSessionMutation])
270 | 
271 |   // Delete session
272 |   const deleteSession = useCallback((sessionId: string) => {
273 |     return deleteSessionMutation.mutate(sessionId)
274 |   }, [deleteSessionMutation])
275 | 
276 |   // Set model override - handles both existing sessions and pending state
277 |   const setModelOverride = useCallback((model: string | null) => {
278 |     if (currentSessionId) {
279 |       // Session exists - update it directly
280 |       updateSessionMutation.mutate({
281 |         sessionId: currentSessionId,
282 |         data: { model_override: model }
283 |       })
284 |     } else {
285 |       // No session yet - store as pending
286 |       setPendingModelOverride(model)
287 |     }
288 |   }, [currentSessionId, updateSessionMutation])
289 | 
290 |   // Update token/char counts when context selections change
291 |   useEffect(() => {
292 |     const updateContextCounts = async () => {
293 |       try {
294 |         await buildContext()
295 |       } catch (error) {
296 |         console.error('Error updating context counts:', error)
297 |       }
298 |     }
299 |     updateContextCounts()
300 |   }, [buildContext])
301 | 
302 |   return {
303 |     // State
304 |     sessions,
305 |     currentSession: currentSession || sessions.find(s => s.id === currentSessionId),
306 |     currentSessionId,
307 |     messages,
308 |     isSending,
309 |     loadingSessions,
310 |     tokenCount,
311 |     charCount,
312 |     pendingModelOverride,
313 | 
314 |     // Actions
315 |     createSession,
316 |     updateSession,
317 |     deleteSession,
318 |     switchSession,
319 |     sendMessage,
320 |     setModelOverride,
321 |     refetchSessions
322 |   }
323 | }
324 |

  1 | """
  2 | Sources service layer using API.
  3 | """
  4 | 
  5 | from dataclasses import dataclass
  6 | from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Union
  7 | 
  8 | from loguru import logger
  9 | 
 10 | from api.client import api_client
 11 | from open_notebook.domain.notebook import Asset, Source
 12 | 
 13 | 
 14 | @dataclass
 15 | class SourceProcessingResult:
 16 |     """Result of source creation with optional async processing info."""
 17 | 
 18 |     source: Source
 19 |     is_async: bool = False
 20 |     command_id: Optional[str] = None
 21 |     status: Optional[str] = None
 22 |     processing_info: Optional[Dict] = None
 23 | 
 24 | 
 25 | @dataclass
 26 | class SourceWithMetadata:
 27 |     """Source object with additional metadata from API."""
 28 | 
 29 |     source: Source
 30 |     embedded_chunks: int
 31 | 
 32 |     # Expose common source properties for easy access
 33 |     @property
 34 |     def id(self):
 35 |         return self.source.id
 36 | 
 37 |     @property
 38 |     def title(self):
 39 |         return self.source.title
 40 | 
 41 |     @title.setter
 42 |     def title(self, value):
 43 |         self.source.title = value
 44 | 
 45 |     @property
 46 |     def topics(self):
 47 |         return self.source.topics
 48 | 
 49 |     @property
 50 |     def asset(self):
 51 |         return self.source.asset
 52 | 
 53 |     @property
 54 |     def full_text(self):
 55 |         return self.source.full_text
 56 | 
 57 |     @property
 58 |     def created(self):
 59 |         return self.source.created
 60 | 
 61 |     @property
 62 |     def updated(self):
 63 |         return self.source.updated
 64 | 
 65 | 
 66 | class SourcesService:
 67 |     """Service layer for sources operations using API."""
 68 | 
 69 |     def __init__(self):
 70 |         logger.info("Using API for sources operations")
 71 | 
 72 |     def get_all_sources(
 73 |         self, notebook_id: Optional[str] = None
 74 |     ) -> List[SourceWithMetadata]:
 75 |         """Get all sources with optional notebook filtering."""
 76 |         sources_data = api_client.get_sources(notebook_id=notebook_id)
 77 |         # Convert API response to SourceWithMetadata objects
 78 |         sources = []
 79 |         for source_data in sources_data:
 80 |             source = Source(
 81 |                 title=source_data["title"],
 82 |                 topics=source_data["topics"],
 83 |                 asset=Asset(
 84 |                     file_path=source_data["asset"]["file_path"]
 85 |                     if source_data["asset"]
 86 |                     else None,
 87 |                     url=source_data["asset"]["url"] if source_data["asset"] else None,
 88 |                 )
 89 |                 if source_data["asset"]
 90 |                 else None,
 91 |             )
 92 |             source.id = source_data["id"]
 93 |             source.created = source_data["created"]
 94 |             source.updated = source_data["updated"]
 95 | 
 96 |             # Wrap in SourceWithMetadata
 97 |             source_with_metadata = SourceWithMetadata(
 98 |                 source=source, embedded_chunks=source_data.get("embedded_chunks", 0)
 99 |             )
100 |             sources.append(source_with_metadata)
101 |         return sources
102 | 
103 |     def get_source(self, source_id: str) -> SourceWithMetadata:
104 |         """Get a specific source."""
105 |         response = api_client.get_source(source_id)
106 |         source_data = response if isinstance(response, dict) else response[0]
107 |         source = Source(
108 |             title=source_data["title"],
109 |             topics=source_data["topics"],
110 |             full_text=source_data["full_text"],
111 |             asset=Asset(
112 |                 file_path=source_data["asset"]["file_path"]
113 |                 if source_data["asset"]
114 |                 else None,
115 |                 url=source_data["asset"]["url"] if source_data["asset"] else None,
116 |             )
117 |             if source_data["asset"]
118 |             else None,
119 |         )
120 |         source.id = source_data["id"]
121 |         source.created = source_data["created"]
122 |         source.updated = source_data["updated"]
123 | 
124 |         return SourceWithMetadata(
125 |             source=source, embedded_chunks=source_data.get("embedded_chunks", 0)
126 |         )
127 | 
128 |     def create_source(
129 |         self,
130 |         notebook_id: Optional[str] = None,
131 |         source_type: str = "text",
132 |         url: Optional[str] = None,
133 |         file_path: Optional[str] = None,
134 |         content: Optional[str] = None,
135 |         title: Optional[str] = None,
136 |         transformations: Optional[List[str]] = None,
137 |         embed: bool = False,
138 |         delete_source: bool = False,
139 |         notebooks: Optional[List[str]] = None,
140 |         async_processing: bool = False,
141 |     ) -> Union[Source, SourceProcessingResult]:
142 |         """
143 |         Create a new source with support for async processing.
144 | 
145 |         Args:
146 |             notebook_id: Single notebook ID (deprecated, use notebooks parameter)
147 |             source_type: Type of source (link, upload, text)
148 |             url: URL for link sources
149 |             file_path: File path for upload sources
150 |             content: Text content for text sources
151 |             title: Optional source title
152 |             transformations: List of transformation IDs to apply
153 |             embed: Whether to embed content for vector search
154 |             delete_source: Whether to delete uploaded file after processing
155 |             notebooks: List of notebook IDs to add source to (preferred over notebook_id)
156 |             async_processing: Whether to process source asynchronously
157 | 
158 |         Returns:
159 |             Source object for sync processing (backward compatibility)
160 |             SourceProcessingResult for async processing (contains additional metadata)
161 |         """
162 |         source_data = api_client.create_source(
163 |             notebook_id=notebook_id,
164 |             notebooks=notebooks,
165 |             source_type=source_type,
166 |             url=url,
167 |             file_path=file_path,
168 |             content=content,
169 |             title=title,
170 |             transformations=transformations,
171 |             embed=embed,
172 |             delete_source=delete_source,
173 |             async_processing=async_processing,
174 |         )
175 | 
176 |         # Create Source object from response
177 |         response_data = source_data if isinstance(source_data, dict) else source_data[0]
178 |         source = Source(
179 |             title=response_data["title"],
180 |             topics=response_data.get("topics") or [],
181 |             full_text=response_data.get("full_text"),
182 |             asset=Asset(
183 |                 file_path=response_data["asset"]["file_path"]
184 |                 if response_data.get("asset")
185 |                 else None,
186 |                 url=response_data["asset"]["url"]
187 |                 if response_data.get("asset")
188 |                 else None,
189 |             )
190 |             if response_data.get("asset")
191 |             else None,
192 |         )
193 |         source.id = response_data["id"]
194 |         source.created = response_data["created"]
195 |         source.updated = response_data["updated"]
196 | 
197 |         # Check if this is an async processing response
198 |         if (
199 |             response_data.get("command_id")
200 |             or response_data.get("status")
201 |             or response_data.get("processing_info")
202 |         ):
203 |             # Ensure source_data is a dict for accessing attributes
204 |             source_data_dict = (
205 |                 source_data if isinstance(source_data, dict) else source_data[0]
206 |             )
207 |             # Return enhanced result for async processing
208 |             return SourceProcessingResult(
209 |                 source=source,
210 |                 is_async=True,
211 |                 command_id=source_data_dict.get("command_id"),
212 |                 status=source_data_dict.get("status"),
213 |                 processing_info=source_data_dict.get("processing_info"),
214 |             )
215 |         else:
216 |             # Return simple Source for backward compatibility
217 |             return source
218 | 
219 |     def get_source_status(self, source_id: str) -> Dict:
220 |         """Get processing status for a source."""
221 |         response = api_client.get_source_status(source_id)
222 |         return response if isinstance(response, dict) else response[0]
223 | 
224 |     def create_source_async(
225 |         self,
226 |         notebook_id: Optional[str] = None,
227 |         source_type: str = "text",
228 |         url: Optional[str] = None,
229 |         file_path: Optional[str] = None,
230 |         content: Optional[str] = None,
231 |         title: Optional[str] = None,
232 |         transformations: Optional[List[str]] = None,
233 |         embed: bool = False,
234 |         delete_source: bool = False,
235 |         notebooks: Optional[List[str]] = None,
236 |     ) -> SourceProcessingResult:
237 |         """
238 |         Create a new source with async processing enabled.
239 | 
240 |         This is a convenience method that always uses async processing.
241 |         Returns a SourceProcessingResult with processing status information.
242 |         """
243 |         result = self.create_source(
244 |             notebook_id=notebook_id,
245 |             notebooks=notebooks,
246 |             source_type=source_type,
247 |             url=url,
248 |             file_path=file_path,
249 |             content=content,
250 |             title=title,
251 |             transformations=transformations,
252 |             embed=embed,
253 |             delete_source=delete_source,
254 |             async_processing=True,
255 |         )
256 | 
257 |         # Since we forced async_processing=True, this should always be a SourceProcessingResult
258 |         if isinstance(result, SourceProcessingResult):
259 |             return result
260 |         else:
261 |             # Fallback: wrap Source in SourceProcessingResult
262 |             return SourceProcessingResult(
263 |                 source=result,
264 |                 is_async=False,  # This shouldn't happen, but handle it gracefully
265 |             )
266 | 
267 |     def is_source_processing_complete(self, source_id: str) -> bool:
268 |         """
269 |         Check if a source's async processing is complete.
270 | 
271 |         Returns True if processing is complete (success or failure),
272 |         False if still processing or queued.
273 |         """
274 |         try:
275 |             status_data = self.get_source_status(source_id)
276 |             status = status_data.get("status")
277 |             return status in [
278 |                 "completed",
279 |                 "failed",
280 |                 None,
281 |             ]  # None indicates legacy/sync source
282 |         except Exception as e:
283 |             logger.error(f"Error checking source processing status: {e}")
284 |             return True  # Assume complete on error
285 | 
286 |     def update_source(self, source: Source) -> Source:
287 |         """Update a source."""
288 |         if not source.id:
289 |             raise ValueError("Source ID is required for update")
290 | 
291 |         updates = {
292 |             "title": source.title,
293 |             "topics": source.topics,
294 |         }
295 |         source_data = api_client.update_source(source.id, **updates)
296 | 
297 |         # Ensure source_data is a dict
298 |         source_data_dict = (
299 |             source_data if isinstance(source_data, dict) else source_data[0]
300 |         )
301 | 
302 |         # Update the source object with the response
303 |         source.title = source_data_dict["title"]
304 |         source.topics = source_data_dict["topics"]
305 |         source.updated = source_data_dict["updated"]
306 | 
307 |         return source
308 | 
309 |     def delete_source(self, source_id: str) -> bool:
310 |         """Delete a source."""
311 |         api_client.delete_source(source_id)
312 |         return True
313 | 
314 | 
315 | # Global service instance
316 | sources_service = SourcesService()
317 | 
318 | # Export important classes for easy importing
319 | __all__ = [
320 |     "SourcesService",
321 |     "SourceWithMetadata",
322 |     "SourceProcessingResult",
323 |     "sources_service",
324 | ]

/open_notebook/CLAUDE.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Open Notebook Core Backend
  2 | 
  3 | The `open_notebook` module is the heart of the system: a multi-layer backend orchestrating AI-powered research workflows. It bridges domain models, asynchronous database operations, LangGraph-based content processing, and multi-provider AI model management.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Purpose
  6 | 
  7 | Encapsulates the entire backend architecture:
  8 | 1. **Data layer**: SurrealDB persistence with async CRUD and migrations
  9 | 2. **Domain layer**: Research models (Notebook, Source, Note, etc.) with embedded relationships
 10 | 3. **Workflow layer**: LangGraph state machines for content ingestion, chat, and transformations
 11 | 4. **AI provisioning**: Multi-provider model management with smart fallback logic
 12 | 5. **Support services**: Context building, tokenization, and utility functions
 13 | 
 14 | All components communicate through async/await patterns and use Pydantic for validation.
 15 | 
 16 | ## Architecture Overview
 17 | 
 18 | ```
 19 | ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 20 | │                    API / Streamlit UI                        │
 21 | └──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
 22 |                        │
 23 |     ┌──────────────────┴──────────────────┐
 24 |     │                                     │
 25 | ┌───▼────────────────────┐   ┌──────────▼────────────────┐
 26 | │    Graphs (LangGraph)   │   │   Domain Models (Data)    │
 27 | │ - source.py (ingestion) │   │ - Notebook, Source, Note  │
 28 | │ - chat.py              │   │ - ChatSession, Asset       │
 29 | │ - ask.py (search)      │   │ - SourceInsight, Embedding│
 30 | │ - transformation.py    │   │ - Transformation, Settings│
 31 | └───┬────────────────────┘   │ - EpisodeProfile, Podcast │
 32 |     │                        └──────────┬─────────────────┘
 33 |     │                                   │
 34 |     └───────────────────┬───────────────┘
 35 |                         │
 36 |     ┌───────────────────┴────────────────────┐
 37 |     │                                        │
 38 | ┌───▼─────────────────┐      ┌──────────────▼──────┐
 39 | │  AI Module (Models)  │      │  Utils (Helpers)     │
 40 | │ - ModelManager       │      │ - ContextBuilder     │
 41 | │ - DefaultModels      │      │ - TokenUtils         │
 42 | │ - provision_langchain│      │ - TextUtils          │
 43 | │ - Multi-provider AI  │      │ - VersionUtils       │
 44 | └───┬─────────────────┘      └──────────┬──────────┘
 45 |     │                                   │
 46 |     └───────────────────┬───────────────┘
 47 |                         │
 48 |          ┌──────────────▼────────────────┐
 49 |          │  Database (SurrealDB)          │
 50 |          │ - repository.py (CRUD ops)     │
 51 |          │ - async_migrate.py (schema)    │
 52 |          │ - Configuration                │
 53 |          └────────────────────────────────┘
 54 | ```
 55 | 
 56 | ## Component Catalog
 57 | 
 58 | ### Core Layers
 59 | 
 60 | **See dedicated CLAUDE.md files for detailed patterns and usage:**
 61 | 
 62 | - **`database/`**: Async repository pattern (repo_query, repo_create, repo_upsert), connection pooling, and automatic schema migrations on API startup. See `database/CLAUDE.md`.
 63 | 
 64 | - **`domain/`**: Core data models using Pydantic with SurrealDB persistence. Two base classes: `ObjectModel` (mutable records with auto-increment IDs and embedding) and `RecordModel` (singleton configuration). Includes search functions (text_search, vector_search). See `domain/CLAUDE.md`.
 65 | 
 66 | - **`graphs/`**: LangGraph state machines for async workflows. Content ingestion (source.py), conversational agents (chat.py), search synthesis (ask.py), and transformations. Uses provision_langchain_model() for smart model selection with token-aware fallback. See `graphs/CLAUDE.md`.
 67 | 
 68 | - **`ai/`**: Centralized AI model lifecycle via Esperanto library. ModelManager factory with intelligent fallback (large context detection, type-specific defaults, config override). Supports 8+ providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, Ollama, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI). See `ai/CLAUDE.md`.
 69 | 
 70 | - **`utils/`**: Cross-cutting utilities: ContextBuilder (flexible context assembly from sources/notes/insights with token budgeting), TextUtils (truncation, cleaning), TokenUtils (GPT token counting), VersionUtils (schema compatibility). See `utils/CLAUDE.md`.
 71 | 
 72 | - **`podcasts/`**: Podcast generation models: SpeakerProfile (TTS voice config), EpisodeProfile (generation settings), PodcastEpisode (job tracking via surreal-commands). See `podcasts/CLAUDE.md`.
 73 | 
 74 | ### Configuration & Exceptions
 75 | 
 76 | - **`config.py`**: Paths for data folder, uploads, LangGraph checkpoints, and tiktoken cache. Auto-creates directories.
 77 | - **`exceptions.py`**: Hierarchy of OpenNotebookError subclasses for database, file, network, authentication, and rate-limit failures.
 78 | 
 79 | ## Data Flow: Content Ingestion
 80 | 
 81 | ```
 82 | User uploads file/URL
 83 |          │
 84 |          ▼
 85 | ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
 86 | │ source.py (LangGraph state machine) │
 87 | ├─────────────────────────────────────┤
 88 | │ 1. content_process()                │
 89 | │    - extract_content() from file/URL│
 90 | │    - Use ContentSettings defaults    │
 91 | │    - speech_to_text model from DB   │
 92 | │                                     │
 93 | │ 2. save_source()                    │
 94 | │    - Update Source with full_text   │
 95 | │    - Preserve title if empty        │
 96 | │                                     │
 97 | │ 3. trigger_transformations()        │
 98 | │    - Parallel fan-out to each TXN   │
 99 | └────────────────┬────────────────────┘
100 |                  │
101 |                  ▼
102 |          ┌──────────────┐
103 |          │ transformation.py (parallel)
104 |          │ - Apply prompt to source text
105 |          │ - Generate insights
106 |          │ - Auto-embed results
107 |          └──────────────┘
108 |                  │
109 |                  ▼
110 |         ┌────────────────────┐
111 |         │ Database Storage    │
112 |         │ - Source.full_text  │
113 |         │ - SourceInsight     │
114 |         │ - Embeddings        │
115 |         │ - (async job)       │
116 |         └────────────────────┘
117 | ```
118 | 
119 | **Fire-and-forget embeddings**: Source.vectorize() returns command_id without awaiting; embedding happens asynchronously via surreal-commands job system.
120 | 
121 | ## Data Flow: Chat & Search
122 | 
123 | ```
124 | User message in chat
125 |          │
126 |          ▼
127 | ┌──────────────────────────┐
128 | │ ContextBuilder           │
129 | │ - Select sources/notes   │
130 | │ - Token budget limiting  │
131 | │ - Priority weighting     │
132 | └──────────┬───────────────┘
133 |            │
134 |            ▼
135 | ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
136 | │ chat.py or ask.py (LangGraph)    │
137 | │ - Load context from above        │
138 | │ - provision_langchain_model()    │
139 | │   * Auto-upgrade for large text  │
140 | │   * Apply model_id override      │
141 | │ - Call LLM with context          │
142 | │ - Store message in SqliteSaver   │
143 | └──────────┬───────────────────────┘
144 |            │
145 |            ▼
146 |     ┌──────────────┐
147 |     │ LLM Response │
148 |     │ (persisted)  │
149 |     └──────────────┘
150 | ```
151 | 
152 | ## Key Patterns Across Layers
153 | 
154 | ### Async/Await Everywhere
155 | All database operations, model provisioning, and graph execution are async. Mix with sync code only via `asyncio.run()` or LangGraph's async bridges (see graphs/CLAUDE.md for workarounds).
156 | 
157 | ### Type-Driven Dispatch
158 | Model types (language, embedding, speech_to_text, text_to_speech) drive factory logic in ModelManager. Domain model IDs encode their type: `notebook:uuid`, `source:uuid`, `note:uuid`.
159 | 
160 | ### Smart Fallback Logic
161 | `provision_langchain_model()` auto-detects large contexts (105K+ tokens) and upgrades to dedicated large_context_model. Falls back to default_chat_model if specific type not found.
162 | 
163 | ### Fire-and-Forget Jobs
164 | Time-consuming operations (embedding, podcast generation) return command_id immediately. Caller polls surreal-commands for status; no blocking.
165 | 
166 | ### Fire-and-Forget Embedding
167 | Domain models submit embedding commands after save via `submit_command()` (non-blocking). Note.save() submits `embed_note`, Source.add_insight() submits `embed_insight`, Source.vectorize() submits `embed_source`. Search functions (text_search, vector_search) use embeddings for semantic matching.
168 | 
169 | ### Relationship Management
170 | SurrealDB graph edges link entities: Notebook→Source (has), Source→Note (artifact), Note→Source (refers_to). See `relate()` in domain/base.py.
171 | 
172 | ## Integration Points
173 | 
174 | **API startup** (`api/main.py`):
175 | - AsyncMigrationManager.run_migration_up() on lifespan startup
176 | - Ensures schema is current before handling requests
177 | 
178 | **Streamlit UI** (`pages/stream_app/`):
179 | - Calls domain models directly to fetch/create notebooks, sources, notes
180 | - Invokes graphs (chat, source, ask) via async wrapper
181 | - Relies on API for migrations (deprecated check in UI)
182 | 
183 | **Background Jobs** (`surreal_commands`):
184 | - Source.vectorize() submits async embedding job
185 | - PodcastEpisode.get_job_status() polls job queue
186 | - Decouples long-running operations from request flow
187 | 
188 | ## Important Quirks & Gotchas
189 | 
190 | 1. **Token counting rough estimate**: Uses cl100k_base encoding; may differ 5-10% from actual model
191 | 2. **Large context threshold hard-coded**: 105,000 token limit for large_context_model upgrade (not configurable)
192 | 3. **Async loop gymnastics in graphs**: ThreadPoolExecutor workaround for LangGraph sync nodes calling async functions (fragile)
193 | 4. **DefaultModels always fresh**: get_instance() bypasses singleton cache to pick up live config changes
194 | 5. **Polymorphic model.get()**: Resolves subclass from ID prefix; fails silently if subclass not imported
195 | 6. **RecordID string inconsistency**: repo_update() accepts both "table:id" format and full RecordID
196 | 7. **Snapshot profiles**: podcast profiles stored as dicts, so config updates don't affect past episodes
197 | 8. **No connection pooling**: Each repo_* creates new connection (adequate for HTTP but inefficient for bulk)
198 | 9. **Circular import guard**: utils imports domain; domain must not import utils (breaks on import)
199 | 10. **SqliteSaver shared location**: LangGraph checkpoints from LANGGRAPH_CHECKPOINT_FILE env var; all graphs use same file
200 | 
201 | ## How to Add New Feature
202 | 
203 | **New data model**:
204 | 1. Create class inheriting from `ObjectModel` with `table_name` ClassVar
205 | 2. Define Pydantic fields and validators
206 | 3. Override `save()` to submit embedding command if searchable (use `submit_command("embed_*", id)`)
207 | 4. Add custom methods for domain logic (get_X, add_to_Y)
208 | 5. Register in domain/__init__.py exports
209 | 
210 | **New workflow**:
211 | 1. Create state machine in graphs/WORKFLOW.py using StateGraph
212 | 2. Import domain models and provision_langchain_model()
213 | 3. Define nodes as async functions taking State, returning dict
214 | 4. Compile with graph.compile()
215 | 5. Invoke from API endpoint or Streamlit page
216 | 
217 | **New AI model type**:
218 | 1. Add type string to Model class
219 | 2. Add AIFactory.create_* method in Esperanto
220 | 3. Handle in ModelManager.get_model()
221 | 4. Add DefaultModels field + getter
222 | 
223 | ## Key Dependencies
224 | 
225 | - **surrealdb**: AsyncSurreal client, RecordID type
226 | - **pydantic**: Validation, field_validator
227 | - **langgraph**: StateGraph, Send, SqliteSaver, async/sync bridging
228 | - **langchain_core**: Messages, OutputParser, RunnableConfig
229 | - **esperanto**: Multi-provider AI model abstraction (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, Ollama, etc.)
230 | - **content-core**: File/URL content extraction
231 | - **ai_prompter**: Jinja2 template rendering for prompts
232 | - **surreal_commands**: Async job queue for embeddings, podcast generation
233 | - **loguru**: Structured logging throughout
234 | - **tiktoken**: GPT token encoding for context window estimation
235 | 
236 | ## Codebase Statistics
237 | 
238 | - **Modules**: 6 core layers + support services
239 | - **Async operations**: Database, AI provisioning, graph execution, embedding, job tracking
240 | - **Supported AI providers**: 8+ (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, Ollama, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter)
241 | - **Domain models**: Notebook, Source, Note, SourceInsight, SourceEmbedding, ChatSession, Asset, Transformation, ContentSettings, EpisodeProfile, SpeakerProfile, PodcastEpisode
242 | - **Graph workflows**: 6 (source, chat, source_chat, ask, transformation, prompt)
243 |

168 | class TestDetectContentType:
169 |     """Test suite for combined content type detection."""
170 | 
171 |     def test_extension_takes_priority(self):
172 |         """Test that file extension takes priority over heuristics."""
173 |         # Text looks like markdown but file is .txt
174 |         md_text = "# Header\n\nSome [link](url) content"
175 |         content_type = detect_content_type(md_text, "file.txt")
176 |         # Should use extension (plain) unless heuristics are very high confidence
177 |         # In this case, markdown confidence might override
178 |         assert content_type in (ContentType.PLAIN, ContentType.MARKDOWN)

180 |     def test_no_extension_uses_heuristics(self):
181 |         """Test that heuristics are used when no extension is available."""
182 |         html_text = "<!DOCTYPE html><html><body>Test</body></html>"
183 |         content_type = detect_content_type(html_text, None)
184 |         assert content_type == ContentType.HTML
185 | 
186 |     def test_extension_html(self):
187 |         """Test HTML extension detection."""
188 |         content_type = detect_content_type("some text", "file.html")
189 |         assert content_type == ContentType.HTML
190 | 
191 |     def test_extension_markdown(self):
192 |         """Test Markdown extension detection."""
193 |         content_type = detect_content_type("some text", "file.md")
194 |         assert content_type == ContentType.MARKDOWN
195 | 
196 |     def test_high_confidence_override(self):
197 |         """Test that very high confidence heuristics can override plain extension."""
198 |         # Strong HTML indicators in a .txt file
199 |         html_text = "<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><title>Test</title></head><body><div><p>Content</p></div></body></html>"
200 |         content_type = detect_content_type(html_text, "file.txt")
201 |         # High confidence HTML should override .txt extension
202 |         assert content_type == ContentType.HTML
203 | 
204 | 
205 | # ============================================================================
206 | # TEST SUITE 4: Text Chunking
207 | # ============================================================================
208 | 
209 | 
210 | class TestChunkText:
211 |     """Test suite for text chunking functionality."""
212 | 
213 |     def test_empty_text(self):
214 |         """Test chunking empty text."""
215 |         assert chunk_text("") == []
216 |         assert chunk_text("   ") == []
217 | 
218 |     def test_short_text_no_chunking(self):
219 |         """Test that short text is not chunked."""
220 |         text = "This is a short text."
221 |         chunks = chunk_text(text)
222 |         assert len(chunks) == 1
223 |         assert chunks[0] == text
224 | 
225 |     def test_text_at_chunk_limit(self):
226 |         """Test text at exactly chunk size limit."""
227 |         text = "x" * CHUNK_SIZE
228 |         chunks = chunk_text(text)
229 |         assert len(chunks) == 1
230 | 
231 |     def test_long_text_is_chunked(self):
232 |         """Test that long text is chunked."""
233 |         # Create text longer than chunk size
234 |         text = "This is a sentence. " * 200  # ~4000 chars
235 |         chunks = chunk_text(text)
236 |         assert len(chunks) > 1
237 |         # Each chunk should be <= CHUNK_SIZE
238 |         for chunk in chunks:
239 |             assert len(chunk) <= CHUNK_SIZE + 100  # Allow some flexibility for overlap
240 | 
241 |     def test_explicit_content_type_html(self):
242 |         """Test chunking with explicit HTML content type."""
243 |         html_text = """<html>
244 | <body>
245 | <h1>Main Title</h1>
246 | <p>First paragraph with lots of content.</p>
247 | <h2>Section</h2>
248 | <p>Second paragraph.</p>
249 | </body>
250 | </html>"""
251 |         chunks = chunk_text(html_text, content_type=ContentType.HTML)
252 |         assert len(chunks) >= 1
253 | 
254 |     def test_explicit_content_type_markdown(self):
255 |         """Test chunking with explicit Markdown content type."""
256 |         md_text = """# Main Title
257 | 
258 | Introduction paragraph.
259 | 
260 | ## Section 1
261 | 
262 | Content for section 1.
263 | 
264 | ## Section 2
265 | 
266 | Content for section 2.
267 | """
268 |         chunks = chunk_text(md_text, content_type=ContentType.MARKDOWN)
269 |         assert len(chunks) >= 1
270 | 
271 |     def test_explicit_content_type_plain(self):
272 |         """Test chunking with explicit plain content type."""
273 |         plain_text = "Word " * 500  # ~2500 chars
274 |         chunks = chunk_text(plain_text, content_type=ContentType.PLAIN)
275 |         assert len(chunks) >= 1
276 | 
277 |     def test_file_path_detection(self):
278 |         """Test chunking with file path for content type detection."""
279 |         text = "Some content here"
280 |         chunks = chunk_text(text, file_path="document.md")
281 |         assert len(chunks) == 1
282 | 
283 |     def test_secondary_chunking_for_large_sections(self):
284 |         """Test that large sections from HTML/MD splitters are further chunked."""
285 |         # Create text that would produce a single large section
286 |         large_section = "x" * 3000  # Larger than CHUNK_SIZE
287 |         md_text = f"# Title\n\n{large_section}"
288 |         chunks = chunk_text(md_text, content_type=ContentType.MARKDOWN)
289 |         # Should have multiple chunks due to secondary chunking
290 |         assert len(chunks) >= 1
291 |         for chunk in chunks:
292 |             # Allow some flexibility but chunks should be reasonable size
293 |             assert len(chunk) <= CHUNK_SIZE + 300
294 | 
295 | 
296 | if __name__ == "__main__":
297 |     pytest.main([__file__, "-v"])
298 |

/docs/5-CONFIGURATION/advanced.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Advanced Configuration
  2 | 
  3 | Performance tuning, debugging, and advanced features.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## Performance Tuning
  8 | 
  9 | ### Concurrency Control
 10 | 
 11 | ```env
 12 | # Max concurrent database operations (default: 5)
 13 | # Increase: Faster processing, more conflicts
 14 | # Decrease: Slower, fewer conflicts
 15 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS=5
 16 | ```
 17 | 
 18 | **Guidelines:**
 19 | - CPU: 2 cores → 2-3 tasks
 20 | - CPU: 4 cores → 5 tasks (default)
 21 | - CPU: 8+ cores → 10-20 tasks
 22 | 
 23 | Higher concurrency = more throughput but more database conflicts (retries handle this).
 24 | 
 25 | ### Retry Strategy
 26 | 
 27 | ```env
 28 | # How to wait between retries
 29 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_WAIT_STRATEGY=exponential_jitter
 30 | 
 31 | # Options:
 32 | # - exponential_jitter (recommended)
 33 | # - exponential
 34 | # - fixed
 35 | # - random
 36 | ```
 37 | 
 38 | For high-concurrency deployments, use `exponential_jitter` to prevent thundering herd.
 39 | 
 40 | ### Timeout Tuning
 41 | 
 42 | ```env
 43 | # Client timeout (default: 300 seconds)
 44 | API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=300
 45 | 
 46 | # LLM timeout (default: 60 seconds)
 47 | ESPERANTO_LLM_TIMEOUT=60
 48 | ```
 49 | 
 50 | **Guideline:** Set `API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT` > `ESPERANTO_LLM_TIMEOUT` + buffer
 51 | 
 52 | ```
 53 | Example:
 54 |   ESPERANTO_LLM_TIMEOUT=120
 55 |   API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=180  # 120 + 60 second buffer
 56 | ```
 57 | 
 58 | ---
 59 | 
 60 | ## Batching
 61 | 
 62 | ### TTS Batch Size
 63 | 
 64 | For podcast generation, control concurrent TTS requests:
 65 | 
 66 | ```env
 67 | # Default: 5
 68 | TTS_BATCH_SIZE=2
 69 | ```
 70 | 
 71 | **Providers and recommendations:**
 72 | - OpenAI: 5 (can handle many concurrent)
 73 | - Google: 4 (good concurrency)
 74 | - ElevenLabs: 2 (limited concurrent requests)
 75 | - Local TTS: 1 (single-threaded)
 76 | 
 77 | Lower = slower but more stable. Higher = faster but more load on provider.
 78 | 
 79 | ---
 80 | 
 81 | ## Logging & Debugging
 82 | 
 83 | ### Enable Detailed Logging
 84 | 
 85 | ```bash
 86 | # Start with debug logging
 87 | RUST_LOG=debug  # For Rust components
 88 | LOGLEVEL=DEBUG  # For Python components
 89 | ```
 90 | 
 91 | ### Debug Specific Components
 92 | 
 93 | ```bash
 94 | # Only surreal operations
 95 | RUST_LOG=surrealdb=debug
 96 | 
 97 | # Only langchain
 98 | LOGLEVEL=langchain:debug
 99 | 
100 | # Only specific module
101 | RUST_LOG=open_notebook::database=debug
102 | ```
103 | 
104 | ### LangSmith Tracing
105 | 
106 | For debugging LLM workflows:
107 | 
108 | ```env
109 | LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=true
110 | LANGCHAIN_ENDPOINT="https://api.smith.langchain.com"
111 | LANGCHAIN_API_KEY=your-key
112 | LANGCHAIN_PROJECT="Open Notebook"
113 | ```
114 | 
115 | Then visit https://smith.langchain.com to see traces.
116 | 
117 | ---
118 | 
119 | ## Port Configuration
120 | 
121 | ### Default Ports
122 | 
123 | ```
124 | Frontend: 8502 (Docker deployment)
125 | Frontend: 3000 (Development from source)
126 | API: 5055
127 | SurrealDB: 8000
128 | ```
129 | 
130 | ### Changing Frontend Port
131 | 
132 | Edit `docker-compose.yml`:
133 | 
134 | ```yaml
135 | services:
136 |   open-notebook:
137 |     ports:
138 |       - "8001:8502"  # Change from 8502 to 8001
139 | ```
140 | 
141 | Access at: `http://localhost:8001`
142 | 
143 | API auto-detects to: `http://localhost:5055` ✓
144 | 
145 | ### Changing API Port
146 | 
147 | ```yaml
148 | services:
149 |   open-notebook:
150 |     ports:
151 |       - "127.0.0.1:8502:8502"  # Frontend
152 |       - "5056:5055"            # Change API from 5055 to 5056
153 |     environment:
154 |       - API_URL=http://localhost:5056  # Update API_URL
155 | ```
156 | 
157 | Access API directly: `http://localhost:5056/docs`
158 | 
159 | **Note:** When changing API port, you must set `API_URL` explicitly since auto-detection assumes port 5055.
160 | 
161 | ### Changing SurrealDB Port
162 | 
163 | ```yaml
164 | services:
165 |   surrealdb:
166 |     ports:
167 |       - "8001:8000"  # Change from 8000 to 8001
168 |     environment:
169 |       - SURREAL_URL=ws://surrealdb:8001/rpc  # Update connection URL
170 | ```
171 | 
172 | **Important:** Internal Docker network uses container name (`surrealdb`), not `localhost`.
173 | 
174 | ---
175 | 
176 | ## SSL/TLS Configuration
177 | 
178 | ### Custom CA Certificate
179 | 
180 | For self-signed certs on local providers:
181 | 
182 | ```env
183 | ESPERANTO_SSL_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/ca-bundle.pem
184 | ```
185 | 
186 | ### Disable Verification (Development Only)
187 | 
188 | ```env
189 | # WARNING: Only for testing/development
190 | # Vulnerable to MITM attacks
191 | ESPERANTO_SSL_VERIFY=false
192 | ```
193 | 
194 | ---
195 | 
196 | ## Multi-Provider Setup
197 | 
198 | ### Use Different Providers for Different Tasks
199 | 
200 | ```env
201 | # Language model (main)
202 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...
203 | 
204 | # Embeddings (alternative)
205 | # (Future: Configure different embedding provider)
206 | 
207 | # TTS (different provider)
208 | ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=...
209 | ```
210 | 
211 | ### OpenAI-Compatible with Fallback
212 | 
213 | ```env
214 | # Primary
215 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:1234/v1
216 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY=key1
217 | 
218 | # Can also set specific modality endpoints
219 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_LLM=http://localhost:1234/v1
220 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_EMBEDDING=http://localhost:8001/v1
221 | ```
222 | 
223 | ---
224 | 
225 | ## Security Hardening
226 | 
227 | ### Change Default Credentials
228 | 
229 | ```env
230 | # Don't use defaults in production
231 | SURREAL_USER=your_secure_username
232 | SURREAL_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -base64 32)  # Generate secure password
233 | ```
234 | 
235 | ### Add Password Protection
236 | 
237 | ```env
238 | # Protect your Open Notebook instance
239 | OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD=your_secure_password
240 | ```
241 | 
242 | ### Use HTTPS
243 | 
244 | ```env
245 | # Always use HTTPS in production
246 | API_URL=https://mynotebook.example.com
247 | ```
248 | 
249 | ### Firewall Rules
250 | 
251 | Restrict access to your Open Notebook:
252 | - Port 8502 (frontend): Only from your IP
253 | - Port 5055 (API): Only from frontend
254 | - Port 8000 (SurrealDB): Never expose to internet
255 | 
256 | ---
257 | 
258 | ## Web Scraping & Content Extraction
259 | 
260 | Open Notebook uses multiple services for content extraction:
261 | 
262 | ### Firecrawl
263 | 
264 | For advanced web scraping:
265 | 
266 | ```env
267 | FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=your-key
268 | ```
269 | 
270 | Get key from: https://firecrawl.dev/
271 | 
272 | ### Jina AI
273 | 
274 | Alternative web extraction:
275 | 
276 | ```env
277 | JINA_API_KEY=your-key
278 | ```
279 | 
280 | Get key from: https://jina.ai/
281 | 
282 | ---
283 | 
284 | ## Environment Variable Groups
285 | 
286 | ### API Keys (Choose at least one)
287 | ```env
288 | OPENAI_API_KEY
289 | ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
290 | GOOGLE_API_KEY
291 | GROQ_API_KEY
292 | MISTRAL_API_KEY
293 | DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
294 | OPENROUTER_API_KEY
295 | XAI_API_KEY
296 | ```
297 | 
298 | ### AI Provider Endpoints
299 | ```env
300 | OLLAMA_API_BASE
301 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL
302 | AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT
303 | GEMINI_API_BASE_URL
304 | ```
305 | 
306 | ### Database
307 | ```env
308 | SURREAL_URL
309 | SURREAL_USER
310 | SURREAL_PASSWORD
311 | SURREAL_NAMESPACE
312 | SURREAL_DATABASE
313 | ```
314 | 
315 | ### Performance
316 | ```env
317 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS
318 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_ENABLED
319 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS
320 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_WAIT_STRATEGY
321 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_WAIT_MIN
322 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_WAIT_MAX
323 | ```
324 | 
325 | ### API Settings
326 | ```env
327 | API_URL
328 | INTERNAL_API_URL
329 | API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT
330 | ESPERANTO_LLM_TIMEOUT
331 | ```
332 | 
333 | ### Audio/TTS
334 | ```env
335 | ELEVENLABS_API_KEY
336 | TTS_BATCH_SIZE
337 | ```
338 | 
339 | ### Debugging
340 | ```env
341 | LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2
342 | LANGCHAIN_ENDPOINT
343 | LANGCHAIN_API_KEY
344 | LANGCHAIN_PROJECT
345 | ```
346 | 
347 | ---
348 | 
349 | ## Testing Configuration
350 | 
351 | ### Quick Test
352 | 
353 | ```bash
354 | # Add test config
355 | export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-test-key
356 | export API_URL=http://localhost:5055
357 | 
358 | # Test connection
359 | curl http://localhost:5055/health
360 | 
361 | # Test with sample
362 | curl -X POST http://localhost:5055/api/chat \
363 |   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
364 |   -d '{"message":"Hello"}'
365 | ```
366 | 
367 | ### Validate Config
368 | 
369 | ```bash
370 | # Check environment variables are set
371 | env | grep OPENAI_API_KEY
372 | 
373 | # Verify database connection
374 | python -c "import os; print(os.getenv('SURREAL_URL'))"
375 | ```
376 | 
377 | ---
378 | 
379 | ## Troubleshooting Performance
380 | 
381 | ### High Memory Usage
382 | 
383 | ```env
384 | # Reduce concurrency
385 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS=2
386 | 
387 | # Reduce TTS batch size
388 | TTS_BATCH_SIZE=1
389 | ```
390 | 
391 | ### High CPU Usage
392 | 
393 | ```env
394 | # Check worker count
395 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS
396 | 
397 | # Reduce if maxed out:
398 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS=5
399 | ```
400 | 
401 | ### Slow Responses
402 | 
403 | ```env
404 | # Check timeout settings
405 | API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=300
406 | 
407 | # Check retry config
408 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3
409 | ```
410 | 
411 | ### Database Conflicts
412 | 
413 | ```env
414 | # Reduce concurrency
415 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS=3
416 | 
417 | # Use jitter strategy
418 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_WAIT_STRATEGY=exponential_jitter
419 | ```
420 | 
421 | ---
422 | 
423 | ## Backup & Restore
424 | 
425 | ### Data Locations
426 | 
427 | | Path | Contents |
428 | |------|----------|
429 | | `./data` or `/app/data` | Uploads, podcasts, checkpoints |
430 | | `./surreal_data` or `/mydata` | SurrealDB database files |
431 | 
432 | ### Quick Backup
433 | 
434 | ```bash
435 | # Stop services (recommended for consistency)
436 | docker compose down
437 | 
438 | # Create timestamped backup
439 | tar -czf backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).tar.gz \
440 |   notebook_data/ surreal_data/
441 | 
442 | # Restart services
443 | docker compose up -d
444 | ```
445 | 
446 | ### Automated Backup Script
447 | 
448 | ```bash
449 | #!/bin/bash
450 | # backup.sh - Run daily via cron
451 | 
452 | BACKUP_DIR="/path/to/backups"
453 | DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
454 | 
455 | # Create backup
456 | tar -czf "$BACKUP_DIR/open-notebook-$DATE.tar.gz" \
457 |   /path/to/notebook_data \
458 |   /path/to/surreal_data
459 | 
460 | # Keep only last 7 days
461 | find "$BACKUP_DIR" -name "open-notebook-*.tar.gz" -mtime +7 -delete
462 | 
463 | echo "Backup complete: open-notebook-$DATE.tar.gz"
464 | ```
465 | 
466 | Add to cron:
467 | ```bash
468 | # Daily backup at 2 AM
469 | 0 2 * * * /path/to/backup.sh >> /var/log/open-notebook-backup.log 2>&1
470 | ```
471 | 
472 | ### Restore
473 | 
474 | ```bash
475 | # Stop services
476 | docker compose down
477 | 
478 | # Remove old data (careful!)
479 | rm -rf notebook_data/ surreal_data/
480 | 
481 | # Extract backup
482 | tar -xzf backup-20240115-120000.tar.gz
483 | 
484 | # Restart services
485 | docker compose up -d
486 | ```
487 | 
488 | ### Migration Between Servers
489 | 
490 | ```bash
491 | # On source server
492 | docker compose down
493 | tar -czf open-notebook-migration.tar.gz notebook_data/ surreal_data/
494 | 
495 | # Transfer to new server
496 | scp open-notebook-migration.tar.gz user@newserver:/path/
497 | 
498 | # On new server
499 | tar -xzf open-notebook-migration.tar.gz
500 | docker compose up -d
501 | ```
502 | 
503 | ---
504 | 
505 | ## Container Management
506 | 
507 | ### Common Commands
508 | 
509 | ```bash
510 | # Start services
511 | docker compose up -d
512 | 
513 | # Stop services
514 | docker compose down
515 | 
516 | # View logs (all services)
517 | docker compose logs -f
518 | 
519 | # View logs (specific service)
520 | docker compose logs -f api
521 | 
522 | # Restart specific service
523 | docker compose restart api
524 | 
525 | # Update to latest version
526 | docker compose down
527 | docker compose pull
528 | docker compose up -d
529 | 
530 | # Check resource usage
531 | docker stats
532 | 
533 | # Check service health
534 | docker compose ps
535 | ```
536 | 
537 | ### Clean Up
538 | 
539 | ```bash
540 | # Remove stopped containers
541 | docker compose rm
542 | 
543 | # Remove unused images
544 | docker image prune
545 | 
546 | # Full cleanup (careful!)
547 | docker system prune -a
548 | ```
549 | 
550 | ---
551 | 
552 | ## Summary
553 | 
554 | **Most deployments need:**
555 | - One AI provider API key
556 | - Default database settings
557 | - Default timeouts
558 | 
559 | **Tune performance only if:**
560 | - You have specific bottlenecks
561 | - High-concurrency workload
562 | - Custom hardware (very fast or very slow)
563 | 
564 | **Advanced features:**
565 | - Firecrawl for better web scraping
566 | - LangSmith for debugging workflows
567 | - Custom CA bundles for self-signed certs
568 |
