/docs/2-CORE-CONCEPTS/podcasts-explained.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Podcasts Explained - Research as Audio Dialogue
  2 | 
  3 | Podcasts are Open Notebook's highest-level transformation: converting your research into audio dialogue for a different consumption pattern.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## Why Podcasts Matter
  8 | 
  9 | ### The Problem
 10 | Research naturally accumulates as text: PDFs, articles, web pages, notes. This creates a friction point:
 11 | 
 12 | **To consume research, you must:**
 13 | - Sit down at a desk
 14 | - Focus intently
 15 | - Read actively
 16 | - Take notes
 17 | - Set aside dedicated time
 18 | 
 19 | **But much of life is passive time:**
 20 | - Commuting
 21 | - Exercising
 22 | - Doing dishes
 23 | - Driving
 24 | - Walking
 25 | - Idle moments
 26 | 
 27 | ### The Solution
 28 | Convert your research into audio dialogue so you can consume it passively.
 29 | 
 30 | ```
 31 | Before (Text-based):
 32 |   Research pile → Must schedule reading time → Requires focus
 33 | 
 34 | After (Podcast):
 35 |   Research pile → Podcast → Can listen while commuting
 36 |                          → Absorb while exercising
 37 |                          → Understand while walking
 38 |                          → Engage without screen time
 39 | ```
 40 | 
 41 | ---
 42 | 
 43 | ## What Makes It Special: Open Notebook vs. Competitors
 44 | 
 45 | ### Google Notebook LM Podcasts
 46 | - **Fixed format**: 2 hosts, always conversational
 47 | - **Limited customization**: You can't choose who the "hosts" are
 48 | - **One TTS voice per speaker**: Can't customize voices
 49 | - **Only uses cloud services**: No local options
 50 | 
 51 | ### Open Notebook Podcasts
 52 | - **Customizable format**: 1-4 speakers, you design them
 53 | - **Rich speaker profiles**: Create personas with backstories and expertise
 54 | - **Multiple TTS options**:
 55 |   - OpenAI (natural, fast)
 56 |   - Google TTS (high quality)
 57 |   - ElevenLabs (beautiful voices, accents)
 58 |   - Local TTS (privacy-first, no API calls)
 59 | - **Async generation**: Doesn't block your work
 60 | - **Full control**: Choose outline structure, tone, depth
 61 | 
 62 | ---
 63 | 
 64 | ## How Podcast Generation Works
 65 | 
 66 | ### Stage 1: Content Selection
 67 | 
 68 | You choose what goes into the podcast:
 69 | ```
 70 | Notebook content → Which sources? → Which notes?
 71 |                 → Which topics to focus on?
 72 |                 → Depth of coverage?
 73 | ```
 74 | 
 75 | ### Stage 2: Episode Profile
 76 | 
 77 | You define how you want the podcast structured:
 78 | ```
 79 | Episode Profile
 80 | ├─ Topic: "AI Safety Approaches"
 81 | ├─ Length: 20 minutes
 82 | ├─ Tone: Academic but accessible
 83 | ├─ Format: Debate (2 speakers with opposing views)
 84 | ├─ Audience: Researchers new to the field
 85 | └─ Focus areas: Main approaches, pros/cons, open questions
 86 | ```
 87 | 
 88 | ### Stage 3: Speaker Configuration
 89 | 
 90 | You create speaker personas (1-4 speakers):
 91 | 
 92 | ```
 93 | Speaker 1: "Expert Alex"
 94 | ├─ Expertise: "Deep knowledge of alignment research"
 95 | ├─ Personality: "Rigorous, academic, patient with explanation"
 96 | ├─ Accent: (Optional) "British English"
 97 | └─ TTS Voice: "OpenAI Onyx" (or ElevenLabs, Google, etc.)
 98 | 
 99 | Speaker 2: "Researcher Sam"
100 | ├─ Expertise: "Field observer, pragmatic perspective"
101 | ├─ Personality: "Curious, asks clarifying questions"
102 | ├─ Accent: "American English"
103 | └─ TTS Voice: "ElevenLabs - thoughtful"
104 | ```
105 | 
106 | ### Stage 4: Outline Generation
107 | 
108 | System generates episode outline:
109 | ```
110 | EPISODE: "AI Safety Approaches"
111 | 
112 | 1. Introduction (2 min)
113 |    Alex: Introduces topic and speakers
114 |    Sam: What will we cover today?
115 | 
116 | 2. Main Approaches (8 min)
117 |    Alex: Explains top 3 approaches
118 |    Sam: Asks about tradeoffs
119 | 
120 | 3. Debate: Best approach? (6 min)
121 |    Alex: Advocates for approach A
122 |    Sam: Argues for approach B
123 | 
124 | 4. Open Questions (3 min)
125 |    Both: What's unsolved?
126 | 
127 | 5. Conclusion (1 min)
128 |    Recap and where to learn more
129 | ```
130 | 
131 | ### Stage 5: Dialogue Generation
132 | 
133 | System generates dialogue based on outline:
134 | ```
135 | Alex: "Today we're exploring three major approaches to AI alignment..."
136 | 
137 | Sam: "That's a great start. Can you break down what we mean by alignment?"
138 | 
139 | Alex: "Good question. Alignment means ensuring AI systems pursue the goals
140 |        we actually want them to pursue, not just what we literally asked for.
141 |        There's a classic example of a paperclip maximizer..."
142 | 
143 | Sam: "Interesting. So it's about solving the intention problem?"
144 | 
145 | Alex: "Exactly. And that's where the three approaches come in..."
146 | ```
147 | 
148 | ### Stage 6: Text-to-Speech
149 | 
150 | System converts dialogue to audio:
151 | ```
152 | Alex's text → OpenAI TTS → Alex's voice (audio file)
153 | Sam's text → ElevenLabs TTS → Sam's voice (audio file)
154 | Audio files → Mix together → Final podcast MP3
155 | ```
156 | 
157 | ---
158 | 
159 | ## Key Architecture Decisions
160 | 
161 | ### 1. Asynchronous Processing
162 | Podcasts are generated in the background. You upload → system processes → you download when ready.
163 | 
164 | **Why?** Podcast generation takes time (10+ minutes for a 30-minute episode). Blocking would lock up your interface.
165 | 
166 | ### 2. Multi-Speaker Support
167 | Unlike Google Notebook LM (always 2 hosts), you choose 1-4 speakers.
168 | 
169 | **Why?** Different discussions work better with different formats:
170 | - Expert monologue (1 speaker)
171 | - Interview (2 speakers: host + expert)
172 | - Debate (2 speakers: opposing views)
173 | - Panel discussion (3-4 speakers: different expertise)
174 | 
175 | ### 3. Speaker Customization
176 | You create rich speaker profiles, not just "Host A" and "Host B".
177 | 
178 | **Why?** Makes podcasts more engaging and authentic. Different speakers bring different perspectives.
179 | 
180 | ### 4. Multiple TTS Providers
181 | You're not locked into one voice provider.
182 | 
183 | **Why?**
184 | - Cost optimization (some providers cheaper)
185 | - Quality preferences (some voices more natural)
186 | - Privacy options (local TTS for sensitive content)
187 | - Accessibility (different accents, genders, styles)
188 | 
189 | ### 5. Local TTS Option
190 | Can generate podcasts entirely offline with local text-to-speech.
191 | 
192 | **Why?** For sensitive research, never send audio to external APIs.
193 | 
194 | ---
195 | 
196 | ## Use Cases Show Why This Matters
197 | 
198 | ### Academic Publishing
199 | ```
200 | Traditional: Academic paper → PDF
201 | Problem: Hard to consume, linear reading required
202 | 
203 | Open Notebook:
204 | Research materials → Podcast (expert explaining methodology)
205 |                   → Podcast (debate format: different interpretations)
206 |                   → Different consumption for different audiences
207 | ```
208 | 
209 | ### Content Creation
210 | ```
211 | Blog creator: Has research pile on a topic
212 | Problem: Doesn't have time to write the article
213 | 
214 | Solution:
215 | Add research → Create podcast → Transcribe → Becomes article
216 | OR: Podcast BECOMES the content (upload to podcast platforms)
217 | ```
218 | 
219 | ### Educational Content
220 | ```
221 | Educator: Has reading materials for a course
222 | Problem: Students don't read the papers
223 | 
224 | Solution:
225 | Create podcast with expert explaining papers
226 | Students listen → Better engagement → Discussions can reference podcast
227 | ```
228 | 
229 | ### Market Research
230 | ```
231 | Product manager: Has interviews with customers
232 | Problem: Too many hours of audio to review
233 | 
234 | Solution:
235 | Create podcast with debate format (customer perspective vs. team perspective)
236 | Much more engaging than raw transcripts
237 | ```
238 | 
239 | ### Knowledge Transfer
240 | ```
241 | Domain expert: Leaving the organization
242 | Problem: How to preserve expertise?
243 | 
244 | Solution:
245 | Create expert-mode podcast explaining frameworks, decision-making, context
246 | New team member listens, gets context faster than reading 100 documents
247 | ```
248 | 
249 | ---
250 | 
251 | ## The Difference: Active vs. Passive Learning
252 | 
253 | ### Text-Based Research (Active)
254 | - **Effort**: High (must focus, read, synthesize)
255 | - **When**: Dedicated study time
256 | - **Cost**: Time is expensive (can't multitask)
257 | - **Best for**: Deep dives, precise information
258 | - **Format**: Whatever you write (notes, articles, books)
259 | 
260 | ### Audio Podcast (Passive)
261 | - **Effort**: Low (just listen)
262 | - **When**: Anywhere, anytime
263 | - **Cost**: Low (can multitask)
264 | - **Best for**: Overview, context, exploration
265 | - **Format**: Dialogue (more engaging than narration)
266 | 
267 | **They complement each other:**
268 | 1. **First encounter**: Listen to podcast (passive, get context)
269 | 2. **Deep dive**: Read source materials (active, precise)
270 | 3. **Mastery**: Both together (understand big picture + details)
271 | 
272 | ---
273 | 
274 | ## How Podcasts Fit Into Your Workflow
275 | 
276 | ```
277 | 1. Build notebook (add sources)
278 |    ↓
279 | 2. Apply transformations (extract insights)
280 |    ↓
281 | 3. Chat/Ask (explore content)
282 |    ↓
283 | 4. Decide on podcast
284 |    ├─→ Create speaker profiles
285 |    ├─→ Define episode profile
286 |    ├─→ Choose TTS provider
287 |    └─→ Generate podcast
288 |    ↓
289 | 5. Listen while commuting/exercising
290 |    ↓
291 | 6. Reference sources for deep dive
292 |    ↓
293 | 7. Repeat for different formats/speakers/focus
294 | ```
295 | 
296 | ---
297 | 
298 | ## Advanced: Multiple Podcasts from Same Research
299 | 
300 | You can create different podcasts from the same sources:
301 | 
302 | ### Example: AI Safety Research
303 | ```
304 | Podcast 1: "Expert Monologue"
305 |   Speaker: Researcher explaining field
306 |   Format: Educational, comprehensive
307 |   Audience: Students new to field
308 | 
309 | Podcast 2: "Debate Format"
310 |   Speakers: Optimist vs. skeptic
311 |   Format: Discussion of tradeoffs
312 |   Audience: Advanced researchers
313 | 
314 | Podcast 3: "Interview Format"
315 |   Speakers: Journalist + expert
316 |   Format: Q&A about practical applications
317 |   Audience: Industry practitioners
318 | ```
319 | 
320 | Each tells the same story from different angles.
321 | 
322 | ---
323 | 
324 | ## Privacy & Data Considerations
325 | 
326 | ### Where Your Data Goes
327 | 
328 | **Option 1: Cloud TTS (Faster, Higher Quality)**
329 | ```
330 | Your outline → API call to TTS provider
331 |             → Audio returned
332 |             → Stored in your notebook
333 | 
334 | Provider sees: Your outlined script (not raw sources)
335 | Privacy level: Medium (outline is shared, sources aren't)
336 | ```
337 | 
338 | **Option 2: Local TTS (Slower, Maximum Privacy)**
339 | ```
340 | Your outline → Local TTS engine (runs on your machine)
341 |             → Audio generated locally
342 |             → Stored in your notebook
343 | 
344 | Provider sees: Nothing
345 | Privacy level: Maximum (everything local)
346 | ```
347 | 
348 | ### Recommendation
349 | - **Sensitive research**: Use local TTS, no API calls
350 | - **Less sensitive**: Use ElevenLabs or Google (both handle audio data professionally)
351 | - **Mixed**: Use local TTS for speakers reading sensitive content
352 | 
353 | ---
354 | 
355 | ## Cost Considerations
356 | 
357 | ### Cloud TTS Costs
358 | | Provider | Cost | Quality | Speed |
359 | |----------|------|---------|-------|
360 | | OpenAI | ~$0.015 per minute | Good | Fast |
361 | | Google | ~$0.004 per minute | Excellent | Fast |
362 | | ElevenLabs | ~$0.10 per minute | Exceptional | Medium |
363 | | Local TTS | Free | Basic | Slow |
364 | 
365 | A 30-minute podcast costs:
366 | - OpenAI: ~$0.45
367 | - Google: ~$0.12
368 | - ElevenLabs: ~$3.00
369 | - Local: Free (but slow)
370 | 
371 | ---
372 | 
373 | ## Summary: Why Podcasts Are Special
374 | 
375 | **Podcasts transform your research consumption:**
376 | 
377 | | Aspect | Text | Podcast |
378 | |--------|------|---------|
379 | | **How consumed?** | Active reading | Passive listening |
380 | | **Where consumed?** | Desk | Anywhere |
381 | | **Multitasking** | Hard | Easy |
382 | | **Time commitment** | Scheduled | Flexible |
383 | | **Format** | Whatever | Natural dialogue |
384 | | **Engagement** | Academic | Conversational |
385 | | **Accessibility** | Text-based | Audio-based |
386 | 
387 | **In Open Notebook specifically:**
388 | - **Full customization** — you create speakers and format
389 | - **Privacy options** — local TTS for sensitive content
390 | - **Cost control** — choose TTS provider based on budget
391 | - **Non-blocking** — generates in background
392 | - **Multiple versions** — create different podcasts from same research
393 | 
394 | This is why podcasts matter: they change *when* and *how* you can consume your research.
395 |

/docs/7-DEVELOPMENT/testing.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Testing Guide
  2 | 
  3 | This document provides guidelines for writing tests in Open Notebook. Testing is critical to maintaining code quality and preventing regressions.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Testing Philosophy
  6 | 
  7 | ### What to Test
  8 | 
  9 | Focus on testing the things that matter most:
 10 | 
 11 | - **Business Logic** - Core domain models and their operations
 12 | - **API Contracts** - HTTP endpoint behavior and error handling
 13 | - **Critical Workflows** - End-to-end flows that users depend on
 14 | - **Data Persistence** - Database operations and data integrity
 15 | - **Error Conditions** - How the system handles failures gracefully
 16 | 
 17 | ### What NOT to Test
 18 | 
 19 | Don't waste time testing framework code:
 20 | 
 21 | - Framework functionality (FastAPI, React, etc.)
 22 | - Third-party library implementation
 23 | - Simple getters/setters without logic
 24 | - View/presentation layer rendering (unless it contains logic)
 25 | 
 26 | ## Test Structure
 27 | 
 28 | We use **pytest** with async support for all Python tests:
 29 | 
 30 | ```python
 31 | import pytest
 32 | from httpx import AsyncClient
 33 | from open_notebook.domain.notebook import Notebook
 34 | 
 35 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
 36 | async def test_create_notebook():
 37 |     """Test notebook creation."""
 38 |     notebook = Notebook(name="Test Notebook", description="Test description")
 39 |     await notebook.save()
 40 | 
 41 |     assert notebook.id is not None
 42 |     assert notebook.name == "Test Notebook"
 43 |     assert notebook.created is not None
 44 | 
 45 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
 46 | async def test_api_create_notebook():
 47 |     """Test notebook creation via API."""
 48 |     async with AsyncClient(app=app, base_url="http://test") as client:
 49 |         response = await client.post(
 50 |             "/api/notebooks",
 51 |             json={"name": "Test Notebook", "description": "Test description"}
 52 |         )
 53 |         assert response.status_code == 200
 54 |         data = response.json()
 55 |         assert data["name"] == "Test Notebook"
 56 | ```
 57 | 
 58 | ## Test Categories
 59 | 
 60 | ### 1. Unit Tests
 61 | 
 62 | Test individual functions and methods in isolation:
 63 | 
 64 | ```python
 65 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
 66 | async def test_notebook_validation():
 67 |     """Test that notebook name validation works."""
 68 |     with pytest.raises(InvalidInputError):
 69 |         Notebook(name="", description="test")
 70 | 
 71 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
 72 | async def test_notebook_archive():
 73 |     """Test notebook archiving."""
 74 |     notebook = Notebook(name="Test", description="")
 75 |     notebook.archive()
 76 |     assert notebook.archived is True
 77 | ```
 78 | 
 79 | **Location**: `tests/unit/`
 80 | 
 81 | ### 2. Integration Tests
 82 | 
 83 | Test component interactions and database operations:
 84 | 
 85 | ```python
 86 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
 87 | async def test_create_notebook_with_sources():
 88 |     """Test creating a notebook and adding sources."""
 89 |     notebook = await create_notebook(name="Research", description="")
 90 |     source = await add_source(notebook_id=notebook.id, url="https://example.com")
 91 | 
 92 |     retrieved = await get_notebook_with_sources(notebook.id)
 93 |     assert len(retrieved.sources) == 1
 94 |     assert retrieved.sources[0].id == source.id
 95 | ```
 96 | 
 97 | **Location**: `tests/integration/`
 98 | 
 99 | ### 3. API Tests
100 | 
101 | Test HTTP endpoints and error responses:
102 | 
103 | ```python
104 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
105 | async def test_get_notebooks_endpoint():
106 |     """Test GET /notebooks endpoint."""
107 |     async with AsyncClient(app=app, base_url="http://test") as client:
108 |         response = await client.get("/api/notebooks")
109 |         assert response.status_code == 200
110 |         data = response.json()
111 |         assert isinstance(data, list)
112 | 
113 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
114 | async def test_create_notebook_validation():
115 |     """Test that invalid input is rejected."""
116 |     async with AsyncClient(app=app, base_url="http://test") as client:
117 |         response = await client.post(
118 |             "/api/notebooks",
119 |             json={"name": "", "description": ""}
120 |         )
121 |         assert response.status_code == 400
122 | ```
123 | 
124 | **Location**: `tests/api/`
125 | 
126 | ### 4. Database Tests
127 | 
128 | Test data persistence and query correctness:
129 | 
130 | ```python
131 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
132 | async def test_save_and_retrieve_notebook():
133 |     """Test saving and retrieving a notebook from database."""
134 |     notebook = Notebook(name="Test", description="desc")
135 |     await notebook.save()
136 | 
137 |     retrieved = await Notebook.get(notebook.id)
138 |     assert retrieved.name == "Test"
139 |     assert retrieved.description == "desc"
140 | 
141 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
142 | async def test_query_by_criteria():
143 |     """Test querying notebooks by criteria."""
144 |     await create_notebook("Active", "")
145 |     await create_notebook("Archived", "")
146 | 
147 |     active = await repo_query(
148 |         "SELECT * FROM notebook WHERE archived = false"
149 |     )
150 |     assert len(active) >= 1
151 | ```
152 | 
153 | **Location**: `tests/database/`
154 | 
155 | ## Running Tests
156 | 
157 | ### Run All Tests
158 | 
159 | ```bash
160 | uv run pytest
161 | ```
162 | 
163 | ### Run Specific Test File
164 | 
165 | ```bash
166 | uv run pytest tests/test_notebooks.py
167 | ```
168 | 
169 | ### Run Specific Test Function
170 | 
171 | ```bash
172 | uv run pytest tests/test_notebooks.py::test_create_notebook
173 | ```
174 | 
175 | ### Run with Coverage Report
176 | 
177 | ```bash
178 | uv run pytest --cov=open_notebook
179 | ```
180 | 
181 | ### Run Only Unit Tests
182 | 
183 | ```bash
184 | uv run pytest tests/unit/
185 | ```
186 | 
187 | ### Run Only Integration Tests
188 | 
189 | ```bash
190 | uv run pytest tests/integration/
191 | ```
192 | 
193 | ### Run Tests in Verbose Mode
194 | 
195 | ```bash
196 | uv run pytest -v
197 | ```
198 | 
199 | ### Run Tests with Output
200 | 
201 | ```bash
202 | uv run pytest -s
203 | ```
204 | 
205 | ## Test Fixtures
206 | 
207 | Use pytest fixtures for common setup and teardown:
208 | 
209 | ```python
210 | import pytest
211 | 
212 | @pytest.fixture
213 | async def test_notebook():
214 |     """Create a test notebook."""
215 |     notebook = Notebook(name="Test Notebook", description="Test description")
216 |     await notebook.save()
217 |     yield notebook
218 |     await notebook.delete()
219 | 
220 | @pytest.fixture
221 | async def api_client():
222 |     """Create an API test client."""
223 |     async with AsyncClient(app=app, base_url="http://test") as client:
224 |         yield client
225 | 
226 | @pytest.fixture
227 | async def test_notebook_with_sources(test_notebook):
228 |     """Create a test notebook with sample sources."""
229 |     source1 = Source(notebook_id=test_notebook.id, url="https://example.com")
230 |     source2 = Source(notebook_id=test_notebook.id, url="https://example.org")
231 |     await source1.save()
232 |     await source2.save()
233 | 
234 |     test_notebook.sources = [source1, source2]
235 |     yield test_notebook
236 | 
237 |     # Cleanup
238 |     await source1.delete()
239 |     await source2.delete()
240 | ```
241 | 
242 | ## Best Practices
243 | 
244 | ### 1. Write Descriptive Test Names
245 | 
246 | ```python
247 | # Good - clearly describes what is being tested
248 | async def test_create_notebook_with_valid_name_succeeds():
249 |     ...
250 | 
251 | # Bad - vague about what's being tested
252 | async def test_notebook():
253 |     ...
254 | ```
255 | 
256 | ### 2. Use Docstrings
257 | 
258 | ```python
259 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
260 | async def test_vector_search_returns_sorted_results():
261 |     """Test that vector search results are sorted by relevance score."""
262 |     # Implementation
263 | ```
264 | 
265 | ### 3. Test Edge Cases
266 | 
267 | ```python
268 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
269 | async def test_search_with_empty_query():
270 |     """Test that empty query raises error."""
271 |     with pytest.raises(InvalidInputError):
272 |         await vector_search("")
273 | 
274 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
275 | async def test_search_with_very_long_query():
276 |     """Test that very long query is handled."""
277 |     long_query = "x" * 10000
278 |     results = await vector_search(long_query)
279 |     assert isinstance(results, list)
280 | 
281 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
282 | async def test_search_with_special_characters():
283 |     """Test that special characters are handled."""
284 |     results = await vector_search("@#$%^&*()")
285 |     assert isinstance(results, list)
286 | ```
287 | 
288 | ### 4. Use Assertions Effectively
289 | 
290 | ```python
291 | # Good - specific assertions
292 | assert notebook.name == "Test"
293 | assert len(notebook.sources) == 3
294 | assert notebook.created is not None
295 | 
296 | # Less good - too broad
297 | assert notebook is not None
298 | assert notebook  # ambiguous what's being tested
299 | ```
300 | 
301 | ### 5. Test Both Success and Failure Cases
302 | 
303 | ```python
304 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
305 | async def test_create_notebook_success():
306 |     """Test successful notebook creation."""
307 |     notebook = await create_notebook(name="Research", description="AI")
308 |     assert notebook.id is not None
309 |     assert notebook.name == "Research"
310 | 
311 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
312 | async def test_create_notebook_empty_name_fails():
313 |     """Test that empty name raises error."""
314 |     with pytest.raises(InvalidInputError):
315 |         await create_notebook(name="", description="")
316 | 
317 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
318 | async def test_create_notebook_duplicate_fails():
319 |     """Test that duplicate names are handled."""
320 |     await create_notebook(name="Research", description="")
321 |     with pytest.raises(DuplicateError):
322 |         await create_notebook(name="Research", description="")
323 | ```
324 | 
325 | ### 6. Keep Tests Independent
326 | 
327 | ```python
328 | # Good - test is self-contained
329 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
330 | async def test_archive_notebook():
331 |     notebook = Notebook(name="Test", description="")
332 |     await notebook.save()
333 |     await notebook.archive()
334 |     assert notebook.archived is True
335 | 
336 | # Bad - depends on another test's state
337 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
338 | async def test_archive_existing_notebook():
339 |     # Assumes test_create_notebook ran first
340 |     await notebook.archive()  # notebook undefined
341 | ```
342 | 
343 | ### 7. Use Fixtures for Reusable Setup
344 | 
345 | ```python
346 | # Instead of repeating setup:
347 | @pytest.fixture
348 | async def client_with_auth(api_client, mock_auth):
349 |     """Client with authentication set up."""
350 |     api_client.headers.update({"Authorization": f"Bearer {mock_auth.token}"})
351 |     yield api_client
352 | 
353 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
354 | async def test_protected_endpoint(client_with_auth):
355 |     """Test protected endpoint."""
356 |     response = await client_with_auth.get("/api/protected")
357 |     assert response.status_code == 200
358 | ```
359 | 
360 | ## Coverage Goals
361 | 
362 | - Aim for 70%+ overall coverage
363 | - 90%+ coverage for critical business logic
364 | - Don't obsess over 100% - focus on meaningful tests
365 | - Use `--cov` flag to check coverage: `uv run pytest --cov=open_notebook`
366 | 
367 | ## Async Test Patterns
368 | 
369 | ### Testing Async Functions
370 | 
371 | ```python
372 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
373 | async def test_async_operation():
374 |     """Test async function."""
375 |     result = await some_async_function()
376 |     assert result is not None
377 | ```
378 | 
379 | ### Testing Concurrent Operations
380 | 
381 | ```python
382 | @pytest.mark.asyncio
383 | async def test_concurrent_notebook_creation():
384 |     """Test creating multiple notebooks concurrently."""
385 |     tasks = [
386 |         create_notebook(f"Notebook {i}", "")
387 |         for i in range(10)
388 |     ]
389 |     notebooks = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
390 |     assert len(notebooks) == 10
391 |     assert all(n.id for n in notebooks)
392 | ```
393 | 
394 | ## Common Testing Errors
395 | 
396 | ### Error: "event loop is closed"
397 | 
398 | Solution: Use the async fixture properly:
399 | ```python
400 | @pytest.fixture
401 | async def notebook():  # Use async fixture
402 |     notebook = Notebook(name="Test", description="")
403 |     await notebook.save()
404 |     yield notebook
405 |     await notebook.delete()
406 | ```
407 | 
408 | ### Error: "object is not awaitable"
409 | 
410 | Solution: Make sure you're using await:
411 | ```python
412 | # Wrong
413 | result = create_notebook("Test", "")
414 | 
415 | # Right
416 | result = await create_notebook("Test", "")
417 | ```
418 | 
419 | ---
420 | 
421 | **See also:**
422 | - [Code Standards](code-standards.md) - Code formatting and style
423 | - [Contributing Guide](contributing.md) - Overall contribution workflow
424 |

/docs/7-DEVELOPMENT/design-principles.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Design Principles & Project Vision
  2 | 
  3 | This document outlines the core principles, vision, and design philosophy that guide Open Notebook's development. All contributors should read and understand these principles before proposing changes or new features.
  4 | 
  5 | ## 🎯 Project Vision
  6 | 
  7 | Open Notebook aims to be a **privacy-focused, self-hosted alternative to Google's Notebook LM** that empowers users to:
  8 | 
  9 | 1. **Own their research data** - Full control over where data lives and who can access it
 10 | 2. **Choose their AI providers** - Freedom to use any AI provider or run models locally
 11 | 3. **Customize their workflows** - Flexibility to adapt the tool to different research needs
 12 | 4. **Access their work anywhere** - Through web UI, API, or integrations
 13 | 
 14 | ### What Open Notebook IS
 15 | 
 16 | - A **research assistant** for managing and understanding content
 17 | - A **platform** that connects various AI providers
 18 | - A **privacy-first** tool that keeps your data under your control
 19 | - An **extensible system** with APIs and customization options
 20 | 
 21 | ### What Open Notebook IS NOT
 22 | 
 23 | - A document editor (use Google Docs, Notion, etc. for that)
 24 | - A file storage system (use Dropbox, S3, etc. for that)
 25 | - A general-purpose chatbot (use ChatGPT, Claude, etc. for that)
 26 | - A replacement for your entire workflow (it's one tool in your toolkit)
 27 | 
 28 | ## 🏗️ Core Design Principles
 29 | 
 30 | ### 1. Privacy First
 31 | 
 32 | **Principle**: User data and research should stay under user control by default.
 33 | 
 34 | **In Practice**:
 35 | - Self-hosted deployment is the primary use case
 36 | - No telemetry or analytics without explicit opt-in
 37 | - No hard dependency on specific cloud services
 38 | - Clear documentation on what data goes where
 39 | 
 40 | **Example Decisions**:
 41 | - ✅ Support for local Ollama models
 42 | - ✅ Configurable AI provider selection
 43 | - ❌ Hard-coded cloud service integrations
 44 | - ❌ Required external service dependencies
 45 | 
 46 | ### 2. Simplicity Over Features
 47 | 
 48 | **Principle**: The tool should be easy to understand and use, even if it means fewer features.
 49 | 
 50 | **In Practice**:
 51 | - Clear, focused UI with well-defined sections
 52 | - Sensible defaults that work for most users
 53 | - Advanced features hidden behind optional configuration
 54 | - Documentation written for non-technical users
 55 | 
 56 | **Example Decisions**:
 57 | - ✅ Three-column layout (Sources, Notes, Chat)
 58 | - ✅ Default models that work out of the box
 59 | - ❌ Overwhelming users with too many options upfront
 60 | - ❌ Complex multi-step workflows for basic tasks
 61 | 
 62 | ### 3. API-First Architecture
 63 | 
 64 | **Principle**: All functionality should be accessible via API, not just the UI.
 65 | 
 66 | **In Practice**:
 67 | - UI calls the same API that external clients use
 68 | - Comprehensive REST API with OpenAPI documentation
 69 | - No "UI-only" features that can't be automated
 70 | - Clear separation between frontend and backend
 71 | 
 72 | **Example Decisions**:
 73 | - ✅ FastAPI backend with full API documentation
 74 | - ✅ Consistent API patterns across all endpoints
 75 | - ❌ Business logic in UI components
 76 | - ❌ Features that require direct database access
 77 | 
 78 | ### 4. Multi-Provider Flexibility
 79 | 
 80 | **Principle**: Users should never be locked into a single AI provider.
 81 | 
 82 | **In Practice**:
 83 | - Support for multiple AI providers through Esperanto library
 84 | - Easy switching between providers and models
 85 | - Clear documentation on provider limitations
 86 | - Graceful degradation when providers are unavailable
 87 | 
 88 | **Example Decisions**:
 89 | - ✅ Support for 16+ AI providers
 90 | - ✅ Per-feature model selection (chat, embeddings, TTS)
 91 | - ❌ Features that only work with OpenAI
 92 | - ❌ Hard-coded API endpoints for specific providers
 93 | 
 94 | ### 5. Extensibility Through Standards
 95 | 
 96 | **Principle**: The system should be extensible through well-defined interfaces, not by forking.
 97 | 
 98 | **In Practice**:
 99 | - Plugin systems for transformations and commands
100 | - Standard data formats (JSON, Markdown)
101 | - Clear extension points in the architecture
102 | - Documentation for common customization scenarios
103 | 
104 | **Example Decisions**:
105 | - ✅ Custom transformation templates
106 | - ✅ Background command system
107 | - ✅ Jinja2 prompt templates
108 | - ❌ Hard-coded business logic without extension points
109 | 
110 | ### 6. Async-First for Performance
111 | 
112 | **Principle**: Long-running operations should not block the user interface or API.
113 | 
114 | **In Practice**:
115 | - Async/await patterns throughout the backend
116 | - Background job processing for heavy workloads
117 | - Status updates and progress tracking
118 | - Graceful handling of slow AI provider responses
119 | 
120 | **Example Decisions**:
121 | - ✅ AsyncIO for database operations
122 | - ✅ Background commands for podcast generation
123 | - ✅ Streaming responses for chat
124 | - ❌ Synchronous blocking operations in API endpoints
125 | 
126 | ## 🎨 UI/UX Principles
127 | 
128 | ### Focus on Content, Not Chrome
129 | 
130 | - Minimize UI clutter and distractions
131 | - Content should occupy most of the screen space
132 | - Controls appear when needed, not always visible
133 | - Consistent layout across different views
134 | 
135 | ### Progressive Disclosure
136 | 
137 | - Show simple options first, advanced options on demand
138 | - Don't overwhelm new users with every possible setting
139 | - Provide sensible defaults that work for 80% of use cases
140 | - Make power features discoverable but not intrusive
141 | 
142 | ### Responsive and Fast
143 | 
144 | - UI should feel instant for common operations
145 | - Show loading states for operations that take time
146 | - Cache and optimize where possible
147 | - Degrade gracefully on slow connections
148 | 
149 | ## 🔧 Technical Principles
150 | 
151 | ### Clean Separation of Concerns
152 | 
153 | **Layers should not leak**:
154 | - Frontend should not know about database structure
155 | - API should not contain business logic (delegate to domain layer)
156 | - Domain models should not know about HTTP requests
157 | - Database layer should not know about AI providers
158 | 
159 | ### Type Safety and Validation
160 | 
161 | **Catch errors early**:
162 | - Use Pydantic models for all API boundaries
163 | - Type hints throughout Python codebase
164 | - TypeScript for frontend code
165 | - Validate data at system boundaries
166 | 
167 | ### Test What Matters
168 | 
169 | **Focus on valuable tests**:
170 | - Test business logic and domain models
171 | - Test API contracts and error handling
172 | - Don't test framework code (FastAPI, React, etc.)
173 | - Integration tests for critical workflows
174 | 
175 | ### Database as Source of Truth
176 | 
177 | **SurrealDB is our single source of truth**:
178 | - All state persisted in database
179 | - No business logic in database layer
180 | - Use SurrealDB features (record links, queries) appropriately
181 | - Schema migrations for all schema changes
182 | 
183 | ## 🚫 Anti-Patterns to Avoid
184 | 
185 | ### Feature Creep
186 | 
187 | **What it looks like**:
188 | - Adding features because they're "cool" or "easy"
189 | - Building features for edge cases before common cases work well
190 | - Trying to be everything to everyone
191 | 
192 | **Why we avoid it**:
193 | - Increases complexity and maintenance burden
194 | - Makes the tool harder to learn and use
195 | - Dilutes the core value proposition
196 | 
197 | **Instead**:
198 | - Focus on core use cases
199 | - Say no to features that don't align with vision
200 | - Build extensibility points for edge cases
201 | 
202 | ### Premature Optimization
203 | 
204 | **What it looks like**:
205 | - Optimizing code before knowing if it's slow
206 | - Complex caching strategies without measuring impact
207 | - Trading code clarity for marginal performance gains
208 | 
209 | **Why we avoid it**:
210 | - Makes code harder to understand and maintain
211 | - Optimizes the wrong things
212 | - Wastes development time
213 | 
214 | **Instead**:
215 | - Measure first, optimize second
216 | - Focus on algorithmic improvements
217 | - Profile before making performance changes
218 | 
219 | ### Over-Engineering
220 | 
221 | **What it looks like**:
222 | - Building abstraction layers "in case we need them later"
223 | - Implementing design patterns for 3-line functions
224 | - Creating frameworks instead of solving problems
225 | 
226 | **Why we avoid it**:
227 | - Increases cognitive load for contributors
228 | - Makes simple changes require touching many files
229 | - Hides the actual business logic
230 | 
231 | **Instead**:
232 | - Start simple, refactor when patterns emerge
233 | - Optimize for readability and clarity
234 | - Use abstractions when they simplify, not complicate
235 | 
236 | ### Breaking Changes Without Migration Path
237 | 
238 | **What it looks like**:
239 | - Changing database schema without migration scripts
240 | - Modifying API contracts without versioning
241 | - Removing features without deprecation warnings
242 | 
243 | **Why we avoid it**:
244 | - Breaks existing installations
245 | - Frustrates users and contributors
246 | - Creates maintenance nightmares
247 | 
248 | **Instead**:
249 | - Always provide migration scripts for schema changes
250 | - Deprecate before removing
251 | - Document breaking changes clearly
252 | 
253 | ## 🤝 Decision-Making Framework
254 | 
255 | When evaluating new features or changes, ask:
256 | 
257 | ### 1. Does it align with our vision?
258 | - Does it help users own their research data?
259 | - Does it support privacy and self-hosting?
260 | - Does it fit our core use cases?
261 | 
262 | ### 2. Does it follow our principles?
263 | - Is it simple to use and understand?
264 | - Does it work via API?
265 | - Does it support multiple providers?
266 | - Can it be extended by users?
267 | 
268 | ### 3. Is the implementation sound?
269 | - Does it maintain separation of concerns?
270 | - Is it properly typed and validated?
271 | - Does it include tests?
272 | - Is it documented?
273 | 
274 | ### 4. What is the cost?
275 | - How much complexity does it add?
276 | - How much maintenance burden?
277 | - Does it introduce new dependencies?
278 | - Will it be used enough to justify the cost?
279 | 
280 | ### 5. Are there alternatives?
281 | - Can existing features solve this problem?
282 | - Can this be built as a plugin or extension?
283 | - Should this be a separate tool instead?
284 | 
285 | ## 📚 Examples of Principle-Driven Decisions
286 | 
287 | ### Why we migrated from Streamlit to Next.js
288 | 
289 | **Principle**: API-First Architecture
290 | 
291 | **Reasoning**:
292 | - Streamlit coupled UI and backend logic
293 | - Difficult to build external integrations
294 | - Limited control over API behavior
295 | - Next.js + FastAPI provides clear separation
296 | 
297 | ### Why we use Esperanto for AI providers
298 | 
299 | **Principle**: Multi-Provider Flexibility
300 | 
301 | **Reasoning**:
302 | - Abstracts provider-specific details
303 | - Easy to add new providers
304 | - Consistent interface across providers
305 | - No vendor lock-in
306 | 
307 | ### Why we have a Background Command System
308 | 
309 | **Principle**: Async-First for Performance
310 | 
311 | **Reasoning**:
312 | - Podcast generation takes minutes
313 | - Users shouldn't wait for long operations
314 | - Need status tracking and error handling
315 | - Supports future batch operations
316 | 
317 | ### Why we support Local Ollama
318 | 
319 | **Principle**: Privacy First
320 | 
321 | **Reasoning**:
322 | - Enables fully offline operation
323 | - No data sent to external services
324 | - Free for users after hardware cost
325 | - Aligns with self-hosted philosophy
326 | 
327 | ## 🔄 Evolution of Principles
328 | 
329 | These principles are not set in stone. As the project grows and we learn from users, some principles may evolve. However, changes to core principles should be:
330 | 
331 | 1. **Well-justified** - Clear reasoning for why the change is needed
332 | 2. **Discussed openly** - Community input on major changes
333 | 3. **Documented** - Updated in this document with explanation
334 | 4. **Gradual** - Not implemented as breaking changes when possible
335 | 
336 | ---
337 | 
338 | ## For Contributors
339 | 
340 | When proposing a feature or change:
341 | 
342 | 1. **Reference these principles** - Explain how your proposal aligns
343 | 2. **Identify trade-offs** - Be honest about what you're trading for what
344 | 3. **Suggest alternatives** - Show you've considered other approaches
345 | 4. **Be open to feedback** - Maintainers may see concerns you don't
346 | 
347 | **Remember**: A "no" to a feature isn't a judgment on you or your idea. It means we're staying focused on our core vision. We appreciate all contributions and ideas!
348 | 
349 | ---
350 | 
351 | **Questions about these principles?** Open a discussion on GitHub or join our [Discord](https://discord.gg/37XJPXfz2w).
352 |

  4 | import { podcastsApi, EpisodeProfileInput, SpeakerProfileInput } from '@/lib/api/podcasts'
  5 | import { QUERY_KEYS } from '@/lib/api/query-client'
  6 | import { useToast } from '@/lib/hooks/use-toast'
  7 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
  8 | import { getApiErrorKey } from '@/lib/utils/error-handler'
  9 | import {
 10 |   ACTIVE_EPISODE_STATUSES,
 11 |   EpisodeProfile,
 12 |   EpisodeStatusGroups,
 13 |   PodcastEpisode,
 14 |   PodcastGenerationRequest,
 15 |   groupEpisodesByStatus,
 16 |   speakerUsageMap,
 17 | } from '@/lib/types/podcasts'
 18 | 
 19 | interface EpisodeStatusCounts {
 20 |   total: number
 21 |   running: number
 22 |   completed: number
 23 |   failed: number
 24 |   pending: number
 25 | }
 26 | 
 27 | function hasActiveEpisodes(episodes: PodcastEpisode[]) {
 28 |   return episodes.some((episode) => {
 29 |     const status = episode.job_status ?? 'unknown'
 30 |     return ACTIVE_EPISODE_STATUSES.includes(status)
 31 |   })
 32 | }
 33 | 
 34 | export function usePodcastEpisodes(options?: { autoRefresh?: boolean }) {
 35 |   const { autoRefresh = true } = options ?? {}
 36 | 
 37 |   const query = useQuery({
 38 |     queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.podcastEpisodes,
 39 |     queryFn: podcastsApi.listEpisodes,
 40 |     refetchInterval: (current) => {
 41 |       if (!autoRefresh) {
 42 |         return false
 43 |       }
 44 | 
 45 |       const data = current.state.data as PodcastEpisode[] | undefined
 46 |       if (!data || data.length === 0) {
 47 |         return false
 48 |       }
 49 | 
 50 |       return hasActiveEpisodes(data) ? 15_000 : false
 51 |     },
 52 |   })
 53 | 
 54 |   const episodes = useMemo(() => query.data ?? [], [query.data])
 55 | 
 56 |   const statusGroups = useMemo<EpisodeStatusGroups>(
 57 |     () => groupEpisodesByStatus(episodes),
 58 |     [episodes]
 59 |   )
 60 | 
 61 |   const statusCounts = useMemo<EpisodeStatusCounts>(
 62 |     () => ({
 63 |       total: episodes.length,
 64 |       running: statusGroups.running.length,
 65 |       completed: statusGroups.completed.length,
 66 |       failed: statusGroups.failed.length,
 67 |       pending: statusGroups.pending.length,
 68 |     }),
 69 |     [episodes.length, statusGroups]
 70 |   )
 71 | 
 72 |   const active = useMemo(() => hasActiveEpisodes(episodes), [episodes])
 73 | 
 74 |   return {
 75 |     ...query,
 76 |     episodes,
 77 |     statusGroups,
 78 |     statusCounts,
 79 |     hasActiveEpisodes: active,
 80 |   }
 81 | }

  1 | from typing import List, Optional
  2 | 
  3 | from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query
  4 | from loguru import logger
  5 | 
  6 | from api.models import (
  7 |     NotebookCreate,
  8 |     NotebookDeletePreview,
  9 |     NotebookDeleteResponse,
 10 |     NotebookResponse,
 11 |     NotebookUpdate,
 12 | )
 13 | from open_notebook.database.repository import ensure_record_id, repo_query
 14 | from open_notebook.domain.notebook import Notebook, Source
 15 | from open_notebook.exceptions import InvalidInputError
 16 | 
 17 | router = APIRouter()
 18 | 
 19 | 
 20 | @router.get("/notebooks", response_model=List[NotebookResponse])
 21 | async def get_notebooks(
 22 |     archived: Optional[bool] = Query(None, description="Filter by archived status"),
 23 |     order_by: str = Query("updated desc", description="Order by field and direction"),
 24 | ):
 25 |     """Get all notebooks with optional filtering and ordering."""
 26 |     try:
 27 |         # Build the query with counts
 28 |         query = f"""
 29 |             SELECT *,
 30 |             count(<-reference.in) as source_count,
 31 |             count(<-artifact.in) as note_count
 32 |             FROM notebook
 33 |             ORDER BY {order_by}
 34 |         """
 35 | 
 36 |         result = await repo_query(query)
 37 | 
 38 |         # Filter by archived status if specified
 39 |         if archived is not None:
 40 |             result = [nb for nb in result if nb.get("archived") == archived]
 41 | 
 42 |         return [
 43 |             NotebookResponse(
 44 |                 id=str(nb.get("id", "")),
 45 |                 name=nb.get("name", ""),
 46 |                 description=nb.get("description", ""),
 47 |                 archived=nb.get("archived", False),
 48 |                 created=str(nb.get("created", "")),
 49 |                 updated=str(nb.get("updated", "")),
 50 |                 source_count=nb.get("source_count", 0),
 51 |                 note_count=nb.get("note_count", 0),
 52 |             )
 53 |             for nb in result
 54 |         ]
 55 |     except Exception as e:
 56 |         logger.error(f"Error fetching notebooks: {str(e)}")
 57 |         raise HTTPException(
 58 |             status_code=500, detail=f"Error fetching notebooks: {str(e)}"
 59 |         )

 71 | 
 72 |         return NotebookResponse(

 75 |             description=new_notebook.description,
 76 |             archived=new_notebook.archived or False,

 80 |             note_count=0,  # New notebook has no notes
 81 |         )
 82 |     except InvalidInputError as e:

161 |         if not notebook:

168 |             notebook.description = notebook_update.description
169 |         if notebook_update.archived is not None:
170 |             notebook.archived = notebook_update.archived
171 | 
172 |         await notebook.save()
173 | 
174 |         # Query with counts after update
175 |         query = """
176 |             SELECT *,
177 |             count(<-reference.in) as source_count,
178 |             count(<-artifact.in) as note_count
179 |             FROM $notebook_id
180 |         """

184 |             nb = result[0]
185 |             return NotebookResponse(

191 |                 updated=str(nb.get("updated", "")),
192 |                 source_count=nb.get("source_count", 0),
193 |                 note_count=nb.get("note_count", 0),
194 |             )
195 | 
196 |         # Fallback if query fails

198 |             id=notebook.id or "",

200 |             description=notebook.description,
201 |             archived=notebook.archived or False,

218 | @router.post("/notebooks/{notebook_id}/sources/{source_id}")
219 | async def add_source_to_notebook(notebook_id: str, source_id: str):
220 |     """Add an existing source to a notebook (create the reference)."""
221 |     try:
222 |         # Check if notebook exists
223 |         notebook = await Notebook.get(notebook_id)
224 |         if not notebook:
225 |             raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Notebook not found")
226 | 
227 |         # Check if source exists
228 |         source = await Source.get(source_id)
229 |         if not source:
230 |             raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Source not found")
231 | 
232 |         # Check if reference already exists (idempotency)
233 |         existing_ref = await repo_query(
234 |             "SELECT * FROM reference WHERE out = $source_id AND in = $notebook_id",
235 |             {
236 |                 "notebook_id": ensure_record_id(notebook_id),
237 |                 "source_id": ensure_record_id(source_id),
238 |             },
239 |         )
240 | 
241 |         # If reference doesn't exist, create it
242 |         if not existing_ref:
243 |             await repo_query(
244 |                 "RELATE $source_id->reference->$notebook_id",
245 |                 {
246 |                     "notebook_id": ensure_record_id(notebook_id),
247 |                     "source_id": ensure_record_id(source_id),
248 |                 },
249 |             )
250 | 
251 |         return {"message": "Source linked to notebook successfully"}
252 |     except HTTPException:
253 |         raise
254 |     except Exception as e:
255 |         logger.error(
256 |             f"Error linking source {source_id} to notebook {notebook_id}: {str(e)}"
257 |         )
258 |         raise HTTPException(
259 |             status_code=500, detail=f"Error linking source to notebook: {str(e)}"
260 |         )

273 |         await repo_query(

275 |             {
276 |                 "notebook_id": ensure_record_id(notebook_id),
277 |                 "source_id": ensure_record_id(source_id),
278 |             },
279 |         )

293 | @router.delete("/notebooks/{notebook_id}", response_model=NotebookDeleteResponse)
294 | async def delete_notebook(
295 |     notebook_id: str,
296 |     delete_exclusive_sources: bool = Query(
297 |         False,
298 |         description="Whether to delete sources that belong only to this notebook",
299 |     ),
300 | ):
301 |     """
302 |     Delete a notebook with cascade deletion.
303 | 
304 |     Always deletes all notes associated with the notebook.
305 |     If delete_exclusive_sources is True, also deletes sources that belong only
306 |     to this notebook (not linked to any other notebooks).
307 |     """
308 |     try:

/docs/3-USER-GUIDE/adding-sources.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Adding Sources - Getting Content Into Your Notebook
  2 | 
  3 | Sources are the raw materials of your research. This guide covers how to add different types of content.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## Quick-Start: Add Your First Source
  8 | 
  9 | ### Option 1: Upload a File (PDF, Word, etc.)
 10 | 
 11 | ```
 12 | 1. In your notebook, click "Add Source"
 13 | 2. Select "Upload File"
 14 | 3. Choose a file from your computer
 15 | 4. Click "Upload"
 16 | 5. Wait 30-60 seconds for processing
 17 | 6. Done! Source appears in your notebook
 18 | ```
 19 | 
 20 | ### Option 2: Add a Web Link
 21 | 
 22 | ```
 23 | 1. Click "Add Source"
 24 | 2. Select "Web Link"
 25 | 3. Paste URL: https://example.com/article
 26 | 4. Click "Add"
 27 | 5. Wait for processing (usually faster than files)
 28 | 6. Done!
 29 | ```
 30 | 
 31 | ### Option 3: Paste Text
 32 | 
 33 | ```
 34 | 1. Click "Add Source"
 35 | 2. Select "Text"
 36 | 3. Paste or type your content
 37 | 4. Click "Save"
 38 | 5. Done! Immediately available
 39 | ```
 40 | 
 41 | ---
 42 | 
 43 | ## Supported File Types
 44 | 
 45 | ### Documents
 46 | - **PDF** (.pdf) — Best support, including scanned PDFs with OCR
 47 | - **Word** (.docx, .doc) — Full support
 48 | - **PowerPoint** (.pptx) — Slides converted to text
 49 | - **Excel** (.xlsx, .xls) — Spreadsheet data
 50 | - **EPUB** (.epub) — eBook files
 51 | - **Markdown** (.md, .txt) — Plain text formats
 52 | - **HTML** (.html, .htm) — Web page files
 53 | 
 54 | **File size limits:** Up to ~100MB (varies by system)
 55 | 
 56 | **Processing time:** 10 seconds - 2 minutes (depending on length and file type)
 57 | 
 58 | ### Audio & Video
 59 | - **Audio**: MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, FLAC (~30 seconds - 3 minutes per hour)
 60 | - **Video**: MP4, AVI, MOV, MKV, WebM (~3-10 minutes per hour)
 61 | - **YouTube**: Direct URL support
 62 | - **Podcasts**: RSS feed URL
 63 | 
 64 | **Automatic transcription**: Audio/video is transcribed to text automatically. This requires enabling speech-to-text in settings.
 65 | 
 66 | ### Web Content
 67 | - **Articles**: Blog posts, news articles, Medium
 68 | - **YouTube**: Full videos or playlists
 69 | - **PDFs online**: Direct PDF links
 70 | - **News**: News site articles
 71 | 
 72 | **Just paste the URL** in "Web Link" section.
 73 | 
 74 | ### What Doesn't Work
 75 | - Paywalled content (WSJ, FT, etc.) — Can't extract
 76 | - Password-protected PDFs — Can't open
 77 | - Pure image files (.jpg, .png) — Except scanned PDFs which have OCR
 78 | - Very large files (>100MB) — Timeout
 79 | 
 80 | ---
 81 | 
 82 | ## What Happens When You Add a Source
 83 | 
 84 | The system automatically does four things:
 85 | 
 86 | ```
 87 | 1. EXTRACT TEXT
 88 |    File/URL → Readable text
 89 |    (PDFs get OCR if scanned)
 90 |    (Videos get transcribed if enabled)
 91 | 
 92 | 2. BREAK INTO CHUNKS
 93 |    Long text → ~500-word pieces
 94 |    (So search finds specific parts, not whole document)
 95 | 
 96 | 3. CREATE EMBEDDINGS
 97 |    Each chunk → Vector representation
 98 |    (Enables semantic/concept search)
 99 | 
100 | 4. INDEX & STORE
101 |    Everything → Database
102 |    (Ready to search and retrieve)
103 | ```
104 | 
105 | **Time to use:** After the progress bar completes, the source is ready immediately. Embeddings are created in the background.
106 | 
107 | ---
108 | 
109 | ## Step-by-Step for Different Types
110 | 
111 | ### PDFs
112 | 
113 | **Best practices:**
114 | ```
115 | Clean PDFs:
116 |   1. Upload → Done
117 |   2. Processing time: ~30-60 seconds
118 | 
119 | Scanned/Image PDFs:
120 |   1. Upload same way
121 |   2. System auto-detects and uses OCR
122 |   3. Processing time: ~2-3 minutes
123 |   4. (Higher, due to OCR overhead)
124 | 
125 | Large PDFs (50+ pages):
126 |   1. Consider splitting into smaller files
127 |   2. Or upload as-is (system handles it)
128 |   3. Processing time scales with size
129 | ```
130 | 
131 | **Common issues:**
132 | - "Can't extract text" → PDF is corrupted or has copy protection
133 | - Solution: Try opening in Adobe. If it won't, the PDF is likely protected.
134 | 
135 | ### Web Links / Articles
136 | 
137 | **Best practices:**
138 | ```
139 | 1. Copy full URL from browser: https://example.com/article-title
140 | 2. Paste in "Web Link"
141 | 3. Click Add
142 | 4. Wait for extraction
143 | 
144 | Processing time: Usually 5-15 seconds
145 | ```
146 | 
147 | **What works:**
148 | - Standard web articles
149 | - Blog posts
150 | - News articles
151 | - Wikipedia pages
152 | - Medium posts
153 | - Substack articles
154 | 
155 | **What doesn't work:**
156 | - Twitter threads (unreliable)
157 | - Paywalled articles (can't access)
158 | - JavaScript-heavy sites (content not extracted)
159 | 
160 | **Pro tip:** If it doesn't work, copy the article text and paste as "Text" instead.
161 | 
162 | ### Audio Files
163 | 
164 | **Best practices:**
165 | ```
166 | 1. Ensure speech-to-text is enabled in Settings
167 | 2. Upload MP3, WAV, or M4A file
168 | 3. System automatically transcribes to text
169 | 4. Processing time: ~1 minute per 5 minutes of audio
170 | 
171 | Example:
172 |   - 1-hour podcast → 12 minutes processing
173 |   - 10-minute recording → 2 minutes processing
174 | ```
175 | 
176 | **Quality matters:**
177 | - Clear audio: Fast transcription
178 | - Muffled/noisy audio: Slower, less accurate transcription
179 | - Background noise: Try to minimize before uploading
180 | 
181 | **Tip:** If audio quality is poor, the AI might misinterpret content. You can manually correct transcription if needed.
182 | 
183 | ### YouTube Videos
184 | 
185 | **Best practices:**
186 | ```
187 | Two ways to add:
188 | 
189 | Method 1: Direct URL
190 |   1. Copy YouTube URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=...
191 |   2. Paste in "Web Link"
192 |   3. Click Add
193 |   4. System extracts captions (if available) + transcript
194 | 
195 | Method 2: Playlist
196 |   1. Paste playlist URL
197 |   2. System adds all videos as separate sources
198 |   3. Each video processed separately
199 |   4. Takes longer (multiple videos)
200 | ```
201 | 
202 | **What's extracted:**
203 | - Captions/subtitles (if available)
204 | - Transcription (if captions aren't available)
205 | - Basic metadata (title, channel, length)
206 | 
207 | **Processing:**
208 | - 10-minute video: ~2-3 minutes
209 | - 1-hour video: ~10-15 minutes
210 | 
211 | ### Text / Paste Content
212 | 
213 | **Best practices:**
214 | ```
215 | 1. Select "Text" when adding source
216 | 2. Paste or type content
217 | 3. System processes immediately
218 | 4. No wait time needed
219 | 
220 | Good for:
221 |   - Notes you want to reference
222 |   - Quotes from books
223 |   - Transcripts you have handy
224 |   - Quick research snippets
225 | ```
226 | 
227 | ---
228 | 
229 | ## Managing Your Sources
230 | 
231 | ### Viewing Source Details
232 | 
233 | ```
234 | Click on source → See:
235 |   - Original file name/title
236 |   - When it was added
237 |   - Size and format
238 |   - Processing status
239 |   - Number of chunks
240 | ```
241 | 
242 | ### Organizing with Metadata
243 | 
244 | You can add to each source:
245 | - **Title**: Better name than original filename
246 | - **Tags**: Category labels ("primary research", "background", "competitor analysis")
247 | - **Description**: A few notes about what it contains
248 | 
249 | **Why this matters:**
250 | - Makes sources easier to find
251 | - Helps when contextualizing for Chat
252 | - Useful for organizing large notebooks
253 | 
254 | ### Searching Within Sources
255 | 
256 | ```
257 | After sources are added, you can:
258 | 
259 | Text search: "Find exact phrase"
260 | Vector search: "Find conceptually similar"
261 | 
262 | Both search across all sources in notebook.
263 | Results show:
264 |   - Which source
265 |   - Which section
266 |   - Relevance score
267 | ```
268 | 
269 | ---
270 | 
271 | ## Context Management: How Sources Get Used
272 | 
273 | You control how AI accesses sources:
274 | 
275 | ### Three Levels (for Chat)
276 | 
277 | **Full Content:**
278 | ```
279 | AI sees: Complete source text
280 | Cost: 100% of tokens
281 | Use when: Analyzing in detail, need precise citations
282 | Example: "Analyze this methodology paper closely"
283 | ```
284 | 
285 | **Summary Only:**
286 | ```
287 | AI sees: AI-generated summary (not full text)
288 | Cost: ~10-20% of tokens
289 | Use when: Background material, reference context
290 | Example: "Use this as context but focus on the main source"
291 | ```
292 | 
293 | **Not in Context:**
294 | ```
295 | AI sees: Nothing (excluded)
296 | Cost: 0 tokens
297 | Use when: Confidential, not relevant, or archived
298 | Example: "Keep this in notebook but don't use in this conversation"
299 | ```
300 | 
301 | ### How to Set Context (in Chat)
302 | 
303 | ```
304 | 1. Go to Chat
305 | 2. Click "Select Context Sources"
306 | 3. For each source:
307 |    - Toggle ON/OFF (include/exclude)
308 |    - Choose level (Full/Summary/Excluded)
309 | 4. Click "Save"
310 | 5. Now chat uses these settings
311 | ```
312 | 
313 | ---
314 | 
315 | ## Common Mistakes
316 | 
317 | | Mistake | What Happens | How to Fix |
318 | |---------|--------------|-----------|
319 | | Upload 200 sources at once | System gets slow, processing stalls | Add 10-20 at a time, wait for processing |
320 | | Use full content for all sources | Token usage skyrockets, expensive | Use "Summary" or "Excluded" for background material |
321 | | Add huge PDFs without splitting | Processing is slow, search results less precise | Consider splitting large PDFs into chapters |
322 | | Forget source titles | Can't distinguish between similar sources | Rename sources with descriptive titles right after uploading |
323 | | Don't tag sources | Hard to find and organize later | Add tags immediately: "primary", "background", etc. |
324 | | Mix languages in one source | Transcription/embedding quality drops | Keep each language in separate sources |
325 | | Use same source multiple times | Takes up space, creates confusion | Add once; reuse in multiple chats/notebooks |
326 | 
327 | ---
328 | 
329 | ## Processing Status & Troubleshooting
330 | 
331 | ### What the Status Indicators Mean
332 | 
333 | ```
334 | 🟡 Processing
335 |   → Source is being extracted and embedded
336 |   → Wait 30 seconds - 3 minutes depending on size
337 |   → Don't use in Chat yet
338 | 
339 | 🟢 Ready
340 |   → Source is processed and searchable
341 |   → Can use immediately in Chat
342 |   → Can apply transformations
343 | 
344 | 🔴 Error
345 |   → Something went wrong
346 |   → Common reasons:
347 |     - Unsupported file format
348 |     - File too large or corrupted
349 |     - Network timeout
350 | 
351 | ⚪ Not in Context
352 |   → Source added but excluded from Chat
353 |   → Still searchable, not sent to AI
354 | ```
355 | 
356 | ### Common Errors & Solutions
357 | 
358 | **"Unsupported file type"**
359 | - You tried to upload a format not in the list (e.g., `.webp` image)
360 | - Solution: Convert to supported format (PDF for documents, MP3 for audio)
361 | 
362 | **"Processing timeout"**
363 | - Very large file (>100MB) or very long audio
364 | - Solution: Split into smaller pieces or try uploading again
365 | 
366 | **"Transcription failed"**
367 | - Audio quality too poor or language not detected
368 | - Solution: Re-record with better quality, or paste text transcript manually
369 | 
370 | **"Web link won't extract"**
371 | - Website blocks automated access or uses JavaScript for content
372 | - Solution: Copy the article text and paste as "Text" instead
373 | 
374 | ---
375 | 
376 | ## Tips for Best Results
377 | 
378 | ### For PDFs
379 | - Clean, digital PDFs work best
380 | - Remove copy protection if present (legally)
381 | - Scanned PDFs work but take longer
382 | 
383 | ### For Web Articles
384 | - Use full URL including domain
385 | - Avoid cookie/popup-laden sites
386 | - If extraction fails, copy-paste text instead
387 | 
388 | ### For Audio
389 | - Clear, well-recorded audio transcribes better
390 | - Remove background noise if possible
391 | - YouTube videos usually have good transcriptions built-in
392 | 
393 | ### For Large Documents
394 | - Consider splitting into smaller sources
395 | - Gives more precise search results
396 | - Processing is faster for smaller pieces
397 | 
398 | ### For Organization
399 | - Name sources clearly (not "document_2.pdf")
400 | - Add tags immediately after uploading
401 | - Use descriptions for complex documents
402 | 
403 | ---
404 | 
405 | ## What Comes After: Using Your Sources
406 | 
407 | Once you've added sources, you can:
408 | 
409 | - **Chat** → Ask questions (see [Chat Effectively](chat-effectively.md))
410 | - **Search** → Find specific content (see [Search Effectively](search.md))
411 | - **Transformations** → Extract structured insights (see [Working with Notes](working-with-notes.md))
412 | - **Ask** → Get comprehensive answers (see [Search Effectively](search.md))
413 | - **Podcasts** → Turn into audio (see [Creating Podcasts](creating-podcasts.md))
414 | 
415 | ---
416 | 
417 | ## Summary Checklist
418 | 
419 | Before adding sources, confirm:
420 | 
421 | - [ ] File is in supported format
422 | - [ ] File is under 100MB (or splitting large ones)
423 | - [ ] Web links are full URLs (not shortened)
424 | - [ ] Audio files have clear speech (if transcription-dependent)
425 | - [ ] You've named source clearly
426 | - [ ] You've added tags for organization
427 | - [ ] You understand context levels (Full/Summary/Excluded)
428 | 
429 | Done! Sources are now ready for Chat, Search, Transformations, and more.
430 |

/.github/workflows/build-and-release.yml:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | name: Build and Release
  2 | 
  3 | on:
  4 |   workflow_dispatch:
  5 |     inputs:
  6 |       push_latest:
  7 |         description: 'Also push v1-latest tags'
  8 |         required: true
  9 |         default: false
 10 |         type: boolean
 11 |   release:
 12 |     types: [published]
 13 | 
 14 | permissions:
 15 |   contents: read
 16 |   packages: write
 17 | 
 18 | env:
 19 |   GHCR_IMAGE: ghcr.io/lfnovo/open-notebook
 20 |   DOCKERHUB_IMAGE: lfnovo/open_notebook
 21 | 
 22 | jobs:
 23 |   extract-version:
 24 |     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 25 |     outputs:
 26 |       version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
 27 |       has_dockerhub_secrets: ${{ steps.check.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets }}
 28 |     steps:
 29 |       - name: Checkout
 30 |         uses: actions/checkout@v4
 31 | 
 32 |       - name: Extract version from pyproject.toml
 33 |         id: version
 34 |         run: |
 35 |           VERSION=$(grep -m1 '^version = ' pyproject.toml | cut -d'"' -f2)
 36 |           echo "version=$VERSION" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 37 |           echo "Extracted version: $VERSION"
 38 | 
 39 |       - name: Check for Docker Hub credentials
 40 |         id: check
 41 |         env:
 42 |           SECRET_DOCKER_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
 43 |           SECRET_DOCKER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}
 44 |         run: |
 45 |           if [[ -n ""$SECRET_DOCKER_USERNAME"" && -n ""$SECRET_DOCKER_PASSWORD"" ]]; then
 46 |             echo "has_dockerhub_secrets=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 47 |             echo "Docker Hub credentials available"
 48 |           else
 49 |             echo "has_dockerhub_secrets=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 50 |             echo "Docker Hub credentials not available - will only push to GHCR"
 51 |           fi
 52 | 
 53 |   build-regular:
 54 |     needs: extract-version
 55 |     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 56 |     steps:
 57 |       - name: Checkout
 58 |         uses: actions/checkout@v4
 59 | 
 60 |       - name: Free up disk space
 61 |         run: |
 62 |           sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet
 63 |           sudo rm -rf /usr/local/lib/android
 64 |           sudo rm -rf /opt/ghc
 65 |           sudo rm -rf /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL
 66 |           sudo docker image prune --all --force
 67 |           df -h
 68 | 
 69 |       - name: Set up Docker Buildx
 70 |         uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
 71 | 
 72 |       - name: Login to GitHub Container Registry
 73 |         uses: docker/login-action@v3
 74 |         with:
 75 |           registry: ghcr.io
 76 |           username: ${{ github.actor }}
 77 |           password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
 78 | 
 79 |       - name: Login to Docker Hub
 80 |         if: needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets == 'true'
 81 |         uses: docker/login-action@v3
 82 |         with:
 83 |           username: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
 84 |           password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}
 85 | 
 86 |       - name: Cache Docker layers
 87 |         uses: actions/cache@v3
 88 |         with:
 89 |           path: /tmp/.buildx-cache
 90 |           key: ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-regular-${{ github.sha }}
 91 |           restore-keys: |
 92 |             ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-regular-
 93 | 
 94 |       - name: Prepare Docker tags for regular build
 95 |         id: tags-regular
 96 |         env:
 97 |           ENV_GHCR_IMAGE: ${{ env.GHCR_IMAGE }}
 98 |           GITHUB_EVENT_INPUTS_PUSH_LATEST: ${{ github.event.inputs.push_latest }}
 99 |           GITHUB_EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
100 |           GITHUB_EVENT_RELEASE_PRERELEASE: ${{ github.event.release.prerelease }}
101 |           ENV_DOCKERHUB_IMAGE: ${{ env.DOCKERHUB_IMAGE }}
102 |         run: |
103 |           TAGS=""$ENV_GHCR_IMAGE":${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.version }}"
104 | 
105 |           # Determine if we should push latest tags
106 |           PUSH_LATEST=""$GITHUB_EVENT_INPUTS_PUSH_LATEST""
107 |           if [[ -z "$PUSH_LATEST" ]]; then
108 |             PUSH_LATEST="false"
109 |           fi
110 | 
111 |           # Add GHCR latest tag if requested or for non-prerelease releases
112 |           if [[ "$PUSH_LATEST" == "true" ]] || [[ ""$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME"" == "release" && ""$GITHUB_EVENT_RELEASE_PRERELEASE"" != "true" ]]; then
113 |             TAGS="${TAGS},"$ENV_GHCR_IMAGE":v1-latest"
114 |           fi
115 | 
116 |           # Add Docker Hub tags if credentials available
117 |           if [[ "${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets }}" == "true" ]]; then
118 |             TAGS="${TAGS},"$ENV_DOCKERHUB_IMAGE":${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.version }}"
119 | 
120 |             if [[ "$PUSH_LATEST" == "true" ]] || [[ ""$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME"" == "release" && ""$GITHUB_EVENT_RELEASE_PRERELEASE"" != "true" ]]; then
121 |               TAGS="${TAGS},"$ENV_DOCKERHUB_IMAGE":v1-latest"
122 |             fi
123 |           fi
124 | 
125 |           echo "tags=${TAGS}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
126 |           echo "Generated tags: ${TAGS}"
127 | 
128 |       - name: Build and push regular image
129 |         uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
130 |         with:
131 |           context: .
132 |           file: ./Dockerfile
133 |           platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
134 |           push: true
135 |           tags: ${{ steps.tags-regular.outputs.tags }}
136 |           cache-from: type=local,src=/tmp/.buildx-cache
137 |           cache-to: type=local,dest=/tmp/.buildx-cache-new,mode=max
138 | 
139 |       - name: Move cache
140 |         run: |
141 |           rm -rf /tmp/.buildx-cache
142 |           mv /tmp/.buildx-cache-new /tmp/.buildx-cache
143 | 
144 |   build-single:
145 |     needs: extract-version
146 |     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
147 |     steps:
148 |       - name: Checkout
149 |         uses: actions/checkout@v4
150 | 
151 |       - name: Free up disk space
152 |         run: |
153 |           sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet
154 |           sudo rm -rf /usr/local/lib/android
155 |           sudo rm -rf /opt/ghc
156 |           sudo rm -rf /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL
157 |           sudo docker image prune --all --force
158 |           df -h
159 | 
160 |       - name: Set up Docker Buildx
161 |         uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
162 | 
163 |       - name: Login to GitHub Container Registry
164 |         uses: docker/login-action@v3
165 |         with:
166 |           registry: ghcr.io
167 |           username: ${{ github.actor }}
168 |           password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
169 | 
170 |       - name: Login to Docker Hub
171 |         if: needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets == 'true'
172 |         uses: docker/login-action@v3
173 |         with:
174 |           username: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
175 |           password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}
176 | 
177 |       - name: Cache Docker layers
178 |         uses: actions/cache@v3
179 |         with:
180 |           path: /tmp/.buildx-cache-single
181 |           key: ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-single-${{ github.sha }}
182 |           restore-keys: |
183 |             ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-single-
184 | 
185 |       - name: Prepare Docker tags for single build
186 |         id: tags-single
187 |         env:
188 |           ENV_GHCR_IMAGE: ${{ env.GHCR_IMAGE }}
189 |           GITHUB_EVENT_INPUTS_PUSH_LATEST: ${{ github.event.inputs.push_latest }}
190 |           GITHUB_EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
191 |           GITHUB_EVENT_RELEASE_PRERELEASE: ${{ github.event.release.prerelease }}
192 |           ENV_DOCKERHUB_IMAGE: ${{ env.DOCKERHUB_IMAGE }}
193 |         run: |
194 |           TAGS=""$ENV_GHCR_IMAGE":${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.version }}-single"
195 | 
196 |           # Determine if we should push latest tags
197 |           PUSH_LATEST=""$GITHUB_EVENT_INPUTS_PUSH_LATEST""
198 |           if [[ -z "$PUSH_LATEST" ]]; then
199 |             PUSH_LATEST="false"
200 |           fi
201 | 
202 |           # Add GHCR latest tag if requested or for non-prerelease releases
203 |           if [[ "$PUSH_LATEST" == "true" ]] || [[ ""$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME"" == "release" && ""$GITHUB_EVENT_RELEASE_PRERELEASE"" != "true" ]]; then
204 |             TAGS="${TAGS},"$ENV_GHCR_IMAGE":v1-latest-single"
205 |           fi
206 | 
207 |           # Add Docker Hub tags if credentials available
208 |           if [[ "${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets }}" == "true" ]]; then
209 |             TAGS="${TAGS},"$ENV_DOCKERHUB_IMAGE":${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.version }}-single"
210 | 
211 |             if [[ "$PUSH_LATEST" == "true" ]] || [[ ""$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME"" == "release" && ""$GITHUB_EVENT_RELEASE_PRERELEASE"" != "true" ]]; then
212 |               TAGS="${TAGS},"$ENV_DOCKERHUB_IMAGE":v1-latest-single"
213 |             fi
214 |           fi
215 | 
216 |           echo "tags=${TAGS}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
217 |           echo "Generated tags: ${TAGS}"
218 | 
219 |       - name: Build and push single-container image
220 |         uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
221 |         with:
222 |           context: .
223 |           file: ./Dockerfile.single
224 |           platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
225 |           push: true
226 |           tags: ${{ steps.tags-single.outputs.tags }}
227 |           cache-from: type=local,src=/tmp/.buildx-cache-single
228 |           cache-to: type=local,dest=/tmp/.buildx-cache-single-new,mode=max
229 | 
230 |       - name: Move cache
231 |         run: |
232 |           rm -rf /tmp/.buildx-cache-single
233 |           mv /tmp/.buildx-cache-single-new /tmp/.buildx-cache-single
234 | 
235 |   summary:
236 |     needs: [extract-version, build-regular, build-single]
237 |     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
238 |     if: always()
239 |     steps:
240 |       - name: Build Summary
241 |         env:
242 |           GITHUB_EVENT_INPUTS_PUSH_LATEST_____FALSE_: ${{ github.event.inputs.push_latest || 'false' }}
243 |           ENV_GHCR_IMAGE: ${{ env.GHCR_IMAGE }}
244 |           ENV_DOCKERHUB_IMAGE: ${{ env.DOCKERHUB_IMAGE }}
245 |           GITHUB_EVENT_INPUTS_PUSH_LATEST: ${{ github.event.inputs.push_latest }}
246 |         run: |
247 |           echo "## Build Summary" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
248 |           echo "**Version:** ${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.version }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
249 |           echo "**Push v1-Latest:** "$GITHUB_EVENT_INPUTS_PUSH_LATEST_____FALSE_"" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
250 |           echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
251 |           echo "### Registries:" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
252 |           echo "✅ **GHCR:** \`"$ENV_GHCR_IMAGE"\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
253 |           if [[ "${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets }}" == "true" ]]; then
254 |             echo "✅ **Docker Hub:** \`"$ENV_DOCKERHUB_IMAGE"\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
255 |           else
256 |             echo "⏭️ **Docker Hub:** Skipped (credentials not configured)" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
257 |           fi
258 |           echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
259 |           echo "### Images Built:" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
260 | 
261 |           if [[ "${{ needs.build-regular.result }}" == "success" ]]; then
262 |             echo "✅ **Regular (GHCR):** \`"$ENV_GHCR_IMAGE":${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.version }}\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
263 |             if [[ ""$GITHUB_EVENT_INPUTS_PUSH_LATEST"" == "true" ]]; then
264 |               echo "✅ **Regular v1-Latest (GHCR):** \`"$ENV_GHCR_IMAGE":v1-latest\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
265 |             fi
266 |             if [[ "${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets }}" == "true" ]]; then
267 |               echo "✅ **Regular (Docker Hub):** \`"$ENV_DOCKERHUB_IMAGE":${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.version }}\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
268 |               if [[ ""$GITHUB_EVENT_INPUTS_PUSH_LATEST"" == "true" ]]; then
269 |                 echo "✅ **Regular v1-Latest (Docker Hub):** \`"$ENV_DOCKERHUB_IMAGE":v1-latest\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
270 |               fi
271 |             fi
272 |           elif [[ "${{ needs.build-regular.result }}" == "skipped" ]]; then
273 |             echo "⏭️ **Regular:** Skipped" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
274 |           else
275 |             echo "❌ **Regular:** Failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
276 |           fi
277 | 
278 |           if [[ "${{ needs.build-single.result }}" == "success" ]]; then
279 |             echo "✅ **Single (GHCR):** \`"$ENV_GHCR_IMAGE":${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.version }}-single\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
280 |             if [[ ""$GITHUB_EVENT_INPUTS_PUSH_LATEST"" == "true" ]]; then
281 |               echo "✅ **Single v1-Latest (GHCR):** \`"$ENV_GHCR_IMAGE":v1-latest-single\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
282 |             fi
283 |             if [[ "${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.has_dockerhub_secrets }}" == "true" ]]; then
284 |               echo "✅ **Single (Docker Hub):** \`"$ENV_DOCKERHUB_IMAGE":${{ needs.extract-version.outputs.version }}-single\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
285 |               if [[ ""$GITHUB_EVENT_INPUTS_PUSH_LATEST"" == "true" ]]; then
286 |                 echo "✅ **Single v1-Latest (Docker Hub):** \`"$ENV_DOCKERHUB_IMAGE":v1-latest-single\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
287 |               fi
288 |             fi
289 |           elif [[ "${{ needs.build-single.result }}" == "skipped" ]]; then
290 |             echo "⏭️ **Single:** Skipped" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
291 |           else
292 |             echo "❌ **Single:** Failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
293 |           fi
294 | 
295 |           echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
296 |           echo "### Platforms:" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
297 |           echo "- linux/amd64" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
298 |           echo "- linux/arm64" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

  1 | # Complete Environment Reference
  2 | 
  3 | Comprehensive list of all environment variables available in Open Notebook.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## API Configuration
  8 | 
  9 | | Variable | Required? | Default | Description |
 10 | |----------|-----------|---------|-------------|
 11 | | `API_URL` | No | Auto-detected | URL where frontend reaches API (e.g., http://localhost:5055) |
 12 | | `INTERNAL_API_URL` | No | http://localhost:5055 | Internal API URL for Next.js server-side proxying |
 13 | | `API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT` | No | 300 | Client timeout in seconds (how long to wait for API response) |
 14 | | `OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD` | No | None | Password to protect Open Notebook instance |
 15 | | `HOSTNAME` | No | `0.0.0.0` (in Docker) | Network interface for Next.js to bind to. Default `0.0.0.0` ensures accessibility from reverse proxies |
 16 | 
 17 | ---
 18 |

 21 | | Variable | Required? | Default | Description |
 22 | |----------|-----------|---------|-------------|

151 | ## AI Provider: VoyageAI (Embeddings)

160 | 
161 | ## Text-to-Speech (TTS)
162 | 
163 | | Variable | Required? | Default | Description |
164 | |----------|-----------|---------|-------------|
165 | | `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | If using ElevenLabs TTS | None | ElevenLabs API key for voice generation |
166 | | `TTS_BATCH_SIZE` | No | 5 | Concurrent TTS requests (1-5, depends on provider) |

168 | **Setup:** Get from https://elevenlabs.io/
