170 | ---
171 | 
172 | ## Database: SurrealDB
173 | 
174 | | Variable | Required? | Default | Description |
175 | |----------|-----------|---------|-------------|
176 | | `SURREAL_URL` | Yes | ws://surrealdb:8000/rpc | SurrealDB WebSocket connection URL |
177 | | `SURREAL_USER` | Yes | root | SurrealDB username |
178 | | `SURREAL_PASSWORD` | Yes | root | SurrealDB password |
179 | | `SURREAL_NAMESPACE` | Yes | open_notebook | SurrealDB namespace |
180 | | `SURREAL_DATABASE` | Yes | open_notebook | SurrealDB database name |
181 | 
182 | ---
183 | 
184 | ## Database: Retry Configuration
185 | 
186 | | Variable | Required? | Default | Description |
187 | |----------|-----------|---------|-------------|
188 | | `SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_ENABLED` | No | true | Enable retries on failure |
189 | | `SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | No | 3 | Maximum retry attempts |
190 | | `SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_WAIT_STRATEGY` | No | exponential_jitter | Retry wait strategy (exponential_jitter/exponential/fixed/random) |
191 | | `SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_WAIT_MIN` | No | 1 | Minimum wait time between retries (seconds) |
192 | | `SURREAL_COMMANDS_RETRY_WAIT_MAX` | No | 30 | Maximum wait time between retries (seconds) |
193 | 
194 | ---
195 | 
196 | ## Database: Concurrency
197 | 
198 | | Variable | Required? | Default | Description |
199 | |----------|-----------|---------|-------------|
200 | | `SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS` | No | 5 | Maximum concurrent database tasks |
201 | 
202 | ---
203 | 
204 | ## LLM Timeouts
205 | 
206 | | Variable | Required? | Default | Description |
207 | |----------|-----------|---------|-------------|
208 | | `ESPERANTO_LLM_TIMEOUT` | No | 60 | LLM inference timeout in seconds |
209 | | `ESPERANTO_SSL_VERIFY` | No | true | Verify SSL certificates (false = development only) |
210 | | `ESPERANTO_SSL_CA_BUNDLE` | No | None | Path to custom CA certificate bundle |
211 | 
212 | ---
213 | 
214 | ## Content Extraction
215 | 
216 | | Variable | Required? | Default | Description |
217 | |----------|-----------|---------|-------------|
218 | | `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` | No | None | Firecrawl API key for advanced web scraping |
219 | | `JINA_API_KEY` | No | None | Jina AI API key for web extraction |
220 | 
221 | **Setup:**
222 | - Firecrawl: https://firecrawl.dev/
223 | - Jina: https://jina.ai/
224 | 
225 | ---
226 | 
227 | ## Network / Proxy
228 | 
229 | | Variable | Required? | Default | Description |
230 | |----------|-----------|---------|-------------|
231 | | `HTTP_PROXY` | No | None | HTTP proxy URL for outbound HTTP requests |
232 | | `HTTPS_PROXY` | No | None | HTTPS proxy URL for outbound HTTPS requests |
233 | | `NO_PROXY` | No | None | Comma-separated list of hosts to bypass proxy |
234 | 
235 | Route all outbound HTTP requests through a proxy server. Useful for corporate/firewalled environments.
236 | 
237 | The underlying libraries (esperanto, content-core, podcast-creator) automatically detect proxy settings from these standard environment variables.
238 | 
239 | **Affects:**
240 | - AI provider API calls (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, etc.)
241 | - Content extraction from URLs (web scraping, YouTube transcripts)
242 | - Podcast generation (LLM and TTS provider calls)
243 | 
244 | **Format:** `http://[user:pass@]host:port` or `https://[user:pass@]host:port`
245 | 
246 | **Examples:**
247 | ```bash
248 | # Basic proxy
249 | HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.com:8080
250 | HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.com:8080
251 | 
252 | # Authenticated proxy
253 | HTTP_PROXY=http://user:password@proxy.corp.com:8080
254 | HTTPS_PROXY=http://user:password@proxy.corp.com:8080
255 | 
256 | # Bypass proxy for local hosts
257 | NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,.local
258 | ```
259 | 
260 | ---
261 | 
262 | ## Debugging & Monitoring
263 | 
264 | | Variable | Required? | Default | Description |
265 | |----------|-----------|---------|-------------|
266 | | `LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2` | No | false | Enable LangSmith tracing |
267 | | `LANGCHAIN_ENDPOINT` | No | https://api.smith.langchain.com | LangSmith endpoint |
268 | | `LANGCHAIN_API_KEY` | No | None | LangSmith API key |
269 | | `LANGCHAIN_PROJECT` | No | Open Notebook | LangSmith project name |
270 | 
271 | **Setup:** https://smith.langchain.com/
272 | 
273 | ---
274 | 
275 | ## Environment Variables by Use Case
276 | 
277 | ### Minimal Setup (Cloud Provider)
278 | ```
279 | OPENAI_API_KEY (or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, etc.)
280 | ```
281 | 
282 | ### Local Development (Ollama)
283 | ```
284 | OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://localhost:11434
285 | ```
286 | 
287 | ### Production (OpenAI + Custom Domain)
288 | ```
289 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...
290 | API_URL=https://mynotebook.example.com
291 | SURREAL_USER=production_user
292 | SURREAL_PASSWORD=secure_password
293 | ```
294 | 
295 | ### Self-Hosted Behind Reverse Proxy
296 | ```
297 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:1234/v1
298 | API_URL=https://mynotebook.example.com
299 | ```
300 | 
301 | ### Corporate Environment (Behind Proxy)
302 | ```
303 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...
304 | HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.com:8080
305 | HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.com:8080
306 | NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1
307 | ```
308 | 
309 | ### High-Performance Deployment
310 | ```
311 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...
312 | SURREAL_COMMANDS_MAX_TASKS=10
313 | TTS_BATCH_SIZE=5
314 | API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=600
315 | ```
316 | 
317 | ### Debugging
318 | ```
319 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...
320 | LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=true
321 | LANGCHAIN_API_KEY=your-key
322 | ```
323 | 
324 | ---
325 | 
326 | ## Validation
327 | 
328 | Check if a variable is set:
329 | 
330 | ```bash
331 | # Check single variable
332 | echo $OPENAI_API_KEY
333 | 
334 | # Check multiple
335 | env | grep -E "OPENAI|API_URL"
336 | 
337 | # Print all config
338 | env | grep -E "^[A-Z_]+=" | sort
339 | ```
340 | 
341 | ---
342 | 
343 | ## Notes
344 | 
345 | - **Case-sensitive:** `OPENAI_API_KEY` ≠ `openai_api_key`
346 | - **No spaces:** `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...` not `OPENAI_API_KEY = sk-proj-...`
347 | - **Quote values:** Use quotes for values with spaces: `API_URL="http://my server:5055"`
348 | - **Restart required:** Changes take effect after restarting services
349 | - **Secrets:** Don't commit API keys to git
350 | 
351 | ---
352 | 
353 | ## Quick Setup Checklist
354 | 
355 | - [ ] Choose AI provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, etc.)
356 | - [ ] Get API key if cloud provider
357 | - [ ] Add to .env or docker.env
358 | - [ ] Set `API_URL` if behind reverse proxy
359 | - [ ] Change `SURREAL_PASSWORD` in production
360 | - [ ] Verify with: `docker compose logs api | grep -i "error"`
361 | - [ ] Test in browser: Go to Settings → Models
362 | - [ ] Try a test chat
363 | 
364 | Done!
365 |

  1 | from datetime import datetime
  2 | from typing import Any, ClassVar, Dict, List, Optional, Type, TypeVar, Union, cast
  3 | 
  4 | from loguru import logger
  5 | from pydantic import (
  6 |     BaseModel,
  7 |     ConfigDict,
  8 |     ValidationError,
  9 |     field_validator,
 10 |     model_validator,
 11 | )
 12 | 
 13 | from open_notebook.database.repository import (
 14 |     ensure_record_id,
 15 |     repo_create,
 16 |     repo_delete,
 17 |     repo_query,
 18 |     repo_relate,
 19 |     repo_update,
 20 |     repo_upsert,
 21 | )
 22 | from open_notebook.exceptions import (
 23 |     DatabaseOperationError,
 24 |     InvalidInputError,
 25 |     NotFoundError,
 26 | )
 27 | 
 28 | T = TypeVar("T", bound="ObjectModel")
 29 | 
 30 | 
 31 | class ObjectModel(BaseModel):
 32 |     id: Optional[str] = None
 33 |     table_name: ClassVar[str] = ""
 34 |     nullable_fields: ClassVar[set[str]] = set()  # Fields that can be saved as None
 35 |     created: Optional[datetime] = None
 36 |     updated: Optional[datetime] = None
 37 | 
 38 |     @classmethod
 39 |     async def get_all(cls: Type[T], order_by=None) -> List[T]:
 40 |         try:
 41 |             # If called from a specific subclass, use its table_name
 42 |             if cls.table_name:
 43 |                 target_class = cls
 44 |                 table_name = cls.table_name
 45 |             else:
 46 |                 # This path is taken if called directly from ObjectModel
 47 |                 raise InvalidInputError(
 48 |                     "get_all() must be called from a specific model class"
 49 |                 )
 50 |             if order_by:
 51 |                 query = f"SELECT * FROM {table_name} ORDER BY {order_by}"
 52 |             else:
 53 |                 query = f"SELECT * FROM {table_name}"
 54 | 
 55 |             result = await repo_query(query)
 56 |             objects = []
 57 |             for obj in result:
 58 |                 try:
 59 |                     objects.append(target_class(**obj))
 60 |                 except Exception as e:
 61 |                     logger.critical(f"Error creating object: {str(e)}")
 62 | 
 63 |             return objects
 64 |         except Exception as e:
 65 |             logger.error(f"Error fetching all {cls.table_name}: {str(e)}")
 66 |             logger.exception(e)
 67 |             raise DatabaseOperationError(e)
 68 | 
 69 |     @classmethod
 70 |     async def get(cls: Type[T], id: str) -> T:
 71 |         if not id:
 72 |             raise InvalidInputError("ID cannot be empty")
 73 |         try:
 74 |             # Get the table name from the ID (everything before the first colon)
 75 |             table_name = id.split(":")[0] if ":" in id else id
 76 | 
 77 |             # If we're calling from a specific subclass and IDs match, use that class
 78 |             if cls.table_name and cls.table_name == table_name:
 79 |                 target_class: Type[T] = cls
 80 |             else:
 81 |                 # Otherwise, find the appropriate subclass based on table_name
 82 |                 found_class = cls._get_class_by_table_name(table_name)
 83 |                 if not found_class:
 84 |                     raise InvalidInputError(f"No class found for table {table_name}")
 85 |                 target_class = cast(Type[T], found_class)
 86 | 
 87 |             result = await repo_query("SELECT * FROM $id", {"id": ensure_record_id(id)})
 88 |             if result:
 89 |                 return target_class(**result[0])
 90 |             else:
 91 |                 raise NotFoundError(f"{table_name} with id {id} not found")
 92 |         except Exception as e:
 93 |             logger.error(f"Error fetching object with id {id}: {str(e)}")
 94 |             logger.exception(e)
 95 |             raise NotFoundError(f"Object with id {id} not found - {str(e)}")
 96 | 
 97 |     @classmethod
 98 |     def _get_class_by_table_name(cls, table_name: str) -> Optional[Type["ObjectModel"]]:
 99 |         """Find the appropriate subclass based on table_name."""
100 | 
101 |         def get_all_subclasses(c: Type["ObjectModel"]) -> List[Type["ObjectModel"]]:
102 |             all_subclasses: List[Type["ObjectModel"]] = []
103 |             for subclass in c.__subclasses__():
104 |                 all_subclasses.append(subclass)
105 |                 all_subclasses.extend(get_all_subclasses(subclass))
106 |             return all_subclasses
107 | 
108 |         for subclass in get_all_subclasses(ObjectModel):
109 |             if hasattr(subclass, "table_name") and subclass.table_name == table_name:
110 |                 return subclass
111 |         return None
112 | 
113 |     async def save(self) -> None:
114 |         """
115 |         Save the model to the database.
116 | 
117 |         Note: Embedding is no longer generated inline. Subclasses that need
118 |         embedding should override save() to submit the appropriate embed_*
119 |         command after calling super().save().
120 |         """
121 |         try:
122 |             self.model_validate(self.model_dump(), strict=True)
123 |             data = self._prepare_save_data()
124 |             data["updated"] = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
125 | 
126 |             repo_result: Union[List[Dict[str, Any]], Dict[str, Any]]
127 |             if self.id is None:
128 |                 data["created"] = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
129 |                 repo_result = await repo_create(self.__class__.table_name, data)
130 |             else:
131 |                 data["created"] = (
132 |                     self.created.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
133 |                     if isinstance(self.created, datetime)
134 |                     else self.created
135 |                 )
136 |                 logger.debug(f"Updating record with id {self.id}")
137 |                 repo_result = await repo_update(
138 |                     self.__class__.table_name, self.id, data
139 |                 )
140 |             # Update the current instance with the result
141 |             # repo_result is a list of dictionaries
142 |             result_list: List[Dict[str, Any]] = (
143 |                 repo_result if isinstance(repo_result, list) else [repo_result]
144 |             )
145 |             for key, value in result_list[0].items():
146 |                 if hasattr(self, key):
147 |                     if isinstance(getattr(self, key), BaseModel):
148 |                         setattr(self, key, type(getattr(self, key))(**value))
149 |                     else:
150 |                         setattr(self, key, value)
151 | 
152 |         except ValidationError as e:
153 |             logger.error(f"Validation failed: {e}")
154 |             raise
155 |         except RuntimeError:
156 |             # Transaction conflicts should propagate for retry
157 |             raise
158 |         except Exception as e:
159 |             logger.error(f"Error saving record: {e}")
160 |             raise DatabaseOperationError(e)
161 | 
162 |     def _prepare_save_data(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
163 |         data = self.model_dump()
164 |         return {
165 |             key: value
166 |             for key, value in data.items()
167 |             if value is not None or key in self.__class__.nullable_fields
168 |         }
169 | 
170 |     async def delete(self) -> bool:
171 |         if self.id is None:
172 |             raise InvalidInputError("Cannot delete object without an ID")
173 |         try:
174 |             logger.debug(f"Deleting record with id {self.id}")
175 |             return await repo_delete(self.id)
176 |         except Exception as e:
177 |             logger.error(
178 |                 f"Error deleting {self.__class__.table_name} with id {self.id}: {str(e)}"
179 |             )
180 |             raise DatabaseOperationError(
181 |                 f"Failed to delete {self.__class__.table_name}"
182 |             )
183 | 
184 |     async def relate(
185 |         self, relationship: str, target_id: str, data: Optional[Dict] = {}
186 |     ) -> Any:
187 |         if not relationship or not target_id or not self.id:
188 |             raise InvalidInputError("Relationship and target ID must be provided")
189 |         try:
190 |             return await repo_relate(
191 |                 source=self.id, relationship=relationship, target=target_id, data=data
192 |             )
193 |         except Exception as e:
194 |             logger.error(f"Error creating relationship: {str(e)}")
195 |             logger.exception(e)
196 |             raise DatabaseOperationError(e)
197 | 
198 |     @field_validator("created", "updated", mode="before")
199 |     @classmethod
200 |     def parse_datetime(cls, value):
201 |         if isinstance(value, str):
202 |             return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
203 |         return value
204 | 
205 | 
206 | class RecordModel(BaseModel):
207 |     model_config = ConfigDict(
208 |         validate_assignment=True,
209 |         arbitrary_types_allowed=True,
210 |         extra="allow",
211 |         from_attributes=True,
212 |         defer_build=True,
213 |     )
214 | 
215 |     record_id: ClassVar[str]
216 |     auto_save: ClassVar[bool] = (
217 |         False  # Default to False, can be overridden in subclasses
218 |     )
219 |     _instances: ClassVar[Dict[str, "RecordModel"]] = {}  # Store instances by record_id
220 | 
221 |     def __new__(cls, **kwargs):
222 |         # If an instance already exists for this record_id, return it
223 |         if cls.record_id in cls._instances:
224 |             instance = cls._instances[cls.record_id]
225 |             # Update instance with any new kwargs if provided
226 |             if kwargs:
227 |                 for key, value in kwargs.items():
228 |                     setattr(instance, key, value)
229 |             return instance
230 | 
231 |         # If no instance exists, create a new one
232 |         instance = super().__new__(cls)
233 |         cls._instances[cls.record_id] = instance
234 |         return instance
235 | 
236 |     def __init__(self, **kwargs):
237 |         # Only initialize if this is a new instance
238 |         if not hasattr(self, "_initialized"):
239 |             object.__setattr__(self, "__dict__", {})
240 | 
241 |             # For RecordModel, we need to handle async initialization differently
242 |             # Initialize with provided kwargs only for now
243 |             super().__init__(**kwargs)
244 | 
245 |             # Mark as initialized but not loaded from DB yet
246 |             object.__setattr__(self, "_initialized", True)
247 |             object.__setattr__(self, "_db_loaded", False)
248 | 
249 |     async def _load_from_db(self):
250 |         """Load data from database if not already loaded"""
251 |         if not getattr(self, "_db_loaded", False):
252 |             result = await repo_query(
253 |                 "SELECT * FROM ONLY $record_id",
254 |                 {"record_id": ensure_record_id(self.record_id)},
255 |             )
256 | 
257 |             # Handle case where record doesn't exist yet
258 |             if result:
259 |                 if isinstance(result, list) and len(result) > 0:
260 |                     # Standard list response
261 |                     row = result[0]
262 |                     if isinstance(row, dict):
263 |                         for key, value in row.items():
264 |                             if hasattr(self, key):
265 |                                 object.__setattr__(self, key, value)
266 |                 elif isinstance(result, dict):
267 |                     # Direct dict response
268 |                     for key, value in result.items():
269 |                         if hasattr(self, key):
270 |                             object.__setattr__(self, key, value)
271 | 
272 |             object.__setattr__(self, "_db_loaded", True)
273 | 
274 |     @classmethod
275 |     async def get_instance(cls) -> "RecordModel":
276 |         """Get or create the singleton instance and load from DB"""
277 |         instance = cls()
278 |         await instance._load_from_db()
279 |         return instance
280 | 
281 |     @model_validator(mode="after")
282 |     def auto_save_validator(self):
283 |         if self.__class__.auto_save:
284 |             # Auto-save can't work with async - log warning
285 |             logger.warning(
286 |                 f"Auto-save is enabled for {self.__class__.__name__} but update() is now async. Call await instance.update() manually."
287 |             )
288 |         return self
289 | 
290 |     async def update(self):
291 |         # Get all non-ClassVar fields and their values
292 |         data = {
293 |             field_name: getattr(self, field_name)
294 |             for field_name, field_info in self.model_fields.items()
295 |             if not str(field_info.annotation).startswith("typing.ClassVar")
296 |         }
297 | 
298 |         await repo_upsert(
299 |             self.__class__.table_name
300 |             if hasattr(self.__class__, "table_name")
301 |             else "record",
302 |             self.record_id,
303 |             data,
304 |         )
305 | 
306 |         result = await repo_query(
307 |             "SELECT * FROM $record_id", {"record_id": ensure_record_id(self.record_id)}
308 |         )
309 |         if result:
310 |             for key, value in result[0].items():
311 |                 if hasattr(self, key):
312 |                     object.__setattr__(
313 |                         self, key, value
314 |                     )  # Use object.__setattr__ to avoid triggering validation again
315 | 
316 |         return self
317 | 
318 |     @classmethod
319 |     def clear_instance(cls):
320 |         """Clear the singleton instance (useful for testing)"""
321 |         if cls.record_id in cls._instances:
322 |             del cls._instances[cls.record_id]
323 | 
324 |     async def patch(self, model_dict: dict):
325 |         """Update model attributes from dictionary and save"""
326 |         for key, value in model_dict.items():
327 |             setattr(self, key, value)
328 |         await self.update()
329 |

  1 | import { useQuery, useMutation, useQueryClient, useInfiniteQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
  2 | import { useCallback, useMemo } from 'react'
  3 | import { sourcesApi } from '@/lib/api/sources'
  4 | import { QUERY_KEYS } from '@/lib/api/query-client'
  5 | import { useToast } from '@/lib/hooks/use-toast'
  6 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
  7 | import { getApiErrorKey } from '@/lib/utils/error-handler'
  8 | import {
  9 |   CreateSourceRequest,
 10 |   UpdateSourceRequest,
 11 |   SourceResponse,
 12 |   SourceStatusResponse,
 13 |   SourceListResponse
 14 | } from '@/lib/types/api'
 15 | 
 16 | const NOTEBOOK_SOURCES_PAGE_SIZE = 30
 17 | 
 18 | export function useSources(notebookId?: string) {
 19 |   return useQuery({
 20 |     queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.sources(notebookId),
 21 |     queryFn: () => sourcesApi.list({ notebook_id: notebookId }),
 22 |     enabled: !!notebookId,
 23 |     staleTime: 5 * 1000, // 5 seconds - more responsive for real-time source updates
 24 |     refetchOnWindowFocus: true, // Refetch when user comes back to the tab
 25 |   })
 26 | }
 27 | 
 28 | /**
 29 |  * Hook for fetching notebook sources with infinite scroll pagination.
 30 |  * Returns flattened sources array and pagination controls.
 31 |  */
 32 | export function useNotebookSources(notebookId: string) {
 33 |   const queryClient = useQueryClient()
 34 | 
 35 |   const query = useInfiniteQuery({
 36 |     queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.sourcesInfinite(notebookId),
 37 |     queryFn: async ({ pageParam = 0 }) => {
 38 |       const data = await sourcesApi.list({
 39 |         notebook_id: notebookId,
 40 |         limit: NOTEBOOK_SOURCES_PAGE_SIZE,
 41 |         offset: pageParam,
 42 |         sort_by: 'updated',
 43 |         sort_order: 'desc',
 44 |       })
 45 |       return {
 46 |         sources: data,
 47 |         nextOffset: data.length === NOTEBOOK_SOURCES_PAGE_SIZE ? pageParam + data.length : undefined,
 48 |       }
 49 |     },
 50 |     initialPageParam: 0,
 51 |     getNextPageParam: (lastPage) => lastPage.nextOffset,
 52 |     enabled: !!notebookId,
 53 |     staleTime: 5 * 1000,
 54 |     refetchOnWindowFocus: true,
 55 |   })
 56 | 
 57 |   // Flatten all pages into a single array (memoized to prevent infinite re-renders)
 58 |   const sources: SourceListResponse[] = useMemo(
 59 |     () => query.data?.pages.flatMap(page => page.sources) ?? [],
 60 |     [query.data?.pages]
 61 |   )
 62 | 
 63 |   // Refetch function that resets to first page
 64 |   const refetch = useCallback(() => {
 65 |     queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.sourcesInfinite(notebookId) })
 66 |   }, [queryClient, notebookId])
 67 | 
 68 |   return {
 69 |     sources,
 70 |     isLoading: query.isLoading,
 71 |     isFetchingNextPage: query.isFetchingNextPage,
 72 |     hasNextPage: query.hasNextPage,
 73 |     fetchNextPage: query.fetchNextPage,
 74 |     refetch,
 75 |     error: query.error,
 76 |   }
 77 | }
 78 | 
 79 | export function useSource(id: string) {
 80 |   return useQuery({
 81 |     queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.source(id),
 82 |     queryFn: () => sourcesApi.get(id),
 83 |     enabled: !!id,
 84 |     staleTime: 30 * 1000, // 30 seconds - shorter stale time for more responsive updates
 85 |     refetchOnWindowFocus: true, // Refetch when user comes back to the tab
 86 |   })
 87 | }
 88 | 
 89 | export function useCreateSource() {
 90 |   const queryClient = useQueryClient()
 91 |   const { toast } = useToast()
 92 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 93 | 
 94 |   return useMutation({
 95 |     mutationFn: (data: CreateSourceRequest) => sourcesApi.create(data),
 96 |     onSuccess: (result: SourceResponse, variables) => {
 97 |       // Invalidate queries for all relevant notebooks with immediate refetch
 98 |       if (variables.notebooks) {
 99 |         variables.notebooks.forEach(notebookId => {
100 |           queryClient.invalidateQueries({
101 |             queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.sources(notebookId),
102 |             refetchType: 'active' // Refetch active queries immediately
103 |           })
104 |         })
105 |       } else if (variables.notebook_id) {
106 |         queryClient.invalidateQueries({
107 |           queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.sources(variables.notebook_id),
108 |           refetchType: 'active'
109 |         })
110 |       }
111 | 
112 |       // Invalidate general sources query too with immediate refetch
113 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({
114 |         queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.sources(),
115 |         refetchType: 'active'
116 |       })
117 | 
118 |       // Show different messages based on processing mode
119 |       if (variables.async_processing) {
120 |         toast({
121 |           title: t.sources.sourceQueued,
122 |           description: t.sources.sourceQueuedDesc,
123 |         })
124 |       } else {
125 |         toast({
126 |           title: t.common.success,
127 |           description: t.sources.sourceAddedSuccess,
128 |         })
129 |       }
130 |     },
131 |     onError: (error: unknown) => {
132 |       toast({
133 |         title: t.common.error,
134 |         description: t(getApiErrorKey(error, t.sources.failedToAddSource)),
135 |         variant: 'destructive',
136 |       })
137 |     },
138 |   })
139 | }

222 | export function useSourceStatus(sourceId: string, enabled = true) {
223 |   return useQuery({
224 |     queryKey: ['sources', sourceId, 'status'],
225 |     queryFn: () => sourcesApi.status(sourceId),
226 |     enabled: !!sourceId && enabled,
227 |     refetchInterval: (query) => {
228 |       // Auto-refresh every 2 seconds if processing
229 |       // The query.state.data contains the SourceStatusResponse
230 |       const data = query.state.data as SourceStatusResponse | undefined
231 |       if (data?.status === 'running' || data?.status === 'queued' || data?.status === 'new') {
232 |         return 2000
233 |       }
234 |       // No auto-refresh if completed, failed, or unknown
235 |       return false
236 |     },
237 |     staleTime: 0, // Always consider status data stale for real-time updates
238 |     retry: (failureCount, error) => {
239 |       // Don't retry on 404 (source not found)
240 |       const axiosError = error as { response?: { status?: number } }
241 |       if (axiosError?.response?.status === 404) {
242 |         return false
243 |       }
244 |       return failureCount < 3
245 |     },
246 |   })
247 | }

256 |     onSuccess: (result, sourceId) => {

258 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({
259 |         queryKey: ['sources', sourceId, 'status']
260 |       })
261 |       // Invalidate ALL sources queries to refresh the UI

264 | 
265 |       toast({

268 |       })

274 |         variant: 'destructive',
275 |       })
276 |     },
277 |   })

280 | export function useAddSourcesToNotebook() {
281 |   const queryClient = useQueryClient()
282 |   const { toast } = useToast()
283 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
284 | 
285 |   return useMutation({
286 |     mutationFn: async ({ notebookId, sourceIds }: { notebookId: string; sourceIds: string[] }) => {
287 |       const { notebooksApi } = await import('@/lib/api/notebooks')
288 | 
289 |       // Use Promise.allSettled to handle partial failures gracefully
290 |       const results = await Promise.allSettled(
291 |         sourceIds.map(sourceId => notebooksApi.addSource(notebookId, sourceId))
292 |       )
293 | 
294 |       // Count successes and failures
295 |       const successes = results.filter(r => r.status === 'fulfilled').length
296 |       const failures = results.filter(r => r.status === 'rejected').length
297 | 
298 |       return { successes, failures, total: sourceIds.length }
299 |     },
300 |     onSuccess: (result, { notebookId, sourceIds }) => {
301 |       // Invalidate ALL sources queries to refresh all lists
302 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['sources'] })
303 |       // Specifically invalidate the notebook's sources
304 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.sources(notebookId) })
305 |       // Invalidate each affected source
306 |       sourceIds.forEach(sourceId => {
307 |         queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: QUERY_KEYS.source(sourceId) })
308 |       })
309 | 
310 |       // Show appropriate toast based on results
311 |       if (result.failures === 0) {
312 |         toast({
313 |           title: t.common.success,
314 |           description: t.sources.sourcesAddedToNotebook.replace('{count}', result.successes.toString()),
315 |         })
316 |       } else if (result.successes === 0) {
317 |         toast({
318 |           title: t.common.error,
319 |           description: t.sources.failedToAddSourcesToNotebook,
320 |           variant: 'destructive',
321 |         })
322 |       } else {
323 |         toast({
324 |           title: t.common.success,
325 |           description: t.sources.partialAddSuccess
326 |             .replace('{success}', result.successes.toString())
327 |             .replace('{failed}', result.failures.toString()),
328 |           variant: 'default',
329 |         })
330 |       }
331 |     },
332 |     onError: (error: unknown) => {
333 |       toast({
334 |         title: t.common.error,
335 |         description: t(getApiErrorKey(error, t.sources.failedToAddSourcesToNotebook)),
336 |         variant: 'destructive',
337 |       })
338 |     },
339 |   })
340 | }

342 | export function useRemoveSourceFromNotebook() {
343 |   const queryClient = useQueryClient()

352 |     },

358 |       // Also invalidate the specific source

360 | 
361 |       toast({
362 |         title: t.common.success,
363 |         description: t.sources.sourceRemovedFromNotebook,
364 |       })
365 |     },
366 |     onError: (error: unknown) => {
367 |       toast({
368 |         title: t.common.error,
369 |         description: t(getApiErrorKey(error, t.sources.failedToRemoveSourceFromNotebook)),

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # AI Providers - Configuration Reference
  2 | 
  3 | Complete setup instructions for each AI provider. Pick the one you're using.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## Cloud Providers (Recommended for Most)
  8 | 
  9 | ### OpenAI
 10 | 
 11 | **Cost:** ~$0.03-0.15 per 1K tokens (varies by model)
 12 | 
 13 | **Setup:**
 14 | ```bash
 15 | 1. Go to https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
 16 | 2. Create account (if needed)
 17 | 3. Create new API key (starts with "sk-proj-")
 18 | 4. Add $5+ credits to account
 19 | 5. Add to .env:
 20 |    OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...
 21 | 6. Restart services
 22 | ```
 23 | 
 24 | **Environment Variable:**
 25 | ```
 26 | OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-xxxxx
 27 | ```
 28 | 
 29 | **Available Models (in Open Notebook):**
 30 | - `gpt-4o` — Best quality, fast (latest version)
 31 | - `gpt-4o-mini` — Fast, cheap, good for testing
 32 | - `o1` — Advanced reasoning model (slower, more expensive)
 33 | - `o1-mini` — Faster reasoning model
 34 | 
 35 | **Recommended:**
 36 | - For general use: `gpt-4o` (best balance)
 37 | - For testing/cheap: `gpt-4o-mini` (90% cheaper)
 38 | - For complex reasoning: `o1` (best for hard problems)
 39 | 
 40 | **Cost Estimate:**
 41 | ```
 42 | Light use: $1-5/month
 43 | Medium use: $10-30/month
 44 | Heavy use: $50-100+/month
 45 | ```
 46 | 
 47 | **Troubleshooting:**
 48 | - "Invalid API key" → Check key starts with "sk-proj-"
 49 | - "Rate limit exceeded" → Wait or upgrade account
 50 | - "Model not available" → Try gpt-4o-mini instead
 51 | 
 52 | ---
 53 | 
 54 | ### Anthropic (Claude)
 55 | 
 56 | **Cost:** ~$0.80-3.00 per 1M tokens (cheaper than OpenAI for long context)
 57 | 
 58 | **Setup:**
 59 | ```bash
 60 | 1. Go to https://console.anthropic.com/
 61 | 2. Create account or login
 62 | 3. Go to API keys section
 63 | 4. Create new API key (starts with "sk-ant-")
 64 | 5. Add to .env:
 65 |    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
 66 | 6. Restart services
 67 | ```
 68 | 
 69 | **Environment Variable:**
 70 | ```
 71 | ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-xxxxx
 72 | ```
 73 | 
 74 | **Available Models:**
 75 | - `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` — Latest, best quality (recommended)
 76 | - `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022` — Previous generation, still excellent
 77 | - `claude-3-5-haiku-20241022` — Fast, cheap
 78 | - `claude-opus-4-5-20251101` — Most powerful, expensive
 79 | 
 80 | **Recommended:**
 81 | - For general use: `claude-sonnet-4-5` (best overall, latest)
 82 | - For cheap: `claude-3-5-haiku` (80% cheaper)
 83 | - For complex: `claude-opus-4-5` (most capable)
 84 | 
 85 | **Cost Estimate:**
 86 | ```
 87 | Sonnet: $3-20/month (typical use)
 88 | Haiku: $0.50-3/month
 89 | Opus: $10-50+/month
 90 | ```
 91 | 
 92 | **Advantages:**
 93 | - Great long-context support (200K tokens)
 94 | - Excellent reasoning
 95 | - Fast processing
 96 | 
 97 | **Troubleshooting:**
 98 | - "Invalid API key" → Check it starts with "sk-ant-"
 99 | - "Overloaded" → Anthropic is busy, retry later
100 | - "Model unavailable" → Check model name is correct
101 | 
102 | ---
103 | 
104 | ### Google Gemini
105 | 
106 | **Cost:** ~$0.075-0.30 per 1K tokens (competitive with OpenAI)
107 | 
108 | **Setup:**
109 | ```bash
110 | 1. Go to https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey
111 | 2. Create account or login
112 | 3. Create new API key
113 | 4. Add to .env:
114 |    GOOGLE_API_KEY=AIzaSy...
115 | 5. Restart services
116 | ```
117 | 
118 | **Environment Variable:**
119 | ```
120 | GOOGLE_API_KEY=AIzaSy...
121 | # Optional: override default endpoint
122 | GEMINI_API_BASE_URL=https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models
123 | ```
124 | 
125 | **Available Models:**
126 | - `gemini-2.0-flash-exp` — Latest experimental, fastest (recommended)
127 | - `gemini-2.0-flash` — Stable version, fast, cheap
128 | - `gemini-1.5-pro-latest` — More capable, longer context
129 | - `gemini-1.5-flash` — Previous generation, very cheap
130 | 
131 | **Recommended:**
132 | - For general use: `gemini-2.0-flash-exp` (best value, latest)
133 | - For cheap: `gemini-1.5-flash` (very cheap)
134 | - For complex/long context: `gemini-1.5-pro-latest` (2M token context)
135 | 
136 | **Advantages:**
137 | - Very long context (1M tokens)
138 | - Multimodal (images, audio, video)
139 | - Good for podcasts
140 | 
141 | **Troubleshooting:**
142 | - "API key invalid" → Get fresh key from aistudio.google.com
143 | - "Quota exceeded" → Free tier limited, upgrade account
144 | - "Model not found" → Check model name spelling
145 | 
146 | ---
147 | 
148 | ### Groq
149 | 
150 | **Cost:** ~$0.05 per 1M tokens (cheapest, but limited models)
151 | 
152 | **Setup:**
153 | ```bash
154 | 1. Go to https://console.groq.com/keys
155 | 2. Create account or login
156 | 3. Create new API key
157 | 4. Add to .env:
158 |    GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_...
159 | 5. Restart services
160 | ```
161 | 
162 | **Environment Variable:**
163 | ```
164 | GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_xxxxx
165 | ```
166 | 
167 | **Available Models:**
168 | - `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` — Best on Groq (recommended)
169 | - `llama-3.1-70b-versatile` — Fast, capable
170 | - `mixtral-8x7b-32768` — Good alternative
171 | - `gemma2-9b-it` — Small, very fast
172 | 
173 | **Recommended:**
174 | - For quality: `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` (best overall)
175 | - For speed: `gemma2-9b-it` (ultra-fast)
176 | - For balance: `llama-3.1-70b-versatile`
177 | 
178 | **Advantages:**
179 | - Ultra-fast inference
180 | - Very cheap
181 | - Great for transformations/batch work
182 | 
183 | **Disadvantages:**
184 | - Limited model selection
185 | - Smaller models than OpenAI/Anthropic
186 | 
187 | **Troubleshooting:**
188 | - "Rate limited" → Free tier has limits, upgrade
189 | - "Model not available" → Check supported models list
190 | 
191 | ---
192 | 
193 | ### OpenRouter
194 | 
195 | **Cost:** Varies by model ($0.05-15 per 1M tokens)
196 | 
197 | **Setup:**
198 | ```bash
199 | 1. Go to https://openrouter.ai/keys
200 | 2. Create account or login
201 | 3. Add credits to your account
202 | 4. Create new API key
203 | 5. Add to .env:
204 |    OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...
205 | 6. Restart services
206 | ```
207 | 
208 | **Environment Variable:**
209 | ```
210 | OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-xxxxx
211 | ```
212 | 
213 | **Available Models (100+ options):**
214 | - OpenAI: `openai/gpt-4o`, `openai/o1`
215 | - Anthropic: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`, `anthropic/claude-3.5-haiku`
216 | - Google: `google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp`, `google/gemini-1.5-pro`
217 | - Meta: `meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct`, `meta-llama/llama-3.1-405b-instruct`
218 | - Mistral: `mistralai/mistral-large-2411`
219 | - DeepSeek: `deepseek/deepseek-chat`
220 | - And many more...
221 | 
222 | **Recommended:**
223 | - For quality: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` (best overall)
224 | - For speed/cost: `google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp` (very fast, cheap)
225 | - For open-source: `meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct`
226 | - For reasoning: `openai/o1`
227 | 
228 | **Advantages:**
229 | - One API key for 100+ models
230 | - Unified billing
231 | - Easy model comparison
232 | - Access to models that may have waitlists elsewhere
233 | 
234 | **Cost Estimate:**
235 | ```
236 | Light use: $1-5/month
237 | Medium use: $10-30/month
238 | Heavy use: Depends on models chosen
239 | ```
240 | 
241 | **Troubleshooting:**
242 | - "Invalid API key" → Check it starts with "sk-or-"
243 | - "Insufficient credits" → Add credits at openrouter.ai
244 | - "Model not available" → Check model ID spelling (use full path)
245 | 
246 | ---
247 | 
248 | ## Self-Hosted / Local
249 | 
250 | ### Ollama (Recommended for Local)
251 | 
252 | **Cost:** Free (electricity only)
253 | 
254 | **Setup:**
255 | ```bash
256 | 1. Install Ollama: https://ollama.ai
257 | 2. Run Ollama in background:
258 |    ollama serve
259 | 
260 | 3. Download a model:
261 |    ollama pull mistral
262 |    # or llama2, neural-chat, phi, etc.
263 | 
264 | 4. Add to .env:
265 |    OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://localhost:11434
266 |    # If on different machine:
267 |    # OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://10.0.0.5:11434
268 | 
269 | 5. Restart services
270 | ```
271 | 
272 | **Environment Variable:**
273 | ```
274 | OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://localhost:11434
275 | ```
276 | 
277 | **Available Models:**
278 | - `llama3.3:70b` — Best quality (requires 40GB+ RAM)
279 | - `llama3.1:8b` — Recommended, balanced (8GB RAM)
280 | - `qwen2.5:7b` — Excellent for code and reasoning
281 | - `mistral:7b` — Good general purpose
282 | - `phi3:3.8b` — Small, fast (4GB RAM)
283 | - `gemma2:9b` — Google's model, balanced
284 | - Many more: `ollama list` to see available
285 | 
286 | **Recommended:**
287 | - For quality (with GPU): `llama3.3:70b` (best)
288 | - For general use: `llama3.1:8b` (best balance)
289 | - For speed/low memory: `phi3:3.8b` (very fast)
290 | - For coding: `qwen2.5:7b` (excellent at code)
291 | 
292 | **Hardware Requirements:**
293 | ```
294 | GPU (NVIDIA/AMD):
295 |   8GB VRAM: Runs most models fine
296 |   6GB VRAM: Works, slower
297 |   4GB VRAM: Small models only
298 | 
299 | CPU-only:
300 |   16GB+ RAM: Slow but works
301 |   8GB RAM: Very slow
302 |   4GB RAM: Not recommended
303 | ```
304 | 
305 | **Advantages:**
306 | - Completely private (runs locally)
307 | - Free (electricity only)
308 | - No API key needed
309 | - Works offline
310 | 
311 | **Disadvantages:**
312 | - Slower than cloud (unless on GPU)
313 | - Smaller models than cloud
314 | - Requires local hardware
315 | 
316 | **Troubleshooting:**
317 | - "Connection refused" → Ollama not running or wrong port
318 | - "Model not found" → Download it: `ollama pull modelname`
319 | - "Out of memory" → Use smaller model or add more RAM
320 | 
321 | ---
322 | 
323 | ### LM Studio (Local Alternative)
324 | 
325 | **Cost:** Free
326 | 
327 | **Setup:**
328 | ```bash
329 | 1. Download LM Studio: https://lmstudio.ai
330 | 2. Open app
331 | 3. Download a model from library
332 | 4. Go to "Local Server" tab
333 | 5. Start server (default port: 1234)
334 | 6. Add to .env:
335 |    OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:1234/v1
336 |    OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY=not-needed
337 | 7. Restart services
338 | ```
339 | 
340 | **Environment Variables:**
341 | ```
342 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:1234/v1
343 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY=lm-studio  # Just a placeholder
344 | ```
345 | 
346 | **Advantages:**
347 | - GUI interface (easier than Ollama CLI)
348 | - Good model selection
349 | - Privacy-focused
350 | - Works offline
351 | 
352 | **Disadvantages:**
353 | - Desktop only (Mac/Windows/Linux)
354 | - Slower than cloud
355 | - Requires local GPU
356 | 
357 | ---
358 | 
359 | ### Custom OpenAI-Compatible
360 | 
361 | For Text Generation UI, vLLM, or other OpenAI-compatible endpoints:
362 | 
363 | ```bash
364 | Add to .env:
365 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=http://your-endpoint/v1
366 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY=your-api-key
367 | ```
368 | 
369 | If you need different endpoints for different modalities:
370 | 
371 | ```bash
372 | # Language model
373 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_LLM=http://localhost:8000/v1
374 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY_LLM=sk-...
375 | 
376 | # Embeddings
377 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_EMBEDDING=http://localhost:8001/v1
378 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY_EMBEDDING=sk-...
379 | 
380 | # TTS (text-to-speech)
381 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_TTS=http://localhost:8002/v1
382 | OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY_TTS=sk-...
383 | ```
384 | 
385 | ---
386 | 
387 | ## Enterprise
388 | 
389 | ### Azure OpenAI
390 | 
391 | **Cost:** Same as OpenAI (usage-based)
392 | 
393 | **Setup:**
394 | ```bash
395 | 1. Create Azure OpenAI service in Azure portal
396 | 2. Deploy GPT-4/3.5-turbo model
397 | 3. Get your endpoint and key
398 | 4. Add to .env:
399 |    AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key
400 |    AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT=https://your-name.openai.azure.com/
401 |    AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION=2024-12-01-preview
402 | 5. Restart services
403 | ```
404 | 
405 | **Environment Variables:**
406 | ```
407 | AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY=xxxxx
408 | AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT=https://your-instance.openai.azure.com/
409 | AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION=2024-12-01-preview
410 | 
411 | # Optional: Different deployments for different modalities
412 | AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY_LLM=xxxxx
413 | AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT_LLM=https://your-instance.openai.azure.com/
414 | AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION_LLM=2024-12-01-preview
415 | ```
416 | 
417 | **Advantages:**
418 | - Enterprise support
419 | - VPC integration
420 | - Compliance (HIPAA, SOC2, etc.)
421 | 
422 | **Disadvantages:**
423 | - More complex setup
424 | - Higher overhead
425 | - Requires Azure account
426 | 
427 | ---
428 | 
429 | ## Embeddings (For Search/Semantic Features)
430 | 
431 | By default, Open Notebook uses the LLM provider's embeddings. To use a different provider:
432 | 
433 | ### OpenAI Embeddings (Default)
434 | ```
435 | # Uses OpenAI's embedding model automatically
436 | # Requires OPENAI_API_KEY
437 | # No separate configuration needed
438 | ```
439 | 
440 | ### Custom Embeddings
441 | ```
442 | # For other embedding providers (future feature)
443 | EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai  # or custom
444 | ```
445 | 
446 | ---
447 | 
448 | ## Choosing Your Provider
449 | 
450 | **1. Don't want to run locally and don't want to mess around with different providers:** 
451 | 
452 | Use OpenAI
453 | - Cloud-based
454 | - Good quality
455 | - Reasonable cost
456 | - Simplest setup, supports all modes (text, embedding, tts, stt, etc)
457 | 
458 | **For budget-conscious:** Groq, OpenRouter or Ollama
459 | - Groq: Super cheap cloud
460 | - Ollama: Free, but local
461 | - OpenRouter: many open source models very accessible
462 | 
463 | **For privacy-first:** Ollama or LM Studio and Speaches ([TTS](local-tts.md), [STT](local-stt.md))
464 | - Everything stays local
465 | - Works offline
466 | - No API keys sent anywhere
467 | 
468 | **For enterprise:** Azure OpenAI
469 | - Compliance
470 | - VPC integration
471 | - Support
472 | 
473 | ---
474 | 
475 | ## Next Steps
476 | 
477 | 1. **Choose your provider** from above
478 | 2. **Get API key** (if cloud) or install locally (if Ollama)
479 | 3. **Add to .env**
480 | 4. **Restart services**
481 | 5. **Go to Settings → Models** in Open Notebook
482 | 6. **Verify it works** with a test chat
483 | 
484 | Done!
485 | 
486 | ---
487 |

489 |

491 | - **[Advanced Configuration](advanced.md)** - Timeouts, SSL, performance tuning
492 | - **[Ollama Setup](ollama.md)** - Detailed Ollama configuration guide
493 | - **[OpenAI-Compatible](openai-compatible.md)** - LM Studio and other compatible providers
494 | - **[Local TTS Setup](local-tts.md)** - Text-to-speech with Speaches
495 | - **[Local STT Setup](local-stt.md)** - Speech-to-text with Speaches
496 | - **[Troubleshooting](../6-TROUBLESHOOTING/quick-fixes.md)** - Common issues and fixes
497 |

336 |                   <TooltipTrigger asChild>
337 |                     <div>
338 |                       <LanguageToggle iconOnly />
339 |                     </div>
340 |                   </TooltipTrigger>
341 |                   <TooltipContent side="right">{t.common.language}</TooltipContent>
342 |                 </Tooltip>
343 |               </>
344 |             ) : (
345 |               <>
346 |                 <ThemeToggle />
347 |                 <LanguageToggle />
348 |               </>
349 |             )}
350 |           </div>
351 | 
352 |           {isCollapsed ? (
353 |             <Tooltip>
354 |               <TooltipTrigger asChild>
355 |                 <Button
356 |                   variant="outline"
357 |                   className="w-full justify-center sidebar-menu-item"
358 |                   onClick={logout}
359 |                   aria-label={t.common.signOut}
360 |                 >
361 |                   <LogOut className="h-4 w-4" />
362 |                 </Button>
363 |               </TooltipTrigger>
364 |                <TooltipContent side="right">{t.common.signOut}</TooltipContent>
365 |             </Tooltip>
366 |           ) : (
367 |             <Button
368 |               variant="outline"
369 |               className="w-full justify-start gap-3 sidebar-menu-item"
370 |               onClick={logout}
371 |               aria-label={t.common.signOut}
372 |              >
373 |               <LogOut className="h-4 w-4" />
374 |               {t.common.signOut}
375 |             </Button>
376 |           )}
377 |         </div>
378 |       </div>
379 |     </TooltipProvider>
380 |   )
381 | }

/docs/7-DEVELOPMENT/maintainer-guide.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Maintainer Guide
  2 | 
  3 | This guide is for project maintainers to help manage contributions effectively while maintaining project quality and vision.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Table of Contents
  6 | 
  7 | - [Issue Management](#issue-management)
  8 | - [Pull Request Review](#pull-request-review)
  9 | - [Common Scenarios](#common-scenarios)
 10 | - [Communication Templates](#communication-templates)
 11 | 
 12 | ## Issue Management
 13 | 
 14 | ### When a New Issue is Created
 15 | 
 16 | **1. Initial Triage** (within 24-48 hours)
 17 | 
 18 | - Add appropriate labels:
 19 |   - `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, etc.
 20 |   - `good first issue` for beginner-friendly tasks
 21 |   - `needs-triage` until reviewed
 22 |   - `help wanted` if you'd welcome community contributions
 23 | 
 24 | - Quick assessment:
 25 |   - Is it clear and well-described?
 26 |   - Is it aligned with project vision? (See [design-principles.md](design-principles.md))
 27 |   - Does it duplicate an existing issue?
 28 | 
 29 | **2. Initial Response**
 30 | 
 31 | ```markdown
 32 | Thanks for opening this issue! We'll review it and get back to you soon.
 33 | 
 34 | [If it's a bug] In the meantime, have you checked our troubleshooting guide?
 35 | 
 36 | [If it's a feature] You might find our [design principles](design-principles.md) helpful for understanding what we're building toward.
 37 | ```
 38 | 
 39 | **3. Decision Making**
 40 | 
 41 | Ask yourself:
 42 | - Does this align with our [design principles](design-principles.md)?
 43 | - Is this something we want in the core project, or better as a plugin/extension?
 44 | - Do we have the capacity to support this feature long-term?
 45 | - Will this benefit most users, or just a specific use case?
 46 | 
 47 | **4. Issue Assignment**
 48 | 
 49 | If the contributor checked "I am a developer and would like to work on this":
 50 | 
 51 | **For Accepted Issues:**
 52 | ```markdown
 53 | Great idea! This aligns well with our goals, particularly [specific design principle].
 54 | 
 55 | I see you'd like to work on this. Before you start:
 56 | 
 57 | 1. Please share your proposed approach/solution
 58 | 2. Review our [Contributing Guide](contributing.md) and [Design Principles](design-principles.md)
 59 | 3. Once we agree on the approach, I'll assign this to you
 60 | 
 61 | Looking forward to your thoughts!
 62 | ```
 63 | 
 64 | **For Issues Needing Clarification:**
 65 | ```markdown
 66 | Thanks for offering to work on this! Before we proceed, we need to clarify a few things:
 67 | 
 68 | 1. [Question 1]
 69 | 2. [Question 2]
 70 | 
 71 | Once we have these details, we can discuss the best approach.
 72 | ```
 73 | 
 74 | **For Issues Not Aligned with Vision:**
 75 | ```markdown
 76 | Thank you for the suggestion and for offering to work on this!
 77 | 
 78 | After reviewing against our [design principles](design-principles.md), we've decided not to pursue this in the core project because [specific reason].
 79 | 
 80 | However, you might be able to achieve this through [alternative approach, if applicable].
 81 | 
 82 | We appreciate your interest in contributing! Feel free to check out our [open issues](link) for other ways to contribute.
 83 | ```
 84 | 
 85 | ### Labels to Use
 86 | 
 87 | **Priority:**
 88 | - `priority: critical` - Security issues, data loss bugs
 89 | - `priority: high` - Major functionality broken
 90 | - `priority: medium` - Annoying bugs, useful features
 91 | - `priority: low` - Nice to have, edge cases
 92 | 
 93 | **Status:**
 94 | - `needs-triage` - Not yet reviewed by maintainer
 95 | - `needs-info` - Waiting for more information from reporter
 96 | - `needs-discussion` - Requires community/team discussion
 97 | - `ready` - Approved and ready to be worked on
 98 | - `in-progress` - Someone is actively working on this
 99 | - `blocked` - Cannot proceed due to external dependency
100 | 
101 | **Type:**
102 | - `bug` - Something is broken
103 | - `enhancement` - New feature or improvement
104 | - `documentation` - Documentation improvements
105 | - `question` - General questions
106 | - `refactor` - Code cleanup/restructuring
107 | 
108 | **Difficulty:**
109 | - `good first issue` - Good for newcomers
110 | - `help wanted` - Community contributions welcome
111 | - `advanced` - Requires deep codebase knowledge
112 | 
113 | ## Pull Request Review
114 | 
115 | ### Initial PR Review Checklist
116 | 
117 | **Before diving into code:**
118 | 
119 | - [ ] Is there an associated approved issue?
120 | - [ ] Does the PR reference the issue number?
121 | - [ ] Is the PR description clear about what changed and why?
122 | - [ ] Did the contributor check the relevant boxes in the PR template?
123 | - [ ] Are there tests? Screenshots (for UI changes)?
124 | 
125 | **Red Flags** (may require closing PR):
126 | - No associated issue
127 | - Issue was not assigned to contributor
128 | - PR tries to solve multiple unrelated problems
129 | - Breaking changes without discussion
130 | - Conflicts with project vision
131 | 
132 | ### Code Review Process
133 | 
134 | **1. High-Level Review**
135 | 
136 | - Does the approach align with our architecture?
137 | - Is the solution appropriately scoped?
138 | - Are there simpler alternatives?
139 | - Does it follow our design principles?
140 | 
141 | **2. Code Quality Review**
142 | 
143 | Python:
144 | - [ ] Follows PEP 8
145 | - [ ] Has type hints
146 | - [ ] Has docstrings
147 | - [ ] Proper error handling
148 | - [ ] No security vulnerabilities
149 | 
150 | TypeScript/Frontend:
151 | - [ ] Follows TypeScript best practices
152 | - [ ] Proper component structure
153 | - [ ] No console.logs left in production code
154 | - [ ] Accessible UI components
155 | 
156 | **3. Testing Review**
157 | 
158 | - [ ] Has appropriate test coverage
159 | - [ ] Tests are meaningful (not just for coverage percentage)
160 | - [ ] Tests pass locally and in CI
161 | - [ ] Edge cases are tested
162 | 
163 | **4. Documentation Review**
164 | 
165 | - [ ] Code is well-commented
166 | - [ ] Complex logic is explained
167 | - [ ] User-facing documentation updated (if applicable)
168 | - [ ] API documentation updated (if API changed)
169 | - [ ] Migration guide provided (if breaking change)
170 | 
171 | ### Providing Feedback
172 | 
173 | **Positive Feedback** (important!):
174 | ```markdown
175 | Thanks for this PR! I really like [specific thing they did well].
176 | 
177 | [Feedback on what needs to change]
178 | ```
179 | 
180 | **Requesting Changes:**
181 | ```markdown
182 | This is a great start! A few things to address:
183 | 
184 | 1. **[High-level concern]**: [Explanation and suggested approach]
185 | 2. **[Code quality issue]**: [Specific example and fix]
186 | 3. **[Testing gap]**: [What scenarios need coverage]
187 | 
188 | Let me know if you have questions about any of this!
189 | ```
190 | 
191 | **Suggesting Alternative Approach:**
192 | ```markdown
193 | I appreciate the effort you put into this! However, I'm concerned about [specific issue].
194 | 
195 | Have you considered [alternative approach]? It might be better because [reasons].
196 | 
197 | What do you think?
198 | ```
199 | 
200 | ## Common Scenarios
201 | 
202 | ### Scenario 1: Good Code, Wrong Approach
203 | 
204 | **Situation**: Contributor wrote quality code, but solved the problem in a way that doesn't fit our architecture.
205 | 
206 | **Response:**
207 | ```markdown
208 | Thank you for this PR! The code quality is great, and I can see you put thought into this.
209 | 
210 | However, I'm concerned that this approach [specific architectural concern]. In our architecture, we [explain the pattern we follow].
211 | 
212 | Would you be open to refactoring this to [suggested approach]? I'm happy to provide guidance on the specifics.
213 | 
214 | Alternatively, if you don't have time for a refactor, I can take over and finish this up (with credit to you, of course).
215 | 
216 | Let me know what you prefer!
217 | ```
218 | 
219 | ### Scenario 2: PR Without Assigned Issue
220 | 
221 | **Situation**: Contributor submitted PR without going through issue approval process.
222 | 
223 | **Response:**
224 | ```markdown
225 | Thanks for the PR! I appreciate you taking the time to contribute.
226 | 
227 | However, to maintain project coherence, we require all PRs to be linked to an approved issue that was assigned to the contributor. This is explained in our [Contributing Guide](contributing.md).
228 | 
229 | This helps us:
230 | - Ensure work aligns with project vision
231 | - Prevent duplicate efforts
232 | - Discuss approach before implementation
233 | 
234 | Could you please:
235 | 1. Create an issue describing this change
236 | 2. Wait for it to be reviewed and assigned to you
237 | 3. We can then reopen this PR or you can create a new one
238 | 
239 | Sorry for the inconvenience - this process helps us manage the project effectively.
240 | ```
241 | 
242 | ### Scenario 3: Feature Request Not Aligned with Vision
243 | 
244 | **Situation**: Well-intentioned feature that doesn't fit project goals.
245 | 
246 | **Response:**
247 | ```markdown
248 | Thank you for this suggestion! I can see how this would be useful for [specific use case].
249 | 
250 | After reviewing against our [design principles](design-principles.md), we've decided not to include this in the core project because [specific reason - e.g., "it conflicts with our 'Simplicity Over Features' principle" or "it would require dependencies that conflict with our privacy-first approach"].
251 | 
252 | Some alternatives:
253 | - [If applicable] This could be built as a plugin/extension
254 | - [If applicable] This functionality might be achievable through [existing feature]
255 | - [If applicable] You might be interested in [other tool] which is designed for this use case
256 | 
257 | We appreciate your contribution and hope you understand. Feel free to check our roadmap or open issues for other ways to contribute!
258 | ```
259 | 
260 | ### Scenario 4: Contributor Ghosts After Feedback
261 | 
262 | **Situation**: You requested changes, but contributor hasn't responded in 2+ weeks.
263 | 
264 | **After 2 weeks:**
265 | ```markdown
266 | Hey there! Just checking in on this PR. Do you have time to address the feedback, or would you like someone else to take over?
267 | 
268 | No pressure either way - just want to make sure this doesn't fall through the cracks.
269 | ```
270 | 
271 | **After 1 month with no response:**
272 | ```markdown
273 | Thanks again for starting this work! Since we haven't heard back, I'm going to close this PR for now.
274 | 
275 | If you want to pick this up again in the future, feel free to reopen it or create a new PR. Alternatively, I'll mark the issue as available for someone else to work on.
276 | 
277 | We appreciate your contribution!
278 | ```
279 | 
280 | Then:
281 | - Close the PR
282 | - Unassign the issue
283 | - Add `help wanted` label to the issue
284 | 
285 | ### Scenario 5: Breaking Changes Without Discussion
286 | 
287 | **Situation**: PR introduces breaking changes that weren't discussed.
288 | 
289 | **Response:**
290 | ```markdown
291 | Thanks for this PR! However, I notice this introduces breaking changes that weren't discussed in the original issue.
292 | 
293 | Breaking changes require:
294 | 1. Prior discussion and approval
295 | 2. Migration guide for users
296 | 3. Deprecation period (when possible)
297 | 4. Clear documentation of the change
298 | 
299 | Could we discuss the breaking changes first? Specifically:
300 | - [What breaks and why]
301 | - [Who will be affected]
302 | - [Migration path]
303 | 
304 | We may need to adjust the approach to minimize impact on existing users.
305 | ```
306 | 
307 | ## Communication Templates
308 | 
309 | ### Closing a PR (Misaligned with Vision)
310 | 
311 | ```markdown
312 | Thank you for taking the time to contribute! We really appreciate it.
313 | 
314 | After careful review, we've decided not to merge this PR because [specific reason related to design principles].
315 | 
316 | This isn't a reflection on your code quality - it's about maintaining focus on our core goals as outlined in [design-principles.md](design-principles.md).
317 | 
318 | We'd love to have you contribute in other ways! Check out:
319 | - Good first issues
320 | - Help wanted issues
321 | - Our roadmap
322 | 
323 | Thanks again for your interest in Open Notebook!
324 | ```
325 | 
326 | ### Closing a Stale Issue
327 | 
328 | ```markdown
329 | We're closing this issue due to inactivity. If this is still relevant, feel free to reopen it with updated information.
330 | 
331 | Thanks!
332 | ```
333 | 
334 | ### Asking for More Information
335 | 
336 | ```markdown
337 | Thanks for reporting this! To help us investigate, could you provide:
338 | 
339 | 1. [Specific information needed]
340 | 2. [Logs, screenshots, etc.]
341 | 3. [Steps to reproduce]
342 | 
343 | This will help us understand the issue better and find a solution.
344 | ```
345 | 
346 | ### Thanking a Contributor
347 | 
348 | ```markdown
349 | Merged!
350 | 
351 | Thank you so much for this contribution, @username! [Specific thing they did well].
352 | 
353 | This will be included in the next release.
354 | ```
355 | 
356 | ## Best Practices
357 | 
358 | ### Be Kind and Respectful
359 | 
360 | - Thank contributors for their time and effort
361 | - Assume good intentions
362 | - Be patient with newcomers
363 | - Explain *why*, not just *what*
364 | 
365 | ### Be Clear and Direct
366 | 
367 | - Don't leave ambiguity about next steps
368 | - Be specific about what needs to change
369 | - Explain architectural decisions
370 | - Set clear expectations
371 | 
372 | ### Be Consistent
373 | 
374 | - Apply the same standards to all contributors
375 | - Follow the process you've defined
376 | - Document decisions for future reference
377 | 
378 | ### Be Protective of Project Vision
379 | 
380 | - It's okay to say "no"
381 | - Prioritize long-term maintainability
382 | - Don't accept features you can't support
383 | - Keep the project focused
384 | 
385 | ### Be Responsive
386 | 
387 | - Respond to issues within 48 hours (even just to acknowledge)
388 | - Review PRs within a week when possible
389 | - Keep contributors updated on status
390 | - Close stale issues/PRs to keep things tidy
391 | 
392 | ## When in Doubt
393 | 
394 | Ask yourself:
395 | 1. Does this align with our [design principles](design-principles.md)?
396 | 2. Will we be able to maintain this feature long-term?
397 | 3. Does this benefit most users, or just an edge case?
398 | 4. Is there a simpler alternative?
399 | 5. Would I want to support this in 2 years?
400 | 
401 | If you're unsure, it's perfectly fine to:
402 | - Ask for input from other maintainers
403 | - Start a discussion issue
404 | - Sleep on it before making a decision
405 | 
406 | ---
407 | 
408 | **Remember**: Good maintainership is about balancing openness to contributions with protection of project vision. You're not being mean by saying "no" to things that don't fit - you're being a responsible steward of the project.
409 |

/docs/3-USER-GUIDE/search.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Search Effectively - Finding What You Need
  2 | 
  3 | Search is your gateway into your research. This guide covers two search modes and when to use each.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## Quick-Start: Find Something
  8 | 
  9 | ### Simple Search
 10 | 
 11 | ```
 12 | 1. Go to your notebook
 13 | 2. Type in search box
 14 | 3. See results (both sources and notes)
 15 | 4. Click result to view source/note
 16 | 5. Done!
 17 | 
 18 | That works for basic searches.
 19 | But you can do much better...
 20 | ```
 21 | 
 22 | ---
 23 | 
 24 | ## Two Search Modes Explained
 25 | 
 26 | Open Notebook has two fundamentally different search approaches.
 27 | 
 28 | ### Search Type 1: TEXT SEARCH (Keyword Matching)
 29 | 
 30 | **How it works:**
 31 | - You search for words: "transformer"
 32 | - System finds chunks containing "transformer"
 33 | - Ranked by relevance: frequency, position, context
 34 | 
 35 | **Speed:** Very fast (instant)
 36 | 
 37 | **When to use:**
 38 | - You remember exact words or phrases
 39 | - You're looking for specific terms
 40 | - You want precise keyword matches
 41 | - You need exact quotes
 42 | 
 43 | **Example:**
 44 | ```
 45 | Search: "attention mechanism"
 46 | Results:
 47 |   1. "The attention mechanism allows..." (perfect match)
 48 |   2. "Attention and other mechanisms..." (partial match)
 49 |   3. "How mechanisms work in attention..." (includes words separately)
 50 | 
 51 | All contain "attention" AND "mechanism"
 52 | Ranked by how close together they are
 53 | ```
 54 | 
 55 | **What it finds:**
 56 | - Exact phrases: "transformer model"
 57 | - Individual words: transformer OR model (too broad)
 58 | - Names: "Vaswani et al."
 59 | - Numbers: "1994", "GPT-4"
 60 | - Technical terms: "LSTM", "convolution"
 61 | 
 62 | **What it doesn't find:**
 63 | - Similar words: searching "attention" won't find "focus"
 64 | - Synonyms: searching "large" won't find "big"
 65 | - Concepts: searching "similarity" won't find "likeness"
 66 | 
 67 | ---
 68 | 
 69 | ### Search Type 2: VECTOR SEARCH (Semantic/Concept Matching)
 70 | 
 71 | **How it works:**
 72 | - Your search converted to embedding (vector)
 73 | - All chunks converted to embeddings
 74 | - System finds most similar embeddings
 75 | - Ranked by semantic similarity
 76 | 
 77 | **Speed:** A bit slower (1-2 seconds)
 78 | 
 79 | **When to use:**
 80 | - You're exploring a concept
 81 | - You don't know exact words
 82 | - You want semantically similar content
 83 | - You're discovering, not searching
 84 | 
 85 | **Example:**
 86 | ```
 87 | Search: "What's the mechanism for understanding in models?"
 88 | (Notice: No chunk likely says exactly that)
 89 | 
 90 | Results:
 91 |   1. "Mechanistic interpretability allows understanding..." (semantic match)
 92 |   2. "Feature attribution reveals how models work..." (conceptually similar)
 93 |   3. "Attention visualization shows model decisions..." (same topic)
 94 | 
 95 | None contain your exact words
 96 | But all are semantically related
 97 | ```
 98 | 
 99 | **What it finds:**
100 | - Similar concepts: "understanding" + "interpretation" + "explainability" (all related)
101 | - Paraphrases: "big" and "large" (same meaning)
102 | - Related ideas: "safety" relates to "alignment" (connected concepts)
103 | - Analogies: content about biological learning when searching "learning"
104 | 
105 | **What it doesn't find:**
106 | - Exact keywords: if you search a rare word, vector search might miss it
107 | - Specific numbers: "1994" vs "1993" are semantically different
108 | - Technical jargon: "LSTM" and "RNN" are different even if related
109 | 
110 | ---
111 | 
112 | ## Decision: Text Search vs. Vector Search?
113 | 
114 | ```
115 | Question: "Do I remember the exact words?"
116 | 
117 | → YES: Use TEXT SEARCH
118 |    Example: "I remember the paper said 'attention is all you need'"
119 | 
120 | → NO: Use VECTOR SEARCH
121 |    Example: "I'm looking for content about how models process information"
122 | 
123 | → UNSURE: Try TEXT SEARCH first (faster)
124 |          If no results, try VECTOR SEARCH
125 | 
126 | Text search: "I know what I'm looking for"
127 | Vector search: "I'm exploring an idea"
128 | ```
129 | 
130 | ---
131 | 
132 | ## Step-by-Step: Using Each Search
133 | 
134 | ### Text Search
135 | 
136 | ```
137 | 1. Go to search box
138 | 2. Type your keywords: "transformer", "attention", "2017"
139 | 3. Press Enter
140 | 4. Results appear (usually instant)
141 | 5. Click result to see context
142 | 
143 | Results show:
144 |   - Which source contains it
145 |   - How many times it appears
146 |   - Relevance score
147 |   - Preview of surrounding text
148 | ```
149 | 
150 | ### Vector Search
151 | 
152 | ```
153 | 1. Go to search box
154 | 2. Type your concept: "How do models understand language?"
155 | 3. Choose "Vector Search" from dropdown
156 | 4. Press Enter
157 | 5. Results appear (1-2 seconds)
158 | 6. Click result to see context
159 | 
160 | Results show:
161 |   - Semantically related chunks
162 |   - Similarity score (higher = more related)
163 |   - Preview of surrounding text
164 |   - Different sources mixed together
165 | ```
166 | 
167 | ---
168 | 
169 | ## The Ask Feature (Automated Search)
170 | 
171 | Ask is different from simple search. It automatically searches, synthesizes, and answers.
172 | 
173 | ### How Ask Works
174 | 
175 | ```
176 | Stage 1: QUESTION UNDERSTANDING
177 |   "Compare the approaches in my papers"
178 |   → System: "This asks for comparison"
179 | 
180 | Stage 2: SEARCH STRATEGY
181 |   → System: "I should search for each approach separately"
182 | 
183 | Stage 3: PARALLEL SEARCHES
184 |   → Search 1: "Approach in paper A"
185 |   → Search 2: "Approach in paper B"
186 |   (Multiple searches happen at once)
187 | 
188 | Stage 4: ANALYSIS & SYNTHESIS
189 |   → Per-result analysis: "Based on paper A, the approach is..."
190 |   → Per-result analysis: "Based on paper B, the approach is..."
191 |   → Final synthesis: "Comparing A and B: A differs from B in..."
192 | 
193 | Result: Comprehensive answer, not just search results
194 | ```
195 | 
196 | ### When to Use Ask vs. Simple Search
197 | 
198 | | Task | Use | Why |
199 | |------|-----|-----|
200 | | "Find the quote about X" | **TEXT SEARCH** | Need exact words |
201 | | "What does source A say about X?" | **TEXT SEARCH** | Direct, fast answer |
202 | | "Find content about X" | **VECTOR SEARCH** | Semantic discovery |
203 | | "Compare A and B" | **ASK** | Comprehensive synthesis |
204 | | "What's the big picture?" | **ASK** | Full analysis needed |
205 | | "How do these sources relate?" | **ASK** | Cross-source synthesis |
206 | | "I remember something about X" | **TEXT SEARCH** | Recall memory |
207 | | "I'm exploring the topic of X" | **VECTOR SEARCH** | Discovery mode |
208 | 
209 | ---
210 | 
211 | ## Advanced Search Strategies
212 | 
213 | ### Strategy 1: Simple Search with Follow-Up
214 | 
215 | ```
216 | 1. Text search: "attention mechanism"
217 |    Results: 50 matches
218 | 
219 | 2. Too many. Follow up with vector search:
220 |    "Why is attention useful?" (concept search)
221 |    Results: Most relevant papers/notes
222 | 
223 | 3. Better results with less noise
224 | ```
225 | 
226 | ### Strategy 2: Ask for Comprehensive, Then Search for Details
227 | 
228 | ```
229 | 1. Ask: "What are the main approaches to X?"
230 |    Result: Comprehensive answer about A, B, C
231 | 
232 | 2. Use that to identify specific sources
233 | 
234 | 3. Text search in those specific sources:
235 |    "Why did they choose method X?"
236 |    Result: Detailed information
237 | ```
238 | 
239 | ### Strategy 3: Vector Search for Discovery, Text for Verification
240 | 
241 | ```
242 | 1. Vector search: "How do transformers generalize?"
243 |    Results: Related conceptual papers
244 | 
245 | 2. Skim to understand landscape
246 | 
247 | 3. Text search in promising sources:
248 |    "generalization", "extrapolation", "transfer"
249 |    Results: Specific passages to read carefully
250 | ```
251 | 
252 | ### Strategy 4: Combine Search with Chat
253 | 
254 | ```
255 | 1. Vector search: "What's new in AI 2026?"
256 |    Results: Latest papers
257 | 
258 | 2. Go to Chat
259 | 3. Add those papers to context
260 | 4. Ask detailed follow-up questions
261 | 5. Get deep analysis of results
262 | ```
263 | 
264 | ---
265 | 
266 | ## Search Quality Issues & Fixes
267 | 
268 | ### Getting No Results
269 | 
270 | | Problem | Cause | Solution |
271 | |---------|-------|----------|
272 | | Text search: no results | Word doesn't appear | Try vector search instead |
273 | | Vector search: no results | Concept not in content | Try broader search term |
274 | | Both empty | Content not in notebook | Add sources to notebook |
275 | | | Sources not processed | Wait for processing to complete |
276 | 
277 | ### Getting Too Many Results
278 | 
279 | | Problem | Cause | Solution |
280 | |---------|-------|----------|
281 | | 1000+ results | Search too broad | Be more specific |
282 | | | All sources | Filter by source |
283 | | | Keyword matches rare words | Use vector search instead |
284 | 
285 | ### Getting Wrong Results
286 | 
287 | | Problem | Cause | Solution |
288 | |---------|-------|----------|
289 | | Results irrelevant | Search term has multiple meanings | Provide more context |
290 | | | Using text search for concepts | Try vector search |
291 | | Different meaning | Homonym (word means multiple things) | Add context (e.g., "attention mechanism") |
292 | 
293 | ### Getting Low Quality Results
294 | 
295 | | Problem | Cause | Solution |
296 | |---------|-------|----------|
297 | | Results don't match intent | Vague search term | Be specific ("Who invented X?" vs "X") |
298 | | | Concept not well-represented | Add more sources on that topic |
299 | | | Vector embedding not trained on domain | Use text search as fallback |
300 | 
301 | ---
302 | 
303 | ## Tips for Better Searches
304 | 
305 | ### For Text Search
306 | 1. **Be specific** — "attention mechanism" not just "attention"
307 | 2. **Use exact phrases** — Put quotes around: "attention is all you need"
308 | 3. **Include context** — "LSTM vs attention" not just "attention"
309 | 4. **Use technical terms** — These are usually more precise
310 | 5. **Try synonyms** — If first search fails, try related terms
311 | 
312 | ### For Vector Search
313 | 1. **Ask a question** — "What's the best way to X?" is better than "best way"
314 | 2. **Use natural language** — Explain what you're looking for
315 | 3. **Be specific about intent** — "Compare X and Y" not "X and Y"
316 | 4. **Include context** — "In machine learning, how..." vs just "how..."
317 | 5. **Think conceptually** — What idea are you exploring?
318 | 
319 | ### General Tips
320 | 1. **Start broad, then narrow** — "AI papers" → "transformers" → "attention mechanism"
321 | 2. **Try both search types** — Each finds different things
322 | 3. **Use Ask for complex questions** — Don't just search
323 | 4. **Save good results as notes** — Create knowledge base
324 | 5. **Filter by source if needed** — "Search in Paper A only"
325 | 
326 | ---
327 | 
328 | ## Search Examples
329 | 
330 | ### Example 1: Finding a Specific Fact
331 | 
332 | **Goal:** "Find the date the transformer was introduced"
333 | 
334 | ```
335 | Step 1: Text search
336 |   "transformer 2017" (or year you remember)
337 | 
338 | If that works: Done!
339 | 
340 | If no results: Try
341 |   "attention is all you need" (famous paper title)
342 | 
343 | Check result for exact date
344 | ```
345 | 
346 | ### Example 2: Exploring a Concept
347 | 
348 | **Goal:** "Find content about alignment interpretability"
349 | 
350 | ```
351 | Step 1: Vector search
352 |   "How do we make AI interpretable?"
353 | 
354 | Results: Papers on interpretability, transparency, alignment
355 | 
356 | Step 2: Review results
357 |   See which papers are most relevant
358 | 
359 | Step 3: Deep dive
360 |   Go to Chat, add top 2-3 papers
361 |   Ask detailed questions about alignment
362 | ```
363 | 
364 | ### Example 3: Comprehensive Answer
365 | 
366 | **Goal:** "How do different approaches to AI safety compare?"
367 | 
368 | ```
369 | Step 1: Ask
370 |   "Compare the main approaches to AI safety in my sources"
371 | 
372 | Result: Comprehensive analysis comparing approaches
373 | 
374 | Step 2: Identify sources
375 |   From answer, see which papers were most relevant
376 | 
377 | Step 3: Deep dive
378 |   Text search in those papers:
379 |   "limitations", "critiques", "open problems"
380 | 
381 | Step 4: Save as notes
382 |   Create comparison note from Ask result
383 | ```
384 | 
385 | ### Example 4: Finding Pattern
386 | 
387 | **Goal:** "Find all papers mentioning transformers"
388 | 
389 | ```
390 | Step 1: Text search
391 |   "transformer"
392 | 
393 | Results: All papers mentioning "transformer"
394 | 
395 | Step 2: Vector search
396 |   "neural network architecture for sequence processing"
397 | 
398 | Results: Papers that don't say "transformer" but discuss similar concept
399 | 
400 | Step 3: Combine
401 |   Union of text + vector results shows full landscape
402 | 
403 | Step 4: Analyze
404 |   Go to Chat with all results
405 |   Ask: "What's common across all these?"
406 | ```
407 | 
408 | ---
409 | 
410 | ## Search in the Workflow
411 | 
412 | How search fits with other features:
413 | 
414 | ```
415 | SOURCES
416 |   ↓
417 | SEARCH (find what matters)
418 |   ├─ Text search (precise)
419 |   ├─ Vector search (exploration)
420 |   └─ Ask (comprehensive)
421 |   ↓
422 | CHAT (explore with follow-ups)
423 |   ↓
424 | TRANSFORMATIONS (batch extract)
425 |   ↓
426 | NOTES (save insights)
427 | ```
428 | 
429 | ### Workflow Example
430 | 
431 | ```
432 | 1. Add 10 papers to notebook
433 | 
434 | 2. Search: "What's the state of the art?"
435 |    (Vector search explores landscape)
436 | 
437 | 3. Ask: "Compare these 3 approaches"
438 |    (Comprehensive synthesis)
439 | 
440 | 4. Chat: Deep questions about winner
441 |    (Follow-up exploration)
442 | 
443 | 5. Save best insights as notes
444 |    (Knowledge capture)
445 | 
446 | 6. Transform remaining papers
447 |    (Batch extraction for later)
448 | 
449 | 7. Create podcast from notes + sources
450 |    (Share findings)
451 | ```
452 | 
453 | ---
454 | 
455 | ## Summary: Know Your Search
456 | 
457 | **TEXT SEARCH** — "I know what I'm looking for"
458 | - Fast, precise, keyword-based
459 | - Use when you remember exact words/phrases
460 | - Best for: Finding specific facts, quotes, technical terms
461 | - Speed: Instant
462 | 
463 | **VECTOR SEARCH** — "I'm exploring an idea"
464 | - Slow-ish, concept-based, semantic
465 | - Use when you're discovering connections
466 | - Best for: Concept exploration, related ideas, synonyms
467 | - Speed: 1-2 seconds
468 | 
469 | **ASK** — "I want a comprehensive answer"
470 | - Auto-searches, auto-analyzes, synthesizes
471 | - Use for complex questions needing multiple sources
472 | - Best for: Comparisons, big-picture questions, synthesis
473 | - Speed: 10-30 seconds
474 | 
475 | Pick the right tool for your search goal, and you'll find what you need faster.
476 |
