/docs/2-CORE-CONCEPTS/ai-context-rag.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # AI Context & RAG - How Open Notebook Uses Your Research
  2 | 
  3 | Open Notebook uses different approaches to make AI models aware of your research depending on the feature. This section explains **RAG** (used in Ask) and **full-content context** (used in Chat).
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## The Problem: Making AI Aware of Your Data
  8 | 
  9 | ### Traditional Approaches (and their problems)
 10 | 
 11 | **Option 1: Fine-Tuning**
 12 | - Train the model on your data
 13 | - Pro: Model becomes specialized
 14 | - Con: Expensive, slow, permanent (can't unlearn)
 15 | 
 16 | **Option 2: Send Everything to Cloud**
 17 | - Upload all your data to ChatGPT/Claude API
 18 | - Pro: Works well, fast
 19 | - Con: Privacy nightmare, data leaves your control, expensive
 20 | 
 21 | **Option 3: Ignore Your Data**
 22 | - Just use the base model without your research
 23 | - Pro: Private, free
 24 | - Con: AI doesn't know anything about your specific topic
 25 | 
 26 | ### Open Notebook's Dual Approach
 27 | 
 28 | **For Chat**: Sends the entire selected content to the LLM
 29 | - Simple and transparent: You select sources, they're sent in full
 30 | - Maximum context: AI sees everything you choose
 31 | - You control which sources are included
 32 | 
 33 | **For Ask (RAG)**: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
 34 | - RAG = Retrieval-Augmented Generation
 35 | - The insight: *Search your content, find relevant pieces, send only those*
 36 | - Automatic: AI decides what's relevant based on your question
 37 | 
 38 | ---
 39 | 
 40 | ## How RAG Works: Three Stages
 41 | 
 42 | ### Stage 1: Content Preparation
 43 | 
 44 | When you upload a source, Open Notebook prepares it for retrieval:
 45 | 
 46 | ```
 47 | 1. EXTRACT TEXT
 48 |    PDF → text
 49 |    URL → webpage text
 50 |    Audio → transcribed text
 51 |    Video → subtitles + transcription
 52 | 
 53 | 2. CHUNK INTO PIECES
 54 |    Long documents → break into ~500-word chunks
 55 |    Why? AI context has limits; smaller pieces are more precise
 56 | 
 57 | 3. CREATE EMBEDDINGS
 58 |    Each chunk → semantic vector (numbers representing meaning)
 59 |    Why? Allows finding chunks by similarity, not just keywords
 60 | 
 61 | 4. STORE IN DATABASE
 62 |    Chunks + embeddings + metadata → searchable storage
 63 | ```
 64 | 
 65 | **Example:**
 66 | ```
 67 | Source: "AI Safety Research 2026" (50-page PDF)
 68 | ↓
 69 | Extracted: 50 pages of text
 70 | ↓
 71 | Chunked: 150 chunks (~500 words each)
 72 | ↓
 73 | Embedded: Each chunk gets a vector (1536 numbers for OpenAI)
 74 | ↓
 75 | Stored: Ready for search
 76 | ```
 77 | 
 78 | ---
 79 | 
 80 | ### Stage 2: Query Time (What You Search For)
 81 | 
 82 | When you ask a question, the system finds relevant content:
 83 | 
 84 | ```
 85 | 1. YOU ASK A QUESTION
 86 |    "What does the paper say about alignment?"
 87 | 
 88 | 2. SYSTEM CONVERTS QUESTION TO EMBEDDING
 89 |    Your question → vector (same way chunks are vectorized)
 90 | 
 91 | 3. SIMILARITY SEARCH
 92 |    Find chunks most similar to your question
 93 |    (using vector math, not keyword matching)
 94 | 
 95 | 4. RETURN TOP RESULTS
 96 |    Usually top 5-10 most similar chunks
 97 | 
 98 | 5. YOU GET BACK
 99 |    ✓ The relevant chunks
100 |    ✓ Where they came from (sources + page numbers)
101 |    ✓ Relevance scores
102 | ```
103 | 
104 | **Example:**
105 | ```
106 | Q: "What does the paper say about alignment?"
107 | ↓
108 | Q vector: [0.23, -0.51, 0.88, ..., 0.12]
109 | ↓
110 | Search: Compare to all chunk vectors
111 | ↓
112 | Results:
113 |   - Chunk 47 (alignment section): similarity 0.94
114 |   - Chunk 63 (safety approaches): similarity 0.88
115 |   - Chunk 12 (related work): similarity 0.71
116 | ```
117 | 
118 | ---
119 | 
120 | ### Stage 3: Augmentation (How AI Uses It)
121 | 
122 | Now you have the relevant pieces. The AI uses them:
123 | 
124 | ```
125 | SYSTEM BUILDS A PROMPT:
126 |   "You are an AI research assistant.
127 | 
128 |    The user has the following research materials:
129 |    [CHUNK 47 CONTENT]
130 |    [CHUNK 63 CONTENT]
131 | 
132 |    User question: 'What does the paper say about alignment?'
133 | 
134 |    Answer based on the above materials."
135 | 
136 | AI RESPONDS:
137 |   "Based on the research materials, the paper approaches
138 |    alignment through [pulls from chunks] and emphasizes
139 |    [pulls from chunks]..."
140 | 
141 | SYSTEM ADDS CITATIONS:
142 |   "- See research materials page 15 for approach details
143 |    - See research materials page 23 for emphasis on X"
144 | ```
145 | 
146 | ---
147 | 
148 | ## Two Search Modes: Exact vs. Semantic
149 | 
150 | Open Notebook provides two different search strategies for different goals.
151 | 
152 | ### 1. Text Search (Keyword Matching)
153 | 
154 | **How it works:**
155 | - Uses BM25 ranking (the same algorithm Google uses)
156 | - Finds chunks containing your keywords
157 | - Ranks by relevance (how often keywords appear, position, etc.)
158 | 
159 | **When to use:**
160 | - "I remember the exact phrase 'X' and want to find it"
161 | - "I'm looking for a specific name or number"
162 | - "I need the exact quote"
163 | 
164 | **Example:**
165 | ```
166 | Search: "transformer architecture"
167 | Results:
168 |   1. Chunk with "transformer architecture" 3 times
169 |   2. Chunk with "transformer" and "architecture" separately
170 |   3. Chunk with "transformer-based models"
171 | ```
172 | 
173 | ### 2. Vector Search (Semantic Similarity)
174 | 
175 | **How it works:**
176 | - Converts your question to a vector (number embedding)
177 | - Finds chunks with similar vectors
178 | - No keywords needed—finds conceptually similar content
179 | 
180 | **When to use:**
181 | - "Find content about X (without saying exact words)"
182 | - "I'm exploring a concept"
183 | - "Find similar ideas even if worded differently"
184 | 
185 | **Example:**
186 | ```
187 | Search: "what's the mechanism for model understanding?"
188 | Results (no "understanding" in any chunk):
189 |   1. Chunk about interpretability and mechanistic analysis
190 |   2. Chunk about feature analysis
191 |   3. Chunk about attention mechanisms
192 | 
193 | Why? The vectors are semantically similar to your concept.
194 | ```
195 | 
196 | ---
197 | 
198 | ## Context Management: Your Control Panel
199 | 
200 | Here's where Open Notebook is different: **You decide what the AI sees.**
201 | 
202 | ### The Three Levels
203 | 
204 | | Level | What's Shared | Example Cost | Privacy | Use Case |
205 | |-------|---------------|--------------|---------|----------|
206 | | **Full Content** | Complete source text | 10,000 tokens | Low | Detailed analysis, close reading |
207 | | **Summary Only** | AI-generated summary | 2,000 tokens | High | Background material, references |
208 | | **Not in Context** | Nothing | 0 tokens | Max | Confidential, irrelevant, or archived |
209 | 
210 | ### How It Works
211 | 
212 | **Full Content:**
213 | ```
214 | You: "What's the methodology in paper A?"
215 | System:
216 |   - Searches paper A
217 |   - Retrieves full paper content (or large chunks)
218 |   - Sends to AI: "Here's paper A. Answer about methodology."
219 |   - AI analyzes complete content
220 |   - Result: Detailed, precise answer
221 | ```
222 | 
223 | **Summary Only:**
224 | ```
225 | You: "I want to chat using paper A and B"
226 | System:
227 |   - For Paper A: Sends AI-generated summary (not full text)
228 |   - For Paper B: Sends full content (detailed analysis)
229 |   - AI sees 2 sources but in different detail levels
230 |   - Result: Uses summaries for context, details for focused content
231 | ```
232 | 
233 | **Not in Context:**
234 | ```
235 | You: "I have 10 sources but only want 5 in context"
236 | System:
237 |   - Paper A-E: In context (sent to AI)
238 |   - Paper F-J: Not in context (AI can't see them, doesn't search them)
239 |   - AI never knows these 5 sources exist
240 |   - Result: Tight, focused context
241 | ```
242 | 
243 | ### Why This Matters
244 | 
245 | **Privacy**: You control what leaves your system
246 | ```
247 | Scenario: Confidential company docs + public research
248 | Control: Public research in context → Confidential docs excluded
249 | Result: AI never sees confidential content
250 | ```
251 | 
252 | **Cost**: You control token usage
253 | ```
254 | Scenario: 100 sources for background + 5 for detailed analysis
255 | Control: Full content for 5 detailed, summaries for 95 background
256 | Result: 80% lower token cost than sending everything
257 | ```
258 | 
259 | **Quality**: You control what the AI focuses on
260 | ```
261 | Scenario: 20 sources, question requires deep analysis
262 | Control: Full content for relevant source, exclude others
263 | Result: AI doesn't get distracted; gives better answer
264 | ```
265 | 
266 | ---
267 | 
268 | ## The Difference: Chat vs. Ask
269 | 
270 | **IMPORTANT**: These use completely different approaches!
271 | 
272 | ### Chat: Full-Content Context (NO RAG)
273 | 
274 | **How it works:**
275 | ```
276 | YOU:
277 |   1. Select which sources to include in context
278 |   2. Set context level (full/summary/excluded)
279 |   3. Ask question
280 | 
281 | SYSTEM:
282 |   - Takes ALL selected sources (respecting context levels)
283 |   - Sends the ENTIRE content to the LLM at once
284 |   - NO search, NO retrieval, NO chunking
285 |   - AI sees everything you selected
286 | 
287 | AI:
288 |   - Responds based on the full content you provided
289 |   - Can reference any part of selected sources
290 |   - Conversational: context stays for follow-ups
291 | ```
292 | 
293 | **Use this when**:
294 | - You know which sources are relevant
295 | - You want conversational back-and-forth
296 | - You want AI to see the complete context
297 | - You're doing close reading or analysis
298 | 
299 | **Advantages:**
300 | - Simple and transparent
301 | - AI sees everything (no missed content)
302 | - Conversational flow
303 | 
304 | **Limitations:**
305 | - Limited by LLM context window
306 | - You must manually select relevant sources
307 | - Sends more tokens (higher cost with many sources)
308 | 
309 | ---
310 | 
311 | ### Ask: RAG - Automatic Retrieval
312 | 
313 | **How it works:**
314 | ```
315 | YOU:
316 |   Ask one complex question
317 | 
318 | SYSTEM:
319 |   1. Analyzes your question
320 |   2. Searches across ALL your sources automatically
321 |   3. Finds relevant chunks using vector similarity
322 |   4. Retrieves only the most relevant pieces
323 |   5. Sends ONLY those chunks to the LLM
324 |   6. Synthesizes into comprehensive answer
325 | 
326 | AI:
327 |   - Sees ONLY the retrieved chunks (not full sources)
328 |   - Answers based on what was found to be relevant
329 |   - One-shot answer (not conversational)
330 | ```
331 | 
332 | **Use this when**:
333 | - You have many sources and don't know which are relevant
334 | - You want the AI to search automatically
335 | - You need a comprehensive answer to a complex question
336 | - You want to minimize tokens sent to LLM
337 | 
338 | **Advantages:**
339 | - Automatic search (you don't pick sources)
340 | - Works across many sources at once
341 | - Cost-effective (sends only relevant chunks)
342 | 
343 | **Limitations:**
344 | - Not conversational (single question/answer)
345 | - AI only sees retrieved chunks (might miss context)
346 | - Search quality depends on how well question matches content
347 | 
348 | ---
349 | 
350 | ## What This Means: Privacy by Design
351 | 
352 | Open Notebook's RAG approach gives you something you don't get with ChatGPT or Claude directly:
353 | 
354 | **You control the boundary between:**
355 | - What stays private (on your system)
356 | - What goes to AI (explicitly chosen)
357 | - What the AI can see (context levels)
358 | 
359 | ### The Audit Trail
360 | 
361 | Because everything is retrieved explicitly, you can ask:
362 | - "Which sources did the AI use for this answer?" → See citations
363 | - "What exactly did the AI see?" → See chunks in context level
364 | - "Is the AI's claim actually in my sources?" → Verify citation
365 | 
366 | This prevents hallucinations or misrepresentation better than most systems.
367 | 
368 | ---
369 | 
370 | ## How Embeddings Work (Simplified)
371 | 
372 | The magic of semantic search comes from embeddings. Here's the intuition:
373 | 
374 | ### The Idea
375 | Instead of storing text, store it as a list of numbers (vectors) that represent "meaning."
376 | 
377 | ```
378 | Chunk: "The transformer uses attention mechanisms"
379 | Vector: [0.23, -0.51, 0.88, 0.12, ..., 0.34]
380 |         (1536 numbers for OpenAI)
381 | 
382 | Another chunk: "Attention allows models to focus on relevant parts"
383 | Vector: [0.24, -0.48, 0.87, 0.15, ..., 0.35]
384 |         (similar numbers = similar meaning!)
385 | ```
386 | 
387 | ### Why This Works
388 | Words that are semantically similar produce similar vectors. So:
389 | - "alignment" and "interpretability" have similar vectors
390 | - "transformer" and "attention" have related vectors
391 | - "cat" and "dog" are more similar than "cat" and "radiator"
392 | 
393 | ### How Search Works
394 | ```
395 | Your question: "How do models understand their decisions?"
396 | Question vector: [0.25, -0.50, 0.86, 0.14, ..., 0.33]
397 | 
398 | Compare to all stored vectors. Find the most similar:
399 | - Chunk about interpretability: similarity 0.94
400 | - Chunk about explainability: similarity 0.91
401 | - Chunk about feature attribution: similarity 0.88
402 | 
403 | Return the top matches.
404 | ```
405 | 
406 | This is why semantic search finds conceptually similar content even when words are different.
407 | 
408 | ---
409 | 
410 | ## Key Design Decisions
411 | 
412 | ### 1. Search, Don't Train
413 | **Why?** Fine-tuning is slow and permanent. Search is flexible and reversible.
414 | 
415 | ### 2. Explicit Retrieval, Not Implicit Knowledge
416 | **Why?** You can verify what the AI saw. You have audit trails. You control what leaves your system.
417 | 
418 | ### 3. Multiple Search Types
419 | **Why?** Different questions need different search (keyword vs. semantic). Giving you both is more powerful.
420 | 
421 | ### 4. Context as a Permission System
422 | **Why?** Not everything you save needs to reach AI. You control granularly.
423 | 
424 | ---
425 | 
426 | ## Summary
427 | 
428 | Open Notebook gives you **two ways** to work with AI:
429 | 
430 | ### Chat (Full-Content)
431 | - Sends entire selected sources to LLM
432 | - Manual control: you pick sources
433 | - Conversational: back-and-forth dialog
434 | - Transparent: you know exactly what AI sees
435 | - Best for: focused analysis, close reading
436 | 
437 | ### Ask (RAG)
438 | - Searches and retrieves relevant chunks automatically
439 | - Automatic: AI finds what's relevant
440 | - One-shot: single comprehensive answer
441 | - Efficient: sends only relevant pieces
442 | - Best for: broad questions across many sources
443 | 
444 | **Both approaches:**
445 | 1. Keep your data private (doesn't leave your system by default)
446 | 2. Give you control (you choose which features to use)
447 | 3. Create audit trails (citations show what was used)
448 | 4. Support multiple AI providers
449 | 
450 | **Coming Soon**: The community is working on adding RAG capabilities to Chat as well, giving you the best of both worlds.
451 |

  9 |     DefaultModelsResponse,

 17 | router = APIRouter()
 18 | 
 19 | 
 20 | def _check_openai_compatible_support(mode: str) -> bool:
 21 |     """
 22 |     Check if OpenAI-compatible provider is available for a specific mode.
 23 | 
 24 |     Args:
 25 |         mode: One of 'LLM', 'EMBEDDING', 'STT', 'TTS'
 26 | 
 27 |     Returns:
 28 |         bool: True if either generic or mode-specific env var is set
 29 |     """
 30 |     generic = os.environ.get("OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL") is not None
 31 |     specific = os.environ.get(f"OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL_{mode}") is not None
 32 |     return generic or specific
 33 | 
 34 | 
 35 | def _check_azure_support(mode: str) -> bool:
 36 |     """
 37 |     Check if Azure OpenAI provider is available for a specific mode.
 38 | 
 39 |     Args:
 40 |         mode: One of 'LLM', 'EMBEDDING', 'STT', 'TTS'
 41 | 
 42 |     Returns:
 43 |         bool: True if either generic or mode-specific env vars are set
 44 |     """
 45 |     # Check generic configuration (applies to all modes)
 46 |     generic = (
 47 |         os.environ.get("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY") is not None
 48 |         and os.environ.get("AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT") is not None
 49 |         and os.environ.get("AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION") is not None
 50 |     )
 51 | 
 52 |     # Check mode-specific configuration (takes precedence)
 53 |     specific = (
 54 |         os.environ.get(f"AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY_{mode}") is not None
 55 |         and os.environ.get(f"AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT_{mode}") is not None
 56 |         and os.environ.get(f"AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION_{mode}") is not None
 57 |     )
 58 | 
 59 |     return generic or specific
 60 | 
 61 | 
 62 | @router.get("/models", response_model=List[ModelResponse])
 63 | async def get_models(
 64 |     type: Optional[str] = Query(None, description="Filter by model type"),
 65 | ):
 66 |     """Get all configured models with optional type filtering."""
 67 |     try:
 68 |         if type:
 69 |             models = await Model.get_models_by_type(type)
 70 |         else:
 71 |             models = await Model.get_all()
 72 | 
 73 |         return [
 74 |             ModelResponse(
 75 |                 id=model.id,
 76 |                 name=model.name,
 77 |                 provider=model.provider,
 78 |                 type=model.type,
 79 |                 created=str(model.created),
 80 |                 updated=str(model.updated),
 81 |             )
 82 |             for model in models
 83 |         ]
 84 |     except Exception as e:
 85 |         logger.error(f"Error fetching models: {str(e)}")
 86 |         raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Error fetching models: {str(e)}")
 87 |

 89 | @router.post("/models", response_model=ModelResponse)
 90 | async def create_model(model_data: ModelCreate):
 91 |     """Create a new model configuration."""
 92 |     try:
 93 |         # Validate model type
 94 |         valid_types = ["language", "embedding", "text_to_speech", "speech_to_text"]
 95 |         if model_data.type not in valid_types:
 96 |             raise HTTPException(
 97 |                 status_code=400,
 98 |                 detail=f"Invalid model type. Must be one of: {valid_types}",
 99 |             )
100 | 
101 |         # Check for duplicate model name under the same provider and type (case-insensitive)
102 |         from open_notebook.database.repository import repo_query
103 | 
104 |         existing = await repo_query(
105 |             "SELECT * FROM model WHERE string::lowercase(provider) = $provider AND string::lowercase(name) = $name AND string::lowercase(type) = $type LIMIT 1",
106 |             {
107 |                 "provider": model_data.provider.lower(),
108 |                 "name": model_data.name.lower(),
109 |                 "type": model_data.type.lower(),
110 |             },
111 |         )
112 |         if existing:
113 |             raise HTTPException(
114 |                 status_code=400,
115 |                 detail=f"Model '{model_data.name}' already exists for provider '{model_data.provider}' with type '{model_data.type}'",
116 |             )
117 | 
118 |         new_model = Model(
119 |             name=model_data.name,
120 |             provider=model_data.provider,
121 |             type=model_data.type,
122 |         )
123 |         await new_model.save()
124 | 
125 |         return ModelResponse(
126 |             id=new_model.id or "",

232 | @router.get("/models/providers", response_model=ProviderAvailabilityResponse)
233 | async def get_provider_availability():
234 |     """Get provider availability based on environment variables."""
235 |     try:
236 |         # Check which providers have API keys configured
237 |         provider_status = {
238 |             "ollama": os.environ.get("OLLAMA_API_BASE") is not None,
239 |             "openai": os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY") is not None,
240 |             "groq": os.environ.get("GROQ_API_KEY") is not None,
241 |             "xai": os.environ.get("XAI_API_KEY") is not None,
242 |             "vertex": (
243 |                 os.environ.get("VERTEX_PROJECT") is not None
244 |                 and os.environ.get("VERTEX_LOCATION") is not None
245 |                 and os.environ.get("GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS") is not None
246 |             ),
247 |             "google": (
248 |                 os.environ.get("GOOGLE_API_KEY") is not None
249 |                 or os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY") is not None
250 |             ),
251 |             "openrouter": os.environ.get("OPENROUTER_API_KEY") is not None,
252 |             "anthropic": os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY") is not None,
253 |             "elevenlabs": os.environ.get("ELEVENLABS_API_KEY") is not None,
254 |             "voyage": os.environ.get("VOYAGE_API_KEY") is not None,
255 |             "azure": (
256 |                 _check_azure_support("LLM")
257 |                 or _check_azure_support("EMBEDDING")
258 |                 or _check_azure_support("STT")
259 |                 or _check_azure_support("TTS")
260 |             ),
261 |             "mistral": os.environ.get("MISTRAL_API_KEY") is not None,
262 |             "deepseek": os.environ.get("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY") is not None,
263 |             "openai-compatible": (
264 |                 _check_openai_compatible_support("LLM")
265 |                 or _check_openai_compatible_support("EMBEDDING")
266 |                 or _check_openai_compatible_support("STT")
267 |                 or _check_openai_compatible_support("TTS")
268 |             ),
269 |         }
270 | 
271 |         available_providers = [k for k, v in provider_status.items() if v]
272 |         unavailable_providers = [k for k, v in provider_status.items() if not v]
273 | 
274 |         # Get supported model types from Esperanto
275 |         esperanto_available = AIFactory.get_available_providers()
276 | 
277 |         # Build supported types mapping only for available providers
278 |         supported_types: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
279 |         for provider in available_providers:
280 |             supported_types[provider] = []
281 | 
282 |             # Map Esperanto model types to our environment variable modes
283 |             mode_mapping = {
284 |                 "language": "LLM",
285 |                 "embedding": "EMBEDDING",
286 |                 "speech_to_text": "STT",
287 |                 "text_to_speech": "TTS",
288 |             }
289 | 
290 |             # Special handling for openai-compatible to check mode-specific availability
291 |             if provider == "openai-compatible":
292 |                 for model_type, mode in mode_mapping.items():
293 |                     if (
294 |                         model_type in esperanto_available
295 |                         and provider in esperanto_available[model_type]
296 |                     ):
297 |                         if _check_openai_compatible_support(mode):
298 |                             supported_types[provider].append(model_type)
299 |             # Special handling for azure to check mode-specific availability
300 |             elif provider == "azure":
301 |                 for model_type, mode in mode_mapping.items():
302 |                     if (
303 |                         model_type in esperanto_available
304 |                         and provider in esperanto_available[model_type]
305 |                     ):
306 |                         if _check_azure_support(mode):
307 |                             supported_types[provider].append(model_type)
308 |             else:
309 |                 # Standard provider detection
310 |                 for model_type, providers in esperanto_available.items():
311 |                     if provider in providers:
312 |                         supported_types[provider].append(model_type)
313 | 
314 |         return ProviderAvailabilityResponse(
315 |             available=available_providers,
316 |             unavailable=unavailable_providers,
317 |             supported_types=supported_types,
318 |         )
319 |     except Exception as e:
320 |         logger.error(f"Error checking provider availability: {str(e)}")
321 |         raise HTTPException(
322 |             status_code=500, detail=f"Error checking provider availability: {str(e)}"
323 |         )
324 |

 54 | const getStatusConfig = (t: TranslationKeys) => ({
 55 |   new: {
 56 |     icon: Clock,
 57 |     color: 'text-blue-600',
 58 |     bgColor: 'bg-blue-50',
 59 |     borderColor: 'border-blue-200',
 60 |     label: t.sources.statusProcessing,
 61 |     description: t.sources.statusPreparingDesc
 62 |   },
 63 |   queued: {
 64 |     icon: Clock,
 65 |     color: 'text-blue-600',
 66 |     bgColor: 'bg-blue-50',
 67 |     borderColor: 'border-blue-200',
 68 |     label: t.sources.statusQueued,
 69 |     description: t.sources.statusQueuedDesc
 70 |   },
 71 |   running: {
 72 |     icon: Loader2,
 73 |     color: 'text-blue-600',
 74 |     bgColor: 'bg-blue-50',
 75 |     borderColor: 'border-blue-200',
 76 |     label: t.sources.statusProcessing,
 77 |     description: t.sources.statusProcessingDesc
 78 |   },

 80 |     icon: CheckCircle,

 82 |     bgColor: 'bg-green-50',
 83 |     borderColor: 'border-green-200',
 84 |     label: t.sources.statusCompleted,
 85 |     description: t.sources.statusCompletedDesc
 86 |   },

 91 |     borderColor: 'border-red-200',
 92 |     label: t.sources.statusFailed,
 93 |     description: t.sources.statusFailedDesc
 94 |   }
 95 | } as const)
 96 | 
 97 | type SourceStatus = 'new' | 'queued' | 'running' | 'completed' | 'failed'
 98 | 
 99 | function isSourceStatus(status: unknown): status is SourceStatus {
100 |   return typeof status === 'string' && ['new', 'queued', 'running', 'completed', 'failed'].includes(status)
101 | }
102 | 
103 | function getSourceType(source: SourceListResponse): 'link' | 'upload' | 'text' {
104 |   // Determine type based on asset information
105 |   if (source.asset?.url) return 'link'
106 |   if (source.asset?.file_path) return 'upload'
107 |   return 'text'
108 | }
109 | 
110 | export function SourceCard({
111 |   source,
112 |   onClick,
113 |   onDelete,
114 |   onRetry,
115 |   onRemoveFromNotebook,
116 |   onRefresh,
117 |   className,
118 |   showRemoveFromNotebook = false,
119 |   contextMode,
120 |   onContextModeChange
121 | }: SourceCardProps) {
122 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
123 |   const statusConfigMap = getStatusConfig(t)
124 |   
125 |   // Only fetch status for sources that might have async processing
126 |   const sourceWithStatus = source as SourceListResponse & { command_id?: string; status?: string }
127 | 
128 |   // Track processing state to continue polling until we detect completion
129 |   const [wasProcessing, setWasProcessing] = useState(false)
130 | 
131 |   const shouldFetchStatus = !!sourceWithStatus.command_id ||
132 |     sourceWithStatus.status === 'new' ||
133 |     sourceWithStatus.status === 'queued' ||
134 |     sourceWithStatus.status === 'running' ||
135 |     wasProcessing // Keep polling if we were processing to catch the completion
136 | 
137 |   const { data: statusData, isLoading: statusLoading } = useSourceStatus(
138 |     source.id,
139 |     shouldFetchStatus
140 |   )
141 | 
142 |   // Determine current status
143 |   // If source has a command_id but no status, treat as "new" (just created)
144 |   const rawStatus = statusData?.status || sourceWithStatus.status
145 |   const currentStatus: SourceStatus = isSourceStatus(rawStatus)
146 |     ? rawStatus
147 |     : (sourceWithStatus.command_id ? 'new' : 'completed')
148 | 
149 | 
150 |   // Track processing state and detect completion
151 |   useEffect(() => {
152 |     const currentStatusFromData = statusData?.status || sourceWithStatus.status
153 | 
154 |     // If we're currently processing, mark that we were processing
155 |     if (currentStatusFromData === 'new' || currentStatusFromData === 'running' || currentStatusFromData === 'queued') {
156 |       setWasProcessing(true)
157 |     }
158 | 
159 |     // If we were processing and now completed/failed, trigger refresh and stop polling
160 |     if (wasProcessing &&
161 |         (currentStatusFromData === 'completed' || currentStatusFromData === 'failed')) {
162 |       setWasProcessing(false) // Stop polling
163 | 
164 |       if (onRefresh) {
165 |         setTimeout(() => onRefresh(), 500) // Small delay to ensure API is updated
166 |       }
167 |     }
168 |   }, [statusData, sourceWithStatus.status, wasProcessing, onRefresh, source.id])
169 |   
170 |   const statusConfig = statusConfigMap[currentStatus] || statusConfigMap.completed
171 |   const StatusIcon = statusConfig.icon
172 |   const sourceType = getSourceType(source)
173 |   const SourceTypeIcon = SOURCE_TYPE_ICONS[sourceType]
174 |   
175 |    const title = source.title || t.sources.untitledSource
176 | 
177 |   const handleRetry = () => {
178 |     if (onRetry) {
179 |       onRetry(source.id)
180 |     }
181 |   }
182 | 
183 |   const handleDelete = () => {
184 |     if (onDelete) {
185 |       onDelete(source.id)
186 |     }
187 |   }
188 | 
189 |   const handleRemoveFromNotebook = () => {
190 |     if (onRemoveFromNotebook) {
191 |       onRemoveFromNotebook(source.id)
192 |     }
193 |   }
194 | 
195 |   const handleCardClick = () => {
196 |     if (onClick) {
197 |       onClick(source.id)
198 |     }
199 |   }
200 | 
201 |   const isProcessing: boolean = currentStatus === 'new' || currentStatus === 'running' || currentStatus === 'queued'
202 |   const isFailed: boolean = currentStatus === 'failed'
203 |   const isCompleted: boolean = currentStatus === 'completed'
204 | 
205 |   return (
206 |     <Card
207 |       className={cn(
208 |         'transition-all duration-200 hover:shadow-md group relative cursor-pointer border border-border/60 dark:border-border/40',
209 |         className
210 |       )}
211 |       onClick={handleCardClick}
212 |     >
213 |       <CardContent className="px-3 py-1">
214 |         {/* Header with status indicator */}
215 |         <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-3 mb-1">
216 |           <div className="flex-1 min-w-0">
217 |             {/* Status badge - only show if not completed */}
218 |             {!isCompleted && (
219 |               <div className="flex items-center gap-2 mb-2">
220 |                 <div className={cn(
221 |                   'flex items-center gap-1.5 px-2 py-1 rounded-md text-xs font-medium',
222 |                   statusConfig.bgColor,
223 |                   statusConfig.color
224 |                 )}>
225 |                   <StatusIcon className={cn(
226 |                     'h-3 w-3',
227 |                     isProcessing && 'animate-spin'
228 |                   )} />
229 |                   {statusLoading && shouldFetchStatus ? t.sources.checking : statusConfig.label}
230 |                 </div>
231 | 
232 |                 {/* Source type indicator */}
233 |                 <div className="flex items-center gap-1 text-gray-500">
234 |                   <SourceTypeIcon className="h-3 w-3" />
235 |                   <span className="text-xs capitalize">{t.common.source}</span>
236 |                 </div>
237 |               </div>
238 |             )}
239 | 
240 |             {/* Title */}
241 |             <div className={cn('mb-1.5', !isCompleted && 'mb-1')}>
242 |               <h4
243 |                 className="text-sm font-medium leading-tight line-clamp-2"
244 |                 title={title}
245 |               >
246 |                 {title}
247 |               </h4>
248 |             </div>
249 | 
250 |             {/* Processing message for active statuses */}
251 |             {statusData?.message && (isProcessing || isFailed) && (
252 |               <p className="text-xs text-gray-600 mb-2 italic">
253 |                 {statusData.message}
254 |               </p>
255 |             )}
256 | 
257 |             {/* Metadata badges */}
258 |             <div className="flex items-center gap-2 flex-wrap">
259 |               {/* Source type badge */}
260 |               <Badge variant="secondary" className="text-xs flex items-center gap-1">
261 |                 <SourceTypeIcon className="h-3 w-3" />
262 |                 {sourceType === 'link' ? t.sources.addUrl : sourceType === 'upload' ? t.sources.uploadFile : t.sources.enterText}
263 |               </Badge>
264 | 
265 |               {isCompleted && source.insights_count > 0 && (
266 |                 <Badge variant="outline" className="text-xs">
267 |                   {t.sources.insightsCount.replace('{count}', source.insights_count.toString())}
268 |                 </Badge>
269 |               )}
270 |               {source.topics && source.topics.length > 0 && isCompleted && (
271 |                 <>
272 |                   {source.topics.slice(0, 2).map((topic, index) => (
273 |                     <Badge key={index} variant="outline" className="text-xs">
274 |                       {topic}
275 |                     </Badge>
276 |                   ))}
277 |                   {source.topics.length > 2 && (
278 |                     <Badge variant="outline" className="text-xs">
279 |                       +{source.topics.length - 2}
280 |                     </Badge>
281 |                   )}
282 |                 </>
283 |               )}
284 |             </div>
285 |           </div>
286 | 
287 |           {/* Context toggle and actions */}
288 |           <div className="flex items-center gap-1">
289 |             {/* Context toggle - only show if handler provided */}
290 |             {onContextModeChange && contextMode && (
291 |               <ContextToggle
292 |                 mode={contextMode}
293 |                 hasInsights={source.insights_count > 0}
294 |                 onChange={onContextModeChange}
295 |               />
296 |             )}
297 | 
298 |             {/* Actions dropdown */}
299 |             <DropdownMenu>
300 |               <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
301 |                 <Button
302 |                   variant="ghost"
303 |                   size="sm"
304 |                   className="h-8 w-8 p-0 opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 transition-opacity"
305 |                   onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
306 |                 >
307 |                   <MoreVertical className="h-4 w-4" />
308 |                 </Button>
309 |               </DropdownMenuTrigger>
310 |             <DropdownMenuContent align="end" className="w-48">
311 |               {showRemoveFromNotebook && (
312 |                 <>
313 |                   <DropdownMenuItem
314 |                     onClick={(e) => {
315 |                       e.stopPropagation()
316 |                       handleRemoveFromNotebook()
317 |                     }}
318 |                     disabled={!onRemoveFromNotebook}
319 |                   >
320 |                     <Unlink className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
321 |                     {t.sources.removeFromNotebook}
322 |                   </DropdownMenuItem>
323 |                   <DropdownMenuSeparator />
324 |                 </>
325 |               )}
326 | 
327 |               {isFailed && (
328 |                 <>
329 |                   <DropdownMenuItem
330 |                     onClick={(e) => {
331 |                       e.stopPropagation()
332 |                       handleRetry()
333 |                     }}
334 |                     disabled={!onRetry}
335 |                   >
336 |                     <RefreshCw className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
337 |                     {t.sources.retryProcessing}
338 |                   </DropdownMenuItem>
339 |                   <DropdownMenuSeparator />
340 |                 </>
341 |               )}
342 | 
343 |               <DropdownMenuItem
344 |                 onClick={(e) => {
345 |                   e.stopPropagation()
346 |                   handleDelete()
347 |                 }}
348 |                 disabled={!onDelete}
349 |                 className="text-red-600 focus:text-red-600"
350 |               >
351 |                 <Trash2 className="h-4 w-4 mr-2" />
352 |                 {t.sources.deleteSource}
353 |               </DropdownMenuItem>
354 |             </DropdownMenuContent>
355 |           </DropdownMenu>
356 |           </div>
357 |         </div>
358 |         {/* eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any */}
359 |         {(isFailed as any) && (
360 |           <div className="flex gap-2 pt-2 border-t">
361 |             <Button
362 |               variant="outline"
363 |               size="sm"
364 |               onClick={handleRetry}
365 |               disabled={!onRetry}
366 |               className="h-7 text-xs"
367 |             >
368 |               <RefreshCw className="h-3 w-3 mr-1" />
369 |               {t.sources.retry}
370 |             </Button>
371 |           </div>
372 |         )}
373 | 
374 |         {/* Processing progress indicator */}
375 |         {isProcessing && statusData?.processing_info?.progress && (
376 |           <div className="mt-3 pt-2 border-t">
377 |             <div className="flex justify-between items-center mb-1">
378 |             <span className="text-xs text-gray-600">{t.common.progress}</span>

380 |                 {Math.round(statusData.processing_info.progress as number)}%
381 |               </span>

384 |               <div

386 |                 style={{ width: `${statusData.processing_info.progress as number}%` }}
387 |               />
388 |             </div>
389 |           </div>
390 |         )}
391 |       </CardContent>

  8 | import { Checkbox } from '@/components/ui/checkbox'
  9 | import { Label } from '@/components/ui/label'
 10 | import { Alert, AlertDescription } from '@/components/ui/alert'
 11 | import { Progress } from '@/components/ui/progress'
 12 | import { Loader2, AlertCircle, CheckCircle2, XCircle, Clock } from 'lucide-react'
 13 | import {
 14 |   Accordion,
 15 |   AccordionContent,
 16 |   AccordionItem,
 17 |   AccordionTrigger,
 18 | } from '@/components/ui/accordion'
 19 | import { embeddingApi } from '@/lib/api/embedding'
 20 | import type { RebuildEmbeddingsRequest, RebuildStatusResponse } from '@/lib/api/embedding'
 21 | import { useTranslation } from '@/lib/hooks/use-translation'
 22 | 
 23 | export function RebuildEmbeddings() {
 24 |   const { t } = useTranslation()
 25 |   const [mode, setMode] = useState<'existing' | 'all'>('existing')
 26 |   const [includeSources, setIncludeSources] = useState(true)
 27 |   const [includeNotes, setIncludeNotes] = useState(true)
 28 |   const [includeInsights, setIncludeInsights] = useState(true)
 29 |   const [commandId, setCommandId] = useState<string | null>(null)
 30 |   const [status, setStatus] = useState<RebuildStatusResponse | null>(null)
 31 |   const [pollingInterval, setPollingInterval] = useState<NodeJS.Timeout | null>(null)
 32 | 
 33 |   // Rebuild mutation
 34 |   const rebuildMutation = useMutation({
 35 |     mutationFn: async (request: RebuildEmbeddingsRequest) => {
 36 |       return embeddingApi.rebuildEmbeddings(request)
 37 |     },
 38 |     onSuccess: (data) => {
 39 |       setCommandId(data.command_id)
 40 |       // Start polling for status
 41 |       startPolling(data.command_id)
 42 |     }
 43 |   })
 44 | 
 45 |   // Start polling for rebuild status
 46 |   const startPolling = (cmdId: string) => {
 47 |     if (pollingInterval) {
 48 |       clearInterval(pollingInterval)
 49 |     }
 50 | 
 51 |     const interval = setInterval(async () => {
 52 |       try {
 53 |         const statusData = await embeddingApi.getRebuildStatus(cmdId)
 54 |         setStatus(statusData)
 55 | 
 56 |         // Stop polling if completed or failed
 57 |         if (statusData.status === 'completed' || statusData.status === 'failed') {
 58 |           stopPolling()
 59 |         }
 60 |       } catch (error) {
 61 |         console.error('Failed to fetch rebuild status:', error)
 62 |       }
 63 |     }, 5000) // Poll every 5 seconds
 64 | 
 65 |     setPollingInterval(interval)
 66 |   }
 67 | 
 68 |   // Stop polling
 69 |   const stopPolling = useCallback(() => {
 70 |     if (pollingInterval) {
 71 |       clearInterval(pollingInterval)
 72 |       setPollingInterval(null)
 73 |     }
 74 |   }, [pollingInterval])
 75 | 
 76 |   // Cleanup on unmount
 77 |   useEffect(() => {
 78 |     return () => {
 79 |       stopPolling()
 80 |     }
 81 |   }, [stopPolling])
 82 | 
 83 |   const handleStartRebuild = () => {
 84 |     const request: RebuildEmbeddingsRequest = {
 85 |       mode,
 86 |       include_sources: includeSources,
 87 |       include_notes: includeNotes,
 88 |       include_insights: includeInsights
 89 |     }
 90 | 
 91 |     rebuildMutation.mutate(request)
 92 |   }
 93 | 
 94 |   const handleReset = () => {
 95 |     stopPolling()
 96 |     setCommandId(null)
 97 |     setStatus(null)
 98 |     rebuildMutation.reset()
 99 |   }
100 | 
101 |   const isAnyTypeSelected = includeSources || includeNotes || includeInsights
102 |   const isRebuildActive = commandId && status && (status.status === 'queued' || status.status === 'running')
103 | 
104 |   const progressData = status?.progress
105 |   const stats = status?.stats
106 | 
107 |   const totalItems = progressData?.total_items ?? progressData?.total ?? 0
108 |   const processedItems = progressData?.processed_items ?? progressData?.processed ?? 0
109 |   const derivedProgressPercent = progressData?.percentage ?? (totalItems > 0 ? (processedItems / totalItems) * 100 : 0)
110 |   const progressPercent = Number.isFinite(derivedProgressPercent) ? derivedProgressPercent : 0
111 | 
112 |   const sourcesProcessed = stats?.sources_processed ?? stats?.sources ?? 0
113 |   const notesProcessed = stats?.notes_processed ?? stats?.notes ?? 0
114 |   const insightsProcessed = stats?.insights_processed ?? stats?.insights ?? 0
115 |   const failedItems = stats?.failed_items ?? stats?.failed ?? 0
116 | 
117 |   const computedDuration = status?.started_at && status?.completed_at
118 |     ? (new Date(status.completed_at).getTime() - new Date(status.started_at).getTime()) / 1000
119 |     : undefined
120 |   const processingTimeSeconds = stats?.processing_time ?? computedDuration
121 | 
122 |   return (
123 |     <Card>
124 |       <CardHeader>
125 |         <CardTitle className="flex items-center gap-2">
126 |           {t.advanced.rebuildEmbeddings}
127 |         </CardTitle>
128 |         <CardDescription>
129 |           {t.advanced.rebuildEmbeddingsDesc}
130 |         </CardDescription>
131 |       </CardHeader>
132 |       <CardContent className="space-y-6">
133 |         {/* Configuration Form */}
134 |         {!isRebuildActive && (
135 |           <div className="space-y-6">
136 |             <div className="space-y-3">
137 |               <Label htmlFor="mode">{t.advanced.rebuild.mode}</Label>
138 |               <Select value={mode} onValueChange={(value) => setMode(value as 'existing' | 'all')}>
139 |                 <SelectTrigger id="mode">
140 |                   <SelectValue />
141 |                 </SelectTrigger>
142 |                 <SelectContent>
143 |                   <SelectItem value="existing">{t.advanced.rebuild.existing}</SelectItem>
144 |                   <SelectItem value="all">{t.advanced.rebuild.all}</SelectItem>
145 |                 </SelectContent>
146 |               </Select>
147 |               <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
148 |                 {mode === 'existing'
149 |                   ? t.advanced.rebuild.existingDesc
150 |                   : t.advanced.rebuild.allDesc}
151 |               </p>
152 |             </div>
153 | 
154 |             <div className="space-y-3" role="group" aria-labelledby="include-label">
155 |               <span id="include-label" className="text-sm font-medium leading-none">{t.advanced.rebuild.include}</span>
156 |               <div className="space-y-3">
157 |                 <div className="flex items-center space-x-2">
158 |                   <Checkbox
159 |                     id="sources"
160 |                     checked={includeSources}
161 |                     onCheckedChange={(checked) => setIncludeSources(checked === true)}
162 |                   />
163 |                   <Label htmlFor="sources" className="font-normal cursor-pointer">
164 |                     {t.navigation.sources}
165 |                   </Label>
166 |                 </div>
167 |                 <div className="flex items-center space-x-2">
168 |                   <Checkbox
169 |                     id="notes"
170 |                     checked={includeNotes}
171 |                     onCheckedChange={(checked) => setIncludeNotes(checked === true)}
172 |                   />
173 |                   <Label htmlFor="notes" className="font-normal cursor-pointer">
174 |                     {t.common.notes}
175 |                   </Label>
176 |                 </div>
177 |                 <div className="flex items-center space-x-2">
178 |                   <Checkbox
179 |                     id="insights"
180 |                     checked={includeInsights}
181 |                     onCheckedChange={(checked) => setIncludeInsights(checked === true)}
182 |                   />
183 |                   <Label htmlFor="insights" className="font-normal cursor-pointer">
184 |                     {t.common.insights}
185 |                   </Label>
186 |                 </div>
187 |               </div>
188 |               {!isAnyTypeSelected && (
189 |                 <Alert variant="destructive">
190 |                   <AlertCircle className="h-4 w-4" />
191 |                   <AlertDescription>
192 |                     {t.advanced.rebuild.selectOneError}
193 |                   </AlertDescription>
194 |                 </Alert>
195 |               )}
196 |             </div>
197 | 
198 |             <Button
199 |               onClick={handleStartRebuild}
200 |               disabled={!isAnyTypeSelected || rebuildMutation.isPending}
201 |               className="w-full"
202 |             >
203 |               {rebuildMutation.isPending ? (
204 |                 <>
205 |                   <Loader2 className="mr-2 h-4 w-4 animate-spin" />
206 |                   {t.advanced.rebuild.starting}
207 |                 </>
208 |               ) : (
209 |                 t.advanced.rebuild.startBtn
210 |               )}
211 |             </Button>
212 | 
213 |             {rebuildMutation.isError && (
214 |               <Alert variant="destructive">
215 |                 <AlertCircle className="h-4 w-4" />
216 |                 <AlertDescription>
217 |                   {t.advanced.rebuild.failed}: {(rebuildMutation.error as Error)?.message || t.common.error}
218 |                 </AlertDescription>
219 |               </Alert>
220 |             )}
221 |           </div>
222 |         )}
223 | 
224 |         {/* Status Display */}
225 |         {status && (
226 |           <div className="space-y-4">
227 |             <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
228 |               <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
229 |                 {status.status === 'queued' && <Clock className="h-5 w-5 text-yellow-500" />}
230 |                 {status.status === 'running' && <Loader2 className="h-5 w-5 text-blue-500 animate-spin" />}
231 |                 {status.status === 'completed' && <CheckCircle2 className="h-5 w-5 text-green-500" />}
232 |                 {status.status === 'failed' && <XCircle className="h-5 w-5 text-red-500" />}
233 |                 <div className="flex flex-col">
234 |                   <span className="font-medium">
235 |                     {status.status === 'queued' && t.advanced.rebuild.queued}
236 |                     {status.status === 'running' && t.advanced.rebuild.running}
237 |                     {status.status === 'completed' && t.advanced.rebuild.completed}
238 |                     {status.status === 'failed' && t.advanced.rebuild.failed}
239 |                   </span>
240 |                   {status.status === 'running' && (
241 |                     <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
242 |                       {t.advanced.rebuild.leavePageHint}
243 |                     </span>
244 |                   )}
245 |                 </div>
246 |               </div>
247 |               {(status.status === 'completed' || status.status === 'failed') && (
248 |                 <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={handleReset}>
249 |                   {t.advanced.rebuild.startNew}
250 |                 </Button>
251 |               )}
252 |             </div>
253 | 
254 |             {progressData && (
255 |               <div className="space-y-2">
256 |                 <div className="flex justify-between text-sm">
257 |                   <span>{t.common.progress}</span>
258 |                   <span className="font-medium">
259 |                     {t.advanced.rebuild.itemsProcessed
260 |                       .replace('{processed}', processedItems.toString())
261 |                       .replace('{total}', totalItems.toString())
262 |                       .replace('{percent}', progressPercent.toFixed(1))}
263 |                   </span>
264 |                 </div>
265 |                 <Progress value={progressPercent} className="h-2" />
266 |                 {failedItems > 0 && (
267 |                   <p className="text-sm text-yellow-600">
268 |                     ⚠️ {t.advanced.rebuild.failedItems.replace('{count}', failedItems.toString())}
269 |                   </p>
270 |                 )}
271 |               </div>
272 |             )}
273 | 
274 |              {stats && (
275 |               <div className="grid grid-cols-4 gap-4">
276 |                 <div className="space-y-1">
277 |                   <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{t.navigation.sources}</p>
278 |                   <p className="text-2xl font-bold">{sourcesProcessed}</p>
279 |                 </div>
280 |                 <div className="space-y-1">
281 |                   <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{t.common.notes}</p>
282 |                   <p className="text-2xl font-bold">{notesProcessed}</p>
283 |                 </div>
284 |                 <div className="space-y-1">
285 |                   <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{t.common.insights}</p>
286 |                   <p className="text-2xl font-bold">{insightsProcessed}</p>
287 |                 </div>
288 |                 <div className="space-y-1">
289 |                   <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{t.advanced.rebuild.time}</p>
290 |                   <p className="text-2xl font-bold">
291 |                     {processingTimeSeconds !== undefined ? `${processingTimeSeconds.toFixed(1)}s` : '—'}
292 |                   </p>
293 |                 </div>
294 |               </div>
295 |             )}
296 | 
297 |             {status.error_message && (
298 |               <Alert variant="destructive">
299 |                 <AlertCircle className="h-4 w-4" />
300 |                 <AlertDescription>{status.error_message}</AlertDescription>
301 |               </Alert>
302 |             )}
303 | 
304 |             {status.started_at && (
305 |               <div className="text-sm text-muted-foreground space-y-1">
306 |                 <p>{t.common.created.replace('{time}', new Date(status.started_at).toLocaleString())}</p>
307 |                 {status.completed_at && (
308 |                   <p>{t.notebooks.updated}: {new Date(status.completed_at).toLocaleString()}</p>
309 |                 )}
310 |               </div>
311 |             )}
312 |           </div>
313 |         )}
314 | 
315 |         {/* Help Section */}
316 |          <Accordion type="single" collapsible className="w-full">
317 |           <AccordionItem value="when">
318 |             <AccordionTrigger>{t.advanced.rebuild.whenToRebuild}</AccordionTrigger>
319 |             <AccordionContent className="space-y-2 text-sm">
320 |               <p>{t.advanced.rebuild.whenToRebuildAns}</p>
321 |             </AccordionContent>
322 |           </AccordionItem>
323 | 
324 |           <AccordionItem value="time">
325 |             <AccordionTrigger>{t.advanced.rebuild.howLong}</AccordionTrigger>
326 |             <AccordionContent className="space-y-2 text-sm">
327 |               <p>{t.advanced.rebuild.howLongAns}</p>
328 |             </AccordionContent>
329 |           </AccordionItem>
330 | 
331 |           <AccordionItem value="safe">
332 |             <AccordionTrigger>{t.advanced.rebuild.isSafe}</AccordionTrigger>
333 |             <AccordionContent className="space-y-2 text-sm">
334 |               <p>{t.advanced.rebuild.isSafeAns}</p>
335 |             </AccordionContent>
336 |           </AccordionItem>
337 |         </Accordion>
338 |       </CardContent>
339 |     </Card>
340 |   )
341 | }
342 |

/docs/3-USER-GUIDE/working-with-notes.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Working with Notes - Capturing and Organizing Insights
  2 | 
  3 | Notes are your processed knowledge. This guide covers how to create, organize, and use them effectively.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## What Are Notes?
  8 | 
  9 | Notes are your **research output** — the insights you capture from analyzing sources. They can be:
 10 | 
 11 | - **Manual** — You write them yourself
 12 | - **AI-Generated** — From Chat responses, Ask results, or Transformations
 13 | - **Hybrid** — AI insight + your edits and additions
 14 | 
 15 | Unlike sources (which never change), notes are mutable — you edit, refine, and organize them.
 16 | 
 17 | ---
 18 | 
 19 | ## Quick-Start: Create Your First Note
 20 | 
 21 | ### Method 1: Manual Note (Write Yourself)
 22 | 
 23 | ```
 24 | 1. In your notebook, go to "Notes" section
 25 | 2. Click "Create New Note"
 26 | 3. Give it a title: "Key insights from source X"
 27 | 4. Write your content (markdown supported)
 28 | 5. Click "Save"
 29 | 6. Done! Note appears in your notebook
 30 | ```
 31 | 
 32 | ### Method 2: Save from Chat
 33 | 
 34 | ```
 35 | 1. Have a Chat conversation
 36 | 2. Get a good response from AI
 37 | 3. Click "Save as Note" button under response
 38 | 4. Give the note a title
 39 | 5. Add any additional context
 40 | 6. Click "Save"
 41 | 7. Done! Note appears in your notebook
 42 | ```
 43 | 
 44 | ### Method 3: Apply Transformation
 45 | 
 46 | ```
 47 | 1. Go to "Transformations"
 48 | 2. Select a template (or create custom)
 49 | 3. Click "Apply to sources"
 50 | 4. Select which sources to transform
 51 | 5. Wait for processing
 52 | 6. New notes automatically appear
 53 | 7. Done! Each source produces one note
 54 | ```
 55 | 
 56 | ---
 57 | 
 58 | ## Creating Manual Notes
 59 | 
 60 | ### Basic Structure
 61 | 
 62 | ```
 63 | Title: "What you're capturing"
 64 |        (Make it descriptive)
 65 | 
 66 | Content:
 67 |   - Main points
 68 |   - Your analysis
 69 |   - Questions raised
 70 |   - Next steps
 71 | 
 72 | Metadata:
 73 |   - Tags: How to categorize
 74 |   - Related sources: Which documents influenced this
 75 |   - Date: Auto-added when created
 76 | ```
 77 | 
 78 | ### Markdown Support
 79 | 
 80 | You can format notes with markdown:
 81 | 
 82 | ```markdown
 83 | # Heading
 84 | ## Subheading
 85 | ### Sub-subheading
 86 | 
 87 | **Bold text** for emphasis
 88 | *Italic text* for secondary emphasis
 89 | 
 90 | - Bullet lists
 91 | - Like this
 92 | 
 93 | 1. Numbered lists
 94 | 2. Like this
 95 | 
 96 | > Quotes and important callouts
 97 | 
 98 | [Links work](https://example.com)
 99 | ```
100 | 
101 | ### Example Note Structure
102 | 
103 | ```markdown
104 | # Key Findings from "AI Safety Paper 2025"
105 | 
106 | ## Main Argument
107 | The paper argues that X approach is better than Y because...
108 | 
109 | ## Methodology
110 | The authors use [methodology] to test this hypothesis.
111 | 
112 | ## Key Results
113 | - Result 1: [specific finding with citation]
114 | - Result 2: [specific finding with citation]
115 | - Result 3: [specific finding with citation]
116 | 
117 | ## Gaps & Limitations
118 | 1. The paper assumes X, which might not hold in Y scenario
119 | 2. Limited to Z population/domain
120 | 3. Future work needed on A, B, C
121 | 
122 | ## My Thoughts
123 | - This connects to previous research on...
124 | - Potential application in...
125 | 
126 | ## Next Steps
127 | - [ ] Read the referenced paper on X
128 | - [ ] Find similar studies on Y
129 | - [ ] Discuss implications with team
130 | ```
131 | 
132 | ---
133 | 
134 | ## AI-Generated Notes: Three Sources
135 | 
136 | ### 1. Save from Chat
137 | 
138 | ```
139 | Workflow:
140 |   Chat → Good response → "Save as Note"
141 |          → Edit if needed → Save
142 | 
143 | When to use:
144 |   - AI response answers your question well
145 |   - You want to keep the answer for reference
146 |   - You're building a knowledge base from conversations
147 | 
148 | Quality:
149 |   - Quality = quality of your Chat question
150 |   - Better context = better responses = better notes
151 |   - Ask specific questions for useful notes
152 | ```
153 | 
154 | ### 2. Save from Ask
155 | 
156 | ```
157 | Workflow:
158 |   Ask → Comprehensive answer → "Save as Note"
159 |       → Edit if needed → Save
160 | 
161 | When to use:
162 |   - You need a one-time comprehensive answer
163 |   - You want to save the synthesized result
164 |   - Building a knowledge base of comprehensive answers
165 | 
166 | Quality:
167 |   - System automatically found relevant sources
168 |   - Results already have citations
169 |   - Often higher quality than Chat (more thorough)
170 | ```
171 | 
172 | ### 3. Transformations (Batch Processing)
173 | 
174 | ```
175 | Workflow:
176 |   Define transformation → Apply to sources → Notes auto-created
177 |                       → Review & edit → Organize
178 | 
179 | Example Transformation:
180 |   Template: "Extract: main argument, methodology, key findings"
181 |   Apply to: 5 sources
182 |   Result: 5 new notes with consistent structure
183 | 
184 | When to use:
185 |   - Same extraction from many sources
186 |   - Building structured knowledge base
187 |   - Creating consistent summaries
188 | ```
189 | 
190 | ---
191 | 
192 | ## Using Transformations for Batch Insights
193 | 
194 | ### Built-in Transformations
195 | 
196 | Open Notebook comes with presets:
197 | 
198 | **Summary**
199 | ```
200 | Extracts: Main points, key arguments, conclusions
201 | Output: 200-300 word summary of source
202 | Best for: Quick reference summaries
203 | ```
204 | 
205 | **Key Concepts**
206 | ```
207 | Extracts: Main ideas, concepts, terminology
208 | Output: List of concepts with explanations
209 | Best for: Learning and terminology
210 | ```
211 | 
212 | **Methodology**
213 | ```
214 | Extracts: Research approach, methods, data
215 | Output: How the research was conducted
216 | Best for: Academic sources, methodology review
217 | ```
218 | 
219 | **Takeaways**
220 | ```
221 | Extracts: Actionable insights, recommendations
222 | Output: What you should do with this information
223 | Best for: Practical/business sources
224 | ```
225 | 
226 | ### How to Apply Transformation
227 | 
228 | ```
229 | 1. Go to "Transformations"
230 | 2. Select a template
231 | 3. Click "Apply"
232 | 4. Select which sources (one or many)
233 | 5. Wait for processing (usually 30 seconds - 2 minutes)
234 | 6. New notes appear in your notebook
235 | 7. Edit if needed
236 | ```
237 | 
238 | ### Create Custom Transformation
239 | 
240 | ```
241 | 1. Click "Create Custom Transformation"
242 | 2. Write your extraction template:
243 | 
244 |    Example:
245 |    "For this academic paper, extract:
246 |     - Central research question
247 |     - Hypothesis tested
248 |     - Methodology used
249 |     - Key findings (numbered)
250 |     - Limitations acknowledged
251 |     - Recommendations for future work"
252 | 
253 | 3. Click "Save Template"
254 | 4. Apply to one or many sources
255 | 5. System generates notes with consistent structure
256 | ```
257 | 
258 | ---
259 | 
260 | ## Organizing Notes
261 | 
262 | ### Naming Conventions
263 | 
264 | **Option 1: Date-based**
265 | ```
266 | 2026-01-03 - Key points from X source
267 | 2026-01-04 - Comparison between A and B
268 | Benefit: Easy to see what you did when
269 | ```
270 | 
271 | **Option 2: Topic-based**
272 | ```
273 | AI Safety - Alignment approaches
274 | AI Safety - Interpretability research
275 | Benefit: Groups by subject matter
276 | ```
277 | 
278 | **Option 3: Type-based**
279 | ```
280 | SUMMARY: Paper on X
281 | QUESTION: What about Y?
282 | INSIGHT: Connection between Z and W
283 | Benefit: Easy to filter by type
284 | ```
285 | 
286 | **Option 4: Source-based**
287 | ```
288 | From: Paper A - Main insights
289 | From: Video B - Interesting implications
290 | Benefit: Easy to trace back to sources
291 | ```
292 | 
293 | **Best practice:** Combine approaches
294 | ```
295 | [Date] [Source] - [Topic] - [Type]
296 | 2026-01-03 - Paper A - AI Safety - Takeaways
297 | ```
298 | 
299 | ### Using Tags
300 | 
301 | Tags are labels for categorization. Add them when creating notes:
302 | 
303 | ```
304 | Example tags:
305 |   - "primary-research" (direct source analysis)
306 |   - "background" (supporting material)
307 |   - "methodology" (about research methods)
308 |   - "insights" (your original thinking)
309 |   - "questions" (open questions raised)
310 |   - "follow-up" (needs more work)
311 |   - "published" (ready to share/use)
312 | ```
313 | 
314 | **Benefits of tags:**
315 | - Filter notes by tag
316 | - Find all notes of a type
317 | - Organize workflow (e.g., find all "follow-up" notes)
318 | 
319 | ### Note Linking & References
320 | 
321 | You can reference sources within notes:
322 | 
323 | ```markdown
324 | # Analysis of Paper A
325 | 
326 | As shown in Paper A (see "main argument" section),
327 | the authors argue that...
328 | 
329 | ## Related Sources
330 | - Paper B discusses similar approach
331 | - Video C shows practical application
332 | - My note on "Comparative analysis" has more
333 | ```
334 | 
335 | ---
336 | 
337 | ## Editing and Refining Notes
338 | 
339 | ### Improving AI-Generated Notes
340 | 
341 | ```
342 | AI Note:
343 |   "The paper discusses machine learning"
344 | 
345 | What you might change:
346 |   "The paper proposes a supervised learning approach
347 |    to classification problems, using neural networks
348 |    with attention mechanisms (see pp. 15-18)."
349 | 
350 | How to edit:
351 |   1. Click note
352 |   2. Click "Edit"
353 |   3. Refine the content
354 |   4. Click "Save"
355 | ```
356 | 
357 | ### Adding Citations
358 | 
359 | ```
360 | When saving from Chat/Ask:
361 |   - Citations auto-added
362 |   - Shows which sources informed answer
363 |   - You can verify by clicking
364 | 
365 | When manual notes:
366 |   - Add manually: "From Paper A, page 15: ..."
367 |   - Or reference: "As discussed in [source]"
368 | ```
369 | 
370 | ---
371 | 
372 | ## Searching Your Notes
373 | 
374 | Notes are fully searchable:
375 | 
376 | ### Text Search
377 | ```
378 | Find exact phrase: "attention mechanism"
379 | Results: All notes containing that phrase
380 | Use when: Looking for specific terms or quotes
381 | ```
382 | 
383 | ### Vector/Semantic Search
384 | ```
385 | Find concept: "How do models understand?"
386 | Results: Notes about interpretability, mechanistic understanding, etc.
387 | Use when: Exploring conceptually (words not exact)
388 | ```
389 | 
390 | ### Combined Search
391 | ```
392 | Text search notes → Find keyword matches
393 | Vector search notes → Find conceptual matches
394 | Both work across sources + notes together
395 | ```
396 | 
397 | ---
398 | 
399 | ## Exporting and Sharing Notes
400 | 
401 | ### Options
402 | 
403 | **Copy to clipboard**
404 | ```
405 | Click "Share" → "Copy" → Paste anywhere
406 | Good for: Sharing one note via email/chat
407 | ```
408 | 
409 | **Export as Markdown**
410 | ```
411 | Click "Share" → "Export as MD" → Saves as .md file
412 | Good for: Sharing with others, version control
413 | ```
414 | 
415 | **Create note collection**
416 | ```
417 | Select multiple notes → "Export collection"
418 | → Creates organized markdown document
419 | Good for: Sharing a topic overview
420 | ```
421 | 
422 | **Publish to web**
423 | ```
424 | Click "Publish" → Get shareable link
425 | Good for: Publishing publicly (if desired)
426 | ```
427 | 
428 | ---
429 | 
430 | ## Organizing Your Notebook's Notes
431 | 
432 | ### By Research Phase
433 | 
434 | **Phase 1: Discovery**
435 | - Initial summaries
436 | - Questions raised
437 | - Interesting findings
438 | 
439 | **Phase 2: Deep Dive**
440 | - Detailed analysis
441 | - Comparative insights
442 | - Methodology reviews
443 | 
444 | **Phase 3: Synthesis**
445 | - Connections across sources
446 | - Original thinking
447 | - Conclusions
448 | 
449 | ### By Content Type
450 | 
451 | **Summaries**
452 | - High-level overviews
453 | - Generated by transformations
454 | - Quick reference
455 | 
456 | **Questions**
457 | - Open questions
458 | - Things to research more
459 | - Gaps to fill
460 | 
461 | **Insights**
462 | - Your original analysis
463 | - Connections made
464 | - Conclusions reached
465 | 
466 | **Tasks**
467 | - Follow-up research
468 | - Sources to add
469 | - People to contact
470 | 
471 | ---
472 | 
473 | ## Using Notes in Other Features
474 | 
475 | ### In Chat
476 | 
477 | ```
478 | You can reference notes:
479 | "Based on my note 'Key findings from A',
480 | how does this compare to B?"
481 | 
482 | Notes become part of context.
483 | Treated like sources but smaller/more focused.
484 | ```
485 | 
486 | ### In Transformations
487 | 
488 | ```
489 | Notes can be transformed:
490 | 1. Select notes as input
491 | 2. Apply transformation
492 | 3. Get new derived notes
493 | 
494 | Example: Transform 5 analysis notes → Create synthesis
495 | ```
496 | 
497 | ### In Podcasts
498 | 
499 | ```
500 | Notes are used to create podcast content:
501 | 1. Generate podcast for notebook
502 | 2. System includes notes in content selection
503 | 3. Notes become part of episode outline
504 | ```
505 | 
506 | ---
507 | 
508 | ## Best Practices
509 | 
510 | ### For Manual Notes
511 | 1. **Write clearly** — Future you will appreciate it
512 | 2. **Add context** — Why this matters, not just what it says
513 | 3. **Link to sources** — You can verify later
514 | 4. **Date them** — Track your thinking over time
515 | 5. **Tag immediately** — Don't defer organization
516 | 
517 | ### For AI-Generated Notes
518 | 1. **Review before saving** — Verify quality
519 | 2. **Edit for clarity** — AI might miss nuance
520 | 3. **Add your thoughts** — Make it your own
521 | 4. **Include citations** — Understand sources
522 | 5. **Organize right away** — While context is fresh
523 | 
524 | ### For Organization
525 | 1. **Consistent naming** — Your future self will thank you
526 | 2. **Tag everything** — Makes filtering later much easier
527 | 3. **Link related notes** — Create knowledge network
528 | 4. **Review periodically** — Refactor as understanding evolves
529 | 5. **Archive old notes** — Keep working space clean
530 | 
531 | ---
532 | 
533 | ## Common Mistakes
534 | 
535 | | Mistake | Problem | Solution |
536 | |---------|---------|----------|
537 | | Save every Chat response | Notebook becomes cluttered with low-quality notes | Only save good responses that answer your questions |
538 | | Don't add tags | Can't find notes later | Tag immediately when creating |
539 | | Poor note titles | Can't remember what's in them | Use descriptive titles, include key concept |
540 | | Never link notes together | Miss connections between ideas | Add references to related notes |
541 | | Forget the source | Can't verify claims later | Always link back to source |
542 | | Never edit AI notes | Keep generic AI responses | Refine for clarity and context |
543 | | Create one giant note | Too long to be useful | Split into focused notes by subtopic |
544 | 
545 | ---
546 | 
547 | ## Summary: Note Lifecycle
548 | 
549 | ```
550 | 1. CREATE
551 |    ├─ Manual: Write from scratch
552 |    ├─ From Chat: Save good response
553 |    ├─ From Ask: Save synthesis
554 |    └─ From Transform: Batch process
555 | 
556 | 2. EDIT & REFINE
557 |    ├─ Improve clarity
558 |    ├─ Add context
559 |    ├─ Fix AI mistakes
560 |    └─ Add citations
561 | 
562 | 3. ORGANIZE
563 |    ├─ Name clearly
564 |    ├─ Add tags
565 |    ├─ Link related
566 |    └─ Categorize
567 | 
568 | 4. USE
569 |    ├─ Reference in Chat
570 |    ├─ Transform for synthesis
571 |    ├─ Export for sharing
572 |    └─ Build on with new questions
573 | 
574 | 5. MAINTAIN
575 |    ├─ Periodically review
576 |    ├─ Update as understanding grows
577 |    ├─ Archive when done
578 |    └─ Learn from organized knowledge
579 | ```
580 | 
581 | Your notes become your actual knowledge base. The more you invest in organizing them, the more valuable they become.
582 |

  3 | import { useMemo, useState } from "react"
  4 | import { Control, FieldErrors, UseFormRegister, UseFormSetValue, useWatch } from "react-hook-form"

  7 | import { FormSection } from "@/components/ui/form-section"
  8 | import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@/components/ui/tabs"
  9 | import { Input } from "@/components/ui/input"
 10 | import { Textarea } from "@/components/ui/textarea"

 15 | interface CreateSourceFormData {
 16 |   type: 'link' | 'upload' | 'text'
 17 |   title?: string
 18 |   url?: string
 19 |   content?: string
 20 |   file?: FileList | File
 21 |   notebooks?: string[]

 23 |   embed: boolean

 27 | // Helper functions for batch URL parsing
 28 | function parseUrls(text: string): string[] {
 29 |   return text
 30 |     .split('\n')
 31 |     .map(line => line.trim())
 32 |     .filter(line => line.length > 0)
 33 | }
 34 | 
 35 | function validateUrl(url: string): boolean {
 36 |   try {
 37 |     new URL(url)
 38 |     return true
 39 |   } catch {
 40 |     return false
 41 |   }
 42 | }
 43 | 
 44 | export function parseAndValidateUrls(text: string): {
 45 |   valid: string[]
 46 |   invalid: { url: string; line: number }[]
 47 | } {
 48 |   const lines = text.split('\n')
 49 |   const valid: string[] = []
 50 |   const invalid: { url: string; line: number }[] = []
 51 | 
 52 |   lines.forEach((line, index) => {
 53 |     const trimmed = line.trim()
 54 |     if (trimmed.length === 0) return // skip empty lines
 55 | 
 56 |     if (validateUrl(trimmed)) {
 57 |       valid.push(trimmed)
 58 |     } else {
 59 |       invalid.push({ url: trimmed, line: index + 1 })
 60 |     }
 61 |   })
 62 | 
 63 |   return { valid, invalid }
 64 | }

 66 | import { TranslationKeys } from '@/lib/locales'

 69 |   {
 70 |     value: 'link' as const,
 71 |     label: t.sources.addUrl,
 72 |     icon: LinkIcon,
 73 |     description: t.sources.processDescription,
 74 |   },
 75 |   {
 76 |     value: 'upload' as const,
 77 |     label: t.sources.uploadFile,
 78 |     icon: FileIcon,
 79 |     description: t.sources.processDescription,
 80 |   },

 83 |     label: t.sources.enterText,
