 53 | ## A private, multi-model, 100% local, full-featured alternative to Notebook LM
 54 | 
 55 | ![New Notebook](docs/assets/asset_list.png)
 56 | 
 57 | In a world dominated by Artificial Intelligence, having the ability to think 🧠 and acquire new knowledge 💡, is a skill that should not be a privilege for a few, nor restricted to a single provider.
 58 | 
 59 | **Open Notebook empowers you to:**
 60 | - 🔒 **Control your data** - Keep your research private and secure
 61 | - 🤖 **Choose your AI models** - Support for 16+ providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, LM Studio, and more
 62 | - 📚 **Organize multi-modal content** - PDFs, videos, audio, web pages, and more
 63 | - 🎙️ **Generate professional podcasts** - Advanced multi-speaker podcast generation
 64 | - 🔍 **Search intelligently** - Full-text and vector search across all your content
 65 | - 💬 **Chat with context** - AI conversations powered by your research
 66 | - 🌐 **Multi-language UI** - English, Portuguese, Chinese (Simplified & Traditional), Japanese, and Russian support
 67 | 
 68 | Learn more about our project at [https://www.open-notebook.ai](https://www.open-notebook.ai)
 69 | 
 70 | ---
 71 | 
 72 | ## 🆚 Open Notebook vs Google Notebook LM
 73 | 
 74 | | Feature | Open Notebook | Google Notebook LM | Advantage |
 75 | |---------|---------------|--------------------|-----------|
 76 | | **Privacy & Control** | Self-hosted, your data | Google cloud only | Complete data sovereignty |
 77 | | **AI Provider Choice** | 16+ providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, LM Studio, etc.) | Google models only | Flexibility and cost optimization |
 78 | | **Podcast Speakers** | 1-4 speakers with custom profiles | 2 speakers only | Extreme flexibility |
 79 | | **Content Transformations** | Custom and built-in | Limited options | Unlimited processing power |
 80 | | **API Access** | Full REST API | No API | Complete automation |
 81 | | **Deployment** | Docker, cloud, or local | Google hosted only | Deploy anywhere |
 82 | | **Citations** | Basic references (will improve) | Comprehensive with sources | Research integrity |
 83 | | **Customization** | Open source, fully customizable | Closed system | Unlimited extensibility |
 84 | | **Cost** | Pay only for AI usage | Free tier + Monthly subscription | Transparent and controllable |
 85 | 
 86 | **Why Choose Open Notebook?**
 87 | - 🔒 **Privacy First**: Your sensitive research stays completely private
 88 | - 💰 **Cost Control**: Choose cheaper AI providers or run locally with Ollama
 89 | - 🎙️ **Better Podcasts**: Full script control and multi-speaker flexibility vs limited 2-speaker deep-dive format
 90 | - 🔧 **Unlimited Customization**: Modify, extend, and integrate as needed
 91 | - 🌐 **No Vendor Lock-in**: Switch providers, deploy anywhere, own your data
 92 |

 97 | ## 🚀 Quick Start
 98 | 
 99 | Choose your installation method:
100 | 
101 | ### 🐳 **Docker (Recommended)**
102 | 
103 | **Best for most users** - Fast setup with Docker Compose:
104 | 
105 | → **[Docker Compose Installation Guide](docs/1-INSTALLATION/docker-compose.md)**
106 | - Multi-container setup (recommended)
107 | - 5-10 minutes setup time
108 | - Requires Docker Desktop
109 | 
110 | **Quick Start:**
111 | - Get an API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.) or setup Ollama
112 | - Create docker-compose.yml (example in guide)
113 | - Run: docker compose up -d
114 | - Access: http://localhost:8502
115 |

117 | 
118 | ### 💻 **From Source (Developers)**
119 | 
120 | **For development and contributors:**
121 | 
122 | → **[From Source Installation Guide](docs/1-INSTALLATION/from-source.md)**
123 | - Clone and run locally
124 | - 10-15 minutes setup time
125 | - Requires: Python 3.11+, Node.js 18+, Docker, uv
126 | 
127 | **Quick Start:**
128 | 
129 | ```bash
130 | git clone https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook.git
131 | uv sync
132 | make start-all
133 | ```
134 | 
135 | Access: http://localhost:3000 (dev) or http://localhost:8502 (production)

177 | ## ✨ Key Features
178 | 
179 | ### Core Capabilities
180 | - **🔒 Privacy-First**: Your data stays under your control - no cloud dependencies
181 | - **🎯 Multi-Notebook Organization**: Manage multiple research projects seamlessly
182 | - **📚 Universal Content Support**: PDFs, videos, audio, web pages, Office docs, and more

 21 | export default function SourcesPage() {

 23 |   const [sources, setSources] = useState<SourceListResponse[]>([])
 24 |   const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true)

 26 |   const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)
 27 |   const [selectedIndex, setSelectedIndex] = useState(0)
 28 |   const [sortBy, setSortBy] = useState<'created' | 'updated'>('updated')
 29 |   const [sortOrder, setSortOrder] = useState<'asc' | 'desc'>('desc')
 30 |   const [deleteDialog, setDeleteDialog] = useState<{ open: boolean; source: SourceListResponse | null }>({
 31 |     open: false,
 32 |     source: null
 33 |   })
 34 |   const router = useRouter()
 35 |   const tableRef = useRef<HTMLTableElement>(null)
 36 |   const scrollContainerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
 37 |   const offsetRef = useRef(0)
 38 |   const loadingMoreRef = useRef(false)
 39 |   const hasMoreRef = useRef(true)
 40 |   const PAGE_SIZE = 30
 41 | 
 42 |   const fetchSources = useCallback(async (reset = false) => {
 43 |     try {
 44 |       // Check flags before proceeding
 45 |       if (!reset && (loadingMoreRef.current || !hasMoreRef.current)) {
 46 |         return
 47 |       }
 48 | 
 49 |       if (reset) {
 50 |         setLoading(true)
 51 |         offsetRef.current = 0
 52 |         setSources([])
 53 |         hasMoreRef.current = true
 54 |       } else {
 55 |         loadingMoreRef.current = true
 56 |         setLoadingMore(true)
 57 |       }
 58 | 
 59 |       const data = await sourcesApi.list({
 60 |         limit: PAGE_SIZE,
 61 |         offset: offsetRef.current,
 62 |         sort_by: sortBy,
 63 |         sort_order: sortOrder,
 64 |       })
 65 | 
 66 |       if (reset) {
 67 |         setSources(data)
 68 |       } else {
 69 |         setSources(prev => [...prev, ...data])
 70 |       }
 71 | 
 72 |       // Check if we have more data
 73 |       const hasMoreData = data.length === PAGE_SIZE
 74 |       hasMoreRef.current = hasMoreData
 75 |       offsetRef.current += data.length
 76 |     } catch (err) {
 77 |       console.error('Failed to fetch sources:', err)
 78 |       setError(t.sources.failedToLoad)
 79 |       toast.error(t.sources.failedToLoad)
 80 |     } finally {
 81 |       setLoading(false)
 82 |       setLoadingMore(false)
 83 |       loadingMoreRef.current = false
 84 |     }
 85 |   }, [sortBy, sortOrder, t.sources.failedToLoad])
 86 | 
 87 |   // Initial load and when sort changes
 88 |   useEffect(() => {
 89 |     fetchSources(true)
 90 |     // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
 91 |   }, [sortBy, sortOrder])
 92 | 
 93 |   useEffect(() => {
 94 |     // Focus the table when component mounts or sources change
 95 |     if (sources.length > 0 && tableRef.current) {
 96 |       tableRef.current.focus()
 97 |     }
 98 |   }, [sources])
 99 | 
100 |   useEffect(() => {
101 |     const handleKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
102 |       if (sources.length === 0) return
103 | 
104 |       switch (e.key) {
105 |         case 'ArrowDown':
106 |           e.preventDefault()
107 |           setSelectedIndex((prev) => {
108 |             const newIndex = Math.min(prev + 1, sources.length - 1)
109 |             // Scroll to keep selected row visible
110 |             setTimeout(() => scrollToSelectedRow(newIndex), 0)
111 |             return newIndex
112 |           })
113 |           break
114 |         case 'ArrowUp':
115 |           e.preventDefault()
116 |           setSelectedIndex((prev) => {
117 |             const newIndex = Math.max(prev - 1, 0)
118 |             // Scroll to keep selected row visible
119 |             setTimeout(() => scrollToSelectedRow(newIndex), 0)
120 |             return newIndex
121 |           })
122 |           break
123 |         case 'Enter':
124 |           e.preventDefault()
125 |           if (sources[selectedIndex]) {
126 |             router.push(`/sources/${sources[selectedIndex].id}`)
127 |           }
128 |           break
129 |         case 'Home':
130 |           e.preventDefault()
131 |           setSelectedIndex(0)
132 |           setTimeout(() => scrollToSelectedRow(0), 0)
133 |           break
134 |         case 'End':
135 |           e.preventDefault()
136 |           const lastIndex = sources.length - 1
137 |           setSelectedIndex(lastIndex)
138 |           setTimeout(() => scrollToSelectedRow(lastIndex), 0)
139 |           break
140 |       }
141 |     }
142 | 
143 |     window.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown)
144 |     return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown)
145 |   }, [sources, selectedIndex, router])
146 | 
147 |   const scrollToSelectedRow = (index: number) => {
148 |     const scrollContainer = scrollContainerRef.current
149 |     if (!scrollContainer) return
150 | 
151 |     // Find the selected row element
152 |     const rows = scrollContainer.querySelectorAll('tbody tr')
153 |     const selectedRow = rows[index] as HTMLElement
154 |     if (!selectedRow) return
155 | 
156 |     const containerRect = scrollContainer.getBoundingClientRect()
157 |     const rowRect = selectedRow.getBoundingClientRect()
158 | 
159 |     // Check if row is above visible area
160 |     if (rowRect.top < containerRect.top) {
161 |       selectedRow.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' })
162 |     }
163 |     // Check if row is below visible area
164 |     else if (rowRect.bottom > containerRect.bottom) {
165 |       selectedRow.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'end' })
166 |     }
167 |   }
168 | 
169 |   // Set up scroll listener after sources are loaded
170 |   useEffect(() => {
171 |     const scrollContainer = scrollContainerRef.current
172 |     if (!scrollContainer) return
173 | 
174 |     let scrollTimeout: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null
175 | 
176 |     const handleScroll = () => {
177 |       if (scrollTimeout) {
178 |         clearTimeout(scrollTimeout)
179 |       }
180 | 
181 |       scrollTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
182 |         if (!scrollContainerRef.current) return
183 | 
184 |         const { scrollTop, scrollHeight, clientHeight } = scrollContainerRef.current
185 |         const distanceFromBottom = scrollHeight - scrollTop - clientHeight
186 | 
187 |         // Load more when within 200px of the bottom
188 |         if (distanceFromBottom < 200 && !loadingMoreRef.current && hasMoreRef.current) {
189 |           fetchSources(false)
190 |         }
191 |       }, 100)
192 |     }
193 | 
194 |     scrollContainer.addEventListener('scroll', handleScroll)
195 |     handleScroll() // Check on mount
196 | 
197 |     return () => {
198 |       scrollContainer.removeEventListener('scroll', handleScroll)
199 |       if (scrollTimeout) {
200 |         clearTimeout(scrollTimeout)
201 |       }
202 |     }
203 |   }, [fetchSources, sources.length])
204 |

206 |     if (sortBy === field) {

208 |       setSortOrder(prev => prev === 'asc' ? 'desc' : 'asc')
209 |     } else {

263 |

266 |       <AppShell>

403 |                     </Button>
404 |                   </td>
405 |                 </tr>
406 |               ))}
407 |               {loadingMore && (
408 |                 <tr>
409 |                   <td colSpan={6} className="h-16 text-center">
410 |                     <div className="flex items-center justify-center">
411 |                       <LoadingSpinner />
412 |                       <span className="ml-2 text-muted-foreground">{t.sources.loadingMore}</span>
413 |                     </div>
414 |                   </td>
415 |                 </tr>
416 |               )}
417 |             </tbody>
418 |           </table>
419 |         </div>
420 |       </div>
421 | 
422 |       <ConfirmDialog
423 |         open={deleteDialog.open}
424 |         onOpenChange={(open) => setDeleteDialog({ open, source: deleteDialog.source })}
425 |         title={t.sources.delete}
426 |         description={t.sources.deleteConfirmWithTitle.replace('{title}', deleteDialog.source?.title || t.sources.untitledSource)}
427 |         confirmText={t.common.delete}
428 |         confirmVariant="destructive"
429 |         onConfirm={handleDeleteConfirm}
430 |       />
431 |     </AppShell>
432 |   )
433 | }

/docs/3-USER-GUIDE/creating-podcasts.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Creating Podcasts - Turn Research into Audio
  2 | 
  3 | Podcasts let you consume your research passively. This guide covers the complete workflow from setup to download.
  4 | 
  5 | ---
  6 | 
  7 | ## Quick-Start: Your First Podcast (5 Minutes)
  8 | 
  9 | ```
 10 | 1. Go to your notebook
 11 | 2. Click "Generate Podcast"
 12 | 3. Select sources to include
 13 | 4. Choose a speaker profile (or use default)
 14 | 5. Click "Generate"
 15 | 6. Wait 3-10 minutes (non-blocking)
 16 | 7. Download MP3 when ready
 17 | 8. Done!
 18 | ```
 19 | 
 20 | That's the minimum. Let's make it better.
 21 | 
 22 | ---
 23 | 
 24 | ## Step-by-Step: The Complete Workflow
 25 | 
 26 | ### Step 1: Prepare Your Notebook
 27 | 
 28 | ```
 29 | Before generating, make sure:
 30 | 
 31 | ✓ You have sources added
 32 |   (At least 1-2 sources)
 33 | 
 34 | ✓ Sources have been processed
 35 |   (Green "Ready" status)
 36 | 
 37 | ✓ Notes are organized
 38 |   (If you want notes included)
 39 | 
 40 | ✓ You know your message
 41 |   (What's the main story?)
 42 | 
 43 | Typical preparation: 5-10 minutes
 44 | ```
 45 | 
 46 | ### Step 2: Choose Content
 47 | 
 48 | ```
 49 | Click "Generate Podcast"
 50 | 
 51 | You'll see:
 52 | - List of all sources in notebook
 53 | - List of all notes
 54 | 
 55 | Select which to include:
 56 | ☑ Paper A (primary source)
 57 | ☑ Paper B (supporting source)
 58 | ☐ Old note (not relevant)
 59 | ✓ Analysis note (important)
 60 | 
 61 | What to include:
 62 | - Primary sources: Always include
 63 | - Supporting sources: Usually include
 64 | - Notes: Include your analysis/insights
 65 | - Everything: Can overload podcast
 66 | 
 67 | Recommended: 3-5 sources per podcast
 68 | ```
 69 | 
 70 | ### Step 3: Choose Episode Profile
 71 | 
 72 | An episode profile defines the structure and tone.
 73 | 
 74 | **Option A: Use Preset Profile**
 75 | 
 76 | ```
 77 | Open Notebook provides templates:
 78 | 
 79 | Academic Presentation (Monologue)
 80 | ├─ 1 speaker
 81 | ├─ Tone: Educational
 82 | └─ Format: Expert explaining topic
 83 | 
 84 | Expert Interview (2-speaker)
 85 | ├─ 2 speakers: Host + Expert
 86 | ├─ Tone: Q&A, conversational
 87 | └─ Format: Interview with expert
 88 | 
 89 | Debate Format (2-speaker)
 90 | ├─ 2 speakers: Pro vs. Con
 91 | ├─ Tone: Discussion, disagreement
 92 | └─ Format: Debate about the topic
 93 | 
 94 | Panel Discussion (3-4 speaker)
 95 | ├─ 3-4 speakers: Different perspectives
 96 | ├─ Tone: Thoughtful discussion
 97 | └─ Format: Each brings different expertise
 98 | 
 99 | Solo Explanation (Monologue)
100 | ├─ 1 speaker
101 | ├─ Tone: Conversational, friendly
102 | └─ Format: Personal explanation
103 | ```
104 | 
105 | **Pick based on your content:**
106 | - One main idea → Academic Presentation
107 | - You want to explain → Solo Explanation
108 | - Two competing views → Debate Format
109 | - Multiple perspectives → Panel Discussion
110 | - Want to explore → Expert Interview
111 | 
112 | ### Step 4: Customize Episode Profile (Optional)
113 | 
114 | If presets don't fit, customize:
115 | 
116 | ```
117 | Episode Profile
118 | ├─ Title: "AI Safety in 2026"
119 | ├─ Description: "Exploring current approaches"
120 | ├─ Length target: 20 minutes
121 | ├─ Tone: "Academic but accessible"
122 | ├─ Focus areas:
123 | │  ├─ Main approaches to alignment
124 | │  ├─ Pros and cons comparison
125 | │  └─ Open questions
126 | ├─ Audience: "Researchers new to field"
127 | └─ Format: "Debate between two perspectives"
128 | 
129 | How to set:
130 | 1. Click "Customize"
131 | 2. Edit each field
132 | 3. Click "Save Profile"
133 | 4. System uses your profile for outline generation
134 | ```
135 | 
136 | ### Step 5: Create or Select Speakers
137 | 
138 | Speakers are the "voice" of your podcast.
139 | 
140 | **Option A: Use Preset Speakers**
141 | 
142 | ```
143 | Open Notebook provides templates:
144 | 
145 | "Expert Alex"
146 | - Expertise: Deep knowledge
147 | - Personality: Rigorous, patient
148 | - TTS: OpenAI (clear voice)
149 | 
150 | "Curious Sam"
151 | - Expertise: Curious newcomer
152 | - Personality: Asks questions
153 | - TTS: Google (natural voice)
154 | 
155 | "Skeptic Jordan"
156 | - Expertise: Critical perspective
157 | - Personality: Challenges assumptions
158 | - TTS: ElevenLabs (warm voice)
159 | 
160 | For your first podcast: Use presets
161 | For custom podcast: Create your own
162 | ```
163 | 
164 | **Option B: Create Custom Speakers**
165 | 
166 | ```
167 | Click "Add Speaker"
168 | 
169 | Fill in:
170 | 
171 | Name: "Dr. Research Expert"
172 | 
173 | Expertise:
174 | "20 years in AI safety research,
175 |  deep knowledge of alignment approaches"
176 | 
177 | Personality:
178 | "Rigorous, academic style,
179 |  explains clearly, asks good questions"
180 | 
181 | Voice Configuration:
182 | - TTS Provider: OpenAI / Google / ElevenLabs / Local
183 | - Voice selection: Choose from available voices
184 | - Accent (optional): British / American / etc.
185 | 
186 | Example:
187 | Name: Dr. Research Expert
188 | Expertise: AI safety alignment research
189 | Personality: Rigorous, academic but accessible
190 | Voice: ElevenLabs - professional male voice
191 | ```
192 | 
193 | ### Step 6: Generate Podcast
194 | 
195 | ```
196 | 1. Review your setup:
197 |    Sources: ✓ Selected
198 |    Profile: ✓ Episode profile chosen
199 |    Speakers: ✓ Speakers configured
200 | 
201 | 2. Click "Generate Podcast"
202 | 
203 | 3. System begins:
204 |    - Analyzing your content
205 |    - Creating outline
206 |    - Writing dialogue
207 |    - Generating audio
208 |    - Mixing speakers
209 | 
210 | 4. Status shows progress:
211 |    20% Outline generation
212 |    40% Dialogue writing
213 |    60% Audio synthesis
214 |    80% Mixing
215 |    100% Complete
216 | 
217 | Processing time:
218 | - 5 minutes of content: 3-5 minutes
219 | - 15 minutes of content: 5-10 minutes
220 | - 30 minutes of content: 10-20 minutes
221 | ```
222 | 
223 | ### Step 7: Review and Download
224 | 
225 | ```
226 | When complete:
227 | 
228 | Preview:
229 | - Play audio sample
230 | - Review transcript
231 | - Check duration
232 | 
233 | Options:
234 | ✓ Download as MP3 - Save to computer
235 | ✓ Stream directly - Listen in browser
236 | ✓ Share link - Get shareable URL (if public)
237 | ✓ Regenerate - Try different speakers/profile
238 | 
239 | Download:
240 | 1. Click "Download as MP3"
241 | 2. Choose quality: 128kbps / 192kbps / 320kbps
242 | 3. Save file: podcast_[notebook]_[date].mp3
243 | 4. Listen!
244 | ```
245 | 
246 | ---
247 | 
248 | ## Understanding What Happens Behind the Scenes
249 | 
250 | ### The Generation Pipeline
251 | 
252 | ```
253 | Stage 1: CONTENT ANALYSIS (1 minute)
254 |   Your sources → What's the main story?
255 |                → Key themes?
256 |                → Debate points?
257 | 
258 | Stage 2: OUTLINE CREATION (2-3 minutes)
259 |   Themes → Episode structure
260 |         → Section breakdown
261 |         → Talking points
262 | 
263 | Stage 3: DIALOGUE WRITING (2-3 minutes)
264 |   Outline → Convert to natural dialogue
265 |          → Add speaker personalities
266 |          → Create flow and transitions
267 | 
268 | Stage 4: AUDIO SYNTHESIS (3-5 minutes per speaker)
269 |   Script + Speaker → Text-to-speech
270 |                   → Individual audio files
271 |                   → High quality audio
272 | 
273 | Stage 5: MIXING & MASTERING (1-2 minutes)
274 |   Multiple audio → Combine speakers
275 |                → Level audio
276 |                → Add polish
277 |                → Final MP3
278 | 
279 | Total: 10-20 minutes for typical podcast
280 | ```
281 | 
282 | ---
283 | 
284 | ## Text-to-Speech Providers
285 | 
286 | Different providers, different qualities.
287 | 
288 | ### OpenAI (Recommended)
289 | 
290 | ```
291 | Voices: 5 options (Alloy, Echo, Fable, Onyx, Shimmer)
292 | Quality: Good, natural sounding
293 | Speed: Fast
294 | Cost: ~$0.015 per minute
295 | Best for: General purpose, natural speech
296 | Example: "I have to say, the research shows..."
297 | ```
298 | 
299 | ### Google TTS
300 | 
301 | ```
302 | Voices: Many options, various accents
303 | Quality: Excellent, very natural
304 | Speed: Fast
305 | Cost: ~$0.004 per minute
306 | Best for: High quality output, accents
307 | Example: "The research demonstrates that..."
308 | ```
309 | 
310 | ### ElevenLabs
311 | 
312 | ```
313 | Voices: 100+ voices, highly customizable
314 | Quality: Exceptional, very expressive
315 | Speed: Slower (5-10 seconds per phrase)
316 | Cost: ~$0.10 per minute
317 | Best for: Premium quality, emotional range
318 | Example: [Can convey emotion and tone]
319 | ```
320 | 
321 | ### Local TTS (Free)
322 | 
323 | ```
324 | Voices: Limited, basic options
325 | Quality: Basic, robotic
326 | Speed: Depends on hardware (slow)
327 | Cost: Free (local processing)
328 | Best for: Privacy, testing, offline use
329 | Example: "The research shows..."
330 | Privacy: Everything stays on your computer
331 | ```
332 | 
333 | ### Which Provider to Choose?
334 | 
335 | ```
336 | For your first podcast: Google (quality/cost balance)
337 | For privacy-sensitive: Local TTS (free, private)
338 | For premium quality: ElevenLabs (best voices)
339 | For budget: Google (cheapest quality option)
340 | For speed: OpenAI (fast generation)
341 | ```
342 | 
343 | ---
344 | 
345 | ## Tips for Better Podcasts
346 | 
347 | ### Choose Right Profile
348 | 
349 | ```
350 | Single source analysis → Academic Presentation
351 |   "Explaining one paper to someone new"
352 | 
353 | Comparing two approaches → Debate Format
354 |   "Pros and cons of different methods"
355 | 
356 | Multiple sources + insights → Panel Discussion
357 |   "Different experts discussing topic"
358 | 
359 | Narrative exploration → Expert Interview
360 |   "Host interviewing research expert"
361 | 
362 | Personal take → Solo Explanation
363 |   "You explaining your analysis"
364 | ```
365 | 
366 | ### Create Good Speakers
367 | 
368 | ```
369 | Good Speaker:
370 | ✓ Clear expertise (know what they're talking about)
371 | ✓ Distinct personality (not generic)
372 | ✓ Good voice choice (matches personality)
373 | ✓ Realistic backstory (feels like real person)
374 | 
375 | Bad Speaker:
376 | ✗ Generic expertise ("good at research")
377 | ✗ No personality ("just reads")
378 | ✗ Mismatched voice (deep voice for young person)
379 | ✗ Contradicts personality (serious person uses casual voice)
380 | ```
381 | 
382 | ### Focus Content
383 | 
384 | ```
385 | Better: Podcast on ONE specific topic
386 |   "How transformers work" (15 minutes, focused)
387 | 
388 | Worse: Podcast on everything
389 |   "All of AI 2025" (2 hours, unfocused)
390 | 
391 | Guideline:
392 | - 5-10 minutes: One narrow topic
393 | - 15-20 minutes: One broad topic
394 | - 30+ minutes: Multiple related subtopics
395 | 
396 | Shorter is usually better for podcasts.
397 | ```
398 | 
399 | ### Optimize Source Selection
400 | 
401 | ```
402 | Too much content:
403 |   "Here are all 20 papers"
404 |   → Podcast becomes 2+ hours
405 |   → Unfocused
406 |   → Low quality
407 | 
408 | Right amount:
409 |   "Here are 3 key papers"
410 |   → Podcast is 15-20 minutes
411 |   → Focused
412 |   → High quality
413 | 
414 | Rule: 3-5 sources per podcast
415 |      Remove long background papers
416 |      Keep focused on main topic
417 | ```
418 | 
419 | ---
420 | 
421 | ## Quality Troubleshooting
422 | 
423 | ### Audio Sounds Robotic
424 | 
425 | **Problem**: TTS voice sounds unnatural
426 | 
427 | **Solutions**:
428 | ```
429 | 1. Switch provider: Try Google or ElevenLabs instead
430 | 2. Choose different voice: Some voices more natural
431 | 3. Shorter sentences: Very long sentences sound robotic
432 | 4. Adjust pacing: Ask for "natural, conversational pacing"
433 | ```
434 | 
435 | ### Audio Sounds Unclear
436 | 
437 | **Problem**: Hard to understand what's being said
438 | 
439 | **Solutions**:
440 | ```
441 | 1. Re-generate with different speaker
442 | 2. Try different TTS provider
443 | 3. Use speakers with clear accents
444 | 4. Lower background noise (if any)
445 | 5. Increase speech rate (if too slow)
446 | ```
447 | 
448 | ### Missing Content
449 | 
450 | **Problem**: Important information isn't in podcast
451 | 
452 | **Solutions**:
453 | ```
454 | 1. Include that source in content selection
455 | 2. Review generated outline (check before generating)
456 | 3. Regenerate with clearer profile instructions
457 | 4. Try different model (more thorough model)
458 | ```
459 | 
460 | ### Speakers Don't Match
461 | 
462 | **Problem**: Speakers sound like same person
463 | 
464 | **Solutions**:
465 | ```
466 | 1. Choose different TTS providers (OpenAI + Google)
467 | 2. Choose very different voice options
468 | 3. Increase personality differences in profile
469 | 4. Try different speaker count (2 vs 3 vs 4)
470 | ```
471 | 
472 | ### Generation Failed
473 | 
474 | **Problem**: "Podcast generation failed"
475 | 
476 | **Solutions**:
477 | ```
478 | 1. Check internet connection (especially TTS)
479 | 2. Try again (might be temporary issue)
480 | 3. Use local TTS (doesn't need internet)
481 | 4. Reduce source count (less to process)
482 | 5. Contact support if persistent
483 | ```
484 | 
485 | ---
486 | 
487 | ## Advanced: Multiple Podcasts from Same Research
488 | 
489 | You can generate different podcasts from one notebook:
490 | 
491 | ```
492 | Podcast 1: Overview
493 |   Profile: Academic Presentation
494 |   Sources: Papers A, B, C
495 |   Speakers: One expert
496 |   Length: 15 minutes
497 | 
498 | → Use for "What's this about?" understanding
499 | 
500 | Podcast 2: Deep Dive
501 |   Profile: Expert Interview
502 |   Sources: Paper A (Full) + B, C (Summary)
503 |   Speakers: Expert + Interviewer
504 |   Length: 30 minutes
505 | 
506 | → Use for detailed exploration
507 | 
508 | Podcast 3: Debate
509 |   Profile: Debate Format
510 |   Sources: Papers A vs B (different approaches)
511 |   Speakers: Pro-A speaker + Pro-B speaker
512 |   Length: 20 minutes
513 | 
514 | → Use for comparing approaches
515 | ```
516 | 
517 | Each tells the same story from different angles.
518 | 
519 | ---
520 | 
521 | ## Exporting and Sharing
522 | 
523 | ### Download MP3
524 | 
525 | ```
526 | 1. Generation complete
527 | 2. Click "Download"
528 | 3. Choose quality:
529 |    - 128 kbps: Smallest file, lower quality
530 |    - 192 kbps: Balanced (recommended)
531 |    - 320 kbps: Highest quality, largest file
532 | 4. Save to computer
533 | 5. Use in podcast app, upload to platform, etc.
534 | ```
535 | 
536 | ### Export Transcript
537 | 
538 | ```
539 | 1. Click "Export Transcript"
540 | 2. Get full dialogue as text
541 | 3. Useful for:
542 |    - Blog post content
543 |    - Show notes
544 |    - Searchable text version
545 |    - Accessibility
546 | ```
547 | 
548 | ### Share Link
549 | 
550 | ```
551 | If podcast is public:
552 | 1. Click "Share"
553 | 2. Get shareable link
554 | 3. Others can listen/download
555 | 4. Useful for:
556 |    - Sharing with team
557 |    - Public distribution
558 |    - Embedding on website
559 | ```
560 | 
561 | ### Publish to Podcast Platforms
562 | 
563 | ```
564 | If you want to distribute (future feature):
565 | 1. Download MP3
566 | 2. Upload to platform (Spotify, Apple Podcasts, etc.)
567 | 3. Add metadata (title, description, episode notes)
568 | 4. Your research becomes a published podcast!
569 | ```
570 | 
571 | ---
572 | 
573 | ## Best Practices
574 | 
575 | ### Before Generation
576 | - [ ] Sources are processed and ready
577 | - [ ] You've chosen content to include
578 | - [ ] You have a clear episode profile
579 | - [ ] Speakers are well-defined
580 | - [ ] Content is focused (3-5 sources max)
581 | 
582 | ### During Generation
583 | - Don't close the browser (use background processing)
584 | - Check back in 5-15 minutes
585 | - Review transcript when complete
586 | - Listen to sample before downloading
587 | 
588 | ### After Generation
589 | - [ ] Download MP3 to computer
590 | - [ ] Save in organized folder
591 | - [ ] Add metadata (title, description, date)
592 | - [ ] Test listening in podcast app
593 | - [ ] Share with colleagues for feedback
594 | 
595 | ---
596 | 
597 | ## Use Cases
598 | 
599 | ### Academic Researcher
600 | ```
601 | Podcast: Explaining your dissertation
602 | Speakers: You + colleague
603 | Content: Your papers + supporting research
604 | Use: Share with advisors, test explanations
605 | ```
606 | 
607 | ### Content Creator
608 | ```
609 | Podcast: Research-to-podcast article
610 | Speakers: Narrator + expert
611 | Content: Articles you've researched
612 | Use: Transform article into podcast version
613 | ```
614 | 
615 | ### Team Research
616 | ```
617 | Podcast: Weekly research updates
618 | Speakers: Multiple team members
619 | Content: This week's papers
620 | Use: Team updates, knowledge sharing
621 | ```
622 | 
623 | ### Learning/Teaching
624 | ```
625 | Podcast: Teaching material
626 | Speakers: Teacher + inquisitive student
627 | Content: Textbook + examples
628 | Use: Students learn while commuting
629 | ```
630 | 
631 | ---
632 | 
633 | ## Cost Breakdown Example
634 | 
635 | ### Generate 15-minute podcast with ElevenLabs
636 | 
637 | ```
638 | Generation (outline + dialogue):
639 |   No charge (included in service)
640 | 
641 | Text-to-speech:
642 |   2 speakers × 15 minutes = 30 minutes TTS
643 |   ElevenLabs: $0.10 per minute
644 |   Cost: 30 × $0.10 = $3.00
645 | 
646 | Processing:
647 |   Included (no additional cost)
648 | 
649 | Total: $3.00 per podcast
650 | 
651 | Cheaper options:
652 |   With Google TTS: ~$0.12
653 |   With OpenAI: ~$0.45
654 |   With Local TTS: ~$0.00
655 | ```
656 | 
657 | ---
658 | 
659 | ## Summary: Podcasts as Research Tool
660 | 
661 | Podcasts transform how you consume research:
662 | 
663 | ```
664 | Before: Reading papers takes time, focus
665 | After: Listen while commuting, exercising, doing chores
666 | 
667 | Before: Can't share complex research easily
668 | After: Share audio of your analysis
669 | 
670 | Before: Different consumption styles isolated
671 | After: Same research, multiple formats (read/listen)
672 | ```
673 | 
674 | Podcasts aren't just for entertainment—they're a tool for making research more accessible, shareable, and consumable.
675 | 
676 | That's why they're important for Open Notebook.
677 |

303 |     @model_validator(mode="after")

119 | function extractOutlineSegments(outline: unknown): OutlineSegment[] {
120 |   if (outline && typeof outline === 'object' && 'segments' in outline) {
121 |     const data = outline as OutlineData
122 |     if (Array.isArray(data.segments)) {
123 |       return data.segments
124 |     }
125 |   }
126 |   return []
127 | }

129 | function extractTranscriptEntries(transcript: unknown): TranscriptEntry[] {
130 |   if (transcript && typeof transcript === 'object' && 'transcript' in transcript) {
131 |     const data = transcript as TranscriptData
132 |     if (Array.isArray(data.transcript)) {
133 |       return data.transcript
134 |     }
135 |   }
136 |   return []
137 | }

139 | export function EpisodeCard({ episode, onDelete, deleting }: EpisodeCardProps) {
140 |   const { t, language } = useTranslation()
141 |   const [audioSrc, setAudioSrc] = useState<string | undefined>()
142 |   const [audioError, setAudioError] = useState<string | null>(null)
143 |   const [detailsOpen, setDetailsOpen] = useState(false)
144 | 
145 |   const outlineSegments = useMemo(() => extractOutlineSegments(episode.outline), [episode.outline])
146 |   const transcriptEntries = useMemo(() => extractTranscriptEntries(episode.transcript), [episode.transcript])
147 | 
148 |   useEffect(() => {
149 |     let revokeUrl: string | undefined
150 |     setAudioError(null)
151 | 
152 |     // If backend exposed a protected endpoint, fetch it with auth headers
153 |     const loadProtectedAudio = async () => {
154 |       // First resolve the audio URL
155 |       const directAudioUrl = await resolvePodcastAssetUrl(episode.audio_url ?? episode.audio_file)
156 | 
157 |       if (!directAudioUrl || !episode.audio_url) {
158 |         setAudioSrc(directAudioUrl)
159 |         return
160 |       }
161 | 
162 |       try {
163 |         let token: string | undefined
164 |         if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
165 |           const raw = window.localStorage.getItem('auth-storage')
166 |           if (raw) {
167 |             try {
168 |               const parsed = JSON.parse(raw)
169 |               token = parsed?.state?.token
170 |             } catch (error) {
171 |               console.error('Failed to parse auth storage', error)
172 |             }
173 |           }
174 |         }
175 | 
176 |         const headers: HeadersInit = {}
177 |         if (token) {
178 |           headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`
179 |         }
180 | 
181 |         const response = await fetch(directAudioUrl, { headers })
182 |         if (!response.ok) {
183 |           throw new Error(`Audio request failed with status ${response.status}`)
184 |         }
185 | 
186 |         const blob = await response.blob()
187 |         revokeUrl = URL.createObjectURL(blob)
188 |         setAudioSrc(revokeUrl)
189 |       } catch (error) {
190 |         console.error('Unable to load podcast audio', error)
191 |         setAudioError(t.podcasts.audioUnavailable)
192 |         setAudioSrc(undefined)
193 |       }
194 |     }
195 | 
196 |     void loadProtectedAudio()
197 | 
198 |     return () => {
199 |       if (revokeUrl) {
200 |         URL.revokeObjectURL(revokeUrl)
201 |       }
202 |     }
203 |   }, [episode.audio_url, episode.audio_file, t])
204 | 
205 |   const distance = episode.created
206 |     ? formatDistanceToNow(new Date(episode.created), {
207 |         addSuffix: true,
208 |         locale: getDateLocale(language),
209 |       })
210 |     : null
211 | 
212 |   const createdLabel = distance
213 |     ? t.podcasts.created.replace('{time}', distance)
214 |     : null
215 | 
216 |   const handleDelete = () => {
217 |     void onDelete(episode.id)
218 |   }
219 | 
220 |   return (
221 |     <Card className="shadow-sm">
222 |       <CardContent className="space-y-4 p-4">
223 |         <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 sm:flex-row sm:items-center sm:justify-between">
224 |           <div className="space-y-1">
225 |             <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
226 |               <h3 className="text-base font-semibold text-foreground">
227 |                 {episode.name}
228 |               </h3>
229 |               <StatusBadge status={episode.job_status} />
230 |             </div>
231 |             <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
232 |               {t.podcasts.profile}: {episode.episode_profile?.name || t.common.unknown}
233 |               {createdLabel ? ` • ${createdLabel}` : ''}
234 |             </p>
235 |           </div>
236 |           <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
237 |             <Dialog open={detailsOpen} onOpenChange={setDetailsOpen}>
238 |               <DialogTrigger asChild>
239 |                 <Button variant="outline" size="sm">
240 |                   <InfoIcon className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> {t.podcasts.details}
241 |                 </Button>
242 |               </DialogTrigger>
243 |               <DialogContent className="w-[min(90vw,720px)] max-h-[85vh] overflow-hidden">
244 |                 <DialogHeader>
245 |                   <DialogTitle>{episode.name}</DialogTitle>
246 |                   <DialogDescription>
247 |                     {episode.episode_profile?.name || t.common.unknown}
248 |                     {createdLabel ? ` • ${createdLabel}` : ''}
249 |                   </DialogDescription>
250 |                 </DialogHeader>
251 |                 <div className="space-y-4 overflow-hidden">
252 |                   {audioSrc ? (

254 |                   ) : audioError ? (

256 |                   ) : null}
257 | 
258 |                   <Tabs defaultValue="summary" className="h-[60vh] flex flex-col">
259 |                     <TabsList className="grid w-full grid-cols-3">
260 |                       <TabsTrigger value="summary">{t.podcasts.summaryTab}</TabsTrigger>
261 |                       <TabsTrigger value="outline">{t.podcasts.outlineTab}</TabsTrigger>

  6 | export interface ParsedReference {

  8 |   id: string
  9 |   originalText: string

 34 | /**
 35 |  * Parse source references from text
 36 |  *
 37 |  * Handles various formats:
 38 |  * - [source:abc123] → single reference
 39 |  * - [note:a], [note:b] → multiple references
 40 |  * - [note:a, note:b] → comma-separated references (edge case from LLM)
 41 |  * - Mixed: [source:x, note:y, source_insight:z]
 42 |  *
 43 |  * @param text - Text containing references
 44 |  * @returns Array of parsed references
 45 |  */
 46 | export function parseSourceReferences(text: string): ParsedReference[] {
 47 |   // Match pattern: (source_insight|note|source):alphanumeric_id
 48 |   // This handles references both inside and outside brackets
 49 |   const pattern = /(source_insight|note|source):([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)/g
 50 |   const matches: ParsedReference[] = []
 51 | 
 52 |   let match
 53 |   while ((match = pattern.exec(text)) !== null) {
 54 |     const type = match[1] as ReferenceType
 55 |     const id = match[2]
 56 | 
 57 |     matches.push({
 58 |       type,
 59 |       id,
 60 |       originalText: match[0],
 61 |       startIndex: match.index,
 62 |       endIndex: pattern.lastIndex
 63 |     })
 64 |   }
 65 | 
 66 |   return matches
 67 | }
 68 | 
 69 | /**
 70 |  * Convert source references in text to clickable React elements
 71 |  *
 72 |  * @param text - Text containing references
 73 |  * @param onReferenceClick - Callback when reference is clicked (type, id)
 74 |  * @returns React nodes with clickable reference buttons
 75 |  */
 76 | export function convertSourceReferences(
 77 |   text: string,
 78 |   onReferenceClick: (type: ReferenceType, id: string) => void
 79 | ): React.ReactNode {
 80 |   const matches = parseSourceReferences(text)
 81 | 
 82 |   if (matches.length === 0) return text
 83 | 
 84 |   const parts: React.ReactNode[] = []
 85 |   let lastIndex = 0
 86 | 
 87 |   matches.forEach((match, idx) => {
 88 |     // Check if there are brackets before the match
 89 |     const beforeMatch = text.substring(Math.max(0, match.startIndex - 2), match.startIndex)
 90 |     const hasDoubleBracketBefore = beforeMatch === '[['
 91 |     const hasSingleBracketBefore = beforeMatch.endsWith('[') && !hasDoubleBracketBefore
 92 | 
 93 |     // Determine where to start including text
 94 |     let textStartIndex = lastIndex
 95 |     if (hasDoubleBracketBefore && lastIndex === match.startIndex - 2) {
 96 |       textStartIndex = match.startIndex - 2
 97 |     } else if (hasSingleBracketBefore && lastIndex === match.startIndex - 1) {
 98 |       textStartIndex = match.startIndex - 1
 99 |     }
100 | 
101 |     // Add text before match (excluding brackets we'll include in the button)
102 |     if (textStartIndex < match.startIndex && lastIndex < textStartIndex) {
103 |       parts.push(text.substring(lastIndex, textStartIndex))
104 |     } else if (lastIndex < match.startIndex && !hasSingleBracketBefore && !hasDoubleBracketBefore) {
105 |       parts.push(text.substring(lastIndex, match.startIndex))
106 |     }
107 | 
108 |     // Check if there are brackets after the match
109 |     const afterMatch = text.substring(match.endIndex, Math.min(text.length, match.endIndex + 2))
110 |     const hasDoubleBracketAfter = afterMatch === ']]'
111 |     const hasSingleBracketAfter = afterMatch.startsWith(']') && !hasDoubleBracketAfter
112 | 
113 |     // Determine the display text with appropriate brackets
114 |     let displayText = match.originalText
115 |     if (hasDoubleBracketBefore && hasDoubleBracketAfter) {
116 |       displayText = `[[${match.originalText}]]`
117 |     } else if (hasSingleBracketBefore && hasSingleBracketAfter) {
118 |       displayText = `[${match.originalText}]`
119 |     } else {
120 |       displayText = match.originalText
121 |     }
122 | 
123 |     // Add clickable reference button
124 |     parts.push(
125 |       <button
126 |         key={`ref-${idx}-${match.type}-${match.id}`}
127 |         onClick={(e) => {
128 |           e.preventDefault()
129 |           e.stopPropagation()
130 |           onReferenceClick(match.type, match.id)
131 |         }}
132 |         className="text-primary hover:underline cursor-pointer inline font-medium"
133 |         type="button"
134 |       >
135 |         {displayText}
136 |       </button>
137 |     )
138 | 
139 |     // Update lastIndex to skip the closing brackets
140 |     if (hasDoubleBracketAfter) {
141 |       lastIndex = match.endIndex + 2
142 |     } else if (hasSingleBracketAfter) {
143 |       lastIndex = match.endIndex + 1
144 |     } else {
145 |       lastIndex = match.endIndex
146 |     }
147 |   })
148 | 
149 |   // Add remaining text
150 |   if (lastIndex < text.length) {
151 |     parts.push(text.substring(lastIndex))
152 |   }
153 | 
154 |   return <>{parts}</>
155 | }
156 | 
157 | /**
158 |  * Convert references in text to markdown links
159 |  * Use this BEFORE passing text to ReactMarkdown
160 |  *
161 |  * Handles complex patterns including:
162 |  * - Plain references: source:abc → [source:abc](#ref-source-abc)
163 |  * - Bracketed: [source:abc] → [[source:abc]](#ref-source-abc)
164 |  * - Double brackets: [[source:abc]] → [[[source:abc]]](#ref-source-abc)
165 |  * - With bold: [**source:abc**] → [**source:abc**](#ref-source-abc)
166 |  * - After commas: [source:a, note:b] → each converted separately
167 |  * - Nested: [**source:a**, [source_insight:b]] → both converted
168 |  *
169 |  * Uses greedy matching to catch all references regardless of surrounding context.
170 |  *
171 |  * @param text - Original text with references
172 |  * @returns Text with references converted to markdown links
173 |  */
174 | export function convertReferencesToMarkdownLinks(text: string): string {
175 |   // Step 1: Find ALL references using simple greedy pattern
176 |   const refPattern = /(source_insight|note|source):([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)/g
177 |   const references: Array<{ type: string; id: string; index: number; length: number }> = []
178 | 
179 |   let match
180 |   while ((match = refPattern.exec(text)) !== null) {
181 |     const type = match[1]
182 |     const id = match[2]
183 | 
184 |     // Validate the reference
185 |     const validTypes = ['source', 'source_insight', 'note']
186 |     if (!validTypes.includes(type) || !id || id.length === 0 || id.length > 100) {
187 |       continue // Skip invalid references
188 |     }
189 | 
190 |     references.push({
191 |       type,
192 |       id,
193 |       index: match.index,
194 |       length: match[0].length
195 |     })
196 |   }
197 | 
198 |   // If no references found, return original text
199 |   if (references.length === 0) return text
200 | 
201 |   // Step 2: Process references from end to start (to preserve indices)
202 |   let result = text
203 |   for (let i = references.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
204 |     const ref = references[i]
205 |     const refStart = ref.index
206 |     const refEnd = refStart + ref.length
207 |     const refText = `${ref.type}:${ref.id}`
208 | 
209 |     // Step 3: Analyze context around the reference
210 |     // Look back up to 50 chars for opening brackets/bold markers
211 |     const contextBefore = result.substring(Math.max(0, refStart - 50), refStart)
212 |     // Look ahead up to 50 chars for closing brackets/bold markers
213 |     const contextAfter = result.substring(refEnd, Math.min(result.length, refEnd + 50))
214 | 
215 |     // Determine display text by checking immediate surroundings
216 |     let displayText = refText
217 |     let replaceStart = refStart
218 |     let replaceEnd = refEnd
219 | 
220 |     // Check for double brackets [[ref]]
221 |     if (contextBefore.endsWith('[[') && contextAfter.startsWith(']]')) {
222 |       displayText = `[[${refText}]]`
223 |       replaceStart = refStart - 2
224 |       replaceEnd = refEnd + 2
225 |     }
226 |     // Check for single brackets [ref]
227 |     else if (contextBefore.endsWith('[') && contextAfter.startsWith(']')) {
228 |       displayText = `[${refText}]`
229 |       replaceStart = refStart - 1
230 |       replaceEnd = refEnd + 1
231 |     }
232 |     // Check for bold with brackets [**ref**]
233 |     else if (contextBefore.endsWith('[**') && contextAfter.startsWith('**]')) {
234 |       displayText = `[**${refText}**]`
235 |       replaceStart = refStart - 3
236 |       replaceEnd = refEnd + 3
237 |     }
238 |     // Check for just bold **ref**
239 |     else if (contextBefore.endsWith('**') && contextAfter.startsWith('**')) {
240 |       displayText = `**${refText}**`
241 |       replaceStart = refStart - 2
242 |       replaceEnd = refEnd + 2
243 |     }
244 |     // Plain reference (no brackets)
245 |     else {
246 |       displayText = refText
247 |     }
248 | 
249 |     // Step 4: Build the markdown link
250 |     const href = `#ref-${ref.type}-${ref.id}`
251 |     const markdownLink = `[${displayText}](${href})`
252 | 
253 |     // Step 5: Replace in the result string
254 |     result = result.substring(0, replaceStart) + markdownLink + result.substring(replaceEnd)
255 |   }
256 | 
257 |   return result
258 | }

260 | /**
261 |  * Create a custom link component for ReactMarkdown that handles reference links
262 |  *
263 |  * @param onReferenceClick - Callback for when a reference link is clicked
264 |  * @returns React component for rendering links
265 |  */
266 | export function createReferenceLinkComponent(
267 |   onReferenceClick: (type: ReferenceType, id: string) => void
268 | ) {
269 |   const ReferenceLinkComponent = ({
270 |     href,
271 |     children,
272 |     ...props
273 |   }: React.AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement> & {
274 |     href?: string
275 |     children?: React.ReactNode
276 |   }) => {
277 |     // Check if this is a reference link (starts with #ref-)
278 |     if (href?.startsWith('#ref-')) {
279 |       // Parse: #ref-source-abc123 → type=source, id=abc123
280 |       const parts = href.substring(5).split('-') // Remove '#ref-'
281 |       const type = parts[0] as ReferenceType
282 |       const id = parts.slice(1).join('-') // Rejoin in case ID has dashes
283 | 
284 |       // Select appropriate icon based on reference type
285 |       const IconComponent =
286 |         type === 'source' ? FileText :
287 |         type === 'source_insight' ? Lightbulb :
288 |         FileEdit // note
289 | 
290 |       return (
291 |         <button
292 |           onClick={(e) => {
293 |             e.preventDefault()
294 |             e.stopPropagation()
295 |             onReferenceClick(type, id)
296 |           }}
297 |           className="text-primary hover:underline cursor-pointer inline font-medium"
298 |           type="button"
299 |         >
300 |           <IconComponent className="h-3 w-3 inline mr-1" aria-hidden="true" />
301 |           {children}
302 |         </button>
303 |       )
304 |     }
305 | 
306 |     // Regular link - open in new tab
307 |     return (
308 |       <a href={href} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" {...props} className="text-primary hover:underline">
309 |         {children}
310 |       </a>
311 |     )
312 |   }
313 | 
314 |   ReferenceLinkComponent.displayName = 'ReferenceLinkComponent'
315 |   return ReferenceLinkComponent
316 | }

318 | /**
319 |  * Convert references in text to compact numbered format with reference list
320 |  *
321 |  * This function transforms verbose inline references like [source:abc123] into
322 |  * compact numbered citations [1], [2], etc., and appends a "References:" section
323 |  * at the bottom of the message with the full reference details.
324 |  *
325 |  * Algorithm:
326 |  * 1. Parse all references using parseSourceReferences()
327 |  * 2. Build a reference map to deduplicate and assign numbers
328 |  * 3. Replace inline references with numbered citations
329 |  * 4. Append reference list at the bottom
330 |  *
331 |  * @param text - Original text with references
332 |  * @param referencesLabel - Locales label for "References" title (default: "References")
333 |  * @returns Text with numbered citations and reference list appended
334 |  *
335 |  * @example
336 |  * Input: "See [source:abc] and [note:xyz]. Also [source:abc] again."
337 |  * Output: "See [1] and [2]. Also [1] again.\n\nReferences:\n[1] - [source:abc]\n[2] - [note:xyz]"
338 |  */
339 | export function convertReferencesToCompactMarkdown(text: string, referencesLabel: string = 'References'): string {
340 |   // Step 1: Parse all references using existing function
341 |   const references = parseSourceReferences(text)
342 | 
343 |   // Step 2: If no references found, return original text
344 |   if (references.length === 0) {
345 |     return text
346 |   }
347 | 
348 |   // Step 3: Build reference map (deduplicate and assign numbers)
349 |   const referenceMap = new Map<string, ReferenceData>()
350 |   let nextNumber = 1
351 | 
352 |   for (const reference of references) {
353 |     const key = `${reference.type}:${reference.id}`
354 |     if (!referenceMap.has(key)) {
355 |       referenceMap.set(key, {
356 |         number: nextNumber++,
357 |         type: reference.type,
358 |         id: reference.id
359 |       })
360 |     }
361 |   }
362 | 
363 |   // Step 4: Replace references with numbered citations (process from end to start)
364 |   let result = text
365 |   for (let i = references.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
366 |     const reference = references[i]
367 |     const key = `${reference.type}:${reference.id}`
368 |     const refData = referenceMap.get(key)!
369 |     const number = refData.number
370 | 
371 |     // Analyze context around the reference
372 |     const refStart = reference.startIndex
373 |     const refEnd = reference.endIndex
374 |     const contextBefore = result.substring(Math.max(0, refStart - 2), refStart)
375 |     const contextAfter = result.substring(refEnd, Math.min(result.length, refEnd + 2))
376 | 
377 |     // Determine what to replace based on bracket context
378 |     let replaceStart = refStart
379 |     let replaceEnd = refEnd
380 | 
381 |     // Check for double brackets [[ref]]
382 |     if (contextBefore === '[[' && contextAfter.startsWith(']]')) {
383 |       replaceStart = refStart - 2
384 |       replaceEnd = refEnd + 2
385 |     }
386 |     // Check for single brackets [ref]
387 |     else if (contextBefore.endsWith('[') && contextAfter.startsWith(']')) {
388 |       replaceStart = refStart - 1
389 |       replaceEnd = refEnd + 1
390 |     }
391 | 
392 |     // Build the numbered citation with full reference in href
393 |     const citationLink = `[${number}](#ref-${reference.type}-${reference.id})`
394 | 
395 |     // Replace in the result string
396 |     result = result.substring(0, replaceStart) + citationLink + result.substring(replaceEnd)
397 |   }
398 | 
399 |   // Step 5: Build reference list
400 |   const refListLines: string[] = [`\n\n${referencesLabel}:`]
401 | 
402 |   // Iterate through reference map in insertion order (Map preserves order)
403 |   for (const [, refData] of referenceMap) {
404 |     const refListItem = `[${refData.number}] - [${refData.type}:${refData.id}](#ref-${refData.type}-${refData.id})`
405 |     refListLines.push(refListItem)
406 |   }
407 | 
408 |   // Step 6: Append reference list to result
409 |   result = result + refListLines.join('\n')
410 | 
411 |   return result
412 | }

445 |       const parts = href.substring(5).split('-') // Remove '#ref-'
446 |       const type = parts[0] as ReferenceType
447 |       const id = parts.slice(1).join('-') // Rejoin in case ID has dashes
448 | 
449 |       return (
450 |         <button
451 |           onClick={(e) => {
452 |             e.preventDefault()
453 |             e.stopPropagation()

455 |           }}
456 |           className="text-primary hover:underline cursor-pointer inline font-medium"
457 |           type="button"
458 |         >
459 |           {children}
460 |         </button>
461 |       )
462 |     }
463 | 
464 |     // Regular link - open in new tab
465 |     return (

467 |         {children}
468 |       </a>
469 |     )
470 |   }
471 | 
472 |   CompactReferenceLinkComponent.displayName = 'CompactReferenceLinkComponent'
473 |   return CompactReferenceLinkComponent

 53 | interface EpisodeProfileFormDialogProps {

  1 | """
  2 | Generic ContextBuilder for the Open Notebook project.
  3 | 
  4 | This module provides a flexible ContextBuilder class that can handle any parameters
  5 | and build context from sources, notebooks, insights, and notes.
  6 | """
  7 | 
  8 | from __future__ import annotations
  9 | 
 10 | from dataclasses import dataclass
 11 | from typing import Any, Dict, List, Literal, Optional
 12 | 
 13 | from loguru import logger
 14 | 
 15 | from open_notebook.domain.notebook import Note, Notebook, Source
 16 | from open_notebook.exceptions import DatabaseOperationError, NotFoundError
 17 | 
 18 | from .token_utils import token_count
 19 | 
 20 | 
 21 | @dataclass
 22 | class ContextItem:
 23 |     """Represents a single item in the context."""
 24 | 
 25 |     id: str
 26 |     type: Literal["source", "note", "insight"]
 27 |     content: Dict[str, Any]
 28 |     priority: int = 0
 29 |     token_count: Optional[int] = None
 30 | 
 31 |     def __post_init__(self):
 32 |         """Calculate token count for the content if not provided."""
 33 |         if self.token_count is None:
 34 |             content_str = str(self.content)
 35 |             self.token_count = token_count(content_str)
 36 | 
 37 | 
 38 | @dataclass
 39 | class ContextConfig:
 40 |     """Configuration for context building."""
 41 | 
 42 |     sources: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None  # {source_id: inclusion_level}
 43 |     notes: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None  # {note_id: inclusion_level}
 44 |     include_insights: bool = True
 45 |     include_notes: bool = True
 46 |     max_tokens: Optional[int] = None
 47 |     priority_weights: Optional[Dict[str, int]] = None  # {type: weight}
 48 | 
 49 |     def __post_init__(self):
 50 |         """Initialize default values."""
 51 |         if self.sources is None:
 52 |             self.sources = {}
 53 |         if self.notes is None:
 54 |             self.notes = {}
 55 |         if self.priority_weights is None:
 56 |             self.priority_weights = {"source": 100, "note": 50, "insight": 75}
 57 | 
 58 | 
 59 | class ContextBuilder:
 60 |     """
 61 |     Generic ContextBuilder that can handle any parameters and build context
 62 |     from sources, notebooks, insights, and notes.
 63 |     """
 64 | 
 65 |     def __init__(self, **kwargs):
 66 |         """
 67 |         Initialize ContextBuilder with flexible parameters.
 68 | 
 69 |         Supported parameters:
 70 |         - source_id: str - Include specific source
 71 |         - notebook_id: str - Include notebook content
 72 |         - include_insights: bool - Include source insights
 73 |         - include_notes: bool - Include notes
 74 |         - context_config: ContextConfig - Custom context configuration
 75 |         - max_tokens: int - Maximum token limit
 76 |         - priority_order: List[str] - Custom priority order
 77 |         """
 78 |         # Store all parameters for flexibility
 79 |         self.params = kwargs
 80 | 
 81 |         # Extract commonly used parameters
 82 |         self.source_id: Optional[str] = kwargs.get("source_id")
 83 |         self.notebook_id: Optional[str] = kwargs.get("notebook_id")
 84 |         self.include_insights: bool = kwargs.get("include_insights", True)
 85 |         self.include_notes: bool = kwargs.get("include_notes", True)
 86 |         self.max_tokens: Optional[int] = kwargs.get("max_tokens")
 87 | 
 88 |         # Context configuration
 89 |         context_config_arg: Optional[ContextConfig] = kwargs.get("context_config")
 90 |         self.context_config: ContextConfig
 91 |         if context_config_arg is None:
 92 |             self.context_config = ContextConfig(
 93 |                 include_insights=self.include_insights,
 94 |                 include_notes=self.include_notes,
 95 |                 max_tokens=self.max_tokens,
 96 |             )
 97 |         else:
 98 |             self.context_config = context_config_arg
 99 | 
100 |         # Items storage
101 |         self.items: List[ContextItem] = []
102 | 
103 |         logger.debug(f"ContextBuilder initialized with params: {list(kwargs.keys())}")
104 | 
105 |     async def build(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
106 |         """
107 |         Build context based on provided parameters.
108 | 
109 |         Returns:
110 |             Dict containing the built context with metadata
111 |         """
112 |         try:
113 |             logger.info("Starting context building")
114 | 
115 |             # Clear existing items
116 |             self.items = []
117 | 
118 |             # Build context based on parameters
119 |             if self.source_id:
120 |                 await self._add_source_context(self.source_id)
121 | 
122 |             if self.notebook_id:
123 |                 await self._add_notebook_context(self.notebook_id)
124 | 
125 |             # Process any additional custom parameters
126 |             await self._process_custom_params()
127 | 
128 |             # Apply post-processing
129 |             self.remove_duplicates()
130 |             self.prioritize()
131 | 
132 |             if self.max_tokens:
133 |                 self.truncate_to_fit(self.max_tokens)
134 | 
135 |             # Format and return response
136 |             return self._format_response()
137 | 
138 |         except Exception as e:
139 |             logger.error(f"Error building context: {str(e)}")
140 |             raise DatabaseOperationError(f"Failed to build context: {str(e)}")
141 | 
142 |     async def _add_source_context(
143 |         self, source_id: str, inclusion_level: str = "insights"
144 |     ) -> None:
145 |         """
146 |         Add source and its insights to context.
147 | 
148 |         Args:
149 |             source_id: ID of the source
150 |             inclusion_level: "insights", "full content", or "not in"
151 |         """
152 |         if inclusion_level == "not in":
153 |             return
154 | 
155 |         try:
156 |             # Ensure source ID has table prefix
157 |             full_source_id = (
158 |                 source_id if source_id.startswith("source:") else f"source:{source_id}"
159 |             )
160 | 
161 |             source = await Source.get(full_source_id)
162 |             if not source:
163 |                 logger.warning(f"Source {source_id} not found")
164 |                 return
165 | 
166 |             # Determine context size based on inclusion level
167 |             context_size: Literal["short", "long"] = (
168 |                 "long" if "full content" in inclusion_level else "short"
169 |             )
170 |             source_context = await source.get_context(context_size=context_size)
171 | 
172 |             # Add source item
173 |             priority = (self.context_config.priority_weights or {}).get("source", 100)
174 |             item = ContextItem(
175 |                 id=source.id or "",
176 |                 type="source",
177 |                 content=source_context,
178 |                 priority=priority,
179 |             )
180 |             self.add_item(item)
181 | 
182 |             # Add insights if requested and available
183 |             if self.include_insights and "insights" in inclusion_level:
184 |                 insights = await source.get_insights()
185 |                 for insight in insights:
186 |                     insight_priority = (self.context_config.priority_weights or {}).get(
187 |                         "insight", 75
188 |                     )
189 |                     insight_item = ContextItem(
190 |                         id=insight.id or "",
191 |                         type="insight",
192 |                         content={
193 |                             "id": insight.id,
194 |                             "source_id": source.id,
195 |                             "insight_type": insight.insight_type,
196 |                             "content": insight.content,
197 |                         },
198 |                         priority=insight_priority,
199 |                     )
200 |                     self.add_item(insight_item)
201 | 
202 |             logger.debug(f"Added source context for {source_id}")
203 | 
204 |         except NotFoundError:
205 |             logger.warning(f"Source {source_id} not found")
206 |         except Exception as e:
207 |             logger.error(f"Error adding source context for {source_id}: {str(e)}")
208 |             raise
209 | 
210 |     async def _add_notebook_context(self, notebook_id: str) -> None:
211 |         """
212 |         Add notebook content based on context configuration.
213 | 
214 |         Args:
215 |             notebook_id: ID of the notebook
216 |         """
217 |         try:
218 |             notebook = await Notebook.get(notebook_id)
219 |             if not notebook:
220 |                 raise NotFoundError(f"Notebook {notebook_id} not found")
221 | 
222 |             # Process sources from context config or get all
223 |             config_sources = self.context_config.sources
224 |             if config_sources:
225 |                 for source_id, status in config_sources.items():
226 |                     await self._add_source_context(source_id, status)
227 |             else:
228 |                 # Default: get all sources with insights
229 |                 sources = await notebook.get_sources()
230 |                 for source in sources:
231 |                     if source.id:
232 |                         await self._add_source_context(source.id, "insights")
233 | 
234 |             # Process notes from context config or get all
235 |             if self.include_notes:
236 |                 config_notes = self.context_config.notes
237 |                 if config_notes:
238 |                     for note_id, status in config_notes.items():
239 |                         if "not in" not in status:
240 |                             await self._add_note_context(note_id, status)
241 |                 else:
242 |                     # Default: get all notes with short content
243 |                     notes = await notebook.get_notes()
244 |                     for note in notes:
245 |                         if note.id:
246 |                             await self._add_note_context(note.id, "full content")
247 | 
248 |             logger.debug(f"Added notebook context for {notebook_id}")
249 | 
250 |         except Exception as e:
251 |             logger.error(f"Error adding notebook context for {notebook_id}: {str(e)}")
252 |             raise
253 | 
254 |     async def _add_note_context(
255 |         self, note_id: str, inclusion_level: str = "full content"
256 |     ) -> None:
257 |         """
258 |         Add note to context.
259 | 
260 |         Args:
261 |             note_id: ID of the note
262 |             inclusion_level: "full content" or "not in"
263 |         """
264 |         if inclusion_level == "not in":
265 |             return
266 | 
267 |         try:
268 |             # Ensure note ID has table prefix
269 |             full_note_id = note_id if note_id.startswith("note:") else f"note:{note_id}"
270 | 
271 |             note = await Note.get(full_note_id)
272 |             if not note:
273 |                 logger.warning(f"Note {note_id} not found")
274 |                 return
275 | 
276 |             # Get note context
277 |             context_size: Literal["short", "long"] = (
278 |                 "long" if "full content" in inclusion_level else "short"
279 |             )
280 |             note_context = note.get_context(context_size=context_size)
281 | 
282 |             # Add note item
283 |             priority = (self.context_config.priority_weights or {}).get("note", 50)
284 |             item = ContextItem(
285 |                 id=note.id or "", type="note", content=note_context, priority=priority
286 |             )
287 |             self.add_item(item)
288 | 
289 |             logger.debug(f"Added note context for {note_id}")
290 | 
291 |         except NotFoundError:
292 |             logger.warning(f"Note {note_id} not found")
293 |         except Exception as e:
294 |             logger.error(f"Error adding note context for {note_id}: {str(e)}")
295 | 
296 |     async def _process_custom_params(self) -> None:
297 |         """Process any additional custom parameters."""
298 |         # Hook for future extensions - can be overridden in subclasses
299 |         # or used to process additional kwargs
300 |         for key, value in self.params.items():
301 |             if key.startswith("custom_"):
302 |                 logger.debug(f"Processing custom parameter: {key}={value}")
303 |                 # Custom processing logic can be added here
304 | 
305 |     def add_item(self, item: ContextItem) -> None:
306 |         """
307 |         Add a ContextItem to the builder.
308 | 
309 |         Args:
310 |             item: ContextItem to add
311 |         """
312 |         self.items.append(item)
313 |         logger.debug(f"Added item {item.id} with priority {item.priority}")
314 | 
315 |     def prioritize(self) -> None:
316 |         """Sort items by priority (higher priority first)."""
317 |         self.items.sort(key=lambda x: x.priority, reverse=True)
318 |         logger.debug(f"Prioritized {len(self.items)} items")
319 | 
320 |     def truncate_to_fit(self, max_tokens: int) -> None:
321 |         """
322 |         Remove items if total token count exceeds limit.
323 | 
324 |         Args:
325 |             max_tokens: Maximum allowed tokens
326 |         """
327 |         if not max_tokens:
328 |             return
329 | 
330 |         total_tokens = sum(item.token_count or 0 for item in self.items)
331 | 
332 |         if total_tokens <= max_tokens:
333 |             logger.debug(f"Token count {total_tokens} within limit {max_tokens}")
334 |             return
335 | 
336 |         logger.info(f"Truncating from {total_tokens} to {max_tokens} tokens")
337 | 
338 |         # Remove items from the end (lowest priority) until under limit
339 |         current_tokens = total_tokens
340 |         removed_count = 0
341 | 
342 |         while current_tokens > max_tokens and self.items:
343 |             removed_item = self.items.pop()
344 |             current_tokens -= removed_item.token_count or 0
345 |             removed_count += 1
346 | 
347 |         logger.info(
348 |             f"Removed {removed_count} items, final token count: {current_tokens}"
349 |         )
350 | 
351 |     def remove_duplicates(self) -> None:
352 |         """Remove duplicate items based on ID."""
353 |         seen_ids = set()
354 |         deduplicated_items = []
355 | 
356 |         for item in self.items:
357 |             if item.id not in seen_ids:
358 |                 deduplicated_items.append(item)
359 |                 seen_ids.add(item.id)
360 | 
361 |         removed_count = len(self.items) - len(deduplicated_items)
362 |         self.items = deduplicated_items
363 | 
364 |         if removed_count > 0:
365 |             logger.debug(f"Removed {removed_count} duplicate items")
366 | 
367 |     def _format_response(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
368 |         """
369 |         Format the final response.
370 | 
371 |         Returns:
372 |             Formatted context response
373 |         """
374 |         # Group items by type
375 |         sources = []
376 |         notes = []
377 |         insights = []
378 | 
379 |         for item in self.items:
380 |             if item.type == "source":
381 |                 sources.append(item.content)
382 |             elif item.type == "note":
383 |                 notes.append(item.content)
384 |             elif item.type == "insight":
385 |                 insights.append(item.content)
386 | 
387 |         # Calculate total tokens
388 |         total_tokens = sum(item.token_count or 0 for item in self.items)
389 | 
390 |         response = {
391 |             "sources": sources,
392 |             "notes": notes,
393 |             "insights": insights,
394 |             "total_tokens": total_tokens,
395 |             "total_items": len(self.items),
396 |             "metadata": {
397 |                 "source_count": len(sources),
398 |                 "note_count": len(notes),
399 |                 "insight_count": len(insights),
400 |                 "config": {
401 |                     "include_insights": self.include_insights,
402 |                     "include_notes": self.include_notes,
403 |                     "max_tokens": self.max_tokens,
404 |                 },
405 |             },
406 |         }
407 | 
408 |         # Add notebook_id if provided
409 |         if self.notebook_id:
410 |             response["notebook_id"] = self.notebook_id
411 | 
412 |         logger.info(
413 |             f"Built context with {len(self.items)} items, {total_tokens} tokens"
414 |         )
415 | 
416 |         return response
417 |

466 |     note_ids: Optional[List[str]] = None,
467 |     notebook_id: Optional[str] = None,
468 |     max_tokens: Optional[int] = None,
469 | ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
470 |     """
471 |     Build context from mixed sources.
472 | 
473 |     Args:
474 |         source_ids: List of source IDs
475 |         note_ids: List of note IDs
476 |         notebook_id: Optional notebook ID
477 |         max_tokens: Optional token limit
478 | 
479 |     Returns:
480 |         Built context
481 |     """
482 |     context_config = ContextConfig(max_tokens=max_tokens)
483 | 
484 |     # Configure sources
485 |     if source_ids:
486 |         context_config.sources = {sid: "insights" for sid in source_ids}
487 | 
488 |     # Configure notes
489 |     if note_ids:
490 |         context_config.notes = {nid: "full content" for nid in note_ids}
491 | 
492 |     builder = ContextBuilder(
493 |         notebook_id=notebook_id, context_config=context_config, max_tokens=max_tokens
494 |     )

329 | async def execute_chat(request: ExecuteChatRequest):
330 |     """Execute a chat request and get AI response."""
331 |     try:
332 |         # Verify session exists
333 |         # Ensure session_id has proper table prefix
334 |         full_session_id = (
335 |             request.session_id
336 |             if request.session_id.startswith("chat_session:")
337 |             else f"chat_session:{request.session_id}"
338 |         )
339 |         session = await ChatSession.get(full_session_id)
340 |         if not session:
341 |             raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Session not found")
342 | 
343 |         # Determine model override (per-request override takes precedence over session-level)
344 |         model_override = (
345 |             request.model_override
346 |             if request.model_override is not None
347 |             else getattr(session, "model_override", None)
348 |         )
349 | 
350 |         # Get current state
351 |         current_state = await chat_graph.aget_state(
352 |             config=RunnableConfig(configurable={"thread_id": full_session_id})
353 |         )
354 | 
355 |         # Prepare state for execution
356 |         state_values = current_state.values if current_state else {}
357 |         state_values["messages"] = state_values.get("messages", [])
358 |         state_values["context"] = request.context
359 |         state_values["model_override"] = model_override
360 | 
361 |         # Add user message to state
362 |         from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
363 | 
364 |         user_message = HumanMessage(content=request.message)
365 |         state_values["messages"].append(user_message)
366 | 
367 |         # Execute chat graph
368 |         result = chat_graph.invoke(
369 |             input=state_values,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
370 |             config=RunnableConfig(
371 |                 configurable={
372 |                     "thread_id": full_session_id,
373 |                     "model_id": model_override,
374 |                 }
375 |             ),
376 |         )
377 | 
378 |         # Update session timestamp
379 |         await session.save()
380 | 
381 |         # Convert messages to response format
382 |         messages: list[ChatMessage] = []
383 |         for msg in result.get("messages", []):
384 |             messages.append(
385 |                 ChatMessage(
386 |                     id=getattr(msg, "id", f"msg_{len(messages)}"),
387 |                     type=msg.type if hasattr(msg, "type") else "unknown",
388 |                     content=msg.content if hasattr(msg, "content") else str(msg),
389 |                     timestamp=None,
390 |                 )
391 |             )
392 | 
393 |         return ExecuteChatResponse(session_id=request.session_id, messages=messages)
394 |     except NotFoundError:
395 |         raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Session not found")
396 |     except Exception as e:
397 |         # Log detailed error with context for debugging
398 |         logger.error(
399 |             f"Error executing chat: {str(e)}\n"
400 |             f"  Session ID: {request.session_id}\n"
401 |             f"  Model override: {request.model_override}\n"
402 |             f"  Traceback:\n{traceback.format_exc()}"
403 |         )
404 |         raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Error executing chat: {str(e)}")

409 |     """Build context for a notebook based on context configuration."""
410 |     try:
411 |         # Verify notebook exists
412 |         notebook = await Notebook.get(request.notebook_id)
413 |         if not notebook:
414 |             raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Notebook not found")
415 | 
416 |         context_data: dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]] = {"sources": [], "notes": []}
417 |         total_content = ""
418 | 
419 |         # Process context configuration if provided
420 |         if request.context_config:
421 |             # Process sources
422 |             for source_id, status in request.context_config.get("sources", {}).items():
423 |                 if "not in" in status:
424 |                     continue
425 | 
426 |                 try:
427 |                     # Add table prefix if not present
428 |                     full_source_id = (
429 |                         source_id
430 |                         if source_id.startswith("source:")
431 |                         else f"source:{source_id}"
432 |                     )
433 | 
434 |                     try:
435 |                         source = await Source.get(full_source_id)
436 |                     except Exception:
437 |                         continue
438 | 
439 |                     if "insights" in status:
440 |                         source_context = await source.get_context(context_size="short")
441 |                         context_data["sources"].append(source_context)
442 |                         total_content += str(source_context)
443 |                     elif "full content" in status:
444 |                         source_context = await source.get_context(context_size="long")
445 |                         context_data["sources"].append(source_context)
446 |                         total_content += str(source_context)
447 |                 except Exception as e:
448 |                     logger.warning(f"Error processing source {source_id}: {str(e)}")
449 |                     continue
450 | 
451 |             # Process notes
452 |             for note_id, status in request.context_config.get("notes", {}).items():
453 |                 if "not in" in status:
454 |                     continue
455 | 
456 |                 try:
457 |                     # Add table prefix if not present
458 |                     full_note_id = (
459 |                         note_id if note_id.startswith("note:") else f"note:{note_id}"
460 |                     )
461 |                     note = await Note.get(full_note_id)
462 |                     if not note:
463 |                         continue
464 | 
465 |                     if "full content" in status:
466 |                         note_context = note.get_context(context_size="long")
467 |                         context_data["notes"].append(note_context)
468 |                         total_content += str(note_context)
469 |                 except Exception as e:
470 |                     logger.warning(f"Error processing note {note_id}: {str(e)}")
471 |                     continue
472 |         else:
473 |             # Default behavior - include all sources and notes with short context
474 |             sources = await notebook.get_sources()
475 |             for source in sources:
476 |                 try:
477 |                     source_context = await source.get_context(context_size="short")
478 |                     context_data["sources"].append(source_context)
479 |                     total_content += str(source_context)
480 |                 except Exception as e:
481 |                     logger.warning(f"Error processing source {source.id}: {str(e)}")
482 |                     continue
483 | 
484 |             notes = await notebook.get_notes()
485 |             for note in notes:
486 |                 try:
487 |                     note_context = note.get_context(context_size="short")
488 |                     context_data["notes"].append(note_context)
489 |                     total_content += str(note_context)
490 |                 except Exception as e:
491 |                     logger.warning(f"Error processing note {note.id}: {str(e)}")
492 |                     continue
493 | 
494 |         # Calculate character and token counts
495 |         char_count = len(total_content)
496 |         # Use token count utility if available
497 |         try:
498 |             from open_notebook.utils import token_count
499 | 
500 |             estimated_tokens = token_count(total_content) if total_content else 0
501 |         except ImportError:
502 |             # Fallback to simple estimation
503 |             estimated_tokens = char_count // 4
504 | 
505 |         return BuildContextResponse(
506 |             context=context_data, token_count=estimated_tokens, char_count=char_count
507 |         )
508 |     except HTTPException:
509 |         raise
510 |     except Exception as e:
511 |         logger.error(f"Error building context: {str(e)}")
512 |         raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Error building context: {str(e)}")
