/docs/7-DEVELOPMENT/architecture.md:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 | # Open Notebook Architecture
  2 | 
  3 | ## High-Level Overview
  4 | 
  5 | Open Notebook follows a three-tier architecture with clear separation of concerns:
  6 | 
  7 | ```
  8 | ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  9 | │  Your Browser                                           │
 10 | │  Access: http://your-server-ip:8502                     │
 11 | └────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘
 12 |                  │
 13 |                  ▼
 14 |          ┌───────────────┐
 15 |          │   Port 8502   │  ← Next.js Frontend (what you see)
 16 |          │   Frontend    │    Also proxies API requests internally!
 17 |          └───────┬───────┘
 18 |                  │ proxies /api/* requests ↓
 19 |                  ▼
 20 |          ┌───────────────┐
 21 |          │   Port 5055   │  ← FastAPI Backend (handles requests)
 22 |          │     API       │
 23 |          └───────┬───────┘
 24 |                  │
 25 |                  ▼
 26 |          ┌───────────────┐
 27 |          │   SurrealDB   │  ← Database (internal, auto-configured)
 28 |          │   (Port 8000) │
 29 |          └───────────────┘
 30 | ```
 31 | 
 32 | **Key Points:**
 33 | - **v1.1+**: Next.js automatically proxies `/api/*` requests to the backend, simplifying reverse proxy setup
 34 | - Your browser loads the frontend from port 8502
 35 | - The frontend needs to know where to find the API - when accessing remotely, set: `API_URL=http://your-server-ip:5055`
 36 | - **Behind reverse proxy?** You only need to proxy to port 8502 now! See [Reverse Proxy Configuration](../5-CONFIGURATION/reverse-proxy.md)
 37 | 
 38 | ---
 39 | 
 40 | ## Detailed Architecture
 41 | 
 42 | Open Notebook is built on a **three-tier, async-first architecture** designed for scalability, modularity, and multi-provider AI flexibility. The system separates concerns across frontend, API, and database layers, with LangGraph powering intelligent workflows and Esperanto enabling seamless integration with 8+ AI providers.
 43 | 
 44 | **Core Philosophy**:
 45 | - Privacy-first: Users control their data and AI provider choice
 46 | - Async/await throughout: Non-blocking operations for responsive UX
 47 | - Domain-Driven Design: Clear separation between domain models, repositories, and orchestrators
 48 | - Multi-provider flexibility: Swap AI providers without changing application code
 49 | - Self-hosted capable: All components deployable in isolated environments
 50 | 
 51 | ---
 52 | 
 53 | ## Three-Tier Architecture
 54 | 
 55 | ### Layer 1: Frontend (React/Next.js @ port 3000)
 56 | 
 57 | **Purpose**: Responsive, interactive user interface for research, notes, chat, and podcast management.
 58 | 
 59 | **Technology Stack**:
 60 | - **Framework**: Next.js 15 with React 19
 61 | - **Language**: TypeScript with strict type checking
 62 | - **State Management**: Zustand (lightweight store) + TanStack Query (server state)
 63 | - **Styling**: Tailwind CSS + Shadcn/ui component library
 64 | - **Build Tool**: Webpack (bundled via Next.js)
 65 | 
 66 | **Key Responsibilities**:
 67 | - Render notebooks, sources, notes, chat sessions, and podcasts
 68 | - Handle user interactions (create, read, update, delete operations)
 69 | - Manage complex UI state (modals, file uploads, real-time search)
 70 | - Stream responses from API (chat, podcast generation)
 71 | - Display embeddings, vector search results, and insights
 72 | 
 73 | **Communication Pattern**:
 74 | - All data fetched via REST API (async requests to port 5055)
 75 | - Configured base URL: `http://localhost:5055` (dev) or environment-specific (prod)
 76 | - TanStack Query handles caching, refetching, and data synchronization
 77 | - Zustand stores global state (user, notebooks, selected context)
 78 | - CORS enabled on API side for cross-origin requests
 79 | 
 80 | **Component Architecture**:
 81 | - `/src/app/`: Next.js App Router (pages, layouts)
 82 | - `/src/components/`: Reusable React components (buttons, forms, cards)
 83 | - `/src/hooks/`: Custom hooks (useNotebook, useChat, useSearch)
 84 | - `/src/lib/`: Utility functions, API clients, validators
 85 | - `/src/styles/`: Global CSS, Tailwind config
 86 | 
 87 | ---
 88 | 
 89 | ### Layer 2: API (FastAPI @ port 5055)
 90 | 
 91 | **Purpose**: RESTful backend exposing operations on notebooks, sources, notes, chat sessions, and AI models.
 92 | 
 93 | **Technology Stack**:
 94 | - **Framework**: FastAPI 0.104+ (async Python web framework)
 95 | - **Language**: Python 3.11+
 96 | - **Validation**: Pydantic v2 (request/response schemas)
 97 | - **Logging**: Loguru (structured JSON logging)
 98 | - **Testing**: Pytest (unit and integration tests)
 99 | 
100 | **Architecture**:
101 | ```
102 | FastAPI App (main.py)
103 |   ├── Routers (HTTP endpoints)
104 |   │   ├── routers/notebooks.py (CRUD operations)
105 |   │   ├── routers/sources.py (content ingestion, upload)
106 |   │   ├── routers/notes.py (note management)
107 |   │   ├── routers/chat.py (conversation sessions)
108 |   │   ├── routers/search.py (full-text + vector search)
109 |   │   ├── routers/transformations.py (custom transformations)
110 |   │   ├── routers/models.py (AI model configuration)
111 |   │   └── routers/*.py (11 additional routers)
112 |   │
113 |   ├── Services (business logic)
114 |   │   ├── *_service.py (orchestration, graph invocation)
115 |   │   ├── command_service.py (async job submission)
116 |   │   └── middleware (auth, logging)
117 |   │
118 |   ├── Models (Pydantic schemas)
119 |   │   └── models.py (validation, serialization)
120 |   │
121 |   └── Lifespan (startup/shutdown)
122 |       └── AsyncMigrationManager (database schema migrations)
123 | ```
124 | 
125 | **Key Responsibilities**:
126 | 1. **HTTP Interface**: Accept REST requests, validate, return JSON responses
127 | 2. **Business Logic**: Orchestrate domain models, repository operations, and workflows
128 | 3. **Async Job Queue**: Submit long-running tasks (podcast generation, source processing)
129 | 4. **Database Migrations**: Run schema updates on startup
130 | 5. **Error Handling**: Catch exceptions, return appropriate HTTP status codes
131 | 6. **Logging**: Track operations for debugging and monitoring
132 | 
133 | **Startup Flow**:
134 | 1. Load `.env` environment variables
135 | 2. Initialize FastAPI app with CORS + auth middleware
136 | 3. Run AsyncMigrationManager (creates/updates database schema)
137 | 4. Register all routers (20+ endpoints)
138 | 5. Server ready on port 5055
139 | 
140 | **Request-Response Cycle**:
141 | ```
142 | HTTP Request → Router → Service → Domain/Repository → SurrealDB
143 |                                        ↓
144 |                                   LangGraph (optional)
145 |                                        ↓
146 | Response ← Pydantic serialization ← Service ← Result
147 | ```
148 | 
149 | ---
150 | 
151 | ### Layer 3: Database (SurrealDB @ port 8000)
152 | 
153 | **Purpose**: Graph database with built-in vector embeddings, semantic search, and relationship management.
154 | 
155 | **Technology Stack**:
156 | - **Database**: SurrealDB (multi-model, ACID transactions)
157 | - **Query Language**: SurrealQL (SQL-like syntax with graph operations)
158 | - **Async Driver**: Async Rust client for Python
159 | - **Migrations**: Manual `.surql` files in `/migrations/` (auto-run on API startup)
160 | 
161 | **Core Tables**:
162 | 
163 | | Table | Purpose | Key Fields |
164 | |-------|---------|-----------|
165 | | `notebook` | Research project container | id, name, description, archived, created, updated |
166 | | `source` | Content item (PDF, URL, text) | id, title, full_text, topics, asset, created, updated |
167 | | `source_embedding` | Vector embeddings for semantic search | id, source, embedding, chunk_text, chunk_index |
168 | | `note` | User-created research notes | id, title, content, note_type (human/ai), created, updated |
169 | | `chat_session` | Conversation session | id, notebook_id, title, messages (JSON), created, updated |
170 | | `transformation` | Custom transformation rules | id, name, description, prompt, created, updated |
171 | | `source_insight` | Transformation output | id, source_id, insight_type, content, created, updated |
172 | | `reference` | Relationship: source → notebook | out (source), in (notebook) |
173 | | `artifact` | Relationship: note → notebook | out (note), in (notebook) |
174 | 
175 | **Relationship Graph**:
176 | ```
177 | Notebook
178 |   ↓ (referenced_by)
179 | Source
180 |   ├→ SourceEmbedding (1:many for chunked text)
181 |   ├→ SourceInsight (1:many for transformation outputs)
182 |   └→ Note (via artifact relationship)
183 |     ├→ Embedding (semantic search)
184 |     └→ Topics (tags)
185 | 
186 | ChatSession
187 |   ├→ Notebook
188 |   └→ Messages (stored as JSON array)
189 | ```
190 | 
191 | **Vector Search Capability**:
192 | - Embeddings stored natively in SurrealDB
193 | - Full-text search on `source.full_text` and `note.content`
194 | - Cosine similarity search on embedding vectors
195 | - Semantic search integrates with search endpoint
196 | 
197 | **Connection Management**:
198 | - Async connection pooling (configurable size)
199 | - Transaction support for multi-record operations
200 | - Schema auto-validation via migrations
201 | - Query timeout protection (prevent infinite queries)
202 | 
203 | ---
204 | 
205 | ## Tech Stack Rationale
206 | 
207 | ### Why Python + FastAPI?
208 | 
209 | **Python**:
210 | - Rich AI/ML ecosystem (LangChain, LangGraph, transformers, scikit-learn)
211 | - Rapid prototyping and deployment
212 | - Extensive async support (asyncio, async/await)
213 | - Strong type hints (Pydantic, mypy)
214 | 
215 | **FastAPI**:
216 | - Modern, async-first framework
217 | - Automatic OpenAPI documentation (Swagger UI @ /docs)
218 | - Built-in request validation (Pydantic)
219 | - Excellent performance (benchmarked near C/Rust speeds)
220 | - Easy middleware/dependency injection
221 | 
222 | ### Why Next.js + React + TypeScript?
223 | 
224 | **Next.js**:
225 | - Full-stack React framework with SSR/SSG
226 | - File-based routing (intuitive project structure)
227 | - Built-in API routes (optional backend co-location)
228 | - Optimized image/code splitting
229 | - Easy deployment (Vercel, Docker, self-hosted)
230 | 
231 | **React 19**:
232 | - Component-based UI (reusable, testable)
233 | - Excellent tooling and community
234 | - Client-side state management (Zustand)
235 | - Server-side state sync (TanStack Query)
236 | 
237 | **TypeScript**:
238 | - Type safety catches errors at compile time
239 | - Better IDE autocomplete and refactoring
240 | - Documentation via types (self-documenting code)
241 | - Easier onboarding for new contributors
242 | 
243 | ### Why SurrealDB?
244 | 
245 | **SurrealDB**:
246 | - Native graph database (relationships are first-class)
247 | - Built-in vector embeddings (no separate vector DB)
248 | - ACID transactions (data consistency)
249 | - Multi-model (relational + document + graph)
250 | - Full-text search + semantic search in one query
251 | - Self-hosted (unlike managed Pinecone/Weaviate)
252 | - Flexible SurrealQL (SQL-like syntax)
253 | 
254 | **Alternative Considered**: PostgreSQL + pgvector (more mature but separate extensions)
255 | 
256 | ### Why Esperanto for AI Providers?
257 | 
258 | **Esperanto Library**:
259 | - Unified interface to 8+ LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, Ollama, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI)
260 | - Multi-provider embeddings (OpenAI, Google, Ollama, Mistral, Voyage)
261 | - TTS/STT integration (OpenAI, Groq, ElevenLabs, Google)
262 | - Smart provider selection (fallback logic, cost optimization)
263 | - Per-request model override support
264 | - Local Ollama support (completely self-hosted option)
265 | 
266 | **Alternative Considered**: LangChain's provider abstraction (more verbose, less flexible)
267 | 
268 | ---
269 | 
270 | ## LangGraph Workflows
271 | 
272 | LangGraph is a state machine library that orchestrates multi-step AI workflows. Open Notebook uses five core workflows:
273 | 
274 | ### 1. **Source Processing Workflow** (`open_notebook/graphs/source.py`)
275 | 
276 | **Purpose**: Ingest content (PDF, URL, text) and prepare for search/insights.
277 | 
278 | **Flow**:
279 | ```
280 | Input (file/URL/text)
281 |   ↓
282 | Extract Content (content-core library)
283 |   ↓
284 | Clean & tokenize text
285 |   ↓
286 | Generate Embeddings (Esperanto)
287 |   ↓
288 | Create SourceEmbedding records (chunked + indexed)
289 |   ↓
290 | Extract Topics (LLM summarization)
291 |   ↓
292 | Save to SurrealDB
293 |   ↓
294 | Output (Source record with embeddings)
295 | ```
296 | 
297 | **State Dict**:
298 | ```python
299 | {
300 |   "content_state": {"file_path" | "url" | "content": str},
301 |   "source_id": str,
302 |   "full_text": str,
303 |   "embeddings": List[Dict],
304 |   "topics": List[str],
305 |   "notebook_ids": List[str],
306 | }
307 | ```
308 | 
309 | **Invoked By**: Sources API (`POST /sources`)
310 | 
311 | ---
312 | 
313 | ### 2. **Chat Workflow** (`open_notebook/graphs/chat.py`)
314 | 
315 | **Purpose**: Conduct multi-turn conversations with AI model, referencing notebook context.
316 | 
317 | **Flow**:
318 | ```
319 | User Message
320 |   ↓
321 | Build Context (selected sources/notes)
322 |   ↓
323 | Add Message to Session
324 |   ↓
325 | Create Chat Prompt (system + history + context)
326 |   ↓
327 | Call LLM (via Esperanto)
328 |   ↓
329 | Stream Response
330 |   ↓
331 | Save AI Message to ChatSession
332 |   ↓
333 | Output (complete message)
334 | ```
335 | 
336 | **State Dict**:
337 | ```python
338 | {
339 |   "session_id": str,
340 |   "messages": List[BaseMessage],
341 |   "context": Dict[str, Any],  # sources, notes, snippets
342 |   "response": str,
343 |   "model_override": Optional[str],
344 | }
345 | ```
346 | 
347 | **Key Features**:
348 | - Message history persisted in SurrealDB (SqliteSaver checkpoint)
349 | - Context building via `build_context_for_chat()` utility
350 | - Token counting to prevent overflow
351 | - Per-message model override support
352 | 
353 | **Invoked By**: Chat API (`POST /chat/execute`)
354 | 
355 | ---
356 | 
357 | ### 3. **Ask Workflow** (`open_notebook/graphs/ask.py`)
358 | 
359 | **Purpose**: Answer user questions by searching sources and synthesizing responses.
360 | 
361 | **Flow**:
362 | ```
363 | User Question
364 |   ↓
365 | Plan Search Strategy (LLM generates searches)
366 |   ↓
367 | Execute Searches (vector + text search)
368 |   ↓
369 | Score & Rank Results
370 |   ↓
371 | Provide Answers (LLM synthesizes from results)
372 |   ↓
373 | Stream Responses
374 |   ↓
375 | Output (final answer)
376 | ```
377 | 
378 | **State Dict**:
379 | ```python
380 | {
381 |   "question": str,
382 |   "strategy": SearchStrategy,
383 |   "answers": List[str],
384 |   "final_answer": str,
385 |   "sources_used": List[Source],
386 | }
387 | ```
388 | 
389 | **Streaming**: Uses `astream()` to emit updates in real-time (strategy → answers → final answer)
390 | 
391 | **Invoked By**: Search API (`POST /ask` with streaming)
392 | 
393 | ---
394 | 
395 | ### 4. **Transformation Workflow** (`open_notebook/graphs/transformation.py`)
396 | 
397 | **Purpose**: Apply custom transformations to sources (extract summaries, key points, etc).
398 | 
399 | **Flow**:
400 | ```
401 | Source + Transformation Rule
402 |   ↓
403 | Generate Prompt (Jinja2 template)
404 |   ↓
405 | Call LLM
406 |   ↓
407 | Parse Output
408 |   ↓
409 | Create SourceInsight record
410 |   ↓
411 | Output (insight with type + content)
412 | ```
413 | 
414 | **Example Transformations**:
415 | - Summary (5-sentence overview)
416 | - Key Points (bulleted list)
417 | - Quotes (notable excerpts)
418 | - Q&A (generated questions and answers)
419 | 
420 | **Invoked By**: Sources API (`POST /sources/{id}/insights`)
421 | 
422 | ---
423 | 
424 | ### 5. **Prompt Workflow** (`open_notebook/graphs/prompt.py`)
425 | 
426 | **Purpose**: Generic LLM task execution (e.g., auto-generate note titles, analyze content).
427 | 
428 | **Flow**:
429 | ```
430 | Input Text + Prompt
431 |   ↓
432 | Call LLM (simple request-response)
433 |   ↓
434 | Output (completion)
435 | ```
436 | 
437 | **Used For**: Note title generation, content analysis, etc.
438 | 
439 | ---
440 | 
441 | ## AI Provider Integration Pattern
442 | 
443 | ### ModelManager: Centralized Factory
444 | 
445 | Located in `open_notebook/ai/models.py`, ModelManager handles:
446 | 
447 | 1. **Provider Detection**: Check environment variables for available providers
448 | 2. **Model Selection**: Choose best model based on context size and task
449 | 3. **Fallback Logic**: If primary provider unavailable, try backup
450 | 4. **Cost Optimization**: Prefer cheaper models for simple tasks
451 | 5. **Token Calculation**: Estimate cost before LLM call
452 | 
453 | **Usage**:
454 | ```python
455 | from open_notebook.ai.provision import provision_langchain_model
456 | 
457 | # Get best LLM for context size
458 | model = await provision_langchain_model(
459 |     task="chat",  # or "search", "extraction"
460 |     model_override="anthropic/claude-opus-4",  # optional
461 |     context_size=8000,  # estimated tokens
462 | )
463 | 
464 | # Invoke model
465 | response = await model.ainvoke({"input": prompt})
466 | ```
467 | 
468 | ### Multi-Provider Support
469 | 
470 | **LLM Providers**:
471 | - OpenAI (gpt-4, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-3.5-turbo)
472 | - Anthropic (claude-opus, claude-sonnet, claude-haiku)
473 | - Google (gemini-pro, gemini-1.5)
474 | - Groq (mixtral, llama-2)
475 | - Ollama (local models)
476 | - Mistral (mistral-large, mistral-medium)
477 | - DeepSeek (deepseek-chat)
478 | - xAI (grok)
479 | 
480 | **Embedding Providers**:
481 | - OpenAI (text-embedding-3-large, text-embedding-3-small)
482 | - Google (embedding-001)
483 | - Ollama (local embeddings)
484 | - Mistral (mistral-embed)
485 | - Voyage (voyage-large-2)
486 | 
487 | **TTS Providers**:
488 | - OpenAI (tts-1, tts-1-hd)
489 | - Groq (no TTS, fallback to OpenAI)
490 | - ElevenLabs (multilingual voices)
491 | - Google TTS (text-to-speech)
492 | 
493 | ### Per-Request Override
494 | 
495 | Every LangGraph invocation accepts a `config` parameter to override models:
496 | 
497 | ```python
498 | result = await graph.ainvoke(
499 |     input={...},
500 |     config={
501 |         "configurable": {
502 |             "model_override": "anthropic/claude-opus-4"  # Use Claude instead
503 |         }
504 |     }
505 | )
506 | ```
507 | 
508 | ---
509 | 
510 | ## Design Patterns
511 | 
512 | ### 1. **Domain-Driven Design (DDD)**
513 | 
514 | **Domain Objects** (`open_notebook/domain/`):
515 | - `Notebook`: Research container with relationships to sources/notes
516 | - `Source`: Content item (PDF, URL, text) with embeddings
517 | - `Note`: User-created or AI-generated research note
518 | - `ChatSession`: Conversation history for a notebook
519 | - `Transformation`: Custom rule for extracting insights
520 | 
521 | **Repository Pattern**:
522 | - Database access layer (`open_notebook/database/repository.py`)
523 | - `repo_query()`: Execute SurrealQL queries
524 | - `repo_create()`: Insert records
525 | - `repo_upsert()`: Merge records
526 | - `repo_delete()`: Remove records
527 | 
528 | **Entity Methods**:
529 | ```python
530 | # Domain methods (business logic)
531 | notebook = await Notebook.get(id)
532 | await notebook.save()
533 | notes = await notebook.get_notes()
534 | sources = await notebook.get_sources()
535 | ```
536 | 
537 | ### 2. **Async-First Architecture**
538 | 
539 | **All I/O is async**:
540 | - Database queries: `await repo_query(...)`
541 | - LLM calls: `await model.ainvoke(...)`
542 | - File I/O: `await upload_file.read()`
543 | - Graph invocations: `await graph.ainvoke(...)`
544 | 
545 | **Benefits**:
546 | - Non-blocking request handling (FastAPI serves multiple concurrent requests)
547 | - Better resource utilization (I/O waiting doesn't block CPU)
548 | - Natural fit for Python async/await syntax
549 | 
550 | **Example**:
551 | ```python
552 | @router.post("/sources")
553 | async def create_source(source_data: SourceCreate):
554 |     # All operations are non-blocking
555 |     source = Source(title=source_data.title)
556 |     await source.save()  # async database operation
557 |     await graph.ainvoke({...})  # async LangGraph invocation
558 |     return SourceResponse(...)
559 | ```
560 | 
561 | ### 3. **Service Pattern**
562 | 
563 | Services orchestrate domain objects, repositories, and workflows:
564 | 
565 | ```python
566 | # api/notebook_service.py
567 | class NotebookService:
568 |     async def get_notebook_with_stats(notebook_id: str):
569 |         notebook = await Notebook.get(notebook_id)
570 |         sources = await notebook.get_sources()
571 |         notes = await notebook.get_notes()
572 |         return {
573 |             "notebook": notebook,
574 |             "source_count": len(sources),
575 |             "note_count": len(notes),
576 |         }
577 | ```
578 | 
579 | **Responsibilities**:
580 | - Validate inputs (Pydantic)
581 | - Orchestrate database operations
582 | - Invoke workflows (LangGraph graphs)
583 | - Handle errors and return appropriate status codes
584 | - Log operations
585 | 
586 | ### 4. **Streaming Pattern**
587 | 
588 | For long-running operations (ask workflow, podcast generation), stream results as Server-Sent Events:
589 | 
590 | ```python
591 | @router.post("/ask", response_class=StreamingResponse)
592 | async def ask(request: AskRequest):
593 |     async def stream_response():
594 |         async for chunk in ask_graph.astream(input={...}):
595 |             yield f"data: {json.dumps(chunk)}\n\n"
596 |     return StreamingResponse(stream_response(), media_type="text/event-stream")
597 | ```
598 | 
599 | ### 5. **Job Queue Pattern**
600 | 
601 | For async background tasks (source processing), use Surreal-Commands job queue:
602 | 
603 | ```python
604 | # Submit job
605 | command_id = await CommandService.submit_command_job(
606 |     app="open_notebook",
607 |     command="process_source",
608 |     input={...}
609 | )
610 | 
611 | # Poll status
612 | status = await source.get_status()
613 | ```
614 | 
615 | ---
616 | 
617 | ## Service Communication Patterns
618 | 
619 | ### Frontend → API
620 | 
621 | 1. **REST requests** (HTTP GET/POST/PUT/DELETE)
622 | 2. **JSON request/response bodies**
623 | 3. **Standard HTTP status codes** (200, 400, 404, 500)
624 | 4. **Optional streaming** (Server-Sent Events for long operations)
625 | 
626 | **Example**:
627 | ```typescript
628 | // Frontend
629 | const response = await fetch("http://localhost:5055/sources", {
630 |   method: "POST",
631 |   body: formData,  // multipart/form-data for file upload
632 | });
633 | const source = await response.json();
634 | ```
635 | 
636 | ### API → SurrealDB
637 | 
638 | 1. **SurrealQL queries** (similar to SQL)
639 | 2. **Async driver** with connection pooling
640 | 3. **Type-safe record IDs** (record_id syntax)
641 | 4. **Transaction support** for multi-step operations
642 | 
643 | **Example**:
644 | ```python
645 | # API
646 | result = await repo_query(
647 |     "SELECT * FROM source WHERE notebook = $notebook_id",
648 |     {"notebook_id": ensure_record_id(notebook_id)}
649 | )
650 | ```
651 | 
652 | ### API → AI Providers (via Esperanto)
653 | 
654 | 1. **Esperanto unified interface**
655 | 2. **Per-request provider override**
656 | 3. **Automatic fallback on failure**
657 | 4. **Token counting and cost estimation**
658 | 
659 | **Example**:
660 | ```python
661 | # API
662 | model = await provision_langchain_model(task="chat")
663 | response = await model.ainvoke({"input": prompt})
664 | ```
665 | 
666 | ### API → Job Queue (Surreal-Commands)
667 | 
668 | 1. **Async job submission**
669 | 2. **Fire-and-forget pattern**
670 | 3. **Status polling via `/commands/{id}` endpoint**
671 | 4. **Job completion callbacks (optional)**
672 | 
673 | **Example**:
674 | ```python
675 | # Submit async source processing
676 | command_id = await CommandService.submit_command_job(...)
677 | 
678 | # Client polls status
679 | response = await fetch(f"http://localhost:5055/commands/{command_id}")
680 | status = await response.json()  # returns { status: "running|queued|completed|failed" }
681 | ```
682 | 
683 | ---
684 | 
685 | ## Database Schema Overview
686 | 
687 | ### Core Schema Structure
688 | 
689 | **Tables** (20+):
690 | - Notebooks (with soft-delete via `archived` flag)
691 | - Sources (content + metadata)
692 | - SourceEmbeddings (vector chunks)
693 | - Notes (user-created + AI-generated)
694 | - ChatSessions (conversation history)
695 | - Transformations (custom rules)
696 | - SourceInsights (transformation outputs)
697 | - Relationships (notebook→source, notebook→note)
698 | 
699 | **Migrations**:
700 | - Automatic on API startup
701 | - Located in `/migrations/` directory
702 | - Numbered sequentially (001_*.surql, 002_*.surql, etc)
703 | - Tracked in `_sbl_migrations` table
704 | - Rollback via `_down.surql` files (manual)
705 | 
706 | ### Relationship Model
707 | 
708 | **Graph Relationships**:
709 | ```
710 | Notebook
711 |   ← reference ← Source (many:many)
712 |   ← artifact ← Note (many:many)
713 | 
714 | Source
715 |   → source_embedding (one:many)
716 |   → source_insight (one:many)
717 |   → embedding (via source_embedding)
718 | 
719 | ChatSession
720 |   → messages (JSON array in database)
721 |   → notebook_id (reference to Notebook)
722 | 
723 | Transformation
724 |   → source_insight (one:many)
725 | ```
726 | 
727 | **Query Example** (get all sources in a notebook with counts):
728 | ```sql
729 | SELECT id, title,
730 |   count(<-reference.in) as note_count,
731 |   count(<-embedding.in) as embedded_chunks
732 | FROM source
733 | WHERE notebook = $notebook_id
734 | ORDER BY updated DESC
735 | ```
736 | 
737 | ---
738 | 
739 | ## Key Architectural Decisions
740 | 
741 | ### 1. **Async Throughout**
742 | 
743 | All I/O operations are non-blocking to maximize concurrency and responsiveness.
744 | 
745 | **Trade-off**: Slightly more complex code (async/await syntax) vs. high throughput.
746 | 
747 | ### 2. **Multi-Provider from Day 1**
748 | 
749 | Built-in support for 8+ AI providers prevents vendor lock-in.
750 | 
751 | **Trade-off**: Added complexity in ModelManager vs. flexibility and cost optimization.
752 | 
753 | ### 3. **Graph-First Workflows**
754 | 
755 | LangGraph state machines for complex multi-step operations (ask, chat, transformations).
756 | 
757 | **Trade-off**: Steeper learning curve vs. maintainable, debuggable workflows.
758 | 
759 | ### 4. **Self-Hosted Database**
760 | 
761 | SurrealDB for graph + vector search in one system (no external dependencies).
762 | 
763 | **Trade-off**: Operational responsibility vs. simplified architecture and cost savings.
764 | 
765 | ### 5. **Job Queue for Long-Running Tasks**
766 | 
767 | Async job submission (source processing, podcast generation) prevents request timeouts.
768 | 
769 | **Trade-off**: Eventual consistency vs. responsive user experience.
770 | 
771 | ---
772 | 
773 | ## Important Quirks & Gotchas
774 | 
775 | ### API Startup
776 | 
777 | - **Migrations run automatically** on every startup; check logs for errors
778 | - **SurrealDB must be running** before starting API (connection test in lifespan)
779 | - **Auth middleware is basic** (password-only); upgrade to OAuth/JWT for production
780 | 
781 | ### Database Operations
782 | 
783 | - **Record IDs use SurrealDB syntax** (table:id format, e.g., "notebook:abc123")
784 | - **ensure_record_id()** helper prevents malformed IDs
785 | - **Soft deletes** via `archived` field (data not removed, just marked inactive)
786 | - **Timestamps in ISO 8601 format** (created, updated fields)
787 | 
788 | ### LangGraph Workflows
789 | 
790 | - **State persistence** via SqliteSaver in `/data/sqlite-db/`
791 | - **No built-in timeout**; long workflows may block requests (use streaming for UX)
792 | - **Model fallback** automatic if primary provider unavailable
793 | - **Checkpoint IDs** must be unique per session (avoid collisions)
794 | 
795 | ### AI Provider Integration
796 | 
797 | - **Esperanto library** handles all provider APIs (no direct API calls)
798 | - **Per-request override** via RunnableConfig (temporary, not persistent)
799 | - **Cost estimation** via token counting (not 100% accurate, use for guidance)
800 | - **Fallback logic** tries cheaper models if primary fails
801 | 
802 | ### File Uploads
803 | 
804 | - **Stored in `/data/uploads/`** directory (not database)
805 | - **Unique filename generation** prevents overwrites (counter suffix)
806 | - **Content-core library** extracts text from 50+ file types
807 | - **Large files** may block API briefly (sync content extraction)
808 | 
809 | ---
810 | 
811 | ## Performance Considerations
812 | 
813 | ### Optimization Strategies
814 | 
815 | 1. **Connection Pooling**: SurrealDB async driver with configurable pool size
816 | 2. **Query Caching**: TanStack Query on frontend (client-side caching)
817 | 3. **Embedding Reuse**: Vector search uses pre-computed embeddings
818 | 4. **Chunking**: Sources split into chunks for better search relevance
819 | 5. **Async Operations**: Non-blocking I/O for high concurrency
820 | 6. **Lazy Loading**: Frontend requests only needed data (pagination)
821 | 
822 | ### Bottlenecks
823 | 
824 | 1. **LLM Calls**: Latency depends on provider (typically 1-30 seconds)
825 | 2. **Embedding Generation**: Time proportional to content size and provider
826 | 3. **Vector Search**: Similarity computation over all embeddings
827 | 4. **Content Extraction**: Sync operation in source processing
828 | 
829 | ### Monitoring
830 | 
831 | - **API Logs**: Check loguru output for errors and slow operations
832 | - **Database Queries**: SurrealDB metrics available via admin UI
833 | - **Token Usage**: Estimated via `estimate_tokens()` utility
834 | - **Job Status**: Poll `/commands/{id}` for async operations
835 | 
836 | ---
837 | 
838 | ## Extension Points
839 | 
840 | ### Adding a New Workflow
841 | 
842 | 1. Create `open_notebook/graphs/workflow_name.py`
843 | 2. Define StateDict and node functions
844 | 3. Build graph with `.add_node()` / `.add_edge()`
845 | 4. Create service in `api/workflow_service.py`
846 | 5. Register router in `api/main.py`
847 | 6. Add tests in `tests/test_workflow.py`
848 | 
849 | ### Adding a New Data Model
850 | 
851 | 1. Create model in `open_notebook/domain/model_name.py`
852 | 2. Inherit from BaseModel (domain object)
853 | 3. Implement `save()`, `get()`, `delete()` methods (CRUD)
854 | 4. Add repository functions if complex queries needed
855 | 5. Create database migration in `migrations/`
856 | 6. Add API routes and models in `api/`
857 | 
858 | ### Adding a New AI Provider
859 | 
860 | 1. Configure Esperanto for new provider (see .env.example)
861 | 2. ModelManager automatically detects via environment variables
862 | 3. Override via per-request config (no code changes needed)
863 | 4. Test fallback logic if provider unavailable
864 | 
865 | ---
866 | 
867 | ## Deployment Considerations
868 | 
869 | ### Development
870 | 
871 | - All services on localhost (3000, 5055, 8000)
872 | - Auto-reload on file changes (Next.js, FastAPI)
873 | - Hot-reload database migrations
874 | - Open API docs at http://localhost:5055/docs
875 | 
876 | ### Production
877 | 
878 | - **Frontend**: Deploy to Vercel, Netlify, or Docker
879 | - **API**: Docker container (see Dockerfile)
880 | - **Database**: SurrealDB container or managed service
881 | - **Environment**: Secure .env file with API keys
882 | - **SSL/TLS**: Reverse proxy (Nginx, CloudFlare)
883 | - **Rate Limiting**: Add at proxy layer
884 | - **Auth**: Replace PasswordAuthMiddleware with OAuth/JWT
885 | - **Monitoring**: Log aggregation (CloudWatch, DataDog, etc)
886 | 
887 | ---
888 | 
889 | ## Summary
890 | 
891 | Open Notebook's architecture provides a solid foundation for privacy-focused, AI-powered research. The separation of concerns (frontend/API/database), async-first design, and multi-provider flexibility enable rapid development and easy deployment. LangGraph workflows orchestrate complex AI tasks, while Esperanto abstracts provider details. The result is a scalable, maintainable system that puts users in control of their data and AI provider choice.
892 |
